- New tests against a fake Discord on loopback (`lib/door/testing/fake-discord.ts`), which refuses to be used with a real Discord host, a token that is not this run's fake, or a real-looking credential in the environment (guard F7, with a negative control for each).
- Shared-channel scenarios (`shared-channel.test.ts`): only the one channel is heard; elsewhere is dropped with a receipt; an unlisted person is refused; bots and webhooks are ignored; the loop limit holds; DMs are refused; no post outside the channel; secrets in model output are redacted; edits and deletes.
- An independent audit then made 33 more single changes. 31 turned a test red, one is covered by a second check, and one (any ping counted as a mention of the bot) turned nothing red until a test for it was added.
- Mutation: 61 single changes to the rules, the connector, the guard, the config and the launcher. 59 turned a named test red. Two changed nothing observable, because a second check covers the same case.
- `conformance/suites/pi-discord.docker.test.ts` (local, needs Docker): real Pi 1.5.2 in the sealed cell, a fake Discord and a scripted model. A mention is answered through Pi; a message elsewhere never reaches the model; a secret in model output is redacted; neither secret is in a container, file or log; stop removes everything. The dry run's containment checks pass, and turn red for a cell with a way out. It also shows: the model is given the persona and offered no tool, and a model that asks for one runs nothing; what the cell holds is redacted from replies; with the cell dead the door answers nobody; with the door dead the cell stays sealed and silent, and the next start removes it. 12 of 12 pass on Docker Desktop for Mac.

That Discord returns the first post when a post is retried with the same nonce, and that a real model keeps to what it is told about itself, are shown only by running it. `start` on the command line is covered through the library, not as a command.

## Fixed after an independent audit

- A burst of bot messages that arrived together was decided against one count, so the loop limit did not hold for it. The count is now read and written with nothing waiting in between.
- A post answered with a server error was sent again and could appear twice. Each piece now carries a nonce that Discord checks.

Named bots were added after that audit, with 16 single changes to the new code: all 16 turn a test red.

Not changed, and said in the runbook: with no bot named, `bots: "mentions"` hears any bot or webhook in the channel that writes the mention. The budget is counted with the prices in the config. The dry run cannot check the Message Content switch, because that needs a connection.

- The committed matrix files gained one line per new rule, rebuilt from the rows already recorded. No check result changed.
- `conformance/docker/cell-main.ts` reads an optional model name. The lab's own runs leave it unset.

- Builds on #330 (merged). `origin/main` is merged in, so this shows only its own changes.

## What

- The Discord connector learns, per server, the one role Discord made for this bot when it joined (`managed: true` and `tags.bot_id` equal to the bot's id), from `GUILD_CREATE` and `GUILD_ROLE_CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE`. These come with the `GUILDS` intent it already asks for; no new intent.
- A ping of that role counts as a mention of the bot (`mention`), and writing it out in the text counts as writing the bot's name (`inlineMention`). Roles that only share the name, other bots' managed roles, the bot's role in a server it was not started for, `@everyone` and `@here` still do not count.
- A "no mention" drop now says why when a role was pinged: "a role was mentioned, not the agent", or "the agent's own role is not known yet". The hint (`roleMention` on the inbound event) only changes the receipt wording; `decide()` never admits a message because of it.

## Why

Discord's `@` autocomplete offers the bot's managed role beside the bot user. A person who picks the role sends `<@&role>`, not `<@bot>`, and the door dropped it as "This room needs a mention and there was none", so they looked ignored.

Bots: a named bot that writes the bot's role out is heard as if it wrote the bot's name. The `bots.inline-mention` rule exists so a reply-ping from a bot is not taken as addressing the agent; a reply-ping never puts a role in the text, so that intent holds.

Letta Code had passed the lab's checks but could not be started by the launcher or made from the dashboard. The first reply came 2.7 s after the mention (Pi: 1.0 s), since the first turn also makes its agent; later turns took 0.1 to 0.2 s for both. The dry run's containment checks took 5.8 s (Pi: 4.3 s). The launcher suite takes about 45 s.

- **An agent already running from the launcher.** The command, the config keys and the state folder are unchanged, and a config without `harness` is read as Pi. Two things differ for it: the dry run prints four more lines (the harness, its pinned version, its limits), and the images must be built again after pulling, as after any pull, because the cell's code changed.

## What

- Supersedes #275 and keeps its commit: the `useStateVolume` option and the conditional layout in all three compose generators are agent-tz's work, cherry-picked onto current main with the conflicts in `agent-deploy-templates.ts`, `harness-compose.ts`, `harness.ts` and the deploy route resolved.
- Changes the default from "off everywhere" to a per-agent decision made from the Docker engine (`lib/services/state-volume.ts`): on when the engine runs in a VM or cannot be identified, off on native Linux.
- `settings.useStateVolume` becomes a three-state override: `true` / `false` force the layout, unset (or `null` in a settings patch) is automatic.
- An agent whose databases are already on the named volume keeps the layout when its compose file is regenerated, whatever the default or the setting says. The layout is also kept when the data dir cannot be read, and when the compose file being replaced mounts the volume while the data dir holds no regular `state.db`.
- Runbook: when a compose file gets the layout, and the extra rollback step on a host where it is automatic.

## Why

The state-volume layout exists because a bind mount that crosses a VM file-sharing layer (VirtioFS on Docker Desktop for macOS) can tear SQLite writes. On native Linux there is no such layer, so the layout is unnecessary there, and #273 asks for it not to be applied unconditionally. #275 answered that by turning the layout off for everyone, which would also remove it on the hosts it was built for. The right default depends on the engine, so this asks the engine.

### How the engine is identified

Swarm Map always drives Docker through the local `docker` CLI and writes each agent's data dir on its own filesystem, so the engine is normally on the same machine, but not always on the same kernel. `process.platform` alone is not enough: a Node process inside a container or WSL reports `linux` while the engine behind it is a desktop VM, and the CLI can point at another machine through `DOCKER_HOST` or a context.

- Node not on Linux (macOS, Windows): on, without probing. Every engine there runs Linux in a VM.
- Node on Linux: read `docker info` (`OperatingSystem`, `KernelVersion`, `OSType`, `Name`) and the endpoint: `DOCKER_HOST` when set, else the active context's name and endpoint. Each probe has a 5 second limit.
  - Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Rancher Desktop, a linuxkit or WSL kernel: on.
  - Unknown, so on: the engine does not answer; the context cannot be read (other than a CLI that has no `context` command at all); the endpoint is not a local unix socket; Swarm Map itself runs in a container; or the docker context name or socket path contains `colima`, `lima`, `rancher` or `podman` as a whole word (VM engines that report their guest distro); the socket is under `~/.rd/`; or the engine's host name is exactly `colima`, `colima-<profile>` or `lima-<instance>`, the names those tools give their VMs. Any other hostname is ignored. This is the side that cannot damage a database; `useStateVolume: false` is the way out.
  - Otherwise (a distro name, local socket, not containerised): off.

The compose generators themselves turn the layout off only for an explicit `false` (missing or `null` is on), so a call site that forgets to decide gets the protective layout.

### Existing agents

- **Layout turns off under an agent that has it** (for example a migrated agent on native Linux, or `useStateVolume: false`): the agent's data dir holds symlinks into `/state`, so a compose file without the mount would leave them dangling. Such an agent keeps the layout, and a warning is logged if the setting was `false`. Taking it off the volume is the runbook's Rollback (copy the files back, which replaces the symlinks with real files), after which it follows the setting and the engine again on its next regeneration.
- **Interrupted `state-init`**: on a regeneration, a compose file that mounts the volume also keeps the layout when the data dir holds no regular `state.db`. `state-init` handles `state.db` first and removes the data-dir copy before writing the symlink, so that is the state an interrupted run leaves.
- **Regular `state.db`, no symlinks, old compose still mounting the volume** (symlinks removed by hand, real files written since): the live database is in the data dir, so the agent follows the setting and the engine. On native Linux it regenerates to plain bind mounts and its files are left alone; one log line names the volume and says it is left in place, no longer mounted.
- **Unreadable data dir**: the layout is kept, logged as "could not read", under its own reason.
- **Layout turns on under an agent with plain database files** (for example an older agent regenerated on macOS): `state-init` moves the files onto the volume at the next start, with its existing copy, rename, then delete ordering. This is what main already does on every regeneration.
- Compose files are only regenerated on a VPN or resource-limit change; nothing rewrites an existing agent's file otherwise.

Refs #273.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run`: 234 files passed; 4722 tests passed, 1 skipped (the skip is on main too).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npx eslint`: 128 problems, the same count as main. CI does not run lint.
- Deterministic sanitization gate on the branch diff: clean.
- New tests cover the decision table, the engine probe, the settings validation, and the real create, duplicate, import, deploy and regenerate paths with the platform and probe set. Run against the pre-change sources, 37 of the first round fail.
- Mutation checks, each failing at least one test: every compose call site forced off or made to ignore the setting (duplicate and regenerate included); the existing-layout rule dropped; the compose-mount rule applied over a regular `state.db`, dropped altogether, or satisfied by anything at that path; the mount match without its end anchor; unreadable data dir read as absent, reported as existing-layout, or not logged; VM engines unrecognised, with and without the `docker desktop` name; the name rule without its start boundary, its end boundary or case-insensitivity, and without the context name or the socket path; the host-name rule removed, unanchored, loosened to a prefix or made case-sensitive; the `~/.rd/` rule removed or loosened; the volume-left-in-place log line removed or logged in the wrong cases; containerised process ignored or never detected; unknown engine or failed context read treated as local; context probed with `DOCKER_HOST` set; remote endpoint ignored; macOS treated as native; `null` treated as off in either generator; either probe's timeout removed.
- The full suite was also run with the platform forced to Linux and the probe forced to a native engine, to check that no existing test depends on the machine it runs on. Only the tests that set those two things themselves changed result.
- Not verified: no container was started. The engine strings for Docker Desktop on macOS were read from a real engine; the strings for OrbStack, Rancher Desktop, Colima, Lima, Podman, WSL and native distros are fixtures, not captured from those engines, and the tests say so. Two commits are not green on their own: the cherry-picked commit leaves one `shared-vpn` test failing until the call-site commit, and the probe fix does not typecheck until the commit after it. The branch tip is green.

## What
- Generated deploys set `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` from the Swarm Map process owner (plain and VPN compose `environment:` blocks, and the deploy path's `.env`); both names are reserved from `extraEnv`. From #276 by @agent-tz.
- `state-init` chowns `/state` recursively, after migration, to the uid the image's stage2 will remap the gateway to, instead of copying the bind mount's owner. It takes `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` from the init service's environment (the generated values), else from the agent `.env`, else the `PUID`/`PGID` aliases (extraEnv or `.env`), else the image's `hermes` user. From #278 by @utunga. (That commit's message says the uid can come from extraEnv; with `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` now written by Swarm Map, only `PUID`/`PGID` can.)
- New glue: the init service gets the same `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` lines as the hermes service, so the two always agree. The new real-sh ownership tests get the same 30s timeout as the other real-sh block (see #282).

- Ids are limited to 1-65534, the range stage2 remaps to, in both the init script and the generators; outside it both use the image default.
- An agent whose extraEnv already sets `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` to the generated values keeps regenerating. A different value is refused with a message saying to remove it.

## Why
On a native Linux bind mount, an agent whose data dir isn't owned by uid 10000 crash-loops while the container reports Up (#274). On macOS, `/state` could be left owned by the wrong uid after a recreate, so SQLite refused writes. Each PR fixed one half; together, without the glue commit, `/state` would be chowned to the image default while the gateway ran as the host uid.

## Verification
- Both original commits cherry-picked onto current main with their authors kept; conflicts with the since-added `apiBindHost`/`useStateVolume` generator parameters resolved by hand.
- New test: the init and hermes services carry identical `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` (plain and VPN); confirmed it fails with the glue removed.
- New tests for the id range (script and generators) and for extraEnv that matches or differs.
- Targeted test files run locally; the full suite and typecheck run in CI.

## Risk
Upgrade notes:
- Existing compose files change only when regenerated (a settings change that rewrites the compose, or a recreate through the wizard). #278's description has a helper for updating existing agents' init service in place.
- On Linux, the first recreate after regeneration re-owns the agent's data dir to the Swarm Map user's id, and `/state` with it. That can take a while on a large data dir.
- Try one agent first: regenerate and recreate it, check it starts and can write its databases, then do the rest.

## Links
- Supersedes #276 and #278
- Fixes #274

## What

- Add a process-count limit (2048) to the agent service in both compose generators, from one shared constant `AGENT_PIDS_LIMIT`.
- Publish the agent API port on `127.0.0.1` by default in both compose generators (plain, VPN and wizard output). A new setting, `apiBindHost`, chooses another address; it sits beside `vncBindHost` and `controlBindHost` and is set through `PUT /api/settings`.
- Port allocation now counts host ports published on any single address, not only on `0.0.0.0`, so loopback-published ports are still seen in `docker ps` (refs #231).
- The drift check no longer reports a compose folder whose name could not be an agent's (for example `<name>.removed-<date>` or `<name>.bak`).

## Why

Generated agents had memory and CPU limits but no limit on process count, and their API port listened on every host interface although every caller in this repo is on the host. Separately, a compose folder set aside by hand stayed in the drift report as an agent with an unknown build for as long as it existed.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run`: 223 files passed, 4504 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `scripts/check_sanitization.py --diff --deterministic-only --require-config` against `origin/main`: clean.
- `npx eslint` on the changed files reports only what `main` already carries in those files; nothing new.
- Generated the plain, VPN and wizard compose files and ran `docker compose config` on each (Compose v5.1.4): all three parse, with `pids: 2048` under `deploy.resources.limits` and `host_ip: 127.0.0.1` on the API port.
- That check caught one thing worth knowing: a service-level `pids_limit` beside an existing `deploy.resources.limits` block is rejected by `docker compose` ("can't set distinct values on 'pids_limit' and 'deploy.resources.limits.pids'"). The limit is therefore written as `deploy.resources.limits.pids`, and the tests assert `pids_limit` is never emitted.
- `apiBindHost` tests: the default is loopback in all outputs; an explicit address is emitted in the plain, VPN, shared-VPN and wizard outputs; a value that is not an IP address (`[::1]`, `localhost`, `a: b`, whitespace, `127.0.0.1, target: 22`) or not a string is refused by settings validation, and IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and the empty value are accepted; a non-address value handed to either generator is written as loopback; the wizard deploy writes the configured address; a settings-driven regenerate hands the configured address to the generator.
- Rendered six outputs (plain, VPN, shared VPN, wizard, wizard with Google, wizard on shared VPN) for each of `127.0.0.1`, `::`, `::1`, `2001:db8::` and `0.0.0.0`, and ran `docker compose config` on all 30 files: all pass. On the two shared-VPN outputs the port block is commented out while the agent is on the VPN, so there the address is checked by a test that the restored file is byte-identical to the plain one.
- New tests were written first and seen to fail.
- Not verified: no container was created or started from the new files, so the limit and the bind were not observed on a running container.

## Risk

- Only newly generated or regenerated compose files change. Files already on disk are not rewritten. A file is regenerated when an agent's VPN toggle or resource limits are changed in settings, so an existing agent picks the changes up at that point.
- Agents created through the setup wizard keep their existing compose file: settings does not regenerate those. They pick the new defaults up only when recreated through the wizard.
- Loopback publish: anything that reached an agent's API port from another machine, or from another container on a Linux host (where `host.docker.internal` resolves to the bridge address, not loopback), will no longer connect after a regenerate unless `apiBindHost` is set. Nothing in this repo does either: the dashboard's health check and the docs use `localhost`.
- `apiBindHost` is one value for the whole install, like the two existing bind-host settings. It is API only; those two have no UI either. It must be a bare IPv4 or IPv6 address with no zone id (no `%`), or empty for the default; anything else is refused. The address is written into the compose file as a quoted string, so an IPv6 address ending in a colon (`::`, `2001:db8::`) stays valid YAML. The generators apply the same check when they write a file and fall back to loopback, so a stored value that is not an address is never emitted. The validation of the two existing bind-host settings is unchanged.
- Process limit: 2048 counts threads as well as processes. A workload that legitimately holds more would see spawn failures; the value is one constant.
- Drift: the name rule applies to the folder sweep only. Registry rows are never filtered, and a validly named folder with no registry row and no container is still reported.
- The Google OAuth callback port in the wizard generator is unchanged.

## What

- A third harness adapter behind the door: the Claude Agent SDK (`lib/runtimes/claude-sdk/`), with the same four verbs as Pi and Letta Code (start, send, read, veto). Lab only: no launcher, no UI, nothing wired into the app.
- The model route speaks a second wire format, Anthropic Messages, with the key swap, metering and the budget cap. The OpenAI chat format is unchanged.
- A fake SDK and a scripted Anthropic model for CI, twelve shims broken on purpose, a cell image for the sealed Docker rig, and four checks that are this harness's own.
- `docs/lab/claude-sdk.md`: what is proven and what is not.

## Why

The door's promise is that the rules hold whatever the harness is. Two harnesses that both speak the OpenAI chat format were not much of a test of that. The Claude Agent SDK speaks another format, is a compiled program, and has a permission system of its own, so it tests parts of the contract the first two did not.

## Verification

Real Claude Agent SDK 0.3.325 (Claude Code 2.1.325), scripted model, no key and no account:

- **Process level: 18 of 18 checks pass.** Twelve broken shims each turned their named checks red.
- **Sealed Docker cell: 24 of 24 pass** (S0-S3, the shared checks, C8, C9, C10, and the four of its own). Eleven broken rigs each turned their named checks red.
- **Pi 1.5.2 and Letta Code 0.34.60 re-run after the shared changes:** Pi 14 of 14 at process level and 20 of 20 in its cell; Letta Code 16 of 16 and 22 of 22. All four matrix files were made again from those runs.
- **Network, by hand:** a packet capture in the cell during the Docker run. In the in-cell checks that run no probe, every packet the cell sent went to the door or to Docker's resolver. Started with its defaults instead, in the same sealed container, the SDK looked up `api.anthropic.com` ten times; every lookup failed and no packet left for anywhere but the door.
- `npx vitest run`: 255 files, all passing. `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. Sanitize gate, deterministic layer: clean on every changed file. The semantic layer needs a key this machine does not hold, so it runs here in CI.
- **Mutation, by hand:** 89 changes to the new code, one at a time. 84 turned a named test red. Four of the other five now have a test; the fifth was a guard nothing could make refuse, and was removed.

What the real SDK did that the plan did not expect, each now with a test and a broken shim:

- Its permission callback is not asked about every call. It ran a file read in its work folder and a shell `ls` without asking. The shim tells it to ask about each tool by name.
- Its hooks do not run in its minimal mode, so the callback is the veto.
- A failed model call ends the turn as a `result` of subtype `success`, with the error as its text. The shim posts nothing unless the turn says it did not fail.

## Background
Follow-up from PR #92 (empty `SIGNAL_REQUIRE_MENTION` silently un-gating agents). An independent review of that diff surfaced a separate, pre-existing mismatch worth tracking.

## The gap
HSM's settings GET/PUT (`app/api/harnesses/[id]/settings/route.ts`) reads and writes **only the agent's `.env`** for mention-gating. But the runtime (`hermes-agent-mt` `gateway/platforms/signal.py:247-249`) resolves `require_mention` from the **gateway config `extra` (YAML) first**, falling back to the `SIGNAL_REQUIRE_MENTION` env var only when the YAML value is `None` (`gateway/config.py` ~1127-1137).

Consequence: if an agent's YAML sets `require_mention` (or `signal.require_mention`), that **outranks** the `.env` value at runtime, and the HSM UI neither reads nor reflects it. The UI can therefore show a mention-gating state that doesn't match what the agent actually does.

## Current impact
**Latent.** All current NimbleCoAI fleet agents are env-var/`.env`-driven (no YAML `require_mention`), so the UI is accurate today. This only bites if an agent is configured via gateway YAML.

## Options
1. Have the settings GET also read the agent's gateway YAML config and report the effective (YAML-or-env) value; PUT could warn or refuse when a YAML override is present.
2. Document that `.env` is HSM's source of truth and have agent import/normalize strip/avoid YAML `require_mention`.
3. Accept as known-limitation and leave the code comment that's already in `route.ts`.

## References
- PR #92 (merged)
- `route.ts` mention-gating read (has an inline caveat comment)
- `hermes-agent-mt` `gateway/platforms/signal.py`, `gateway/config.py`

To run any ACP agent behind the door with the same rules, receipts and sealed cell as the other harnesses, starting with OpenCode.

Spawned from the credential-request-link discussion (2026-07-03): agents now compose HSM URLs/API calls (`/keys?request=&assign=`), other tools script against `/api/keys` and `/api/harnesses`, and the BYO-credentials epic will add broker endpoints consumed by every gateway. The API is becoming a contract; today it's an accretion.

## Current state (observed)

- Routes are unversioned (`/api/keys`, `/api/harnesses`, `/api/settings`, `/api/people`, `/api/surfaces`, …)
- Auth model is good but implicit: GETs ungated, mutations require the `hsm_session` cookie (operator token HMAC). Nothing documents which routes exist or their shapes except the source.
- No error envelope convention (`{error}` vs bare 404 HTML vs NextResponse defaults)
- Naming drift: agents are "harnesses" in the API (`h_*` ids), "agents" everywhere in conversation; there is no `/api/agents` (a natural first guess — it 404s)
- No machine-readable schema; consumers (agents, scripts, future broker clients) reverse-engineer from `lib/services/*`

## Proposal

1. **`/api/v1` prefix** with the current surface frozen as v1; old paths alias during a deprecation window
2. **OpenAPI spec generated from source** (route handlers + zod schemas), served at `/api/v1/openapi.json`; becomes the doc of record
3. **Uniform error envelope**: `{ error: string, code?: string }` + correct content-type on all API 4xx/5xx (no HTML 404s under `/api`)
4. **Explicit auth policy doc**: ungated-GET / cookie-gated-mutation as a stated invariant, plus a second credential class (scoped automation tokens) for non-browser callers — needed before the credential broker lands
5. **Naming decision**: pick `harnesses` or `agents` once, alias the other
6. **First standardized flow**: the credential-request pattern (`/keys?request=&assign=`) documented as the canonical "intent link" idiom — GET encodes intent, never state change

## Non-goals

Public internet exposure. This stays a tailnet-plane API; standardization is about contract quality, not reach.

Related: BYO-credentials epic (nimbleco-memory `specs/2026-07-03-byo-user-credentials-epic.md`) — broker endpoints should land on this surface, not beside it.

## What

- **Save, Start and pm2.** When pm2 runs a door agent, Save now restarts it through pm2 (`pm2 restart <id>` after the store and re-render), not as a plain background process beside it. Start hands the door to pm2 whenever pm2 has an app for the agent's `start.sh`, running or stopped. The page says what happened and names the app.
- **Refused, with nothing stopped**, when pm2 is up but cannot be asked, when two pm2 apps run the same `start.sh`, or when the door's parent is pm2 and pm2 lists no app for it.
- **A failed stop no longer leaves the door down.** If a save's stop ended the door but reported a failure, the door is started again on the old rules, the same way it was running before.
- **The cell's `/tmp` is capped**: 32 MB, `noexec,nosuid,nodev`, in every container the launcher and the conformance rig write. It is checked as written (S0), as Docker made it (S0d / rig S3), from inside the cell (S3) and by filling it (S4). A must-fail cell with an uncapped `/tmp` turns those four red.

## Why

A door under pm2 that had its rules saved from the dashboard came back as an unsupervised process: pm2 showed it stopped, and the page said "started by page". Nothing restarted it after a crash. Starting one from the page while pm2 had an app for it could also leave two doors waiting to happen. Separately, an audit found the sealed cell's `/tmp` had no size, so a shell in the cell could fill it up to half the machine's memory.

## Verification

- Test first. Red, then green: 10 new service tests with a stubbed pm2 (save, start, stop, refusals, a failed restart, a failed stop), 7 adapter tests against a stand-in `pm2` command (lookup by script path and by pid, no `jlist` while the daemon is down, two apps refused, restart by id as an argument, waits for the door), 4 page tests, and /tmp tests for the report, the launcher's seal check and the rig's.
- Real pm2 6.0.14, isolated `PM2_HOME`, real launcher adapter, stand-in launcher CLI, run by hand: the page's own pm2 command, then Save, Stop and Start through the service. One door process after each step, pm2 `online` with a new pid and the new rules after Save, `stopped` after Stop, `online` after Start. A door that exits 0 and one killed by SIGKILL both stay stopped under `--stop-exit-codes 0`.
- Full unit suite: 5,961 passed, 1 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean. Sanitization gate, deterministic layer: clean.
- Docker Desktop, images built for this code: the Pi launcher suite (21, with the new must-fail `/tmp` cell), the Letta Code launcher suite (15), the persona and memory suite (5), and the rig suites for Pi (66), Letta Code (34) and the Claude Agent SDK (38) all pass with `/tmp` capped and `noexec`. In one run, the `open` must-fail rig for Letta Code and for the Claude Agent SDK did not reach the public internet. Both passed when run again; that rig needs real internet access.
- Mutations: 24 lines broken one at a time in the service, the pm2 adapter, the page, the `/tmp` reader, the seal checks and the rendering. All 24 turned a named test red. Three more, each check removed in turn (as Docker made it, from inside, by filling it), turned the Docker must-fail test red.

## Risk

- Swarm Map now runs `pm2 jlist` before a Start or a Save, but only when pm2's daemon is up. If pm2 is up and not on the `PATH` Swarm Map runs with, Start and Save are refused with that reason rather than run around pm2.
- A door already running under pm2 needs nothing after this lands: the next Save from the page goes through pm2. The new `/tmp` cap applies from the next start of a door, and needs the images built again (`node lib/lab/pi-discord/cli.ts build`, and with `--harness letta-code`), as any change to the cell does.

## What
- A command policy for the shell. The record can hold `tools.commands.allow` and `tools.commands.block`, lists of command names, with shipped defaults. The door reads each shell call whole: a command made only of names on the allow list, writing nothing, runs with no request in the room. One with a blocked name or a clearly destructive part never runs. Everything else asks exactly as before, with the same hash binding.
- A small shell reader of our own (`lib/core/tools/command-policy.ts`, no new dependency). It understands words, quotes, backslashes, `| || && ;`, new lines and redirections. Anything else asks: substitutions, variables, globs, groups, here-docs, comments, background jobs, `VAR=` prefixes, non-ASCII characters. A second, looser reading searches for blocks behind `;`, `$( )`, backticks, `sudo`/`env`/`timeout`/`xargs`, and inside `sh -c` or `eval`.
- Shells, interpreters and wrappers can never be on the allow list, so a yes is never skipped for a script the agent wrote. Receipts name the deciding rule (`command=allow:ls,grep`, `command=block:rm-recursive`), never the command.
- The launcher config takes `tools.commands`, the Tools card shows and edits both lists, a new rule `tools.commands` is added, and there is a new harness check, K1.

## Why
A shell that asks for every `ls` is one nobody leaves on. Read-only commands should not need a person, and destructive ones should not be offered to one.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run`: 5,701 passed. `tsc`, `next build` and the deterministic sanitization layer are clean.
- 174 unit tests of the reader, including hidden writes (`cat x > /etc/y`, `ls; rm -rf /scratch`, `$(…)`, backticks, `env X=…`, quoted tricks), a parser failure, and 3,000 random commands. The K1 commands are also run against a reader that looks at the first word only, which lets most of them through.
- K1, the new check: a listed command runs with no request, ten that each hide a write wait for a yes, and a blocked one never runs. The gate that asks nobody turns it red.
- Real Pi 1.5.2: as a process, 43 of 43. In the sealed cell, 51 of 51, plus 20 of 20 for the launcher suite with a fake Discord.
- Letta Code 0.34.60 and the Claude Agent SDK 0.3.325: unaffected. K1 is listed as not run for both, with the reason. Letta Code: 26 of 26 as a process, 34 in the cell, 15 for the launcher. Claude Agent SDK: 36 of 36 as a process, 38 of 38 in the cell. The first Letta Code process run went red on C5v, a timing check, under a load average near 55. It passed when run again. All matrices were rewritten from these runs.
- 63 hand mutations across the reader, `decide()`, the door, the launcher config, the record check and the Tools card: 59 turned a test red. The other 4 are checks that a later check repeats.

## Risk
- **Default on.** A config with the shell on and no `commands` gets the shipped lists, so read-only commands stop asking. To turn that off, set `"commands": { "allow": [], "block": [...] }`.
- **The reader is ours.** It is narrow on purpose: anything it does not fully read asks. A command it reads differently from bash is the risk. The audit covered quoting, `$'…'`, IFS, line continuations, look-alike letters, `\rm`, `/bin/rm` and wrappers.
- **A listed command runs as found on the cell's PATH.** An earlier yes can change what is there, as the doc already says of any yes.
- **Shared files.** This touches `decide.ts` (one block in `decideTool`), `door.ts` (`commandOf`, and the command passed to `decide` and kept on a held call), `types.ts`/`shape.ts`/`events.ts` (one optional field each), `config.ts` and `door-tools-card.tsx`.

## What

- A door agent's `start.sh` no longer names Node by a versioned Homebrew Cellar path. The path is chosen in order (new `lib/services/door-node.ts`): `SWARM_MAP_NODE` if set; else, when `process.execPath` is `<prefix>/Cellar/<formula>/<version>/bin/node`, the stable `<prefix>/opt/<formula>/bin/node` if it is there and is the same major version; else `process.execPath` unchanged.
- Before a start, and before a save is applied to a running door, the chosen Node is checked: present, executable, and 22.18 or newer (the first line that runs a `.ts` entry with no flag). If not, nothing is run or stopped; the request is refused with a plain message, and the agent page shows it in the "Last dry run" card. A refusal of this kind reports the cell's seal as "not checked", not as "no".
- The Node is chosen on every call, not once when Swarm Map starts, so an upgrade under a running dashboard is seen at the next start.
- `docs/lab/dashboard-slice.md` documents the order, the check, `SWARM_MAP_NODE`, and that an existing agent picks up the new path the next time it is started or saved, because `start.sh` is written again each time.

## Why

A supervisor runs `start.sh` again after a crash or reboot, long after it was written. A Cellar path stops working when `brew upgrade` removes the old keg, so a supervised door would crash-loop. The stable `opt` link is the path Homebrew keeps pointed at the installed version.

- Written test-first: the new tests failed before the change (6 failing), and pass after.
- `npx vitest run`: 242 files, 4833 passed, 1 skipped.

## What
- New `sharedVpn` setting: the agent joins one shared gluetun container (`gluetun-shared`, project `swarm-vpn`), so all VPN'd agents use a single Mullvad device and the host stays off VPN.
- Toggle is a surgical, exactly-reversible edit of the hermes service's networking lines; deploy-born hardening (read_only, tmpfs, cap_drop) is never re-rendered.
- Both compose generators honor `sharedVpn` and emit the same bytes as the toggle, so a regen keeps the VPN. A hand-made `network_mode` makes a regen refuse instead of dropping it.
- Each VPN'd agent's API server gets its own port (its allocated host port) inside the shared namespace. Settings PUT refuses when `.env` or config.yaml names a different port, or when a fixed-port platform (webhook, msgraph_webhook, a2a, teams) is on. The deploy route now uses the shared port scan, so ports of VPN'd agents are not handed out again.

## Why
The hand-made vera setup works but any regeneration would silently drop it, and the existing per-agent VPN cannot be used on deploy-born agents (the #204 guard refuses regeneration there, correctly).

## Verification
- Red-green: `lib/services/shared-vpn.test.ts` and `app/api/harnesses/[id]/settings/route-shared-vpn.test.ts` (real files in a tmp dir): on/off round-trip byte-exact, hardening kept, regen keeps the VPN, port pin, refusals write nothing, the key file is never read, stale-version PUT is refused.
- An independent adversarial review found 6 issues, all fixed with regression tests in the second commit.
- `pnpm vitest run`: 153 files / 2099 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean. No new lint errors.
- Not deployed. The gluetun image digest was read from the Mini (read-only).

## Risk
- While on the VPN, the agent's API port is not published to the host (on purpose: publishing via gluetun would mean recreating gluetun on every toggle and cutting off every joined agent).
- Recreating or restarting gluetun leaves joined agents with no network until they are recreated. Swarm-map only ever runs `up -d --no-recreate`.
- gluetun's control server is locked: a deny-all auth config (one role, no routes, so every route returns 401 in v3.40.0) is mounted read-only. Privileged or net-admin agent services are refused.
- Agents on the VPN share one localhost. Hermes itself only listens on its API port, but servers agents start at runtime (e.g. `python3 -m http.server`, seen on the fleet, some bound to 127.0.0.1) become reachable by every VPN'd agent.

Flagged by the independent audit of the #138 re-cut (2026-07-03). Non-blocking there; filing as the agreed follow-up.

The list route `GET /api/harnesses/[id]/surfaces/[platform]/admins` passes the auth middleware unauthenticated (GETs are intentionally ungated for the plugin's boolean hot paths). But unlike the boolean routes, it returns the **full admin identity list** — Signal phone numbers / UUIDs, Telegram ids — and accepts **any** harness id, so anything that can reach HSM (`host.docker.internal:3000` from every agent container) can enumerate admin PII **cross-harness**, including admins set via the dashboard that appear in no agent's env.

With mutations transport-gated (#139, active), this is information disclosure only — its old role as a confused-deputy `actor` source is defanged. Severity is bounded (each agent already holds its own surface's admin ids in env) but cross-harness enumeration of phone numbers is a real privacy gap.

**Fix options:** require the operator session cookie for this one GET (dashboard is the only intended consumer — the plugin never calls the list route, only the boolean `admins/[userId]` and `groups/[groupId]` paths, which must stay open); or return ids redacted/hashed unless authenticated. Add a test that a cookie-less list GET is refused while the boolean hot paths stay 200.

## What

- **Persona document.** A door agent's rules record takes a Markdown persona (up to 8 KB), edited on the Rules tab with a preview and a short guide. The launcher puts it in the system prompt, and then writes what the agent can do after it, from the rules. A persona cannot add an ability or remove that text. New agents start with a warm, plain default persona.
- **Notes kept by the door.** For each room, three small Markdown files (about the room, people who asked to be remembered, ongoing threads) in the agent's state folder on the host. They are given to the agent when a conversation starts, after a restart too, and never to another room. The agent changes them only through one door tool, `memory_note`. The door checks each change (size, the redactor, no mentions or ids, a person's note only when they asked), writes it, and writes a receipt.
- **Memory tab** for door agents: view, edit, wipe and download the notes. Everything shown is redacted. A kept scratch folder (`tools.keepScratch`, off by default, same size cap) can be wiped there too.
- **Checks.** Six memory checks (M1 to M6) with something broken on purpose for each, a launcher Docker suite with a real stop and start, and a fixture test that an agent made before this loads and runs unchanged.

## Why

Door agents felt robotic: a name and one line, and no memory across a restart. Claude Agent SDK: 36 of 36 as a process, 38 of 38 in Docker. All six matrices were rewritten by these runs (a new rule, `mem.notes`, adds a line to each).

## What

- The door shows that a door agent is working on a message: 👀 on it as soon as it is handed to the agent, Discord's typing indicator renewed about every 8 s while the turn runs, then ✅ in place of 👀 once the reply is posted, or ⚠️ when the turn ends with no reply (a failed model call, an error, a timeout, no answer, or a reply the door refused after delivery).
- Only a message the door delivered to the agent gets any of this. Dropped messages get no reaction and no typing: chatter, people or bots not on the list, other channels. The connector also refuses a reaction or typing call outside the channels it may post to.
- While a tool call waits for an admin's yes, 👀 stays and typing stops. Typing comes back once the admin answers.
- Two switches in the rules record, `discord.statusReactions` and `discord.typing`. Both are on when left out, and neither changes the policy or its hash. Each has a toggle on the dashboard's Rules tab. The dry run says to allow Add Reactions in the channel, and the runbook covers the new permission, the behaviour and the `out.status` receipt.

## Why

A door agent that reads web pages can take 20 to 40 seconds to answer, and it showed nothing in the meantime, so people took it to have ignored them. The other bots in the server show 👀 and typing. The door owns chat, so it shows these signs and the harness plays no part.

⚠️ is used rather than ❌. ❌ is how an admin says no to a request, and a turn with no answer is not a refusal of what the person asked. The door's own line in the room says what went wrong.

## Verification

- Test-first, against the fake Discord: `lib/lab/pi-discord/__tests__/turn-status.test.ts` (end to end with the launcher's policy, the real connector and the door), `lib/door/__tests__/turn-status.test.ts` (fake clock: no timer outlives a turn, renewal, no stacking, paused while held), and new cases in `lib/door/__tests__/discord-connector.test.ts` (scope, rate limits). The fake Discord now answers the reaction and typing endpoints, and can refuse them with 429 or 403.
- Rate limits: a short 429 on reactions is waited out off the turn's path and the swap still lands in order. A long one, or a 403, writes one `out.status` receipt per kind per turn, and the reply is posted at once.
- Mutation run: 17 mutants, all caught. Among them: reacting on dropped messages, never using ⚠️, a timer left running, typing not paused for an admin, the turn waiting on typing, reactions out of order, an unhandled rejection, a long rate limit being waited for, a react outside the channel scope, a failed receipt write left as an unhandled rejection, and the dashboard toggle not wired.
- Full suite, `tsc --noEmit`, and the deterministic sanitization layer on every changed file are all clean. The semantic layer did not run because no key was set.
- Pi Docker launcher suite (`conformance/suites/pi-discord.docker.test.ts`) on freshly built images: 20 of 20 pass. Mutating the launcher so it starts the door without status turns it red. It now checks that the launcher starts the door with status on (✅ and typing on an answered message) and that nothing is put on a dropped message.

## Risk

- Without Add Reactions in the channel, each turn writes one `out.status` receipt (code 403). The turn is not affected.
- A change to either switch takes effect on the next start, like the persona. It is not part of the policy hash, so the Overview's "rules in force" line does not show it.
- A stop while a turn is running leaves 👀 on that message.

## Symptom

Wire a Discord bot via surfaces/connect with `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS=<username>` **before** inviting it to a server → the adapter boots, logs `Could not resolve usernames: <username>`, and then silently ignores everyone. The operator's mental model is "connected = working"; the bot looks dead until someone manually restarts the container after the invite.

Hit on all six bots of the 2026-07-27/28 Cyborg.Garden rollout — each needed one manual `docker restart` after Authorize.

## Cause

Username→ID resolution (`_resolve_allowed_usernames` in the hermes Discord adapter) runs once at `on_ready` against current guild members. A bot invited after boot never re-resolves.

## Options

1. **Real fix (adapter-side, hermes-agent-mt / upstream):** re-run `_resolve_allowed_usernames` on `on_guild_join` (and arguably on a slow periodic retry while unresolved entries remain). Same fork-first pattern as the role-mention fix (hermes-agent-mt#121).
2. **HSM-side workaround:** a "re-resolve / restart" nudge in the harness UI when the Discord surface has unresolved username entries, or an automatic recreate triggered the first time the bot appears in a guild (HSM can poll `/users/@me/guilds` with the stored token post-connect).

Option 1 is where the bug lives; option 2 improves operator visibility either way (surfacing `Could not resolve usernames` in the surface status would have saved four debugging rounds).

Related: gardener seed `memory/handoffs/2026-07/28-juniper-gardener-seed-garden-discord-agents.md` (Task 3).

_Requested by **Miles**_

Before: Swarm Map had no way to keep a tool's output out of an agent's model context, so outputs licensed under terms like the Kaitiakitanga License (Papa Reo's te reo Māori transcripts, which may not go to services that collect or use them) couldn't be handled safely, and there was no Papa Reo transcription for agents.

After: an agent's Settings tab has two new cards.
- **Protected Outputs (oven-mitt)** adds an [ovenmitt](https://github.com/utunga/oven-mitt) vault daemon as a sidecar (no network, read-only, no capabilities). Operators add vaults; per vault they tick which chats may receive its files (editable match, e.g. `signal/*` or one chat) and optionally a host folder to export to. The agent holds outputs by handle and can send them to the chat it's talking to, but can't read them.
- **Transcription (Papa Reo escalation)** installs the papareo-transcribe pack, adds a `papareo` vault, turns voice input off and raises memory for whisper. The agent asks the person "local or Papa Reo?" first; Papa Reo transcripts go through the vault. A "Kaitiakitanga-compliant" declaration checks the agent's model hosts and requires a typed `I CONFIRM` for anything remote before letting the agent read Papa Reo text.

How:

## What

- Adds a Letta Code adapter to the lab: `lib/runtimes/letta-code/` drives Letta Code 0.34.60 through the door with the same four verbs as Pi (start, send, read, veto). It is the second harness to pass the harness-neutral checks.
- Adds a fake Letta Code so the checks run in CI, nine shims broken on purpose that each turn their named checks red, and a sealed Docker cell for it.
- Records the result for the pinned version in two matrix files, made from real runs.
- Adds `docs/lab/letta-code.md`: what is proven, what is not.

Nothing is wired into the Swarm Map app or UI, and nothing here starts or touches a running agent. This is not the old Letta integration brought back: that one stays removed, and its guard test still passes.

## Result, for Letta Code 0.34.60

| Run | Checks passed |
|---|---|
| Plain process on a laptop | 16 of 16 |
| Sealed Docker cell (Docker Desktop for Mac) | 22 of 22 |

Scripted room, scripted model, placeholder keys, loopback only. No account, no real key, no real chat. Started the way the shim starts it, Letta Code made no call off the machine.

Not met, and said so in the matrix and the doc:

- **Memory per room.** Letta Code keeps one memory per agent and reads it into every conversation. So the door gives it one room (or one person's direct messages) and refuses a policy that opens more: new rule `mem.one-scope`, with tests. Check C11n shows the rule with real Letta Code in the loop; a shim that hides the memory from the door is given the second room and the note crosses.
- **Direct messages**, for the same reason as Pi: its sessions share one folder on disk.
- C6, C7, C13, C14, C17 and the wider C11 are not run. The doc says why for each.

## Changes to the shared contracts

Each was a place where the contract had been written around Pi.

1. The model route answers "which models are there?" itself, from its price list. Letta Code asks before its first call. Nothing is forwarded and the real key is not used.
2. A policy has to fit the harness: `fitProblems`, rule `mem.one-scope`, enforced in the door from the `nativeMemory` a shim declares. It is listed as a guardrail, because that declaration comes from the cell.
3. A harness adapter can patch the lab's starting policy (the fixture opens several rooms).
4. The Docker rig takes the cell's harness as a part (`CellKind`): the name of its image, its entry, and how to ask it for its version. A suite says which harness its cells hold with `setCell()`. Pi stays the default, and its Docker suite was run again on this branch.
5. The removal guard lets the npm name of Letta Code through, and one lock file: the cell image's, which lists the packages Letta Code itself depends on.

Pi's process matrix was regenerated from a real Pi run, because the catalogue has one more rule. Pi still passes 14 of 14.

## Why

The lab's claim is that a rule has one implementation and the harness is not part of it. One harness cannot show that. A second one, with a different way of being driven and a memory of its own, did: the checks and the door needed no change to their logic, and the five contract changes above are the whole cost.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run`: all green. `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. Sanitization gate, deterministic layer, on the diff: clean.
- `SWARMLAB_LETTA_CODE_BIN=... npm run conformance -- letta-code` against real Letta Code 0.34.60: 16 of 16, and all nine broken shims caught.
- `npm run conformance:docker -- letta-code`: 22 of 22 with real Letta Code in the cell, and all ten broken rigs caught. The images are named for the source they were built from, and the run compares their files with this branch before it starts.
- `npm run conformance:docker -- pi.docker`: Pi's Docker suite still passes with the rig generalized.
- `SWARMLAB_PI_BIN=... npm run conformance -- pi.real`: 14 of 14 after the contract changes.
- Forty hand mutations of the new code. Two survived at first and now have tests; one of them was a real gap in the shim, now closed. See the doc, "What this does not show", item 11.

## Second audit (independent pass)

Everything was built and run again on this tree, from images named for it: Letta Code 16 of 16 as a process and 22 of 22 in the cell, Pi 14 of 14 and 20 of 20, nine broken shims and ten broken rigs caught for Letta Code, eight and ten for Pi. Found and fixed, each test-first:

- **A moved room carried the memory with it.** Two policies that each open one room both fitted, so a one-memory harness could learn in one room and then be given another. A room under the listed room that is not a thread was a second conversation too. The door now gives such a harness the first conversation only, for as long as the door runs. C11n moves the room and expects the refusal.
- **A harness's patch to the lab's starting policy could loosen it.** It may now only take rooms away, and a lab refuses to start otherwise.
- **Two guard changes could be widened with every test green** (the whole npm scope, every lock file). Both are pinned.

Twenty-five more hand mutations: twenty-three red at once, the two guard ones above now red. A packet capture in the sealed cell saw Letta Code look up only the door and connect out only to the door's model route. The doc has the detail, and what is still not shown.

## Risk

- Lab only. No app code path imports any of this.
- The Docker result is for one machine and one Docker version.
- Letta Code ships several times a day. The shim sends no turn to any version but the pinned one.

## What

- A door agent can be given its first tools, all inside its sealed cell: read files, write files, and a shell. Off by default. No web access.
- Each class of tool has a mode in the rules record: never, ask, allow. Shell starts at ask. `decide()` gives the answer; the harness only carries it.
- In ask mode the door posts the exact call in the room and holds it until an admin replies `approve` or reacts ✅. Anyone else's answer does nothing. No answer in time is a no. The yes is tied to a hash of the call, and the gate in the cell runs only what has that hash.
- File tools are kept in a scratch folder (a 64 MB in-memory mount under the launcher, gone on stop). Limits: time per shell call, output size, calls per conversation per hour.
- Ten harness-neutral tool checks, each with something broken on purpose that must turn it red. Run for Pi as a process and in Docker. Letta Code's matrix lists them as not run, with the reason.
- Dashboard: a Tools card on the Rules tab, and an "Approvals only" box on Receipts.

Design and results: `docs/lab/tools-slice.md`.

## Why

A chat-only agent cannot do much. This lets an agent work on files and run commands without widening what the cell can reach, and puts a person in the loop for the risky class.

## Verification

One machine (Docker Desktop for Mac, engine 29.5.2). A scripted model and a fake chat room throughout: no real model, no real Discord, no real credential. Everything below was run on this branch with `main` merged in.

- `npx vitest run`: 250 files, 5235 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `next build` passes. Sanitization gate (deterministic) clean on the diff.
- Real Pi 1.5.2 as a process: 24 checks pass (14 shared, 10 tool). 13 shims and rigs broken on purpose each turned its named checks red.
- Real Pi 1.5.2 in the sealed Docker cell: 30 checks pass (4 seal, 13 shared, C8, C9, C10, 10 tool). 16 rigs broken on purpose each turned its named checks red, 5 of them cells with a broken gate.
- The launchers' own Docker suites, with a fake Discord: Pi 18 of 18, Letta Code 15 of 15. In them a shell command waited in the channel, did not run on a tick from the asker or a stranger, and ran on the admin's tick. File tools worked in the scratch folder and were refused outside it four ways. A 72 MB write to the 64 MB scratch folder landed no more than 64 MB.
- 77 hand mutations across `decide()`, the door, the gate, the shim, the connector, the launcher and the page: 76 turned a named test red, one changes nothing the code does.
- Letta Code 0.34.60, process and Docker: shared checks pass as before; the tool checks are listed as not run.

Not shown: what a real model does with tools; real Discord; whether a person reads the request well.

A self-audit (bypass, mutation, over-build) found and fixed four things: the dry run said "tools: none" whatever the config asked for; a tool request whose lookup failed moved its turn's deadline; a held call was not dropped when its turn settled; and, after merging `main`, tools could be switched on for a harness that has no gate for them.

## Risk

- **Shared contracts changed, additively.** `decide()` now answers `ask` for a class on the ask list (that field was refused before), and has one new event kind, `approval`. `tool_verdict` carries an optional `hash`. `ConnectorInbound` carries an optional `replyTo`, and connectors may emit a `reaction` event. A harness adapter that reads only `allow` keeps working.
- **Pi's gate now needs a yes that names the call.** A bare `allow` is a no. Every Pi cell image has to be built from this code, which the image naming already forces.
- **A config that hears anyone in the channel now makes a public record.** Its policy hash changes, so a running agent with that setting shows "older rules" until it is restarted. Such a config with a tool switched on is refused.
- **The gate is a guardrail.** It holds a model to what was approved. It does not hold something that has taken over the cell's own processes; the cell is the wall for that, as before.
- **The matrices for both harnesses were regenerated** from real runs, because the list of known checks grew.
- **CI time.** The fake-Pi suite is longer: it now runs ten more checks and five more broken shims.
- **One PR, shell included.** The source change is about 780 lines; the rest is tests, the rig, regenerated matrices and docs. Shell was not split out: it is the tool the suite already drove, so leaving it out would have saved little.
- **Tools are for Pi only.** A config that names another harness and switches a tool on is refused, and the Tools card is switched off for it.
- **A new harness adapter needs its matrix regenerated** after this lands, because the list of known checks grew by ten.

## What happened

A harness's `state.db` (SQLite, WAL mode) was physically corrupted — torn page write (an invalid page-pointer containing content bytes), doubly-referenced FTS pages, orphaned pages. Seeding coincided with a period of Docker Desktop VM memory exhaustion (swap ~100%, repeated container restarts). Recovery via `.recover` succeeded with zero pre-existing row loss, but the agent silently lost ~1 day of new transcripts before anyone noticed, because writes failed continuously while the harness kept running.

## Why this is structural, not a one-off

All harness state DBs live on the macOS host and are reached by containers through a VirtioFS bind mount. SQLite's durability assumptions (fsync ordering, mmap coherence) are not reliably honored across that translation layer; under VM memory pressure a mid-write hard-stop can tear pages. This is a known SQLite-on-Docker-Desktop-bind-mount failure class. The VM memory bump reduces the pressure but does not remove the vector. Every harness shares this architecture.

## Proposed fixes (in value order)

1. **Named-volume migration**: generated compose puts `state.db` (or the whole data dir's DB files) on a named Docker volume (native ext4 inside the VM), with a periodic `sqlite3 .backup` export to the bind-mounted data dir so host-side tooling/backups still see a consistent snapshot.
2. **Scheduled integrity monitoring**: a fleet-wide periodic `PRAGMA quick_check` (read-only) surfaced in the dashboard — in this incident the errors log recorded thousands of failed-write lines for 6 days with no visibility.
3. Consider surfacing sustained DB-write-failure counts from harness error logs as a health signal.

## Notes

- Recovery runbook that worked: quiesce container → `.recover` → rebuild FTS **before** re-inserting any lost_and_found rows (insert triggers write into FTS; wrong order re-corrupts) → `integrity_check` gate → swap in, clear stale `-wal`/`-shm` while stopped.
- Related app-level behavior (writing through SQLITE_CORRUPT after a claimed in-place FTS rebuild) is an upstream hermes-agent concern, tracked separately.

## What

- `extraMounts` / `extraEnv` survive compose regeneration, so hand-added mounts are no longer silently severed by an unrelated settings change.
- Carries them through the **discovered-container** projection, not just the overlay-only path — without this the fix did not reach any running agent, which is every agent it was written for.
- Duplicating an agent no longer copies the source's `extraMounts` onto the duplicate.
- Settings validation moved to the top of the handler: a bad mount path is a 400 with nothing written, instead of a 500 after the `.env` and overlay had already landed.
- Adds tilde expansion for host paths, a reserved-name denylist for `extraEnv`, and excludes stale nested `.wt-*` worktrees from vitest.

## Why

The Iris approval-gate mounts were hand-added to a *generated* compose file, so any settings change would silently sever the agent from the gate that decides what it is allowed to publish. That already happened once.

The first version of this change did not actually close it. `services.harness.get(id)` for a running agent returned `extraMounts: undefined`, because only the undiscovered path carried them — so the next VPN or resources PUT regenerated a compose without the mounts, which is the original bug. Nothing caught it: the unit test exercised the pure function, and the route test mocked the generator away.

It also opened a worse hole. `duplicateOverlay` generated the duplicate's compose without extras and then spread `{...source}`, handing the duplicate rw access to the **source's** host paths. For iris that is the approval-gate spool — a duplicate could write into the gate that decides what gets published, with no UI surfacing it.

## Verification

- 101 files, 1166 tests, green. `npx vitest run`. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Each fix was proven load-bearing by reverting just its hunk and confirming the new test goes red — including the discovered-projection fix, which fails with `expected undefined to deeply equal [ { …(4) } ]` and a regenerated compose missing the spool mount.
- The hollow tests were repaired at the source, not patched around: `settings/route.test.ts` previously replaced the whole `harness-compose` module, so deleting the two forwarding lines left the suite green. It now uses `importActual` and asserts on the options object actually reaching the generator.
- The stale-worktree claim was verified by reverting the vitest exclude: 33 failures, all inside `.wt-*` directories, none in this tree.

## Risk

**Observable behavior change:** pre-write validation is unconditional, so an agent whose persisted `extraMounts` are malformed now gets a 400 on *every* settings PUT, where before a non-regenerating PUT succeeded. Deliberate — 400-with-nothing-written beats 500-with-half-written — but reviewers should see it stated.

**No migration exists.** `extraMounts` is only ever read from the `harnesses.json` overlay. Mounts that live only in a hand-edited compose file are still dropped on the next PUT until someone writes them into the overlay. That is a deployment step, not a code gap.

## Links

Root cause context in `memory/handoffs/2026-08/06-juniper-iris-gate-intake-publish-plan.md`.

Follow-ups deliberately out of scope: no collision/dedupe rule between `extraMounts` and the generated `/opt/data` and `/state` targets; `generateAgentCompose` has no `extraMounts` parameter, so deploy-born agents cannot receive them at all.

## Why

Ahead of moving a whole community onto a Discord server whose bots are operated through HSM, we audited HSM as *the* Discord control surface. The headline result: **HSM manages 4 `DISCORD_*` variables while the deployed adapter reads ~50 — including all four that decide authorization.** None of `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES`, `DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS`, `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS` or `DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` appeared anywhere in this repo. Worse, two settings the console *does* show were reported with inverted semantics, so a wide-open agent and a locked-down one rendered identically.

> **Note on review history.** The first cut of this PR was put through an independent adversarial review, which found that its most visible change was itself a **fail-open regression** (see "What the review caught" below). That is fixed in `8045819`, along with two other blockers. Reviewers: the interesting commit is the second one.

## What changed

**Three newly-managed authorization vars.** Written *only* when the client sends the field, so an older client can't blank a value an operator hardened by hand.

| Var | Why it's load-bearing |
|---|---|
| `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` | OR'd with the user allowlist — the **only** "admin class" primitive the runtime has. There is no Discord-permission check anywhere in the adapter, so an admin class can only ever be a role. |
| `DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS` | Deny beats allow. The **only** channel restriction that binds a bot holding Administrator, since Administrator bypasses channel View overwrites. |
| `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS` | Evaluated **before** the human allowlist and skips it entirely (the adapter's own comment: *"bots aren't in it"*). A permissive value was a fourth authorization class invisible from this console. |

**Empty channel list no longer means "everywhere"** in the on_message and slash gates. Clearing the list — the obvious lockdown action — made the bot *more* permissive, contradicting `env-helpers`' own `"empty = no one allowed"` comment. We now write a sentinel no snowflake can match. (Slack got this fixed via `SLACK_CHANNEL_POLICY`; Discord has no equivalent var, so a sentinel is the only runtime-effective option without an adapter change.)

**`buildSettingsEnvValue` no longer derives `*` from `dmPolicy`.** These vars are the general user allowlist — `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` gates guild messages, slash commands and buttons, not just DMs — so a toggle the UI labels **"DM Access Policy"** granted every member of a Discord server command access to any surface with an empty user list.

**Compose regeneration is gated on an actual VPN change.** `GET` always emits `vpnEnabled` and both clients PUT the whole document back, so regeneration fired on every save, including permissions-only edits.

**New Discord agents are no longer born wide-openable** — seeded with a deny-sentinel channel scope and an explicit `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS=none`.

## What the review caught (all fixed in `8045819`)

1. **Fail-open via the GET→PUT round trip.** The first cut reported an empty/absent channel allowlist as `allowAllGroups: true`. Since both clients PUT the GET document back verbatim, that materialized a literal `*`. Empty and `*` are **not** the same runtime state: `_discord_channel_ids_allowed` returns `False` on empty but `True` on `*`, and `_is_allowed_user` uses it as the channel bypass for agents with no user/role allowlist — so the round trip would have converted a fail-closed agent into one every guild member could command. Now reported as a separate read-only `groupsUnscoped` field that PUT ignores.
2. **`DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS=*` was silently erased**, because `parseCommaList` maps `*` to `[]`. That is a guild-wide mute — the one kill switch that binds an Administrator-holding bot.
3. **Numeric-only channel validation contradicted the runtime.** `_discord_channel_keys_from_channel` builds gate keys from the snowflake, the bare name *and* `#name`. Rejecting names 400'd the **entire** save, including every other platform's settings. Validation now rejects only what would corrupt the env line. The roles rule stays numeric — that one is correctly grounded in the adapter's `.isdigit()` filter.

## Behavior changes worth reviewing

- An agent relying on `dmPolicy: allow-all` + an empty user list to mean "everyone" now writes `''` (deny) instead of `'*'`. Verified across our fleet: no agent depends on this. Fail-closed.
- An agent with a currently-empty `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` flips from "everywhere" to "nowhere" on its next save. That matches the documented intent, and none of our six agents are in that state.

## Testing

`npx vitest run` — **881 passed / 86 files**, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Adds a **round-trip suite** (GET the document, PUT it back verbatim, assert access never widens) — the class of test that would have caught blocker 1 in the first place — plus coverage for both inverted semantics, the three new vars, omission-safety, and the validation rules. Two pre-existing tests that asserted now-wrong behavior are updated with the reasoning rather than deleted.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The sentinel is known only to this route; `surface-admins.ts`, `disconnect/route.ts` and the deploy templates should share one parse/serialize pair.
- `HERMES_DM_POLICY`, `HERMES_APPROVAL_ADMIN_ONLY` and `HERMES_MEMORY_SCOPE` have **zero** runtime consumers, yet the UI still promises what they claim to do.
- No UI controls yet for the three new fields — this PR makes them correct at the API layer first.
- Settings PUT has no ETag/If-Match; concurrent saves still lose updates.

Hi! Anthropic retires Claude Sonnet 4.5 on **30 Nov 2026** ([deprecations page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations)). New harnesses still default to it, so agents created after that date would start with a model that no longer answers.

**What changed**
- `lib/services/harness.ts`: the scaffolded `config.yaml` (`primaryModel`) and `createOverlay`'s default `models` now use `claude-sonnet-4-6`, matching the primary model in `lib/seed.ts`.
- Setup wizard: the Letta suggestion and placeholder use `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`. The `anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet` suggestion was already retired on 28 Oct 2025, so it's replaced with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`.

**Why 4.6 rather than 5.5**
Sonnet 4.6 still accepts `temperature` and `top_p`, so the Hermes and Letta runtimes keep working unchanged. Sonnet 5.5 lasts longer (retirement not before Sept 2027, vs Feb 2027 for 4.6) but rejects those parameters and thinks by default ([migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide)). It's worth switching to once the runtimes are confirmed compatible.

**Not changed:** `lib/seed.ts` still lists `claude-sonnet-4-5` in `models.json`, and the tests use it as fixture data. None of them assert the default.

**Testing**
I checked that the edited files parse. I couldn't run the Vitest suite here, so CI will be the first full run.

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude) and reviewed by me.

- OpenCode 1.19.5 behind it (`lib/runtimes/opencode/`), with a pinned, sealed cell image (`cell-opencode`), the door as its only model provider, its permission rules written by the shim, and a new, empty global config folder for every process. To run any ACP agent behind the door with the same rules, receipts and sealed cell as the other harnesses, starting with OpenCode.

- `lib/runtimes/acp` + `lib/runtimes/opencode` unit tests: 44 pass (no Docker; scripted ACP agent over stdio). Key guards mutation-checked by hand: each mutation turned a named test red.

Fixes four Telegram connector gaps in HSM.

## 1. Connect-path admins: @usernames resolved, multiple admins supported

The connect route previously wrote `config.adminUser` **verbatim** into `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` — a typed `@handle` was stored raw and never matched the numeric sender IDs the gateway compares against, silently locking the admin out.

- Connect dialog admin field now accepts multiple comma-separated entries (numeric IDs and/or @usernames).
- Server-side (`surfaces/connect`): entries are split, `@handles` resolved to numeric IDs via `resolveTelegramAdmins` (strict — an unresolvable handle returns 400, surfaced inline in the dialog; nothing raw is ever stored). The bot token from the request payload is used, since `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` may not be in the agent `.env` yet at connect time.
- Display names persisted to `resolved-identities.json` (merged, same shape as the settings path).
- Settings PUT: telegram allowlists are expanded with resolved numeric IDs (`expandTelegramAllowlist`, mirroring the Signal phone→UUID expansion).

## 2. Admin-store convergence

`TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` (env bootstrap) and the `SurfaceAdminService` overlay (`harnesses.json → surfaceAdmins`, served live to the policy plugin) could diverge. Both the connect route and settings PUT now call `SurfaceAdminService.syncFromAllowlist`, which replaces the explicit overlay (when one exists) with the valid numeric identities from the freshly-written allowlist. Invalid entries (unresolved `@handles`, wildcards) are dropped by validation — never stored. With no explicit overlay, the bootstrap default already reads the env live, so no sync is needed and `setAdmins`'s bootstrap-actor semantics are preserved.

## 3. Telegram group-invite policy is no longer inert

- `GROUP_INVITE_VARS` gains `telegram: 'TELEGRAM_GROUP_INVITE_POLICY'` — the existing Group Invite Policy toggle now actually writes it (`approved-only` / `allow-all`, same values as signal/slack).
- New enforcement endpoint for the `swarm_map_policy` agent plugin (contract below).
- Middleware: the new POST path is exempted from the operator-cookie gate via `AGENT_CALLABLE_POST_PATHS` (agents cannot obtain the cookie — same rationale as the existing agent-read allowlist). Trust model documented in `middleware.ts`: the caller self-reports `addedByUserId`, so blast radius is bounded — the handler can only append one structurally-validated groupId to that surface's group allowlist, still gated by policy + admin check, and audit-logged.

## 4. Privacy-mode warning in the connect flow

The dialog's `getMe` verification now reads `can_read_all_group_messages`; when `false` a non-blocking warning explains Group Privacy is ON, the bot won't see regular group messages, how to disable it (BotFather → `/setprivacy` → Disable), and that the bot must be removed/re-added to existing groups after changing it.

Plus format hints on both the connect-dialog admin field and the settings Admins TagInput (numeric IDs or @usernames; @usernames auto-resolved).

## New plugin contract (consumed by a hermes-agent-mt follow-up)

```
POST /api/harnesses/:id/surfaces/:platform/groups/:groupId
Content-Type: application/json

{ "addedByUserId": "<platform-native user id of whoever added the bot>" }
```

Responses (200 unless the request is malformed):

| Case | Body |
|---|---|
| Approved, allowlist updated | `{ "approved": true, "restarted": <bool> }` (`restarted:false` = env written but container recreate failed, e.g. no compose file yet) |
| Approved, no-op (`*` wildcard or already listed) | `{ "approved": true, "already_allowed": true }` |
| Rejected | `{ "approved": false, "reason": "<why>" }` — plugin should leave the group |
| Malformed (unsupported platform, invalid groupId, missing `addedByUserId`, no agent `.env`) | `400 { "error": "<what>" }` |

Policy semantics: `allow-all` → approve for anyone; `approved-only` **or unset (secure default)** → approve only when `addedByUserId` is an admin (`SurfaceAdminService.isAdmin`, fail-closed). No auth cookie required on this one path (see `AGENT_CALLABLE_POST_PATHS`).

## Test results

- `vitest run`: **85 files, 829 tests passed** (43 new: resolver strict/best-effort matrices, connect-route resolution + multi-admin normalization + 400-on-unresolvable, store convergence, `approveGroupInvite` policy × admin matrix, POST route responses, middleware gate exemptions, privacy-mode flag).
- `eslint .`: identical to baseline (72 pre-existing errors, none introduced).
- `next build`: passes.

## Noted but deliberately not fixed

- `addedByUserId` on the new POST is self-reported by the agent — the server cannot verify who performed the platform-side invite. Documented in `middleware.ts`; consistent with the trust already extended to the plugin's is_admin/is_group_allowed reads.
- The same connect-path verbatim-adminUser behavior still exists for mattermost/discord/slack (out of scope).
- Settings PUT keeps raw `@handles` in the env alongside the appended numeric IDs (display parity with the settings GET merge; harmless — they just never match).
