## Two asks in one

### 1. Add \"Discover existing channels\" for Discord (parity with Signal/Mattermost)

**The pain:** today, wiring an agent into a Discord channel means manually hunting down the channel snowflake ID (enable Discord developer mode → right-click channel → Copy Channel ID → paste into `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS`). For anyone administering more than a couple of channels this is tedious and error-prone.

**The pattern that already exists:** Signal and Mattermost surfaces have a **\"Discover existing groups →\"** button on the harness page (`app/(dashboard)/harnesses/[id]/page.tsx`). It calls `app/api/surfaces/signal/groups/route.ts` (and the Mattermost equivalent), lists the groups the bot account is already a member of, and lets the operator pick which to allowlist — no manual ID copying.

**Requested:** same feature for Discord.

- New route `app/api/surfaces/discord/channels/route.ts` that lists channels across the guilds the bot is a member of (Discord REST: `GET /users/@me/guilds` → per-guild `GET /guilds/{id}/channels`)
- \"Discover existing channels →\" button on the Discord surface card, mirroring the Signal UX
- Multi-select UI filtered to text channels the bot can actually see (skip categories, voice, threads the bot can't read)
- Writes selected snowflakes into `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` the same way the Signal flow writes group UUIDs
- Should respect the existing Discord permission model (see below) — e.g. if `DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS` is set, those channels should be marked/excluded in the picker

ROADMAP already marks this shipped for Signal + Mattermost (`docs/ROADMAP.md`: \"Discover existing groups (Signal, Mattermost)\"). Discord is the gap.

### 2. Review the default Discord permission system

Discord has the richest admission surface of any platform in `lib/surfaces/registry.ts`:

- `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` — user snowflake allowlist
- `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` — channel allowlist
- `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` — role allowlist (OR'd with the user allowlist)
- `DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS` — deny list (deny beats allow)
- `DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION` — only respond when @mentioned
- `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS` — respond to other bots
- `DISCORD_CHANNEL_SCOPED_ACCESS` — per-channel access control

Worth a design review pass on:

- **Are the defaults sensible for a fresh agent?** (Currently: closed by default — every list empty = deny all. That's safe but means Discord is the hardest surface to bring up, compounded by the missing discovery feature above.)
- **Is the allow/deny precedence documented clearly enough?** (`docs/surface-permissions.md` covers the resolver contract, but operator-facing docs for the Discord-specific OR-of-roles + deny-beats-allow semantics could be clearer)
- **Does the UI surface the permission model accurately?** (i.e. does the harness page make it obvious which knobs are Discord-only vs shared across surfaces)
- **Role-based admission UX** — `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` is powerful (\"anyone with the Moderator role can talk to the bot\") but role IDs are even more painful to find than channel IDs. If we add channel discovery, consider role discovery too (`GET /guilds/{id}/roles`).

## Why together

The permission review and the discovery feature interact: any change to the default permission posture (e.g. making Discord default-open within a guild) changes what the discovery UI should suggest. Filing as one issue so they're designed coherently; can be split if implementation prefers.

## References

- Existing Signal discovery: `app/api/surfaces/signal/groups/route.ts`, harness page button
- Discord surface spec: `lib/surfaces/registry.ts` (`discord` entry)
- Permission resolver contract: `docs/surface-permissions.md`
- Roadmap: `docs/ROADMAP.md` (\"Discover existing groups (Signal, Mattermost)\" — Discord not listed)

## What
- `lib/model-versions.ts`: model-id normaliser (family / version / snapshot / unstable), `findSuccessor` (strictly same family, strictly newer version or snapshot), `priceRatio`.
- `lib/services/model-freshness.ts`: live model lists for openrouter / anthropic / zai with a 1h disk cache under `DATA_DIR/model-lists/`, fail-soft (no key, network error, bad body → `null`, entries stay unflagged). Keys resolved through KeysService per request, never persisted or logged. `GET /api/models/live?provider=`.
- Per-harness `modelTracking` overlay (`"provider/model" → true`, carried through both harness projections) and `settings.modelAutoUpdate { enabled, mode: notify|apply, intervalHours, maxPriceMultiplier }`. Routes: `GET/PUT /api/settings/model-auto-update`, `PUT /api/harnesses/[id]/models/tracking` (ollama refused).
- `lib/services/model-update-scheduler.ts`, registered from `instrumentation.ts` (unref'd timers, HMR guard, `MODEL_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS` override). `GET /api/fleet/model-updates` (last persisted report), `POST .../check` (run now), `POST .../apply` (manual one-click apply of a reported successor).
- Catalog: `retired` / `deprecates` fields; `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` flagged retired (OpenRouter expiration 2026-09-28), `google/gemini-2.5-flash` deprecates 2026-10-20. Rows are flagged, never removed, so live cascades stay readable.
- Reconciled onto the cascade-library stack: this branch's own `lib/services/cascade-write.ts` (`writeCascade`) and its tests are gone. The scheduler's auto-apply and `POST /api/fleet/model-updates/apply` call `applyCascadeToHarness` from `lib/services/cascade-writer.ts`, the stack's single validated write path. `PUT /api/harnesses/[id]/models` is exactly as the parent has it. The byte-for-byte splice pin and created-file pin from the dropped test file are ported into `cascade-writer.test.ts`.

## Why
Closes #136. Providers retire ids on a schedule and ship newer same-family versions; today nobody notices until an agent 404s. This makes freshness visible fleet-wide and, per cascade entry, lets an operator opt in to following the newest same-family version.

Policy, in one place:
- **Default OFF.** `modelAutoUpdate.enabled` is `false`; with it off the scheduler does no background network at all (manual `POST .../check` still works).
- **notify mode** reports successors, retirements and price ratios at `GET /api/fleet/model-updates`. Nothing is written.
- **apply mode** auto-bumps only *tracked* entries to a strictly-same-family newer **version** that is present in the live provider list, within the price ceiling (`maxPriceMultiplier`; no published pricing → `price-unknown` → never auto-applied), through the validated writer (`applyCascadeToHarness`: validate → render → splice → write → overlay), followed by a `quick` restart and a `cascade:auto-update` audit row `{ harness, from, to, provider, priceRatio }`. The `modelTracking` key rotates to the new id.
- **ollama / bedrock / custom never auto-apply.** Unstable (preview/beta/exp) successors never apply. A harness with a restart already in flight is skipped.
- **Snapshot-only bumps are notify-only** (a human may apply one via `POST .../apply`).
- A writer refusal (provider with no credential in the agent's `.env`, unsafe YAML scalar) writes nothing, restarts nothing, leaves tracking untouched, and audits `cascade:auto-update:blocked` with the reason.

## Verification
- `pnpm vitest run` → 119 files, 1441 tests, all green (on head `effc6be`).
- `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v '^\.next/'` → clean.
- `lib/services/__tests__/model-update-scheduler.test.ts` (22 tests; `cascade-writer.test.ts` 14) runs the **real** `applyCascadeToHarness` against a tmpdir fleet with real `.env` files, so validate-before-write is exercised on the scheduler path, not mocked away. Every guard (untracked, snapshot, unstable, price ceiling, price-unknown, ollama, restart-in-flight, writer refusal, policy off) has a test asserting nothing was written and nothing was restarted.
- Rebased onto `dev/juniperbevensee/cascade-library`; the `writeCascade` extraction commit was dropped and its consumers rewritten in the same history so each commit builds.

## Risk
The scheduler rewrites a running agent's `config.yaml` with no human in the loop — but only when the operator has flipped `enabled` and chosen `apply`, only for entries they tracked, and only through the same writer the editor uses. Worst case on a bad write is the existing crash-loop, which the validator exists to prevent; the byte-identical splice pin guards against a refactor changing what lands on disk.

Stacked on #233 — merge that first (use a merge commit, not squash, so the stack stays clean).

## What
- Model the cascade the way hermes-agent consumes it: **primary = `model:` section, fallbacks = `fallback_providers` rows**. New `readCascade()` / `cascadeChain()` in `lib/services/harness.ts`; the writer, scheduler, API routes, cascade library and editor all work on that chain.
- Remove the PR #243 `primary-mismatch` 409 and its banner, plus `allowPrimaryChange`: with chain semantics the "mismatch" cannot occur.
- Preserve each file's convention on write: a file that repeats its primary as `fallback_providers[0]` (HSM-saved: cryptids/nimbleco/osint, blackhouse) keeps that duplicate row, in sync with `model.default` across rotations; a file that does not (cyborg, matilde, iris) never gains one. `model.fallback` (unread by the runtime) is rewritten only where it already exists.
- Primary rows are now trackable: the scheduler/report list the primary first with `role: 'primary'`, rotation of the primary rewrites `model.default` (and the duplicate row when present), and `PUT /models/tracking` validates against the chain. A file with rows but **no primary** reports every entry as a fallback and a rotation on it is refused (`blocked: no-primary-in-file`, manual apply 409) instead of inventing a `model.default`.
- API: `GET /models` adds `chain`, `primaryEntry`, `primaryDuplicatedAsRow0` (old fields kept); `PUT` accepts `{ chain, expected_chain }` and `{ cascade }`. The pre-chain `{ fallback_providers }` body is now **fallback-only**: it rewrites the rows and never touches the primary (GET → PUT of the raw `fallbackProviders` is a byte-identical no-op on all five fleet shapes; on a duplicate-row-0 file the primary's row stays the writer's; a file with no primary gets 409 pointing at `{ chain }`). Cascade library records store `chain` (`entries` migrated on read, accepted as an input alias).
- The primary is read the way hermes loads it (`cli.py:487-498`): `model.default`, else `model.model`, else a scalar `model: <id>`. The writer keeps whichever form the file uses (no `default:` added beside `model.model`; the scalar form stays scalar until the primary needs a provider/base_url). README / AGENTS.md updated.

## Why
PR #243 assumed `fallback_providers[0]` is the primary. On the real fleet both conventions coexist: cyborg's primary (`z-ai/glm-5.3`) is only in `model:` and its rows start with `claude-sonnet-4-6`, so the editor showed "the primary is not the first row… Saving is refused" for a perfectly valid file. Verified against the runtime (`hermes-agent-mt`): the primary is `model.default` (`cli.py:528-539`, `gateway/run.py:2571`), the chain is `fallback_providers` in order (`hermes_cli/fallback_config.py:71-97`, `agent/agent_init.py:1187-1199`), and `try_activate_fallback` walks it one row per failure, skipping a row equal to the current (provider, model) (`agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1453-1490`), so a duplicate row 0 is harmless and `model.fallback` is never read. The review round on this PR found the old `{ fallback_providers }` body still took row 0 as the primary (so a raw-rows round trip demoted the primary on 3 of 5 agents), the reader missed hermes' scalar / `model.model` forms, and a no-primary file got a rotated fallback written as a brand-new primary; all three are fixed here with a failing test first.

## Verification
- `pnpm vitest run` → 131 files, 1718 tests passed (was 129 / 1620 on main; 130 / 1665 before review round 1; 131 / 1690 before review round 2). New coverage: `lib/services/__tests__/read-cascade.test.ts` (15), chain-semantics + new-format blocks in `cascade-writer.test.ts` (+16, incl. a byte-identical no-op save over each of the five real fleet shapes in `__tests__/fleet-shapes.ts` and over the scalar / `model.model` forms), `model-update-scheduler.test.ts` (+10, incl. the no-primary file), and a new `app/api/harnesses/[id]/models/route.fleet-shapes.test.ts` (11: the route over the real fixtures on disk with the real readers — GET → PUT round trip is a no-op on every shape, reorder keeps the primary, no-primary → 409). Route/library/UI tests updated rather than deleted.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- `npx eslint` on every touched file → 0 errors; 5 warnings in `page.tsx` are pre-existing on `main` (unused imports), untouched.
- Not run against a live agent (no SSH/browser in this task).

## Risk
- Cascade library records change shape on disk (`entries` → `chain`) on the next write; readers of `GET /api/cascades` that expected `entries` must read `chain` (input still accepts `entries`).
- `{ fallback_providers }` can no longer change the primary (it never should have been able to without saying so). A caller that relied on "row 0 becomes the primary" must send `{ chain }`; on a duplicate-row-0 file a body that omits the primary's row still gets it back at row 0.
- A file with rows but no primary is now refused by the scheduler and by `{ fallback_providers }` rather than gaining a `model.default`. None of the five fleet agents is in that state.
- Pre-chain reports persisted in `model-updates.json` lack `role`; the type marks it optional.

## Review round 2
Fixed (each with a failing test first; the two MAJORs are reproduced on the real fixtures in `route.fleet-shapes.test.ts`):
- **MAJOR 1 — silent promotion on a no-primary file.** `PUT { chain }` on a file with rows but no `model.default` is refused with 409 `no-primary-in-file: …` unless the body carries `set_primary: true` — the same refusal the scheduler / manual apply already make. The editor shows row 1 with a "no primary on disk — save will make this the primary" note instead of the PRIMARY badge when `primaryEntry` is null, and sends `set_primary: true` only from that state. A fresh file with no rows at all still takes a `{ chain }` without the flag (nothing to promote).

## What

- The model route now writes a receipt for every call it does not complete, and says why: refused before forwarding (`model.route`: no price, not a model call, not readable, wrong stand-in key), refused by the budget (`budget.cap`), or failed at the provider (`model.provider`: an error status, no answer in time, a cut-off reply, or a 200 stream or body that carries an error). It passes each one to the door through a new `onFailure` hook. The provider's own words are never written down.
- When a turn ends with nothing to post, the door now posts one short line in the room, under the message that started the turn: `No answer this time.` plus the reason when a model call failed during the turn, or else "finished without a reply", "something went wrong inside the agent", or "took too long, so the door stopped waiting for it" (no harness acts on a cancel). The line goes through the same outbound re-check, redaction and receipts as a reply. A message deleted mid-turn still gets nothing, and a turn a bot started gets only a receipt (`turn.to-bot`), so a failure cannot feed a bot loop. A refusal by the rules for any reason but the budget is told in one fixed sentence.
- New checks C6m, C6b and C6s (`conformance/suites/failure-checks.ts`), run for Pi with a tool in ask mode: the provider refuses the model call after a tool ran, the budget refuses it, and a model call outlasts the turn. Each needs a receipt with the reason and the right line in the room. They are red with a new broken shim link, `covers-failures`, which reports a failed turn as one that answered "All done." (C6m, C6b), and in a cell with the gate that asks nobody (C6m).
- Metering is unchanged: a call that cannot be metered is still never forwarded, and a forwarded call is charged by its reported usage, or by size when there is none. With tools on, the launcher now allows a turn ten minutes (the route's wait for one call) instead of three, since a tool turn makes at least two calls.

## Why

With tools on, a turn makes more model calls, and a slow model can take minutes for one. From the room, an agent waiting on a slow call, an agent whose call failed, and an agent whose turn ended with nothing to say all looked the same: silence. A provider error wrote no receipt, a turn that ended with no reply or with an error posted nothing, and a turn that ran past its deadline was dropped without a word. This change gives each of those a reason in the receipts and a line in the room.

A replay of OpenRouter's stream shape for a tool call (keep-alive comments, reasoning deltas, the tool call in pieces, a finish event, and a usage event that repeats the finish with one empty choice) is metered exactly from its usage figure, before and after this change. That replay is now a test.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run`: the full suite passes. On this machine, under heavy load from other work, each full run had a few timing failures in files this change does not touch (a token-broker script, worker start-up), and a different set each time. Each failed file passed when run again on its own. 13 new model-route tests, including the OpenRouter replay, and 6 new door tests. Four existing door tests that pinned the old silence (no reply, the deadline, a reply after settled, and the deadline after an approval) now expect the line in the room. The live-run rig's tests now tell a reply apart from the door's line.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. ESLint on the changed files: no errors.
- Real Pi 1.5.2 as a process (`npm run conformance`): 42 of 42, including C6m, C6b and C6s. `covers-failures` turned C6m and C6b red and left C1, C6 and C6s green. Matrix regenerated.
- Real Pi 1.5.2 in the sealed Docker cell (`npm run conformance:docker`, `pi.docker.test.ts`): 50 of 50. The gate that asks nobody turned C6m red. Docker matrix regenerated.
- Launcher Docker suite (`pi-discord.docker.test.ts`) with a fake Discord: 20 of 20, including a new end-to-end test where the provider refuses a call and the channel gets the line. With the `onFailure` wiring removed from the launcher, that test went red.
- Hand mutations: 11 lines broken one at a time in the route, the shapes and the door. Each turned a named test red once a test for a finish reason of `error` with no error object was added.
- Independent audit, on the code as it now stands: real Pi 1.5.2 42 of 42, Letta Code 0.34.60 26 of 26, Claude Agent SDK 0.3.325 36 of 36 as processes; in Docker, Pi 50 of 50, Pi launcher 20 of 20, Letta Code 34 of 34, Letta Code launcher 15 of 15, Claude Agent SDK 38 of 38. The first real Agent SDK run found that C4m no longer failed for three broken shims, because the door's line filled in for the missing reply; post counts now leave that line out. Provider error bodies holding key-, account-, URL- and path-shaped strings, across nine statuses and four body types, put none of it in a receipt or a room line. Ten hand mutations to the door, route, shapes and launcher each turned a test red.
- Sanitization gate (deterministic layer) on the diff: clean.

## Risk

- A room now sees a line where it used to see silence, on every failed turn, including when the budget is spent. A turn a bot started is never told, so a failure cannot keep a bot loop going.
- Which turn gets blamed for a failed call is decided by time alone. With two turns running at once, either may be the one that is told. The receipts name the call that failed.

- Adds a Letta Code adapter to the lab: `lib/runtimes/letta-code/` drives Letta Code 0.34.60 through the door with the same four verbs as Pi (start, send, read, veto). It is the second harness to pass the harness-neutral checks.

- Records the result for the pinned version in two matrix files, made from real runs.
- Adds `docs/lab/letta-code.md`: what is proven, what is not.

Nothing is wired into the Swarm Map app or UI, and nothing here starts or touches a running agent. This is not the old Letta integration brought back: that one stays removed, and its guard test still passes.

## Result, for Letta Code 0.34.60

| Run | Checks passed |
|---|---|
| Plain process on a laptop | 16 of 16 |
| Sealed Docker cell (Docker Desktop for Mac) | 22 of 22 |

Scripted room, scripted model, placeholder keys, loopback only. No account, no real key, no real chat. Started the way the shim starts it, Letta Code made no call off the machine.

Not met, and said so in the matrix and the doc:

- **Memory per room.** Letta Code keeps one memory per agent and reads it into every conversation. So the door gives it one room (or one person's direct messages) and refuses a policy that opens more: new rule `mem.one-scope`, with tests. Check C11n shows the rule with real Letta Code in the loop; a shim that hides the memory from the door is given the second room and the note crosses.
- **Direct messages**, for the same reason as Pi: its sessions share one folder on disk.
- C6, C7, C13, C14, C17 and the wider C11 are not run. The doc says why for each.

## Changes to the shared contracts

Each was a place where the contract had been written around Pi.

1. The model route answers "which models are there?" itself, from its price list. Letta Code asks before its first call. Nothing is forwarded and the real key is not used.
2. A policy has to fit the harness: `fitProblems`, rule `mem.one-scope`, enforced in the door from the `nativeMemory` a shim declares. It is listed as a guardrail, because that declaration comes from the cell.
3. A harness adapter can patch the lab's starting policy (the fixture opens several rooms).
4. The Docker rig takes the cell's harness as a part (`CellKind`): the name of its image, its entry, and how to ask it for its version. A suite says which harness its cells hold with `setCell()`. Pi stays the default, and its Docker suite was run again on this branch.

Pi's process matrix was regenerated from a real Pi run, because the catalogue has one more rule. Pi still passes 14 of 14.

## Why

The lab's claim is that a rule has one implementation and the harness is not part of it. One harness cannot show that. - `npm run conformance:docker -- letta-code`: 22 of 22 with real Letta Code in the cell, and all ten broken rigs caught. The images are named for the source they were built from, and the run compares their files with this branch before it starts.
- `npm run conformance:docker -- pi.docker`: Pi's Docker suite still passes with the rig generalized.
- `SWARMLAB_PI_BIN=... npm run conformance -- pi.real`: 14 of 14 after the contract changes.
- Forty hand mutations of the new code. Two survived at first and now have tests; one of them was a real gap in the shim, now closed. See the doc, "What this does not show", item 11.

## Second audit (independent pass)

Everything was built and run again on this tree, from images named for it: Letta Code 16 of 16 as a process and 22 of 22 in the cell, Pi 14 of 14 and 20 of 20, nine broken shims and ten broken rigs caught for Letta Code, eight and ten for Pi. Found and fixed, each test-first:

- **A moved room carried the memory with it.** Two policies that each open one room both fitted, so a one-memory harness could learn in one room and then be given another. A room under the listed room that is not a thread was a second conversation too. The door now gives such a harness the first conversation only, for as long as the door runs. C11n moves the room and expects the refusal.
- **A harness's patch to the lab's starting policy could loosen it.** It may now only take rooms away, and a lab refuses to start otherwise.
- **Two guard changes could be widened with every test green** (the whole npm scope, every lock file). Both are pinned.

Twenty-five more hand mutations: twenty-three red at once, the two guard ones above now red. A packet capture in the sealed cell saw Letta Code look up only the door and connect out only to the door's model route. The doc has the detail, and what is still not shown.

## Risk

- Lab only. No app code path imports any of this.
- The Docker result is for one machine and one Docker version.
- Letta Code ships several times a day. The shim sends no turn to any version but the pinned one.

- A Discord connector for the lab's door (`lib/door/connectors/discord.ts`), behind the same interface as the fake connector. No new dependency: it uses Node 24's own WebSocket and fetch, so no third-party package holds a bot token.
- A launcher for one Pi agent in one Discord channel (`lib/lab/pi-discord/`): config, dry run, start, stop, status, receipts. The door runs on the machine; Pi runs in the sealed cell and reaches the door through a relay that holds nothing.
- `bots.loop` is now a real rule: the door counts bot messages delivered in a row and `decide()` stops at the limit. Two more door rules: a reply size cut (`out.size`) and "a message is read once" for edits and deletes (`in.once`).
- A runbook: `docs/lab/pi-discord.md`.
- `allowedBotIds`: name the only bots that are heard. A policy can name its bots (`bots.ids`), and `decide()` drops any bot that is not named. Every other bot and every webhook is dropped with a receipt. Each named bot has its own loop count.
- A `persona` setting (a name and one line). The launcher tells the agent what it is and, in its own fixed words, what it cannot do: no tools, text only, one channel. It replaces Pi's own introduction, which says it is a coding assistant that can run commands.

Nothing here is wired into the Swarm Map app or any running agent. This PR does not start anything.

The Pi slice proved the rules with a scripted room. The next step is one real surface, with every inbound message still going through `decide()` and every reply through the door's redaction and size limit.

## How it holds the rules

- Every gateway message becomes a door event. The connector decides nothing.
- The reply can only go to the room the message came from. The connector also refuses any post outside the one channel it was started for, before a request is made.
- Replies ping nobody (`allowed_mentions` is empty).

- **Mutation checks**, by hand: 62 changes to the new code, one at a time, each run against the unit tests. 59 turned a test red at once. Two did not and each now has a test. One is not a difference a test can see: the tabs component already opens on its first tab when it is asked for one that does not exist. Six more were run against the Letta Code launcher suite, with the images rebuilt for each: dropping the system prompt at the shim and at the cell, ignoring the model name, and giving Letta Code Pi's cell each turned it red; with the restart taken out the suite ran seven minutes without a first reply and was stopped by hand; taking out the short wait before the cell is started again did not turn it red, so that wait is not held by a test.
- **Hermes agents**: the stored snapshots of the fleet table and the Hermes agent page still match, unedited.

Measured for Letta Code, with a scripted model: the cell image is 2.43 GB (Pi's is 737 MB). The first reply came 2.7 s after the mention (Pi: 1.0 s), since the first turn also makes its agent; later turns took 0.1 to 0.2 s for both. The dry run's containment checks took 5.8 s (Pi: 4.3 s). The launcher suite takes about 45 s.

## Risk

- **An agent already running from the launcher.** The command, the config keys and the state folder are unchanged, and a config without `harness` is read as Pi. Two things differ for it: the dry run prints four more lines (the harness, its pinned version, its limits), and the images must be built again after pulling, as after any pull, because the cell's code changed.
- **Start-up order.** `start` now starts the cell again, once, if it has not reached the door three seconds after the door is up, and checks it from outside again. A start that used to depend on timing no longer does. A slow machine may see one extra restart of the cell, and a log line that says so.
- **What Letta Code is told.** Letta Code adds its own starting notes after the launcher's text, and one calls it a coding assistant. They cannot be left out; the launcher's text says what they are. Whether a real model keeps to that is not tested.
- **"A supervisor"** is read from the door's parent process and only pm2 is recognised. A door under another supervisor is shown as "not this page".
- No test presses Start on a Letta Code agent in the dashboard against Docker: the dashboard half is tested with a stubbed launcher, the launcher half with real containers.
- Not done here: changing an agent's harness or name after it is made; Hermes pages still use browser prompts for import, duplicate and remove.

## What
- The cascade writer re-emits the blank lines and column-0 comments that trail `model:` / `fallback_providers:` (the template's `# --- Context compression` banner), and a comment under a managed key rides with that key. A no-op write over `generateDefaultConfig()` is byte-identical.
- Output ends in exactly one newline; an appended block is separated by one blank line; a CRLF file stays CRLF on every emitted line.
- Flow-form headers (`fallback_providers: []`, `model: {…}`) are recognised by `readModelConfig` / `readModelProvider` / `readFallbackProviders` and the writer, and replaced in place, never duplicated.
- More than one top-level `model:` or `fallback_providers:` header → 409 `duplicate-sections`, nothing written; the scheduler reports the entry blocked with reason `duplicate-sections`.
- Scalars drop a trailing ` # comment` (a glued `#` stays); the primary-mismatch guard only compares when a `default:` key is actually present.
- `components/fleet` toggle row relabelled "Automatic updates" so the card no longer says "Model updates" twice.

## Why
The writer splices a running agent's config.yaml by line with no human in the loop. Every write was deleting the operator's section banners and blank lines, could double up trailing blank lines, silently picked one of two duplicate sections, appended a second block under a flow-form header, and compared `default: x  # note` (comment included) against row 0. Each of those either corrupts a hand-edited file a little more per scheduler tick or refuses a valid write for the wrong reason.

## Verification
- Red-green: 21 new tests written first, all failing on the parent branch's writer, then made green.
  - `lib/services/__tests__/cascade-writer.test.ts` (+15): byte-identical no-op over the anthropic and ollama templates, template + real write diff limited to the two sections, banner/blank re-emission across two writes, blank line inside a section, trailing-newline ×3 inputs, single-blank append, CRLF end-to-end, `fallback_providers: []` and `[{…}]` in place, duplicate `model:` / duplicate `fallback_providers:` → 409, indented `model:` not a header, trailing comments on values, no-`default:` guard.
  - `lib/services/__tests__/model-config.test.ts` (+4): reader comment stripping, flow `model: {…}`, flow `fallback_providers: []` / `[{…}]`.
  - `lib/services/__tests__/model-update-scheduler.test.ts` (+2): scheduler blocked `duplicate-sections` with audit row and nothing written; manual apply 409.
  - `components/fleet/model-updates-card.test.tsx`: heading appears once, switch named "Automatic updates".
- One pinned expectation updated on purpose: the byte-for-byte splice test now keeps the blank line between a section and the next key (that consumption was the bug). The models route test's harness mock now passes through the new shared helpers.
- `pnpm vitest run` → 129 files, 1598 tests passed (was 1577 on the parent).
- `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v '^\.next/'` → clean.
- `npx eslint` on the nine touched files → clean.

## Risk
- Behaviour change for every caller of the writer: blank lines / column-0 comments after the two sections are now kept instead of deleted, and files with two `model:` or `fallback_providers:` headers are refused (409) instead of half-rewritten. Anyone with such a file sees the error text naming the line numbers and has to dedupe by hand.
- `FALLBACK_PROVIDERS_HEADER` is now `/^fallback_providers:(\s|$)/` (any value form) rather than bare-or-comment only; a top-level scalar `fallback_providers: foo` now counts as the section and is replaced in place rather than left beside an appended duplicate.

## What

- Adds `lib/core/`: one policy record, a 35-rule catalogue, and `decide()`, the single function that says who an agent may hear and answer, which tools it may run, and when its budget is spent.
- Adds `lib/door/`: the sidecar that owns chat in, chat out and model traffic. Fake connector only. Receipts for every decision, outbound redaction that fails closed, one reply per turn, a model route that swaps a placeholder for the real key, meters tokens and keeps spend in a ledger by month.
- Adds `lib/runtimes/pi/`: the Pi shim (one `pi --mode rpc` process per session), a prompt preamble a sender cannot forge, and a tool gate extension that blocks on anything but an explicit allow.
- Adds `conformance/`: 38 scenario pairs, fake-proof guards with negative controls, a scripted model, a fake Pi for CI, fourteen shim checks, eight deliberately broken shims, and a matrix file generated from a real Pi 1.5.2 run.
- Adds `conformance/docker/`: a sealed Docker cell for Pi and the rig around it (the sidecar's side, a sink that stands in for the internet, a control that proves the sink can be hit), a probe that tries each way out, a runner that starts one rig per check and removes only what it made, and a second matrix file generated from that run.
- Adds the spec, the plan and a report under `docs/lab/`.

Nothing is wired into the app, the UI, the Hermes path or any running agent. No dependency was added.

## Why

Every harness enforces chat rules differently, so each new harness has meant re-rendering the same rules and hoping they hold. This slice tries the other shape on Pi: rules are decided once, outside the harness, and the per-harness code shrinks to "start it, send text, read text, veto a tool".

## Verification

- `npx vitest run`, after merging main (which now has #337): 211 files, 4149 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Sanitization gate, deterministic layer, on the PR diff: clean. The semantic layer runs in CI only.
- `SWARMLAB_PI_BIN=... npm run conformance` against a real Pi 1.5.2 install: 23 of 23. All fourteen checks pass, and each of the eight broken shims turned its named checks red. `conformance/matrix/pi-1.5.2.process.json` was written by that run, and a CI test now fails if that file no longer matches the suite.
- `npm run conformance:docker` with real Pi 1.5.2 in a sealed cell, on Docker Desktop 4.76 for Mac (engine 29.5.2): 29 of 29. S0-S3, C8, C9 and C10 pass, and so do the thirteen process-level checks run again in the cell. Ten rigs broken on purpose (a route to the sink, an ordinary network, the key in the cell's environment, the key in a file, a writable cell, a host folder mounted, a file where a Docker socket would be, a door with a route out, a sink nobody can prove works, C10 with the gate left in) each turned its named checks red for the reason it names. A rig handed a real-looking key is refused before Docker is asked for anything, and again by the cell itself. `conformance/matrix/pi-1.5.2.docker.json` was written by that run, and a CI test fails if it no longer matches the suite.
- The Docker checks were then broken by hand twice (the sink's log ignored; the probe's answers ignored) and the must-fail tests went red both times.
- An audit of the Docker cell then tried, by hand in a live cell, ways out the probe does not: every TCP port on Docker's side of the cell network, a port another lab container published, DNS watched with a packet capture (with a control that was seen leaving), IPv6 without the cell's own setting, and the model route and the door's port poked from inside. Nothing got out and no key came back. It found the run went red on a network that answers no IPv6 DNS question (fixed), three checks with no broken rig (added), and that S1-S3 did not read what Docker actually gave the container (they now do; a cell given a shared process namespace, a published port and loosened seccomp turned S1 and S2 red when tried). These by-hand trials are not standing checks; the report says which.
- Not run: C13 (no tool verdict depends on who asked yet, so it could not fail for the reason it names), C7, C12b. The Docker run is not in CI.
- Mutation checks, run by hand and not committed: listed in `docs/lab/pi-slice.md`, "What this does not show", item 11.
- Not verified: the Docker run on any other machine, Docker version or engine, or on Linux.

## Risk

- **The wall is shown on one machine, for the ways out that were tried.** With Pi in the lab's Docker cell, a tool it ran reached nothing but the door and read no secret, also with the tool gate removed. That is Docker Desktop for Mac, one version, and a list of probes, not a proof: a way out that is not on the list was not tried. `docs/lab/pi-slice.md` lists the limits (DNS judged by its answer, no IPv6 control, wall-check lines with no broken cell behind them, the cell token readable inside the cell, no limits tested, and more). Do not read this PR as "Pi is safe to deploy".
- **These are lab images and a lab rig.** Nothing in Swarm Map starts a cell like this, and no running agent is in one. In the rig the door has no route out either; a door that talks to a real model and a real chat platform needs one, and that side is not tested.
- **The Docker run needs an internet connection for its controls.** A one-off container asks DNS for three names before a run (and, if this machine's resolver answers no IPv6 question, asks a public resolver itself), and one cell that is broken on purpose is put on an ordinary network and opens one connection from there. No public address is written in the repo.
- **At process level, "nothing left this machine" is shown for Pi's own Node runtime only.** The tripwire there does not see a program Pi starts that is not Node. The Docker cell is what covers that.
- **The key swap and the budget cap exist for one wire format** (OpenAI chat-completions). A harness that speaks another has neither; the route refuses its calls.
- **Pi is given no direct messages**, because its sessions share one folder on disk.
- **The bot loop limit is not enforced.** With bots allowed, two bots can answer each other without end.
- **The credential preflight is a list of names and shapes.** A credential it has not been taught goes through; Pi's environment is listed by hand for that reason.
- **Several check lines have no broken shim behind them** (C2, C4a, C12, C15 and parts of C1, C5v, C8p). The report lists them.
- A scripted model tests plumbing only.
- The fake Pi was wrong once already (real Pi never asks the gate about an undeclared tool). The real-Pi run caught it. The fake can drift again when Pi changes; the pin is 1.5.2.

_Requested by **Miles**_

Before: Swarm Map had no way to keep a tool's output out of an agent's model context, so outputs licensed under terms like the Kaitiakitanga License (Papa Reo's te reo Māori transcripts, which may not go to services that collect or use them) couldn't be handled safely, and there was no Papa Reo transcription for agents.

After: an agent's Settings tab has two new cards.
- **Protected Outputs (oven-mitt)** adds an [ovenmitt](https://github.com/utunga/oven-mitt) vault daemon as a sidecar (no network, read-only, no capabilities). Operators add vaults; per vault they tick which chats may receive its files (editable match, e.g. `signal/*` or one chat) and optionally a host folder to export to. The agent holds outputs by handle and can send them to the chat it's talking to, but can't read them.
- **Transcription (Papa Reo escalation)** installs the papareo-transcribe pack, adds a `papareo` vault, turns voice input off and raises memory for whisper. The agent asks the person "local or Papa Reo?" first; Papa Reo transcripts go through the vault. A "Kaitiakitanga-compliant" declaration checks the agent's model hosts and requires a typed `I CONFIRM` for anything remote before letting the agent read Papa Reo text.

How:
- `lib/services/ovenmitt*.ts`, `protected-outputs.ts`: daemon config rendering (validated vault/destination/match/folder input only), surgical compose edits for both compose lineages, consumer credential kept encrypted in its own 0600 file (never on the harness record or any API), 6-hourly audit-chain check.

- `transcription.ts`, `model-hosting.ts`: the Transcription card's service, the SOUL.md marked block and env flag for the compliance declaration, and a config.yaml reader that classifies model/fallback/auxiliary hosts as local or remote.
- Packs installed from pinned git tags now record their source (`.swarm-map-source`), cards show installed tag vs pin, and switching a card off/on updates a stale plugin.

Follows #331.

## What

- `lib/harness-ref.ts` is the one step every route that takes an agent id goes through: `invalidHarnessId()` checks the shape (400), `requireHarness()` also resolves the id to the agent listed under exactly that id (404), and `refuseUnknownHarnesses()` does the same for a list of ids from a request body.
- Every handler under `/api/harnesses/[id]` calls it first: the shape check on reads, the full resolve on anything that changes something. `/api/keys` POST and PUT, cascade apply and model-update apply resolve the ids in their bodies the same way; the Signal PIN routes check the shape. `KeysService` checks the shape of every agent reference it is given. Pairing DELETE accepts only a known platform name.
- Import and deploy check the new agent's name against the stored agents before they write anything (`HarnessService.nameTaken`), and answer 409.
- `app/api/harness-id-sweep.test.ts` walks every API route file. Each must be classified (id in the URL, id in the body, new-agent name, or no agent id), and each that takes an id must refuse a malformed or unknown one before any service call or file write. A new route fails the sweep until it is classified. The sweep also reads each handler's source for the body and query fields it takes; each must be declared as an agent id (and is then swept) or as something else.

## Why

Routes handled agent ids in different ways: some looked the agent up, some turned the id straight into a data dir, and routes taking ids in a body did neither. One strict step, applied everywhere and enforced by a test, keeps every route working from the same resolved agent and refusing ids that name none.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run`: 175 files, 3182 passed, 1 skipped. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. No new `eslint` errors or warnings in the changed files. `scripts/check_sanitization.py` deterministic layer clean on the changed files.

- `harnesses/[id]/id-validation.test.ts` runs settings, pairing, surface connect/disconnect and policy against real files in a temp home and compares the whole directory tree before and after a refused request. `keys/assigned-agents.test.ts` runs the key routes against the real `KeysService`.

A room that hears anyone loses shell, file, code-exec and chat-admin tools for everyone, admins included, and reads the public web only with an admin's yes. Approvals stay with the admin list in every room.
- Each channel is its own room: its own session, its own notes, and the connector posts only in listed channels. The dashboard's Rules tab can add and remove channels, the dry run lists them, and the runbook documents the two settings.

## Why

One agent should be able to answer in its team channel and in a couple of public channels without running a second agent. The public channels need fewer tools and must never see the team channel's conversation or notes.

## What

- A third harness adapter behind the door: the Claude Agent SDK (`lib/runtimes/claude-sdk/`), with the same four verbs as Pi and Letta Code (start, send, read, veto). Lab only: no launcher, no UI, nothing wired into the app.

- A fake SDK and a scripted Anthropic model for CI, twelve shims broken on purpose, a cell image for the sealed Docker rig, and four checks that are this harness's own.
- `docs/lab/claude-sdk.md`: what is proven and what is not.

## Why

The door's promise is that the rules hold whatever the harness is. Two harnesses that both speak the OpenAI chat format were not much of a test of that. The Claude Agent SDK speaks another format, is a compiled program, and has a permission system of its own, so it tests parts of the contract the first two did not.

## Verification

Real Claude Agent SDK 0.3.325 (Claude Code 2.1.325), scripted model, no key and no account:

- **Process level: 18 of 18 checks pass.** Twelve broken shims each turned their named checks red.
- **Sealed Docker cell: 24 of 24 pass** (S0-S3, the shared checks, C8, C9, C10, and the four of its own). Eleven broken rigs each turned their named checks red.

- **Network, by hand:** a packet capture in the cell during the Docker run. In the in-cell checks that run no probe, every packet the cell sent went to the door or to Docker's resolver. Started with its defaults instead, in the same sealed container, the SDK looked up `api.anthropic.com` ten times; every lookup failed and no packet left for anywhere but the door.
- `npx vitest run`: 255 files, all passing. `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. Sanitize gate, deterministic layer: clean on every changed file. The semantic layer needs a key this machine does not hold, so it runs here in CI.
- **Mutation, by hand:** 89 changes to the new code, one at a time. 84 turned a named test red. Four of the other five now have a test; the fifth was a guard nothing could make refuse, and was removed.

What the real SDK did that the plan did not expect, each now with a test and a broken shim:

- Its permission callback is not asked about every call. It ran a file read in its work folder and a shell `ls` without asking. The shim tells it to ask about each tool by name.
- Its hooks do not run in its minimal mode, so the callback is the veto.
- A failed model call ends the turn as a `result` of subtype `success`, with the error as its text. The shim posts nothing unless the turn says it did not fail.
- It is a compiled program, so no tripwire can be loaded into it. Its traffic is watched through a proxy at process level, which is weaker than for the other two harnesses. Its matrix says so.

Not verified:

- **Nothing was run against Anthropic's API.** A one-turn run is written (`npm run conformance -- anthropic-live`) and needs an SDK folder and a key file. CI runs the same code with a stand-in at each end.

- **Shared contracts changed, each additively:** `ModelShape` gained optional parts; the shared key check reads the key from whichever header the format uses; the credential guard takes two named exceptions and decides itself what each may hold; a harness can add a caveat to its own matrix; the scripted model has a second format; two rule statements name both formats; the Docker rig's entry picks its adapter from a table. Two other branches are changing `lib/door` and `lib/core` at the same time, so expect small merge conflicts there.
- The SDK is not open source and is not a dependency of this repo. It is pinned in `conformance/docker/claude-sdk/` for the test image only, and Dependabot's update pull requests are switched off for that folder, as for Letta Code's.
- "Ask about every tool" rests on one settings line on one pinned version. The shim sends no turn to another version, and C4q is the check that would notice.
- One gap found in the shared suite and left alone: for a harness that keeps its thread, the scripted model's OpenAI side never asks for the removed tool in the third turn of C15t. The doc says why it was not changed here.

## Symptom

Wire a Discord bot via surfaces/connect with `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS=<username>` **before** inviting it to a server → the adapter boots, logs `Could not resolve usernames: <username>`, and then silently ignores everyone. The operator's mental model is "connected = working"; the bot looks dead until someone manually restarts the container after the invite.

Hit on all six bots of the 2026-07-27/28 Cyborg.Garden rollout — each needed one manual `docker restart` after Authorize.

## Cause

Username→ID resolution (`_resolve_allowed_usernames` in the hermes Discord adapter) runs once at `on_ready` against current guild members. A bot invited after boot never re-resolves.

## Options

1. **Real fix (adapter-side, hermes-agent-mt / upstream):** re-run `_resolve_allowed_usernames` on `on_guild_join` (and arguably on a slow periodic retry while unresolved entries remain). Same fork-first pattern as the role-mention fix (hermes-agent-mt#121).
2. **HSM-side workaround:** a "re-resolve / restart" nudge in the harness UI when the Discord surface has unresolved username entries, or an automatic recreate triggered the first time the bot appears in a guild (HSM can poll `/users/@me/guilds` with the stored token post-connect).

Option 1 is where the bug lives; option 2 improves operator visibility either way (surfacing `Could not resolve usernames` in the surface status would have saved four debugging rounds).

Related: gardener seed `memory/handoffs/2026-07/28-juniper-gardener-seed-garden-discord-agents.md` (Task 3).

- New workflow `readme-zh-sync.yml`: when `README.md` changes on main, it updates `README.zh-CN.md` and bumps its source-SHA marker. It lands the change through the gate that main's ruleset requires.

## Why
The Chinese README should never drift from the English one, and nobody should have to sync it by hand. main requires the `sanitize / sanitize` check on the exact commit, and GITHUB_TOKEN pushes and PRs start no workflows. So the flow is: translate and validate, gate the file in-job (so nothing unvetted reaches a public branch), force-push the commit to `bot/readme-zh-sync`, dispatch `sanitization.yml` on that branch, wait for it to pass on that SHA, then fast-forward main to it. If main moved, it stops without rebasing; the next push or the weekly run redoes it. No check runs are created by hand, and no rulesets, settings or secrets change.

The model call is tested with a fake fetch.
- Dispatch probe: `gh workflow run sanitization.yml --ref <test branch>` started a run, and its check is named `sanitize / sanitize` (GitHub Actions app 15368) on that exact SHA and concluded success; the `gh run list --commit` lookup the workflow uses found it.

## Risk

## What
- Scheduler keys substitutions by (provider, model), so two rows sharing a model id under different providers each rotate on their own row; a substitution that matches no row on disk refuses the whole write instead of being reported applied.
- A successor that is already a row of the same provider is never applied (`successor-already-in-cascade`, scheduler and manual apply).
- Writer resolves `carryFrom` before the entry's own row and only within the entry's provider; the models PUT route whitelist-copies body rows so `carryFrom` never enters from the API.
- The editor's 409 handling reads the body: `primary-mismatch` shows the writer's message and keeps the edit; only the stale-rows 409 reloads and remounts.
- `findSuccessor` no longer lets the older-than-current guard fall open when the current row is gone and undated: it reports near misses only, accepts a `currentDate` hint, and the scheduler records each row's release date (`released`) in the report and hands it back on the next run (`retired-current-no-date` when nothing dates the row).

## Why
Round-3 audit findings on the cascade tracking stack: a same-model/different-provider pair rotated one row and lied about both, a rotation onto an existing row swapped credentials and left a duplicate, an API body could move one provider's key_env onto another provider's row past the credential check, the editor wiped a fixable primary-mismatch edit, and a retired bare-id row could be auto-rotated to an older, numerically higher model.

## Verification
- Red first: 14 new tests written against the unfixed code, all failed (`npx vitest run` on the five touched test files → 14 failed | 149 passed).
- After the fix: `npx vitest run` → 129 files, 1611 tests passed (baseline 1598). `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` → clean. `npx eslint` on touched files → 0 errors (5 pre-existing unused-import warnings in page.tsx, untouched).
- One existing test reshaped: "retired-by-absence row with no known pricing" previously depended on the inert date guard (no prior report at all); it now seeds the date via a notify run with `pricing: null` and still asserts the distinct `retired-current-no-pricing` reason.
- New tests: scheduler ×5 (`lib/services/__tests__/model-update-scheduler.test.ts`), writer ×2, route ×1, `cascadeSaveConflict` ×2, `findSuccessor` ×4 (including the fixture from the finding: {grok-4.20 Mar, grok-4.6 Aug}, current grok-4.7 absent → no successor, 4.20 a near miss; and deepseek-v4-flash-0731 ↛ v4.1-flash).

## Risk
- Behaviour change: a retired bare-id row with no previous report now reports **no** successor (near misses only) until a run has recorded its date. The scheduler runs on its interval and records `released` for every listed row, so in steady state the date is on record before the row disappears; a row that was already gone before the first run stays blocked `retired-current-no-date` for the operator.
- The persisted report gains an optional `released` field per entry; old reports without it are read as before.
- The page.tsx change is covered only by the pure `cascadeSaveConflict` helper test; the handler itself has no component test (none exists for that page).

Stacked on #239 — merge that first (merge commit, not squash).

## What

- A door agent can be given its first tools, all inside its sealed cell: read files, write files, and a shell. Off by default. No web access.
- Each class of tool has a mode in the rules record: never, ask, allow. Shell starts at ask. `decide()` gives the answer; the harness only carries it.
- In ask mode the door posts the exact call in the room and holds it until an admin replies `approve` or reacts ✅. Anyone else's answer does nothing. No answer in time is a no. The yes is tied to a hash of the call, and the gate in the cell runs only what has that hash.
- File tools are kept in a scratch folder (a 64 MB in-memory mount under the launcher, gone on stop). Limits: time per shell call, output size, calls per conversation per hour.
- Ten harness-neutral tool checks, each with something broken on purpose that must turn it red. Run for Pi as a process and in Docker. Letta Code's matrix lists them as not run, with the reason.
- Dashboard: a Tools card on the Rules tab, and an "Approvals only" box on Receipts.

Design and results: `docs/lab/tools-slice.md`.

## Why

A chat-only agent cannot do much. This lets an agent work on files and run commands without widening what the cell can reach, and puts a person in the loop for the risky class.

## Verification

One machine (Docker Desktop for Mac, engine 29.5.2). A scripted model and a fake chat room throughout: no real model, no real Discord, no real credential. Everything below was run on this branch with `main` merged in.

- `npx vitest run`: 250 files, 5235 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `next build` passes. Sanitization gate (deterministic) clean on the diff.
- Real Pi 1.5.2 as a process: 24 checks pass (14 shared, 10 tool). 13 shims and rigs broken on purpose each turned its named checks red.
- Real Pi 1.5.2 in the sealed Docker cell: 30 checks pass (4 seal, 13 shared, C8, C9, C10, 10 tool). 16 rigs broken on purpose each turned its named checks red, 5 of them cells with a broken gate.
- The launchers' own Docker suites, with a fake Discord: Pi 18 of 18, Letta Code 15 of 15. In them a shell command waited in the channel, did not run on a tick from the asker or a stranger, and ran on the admin's tick. File tools worked in the scratch folder and were refused outside it four ways. A 72 MB write to the 64 MB scratch folder landed no more than 64 MB.
- 77 hand mutations across `decide()`, the door, the gate, the shim, the connector, the launcher and the page: 76 turned a named test red, one changes nothing the code does.
- Letta Code 0.34.60, process and Docker: shared checks pass as before; the tool checks are listed as not run.

Not shown: what a real model does with tools; real Discord; whether a person reads the request well.

A self-audit (bypass, mutation, over-build) found and fixed four things: the dry run said "tools: none" whatever the config asked for; a tool request whose lookup failed moved its turn's deadline; a held call was not dropped when its turn settled; and, after merging `main`, tools could be switched on for a harness that has no gate for them.

## Risk

- **Shared contracts changed, additively.** `decide()` now answers `ask` for a class on the ask list (that field was refused before), and has one new event kind, `approval`. `tool_verdict` carries an optional `hash`. `ConnectorInbound` carries an optional `replyTo`, and connectors may emit a `reaction` event. A harness adapter that reads only `allow` keeps working.
- **Pi's gate now needs a yes that names the call.** A bare `allow` is a no. Every Pi cell image has to be built from this code, which the image naming already forces.
- **A config that hears anyone in the channel now makes a public record.** Its policy hash changes, so a running agent with that setting shows "older rules" until it is restarted. Such a config with a tool switched on is refused.
- **The gate is a guardrail.** It holds a model to what was approved. It does not hold something that has taken over the cell's own processes; the cell is the wall for that, as before.
- **The matrices for both harnesses were regenerated** from real runs, because the list of known checks grew.
- **CI time.** The fake-Pi suite is longer: it now runs ten more checks and five more broken shims.
- **One PR, shell included.** The source change is about 780 lines; the rest is tests, the rig, regenerated matrices and docs. Shell was not split out: it is the tool the suite already drove, so leaving it out would have saved little.
- **Tools are for Pi only.** A config that names another harness and switches a tool on is refused, and the Tools card is switched off for it.
- **A new harness adapter needs its matrix regenerated** after this lands, because the list of known checks grew by ten.

## What
- `findSuccessor`: among version bumps the newest release wins (version number is the tie-break), the current row is looked up trimmed/case-insensitively and its date is derived from the id when the provider no longer lists it, and a newer-dated lower tuple is surfaced as a near miss. grok-4.1 / grok-4 now resolve to grok-4.7, never 4.20; a retired grok-4.7 resolves to grok-4.9.
- `applyCascadeToHarness`: primary-mismatch guard (409) when the file's `model.default` is not `fallback_providers[0]` and the new row 0 is not that primary either; `allowPrimaryChange` for the cascade library apply and the legacy `{ model }` body. The scheduler's own copy of the check is gone — the writer is the one guard. `CascadeWriteInput.carryFrom` carries a rotated row's `key_env` / `api_mode` / inline `api_key` onto its successor; a row with its own credential is no longer refused for the provider's default var.
- `readFallbackProviders` never returns an inline `api_key` (it reached the browser via GET/PUT `/api/harnesses/:id/models` and was echoed back on every save).
- Scheduler: report entries record the current row's `pricing`; a retired-by-absence row takes its last-known pricing from the previous report so it can rotate unattended, else blocks with `retired-current-no-pricing` (distinct from `price-unknown`). Live pricing lookup is case-insensitive. A manual apply marks the entry `applied` in the persisted report.
- UI: Models tab shows a warning naming `model.default` when it is not row 0; Track latest follows the `modelTracking` prop (apply rotation, in-app harness switch); Check now in apply mode says what was applied and which harnesses are restarting.

## Why
Three re-auditors reproduced nine majors on #236/#237: a save on a matilde-shaped agent silently moved its primary, every scheduler rotation dropped the row's credential re-routing, inline proxy keys were sent to any dashboard viewer, the grok-4.20 trap resurfaced for rows older than both 4.20 and 4.7 (and stuck there), the release-date guard went inert when the current id was absent, retired rows could never rotate unattended, the fleet card re-offered an applied row (second click → 404), the tracking toggles showed stale state after an apply or harness switch, and "Check now" reported "every model is current" after rewriting configs.

## Verification
- `pnpm vitest run` — 129 files, 1577 tests passed (baseline on `cascade-ui`: 1548; 29 new tests, each written red first against the reproduced failure: 6 in `lib/__tests__/model-versions.test.ts`, 10 in `lib/services/__tests__/cascade-writer.test.ts` + reader, 6 in `lib/services/__tests__/model-update-scheduler.test.ts`, 2 route tests, 4 in `models-tab.test.tsx`, 2 in `model-updates-card.test.tsx`). Two existing assertions updated to the new reader contract (no `api_key` in rows).
- `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v '^\.next/'` — clean.
- `npx eslint` on every changed source file — clean.

## Risk
- Editor saves on an agent whose `model.default` drifted from row 0 now 409 instead of silently rewriting the primary; the tab tells the operator what to move. Any API caller relying on the fallback_providers body shape to move the primary on a drifted file needs the legacy `{ model }` body or the cascade library.
- `readFallbackProviders` rows no longer carry `api_key`; no in-repo caller read it (verified by grep), the writer carries the key inside the file by line.
- `model-updates.json` entries gain a `pricing` field; readers ignore unknown fields.
- Not addressed: `model-cascade-editor.tsx` still says "Primary at top" — true once the warning is resolved.

Spawned from the credential-request-link discussion (2026-07-03): agents now compose HSM URLs/API calls (`/keys?request=&assign=`), other tools script against `/api/keys` and `/api/harnesses`, and the BYO-credentials epic will add broker endpoints consumed by every gateway. The API is becoming a contract; today it's an accretion.

## Current state (observed)

- Routes are unversioned (`/api/keys`, `/api/harnesses`, `/api/settings`, `/api/people`, `/api/surfaces`, …)
- Auth model is good but implicit: GETs ungated, mutations require the `hsm_session` cookie (operator token HMAC). Nothing documents which routes exist or their shapes except the source.
- No error envelope convention (`{error}` vs bare 404 HTML vs NextResponse defaults)
- Naming drift: agents are "harnesses" in the API (`h_*` ids), "agents" everywhere in conversation; there is no `/api/agents` (a natural first guess — it 404s)
- No machine-readable schema; consumers (agents, scripts, future broker clients) reverse-engineer from `lib/services/*`

## Proposal

1. **`/api/v1` prefix** with the current surface frozen as v1; old paths alias during a deprecation window
2. **OpenAPI spec generated from source** (route handlers + zod schemas), served at `/api/v1/openapi.json`; becomes the doc of record
3. **Uniform error envelope**: `{ error: string, code?: string }` + correct content-type on all API 4xx/5xx (no HTML 404s under `/api`)
4. **Explicit auth policy doc**: ungated-GET / cookie-gated-mutation as a stated invariant, plus a second credential class (scoped automation tokens) for non-browser callers — needed before the credential broker lands
5. **Naming decision**: pick `harnesses` or `agents` once, alias the other
6. **First standardized flow**: the credential-request pattern (`/keys?request=&assign=`) documented as the canonical "intent link" idiom — GET encodes intent, never state change

## Non-goals

Public internet exposure. This stays a tailnet-plane API; standardization is about contract quality, not reach.

Related: BYO-credentials epic (nimbleco-memory `specs/2026-07-03-byo-user-credentials-epic.md`) — broker endpoints should land on this surface, not beside it.

**Task for the gardener.** Model IDs change often (Anthropic retires older ones); the create-new wizard and existing-harness cascade editor can offer models that are retired → agent crash-loops on restart. Add live freshness checking. Anthropic-first, extensible.

## Design (ready to build)
1. `lib/services/model-freshness.ts` — `fetchLiveModels('anthropic')`: find an Anthropic key via the keys service, call `GET /v1/models` (auth `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, **no beta header**; paginate), cache to disk with ~1h TTL. **Fail-soft**: no key / network error → return `null`, callers fall back to the static `MODEL_CATALOG` unflagged (never block the UI).
2. `GET /api/models/live?provider=anthropic` → `{ models, fetchedAt }`.
3. **Freshness signal = list membership.** Retired models simply disappear from `/v1/models` (404 on retrieve) — there is no "deprecated" flag in the response. So: catalog entries **absent** from the live list → mark `retired: true`; live IDs **not** in `MODEL_CATALOG` → offer as suggestable/new.
4. Consume in **both** the create-new wizard model step **and** the existing-harness cascade editor (`app/api/harnesses/[id]/models`) — show a "retired — pick a current model" warning on stale entries.
5. Provider-keyed so openai/google can be added later; wire **Anthropic only** now.

## Notes / guardrails
- Verify model IDs against the live list, never hardcode from training data.
- The models endpoint object carries `id`, `display_name`, `created_at`, and (since Mar 2026) `max_input_tokens`/`max_tokens`/`capabilities`.
- RGTDD + independent audit before merge, per the repo's dev flow.

Context: raised 2026-07-02; deferred here from a live session so it lands as durable, gardener-pickup-able work rather than dying in chat.

hits.body:
## Problem

A `mode:rebuild` shipped **stale code**. The rebuild path runs `docker compose ... up -d --build --force-recreate <service>`, and the build reads a **local checkout** (`~/Documents/GitHub/hermes-agent-mt`). That checkout was 1 commit behind `main` — missing a merged fix — and nothing pulled it first, so the build silently produced an out-of-date image.

## Fix

Before any build mode (`rebuild`/`purge`), HSM now syncs the build-source checkout to the code it's **supposed** to build, and **fails loud** rather than shipping stale.

- **`DockerService.syncBuildSource(dir)`** — `git fetch` then `merge --ff-only @{u}`. Throws on: not-a-git-repo, dirty working tree, detached HEAD, no upstream tracking branch, or non-fast-forward (diverged history). Logs the branch + commit it built from (`[rebuild] <svc>: building <dir> @ <branch> <sha> (synced to <upstream>)`).
- **`DockerService.restart(..., buildSource?)`** — runs the sync **synchronously before** the detached build spawn, so a failure surfaces to the API caller (HTTP 500 with a clear message) instead of building stale.
- **`HarnessService.restart()`** — resolves the source from the harness's own compose `build:` context (authoritative — exactly what `--build` reads, and honors any per-harness override), falling back to the global `hermesDir` setting. Returns `null` for image-only harnesses (e.g. evil-duck) so nothing is synced.
- **`readComposeBuildContext()`** (harness-compose) — parses both the long-form (`build:` / `context:`) and shorthand (`build: /path`) compose layouts in use on the Mini.
- On a failed sync, `clearRestarting()` so the harness isn't wedged in the "restarting" state — the user can retry after fixing the checkout.

### Source-of-truth note

There is **no per-harness source repo/branch/ref** in HSM config — `harnesses.json` carries only models/platform/compose-file. All local-build harnesses share one checkout + the global `hermesDir`/`useLocalBuild` settings, and there is no configured branch (the build just used whatever was checked out — the root of the bug). This change makes the ref resolution explicit (the checkout's own upstream tracking branch) and logged, and refuses to fast-forward-bypass dirty/diverged state.

## Tests

- Docker sync: ff-success, dirty→fail, non-ff→fail, no-upstream→fail, detached-HEAD→fail, non-build-mode skip, image-only skip.
- Build-context parsing: long form, shorthand, image-only (null), VPN variant.

26 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Audit (read-only, Mac Mini)

Every harness's build source verified — all "set right":

| Harness | Source | Expected ref | Actual state | Set right? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cryptids, mare, nimbleco, osint, personal | `…/hermes-agent-mt` (long-form context) | main | main, clean, 0/0 | ✅ |
| cyborg, egregore, seraph-doer, seraph-generalist, seraph-thinker | `…/hermes-agent-mt` (shorthand build:) | main | main, clean, 0/0 | ✅ |
| evil-duck | `ghcr.io/nimblecoai/hermes-agent:latest` (image, no build) | — | n/a | ✅ |

All local-build harnesses share the **single** checkout `/Users/juni/Documents/GitHub/hermes-agent-mt` → on `main`, tracking `origin/main`, clean, 0 ahead / 0 behind, not detached. The stale state that triggered the bug was transient and has since been pulled current. **No mismatches, nothing ff-pulled, nothing needing a human decision.**

## Deploy note

Deploying this fix itself requires an HSM rebuild/restart on the Mini — **not done here** (per instructions, don't disrupt the running HSM/agents). Flagging for a human.

## What

- Door agents can read the web without the cell getting a route out: a `web_fetch` tool (class `network`) and a `web_search` tool (class `search`) that ask the door, which makes the request itself and hands back text marked as untrusted.
- Two fetch modes, both off by default: `allowlist` reads only listed hosts or host/path prefixes (the record's `egress.hosts`, now read); `public` reads any public address (`egress.default: 'public'`). In both: GET only, no credential or cookie, private/loopback/link-local/metadata addresses refused after every DNS answer and on every redirect, connection pinned to the checked address, size/time/hourly limits, HTML reduced to text, content to the model only, receipts with host/path/size and never content.
- Search through the Brave Search API with a key only the door holds, read from a 0600 file whose path sits with the record's other secret paths. Results are titles, addresses and snippets; a result is readable only if the current mode allows it; its own hourly count; receipts hold the query length and result count, never the query.
- Launcher config `tools.web` (`mode`, `allow`, `approval`, `search`), a web section on the dashboard's Tools card (mode, approval, suggested sites as one-click chips, search toggle and key file path), the rules in the catalogue, and ten harness-neutral conformance checks (N1+, N1 to N9).

## Why

Agents are most useful with research, and the cell cannot reach the network. This gives them a read-only way to reach the web that the door decides and bounds, like every other tool.

## Verification

- Unit suite: 5,581 tests; all pass but two compose tests that read the Docker name prefix the run set on purpose, which pass without it. `tsc`, the sanitization gate (deterministic layer) and `next build` are clean.
- Real Pi 1.5.2: 59 checks pass as a process, 60 in the sealed Docker cell, the ten web checks among them, against a fake web and a fake search provider on loopback with a fake DNS. No test reaches the internet.
- Broken on purpose: seven door rigs and gates (no list check, unchecked redirects, no address check, kept cookies, no limits, a search key when search is off, a gate whose web tool fetches by itself) each turn their named web checks red and leave the others green.
- Launcher Docker suites with a fake Discord: Pi 20 of 20, Letta Code 15 of 15. Letta Code (26 process, 34 Docker) and the Claude Agent SDK (36 process, 38 Docker) pass as before and list the web checks as not run.
- Hand mutations: 67 lines broken one at a time; 63 turned a named test red, 4 change nothing alone because a second line holds the same thing.
- An audit found and fixed, among others: Node's `http.request` with `agent: false` ignores `createConnection` and dials localhost (the request now names the checked address too); a denied approval still left a fetch ticket; an HTML stripper that went quadratic on unclosed tags.

## Risk

- New outbound traffic from the door process, off unless an operator turns it on. Under `public`, what an agent puts in an address or a query reaches that site or the provider.
- No prompt-injection scanning of pages: content is marked untrusted and goes to the model only. A scanner can plug in at the door later.
- The TLS path and the real Brave endpoint are not exercised by tests (the fakes are plain http on loopback); production is https only.
- Pi only, like the other tools. Conflicts with the command-policy PR are expected in `decide.ts`, `door.ts`, `config.ts`, the Tools card and the six matrices.

Fixes four Telegram connector gaps in HSM.

## 1. Connect-path admins: @usernames resolved, multiple admins supported

The connect route previously wrote `config.adminUser` **verbatim** into `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` — a typed `@handle` was stored raw and never matched the numeric sender IDs the gateway compares against, silently locking the admin out.

- Connect dialog admin field now accepts multiple comma-separated entries (numeric IDs and/or @usernames).
- Server-side (`surfaces/connect`): entries are split, `@handles` resolved to numeric IDs via `resolveTelegramAdmins` (strict — an unresolvable handle returns 400, surfaced inline in the dialog; nothing raw is ever stored). The bot token from the request payload is used, since `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` may not be in the agent `.env` yet at connect time.
- Display names persisted to `resolved-identities.json` (merged, same shape as the settings path).
- Settings PUT: telegram allowlists are expanded with resolved numeric IDs (`expandTelegramAllowlist`, mirroring the Signal phone→UUID expansion).

## 2. Admin-store convergence

`TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` (env bootstrap) and the `SurfaceAdminService` overlay (`harnesses.json → surfaceAdmins`, served live to the policy plugin) could diverge. Both the connect route and settings PUT now call `SurfaceAdminService.syncFromAllowlist`, which replaces the explicit overlay (when one exists) with the valid numeric identities from the freshly-written allowlist. Invalid entries (unresolved `@handles`, wildcards) are dropped by validation — never stored. With no explicit overlay, the bootstrap default already reads the env live, so no sync is needed and `setAdmins`'s bootstrap-actor semantics are preserved.

## 3. Telegram group-invite policy is no longer inert

- `GROUP_INVITE_VARS` gains `telegram: 'TELEGRAM_GROUP_INVITE_POLICY'` — the existing Group Invite Policy toggle now actually writes it (`approved-only` / `allow-all`, same values as signal/slack).
- New enforcement endpoint for the `swarm_map_policy` agent plugin (contract below).
- Middleware: the new POST path is exempted from the operator-cookie gate via `AGENT_CALLABLE_POST_PATHS` (agents cannot obtain the cookie — same rationale as the existing agent-read allowlist). Trust model documented in `middleware.ts`: the caller self-reports `addedByUserId`, so blast radius is bounded — the handler can only append one structurally-validated groupId to that surface's group allowlist, still gated by policy + admin check, and audit-logged.

## 4. Privacy-mode warning in the connect flow

The dialog's `getMe` verification now reads `can_read_all_group_messages`; when `false` a non-blocking warning explains Group Privacy is ON, the bot won't see regular group messages, how to disable it (BotFather → `/setprivacy` → Disable), and that the bot must be removed/re-added to existing groups after changing it.

Plus format hints on both the connect-dialog admin field and the settings Admins TagInput (numeric IDs or @usernames; @usernames auto-resolved).

## New plugin contract (consumed by a hermes-agent-mt follow-up)

```
POST /api/harnesses/:id/surfaces/:platform/groups/:groupId
Content-Type: application/json

{ "addedByUserId": "<platform-native user id of whoever added the bot>" }
```

Responses (200 unless the request is malformed):

| Case | Body |
|---|---|
| Approved, allowlist updated | `{ "approved": true, "restarted": <bool> }` (`restarted:false` = env written but container recreate failed, e.g. no compose file yet) |
| Approved, no-op (`*` wildcard or already listed) | `{ "approved": true, "already_allowed": true }` |
| Rejected | `{ "approved": false, "reason": "<why>" }` — plugin should leave the group |
| Malformed (unsupported platform, invalid groupId, missing `addedByUserId`, no agent `.env`) | `400 { "error": "<what>" }` |

Policy semantics: `allow-all` → approve for anyone; `approved-only` **or unset (secure default)** → approve only when `addedByUserId` is an admin (`SurfaceAdminService.isAdmin`, fail-closed). No auth cookie required on this one path (see `AGENT_CALLABLE_POST_PATHS`).

## Test results

- `vitest run`: **85 files, 829 tests passed** (43 new: resolver strict/best-effort matrices, connect-route resolution + multi-admin normalization + 400-on-unresolvable, store convergence, `approveGroupInvite` policy × admin matrix, POST route responses, middleware gate exemptions, privacy-mode flag).
- `eslint .`: identical to baseline (72 pre-existing errors, none introduced).
- `next build`: passes.

## Noted but deliberately not fixed

- `addedByUserId` on the new POST is self-reported by the agent — the server cannot verify who performed the platform-side invite. Documented in `middleware.ts`; consistent with the trust already extended to the plugin's is_admin/is_group_allowed reads.
- The same connect-path verbatim-adminUser behavior still exists for mattermost/discord/slack (out of scope).
- Settings PUT keeps raw `@handles` in the env alongside the appended numeric IDs (display parity with the settings GET merge; harmless — they just never match).
