## What
- **Auto-seed on first contact.** A sender's card is created from *observed* platform facts only — display name, the id forms they present, first/last seen. Nothing about them is inferred. The seed happens before the read, so a first-time sender is recognized on their **first** turn, not their second.
- **Self-learned id aliases.** `pre_llm_call` supplies both id forms per turn (Signal carries a phone number *and* an ACI UUID), so the plugin learns the mapping itself and records it on the card. This works for arbitrary senders; `resolved-identities.json` only ever covers admin-entered identities and so can't cover a stranger who joins a group — it stays as a fallback.
- **`remember_person` tool.** The agent records what it *learns* about how to talk to someone, instead of a human editing frontmatter.
- `PERSON_MEMORY_READONLY=1` restores slice-1 (read-only) behavior; `PERSON_MEMORY_DISABLED=1` still disables the plugin entirely.

## Why
Slice 1 was read-only, so the adaptation layer only worked for people someone had hand-written a markdown card for — in practice, nobody. A memory layer that needs manual seeding isn't a memory layer. This makes the card set populate and improve through ordinary interaction, with no manual step and no admin configuration.

## Verification
30-case harness against the real template: auto-create on first contact, first-turn recognition, both alias directions resolving to one card (no duplicates), no rewrite across repeated turns, tool-driven enrichment reshaping the directive, read-only mode, fail-open on unknown sender / malformed event / unwritable directory, and traversal safety. Existing 0.2.0 alias tests re-run green (8/8), so the `resolved-identities.json` fallback is not regressed.

## Risk
This plugin now **writes**, where before it only read. Mitigations, all tested:
- Writes are atomic (tmp+rename) and gated on actual content change; `last_seen` is date-granular, bounding disk cost to one write per person per day.
- Every write path is fail-open — a write failure degrades to "no memory of this person", never a broken turn.
- Agent-written values are rejected if they contain anything identifier-shaped (phone/email/UUID), because these fields are echoed verbatim into shared group sessions. Writable fields are an allowlist; ids live in the filename and the non-injected `alias_ids` field.
- Untrusted platform display names are stripped of control characters and length-capped before they can reach the model's context.

Worth a second opinion on: auto-seeding means the agent keeps a durable record of everyone who ever messages it, including in groups. That's the point of the feature, but it is a new persistent-record property — `PERSON_MEMORY_READONLY=1` is the opt-out.

## What

Adds a `bluesky` provider to the HSM keys model, for Iris's Bluesky posting lane.

## "What does it need, just the user/pass?"

Almost. A Bluesky **app password is a single secret**, but a session (`com.atproto.server.createSession`) needs the **pair** `(identifier, app-password)`. So the model here is: **one key, two env vars** —

| var | what | secret? |
|---|---|---|
| `BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD` | the app password (`xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`) | yes — the key's encrypted value |
| `BLUESKY_IDENTIFIER` | the account handle (e.g. `nimbleco.ai`) | no — key metadata, new `identifier` field |

The keys model is strictly one-secret-per-key, so the identifier rides in key metadata and both vars are emitted at write time — the same paired-vars posture as the existing Anthropic `API_KEY`/`TOKEN` special case, except both vars are always written instead of one-of-two.

## Behavior

- `BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD` is discovered as provider `bluesky`; `BLUESKY_IDENTIFIER` is **never** discovered as a key of its own, but a discovered app password picks up the identifier written next to it (round-trips on re-assignment).
- `writeKeyToEnv` emits the pair. An identifier-less write never half-clears a hand-written `BLUESKY_IDENTIFIER`.
- Unassign / delete / rotate keep both halves in lockstep with `keys.json` (assign writes both, strip removes both, rotate can update the handle).

## Add Key UX

Prefill link for vaulting Iris's credential once the app password exists:

```
/keys?request=bluesky&assign=h_iris&identifier=<handle>
```

Opens the Add Key form with provider `bluesky`, assignment to the `iris` harness, and the handle prefilled — the operator pastes only the app password. The handle field is required for bluesky (a password without its identifier can't open a session). `identifier` in the URL is fine: it's the public handle, not secret material.

## Tests

77 keys-suite tests pass (17 new): pair write/strip/rotate sync, discovery incl. the identifier-is-not-a-key case, request-param parsing. The 38 failing `harness-*`/`fleet-health` tests fail identically on clean `main` (environment-dependent, docker/host state) — untouched by this PR.

Matilde, osint-engine, agentic-startup-generalist, iris, the use-case template and swarm-map each carried their own copy, and they had drifted: iris/template still ran the old Anthropic-SDK version with no card/JWT/connection-string detectors and a line-scoped allowlist; swarm-map lacked the fail-closed honesty fixes; only ASG had the verdict cache. ## Problem

`PUT /api/harnesses/:id/models` writes the model cascade into a live agent's `config.yaml` and the agent restarts onto it, with no validation. A model whose **provider has no configured credential for that agent** crash-loops it on restart — the motivating case: pushing `moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code` via `openrouter` onto an agent that has no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.

## What changed since the first revision

The original PR validated cascade models against `MODEL_CATALOG`. Review correctly rejected that: `MODEL_CATALOG` is a tiny ~2-per-provider **suggestions** list, **not** an allowlist (anthropic only lists `claude-sonnet-4-6` + `claude-haiku-4-5`). Strict membership would 400 **legitimate in-use models** — `claude-opus-4-8` (the fleet's actual model), newer gemini/gpt, etc. That's a regression. The strict-catalog check is **gone**.

## Fix — validate provider-credential PRESENCE, not catalog membership

In the `PUT` handler, before any config write:

1. **Empty/missing model id → always 400.** The unambiguous crash case; kept.
2. **Provider-credential presence.** Read the agent's configured provider keys and reject a cascade entry **only** when its provider is *definitively un-serviceable* for that agent.

New `readAgentEnvVarNames(dataDir)` (in `lib/services/harness.ts`, alongside the other `read*(dataDir)` readers the route already uses) reads the agent's `.env` and returns the set of var **names** present — never values, never logged. Same parse semantics as `keys.ts` `parseEnvFile` (skips comments, blanks, empty/`${...}` values).

`validateCascadeEntries(entries, presentEnvVars)` rejects an entry **iff**: the provider needs a known single credential, we know which env var(s), **and** none are present.

## Fail-open is the load-bearing constraint

Zero false-rejections of legitimate models is the bar — blocking a valid config is worse than missing an exotic bad one. We reject **only** when positively certain:

- **Enforced (single, unambiguous credential):** `anthropic` (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` *or* `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`), `openai` (`OPENAI_API_KEY`), `openrouter` (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`).
- **`ollama` / `custom` → always allowed.** Local / `base_url`, no key needed.
- **`google` / `gemini` → always allowed.** Multiple auth modes (API key, Vertex+ADC, service-account JSON); a missing `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is *not* proof of un-serviceability → fail open.
- **`bedrock` → always allowed.** AWS multi-var creds / instance role / `~/.aws` that needn't appear in the agent `.env`; absence isn't proof → fail open.
- **Unknown providers (`nous`, proxies, anything else) → always allowed.** No authoritative credential to check.
- **No env-var info → only the empty-id guard applies.**

Model ids are no longer checked against any list (only the provider's credential is). `claude-opus-4-8` and any future/exotic model id pass as long as the agent can actually serve its provider.

## Tests

- `lib/__tests__/model-catalog.test.ts` — credential-presence unit tests (provider-with-key incl. an *uncatalogued* model passes; provider-without-key rejected listing model+provider+expected var; `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN` path; multi-error reporting; `ollama`/`custom`/`google`/`gemini`/`bedrock`/`nous`/empty-provider fail-open; empty-id rejected even for no-key providers). Catalog-membership tests removed.
- `app/api/harnesses/[id]/models/route.test.ts` — route integration (provider-with-key → 200 + write; openrouter-without-key → 400 + no write; `fallback_providers` shape; `ollama` no key → 200; unknown provider fail-open → 200; empty cascade → 400; empty model id → 400). Credential reader mocked.
- **Full suite: 366 pass.** The 4 failures in `usage.test.ts` are a **pre-existing** `better-sqlite3` native ABI mismatch (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127 vs 137), unrelated to this change. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## For the reviewer

- **Where I chose to fail open (please sanity-check):** `google`/`gemini`, `bedrock`, and all unknown providers are **never** rejected on credential grounds. A real but exotic mis-config (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible provider behind `custom` with the wrong/absent key) won't be caught — by design, to guarantee no false-rejections of valid configs. The empty-id guard is the only universal floor.
- **`ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`:** anthropic is serviceable if *either* `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN` is set (the keys.ts bearer-vs-apikey split), so a bearer-only agent isn't falsely rejected.
- No deploy / restart / merge performed. Code-only guard for human review.

Resolves #150.

## Root cause
`lib/services/restart-tracker.ts` holds an in-memory restart lock with a flat 5-minute TTL. The lock is cleared early in exactly one useful place: inside the harness **status GET/list handler** (`harness.ts`, "Override status based on restart tracker" → if the container reads `running`, call `clearRestarting(id)`).

`docker.restart()` is fire-and-forget (detached `spawn` / `child.unref()`) for every mode, so `restart()` returns immediately. A `quick` restart completes and the container is healthy in ~12s — but the only thing that clears the lock early is a client **reading** harness status. A pure-API workflow (POST `/restart`, then verify via docker/logs directly, never GET `/harnesses`) never triggers that clear, so the lock persists the full 5 min and a second restart returns `409 {"error":"Restart already in progress"}` for minutes after the first one finished. This silently blocks the exact iterate-restart-verify loop used for model/config tuning (observed on Matilde, 2026-07-05).

## Fix
Make the TTL reflect how long each mode can actually run, instead of a flat 5 min (issue's option 2, cheapest and fully self-contained):

- `quick` / `recreate` → **90s** (complete in seconds; the short window is just a debounce so we don't hammer a container that's still coming up)
- `rebuild` / `purge` → **5 min** (a Docker build can legitimately run for minutes, so a still-building harness must not be reported as done)

The TTL now stores per-entry mode (already tracked) and `isRestarting()` compares against `ttlFor(mode)`. The GET-based early clear stays as a best-effort fast path; the TTL is now a correct backstop on its own, independent of any client polling status.

## Tests
Added to `lib/services/__tests__/restart-tracker.test.ts` (all green, full suite 670/670 pass):
- quick-mode lock clears after the short TTL (2 min in) — was the failing regression
- recreate-mode also uses the short TTL
- quick-mode lock is still held immediately after a restart (30s debounce)
- build-mode (`rebuild`) lock survives 2 min — long builds keep the full window
- existing `purge` 5-min TTL-expiry test still passes unchanged

## Scope note
This PR fixes **#150** (restart-lock false-409). It does **not** touch #149 (models-PUT cascade rewrites each row's provider to the harness top-level provider, dropping `base_url`) — that's an unrelated subsystem (models route / cascade provider preservation, same family as #126) and not a trivial add-on, so it's left for its own change.

Release notes

Sourced from postcss-selector-parser's releases.

7.2.0

  • feat: add the opt-in maxInputLength option, which rejects a selector longer than the limit before parsing it
  • feat: support the case-sensitive attribute flag s per Selectors Level 4, on Attribute#sensitive and Attribute#sensitiveFlag. [a=b s] previously left insensitive: false and filed the flag in raws.insensitiveFlag (#327 by @​abhu85)
  • docs: add a threat model to SECURITY.md: resource consumption caused by unbounded untrusted input is now handled as a regular bug
  • docs: document the raw-value helpers (stringifyProperty, valueToString, setPropertyAndEscape, appendToPropertyAndEscape, setPropertyWithoutEscape), the seventeen type guards, and the clone() overrides argument (#231)
  • fix: forward the default options given to the parser factory, so parser(fn, { maxInputLength }) and the other options take effect there as documented (#345 by @​Aurantium-47)
  • fix: preserve the spaces declared on selector and root containers, through rawSpaceBefore and rawSpaceAfter (#356 by @​Aschenbath)
  • fix: preserve selector delimiters after an escaped backslash, so .a\\.b parses as two classes (#354 by @​wozhenbang2004)
  • fix: escape class values supplied to the constructor, matching what the value setter already did (#349 by @​SAY-5)
  • fix: escape values assigned to an id through the value setter, and replace a stale raws.value on assignment (#326 by @​mahirhir)
  • fix: keep $ in an attribute name inside a preprocessor interpolation, so [#{$attr}] in SCSS and [@{attr}] in Less round-trip (#336 by @​theRizwan)
  • fix: reject an attribute selector with no valid attribute name, instead of throwing a raw TypeError or emitting the literal text undefined (#335 by @​theRizwan)
  • fix: keep the processor's entry points usable when destructured, as in const { process } = parser() (#145)

Behaviour notes

  • className and id values are escaped when passed to a constructor or assigned through value, so an already-escaped value is now escaped twice. setPropertyWithoutEscape() is the escape hatch.
  • [a=b s] sets sensitive: true rather than filing the flag in raws.insensitiveFlag. Serialization is byte-identical for i, I, s, S and non-standard flags.
  • Selector and Root emit their own rawSpaceBefore and rawSpaceAfter, which changes serialization for ASTs that set them.
  • An attribute selector with no attribute name raises the parser's own error rather than throwing a raw TypeError or serializing the text undefined: [ns|*] and [ * ] are affected. A trailing *, $, ^, ~ or | after a valid name is dropped, as [href=] already was.

7.1.8

  • fix: parse selectors in linear time on four more kinds of crafted input, closing a CPU exhaustion vulnerability (reported by @​zachariah-mithani)
  • chore: replace the cssesc dependency with an internal copy, whose redundant space removal is linear

7.1.7

  • fix: lossless: true preserves trailing whitespace in a selector that ends empty, such as :not(a, ). Note that :not( ) now yields a selector holding one empty string node rather than an empty selector (#337 by @​theRizwan)
  • fix: consume the whitespace that terminates a hexadecimal escape, so [x="\000061 b"] unescapes to ab (#340 by @​jakezwang)

7.1.6

  • fix: parse flat selectors in linear time, closing a CPU exhaustion vulnerability (GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf, reported by Wayde Shi)

7.1.5

  • fix: don't treat a non-prefix token before | as a namespace (#324 by @​spokodev)
  • fix: preserve whitespace before a * namespace in attribute selectors (#325 by @​spokodev)
  • fix: TypeError on unclosed [, ( and trailing | (#330 by @​theRizwan)

## What

- The door shows that a door agent is working on a message: 👀 on it as soon as it is handed to the agent, Discord's typing indicator renewed about every 8 s while the turn runs, then ✅ in place of 👀 once the reply is posted, or ⚠️ when the turn ends with no reply (a failed model call, an error, a timeout, no answer, or a reply the door refused after delivery).
- Only a message the door delivered to the agent gets any of this. Dropped messages get no reaction and no typing: chatter, people or bots not on the list, other channels. The connector also refuses a reaction or typing call outside the channels it may post to.
- While a tool call waits for an admin's yes, 👀 stays and typing stops. Typing comes back once the admin answers.
- Two switches in the rules record, `discord.statusReactions` and `discord.typing`. Both are on when left out, and neither changes the policy or its hash. Each has a toggle on the dashboard's Rules tab. The dry run says to allow Add Reactions in the channel, and the runbook covers the new permission, the behaviour and the `out.status` receipt.

## Why

A door agent that reads web pages can take 20 to 40 seconds to answer, and it showed nothing in the meantime, so people took it to have ignored them. The other bots in the server show 👀 and typing. The door owns chat, so it shows these signs and the harness plays no part.

⚠️ is used rather than ❌. ❌ is how an admin says no to a request, and a turn with no answer is not a refusal of what the person asked. The door's own line in the room says what went wrong.

## Verification

- Test-first, against the fake Discord: `lib/lab/pi-discord/__tests__/turn-status.test.ts` (end to end with the launcher's policy, the real connector and the door), `lib/door/__tests__/turn-status.test.ts` (fake clock: no timer outlives a turn, renewal, no stacking, paused while held), and new cases in `lib/door/__tests__/discord-connector.test.ts` (scope, rate limits). The fake Discord now answers the reaction and typing endpoints, and can refuse them with 429 or 403.
- Rate limits: a short 429 on reactions is waited out off the turn's path and the swap still lands in order. A long one, or a 403, writes one `out.status` receipt per kind per turn, and the reply is posted at once.
- Mutation run: 17 mutants, all caught. Among them: reacting on dropped messages, never using ⚠️, a timer left running, typing not paused for an admin, the turn waiting on typing, reactions out of order, an unhandled rejection, a long rate limit being waited for, a react outside the channel scope, a failed receipt write left as an unhandled rejection, and the dashboard toggle not wired.
- Full suite, `tsc --noEmit`, and the deterministic sanitization layer on every changed file are all clean. The semantic layer did not run because no key was set.
- Pi Docker launcher suite (`conformance/suites/pi-discord.docker.test.ts`) on freshly built images: 20 of 20 pass. Mutating the launcher so it starts the door without status turns it red. It now checks that the launcher starts the door with status on (✅ and typing on an answered message) and that nothing is put on a dropped message.

## Risk

- Without Add Reactions in the channel, each turn writes one `out.status` receipt (code 403). The turn is not affected.
- A change to either switch takes effect on the next start, like the persona. It is not part of the policy hash, so the Overview's "rules in force" line does not show it.
- A stop while a turn is running leaves 👀 on that message.

## The bug (caused live config corruption)
`PUT /api/harnesses/:id/models` rewrites the `model:` and `fallback_providers:` sections of an agent's `config.yaml`. The section-replacer skipped only **indented** old body lines (`/^\s+\S/`). If an agent's existing `fallback_providers` entries were written with the **dash at column 0** —
```yaml
fallback_providers:
- provider: anthropic
  model: claude-sonnet-4-6
```
— those `- provider:` lines aren't indented, so the replacer left them in place *after* the newly-written block. Result: a bare sequence item as a sibling of top-level keys → **invalid YAML → the agent fails to load its config on next restart.**

Hit for real while adding a fleet-wide `glm4:9b` fallback: 4 of 6 agents (whose fallbacks happened to be col-0) got corrupted and had to be hand-repaired.

## The fix
Treat a section as spanning everything up to the **next top-level mapping key**. Skip indented lines, blank lines, **and** column-0 block-sequence items alike — stop only at `^[A-Za-z_][\w-]*:`.

## Test
New regression test feeds a col-0 `fallback_providers` block, PUTs an update, and asserts: no orphaned `^- provider:` lines remain, the trailing top-level key survives exactly once, the new entry lands, and the old block isn't carried over twice.

Full suite: **540 pass**, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## What this is

Batch D of the security-review remediation: the **correctness / data-loss** findings that bite the operator through normal UI use — no attacker required. Independent of Batch A (#157); can merge in any order (minor overlap in `keys.ts`, trivial to reconcile).

All backend fixes are TDD'd (RED→GREEN). The two frontend fixes have no unit-test seam in the current vitest setup and are verified by inspection (noted per-item).

## Findings fixed

**D1 — `personal` harness targets the wrong data dir (data-loss).** personal's data lives at `~/.hermes` (`guessDataDir` special-cases it), but `duplicateOverlay()` and `remove()` hardcoded `~/.hermes-${name}` → `~/.hermes-personal`, which doesn't exist. Duplicating personal produced an **empty clone**; deleting it targeted the wrong dir. Reachable once personal is persisted as an overlay — which happens after any routine edit (e.g. setting its model cascade). Both now resolve through a shared `agentDataDirForName` helper; `remove()` additionally **guards `~/.hermes`** (the root install) from dashboard deletion.

**D2 — UI-created harnesses show zero keys forever.** Key/tool/memory discovery only scanned a hardcoded 8-name list, so any harness created via Create/Duplicate/Import (persisted in `harnesses.json`) was invisible. `list()` and `getDecryptedValue()` now union in the overlay names.

**D5 — decrypt failure returned raw ciphertext as the plaintext credential.** On a rotated/lost `.key`, `getDecryptedValue` returned the `iv:tag:ciphertext` string, so the agent booted with a garbage credential instead of failing loud. Now fails closed (undefined) for values in our ciphertext format, while still returning genuine legacy pre-encryption plaintext as-is (distinguished by format).

**D3 — silent-failed key revoke.** Assign/unassign issued a `quick` restart (`docker compose restart`), which does not reload `env_file` — so an assigned key never loaded and a revoked key stayed live despite the "removed" toast. Both now `recreate`, matching the add-key handler that already documents this.

**D6 — cross-harness cascade bleed.** `ModelCascadeEditor` had no `key`, so React reused the instance across in-app harness navigation; B's Models tab could render and save A's cascade. Added `key={id}`.

## Tests

- `keys-dataloss.test.ts` — rotation → undefined (not ciphertext); legacy plaintext preserved; UI-created harness key discovered.
- `harness-personal-datadir.test.ts` — personal duplicate copies `~/.hermes`; `remove` deletes normal dirs but never `~/.hermes`.
- Existing `harness-duplicate.test.ts` still green (no regression).

**Full suite: 688 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean. No new lint.**

## Deliberately deferred (in the handoff, need Mini or a product call)

- **D4 — fire-and-forget restart reports Docker failure as HTTP 200.** The fix (surface async exit codes without breaking the intentional detached design) is design-touchy and best verified against real Docker on the Mini.
- **Encryption IV 16→12 bytes + key versioning** — changes the ciphertext format; needs a migration against real key data.
- **`unassignKey`/`updateDmPolicy` dead code** — wiring them up is feature work, not a fix (their restart mode is corrected here defensively).

## Context — the inert plugin

The `swarm_map_policy` plugin already ships per-user tool gating: `pre_gateway_dispatch` caches `{platform, chat_id, user_id, is_admin}` per thread and `pre_tool_call` blocks `ADMIN_GATED_TOOLS = {approval, pr_approval}` for non-admins. But it has been **inert**: `is_platform_admin()` calls `GET {HSM}/api/harnesses/{id}/surfaces/{platform}/admins/{user_id}` and `is_group_allowed()` calls `.../groups/{group_id}` — **routes that did not exist on HSM main**. Every call 404'd, so `is_admin` failed closed to `False` for everyone and those tools were blocked for all users. This PR builds the HSM side so the existing fail-closed skeleton comes alive.

This is **A1** of the role-gating design (`memory/specs/2026-07-02-role-gating-and-model-awareness-design.md`, Part A/A1): the role **store** + the missing routes.

## What A1 adds

**Store — `lib/services/surface-admins.ts` (`SurfaceAdminService`).** A per-harness, per-surface admin list keyed by the runtime's real identity (Signal UUID/phone, Telegram numeric id, …). Explicit lists persist on the harness overlay (`harnesses.json`, new optional `Harness.surfaceAdmins`) so they are HSM-side policy served **live** — no container recreate, unlike `.env` vars. Reads the raw overlay directly (not via `HarnessService.list()`, which shells out to Docker) to keep the per-message is-admin path cheap.

**Routes** (shapes matched exactly to what the plugin reads):
- `GET  .../surfaces/:platform/admins/:userId` → `{ is_admin: boolean }`, always 200 (fail-closed hot path) — `is_platform_admin()`
- `GET  .../surfaces/:platform/groups/:groupId` → `{ allowed: boolean }`, always 200 — `is_group_allowed()` (mirrors the existing `/policy?action=group-check` logic at the REST path the plugin expects)
- `GET  .../surfaces/:platform/admins` → effective list + `source: 'explicit'|'allowlist'` (for the Permissions UI)
- `PUT  .../surfaces/:platform/admins` → `{ admins, actor }`; set/replace the list

## Default-to-allowlist — no regression guarantee

When a surface has **no explicit admin list**, the admin set falls back to that surface's DM allowlist (`{PLATFORM}_ALLOWED_USERS` in the agent `.env`) — the existing `_is_approval_admin` "approved = DM-allowlist" convention. An agent with no role config therefore behaves exactly as before. (Before this PR the route 404'd → `is_admin=False` for everyone; now DM-allowlisted users are correctly recognized as admins, which is the plugin's intended behavior.)

A **wildcard** DM allowlist (`*`) means "anyone may DM me", **not** "everyone is admin" — so it yields **zero** default admins (fail-closed, and identical to today's behavior for `*` agents). Surfaced as `allowAllDm` so the UI can explain the empty set.

## Bootstrap-admin + self-escalation decisions

- **Bootstrap admin = the DM allowlist.** The first admins are whoever the operator put in `{PLATFORM}_ALLOWED_USERS` via the trusted connect/settings dashboard plane (e.g. the `adminUser` set at connect time). Those bootstrap admins can then set an explicit list.
- **No self-escalation.** `setAdmins` authorizes against the **current** admin set: `actor` must already be an admin (explicit list, or the bootstrap allowlist before any explicit list exists) or the mutation is rejected `403` — *before* any validation, so it leaks nothing. A group member who is not already an admin cannot add themselves, even by driving the agent to call the route.
- **Route authz.** Mutations are now **transport-gated**: root `middleware.ts` (PR #139, merged + activated 2026-07-03) requires a valid `hsm_session` operator cookie (stateless HMAC of `HSM_OPERATOR_TOKEN`) on every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE under `/api`. Agent containers cannot obtain that cookie, so the confused-deputy path from the original audit (agent reaches `HSM_URL` and calls `PUT` with an admin id it holds or reads off the ungated GET) is **closed at the transport layer**. The `actor`-must-be-current-admin check is retained as **defense-in-depth + semantic authz**: it attributes the change to a concrete surface identity for the audit log, and keeps self-escalation blocked even if the middleware's fail-open kill-switch (`HSM_OPERATOR_TOKEN` unset) is engaged. GETs remain intentionally ungated so the plugin's per-message is-admin/group reads keep working.
- **Input validation.** Identity keys are validated per platform (Signal UUID/phone, Telegram/Discord numeric, Mattermost/Slack id shapes); wildcard, empty, over-long, and any entry with separators/whitespace/control chars is rejected before it enters the store.

## Test evidence

New: `lib/services/__tests__/surface-admins.test.ts` + route tests for all three route files. Covers set/get admin list, is-admin true/false, **default-to-allowlist when unset**, wildcard-allowlist → not admin, fail-closed on unknown user/agent/platform, **non-admin actor cannot mutate (403)**, malformed input rejected (400), dedupe, and explicit-over-allowlist precedence.

Middleware gating itself is covered generically by `middleware.test.ts` on main (route-handler tests invoke handlers directly and bypass middleware — the established convention), so no per-route middleware tests were added.

See **Re-cut 2026-07-03** below for the current full-suite numbers on the rebased branch.

## Re-cut 2026-07-03

Rebased onto `origin/main` on top of the auth primitive (PR #139 merged + activated; also picks up #132 slug normalization, #128 sanitization lane, #140 Slack docs). Rebase was conflict-free; one follow-up commit updates the PUT-route/service comments that described the pre-auth world (actor check as sole protection → transport gate as boundary, actor check as defense-in-depth). No behavior change.

```
$ npx vitest run   # full suite, rebased branch
 Test Files  73 passed (73)
      Tests  638 passed (638)

$ npx tsc --noEmit
(exit 0)
```
(The `docker.sock` lines in full-suite stderr are pre-existing noise from unrelated harness-discovery tests when Docker is down; no test fails.)

## Scope / follow-ups

- **A1 of the role-gating design — re-cut on the live auth gate.** The original draft was PROPOSE-ONLY because HSM had no transport auth and the in-PR actor check would have been the sole boundary. That premise is gone: PR #139's operator-cookie middleware is merged and live, mutations are transport-gated, and this PR no longer rests on an absent auth model. It still awaits a fresh independent security audit before merge/deploy (runtime unaffected by this PR, but the cluster it unblocks needs a coordinated fleet rebuild).
- **A2 (verb-level GitHub read/write split) is a separate follow-up PR** in `hermes-agent-mt`.
- **Permissions UI is a follow-up:** the page (`app/(dashboard)/permissions/page.tsx`) is display-only today; wiring a real per-surface admin editor (which must send the operating admin's native id as `actor`) is a UI lift kept out of this PR to avoid ballooning it. API + store + tests are the core and are complete.

## Phase 2 — use-case packages in create-new

Builds on the trust-gate (#96). Lets a user opt into an opinionated public **package** when creating an agent; **Matilde** (science) is the first. Everything a template pulls is fetched from a pinned git ref and **scanned by the trust gate before install** — copy + gate only, **no script execution**.

### What's added
- **`lib/services/usecase-templates.ts`** — registry loader + `installUseCaseTemplate`: installs a template's git-sourced artifacts via the shared trust-gated `installArtifacts`, then seeds its SOUL. The SOUL file is scanned **in isolation** (copied alone into a scratch dir → `gateArtifactDir`) so sibling files (e.g. a setup script) can't taint the scan and a poisoned SOUL is refused.
- **`GET /api/usecase-templates`** — lists templates (id/name/description/recommends).
- **Deploy route** — resolves the template id (unknown → 400), enables the template's plugins in `config.yaml`, installs it after the baseline; a gate refusal fails the create **before the container starts**.
- **Wizard** — package picker folded into the Identity step (no step renumber); selecting a package prefills the recommended provider/model; threads the template id to deploy.
- **`infra/usecase-templates.json`** — Matilde entry, pinned to `NimbleCoAI/Matilde#v0.1.0` (plugin `matilde_plugin`, skill `hermes-skill`, SOUL `docker/SOUL.Matilde.md`). Matilde was packaged self-contained in NimbleCoAI/Matilde#7 and tagged v0.1.0.

### Decisions
- **Copy + gate, no script exec** (per security stance) — Matilde's `instance-setup.sh` is never run; artifacts are overlaid + scanned.
- **Trust-gate is the dependency** — merged first as #96.

### Verification

## What this is

Batch A of the remediation for the 2026-07 adversarial security review. This PR closes the **injection → RCE** and **config-injection** findings — the highest-severity, most self-contained cluster. It is pure input-hardening: no behavior change for legitimate callers, no deployment coordination required.

Verified against current `main` before writing any fix — all findings here confirmed live (the review's commit was only 3 non-security commits behind). Each fix is TDD'd with an exploit-proving test (RED→GREEN).

## Findings closed

**F8 (critical — container breakout to host root):** `PUT /api/harnesses/:id/image` with a newline in `imageRef` spliced `privileged: true` + a `/:/host` bind into the hermes service's compose YAML; the immediate recreate brought the container up as host root. One unauthenticated request → full host.

**F1–F5 (critical — OS command injection → RCE):** `lib/services/docker.ts` built shell command strings from settings-derived values (`composeFiles`, `defaultImage`, `hermesDir`, `service`) and ran them via `execSync`/`sh -c`. `PUT /api/settings {"composeFiles":["x; <cmd> #"]}` then any `GET /api/harnesses` executed `<cmd>` as the server process.

**F7 (critical — command injection):** the signal `verify` route interpolated `phone` into an `exec()` string with only a truthiness check (the sibling `register` route already validates E.164 + uses `execFile`).

**F9–F11 (high — env/policy injection):** secret values / deploy tokens / connect config written into `.env` files with no newline check → inject arbitrary env lines, including overriding the secure-default policy block.

**P3/F6 (high — no input validation at the trust boundary):** `PUT /api/settings` merged the raw body into stored settings with no schema.

## How

- **Shell-free `docker.ts`:** every subprocess via `execFileSync`/`spawn` with an argv array. Purge mode drops `sh -c "build && up"` for two chained docker argv calls (up only if build exits 0). No shell, no escaping surface.
- **Shared `assertNoNewline(value, field)`** (in `lib/env-helpers.ts`) wired into the four generated-file sinks: `mergeEnvVars`, `upsertEnvVar`, `generateEnvContent`, `setComposeImage`.
- **`verify` route** mirrors `register`: E.164 validation + `execFile` argv for all three docker calls.
- **`validateSettingsPatch`** — explicit allowlist rejecting unknown keys, wrong types, out-of-range ports, and newline-bearing path/image/host strings. Route returns 400 on violation.

## Threat model note

HSM runs single-operator behind Mullvad + tailnet (not public internet), but the reachable attacker class includes **any container on the same Docker network** and anything on the tailnet — both reach these sinks, so the RCE chains are as severe as the review states.

## Tests

New RED→GREEN suites: `docker-injection.test.ts` (sinks no longer execute an injected `touch`), `injection-newline.test.ts` (all four write sinks), `verify-phone-validation.test.ts` (metacharacter phone → 400 before any subprocess), `settings-validation.test.ts` (allowlist). `docker.test.ts` updated to the execFile surface with all behavioral assertions preserved.

**Full suite: 706 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean. eslint: 0 errors.**

## Not in this PR (subsequent batches)

- **B — auth:** `middleware.ts` fail-open kill-switch + decrypted-PIN-over-GET. (Needs the `HSM_OPERATOR_TOKEN` rollout on the Mini — coordinated deploy, not just a merge.)
- **C — signal-cli infra:** daemon bound to `0.0.0.0`, docker.sock in third-party autoheal, root container, DNS-rebinding defeat.
- **D — correctness/data-loss:** `personal`-harness wrong-dir, masked key revoke (`quick` restart doesn't reload env_file), hardcoded key discovery, `ModelCascadeEditor` stale-state.

Also downgraded from the review: **P6 "path traversal" is not exploitable** — Next.js collapses `..`/`%2f` on single-segment routes before matching (worth the dedup as hardening, not urgent); and the port-collision low finding was already fixed by #155.

- `lib/services/agent-deploy-templates.ts` + `lib/services/keys.ts`: write/detect the GLM key as `GLM_API_KEY` (matches the runtime `zai` plugin).

- `provider: zai` is emitted with **no base_url**; the hermes-agent `zai` plugin owns the Z.ai endpoint. The same selection points at **Z.ai today** or a **future self-hosted GPU box** (via `GLM_BASE_URL`) with zero code change.

## SPIKE — do not merge

A minimal, well-commented proof that HSM can act as a control plane over a **Letta runtime** alongside Hermes. Builds spike steps 1–3 from the spec (`memory/specs/2026-07-18-swarm-map-letta-librarian-airlock.md` §4); skips step 4 (airlock) and the Primo deploy. Nothing was deployed anywhere — code + local typecheck/lint only.

### What it proves
1. **Server runs unchanged.** `docker/letta-compose.yml` defines a `letta/letta` server on `:8283` with a Postgres volume. HSM's existing runtime-neutral `DockerService` (`lib/services/docker.ts`) can start/stop/logs it with **zero new Docker code** — a Letta server is just a container.
2. **Agents-as-API-resources.** `lib/services/letta.ts` is a small fetch-based REST client (`listAgents`, `getAgent`, `createAgent`, `sendMessage`, `getMemoryBlocks`) — a **new abstraction distinct from the container model**, since individual Letta agents are rows in Postgres with no container to start/stop.
3. **Read-only view + one action.** `app/(dashboard)/letta` lists agents, sends a single message, and peeks at core-memory blocks, proxied same-origin through `app/api/letta/*`. New "Letta" sidebar entry.

### How to run it (later, not in this PR)
```bash
# on a host with RAM to spare (spec names Primo, but that's a client machine — ask first)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... docker compose -f docker/letta-compose.yml -p letta up -d
# point HSM at it (defaults to :8283 if unset)
export LETTA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8283
# then open the "Letta" page in the HSM dashboard
```

### Intentionally out of scope
- **Airlock** (step 4 / spec §3) — governance/egress-redaction membrane.
- **Wizard integration** — no base-package generator, deploy wizard untouched.
- **Runtime-adapter refactor** — the dormant `lib/types.ts` `runtime` seam is a *container*-runtime concern, orthogonal to Letta; **no `lib/types.ts` changes on main**.
- **No Hermes deploy path touched.** This lives strictly alongside.
- Per-agent message serialization, auth, and hardened typing are noted in comments but not implemented (spike).

### Verification (honest)
- `tsc --noEmit`: **passes clean** (exit 0, no errors) against the full project.
- `eslint` on the new/changed files: **passes clean** (exit 0).
- Not exercised against a live Letta server — endpoints were verified against docs.letta.com (2026-07-18), not a running instance.

### Letta-docs surprises vs the spec
- **Memory-blocks path:** current docs use `GET /v1/agents/{id}/blocks` (the spec hedged `/v1/agents/{id}/core-memory/blocks`). Client uses the current path.
- **Persistence:** the official `docker run` example uses the image's **embedded Postgres** + a volume mount, not a separate pgvector service. The compose follows that; the shared external pgvector shape (production/airlock auditability) is included commented-out with `LETTA_PG_URI`.
- **Provider keys are server-wide** env vars on the container (not per-agent) — a real divergence from Hermes' per-container creds.
- **Maintenance caveat:** Letta's self-host docs now flag the Docker image as "no longer an actively maintained/supported product surface," nudging toward Letta Cloud / local mode. Fine for a spike; a production host decision is a real open question.

## Problem
`installBaselineTemplates` runs only at agent **create/duplicate** (`harness.ts:243`/`:1149`). Artifacts added to `infra/artifacts.json` later never reach already-created agents — `rebuild` is a pure docker-compose op and never re-installs. So #81's reinstated `captcha_cascade` + `captcha-escalation` would never have reached the agents that need them.

## What this adds
`POST /api/harnesses/:id/artifacts/sync` — diffs an agent's data dir against the manifest and installs what's missing, **without clobbering** anything the user added or changed.

Two-layer safety model (`lib/services/artifacts-sync.ts`):
1. **Additive floor** (no history needed): install artifacts that are **missing**; never touch an existing one. This alone solves the driving case (agents *missing* a plugin gain it) with zero clobber risk.
2. **Pristine-update**: an `.artifacts-lock.json` records the shipped content hash at install time. An existing artifact is updated to the new shipped version **only if its on-disk hash still matches the lock** (provably unmodified). User-modified → `skip: user-modified`; not in lock → `skip: untracked`. `force` overrides.

Also: newly-installed `enabled:true` plugins are appended to `config.yaml` `plugins.enabled` (text-based, no YAML dep — also closes the long-standing 'no plugin-enable API' gap for the sync path); the container is recreated **only if something changed**; `dryRun` returns the plan without writing or restarting.

## Three-path framing (per AGENTS.md required reading)
| Path | Behavior |
|---|---|
| create | unchanged — baseline installed at create |
| duplicate | unchanged — inherits source's artifacts |
| **sync (new)** | additive + hash-gated pristine-update, no-clobber |

## No-clobber design notes
- Create path is **untouched** (additive, low-risk): the lock writes on first sync. Until an agent has been synced once it is additive-only (install-missing, skip-existing) — the safe direction. A follow-up could write the lock at create to enable first-sync pristine-updates.
- `force` is the only path that overwrites a user-modified artifact, and it's explicit.

## Tests
- `lib/services/__tests__/artifacts-sync.test.ts` — 13 (hashing, plan matrix: missing/untracked/pristine/user-modified/force/source-missing, apply leaves skips untouched, lock written, idempotence, config-enable incl. fresh-block + idempotent)
- `app/api/harnesses/[id]/artifacts/sync/route.test.ts` — 4 (passthrough, defaults, 404/500 mapping)
- Full suite: **317 passing**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on changed files.

Left as a reviewable PR (not self-merged) given the architectural surface.

## The bug

Adding a key from inside a single harness (`/harnesses/[id]` → Keys) offered a different provider list than the global `/keys` page. Most visibly, it had no **`custom`** option — so a harness could not be given a key for any provider HSM doesn't know by name.

## Why

The list existed **twice**, as two unrelated `const KEY_PROVIDERS` in two files with nothing linking them. They drifted in *both* directions:

| Missing from harness menu | Missing from global keys menu |
|---|---|
| `google`, `custom` | `zai`, `signal`, `mattermost`, `aws-bedrock`, `google-cloud`, `helius`, `coingecko`, `dehashed`, `opencorporates`, `capsolver`, `open-measures`, `pexels` |

Nothing server-side was rejecting `custom` — `POST /api/keys` does no provider validation and `KeyInput.provider` is a plain `string`. The option was simply absent from that array.

## The fix

- New `lib/key-providers.ts` — one list, plus `providerOptions()` carrying over the unknown-provider escape hatch the keys page already had (a `?request=` prefill would otherwise silently vanish from the harness dropdown).
- Both pages import it; both local consts deleted.
- **Env-var field added to the harness form.** `custom` needs it and only the global page had it: with no `PROVIDER_TO_VAR` entry, `resolveEnvVar` falls back to the key's *name* and then to a useless `CUSTOM_API_KEY`, so a custom key added from a harness would have landed in the wrong variable. It clears when the provider changes away from `custom`, and is only sent for `custom`.

`MODEL_PROVIDERS` is deliberately untouched — that drives the model cascade editor, not credential storage. (It *does* contain `custom`, which is probably what made the inconsistency look stranger than it was.)

## Testing

New `lib/__tests__/key-providers.test.ts` pins the parity itself, since a redeclared local list is exactly how this broke. It fails if either page declares its own `KEY_PROVIDERS`, stops importing the shared module, or drops the custom env-var field.

- Verified **red** against a deliberately reintroduced local const, green after.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Full suite: **874 passed / 87 files**.

## Note for a follow-up (not fixed here)

Both `google` and `google-cloud` are now offered. `google-cloud` maps to `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY`; bare `google` has no mapping and falls through to `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. Distinct and defensible, but the two are easy to confuse in the dropdown — worth a label or a merge later.

## What

A new `browser_login` plugin lets an agent obtain an **authenticated browser tab without the model ever seeing the plaintext password**. Phase 1 = persistent Camofox profile + one-time human VNC login.

- `browser_login(platform)` — probes the session (navigate to an authed-only page, match a text signal in the accessibility snapshot). Authenticated → proceed; otherwise navigates to the login page and returns a `login_escalation` block `{vnc_url, hint, screenshot}`. A human logs in via VNC; the session persists in the `.camofox` volume. Mirrors `captcha_cascade`'s escalation shape.
- `check_login_status(platform)` — single, **passive, non-blocking** re-probe; the agent polls it with its own attempt budget.
- Per-platform descriptors via `BROWSER_LOGIN_DESCRIPTORS` (env), merged over bundled defaults; HSM writes it from a new operator-editable `platformLoginDescriptors` setting.

The password travels human-keyboard → Camofox. It never passes through the model.

## Why this shape

- **No new VNC/compose plumbing** — reuses the noVNC port + `.camofox` volume + `VNC_EXTERNAL_URL` that already ship for CAPTCHA escalation.
- **No HSM escalation UI** — there is none for captcha today either; `login_escalation` surfaces via the same model→human messaging path. A generic escalation-render surface (covering captcha + login) is a separate follow-up.

## Review fix included

An adversarial review caught a HIGH: `check_login_status` was re-navigating the single shared Camofox tab on every poll — yanking the page out from under a human mid-login/MFA. Fixed: `check_login_status` is now **passive** (observes the current page, never navigates); only the initial `browser_login` navigates. Also hardened the `.env` descriptor write against U+2028/U+2029.

## Tests

- 34 pytest (plugin) + 11 vitest (descriptor `.env` helper), all green.
- Full vitest suite **505 passed**, `tsc` clean, eslint clean on changed files, sanitization gate clean.
- **Not run:** live real-platform E2E — needs a human + throwaway account + running agent; gated behind an explicit human go.

## Known residual (documented in runbook)

The model never sees the password. It *can* read the post-login **session cookie** via `document.cookie` if Camofox `/evaluate` is enabled (Camofox is CDP-less, so `Network.getAllCookies` is unreachable). Accepted Phase 1 residual — a TTL-bounded session token, not a password. Closing it is a Phase 2 decision with the credential broker.

## Symptom
A quick restart completes and the container is healthy in ~12s, but a second restart within 5 minutes returns 409 `{"error":"Restart already in progress"}` even though nothing is restarting. Hit repeatedly during model-config tuning on Matilde (2026-07-05): restart A (200) → container up in 12s → restart B 4 min later → 409 for the remainder of the 5-min window.

## Root cause
`lib/services/restart-tracker.ts` holds an in-memory lock with a 5-min TTL. It is cleared in exactly two places:
1. TTL expiry (5 min), or
2. `harness.ts:796` `clearRestarting(id)` — which lives **inside the status GET/list handler** (`Override status based on restart tracker` → if container is 'running', clear).

So the lock only clears early if someone **reads** harness status via the UI/GET and observes 'running'. A pure-API workflow (POST /restart, then verify via docker/logs directly, never GET /harnesses) never triggers the clear → the lock persists the full 5 min despite the restart finishing in seconds.

## Recommendation — yes, fix it
The lock-clear must not depend on a client polling status. Options, cheapest first:
- **Decouple the clear:** in `restart()`, for non-build modes schedule a lightweight health-poll (reuse the existing /health check) that calls `clearRestarting(id)` once the container responds, independent of any GET.
- Or shorten the TTL for `quick`/`hard` modes to ~60s (build modes keep the longer window).
- Belt-and-suspenders: on 409, have the route verify actual container health and self-heal the stale lock before rejecting.

Impact: silently blocks the exact iterate-restart-verify loop used for model/config tuning. Low-risk fix, covered by `restart-tracker.test.ts`.

## Problem

The per-harness **Logs** view called `GET /api/harnesses/[id]/logs`, which returned `docker compose logs` (container stdout). For Hermes agents that stdout is **only the gateway startup banner** — e.g. `{"logs":"hermes-mare | ...banner...","lines":5}`. The actually-useful logs are written at INFO level to files **inside** the container at `/opt/data/logs/{gateway,agent,errors}.log`, which map to the host bind-mount `<dataDir>/logs/`. HSM runs on the same host, so it can read these files directly.

## What changed

`app/api/harnesses/[id]/logs/route.ts`:
- Default behavior now reads `<dataDir>/logs/gateway.log` instead of docker stdout.
- New `?source=` query param:
  - `gateway` (default) → `gateway.log`
  - `agent` → `agent.log`
  - `errors` → `errors.log`
  - `docker` → the **old** `docker compose logs` behavior (preserved)
- `?lines=` is respected (default raised to 200).
- `dataDir` is resolved via the existing **`guessDataDir()`** resolver (same pattern the models route uses: `guessDataDir(serviceName ?? name, containerName)`) — no hardcoded `~/.hermes-<name>`.
- Response shape stays compatible: `{ logs, lines, source, path? }` — existing UI consumers keep working.

`lib/services/harness.ts`:
- New exported **`tailLogFile(filePath, lines)`** helper. Reads a bounded window (2MB cap) from the **end** of the file so a multi-MB log never lands fully in memory, drops the partial first line, and returns `''` on missing/empty/error.

## Fallback

If the requested log file is missing or empty, the route **falls back to `docker logs`** so nothing regresses (and still returns the 400 "No compose config" error when there's no compose config and no file).

## Path safety

User input never forms a path segment. The filename is whitelisted by the `source` enum (`gateway.log`/`agent.log`/`errors.log`), and the directory comes only from the harness→`dataDir` mapping. No traversal surface. Unknown `source` values fall through to the default (`gateway`).

## Test evidence

- **5 new unit tests** for `tailLogFile` (missing file, empty file, last-N lines, whole-file-when-fewer-lines, no-partial-first-line on a large file). All pass.
- Existing `harness.test.ts` + `models/route.test.ts` still pass (17 tests green together).
- **`next build` passes** — "Compiled successfully", "Finished TypeScript" with no type errors, `/api/harnesses/[id]/logs` route built.
- Verified against the **live** `~/.hermes-mare/logs/gateway.log` — `tailLogFile` returned real INFO lines (e.g. `... INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=signal ...`, `... INFO gateway.run: Image cache cleanup ...`), **not** the banner.

## Note for reviewer

Built and tested in an isolated git worktree on the Mini; the deployed checkout and its pm2 process were left untouched. Ready for review — merge/deploy handled by the parent session.

## Feature: edit a Signal account's profile/display name from the Surfaces → Signal tab

**Why:** The display name people see when they DM an agent's Signal number lives in the signal-cli daemon (set via `updateProfile`), **not** in HSM, `.env`, or `SOUL.md`. There's currently no way to view/change it from Swarm Map, so a freshly-provisioned or duplicated agent can advertise the wrong name. (Real case: cryptids' account `+18285443506` displayed as "nimbleco" until manually fixed.)

**Ask:** In the harness Surfaces → Signal tab, surface the account's profile name as an editable field. On save, call the signal-cli JSON-RPC `updateProfile`:

```
POST {SIGNAL_HTTP_URL}/api/v1/rpc
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"updateProfile","params":{"account":"<number>","given-name":"<name>"},"id":1}
```

(The daemon is signal-cli's JSON-RPC daemon at `/api/v1/rpc` — note it 404s on the REST `/v1/...` paths.)

## Related: agent duplicate leaves identity stale

`HarnessService.duplicateOverlay` deep-copies the source data dir **including `SOUL.md` and `HERMES_AGENT_NAME` verbatim**. It strips surface creds (`SURFACE_ENV_VARS`) and resets `platform`, but does **not** reset the agent's identity. Findings:
- `HERMES_AGENT_NAME` is **unused by the agent runtime** (cosmetic; e.g. nimbleco runs with `HERMES_AGENT_NAME=cyborg` with no effect). Identity comes from `SOUL.md`; memory is profile/channel-scoped, not name-scoped.
- `SOUL.md` copied verbatim means a duplicate **identifies as its source** until SOUL is hand-edited — easy to miss.

**Suggestion:** on duplicate, either (a) reset `HERMES_AGENT_NAME` to the new name and templatize/blank `SOUL.md` (prompt the user to write the new identity), or (b) clearly flag in the UI that SOUL.md still belongs to the source. Pairs naturally with the Signal-profile-name editor above.

_Filed from a live debugging session; cryptids was fixed manually (profile renamed via updateProfile, gateway brought online)._

## Overview

In a multi-agent deployment where multiple Hermes agent containers share a single inference backend — whether a local Ollama instance or a cloud provider API with a shared org-level key — KV cache is not isolated between agents. This is a latent privacy and security concern worth documenting and mitigating.

## How it arises

HSM deploys multiple agent containers that each make independent inference calls to the same upstream endpoint:

- **Local models (Ollama):** All agents point to the same host Ollama instance (`host.docker.internal:11434`). Ollama has no tenant isolation — it is designed for single-user local use.
- **Cloud APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.):** These providers scope prompt cache to the API key / organization. HSM deployments typically share one org-level API key across all agents, meaning all agents share the same cache namespace at the provider.

## What leaks and how

**Prefix cache sharing (passive):**
LLM inference servers implement KV cache reuse for common prompt prefixes as a performance optimization. When two agents share an identical prefix — which is likely if they use the same base system prompt — the inference server reuses the same cached KV state for both. The model's internal attention state for the shared prefix is the same physical computation for all agents sharing that prefix.

This does not cause spontaneous content bleed (Agent B's output won't contain Agent A's private tokens), but it means the attention state is not isolated between agents.

**Stale slot memory (passive):**
In Ollama and vLLM, KV memory slots are not zeroed on release. When a slot is freed by one agent and reassigned to another, the new agent's prefill overwrites it — but there is a window where physically non-cleared prior state exists. This is a design assumption in both systems (single-user or trusted multi-tenant use).

**Timing side-channel (active/adversarial):**
Peer-reviewed research (PROMPTPEEK, NDSS 2025; Cache Me Catch You, NDSS 2026) demonstrates that an adversarial client sharing the same inference backend can reconstruct other users' recent prompts with >95% accuracy using timing oracles derived from KV cache hit/miss latency differences. This requires intentional probing (~500-1000 requests per token) but only needs API access — no elevated privileges.

The same attack class applies to shared Ollama instances and to shared-key cloud API deployments.

**Published CVEs:**
- CVE-2025-25183 / GHSA-rm76-4mrf-v9r8: vLLM prefix cache hash collision enabling cache poisoning (patched v0.7.2)
- CVE-2025-1953: vLLM/SGLang KV cache hash collision via meet-in-the-middle (NDSS 2026)
- Azure OpenAI Nov 2025: cross-tenant training data contamination via fine-tuning cache race condition (MSRC advisory)

## Risk levels

| Scenario | Passive risk | Active/adversarial risk |
|----------|-------------|------------------------|
| Shared Ollama, all first-party trusted agents | Low | Medium (if any agent ever compromised) |
| Shared cloud API key, same org | Low | Medium (same) |
| Shared Ollama with any untrusted or third-party agent | Medium | High |
| Separate API keys per agent (different orgs) | None | None |

## Mitigations

**Short term — break shared prefix matching:**
Insert a unique non-guessable token (e.g. a per-agent UUID or HMAC) in the first few tokens of each agent's system prompt. Since KV cache reuse is keyed on exact token sequence, this ensures no two agents ever share a cache block, regardless of how similar the rest of their prompts are. Low cost, no infrastructure change required.

**Medium term — per-agent key provisioning:**
Where the provider supports it, provision separate API keys per agent so caching is scoped per-key rather than per-org. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI currently offer a sub-key/per-user key provisioning API, so this is not available today for those providers. Worth tracking as providers evolve their multi-tenant offerings.

**Longer term — inference isolation:**
For deployments with strict privacy requirements between agents, run separate inference backend instances per agent or per trust boundary. This provides full KV isolation at the cost of additional resource overhead.

## References

- arXiv:2502.07776 — Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs (Stanford/CRFM, 2025)
- PROMPTPEEK — I Know What You Asked (NDSS 2025)
- Cache Me, Catch You (NDSS 2026)
- NVIDIA Security Blog — Structuring Applications to Secure the KV Cache (Apr 2025)
- Ollama issue tracker: no documented per-caller KV isolation

- **A form to add a door agent**, in place of the browser's own prompt. A small dialog: a name checked while it is typed (by the rule the server uses, including a clash with an existing agent), a choice of harness (Pi or Letta Code) with what each cannot do, one line of description, and what has to be done by hand (the Discord application, the two secret files) with a link to the runbook. A door agent was made by typing a name into a browser prompt, which could not say what a door agent is, check the name, or offer a harness. ## What

- **Persona document.** A door agent's rules record takes a Markdown persona (up to 8 KB), edited on the Rules tab with a preview and a short guide. The launcher puts it in the system prompt, and then writes what the agent can do after it, from the rules. A persona cannot add an ability or remove that text. New agents start with a warm, plain default persona.
- **Notes kept by the door.** For each room, three small Markdown files (about the room, people who asked to be remembered, ongoing threads) in the agent's state folder on the host. They are given to the agent when a conversation starts, after a restart too, and never to another room. The agent changes them only through one door tool, `memory_note`. The door checks each change (size, the redactor, no mentions or ids, a person's note only when they asked), writes it, and writes a receipt.
- **Memory tab** for door agents: view, edit, wipe and download the notes. Everything shown is redacted. A kept scratch folder (`tools.keepScratch`, off by default, same size cap) can be wiped there too.
- **Checks.** Six memory checks (M1 to M6) with something broken on purpose for each, a launcher Docker suite with a real stop and start, and a fixture test that an agent made before this loads and runs unchanged.

## Why

Door agents felt robotic: a name and one line, and no memory across a restart. A fuller persona and a few checked notes make them friendlier without giving the harness anything it can use to reach past its cell. The notes live with the door, so the door decides what is kept and what each room is given.

## Verification

- Full suite: 5,572 tests, all green. `tsc`, the deterministic sanitization gate on every changed file, and `next build` pass.
- Real Pi 1.5.2 as a process: all 53 checks, including M1 to M6, and all 19 broken variants turned their named checks red. The process matrix was rewritten by that run.
- Real Pi in the sealed Docker cell: 54 of 54, including M2, M3, M4 and M6 in the cell (M1 and M5 are listed as not run there, with the reason, and covered by the launcher's Docker suite). The existing launcher Docker suite: 20 of 20.
- Launcher Docker suite for this change (real Pi, fake Discord, scripted model): the persona and then the statement in the model's own system message; a note saved and a secret note refused through the door; the note and the kept folder back after a stop and a start; both gone after a wipe. 4 of 4.
- Letta Code 0.34.60 and Claude Agent SDK 0.3.325: unchanged and green. Letta Code: 26 of 26 as a process, 34 of 34 in Docker, and its launcher suite 15 of 15. Claude Agent SDK: 36 of 36 as a process, 38 of 38 in Docker. All six matrices were rewritten by these runs (a new rule, `mem.notes`, adds a line to each).
- Mutations: 39 lines broken one at a time in the notes store, the door, the persona parser and prompt, the gate, the RPC pump, the shim, the service and the pages: all 39 turned a named test red (one did not at first; a test was added). 4 more in the launcher, run against Docker: all red (one did not at first, which found a real bug: a kept folder put back before the cell joined the door could be lost; fixed).
- Not verified: a real model, a real Discord. Pi session resume was not built (see Risk).

## Risk

- **Back-compat.** A record with no persona document and no notes renders the same config, prompt and policy hash as before (fixture test). Shared files got small additive changes: the door, the approval text (it says when the scratch folder is kept), the tools card's one line, the Pi gate and shim.
- **Pi with no tools now starts with `--no-tools`** instead of `--no-builtin-tools`, so the door's tool is not declared on a turn that was given none. Real Pi passes every check with it.
- **Pi session resume across restarts is not built.** Pi can open a session by id, but keeping its sessions would carry a folder the cell can write out of the cell, and every approval says a cell is wiped at a stop. The notes do this job instead.
- On an agent anyone can talk to, room and thread notes change only in a turn an admin started; a person's own note works for anyone.

## Git-sourced artifacts + install-time trust gate

Enables `source: "git:<org>/<repo>#<tag>[:<subdir>]"` in the artifacts manifest, fetched securely and scanned before install. Inert until a manifest references a `git:` source (all current sources are `local`). This is the security foundation the **Phase 2 use-case templates** (e.g. Matilde) build on — that's why it lands first.

### What it does
- **Parse + validate** `git:` sources — mandatory pinning, charset guards, path-traversal rejection (`parseGitSource`).
- **Secure fetch** — shallow clone at the pinned ref; auth via `ARTIFACT_GIT_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` through `GIT_ASKPASS` (never in URL/argv/errors); secret redaction; `execFileSync` (no shell) + `--` argv guards.
- **Trust gate** — every fetched text file scanned for prompt-injection/promptware/exfil; install **refused** (throws, nothing copied) on any finding. TS mirror of the image-side Python scanner (defense in depth; the image remains authoritative).

### Security review
Two independent adversarial audits. The first found 3 exploitable gaps; all fixed (TDD) and re-audited **CLOSED-ALL**:
- **Pinning** — mutable refs (`#main`/`#HEAD`/branches) were accepted. Now: `parseGitSource` fast-fails HEAD/main/master/develop, and `fetchGitArtifact` runs an authoritative `git ls-remote --heads` **before** clone, refusing any ref that resolves to a branch (verified against a SHA-shaped branch name).
- **Symlinks** — were copied but never scanned. Now the gate walk flags symlinks (refuse before copy).
- **Scanner evasions** — >1MB files and NUL-byte "binary" files were skipped. Now oversized files are refused and NUL bytes are stripped before scanning.

### Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean · full suite **467 pass / 2 fail** (both pre-existing & unrelated: `harness-image`, `harness-compose-fallback`)
- Rebased on current `main` (post-#95); conflict in `artifacts-manifest.ts` resolved so the don't-clobber guard now covers both local and git paths (and skips before any clone).

### Known follow-ups (pre-existing, non-blocking; both fail closed)
1. Raw commit-SHA pins need fetch-then-checkout (`clone --branch` can't take a SHA) — currently refuses rather than mis-fetches.
2. Consider `strict` scan scope for git-sourced **skill** installs (currently `context`).

## What
- `scripts/check_sanitization.py` becomes the **one canonical** sanitization gate (v1.0.0), merged from every per-repo copy; `scripts/test_check_sanitization.py` is the union of their self-tests (95 tests).
- New reusable workflow `.github/workflows/sanitization-gate.yml` (`on: workflow_call`) that every agent repo calls pinned to a `sanitization-gate-v*` tag; swarm-map's own `sanitization*.yml` now call it locally.
- swarm-map's reviewer prompt moves out of the script into a new `sanitize.config.json`; canonical docs in `docs/sanitization-gate.md`.

## Why
Matilde, osint-engine, agentic-startup-generalist, iris, the use-case template and swarm-map each carried their own copy, and they had drifted: iris/template still ran the old Anthropic-SDK version with no card/JWT/connection-string detectors and a line-scoped allowlist; swarm-map lacked the fail-closed honesty fixes; only ASG had the verdict cache. One script, per-repo config only.

**Behaviours merged:** Matilde/osint base (fail-closed `--require-semantic`, separate deterministic/semantic steps, fork-PR partial-coverage warning, match-scoped allowlist, nonce fence, robust verdict parser, cause-chain hints, honest summary line) + swarm-map (`--diff` three-dot PR range, `SANITIZE_ROOT`, separated international phones, 20+ char GitHub tokens, octet validation, public-IP and 555-phone filters as **opt-in** config, step summary on forks, daily full-tree cron) + ASG (per-content verdict cache, now keyed on prompt+model too) + new `--check-config` / `--require-config` (replaces each repo's config self-tests) and `max_tokens` 4096.

## Threat model
The gate stops **accidental** leaks by trusted committers (the maintainer and her agents). It is not a defence against a malicious committer who can already edit workflows; required status checks (`sanitize / sanitize`), CODEOWNERS (added here and in each consumer) and review cover that. Within the model it fails closed: layer 1 scans every file (all encodings, raw bytes, symlink targets) and cannot be disabled or narrowed by config; PRs are judged with the base branch's config, and in this repo the base branch's script.

- A Discord connector for the lab's door (`lib/door/connectors/discord.ts`), behind the same interface as the fake connector. No new dependency: it uses Node 24's own WebSocket and fetch, so no third-party package holds a bot token.
- A launcher for one Pi agent in one Discord channel (`lib/lab/pi-discord/`): config, dry run, start, stop, status, receipts. The door runs on the machine; Pi runs in the sealed cell and reaches the door through a relay that holds nothing.
- `bots.loop` is now a real rule: the door counts bot messages delivered in a row and `decide()` stops at the limit. Two more door rules: a reply size cut (`out.size`) and "a message is read once" for edits and deletes (`in.once`).
- A runbook: `docs/lab/pi-discord.md`.
- `allowedBotIds`: name the only bots that are heard. A policy can name its bots (`bots.ids`), and `decide()` drops any bot that is not named. Every other bot and every webhook is dropped with a receipt. Each named bot has its own loop count.
- A `persona` setting (a name and one line). The launcher tells the agent what it is and, in its own fixed words, what it cannot do: no tools, text only, one channel. It replaces Pi's own introduction, which says it is a coding assistant that can run commands.

Nothing here is wired into the Swarm Map app or any running agent. This PR does not start anything.

## Why

The Pi slice proved the rules with a scripted room. The next step is one real surface, with every inbound message still going through `decide()` and every reply through the door's redaction and size limit.

## How it holds the rules

- Every gateway message becomes a door event. The connector decides nothing.
- The reply can only go to the room the message came from. The connector also refuses any post outside the one channel it was started for, before a request is made.
- Replies ping nobody (`allowed_mentions` is empty).
- The bot token and the model key are read from two files only their owner can read, named by `SMLAB_DISCORD_TOKEN_FILE` and `SMLAB_MODEL_KEY_FILE`. They are never in the config, the cell, the compose file, a receipt or a log.
- The connector asks Discord for server and server-message events only. It never asks for direct messages, and asks for message text only when the config says so.
- `createDoor()` still refuses any connector that is not the fake one, unless the surface is named as live by whoever starts the door.

- `npx vitest run`: 214 files, 4321 passed, 1 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` clean. Sanitization gate (deterministic layer) clean. The semantic layer was not run here; CI runs it.

A mention is answered through Pi; a message elsewhere never reaches the model; a secret in model output is redacted; neither secret is in a container, file or log; stop removes everything. The dry run's containment checks pass, and turn red for a cell with a way out. It also shows: the model is given the persona and offered no tool, and a model that asks for one runs nothing; what the cell holds is redacted from replies; with the cell dead the door answers nobody; with the door dead the cell stays sealed and silent, and the next start removes it. 12 of 12 pass on Docker Desktop for Mac.

The README headline still said **"Multiplayer admin and orchestrator platform for Hermes"** while the product now claims two first-class runtimes. Several other surfaces went the other way and promised Letta capability we have **not** shipped. This PR fixes the framing and, more importantly, removes the overclaims — every correction below is checkable against `main`.

**Do not merge without reading the evidence column.** The whole point of this PR is that the claims are verifiable.

---

## 1. Headline and framing (claim was contradictory)

| Claim before | Status | Now |

| Headline linked `NimbleCoAI/hermes-agent` | Stale org | `NimbleCoOrg/hermes-agent-mt` |
| Letta link | absent | `letta-ai/letta` — verified live via `gh repo view letta-ai/letta` |

**Not touched on purpose:** the Quick Start `git clone` URL. That is the single README change in open PR #187 — left alone so this PR does not conflict there.

## 2. Overclaims corrected

**Evidence:** `git_enabled` has **zero** occurrences anywhere in this repository (`grep -rn "git_enabled" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git` → no hits), and agents created by our deploy path come up `git_enabled: false`.

`components/harness/letta-agent-detail.tsx` rendered a **"Context files (memfs)"** panel headed by a paragraph describing "the agent's git-backed memory file tree", followed — for every agent we create — by an empty box and the excuse *"No context files (agent may predate memfs, or files aren't exposed on this server)"*. That reads as "your agent happens to have no files", not "this feature is not on".

Fixed:
- Heading now carries a **`not enabled`** badge whenever the list is empty.
- The git-backed-memory explanation only renders when files are actually present (so it stays useful for externally-created agents that do have memfs).
- Empty state now says git-backed memory files are not enabled for agents Swarm Map deploys, points at **Core memory (blocks)** as the real live memory surface, and states that enabling memfs is not shipped.
- `MemoryBlocks` no longer says blocks "project into `system/` files" as present tense.
- Wizard copy `app/(setup)/setup/wizard/page.tsx:590` said *"Letta agents use **memfs** memory (git-backed context files)"* → corrected to core-memory blocks, with memfs marked not enabled.
- Wizard runtime picker (line 452) dropped "(memfs memory)".
- The file's header comment now carries a `MEMFS IS NOT ENABLED — DO NOT WRITE COPY THAT PROMISES IT` note with the evidence, so the next person editing this file cannot reintroduce the claim by accident.

### The Letta API surface is read-only + send-message

**Evidence — full route inventory, reproduced from `docs/runtimes.md`:**

```
--- app/api/letta/harnesses/route.ts            8:export async function GET() {
--- app/api/letta/agents/route.ts               7:export async function GET() {
--- app/api/letta/agents/[id]/blocks/route.ts   6:export async function GET(
--- app/api/letta/agents/[id]/messages/route.ts 6:export async function POST(
--- app/api/letta/agents/[id]/files/route.ts    7:export async function GET(
```

Four GETs and one POST. **No `PATCH`, `PUT` or `DELETE` anywhere under `app/api/letta/`.** So there is no lifecycle or memory-management parity to claim:

- README now tabulates the Letta routes exactly, labelled "read-only plus send-message… there is no `PATCH`, `PUT`, or `DELETE`".
- Detail-view copy no longer says a Letta agent is "managed over REST" — it now says read-only plus sending a message, with editing memory / reconfiguring / deleting called out as not shipped.
- Stated honestly where creation *does* live: `POST /api/setup/deploy` with the Letta runtime selected (`deployLettaAgent`). The one `services.letta.deleteAgent` call is rollback-only for a failed deploy — `docs/runtimes.md` says so explicitly so nobody reads it as a user-facing delete.

### Budget does not inherit on the default path

Approval and audit **do** inherit through a Hermes front — they gate the turn before it runs. Budget does not, because streaming is on by default and a streamed turn reports **zero tokens** to the enforcement hook, so spend is never counted and a soft cap is never approached.

Every place this could be read as three-for-three inheritance now says two-for-three and names the streaming reason:
- README **Runtimes** table + a "Budget caveat, stated plainly" paragraph.
- `docs/runtimes.md` §3, with the explicit instruction *"Do not write 'the bridge inherits the door's approval, audit and budget'."*
- Wizard step 3 Letta panel — the place an operator would most naturally assume the door's guarantees carry over.

The shipped/not-shipped matrix with the verification commands inline, so this stops being tribal knowledge. Linked from the README headline and the Documentation section.

## 3. Repo metadata (done via `gh`, outside this diff)

- **Description** was `Multiplayer admin and orchestration layer for Hermes agents.` → now names both runtimes and the control-plane guarantees.
- **Topics** were `agentic-ai, ai, hermes, local-ai, multiplayer` → now `agent-orchestration, agentic-ai, ai, letta, local-ai, multi-agent, multiplayer, swarm-map`. `hermes` removed (Hermes-only framing), `letta` and `swarm-map` added.

{"key": "other",     "spdx_id": "NOASSERTION", "url": null}

{"key": "agpl-3.0",  "spdx_id": "AGPL-3.0",    "name": "GNU Affero General Public License v3.0"}

## Two things, one root

### 1. The manifest bug (silent, live in prod today)
`person_memory/plugin.yaml` ships `name: person-memory` (dash), but every agent's `config.yaml` enables it as `person_memory` (underscore). The loader matches the enabled-list entry against `manifest.key or manifest.name` (hermes-agent-mt `hermes_cli/plugins.py:1454-1457`), so **dash ≠ underscore → the plugin is discovered but never enabled.** Verified 2026-08-06: on primo chur-bot/im7-bot the log showed `person_memory: registered` = **0** and discovery "N found, M enabled" never counted it. **person_memory had NEVER actually loaded on any agent.** Fix: set `name: person_memory` (underscore, matching the dir + every config). After the fix, all 12 agents (9 garden + chur-bot/im7-bot/pmf) now log `person_memory: registered` and enabled count +1. Whatever ships person_memory as an artifact must carry the underscore name.

### 2. Make it a default (HSM is the right layer)
Enabling a `standalone` hook plugin needs BOTH the files in the agent dir AND the name in `config.yaml → plugins.enabled` (`plugins.py:243-268`, `:1450-1469` — standalone plugins are opt-in). The image can't own enablement; per-template defaults drift across N templates. HSM already writes `plugins.enabled` (`lib/templates/config-yaml.ts generateDefaultConfig`, `app/api/setup/deploy/route.ts`) and installs plugin files — single choke point. Add `person_memory` to the base `enabledPlugins`.

### Boundary/privacy review — clears (SAFE-WITH-CONDITIONS)
- Egregore `boundary-check.sh` is unrelated (governs Claude Code cross-instance file access, not the Hermes runtime).
- Hermes SECURITY.md §2.3/§2.5: in-process plugins may read what the agent reads; person_memory reads only its own `memory_dir/people/*.md`, ephemeral, turn-scoped, never persisted, never into the system prompt (cache-safe).
- `credential_redactor` is already a de-facto default and *modifies* turns; person_memory is read-only + fail-open — a weaker ask.
- **Condition (shared group sessions):** HSM default is `group_sessions_per_user: false`. Confirm the injected directive is behavioral, NOT raw PII — a directive echoing raw phone/Slack IDs would surface sender A's identifiers to B in a shared session. Gate to per-user/DM or strip identifiers if so. (Relevant now that we seed `people/*.md` with phone numbers + Slack IDs on both fleets.)

## Acceptance
- person_memory manifest name is `person_memory`; HSM-provisioned agents load it with no manual config; existing agents pick it up on next artifact sync; the shared-session PII condition is verified before flipping default.

Context: 2026-08-06 fleet rollout — org memory `knowledge/decisions/2026-08-06-identity-ledger-design.md`, board `[identity-ledger-directory]`.
