## What
- New workflow `readme-zh-sync.yml`: when `README.md` changes on main, it updates `README.zh-CN.md` and bumps its source-SHA marker. It lands the change through the gate that main's ruleset requires.
- New `scripts/sync-readme-zh.mjs`: incremental translation (old English at marker, new English, diff, current Chinese → only the changed parts updated), plus mechanical validation of the model's reply.
- `sanitization.yml` gains a `workflow_dispatch` trigger (full-tree, via the existing mode expression).
- 26 tests in `scripts/__tests__/sync-readme-zh.test.ts`, run by the existing `test` workflow.

## Why
The Chinese README should never drift from the English one, and nobody should have to sync it by hand. main requires the `sanitize / sanitize` check on the exact commit, and GITHUB_TOKEN pushes and PRs start no workflows. So the flow is: translate and validate, gate the file in-job (so nothing unvetted reaches a public branch), force-push the commit to `bot/readme-zh-sync`, dispatch `sanitization.yml` on that branch, wait for it to pass on that SHA, then fast-forward main to it. If main moved, it stops without rebasing; the next push or the weekly run redoes it. No check runs are created by hand, and no rulesets, settings or secrets change.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run`: full suite passes; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Tests cover marker parsing and bumping, drift detection against a real temp git repo, prompt assembly, and validation that rejects dropped or invented images and links, dropped code blocks or sections, changed commands, truncation, untranslated English, re-added API route tables, leaked markers, and rewriting unchanged lines. The model call is tested with a fake fetch.
- Dispatch probe: `gh workflow run sanitization.yml --ref <test branch>` started a run, and its check is named `sanitize / sanitize` (GitHub Actions app 15368) on that exact SHA and concluded success; the `gh run list --commit` lookup the workflow uses found it.
- Not verified: the live model call and the final fast-forward (they run only after merge).

## Risk
- `sanitization.yml` now also accepts `workflow_dispatch`. Anyone with write access could already push to main; a dispatch only runs the gate full-tree on a ref.
- The full-tree gate is flaky. Recent full-tree runs on main failed on semantic false positives in existing files (README.md copyright line, `docs/sanitization-gate.md`, `infra/templates/skills/property-testing/SKILL.md`), but the dispatch probe on this branch passed. A flaky failure means that sync does not land; main is untouched and the next push or weekly run retries.
- `github-actions[bot]` fast-forwards main. That only happens after the required gate passes on the exact SHA, and the commit can touch only `README.zh-CN.md`.

## What

- Adds `lib/core/`: one policy record, a 35-rule catalogue, and `decide()`, the single function that says who an agent may hear and answer, which tools it may run, and when its budget is spent.
- Adds `lib/door/`: the sidecar that owns chat in, chat out and model traffic. Fake connector only. Receipts for every decision, outbound redaction that fails closed, one reply per turn, a model route that swaps a placeholder for the real key, meters tokens and keeps spend in a ledger by month.
- Adds `lib/runtimes/pi/`: the Pi shim (one `pi --mode rpc` process per session), a prompt preamble a sender cannot forge, and a tool gate extension that blocks on anything but an explicit allow.
- Adds `conformance/`: 38 scenario pairs, fake-proof guards with negative controls, a scripted model, a fake Pi for CI, fourteen shim checks, eight deliberately broken shims, and a matrix file generated from a real Pi 1.5.2 run.
- Adds `conformance/docker/`: a sealed Docker cell for Pi and the rig around it (the sidecar's side, a sink that stands in for the internet, a control that proves the sink can be hit), a probe that tries each way out, a runner that starts one rig per check and removes only what it made, and a second matrix file generated from that run.
- Adds the spec, the plan and a report under `docs/lab/`.

Nothing is wired into the app, the UI, the Hermes path or any running agent. No dependency was added.

## Why

Every harness enforces chat rules differently, so each new harness has meant re-rendering the same rules and hoping they hold. This slice tries the other shape on Pi: rules are decided once, outside the harness, and the per-harness code shrinks to "start it, send text, read text, veto a tool".

## Verification

- `npx vitest run`, after merging main (which now has #337): 211 files, 4149 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Sanitization gate, deterministic layer, on the PR diff: clean. The semantic layer runs in CI only.
- `SWARMLAB_PI_BIN=... npm run conformance` against a real Pi 1.5.2 install: 23 of 23. All fourteen checks pass, and each of the eight broken shims turned its named checks red. `conformance/matrix/pi-1.5.2.process.json` was written by that run, and a CI test now fails if that file no longer matches the suite.
- `npm run conformance:docker` with real Pi 1.5.2 in a sealed cell, on Docker Desktop 4.76 for Mac (engine 29.5.2): 29 of 29. S0-S3, C8, C9 and C10 pass, and so do the thirteen process-level checks run again in the cell. Ten rigs broken on purpose (a route to the sink, an ordinary network, the key in the cell's environment, the key in a file, a writable cell, a host folder mounted, a file where a Docker socket would be, a door with a route out, a sink nobody can prove works, C10 with the gate left in) each turned its named checks red for the reason it names. A rig handed a real-looking key is refused before Docker is asked for anything, and again by the cell itself. `conformance/matrix/pi-1.5.2.docker.json` was written by that run, and a CI test fails if it no longer matches the suite.
- The Docker checks were then broken by hand twice (the sink's log ignored; the probe's answers ignored) and the must-fail tests went red both times.
- An audit of the Docker cell then tried, by hand in a live cell, ways out the probe does not: every TCP port on Docker's side of the cell network, a port another lab container published, DNS watched with a packet capture (with a control that was seen leaving), IPv6 without the cell's own setting, and the model route and the door's port poked from inside. Nothing got out and no key came back. It found the run went red on a network that answers no IPv6 DNS question (fixed), three checks with no broken rig (added), and that S1-S3 did not read what Docker actually gave the container (they now do; a cell given a shared process namespace, a published port and loosened seccomp turned S1 and S2 red when tried). These by-hand trials are not standing checks; the report says which.
- Not run: C13 (no tool verdict depends on who asked yet, so it could not fail for the reason it names), C7, C12b. The Docker run is not in CI.
- Mutation checks, run by hand and not committed: listed in `docs/lab/pi-slice.md`, "What this does not show", item 11.
- Not verified: the Docker run on any other machine, Docker version or engine, or on Linux.

## Risk

- **The wall is shown on one machine, for the ways out that were tried.** With Pi in the lab's Docker cell, a tool it ran reached nothing but the door and read no secret, also with the tool gate removed. That is Docker Desktop for Mac, one version, and a list of probes, not a proof: a way out that is not on the list was not tried. `docs/lab/pi-slice.md` lists the limits (DNS judged by its answer, no IPv6 control, wall-check lines with no broken cell behind them, the cell token readable inside the cell, no limits tested, and more). Do not read this PR as "Pi is safe to deploy".
- **These are lab images and a lab rig.** Nothing in Swarm Map starts a cell like this, and no running agent is in one. In the rig the door has no route out either; a door that talks to a real model and a real chat platform needs one, and that side is not tested.
- **The Docker run needs an internet connection for its controls.** A one-off container asks DNS for three names before a run (and, if this machine's resolver answers no IPv6 question, asks a public resolver itself), and one cell that is broken on purpose is put on an ordinary network and opens one connection from there. No public address is written in the repo.
- **At process level, "nothing left this machine" is shown for Pi's own Node runtime only.** The tripwire there does not see a program Pi starts that is not Node. The Docker cell is what covers that.
- **The key swap and the budget cap exist for one wire format** (OpenAI chat-completions). A harness that speaks another has neither; the route refuses its calls.
- **Pi is given no direct messages**, because its sessions share one folder on disk.
- **The bot loop limit is not enforced.** With bots allowed, two bots can answer each other without end.
- **The credential preflight is a list of names and shapes.** A credential it has not been taught goes through; Pi's environment is listed by hand for that reason.
- **Several check lines have no broken shim behind them** (C2, C4a, C12, C15 and parts of C1, C5v, C8p). The report lists them.
- A scripted model tests plumbing only.
- The fake Pi was wrong once already (real Pi never asks the gate about an undeclared tool). The real-Pi run caught it. The fake can drift again when Pi changes; the pin is 1.5.2.
- `tsconfig.json` gains `allowImportingTsExtensions`, and `vitest.config.ts` excludes `conformance/suites/*.real.test.ts`. Both are small, but they touch shared config.
- This is one branch rather than the four stacked PRs the plan described. It is large (about 16,100 lines, 1,600 of them a lock file, mostly tests and scenario files). The commits can be read one at a time.
- An earlier commit on this branch held a longer copy of the spec. The tip does not, but the branch history still does. Squash on merge if that matters.

## Links

- `docs/lab/pi-slice.md`: what exists, how to run it, what it does not show.
- `docs/lab/primitives.md`: the spec. `docs/lab/plan-pi.md`: the plan as written.

## What

- Door agents can read the web without the cell getting a route out: a `web_fetch` tool (class `network`) and a `web_search` tool (class `search`) that ask the door, which makes the request itself and hands back text marked as untrusted.
- Two fetch modes, both off by default: `allowlist` reads only listed hosts or host/path prefixes (the record's `egress.hosts`, now read); `public` reads any public address (`egress.default: 'public'`). In both: GET only, no credential or cookie, private/loopback/link-local/metadata addresses refused after every DNS answer and on every redirect, connection pinned to the checked address, size/time/hourly limits, HTML reduced to text, content to the model only, receipts with host/path/size and never content.
- Search through the Brave Search API with a key only the door holds, read from a 0600 file whose path sits with the record's other secret paths. Results are titles, addresses and snippets; a result is readable only if the current mode allows it; its own hourly count; receipts hold the query length and result count, never the query.
- Launcher config `tools.web` (`mode`, `allow`, `approval`, `search`), a web section on the dashboard's Tools card (mode, approval, suggested sites as one-click chips, search toggle and key file path), the rules in the catalogue, and ten harness-neutral conformance checks (N1+, N1 to N9).

## Why

Agents are most useful with research, and the cell cannot reach the network. This gives them a read-only way to reach the web that the door decides and bounds, like every other tool.

## Verification

- Unit suite: 5,581 tests; all pass but two compose tests that read the Docker name prefix the run set on purpose, which pass without it. `tsc`, the sanitization gate (deterministic layer) and `next build` are clean.
- Real Pi 1.5.2: 59 checks pass as a process, 60 in the sealed Docker cell, the ten web checks among them, against a fake web and a fake search provider on loopback with a fake DNS. No test reaches the internet.
- Broken on purpose: seven door rigs and gates (no list check, unchecked redirects, no address check, kept cookies, no limits, a search key when search is off, a gate whose web tool fetches by itself) each turn their named web checks red and leave the others green.
- Launcher Docker suites with a fake Discord: Pi 20 of 20, Letta Code 15 of 15. Letta Code (26 process, 34 Docker) and the Claude Agent SDK (36 process, 38 Docker) pass as before and list the web checks as not run.
- Hand mutations: 67 lines broken one at a time; 63 turned a named test red, 4 change nothing alone because a second line holds the same thing.
- An audit found and fixed, among others: Node's `http.request` with `agent: false` ignores `createConnection` and dials localhost (the request now names the checked address too); a denied approval still left a fetch ticket; an HTML stripper that went quadratic on unclosed tags.

## Risk

- New outbound traffic from the door process, off unless an operator turns it on. Under `public`, what an agent puts in an address or a query reaches that site or the provider.
- No prompt-injection scanning of pages: content is marked untrusted and goes to the model only. A scanner can plug in at the door later.
- The TLS path and the real Brave endpoint are not exercised by tests (the fakes are plain http on loopback); production is https only.
- Pi only, like the other tools. Conflicts with the command-policy PR are expected in `decide.ts`, `door.ts`, `config.ts`, the Tools card and the six matrices.

## Feature: edit a Signal account's profile/display name from the Surfaces → Signal tab

**Why:** The display name people see when they DM an agent's Signal number lives in the signal-cli daemon (set via `updateProfile`), **not** in HSM, `.env`, or `SOUL.md`. There's currently no way to view/change it from Swarm Map, so a freshly-provisioned or duplicated agent can advertise the wrong name. (Real case: cryptids' account `+18285443506` displayed as "nimbleco" until manually fixed.)

**Ask:** In the harness Surfaces → Signal tab, surface the account's profile name as an editable field. On save, call the signal-cli JSON-RPC `updateProfile`:

```
POST {SIGNAL_HTTP_URL}/api/v1/rpc
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"updateProfile","params":{"account":"<number>","given-name":"<name>"},"id":1}
```

(The daemon is signal-cli's JSON-RPC daemon at `/api/v1/rpc` — note it 404s on the REST `/v1/...` paths.)

## Related: agent duplicate leaves identity stale

`HarnessService.duplicateOverlay` deep-copies the source data dir **including `SOUL.md` and `HERMES_AGENT_NAME` verbatim**. It strips surface creds (`SURFACE_ENV_VARS`) and resets `platform`, but does **not** reset the agent's identity. Findings:
- `HERMES_AGENT_NAME` is **unused by the agent runtime** (cosmetic; e.g. nimbleco runs with `HERMES_AGENT_NAME=cyborg` with no effect). Identity comes from `SOUL.md`; memory is profile/channel-scoped, not name-scoped.
- `SOUL.md` copied verbatim means a duplicate **identifies as its source** until SOUL is hand-edited — easy to miss.

**Suggestion:** on duplicate, either (a) reset `HERMES_AGENT_NAME` to the new name and templatize/blank `SOUL.md` (prompt the user to write the new identity), or (b) clearly flag in the UI that SOUL.md still belongs to the source. Pairs naturally with the Signal-profile-name editor above.

_Filed from a live debugging session; cryptids was fixed manually (profile renamed via updateProfile, gateway brought online)._

feat(ci): sanitization gate for the base package (#65)

* feat(ci): sanitization gate for the base package

The base package (infra/templates/**, docs, base skills/soul) ships to every
agent, so it must never contain secrets, PII, or use-case-specific particulars —
even from an automated contribution. Adds a layered, fail-closed gate:

- scripts/check_sanitization.py — deterministic layer (secret/API keys, private
  keys, JWTs, quoted hardcoded creds, real emails, phones; placeholder-aware, no
  API key needed) + an LLM particulars layer (use-case-specific names/orgs/IDs/
  case details). Full-tree (--all) so a pre-existing leak can't hide in an
  untouched file. Both must pass; a missing LLM key fails closed.
- .github/workflows/sanitization.yml — runs the scanner's own tests + the
  full-tree base scan on every PR.
- Sanitized a real pre-existing leak (operator SSH target) from a base doc.

TDD: 18 scanner tests; the base now scans clean (deterministic layer).

NOTE: set the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repo secret to enable the semantic layer; the
deterministic layer enforces without it.

- Added key families: Stripe, Twilio, SendGrid, Slack webhook, Bearer, Basic

- Unquoted hardcoded credentials (YAML/.env) now caught, entropy-gated so code

feat(person_memory): self-seeding person cards (0.3.0) (#219)

Slice 1 was read-only, so the adaptation layer only worked for people
someone had hand-written a markdown card for — which in practice meant
it adapted to nobody. The card set now maintains itself:

- Auto-seed on first contact from OBSERVED platform facts only (display
  name, id forms, first/last seen). Nothing about a person is inferred,
  so the machine never invents a socially loaded judgement about them.
  A first-time sender is recognized on their first turn, not their
  second, because the seed happens before the read.

- Self-learned id aliases. pre_llm_call supplies both id forms per turn
  (Signal carries a phone number AND an ACI UUID), so the plugin learns
  the mapping itself and records it on the card. This works for
  arbitrary senders; resolved-identities.json only ever covers
  admin-entered identities and so cannot cover a stranger in a group.
  It stays as a fallback.

- remember_person tool: the agent records what it LEARNS about how to
  talk to someone, instead of a human editing frontmatter.

Privacy and safety, since these fields are echoed into shared group
sessions: agent-written values are rejected if they contain anything
identifier-shaped (phone/email/UUID); the writable field set is an
allowlist; untrusted platform display names are stripped of control
characters and length-capped; ids live in the filename and the
non-injected alias_ids field. Writes are atomic (tmp+rename), gated on
actual content change (date-granular last_seen bounds this to one write
per person per day), and fail-open throughout. PERSON_MEMORY_READONLY=1
restores slice-1 behavior.

fix(deploy): correct the Google MCP wiring for newly created agents (#189)

* fix(deploy): make Google MCP actually work for newly created agents

A newly created agent's Google MCP could not start, for three independent
reasons. All three had to be wrong for the outage to be invisible, and all
three were.

1. GOOGLE_MCP_DIR defaulted only to ~/Documents/GitHub/google-multiplayer-mcp.
   The repo is commonly cloned as `google-mcp`, so the existsSync probe failed,
   googleMcpDir became undefined, and an operator who ticked "Google" in the
   wizard silently got no Google at all — no mount, no mcp_servers entry, no
   error. Now probes both names, and probes dist/index.js rather than the
   directory so an unbuilt checkout is caught too. When Google is enabled and
   nothing is found, the deploy now FAILS with the paths it looked at instead
   of shipping an agent whose integration does not exist.

2. The generated config pointed --config at /opt/google/config.yaml. Only
   /opt/google/tokens is bind-mounted, so that path never existed and the
   server exited 1 on readFileSync. Now points at
   /opt/data/google-permissions.yaml, inside the agent data dir mount.

3. Nothing wrote a Google permission config anywhere. HSM now generates one.

On (3), a security constraint shapes the default: in google-multiplayer-mcp an
EMPTY `folders` list means NO RESTRICTION (permissions.ts getAllowedFolders),
so emitting e.g. `drive: {access: write, folders: []}` would hand a brand-new
agent unscoped read/write over an entire Google account. The wizard collects no
folder IDs, so every service is generated at access: none, with a header
explaining that granting access requires listing folder IDs and how to run the
one-time OAuth flow. An optional googleIdentity in the request body lets an API
caller match an existing token file; it defaults to the agent slug.

Also creates the google-tokens dir at deploy time so it is owned by the
invoking user — letting Docker create the missing bind-mount source can leave
it root-owned, and the OAuth flow needs to write token JSON into it.

Separately, config.yaml now pins web.search_backend: brave-free. Leaving it
unset makes the runtime auto-detect from whichever API key happens to be
present, so the provider an agent searches with was a side effect of .env
contents rather than a decision — and it changed silently when a key was
added. Both creation paths share generateDefaultConfig, so the wizard and the
harness service both get it.

Tests: 12 new route-level integration tests running the real deploy logic and
its real fs writes against temp dirs — including that Google-off writes no
Google artifacts, and that every generated service defaults to none. Verified
non-vacuous: 9 of 12 fail against origin/main. 905 tests pass, typecheck clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address independent audit — no side effects on reject, and the
credentials/paths the server actually reads

BLOCKING (B1): the Google preflight ran AFTER mkdirSync(agentDataDir) and the
.env write, and returned from inside the try — so the catch's cleanup was
unreachable. Rejecting a deploy left a half-created agent dir containing the
resolved PLAINTEXT LLM key, and then 409'd every retry of that name forever;
recovery needed `rm -rf ~/.hermes-<slug>` from a shell with nothing in the UI
saying so. On the letta runtime it also orphaned an already-created brain agent,
which then 409'd by name too.

Moved the whole preflight above every side effect — above the LLM key
resolution and the letta branch, not merely above mkdir — which is the rule the
letta branch itself states ("before a single door byte is written"). A new test
asserts no dir, no docker start, no key-registry writes, and that the same name
is still deployable afterwards.

Three more from the audit, each the same class of bug this PR set out to fix —
a path or name that nothing on the other side reads:

- S4: GOOGLE_TOKEN_DIR was set nowhere, so the server fell back to
  $HOME/.nimbleco-google/tokens. With HOME=/opt/data the tokens landed
  somewhere the compose file never mounts deliberately, making the
  /opt/google/tokens mount dead weight. Now set explicitly.
- S2: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET were never provisioned, and HSM
  never writes ~/.nimbleco-google/config.json, so loadGlobalConfig() always
  threw and the OAuth flow was impossible regardless of scoping. Now written to
  the agent .env (from the request, else inherited from HSM's own env) and
  referenced from the mcp_servers env block.
- S5: googleIdentity was interpolated into YAML unvalidated. "a: b" broke the
  parse (MCP exits 1 — the exact regression this fixes) and a newline could
  inject permission entries past the deny-by-default. Now `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`.

Found while fixing the above, not in the audit: generateEnvContent wrote a
wizard-supplied Brave key as BRAVE_API_KEY only. The runtime reads exclusively
BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY (plugins/web/brave_free/provider.py, and the auto-detect
table in tools/web_tools.py); nothing reads BRAVE_API_KEY. So the key was
invisible to the agent, brave-free reported itself unavailable, and the
search_backend pin added in this PR would have fallen straight through to
auto-detect — inert. Both names are now written.

Also: N1 the probe now requires node_modules as well as dist/index.js (the
bundle imports bare googleapis/js-yaml, so a pruned checkout passed and exited
1 at runtime); N2 non-absolute GOOGLE_MCP_DIR is rejected (Docker reads a
relative volume source as a named volume, mounting an empty dir over the
bundle); N4 the 400 now carries ok: false like its neighbours; S3 the generated
OAuth runbook now passes GOOGLE_TOKEN_DIR and the client creds, without which
it hit EROFS on the read_only container.

Tests: 18 (was 12). Verified by mutation — reverting each of the six fixes
individually fails a test. 911 pass on the real tree, typecheck clean.

fix: HSM create-new + Signal first-run correctness (6 bugs) (#134)

* fix(wizard): remove redundant inline Signal phone field (double-ask)

The create-new wizard asked for the Signal number twice: an inline
Phone field in the Platforms step AND again in the register/connect
dialog. Worse, the inline field was non-functional — the actual bond
only fires when signalCaptured is set (by the dialog), so a number
typed only inline never connected. Drop the inline field so the number
is entered once, in the dialog (which already handles the
already-registered case). Review step now shows the captured number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(config): derive compression summary_model from provider catalog

The template hardcoded summary_model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview for
every agent regardless of provider — an invalid, provider-agnostic model
that crash-loops compression on non-Google agents. Derive it instead from
MODEL_CATALOG: the provider's fallback-tier entry, else its local-tier
entry, else the caller's fallbackModel/primaryModel, emitted in litellm
provider/model form keyed by the provider itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deploy): deliver github token as literal GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

The agent .env only wrote GITHUB_TOKEN, but the github MCP server reads
GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN. The compose sets that var via ${GITHUB_TOKEN}
interpolation, which resolves from the (empty) process env rather than the
env_file — so the token never reached the server. Also emit the token as a
literal GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN line, mirroring how the llm key is
written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tools): discover platform_toolsets + fix empty-tools discovery guard

Two causes of 'No tools found' for a freshly created agent:

1. harness.ts seeded overlay.tools:[] and used `overlay.tools ?? auto`;
   since [] ?? x === [], auto-discovery never ran. Mirror the models guard:
   use overlay.tools only when non-empty, else auto-discover.

2. tools.ts discovery read a top-level toolsets:/mcp_servers: block, but a
   generated config.yaml writes platform_toolsets: — so a plain agent
   surfaced nothing. Parse platform_toolsets and flatten its per-platform
   arrays into toolset entries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(signal): place host-proxy.conf before compose up (first-run mount bug)

The signal deploy route runs docker compose with cwd=~/.hermes-swarm, so
the compose's ./host-proxy.conf bind-mount resolves there — but the route
never copied the conf, so Docker auto-created it as an empty DIRECTORY and
the nginx mount failed ('not a directory') on every first-time setup.
Copy infra/signal-cli/host-proxy.conf into ~/.hermes-swarm before 'up',
and self-heal a previously auto-created directory. Guards that the conf
source ships and the compose mounts it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(signal): default bot's Signal profile name to the harness name on bond

Fresh registration via the wizard already sets the profile to the bot
name (harnessName -> defaultDisplayName -> verify). But bonding an
already-registered number kept its old/generic profile ('Hermes Agent').
Set the Signal profile given-name to the harness name during connect
(best-effort, doesn't fail the bond) so the agent shows up under the name
it was created with regardless of registration path.

* fix(review): deliver github token via env_file only + fix ollama summary prefix

Addresses independent-audit blockers:
- github: the compose 'environment: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=${GITHUB_TOKEN}'

feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable (#265)

* feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable

Per-repo copies of check_sanitization.py drifted apart, each missing a
protection another copy had. swarm-map becomes the one home: the
script, the union of every copy's self-tests, and a reusable workflow
(sanitization-gate.yml) other repos call pinned to a
sanitization-gate-v* tag. Each repo keeps only sanitize.config.json.

The canonical script merges the Matilde/osint-engine base (fail-closed
semantic layer, fork-PR honesty, match-scoped allowlist, broadest
detector set) with swarm-map's --diff scope, separated international
phones, public-IP and fiction-phone filters (now opt-in config), and
ASG's per-content verdict cache. It adds --check-config and
--require-config. The swarm-map-specific reviewer prompt moves out of
the script into swarm-map's own sanitize.config.json.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close audit bypasses in the gate

An audit of the canonical gate found silent skips that let a real
token pass. git C-quoted non-ASCII paths, so docs/café.md was never
found on disk; one non-UTF-8 byte made layer 1 skip a whole file; an
allow_substrings entry of "" or a skip_paths entry of "."/"**"
disabled layer 1 and was only checked under --check-config; and the
reusable workflow accepted pull_request_target, which scans the base
with the key exposed.

Paths now come from git with -z, a listed path missing from disk is a
hard failure (deletions are excluded from --diff), binaries are judged
by NUL bytes and text is decoded with replacement, structural config
validation runs on every gate run, and pull_request_target is refused.
The workflow docs now say consumers must make the check required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): stop config and encodings from disabling layer 1

A re-audit found the PR under review controlled its own rules and that
some files escaped layer 1 entirely. sanitize.config.json was read from
the PR head and could set deterministic.enabled false, narrow scope,
skip any path, or allow "sk-ant-" as a substring; and one NUL byte or
UTF-16 encoding skipped a file in both layers.

On pull_request the reusable workflow now scans with the base commit's
config (SANITIZE_CONFIG) and notices a config change. Layer 1 cannot be
disabled or narrowed, skip_paths accepts only test-fixture paths, and
allow entries match exactly (plus email-domain and /24 forms). Layer 1
decodes UTF-16/32, reads other NUL-bearing files as latin-1, and scans
symlink target strings. swarm-map's config drops scope and lists its
fixture files and exact known values instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): judge home-repo PRs with the base gate

In swarm-map the gate judged a PR with the PR's own script, so a PR
could weaken the gate that judged it. On pull_request the reusable
workflow now runs the judging steps with the base commit's script; the
PR's script is still exercised by the self-tests, and a notice says when
the script changed. The garden guild id leaves the allowlist: #266
moves it out of source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close round-3 audit gaps

Threat model, now written down: the gate stops accidental leaks by
trusted committers and their agents; required checks and CODEOWNERS
cover a malicious committer.

Layer 1 scans the union of the decoded text and the raw latin-1 bytes,
so a stray BOM cannot hide an ASCII token. skip_paths match by path
segment, never as bare string prefixes; inside them provider tokens and
private keys are still reported, and .env/.pem/.key/id_* files are
never skipped. The workflow no longer runs git fetch (it failed in
private repos without persisted credentials), refuses a gate_ref that
is not a release tag or full SHA, and swarm-map's caller drops its
paths filter so the check reports on every PR. Adds CODEOWNERS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): ship the workflow to consumers' self-tests

The self-tests now check the reusable workflow itself, but consumers'
sparse checkout of the gate left it out, so their self-test step
failed. Also drop a personal name from the threat model wording.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): catch JSON assignments and fleet provider tokens

Round-4 audit. Credential-assignment patterns required the separator
right after the key, so JSON ("api_key": "...") never matched; they
now allow a closing quote on the key, while template words, env-var
names and lowercase slugs stay quiet. Adds high-confidence patterns for
the fleet's providers (OpenRouter, Discord bot tokens and webhooks,
Telegram, Hugging Face, npm, GitLab, OpenAI project and service-account
keys), also reported inside fixture paths, as are JWTs. Card detection
now needs a real issuer prefix and length, so Discord snowflakes no
longer read as card numbers.

feat(runtime): put the Claude Agent SDK behind the door (#351)

* feat(runtime): teach the model route the Anthropic Messages format

The model route swapped the key, metered and capped only for a harness
that spoke the OpenAI chat format. It now has a second wire format,
Anthropic Messages, which is what the Claude Agent SDK speaks.

The placeholder is read from x-api-key and the real key goes out there.
Usage is read from the two events a stream reports it in, with cache
reads counted in full and cache writes counted twice, so the figure is
never less than the bill. A call for a tool the provider runs and bills
by the use is refused, since its cost is not in the usage figure. The
token-count call is answered by the route itself, as an estimate.

The scripted model speaks the same format when told to, and the shared
key check reads the key from whichever header the format puts it in.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(runtime): add a Claude Agent SDK shim behind the door

A third harness adapter. The shim drives one SDK session per door
session, starts it with exactly the tools the door offered, and puts
every tool call to the door first. The SDK runs some calls unasked by
default, so it is told to ask about each tool by name.

The SDK is not a dependency of the repo. It is handed to the shim as a
value, so CI runs the shared checks against a fake and a local run
points at a pinned install. Four checks are its own: a call it would
run unasked still waits, no built-in tool runs when none is offered,
rooms keep separate threads, and a direct message is not delivered.

Its traffic is watched by a proxy it is told to use, since no tripwire
can be loaded into a compiled program. The credential guard accepts a
placeholder and a local route under the two fixed names the SDK reads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): put the Claude Agent SDK in the sealed Docker cell

A third cell image holds the pinned SDK, installed from a lock file
with no install script run. The rig, the probe and the broken rigs are
the ones Pi and Letta Code use. The rig's entry now picks the adapter
by the harness it is told, and the probe knows which files of this
harness must not be writable.

The two checks that need a file in the cell have the harness make it,
so they run where the lab's side cannot write. The scripted model's
Anthropic side and the fake SDK each have tests of their own, which
pin the ways the real SDK is not careful: it runs some calls unasked,
and writes a failed model call where a reply goes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(lab): say what the Claude Agent SDK slice proves, and what it does not

The write-up for the third harness: what was built, each check and
its result, what about the real SDK needed special handling, what it
declares, the model route's second format, what its install pulls in,
and a paragraph on Anthropic's terms with what was not verified.

A one-turn run against a real provider is written for the day there is
a key. It needs an SDK folder and a key file. CI runs the same code
with a stand-in at each end. It has not been run for real.

The route also refuses a call that asks for the same model at another
price. Dependabot's update pull requests are switched off for the
folder that pins the SDK, as for Letta Code's. Tests were added for
the gaps a mutation run found.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): keep credential-shaped strings out of the new tests

The sanitize gate reads a URL with an @ in it as a login, and a quoted
value after a key header as a key. The guard tests that need such
strings now put them together from parts, as the older ones do. Lint
warnings in the new test files and the broken SDK wrapper are cleared.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): re-run Pi and Letta Code after the shared changes

Both were run again as a plain process and in the sealed Docker cell,
after the model route, the credential guard, the scripted model and
the shared key check changed. Pi passes 14 and 20, Letta Code 16 and
22, as before. Their four matrix files are from those runs.

The doc's row on what the cell sends is from the capture taken during
the final Docker run of the third harness.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): refuse a provider redirect instead of following it

The model route sent its calls with the HTTP client's default, which
follows a redirect. A client that follows one sends x-api-key on to
wherever it points: unlike Authorization, that header is not dropped
when a redirect leaves the host. So a provider (or anything answering
in its place) that replied 307 had the real key delivered to another
host, and a redirect to another path of the provider reached a call
the route does not meter.

A redirect is now refused with 502 and a receipt, nothing is charged,
and the key goes nowhere else. This holds for both wire formats.

A second test pins which request headers reach the provider: the ones
the format names and no other. A route that passed every header on
was not caught by any test before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): three ways the Claude SDK shim could leave a room mute

An audit of the adapter against the real SDK 0.3.325 found three, none
of them unsafe and none seen by a check.

The SDK has no write tool in its minimal mode: a shell, a read and an
edit are all it has there. The shim listed `Write` in its tool map and
the fake SDK had one, so a policy that allowed writing files had the
door offer it, the session reported other tools than it was started
with, and every turn ended in an error. `Write` is gone from the map
(the edit tool makes a new file), the fake has the real one's three
tools, and C4m drives each mapped tool with every class allowed.

The SDK waits far longer than the door: about three minutes of retries
on a refused model call, and more than nine on a model that says
nothing. The shim kept no deadline, so a room's later messages queued
behind a turn the door had given up on. It now keeps the turn's own
deadline, stops the session there, and does not start a turn whose
deadline passed while it waited. C1t drives a silent model.

Asked to pick up a transcript that is gone, the SDK ends the turn
without saying it started, and the shim asked for the same transcript
on every later turn. It now forgets one that cannot be picked up. A
turn that ends before the session said what it is gives no reply.

Two broken shims turn the two new checks red. The matrix files are
made again in the next commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): catch a Claude SDK missing a tool it claims

Three gaps a mutation pass on the Claude SDK slice left open, each
now with a test that fails on the mutated code.

- lacks-a-tool: an SDK that starts without its edit tool and says it
  has every tool it was given. Only C4m, which drives each mapped
  tool, can see it.
- A lab that never asked the credential guard passed every check.
  A test now gives a harness a credential-shaped value, under a name
  it named and under one it did not, and shows it is never started.
- A turn that ends with empty text is settled with no reply.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): stop a Claude SDK session that runs a tool unasked

The veto is a callback the SDK chooses to call. The pinned version
calls it for every tool it is told to ask about, but nothing made
that a promise at run time: an SDK that skipped it ran the tool and
the shim carried on as if nothing had happened. Only the version pin
and C4q, on the next full run, stood behind it.

The pump now keeps the id of every call the door was asked about. A
tool result for a call to a tool the session has, that was never put
to the door, means the SDK ran it on

Validate provider-credential presence before pushing model cascade to live agents (PUT /harnesses/:id/models) (#91)

* Validate model cascade against catalog in PUT /harnesses/:id/models

The PUT /api/harnesses/:id/models route wrote any model string into a
live agent's config.yaml and restarted it, with no validation. A bad /
unknown / empty model id could crash-loop a production agent.

Add validateCascadeEntries() in lib/model-catalog (catalog-as-truth) and
call it in the PUT route before any config write. Rejects with 400 +
the offending model id(s) when a catalogued, non-free-form provider
(anthropic / openai / google / bedrock) is given a model not in the
catalog, or when a model id is empty.

Leniency mirrors /suggest: free-form providers (ollama / openrouter /
custom) and any non-catalogued provider accept arbitrary model ids,
since the catalog is not authoritative for them and the UI offers a
free-text model field for exactly that case.

Covers both request shapes (legacy cascade+provider, and
fallback_providers[]). Adds unit tests for the validator and route
integration tests (valid passes, unknown rejected 400, free-form
allowed, empty rejected).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Validate provider-credential presence (not catalog membership) in PUT /models

Review rejected the catalog-membership approach: MODEL_CATALOG is a tiny
2-per-provider *suggestions* list, not an allowlist, so strict membership
would 400 legitimate in-use models (e.g. claude-opus-4-8, newer gemini/gpt).

What actually crash-loops an agent is pushing a model whose provider has no
configured credential for that agent (e.g. openrouter without OPENROUTER_API_KEY).
So validate provider-credential PRESENCE instead.

- KEEP the empty/missing model-id guard (the unambiguous crash case).
- DROP the strict MODEL_CATALOG membership check entirely.
- ADD readAgentEnvVarNames(dataDir) — reads the agent's .env var NAMES (never
  values) using the same parse semantics as keys.ts parseEnvFile.
- validateCascadeEntries now takes the agent's present env-var set and rejects
  an entry ONLY when its provider is DEFINITIVELY un-serviceable: provider needs
  a known single key, we know which env var, and it is absent. Enforced set is
  conservative: anthropic (API_KEY|TOKEN), openai, openrouter.
- FAIL OPEN on all uncertainty: ollama/custom need no key (always allowed);
  google/gemini have ambiguous auth modes (allowed); bedrock uses AWS multi-var
  creds / instance roles (allowed); unknown providers (nous, etc.) allowed.

Tests: replaced catalog-membership tests with credential-presence tests
(provider-with-key passes; provider-without-key 400s; ollama/custom pass;
unknown provider fails open; empty id 400s). Full suite green except the 4
pre-existing better-sqlite3 ABI failures in usage.test.ts.

* models validation: fail open on empty env-set (missing/unreadable .env)

A missing/unreadable agent .env yields an empty env-var set. The credential
check must NOT treat that as 'no credentials' and reject every enforced-provider
model — that's a worse false-reject than the bug being fixed. When the set is
empty, skip credential validation entirely (fail open); the empty-id guard
remains the floor. Verified guessDataDir co-locates .env with the config.yaml
the route already reads, so a non-empty set reliably reflects real keys.

upstream key and stamps every reply with the run's nonce.

fix(harness): prevent port-assignment collisions with .env-only agents (#155)

Root cause: nextAvailablePort scanned only per-agent compose files and
RUNNING docker containers. The monolithic `personal` agent lives at
~/.hermes, declares API_SERVER_PORT=8642 only in its own .env, and has no
compose file under composeBaseDir — so its port was invisible to the scan.
A new agent (cyborg) was handed 8642, and both failed with docker
"port is already allocated" when run together.

Fix — make the used-port scan comprehensive. Extract collectUsedPorts()
(exported, unit-testable) gathering ports from:
  1. per-agent compose files' published: ports (unchanged)
  2. docker ps -a (was `docker ps`) so STOPPED agents' ports count too
  3. NEW: every managed agent's .env API_SERVER_PORT (~/.hermes plus each
     ~/.hermes-<name> sibling) — the catch-all for the monolithic personal
     agent and any agent whose compose isn't under composeBaseDir

nextAvailablePort now takes an options object (composeBaseDir, reservedPorts,
injectable homeDir + dockerPorts for tests) and delegates to collectUsedPorts;
all three callers updated. Defensive throughout: missing dirs / .env /
unparseable values are skipped.

Tests (RGTDD, harness-port.test.ts): a port present ONLY in an agent .env is
treated as used and not reassigned (the exact cyborg↔personal bug); ports step
by PORT_STEP from BASE_PORT to the first free port; compose-file and mock-docker
ports still honored. Red before fix, green after; full lib/services suite green.

Prevents assignment-time collisions. Runtime auto-heal of agents that already
collide is a separate follow-on.

feat(packs): install git-sourced packs into existing agents (#267)

Base-package sync copies only local templates and skips git sources,
so a pack whose plugin lives in its own repo had no install path for
an agent that already exists.

Adds POST /api/harnesses/:id/artifacts/pack and installPackToDir:
fetch at the pinned tag, check the clone is the recorded commit,
trust-gate, copy, enable the plugin, stamp the pack, recreate.

- The agent must carry a base-package stamp. Without one its surface
  is unknown, and a private-only pack could reach a public agent.
- Git sources in the registry record the commit their tag was
  reviewed at; the fetch refuses a clone at any other commit.
- All or nothing: every artifact is fetched and gated into a staging
  dir before the agent's dir is touched, so a refused skill leaves no
  plugin behind. Staging and clone dirs are removed afterwards.
- Refused installs and failed restarts are written to the audit log.

Registers the papareo-transcription pack (papareo-transcribe v0.5.0
plugin + skill), private surfaces only.

layering: bring ONE shared Letta server up, then create each agent over REST —

`<name>.removed-<date>` or `<name>.bak`, was therefore reported as an
agent with an unknown build for as long as it existed.

The folder sweep now only counts a folder whose name gives an id the
API accepts (isValidHarnessId). A validly named folder with no registry
row and no container is still reported, and registry rows are never
filtered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(compose): add a process-count limit to generated agents

Generated agent services had memory and CPU limits but no limit on how
many processes they may hold, so a runaway spawn loop in one container
could fill the host's process table.

Both compose generators now write the same limit, 2048, from one shared
constant. It counts threads too, so it is set well above what an agent
with shells and a headless browser holds, and well below what a host
allows.

The limit is written as deploy.resources.limits.pids. docker compose
rejects a service-level pids_limit beside a deploy.resources.limits
block, which both generators already emit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ports): count host ports published on a single address

Port allocation read `docker ps` for bindings on 0.0.0.0 only, so a
port published with a host address (loopback or any other) was not
counted as used by that source.

The parsing now accepts any IPv4 or bracketed IPv6 host address and is
a small exported function with its own tests. This keeps the Docker
source working once generated agents publish their API port on
loopback.

Refs #231

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): publish the agent API port on loopback only

Both compose generators published the agent's API port without a host
address, so it listened on every interface of the host.

Everything that calls that port runs on the host itself: the
dashboard's post-deploy health check and the documented curl examples
both use localhost. The port is now published on 127.0.0.1, written
long-form with host_ip like the VNC and control ports, from one shared
constant.

Only newly generated or regenerated compose files change. Files already
on disk are not rewritten.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(settings): add apiBindHost to choose the agent API bind address

The agent API port is now published on loopback, with no way to choose
another address for an install that reaches agent APIs from other
machines.

apiBindHost is a setting beside vncBindHost and controlBindHost: same
storage, same validation (a string with no newline), set through
PUT /api/settings, default 127.0.0.1. Every place that writes a compose
file passes it to the generator: create, duplicate, import, the setup
wizard and the settings-driven regenerate, so a regenerate keeps the
configured address. An empty value falls back to loopback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(settings): require apiBindHost to be an IP address

apiBindHost accepted any string without a newline. Values such as
`[::1]`, `localhost` or `a: b` were written into the compose file as
host_ip and only refused by docker at `up`, after a regenerate had
already replaced a working file.

The setting now has to be a bare IPv4 or IPv6 address (net.isIP), or
empty for the default. The generators go through the same check at
render time (resolveApiBindHost) and write loopback for anything else,
so a stored value that predates the check is never emitted. The VNC and
control bind hosts keep their existing rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): quote the API bind address and refuse zone ids

An IPv6 address may end in a colon (`::`, `fe80::`, `2001:db8::`).
Written unquoted as host_ip, that is read as a YAML mapping key and
docker compose refuses the file. An address with a zone id
(`fe80::1%en0`) passed the IP check but is refused by docker as an
invalid address.

Both generators now write the API port's host_ip as a quoted string,
and the shared IP check refuses any value containing `%`, so a zone id
is refused by settings validation and written as loopback at render
time. The shared-VPN stash and restore keep the quoted line byte for
byte.

hits.message:
feat(token-broker): replace agent PATs with one-hour tokens (#283)

* feat(token-broker): add host-side GitHub App token broker

Agents should not hold the App key or a long-lived token. The broker keeps
the one key in a single 0600 file and mints a 1-hour installation token for
each agent on request, cached per agent and scope. An audit log records
events only, never values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(token-broker): roll an agent onto the broker one at a time

Add the rollout: back up .env outside the agent's mount, strip PATs and App
keys, enrol, recreate without building, then check git and gh as the agent
under its real HOME. Any failure restores the agent. It is a dry run by
default and prints names only. The registry example shows the scope format.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(token-broker): add one-command App key change

GitHub has no API to create App keys, so a person clicks Generate. ghkey
then takes the newest key from Downloads by pipe, has the broker prove it
with a test mint, swaps it atomically so nothing goes down, deletes the
local copy and prints the link to delete the old key. It holds that link
back while an agent still carries the old key. It also installs the broker
as a launch agent on the host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(keys): keep GitHub credentials off brokered agents

HSM rewrites .env on key resyncs, rotations and reassignments, which would
quietly undo a move to the token broker. An agent with the
.hsm-github-broker marker now refuses all of those. A duplicate no longer
inherits its source's broker secret, which would let it ask for tokens as
the source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(integrity): flag GitHub credentials in agent .env files

A PAT or App key that comes back on a brokered agent now fails on
/api/integrity, the harnesses page and the pm2 error log, with variable
names only. The same check says when the App key passes 90 days old.
Agents not yet moved show as pending, so a gradual rollout stays quiet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(token-broker): show repo owners before moving an agent

A PAT can reach repos outside the App's org and the broker can't, so moving
an agent off a PAT could cut it off from a repo it uses. The rollout now
lists the owners in the agent's checkouts first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(token-broker): explain the broker and why it uses a port

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): survive a typo in registry.json

Any request read the registry unguarded, so a trailing comma killed the
process, launchd restarted it, and the next request killed it again.
This held even for a wrong secret. A failed audit write did the same.

Keep serving from the last good copy, answer 503 if there has never been
one, and catch whatever else a request throws. Since the edit is then
silently not applied, the GitHub health check now goes red.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(harness): strip the broker identity on import

Duplicate already dropped github-broker.json and the marker. Import did
not, so an imported agent asked for tokens as its source, got the
source's scope, and the audit log blamed the source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): make the check and the strip agree

The check flagged credentials by value shape while the strip removed
only eight fixed names. A PAT under another name stayed in the agent
while the rollout printed OK, and the check's advice changed nothing.
A Google or SSH key looked like a GitHub failure no command could clear.

Strip every token-shaped line under any name, and count a private key
only under a name that says GitHub. Both sides now run through one table
of cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(integrity): make the GitHub check loud for every agent

An agent without the marker counted as pending, which raised no banner
and no log line. New deploys have no marker and could still be given a
PAT, so PATs could return unseen after rollout. CRLF lines, spaced
assignments, an unreadable .env, .env-old and a profile .env.bak all
reported ok.

Once a host has the broker, an unmarked agent holding a credential now
raises the banner and the log line. A deploy with a token is refused
there, and the rollout finds and strips everything the check looks at.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): never delete a stray .env copy

Copies were deleted on a wider test than the one deciding whether to back
up, so non-GitHub data could go for good while a failed roll printed
Restored. Even with a backup, ghkey purge would later lose those lines.

Strip copies in place like .env. Nothing is deleted, and a backup is made
whenever a strip will change a file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): restore only GitHub lines on undo and failed rolls

Undo and a failed roll wrote the whole old .env back, reporting success.
A key rotated or a line added since the roll was lost and the old value
returned, including anything written during the verify wait.

Merge the stripped lines back into the file as it is now. The rest of the
file wins, and so does a GitHub line set since. With no change since the
roll, the backup still comes back byte for byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): recover when a roll fails while editing files

Restore-on-failure only covered a failed recreate or verify. If an edit
threw, the agent stayed marked and enrolled with its .env stripped and
the container not recreated, and she got a raw stack trace.

Any failure now puts the agent back and says why. If that also fails, the
backup is kept and the message names the undo command. An unreadable .env
blocks up front, and undo reports failure instead of throwing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(token-broker): build fake key headers at runtime

The sanitization gate reads a literal private-key header as a real key
and would fail these fixtures in CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): undo through every backup, not just the newest

A re-roll backs up only what is in .env at that moment. If a credential
came back and the agent was rolled again, the newest backup held just
that line, so undo took the agent off the broker without its original
key or PAT and still reported success.

Undo now merges all of an agent's unused backups, newest first. It then
moves them to used/, kept until purge, so a later undo can't bring back
a line removed after this one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): find repo owners at any depth

The owner scan is the guard that stops an agent losing repos outside the
App's org, and it stopped at depth 4, so /opt/data/home/repos/foo was
invisible and the dry run looked clean. xargs also split paths on spaces.

It now searches all of /opt/data, skipping dependency trees and git
objects, and says so when the scan itself failed instead of showing no
owners.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): remove a PAT from git and gh login files

A .git-credentials line not in the x-access-token form, or a hosts.yml
from gh auth login, survived the move: roll said OK, the check said ok,
and the dry run showed neither file. gh then ran on the PAT rather than a
broker token.

The rollout now shows, backs up, strips and restores those files, in the
tool and gateway HOME of each profile. Verify fails unless gh is really
on a broker token. The check flags a return of either file, naming the
file only. Boot still leaves foreign files alone, since it has no backup
to undo from.

feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable (#265)

* feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable

Per-repo copies of check_sanitization.py drifted apart, each missing a
protection another copy had. swarm-map becomes the one home: the
script, the union of every copy's self-tests, and a reusable workflow
(sanitization-gate.yml) other repos call pinned to a
sanitization-gate-v* tag. Each repo keeps only sanitize.config.json.

The canonical script merges the Matilde/osint-engine base (fail-closed
semantic layer, fork-PR honesty, match-scoped allowlist, broadest
detector set) with swarm-map's --diff scope, separated international
phones, public-IP and fiction-phone filters (now opt-in config), and
ASG's per-content verdict cache. It adds --check-config and
--require-config. The swarm-map-specific reviewer prompt moves out of
the script into swarm-map's own sanitize.config.json.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close audit bypasses in the gate

An audit of the canonical gate found silent skips that let a real
token pass. git C-quoted non-ASCII paths, so docs/café.md was never
found on disk; one non-UTF-8 byte made layer 1 skip a whole file; an
allow_substrings entry of "" or a skip_paths entry of "."/"**"
disabled layer 1 and was only checked under --check-config; and the
reusable workflow accepted pull_request_target, which scans the base
with the key exposed.

Paths now come from git with -z, a listed path missing from disk is a
hard failure (deletions are excluded from --diff), binaries are judged
by NUL bytes and text is decoded with replacement, structural config
validation runs on every gate run, and pull_request_target is refused.
The workflow docs now say consumers must make the check required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): stop config and encodings from disabling layer 1

A re-audit found the PR under review controlled its own rules and that
some files escaped layer 1 entirely. sanitize.config.json was read from
the PR head and could set deterministic.enabled false, narrow scope,
skip any path, or allow "sk-ant-" as a substring; and one NUL byte or
UTF-16 encoding skipped a file in both layers.

On pull_request the reusable workflow now scans with the base commit's
config (SANITIZE_CONFIG) and notices a config change. Layer 1 cannot be
disabled or narrowed, skip_paths accepts only test-fixture paths, and
allow entries match exactly (plus email-domain and /24 forms). Layer 1
decodes UTF-16/32, reads other NUL-bearing files as latin-1, and scans
symlink target strings. swarm-map's config drops scope and lists its
fixture files and exact known values instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): judge home-repo PRs with the base gate

In swarm-map the gate judged a PR with the PR's own script, so a PR
could weaken the gate that judged it. On pull_request the reusable
workflow now runs the judging steps with the base commit's script; the
PR's script is still exercised by the self-tests, and a notice says when
the script changed. The garden guild id leaves the allowlist: #266
moves it out of source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close round-3 audit gaps

Threat model, now written down: the gate stops accidental leaks by
trusted committers and their agents; required checks and CODEOWNERS
cover a malicious committer.

Layer 1 scans the union of the decoded text and the raw latin-1 bytes,
so a stray BOM cannot hide an ASCII token. skip_paths match by path
segment, never as bare string prefixes; inside them provider tokens and
private keys are still reported, and .env/.pem/.key/id_* files are
never skipped. The workflow no longer runs git fetch (it failed in
private repos without persisted credentials), refuses a gate_ref that
is not a release tag or full SHA, and swarm-map's caller drops its
paths filter so the check reports on every PR. Adds CODEOWNERS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): ship the workflow to consumers' self-tests

The self-tests now check the reusable workflow itself, but consumers'
sparse checkout of the gate left it out, so their self-test step
failed. Also drop a personal name from the threat model wording.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): catch JSON assignments and fleet provider tokens

Round-4 audit. Credential-assignment patterns required the separator
right after the key, so JSON ("api_key": "...") never matched; they
now allow a closing quote on the key, while template words, env-var
names and lowercase slugs stay quiet. Adds high-confidence patterns for
the fleet's providers (OpenRouter, Discord bot tokens and webhooks,
Telegram, Hugging Face, npm, GitLab, OpenAI project and service-account
keys), also reported inside fixture paths, as are JWTs. Card detection
now needs a real issuer prefix and length, so Discord snowflakes no
longer read as card numbers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(surface-admins): match an id to exactly one agent (#331)

* fix(surface-admins): match an id to exactly one agent

The surface admin store looked an agent up two ways: the stored row by
id, and the agent's data dir by a looser rule that accepts several
spellings of the same name. The two could disagree about which agent an
id meant, and a write for an id with no stored row added a new row for
it.

Every function now resolves the id once, to one agent, and uses that
agent's id for everything after: the admin list, the .env, the audit
entry and the container recreate. An id names an agent by its stored id
or its bare slug. Any other id is treated as no agent: reads return no
admins and no allowed groups, setAdmins and approveGroupInvite return
404, and nothing is written.

setAdmins no longer adds rows itself. An agent with no stored row yet
(a discovered container) is saved through HarnessService, and only when
HarnessService lists that id. The admins and groups routes recreate the
resolved agent instead of the id from the URL.

Tests cover each function and each route against the real service, with
the actor check asserted before any write.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* fix(surface-admins): resolve the agent before a group invite is saved

approveGroupInvite appends a group to an agent's .env. For an id with a
stored row that agent is the row. For an id with no row it now has to be
an agent HarnessService lists (a discovered container), the rule
setAdmins already applies; otherwise the answer is 404 and nothing is
written. The lookup runs only after the invite has passed the policy
and admin check, so a refused invite costs no Docker discovery.

Tests also pin the agent shapes found on a running fleet, each called
by slug and by stored id: a stored row with a name, a stored row whose
name is null, and a running agent with no stored row. All keep their
admins, their group checks and their group-invite approval.

feat(compose): shared gluetun vpn for deploy-born agents (#280)

* feat(compose): shared gluetun vpn for deploy-born agents

Add a sharedVpn setting that puts an agent inside one shared gluetun
container's network namespace, so every VPN'd agent exits through a
single Mullvad device while the host stays off VPN.

The toggle is a surgical, exactly-reversible edit of the hermes
service's networking lines (ports and extra_hosts stashed as comments,
network_mode added, API_SERVER_PORT pinned to the agent's own port so
agents in one namespace cannot collide). Deploy-born hardening is never
re-rendered, so the #204 regeneration guard stays intact. Both compose
generators accept sharedVpn and emit the same bytes as the toggle, so a
regeneration keeps the VPN; a hand-made network_mode makes a regen
refuse instead of silently dropping it.

Swarm-map writes the shared gluetun compose and starts it with
up --no-recreate (recreating it would cut off every joined agent). The
WireGuard key file is only referenced, never read or generated. The
settings version now fingerprints the shared-VPN state so a stale
whole-document PUT cannot revert it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): harden shared vpn after adversarial review

- Deploy route now allocates ports with the shared scan (compose files,
  docker ps -a, agent .env, overlay ports) instead of running
  containers only, which missed every shared-VPN agent and re-handed
  its port.
- Comments at any indent no longer end the service or a stashed key;
  stashed lines are kept raw so turning off is exact. Keys forbidden
  with network_mode: container (hostname, dns, expose, links, ...) are
  refused.
- The API port check no longer emulates hermes' env/config precedence
  (it differs across versions, and hermes reloads .env over the compose
  pin). Every source that names a port must agree with the agent's port.
  Fixed-port platforms (webhook, msgraph_webhook, a2a, teams) are
  refused.
- Compose writes recheck the settings version, so an in-flight stale
  PUT cannot undo a toggle. The transformed compose is validated with
  docker compose config -q. Docker errors are never echoed, since they
  can quote env_file lines (the WireGuard key).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): close shared vpn listener and multi-service gaps

- Fixed-port listeners are now also detected when switched on from env
  alone (webhook, msgraph_webhook, teams, bluebubbles, whatsapp_cloud,
  dashboard). bluebubbles and whatsapp_cloud are added to the list.
- Inline or unusual config.yaml forms are reported as unreadable and
  refused instead of being read as off. Quoted booleans are understood.
- The agent's port is read from its own service, and turning the VPN
  off checks markers only within that service, so files holding more
  than one agent work.
- An existing shared gluetun compose is never overwritten. It may carry
  operator edits, and drift from the running container would make the
  next `up` recreate gluetun.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): allowlist shared vpn listeners, read config like hermes

- Inside one namespace, whatsapp's local bridge lets a second agent
  attach to the first agent's bridge, and other platforms open fixed

  The hermes service's compose environment, where extraEnv lands, is

  agent's service.

fix(api): resolve every agent id through one shared step (#332)

* fix(surface-admins): match an id to exactly one agent

The surface admin store looked an agent up two ways: the stored row by
id, and the agent's data dir by a looser rule that accepts several
spellings of the same name. The two could disagree about which agent an
id meant, and a write for an id with no stored row added a new row for
it.

Every function now resolves the id once, to one agent, and uses that
agent's id for everything after: the admin list, the .env, the audit
entry and the container recreate. An id names an agent by its stored id
or its bare slug. Any other id is treated as no agent: reads return no
admins and no allowed groups, setAdmins and approveGroupInvite return
404, and nothing is written.

setAdmins no longer adds rows itself. An agent with no stored row yet
(a discovered container) is saved through HarnessService, and only when
HarnessService lists that id. The admins and groups routes recreate the
resolved agent instead of the id from the URL.

Tests cover each function and each route against the real service, with
the actor check asserted before any write.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* fix(harness): check a new agent's name before writing anything

Import and deploy make a new agent from a name. Both found out the name
was already a stored agent's only at the last step, when the row is
registered, after the data dir had been copied or scaffolded and the
.env patched.

HarnessService.nameTaken(name) answers from the stored rows whether a
name (as its slug, or the id built from it) is in use. importFromDir
asks it before the copy, the import route answers 409 from it, and the
deploy route answers 409 from it before its first write. The import
route also refuses a name or dataDir that is not a string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* fix(api): resolve every agent id through one shared step

Routes that take an agent id each did their own thing with it. Some
looked the agent up, some turned the id straight into a data dir, and
the routes that take ids in a request body (a key's assignedTo) did
neither.

lib/harness-ref.ts is now the one step. invalidHarnessId() checks the
shape (400). requireHarness() also resolves the id to the agent listed
under exactly that id (404). refuseUnknownHarnesses() does the same for
a list from a request body, keeping ids the record already holds.

- Every handler under /api/harnesses/[id] calls it first: the shape
  check on reads, the full resolve on anything that changes something.
- /api/keys POST and PUT resolve assignedTo before a key is stored or a
  .env is written. KeysService also checks the shape of every agent
  reference at add, setAssignment, rotateValue and writeKeyToEnv.
- Cascade apply and model-update apply resolve the body's harnessId
  first. The Signal PIN routes check its shape.
- Pairing DELETE accepts only a known platform name.

app/api/harness-id-sweep.test.ts walks every route file. Each must be
classified (id in the URL, id in the body, new-agent name, or no agent
id), and each one that takes an id must refuse a malformed or unknown
one before any service call or file write. A new route fails the sweep
until it is classified.

The three surfaces/[platform] routes keep resolving through
SurfaceAdminService, which accepts the bare slug agents send and reads
only the stored rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* fix(surface-admins): resolve the agent before a group invite is saved

approveGroupInvite appends a group to an agent's .env. For an id with a
stored row that agent is the row. For an id with no row it now has to be
an agent HarnessService lists (a discovered container), the rule
setAdmins already applies; otherwise the answer is 404 and nothing is
written. The lookup runs only after the invite has passed the policy
and admin check, so a refused invite costs no Docker discovery.

Tests also pin the agent shapes found on a running fleet, each called
by slug and by stored id: a stored row with a name, a stored row whose
name is null, and a running agent with no stored row. All keep their
admins, their group checks and their group-invite approval.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* test(api): cross-check the body fields each route reads

The route sweep knew which body fields carry an agent id only from its
own table, so a handler could start reading an id under a new field
name without the sweep noticing.

The sweep now reads every handler's source for the fields it takes from
a parsed JSON body or the query string, and each route's set must equal
what is declared for it: the id fields in BODY_ID (each swept on its
own) plus OTHER_FIELDS. A new field fails the sweep until it is
declared one way or the other. Handlers that pass the body on whole are
listed with where it goes, and id-like names declared as something else
each carry a reason.

Also: the key resync route checks the shape of the ids in `harnesses`
and joins the swept routes, and nameTaken's match on a stored name
(a row whose id was built from an earlier name) has its own tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* test(api): keep route bodies to the one form the sweep reads

The sweep's field reader follows `body = await request.json()` and a
destructuring of the same call. A handler that took its body any other
way (a clone, text, form data, the raw stream, or a parsed body under
another variable name) was not followed, so its fields were not
compared with the declared set.

The sweep now fails for a route file that reads the request body in
any form other than those two.
