feat(door): read the web through the door, by allowlist or the public web, with search (#359)

* feat(door): fetch allowlisted web pages through the door

The cell still has no route out. A web_fetch call is decided like any
tool, and its address is put to the web allowlist (egress.hosts). The
door fetches the page itself: GET only, no credentials, every DNS answer
and redirect re-checked against the list and against private ranges,
with size, time and rate limits. The page goes to the model only, marked
as untrusted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(door): let read-only shell commands run without a yes

A shell that asks for every ls is a shell nobody leaves on. The record
can now hold two lists of command names. The door reads each shell call
whole with a small reader of its own: a command made only of names on
the allow list, writing nothing, runs with no request; anything with a
blocked name or a clearly destructive part, wherever it sits, never
runs; everything else asks exactly as before, bound to its hash.

Shipped lists, editable in the launcher config and the Tools card. A
shell, an interpreter or a wrapper can never be allowed. Receipts name
the rule that decided, never the command. New check K1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(conformance): check web through the door for every harness with tools

Seven web checks (N1+, N1 to N6) run against a fake web on loopback with a
fake DNS. Five rigs break the door's fetcher or allowlist check one way
each, and a gate whose web tool skips the door, to show each check can go
red.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): read a wrapper past its own options before blocking

The block search tried every word after a wrapper as a command, so
`xargs grep curl` was blocked as curl. It now skips the wrapper's own
options and values, and reads `su -c` and `env -S` strings as commands.
Adds the tests five surviving mutants showed were missing: a redirect
through `..`, `sh -lc`, upper-case names, a command on a non-shell
tool, and a record whose lists are not valid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(door): web allowlist in the launcher config and the Tools card

tools.web.allow lists hosts or host/path prefixes; empty means off.
The card offers suggested sites as one-click chips, none on by default.
An agent that hears anyone keeps the web, read-only and allowlisted.
Search is written down as a design and not built.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(door): close the gaps hand mutations found in the web checks

A no from an admin, or a turn that is over, leaves no ticket to fetch.
Escaped slashes under an allowed prefix, non-GET methods at the list
itself, and an early stop at the body limit each now have a test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(door): keep web fixtures clear of the sanitization gate

The fake web hands out IPv6 addresses only, credentials in test
addresses are too short to look like secrets, and the three IANA
special-purpose blocks the fetcher refuses are allowlisted by prefix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(conformance): record K1 from real Pi, Letta Code and Claude SDK runs

Matrices regenerated from real runs of all three harnesses, as a
process and in the Docker cell. K1 passes for Pi and is listed as not
run for the two harnesses whose shims cannot hold a call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(door): add the public web mode and Brave web search through the door

tools.web.mode 'public' reads any public address (egress.default
'public'), with every other check unchanged. tools.web.search turns on
web_search: the door calls Brave with a key read from a 0600 file whose
path sits with the record's other secret paths. Results come back as
untrusted titles, addresses and snippets; a result is fetchable only if
the mode allows it. Searches have their own hourly count, and receipts
hold the query length and result count. Both are off by default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(conformance): record the web checks in all six matrices

Rewritten by real runs: Pi 1.5.2 passes the ten web checks as a process
and in the sealed cell; Letta Code and the Claude Agent SDK list them
as not run, with the tools' reason, and pass what they passed before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): keep commands that skip the yes inside the scratch folder

An allowed command could read anything in the cell with no yes:
`cat /proc/1/environ` showed the cell token, and `cat` of the
sessions folder showed other people's conversations. A file tool
cannot reach either, so an allowed command now cannot: a full path,
`..`, a path fixed to an option or `--files0-from` makes it ask.

`seq inf` ran with no yes and its output filled the cell's memory
until Docker killed the whole cell, so seq counts to five digits.
`date --se=` is `--set`, and a redirection to /dev/tcp or /dev/udp
opens a socket, so the first asks and the second never runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pi): refuse the shell when Pi's settings add to each command

Pi reads shellCommandPrefix and shellPath from its own folder and
from .pi/settings.json in the scratch folder when it starts. A prefix
runs before every command, unseen by the door, which only read the
command. One earlier yes that wrote such a file turned every later
allowed `ls` into anything; a run in the cell image showed `ls`
copying the cell token out. The gate now refuses every shell call
while either setting is present, and for the rest of that Pi's life
once it has seen one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): a public agent reads the public web only with a yes

An agent that hears anyone could have the public web with no
approval. Then anyone in the room could send the door, from the
operator's own address, to any public address, and put what the
agent knows into the address. The launcher now refuses that config,
and decide() says no to a network call from a public agent under the
public web unless the class asks. The allowlist is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): limit the Internet Archive chip to its archived pages

The chip listed web.archive.org whole. Its /save/<address> path has
the archive fetch any address, query and all, so one click turned the
allowlist into the whole web. The chip now lists web.archive.org/web.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): write the refused address blocks as octets

The sanitize check failed on this branch from its first push. It runs
with main's trusted config, so the allowance this branch added to
sanitize.config.json for 192.0.0., 192.88.99. and 198.18.0. never
applies, and those blocks in the fetcher's refusal list read as
public hosts. Writing them as octets leaves the list unchanged and
the check clean under main's config.

fix(compose): run agents and /state under the host uid (#368)

* fix(compose): populate HERMES_UID/HERMES_GID from the process owner in generated deploys

hermes-agent-mt's image bakes useradd -u 10000 hermes and only remaps
that uid when HERMES_UID/HERMES_GID are set (s6 stage2 hook); upstream's
own compose documents HERMES_UID=$(id -u) HERMES_GID=$(id -g). Swarm
Map never set either, so on a native Linux bind mount any agent whose
data dir is not owned by 10000 crash-loops with 'SessionStore SQLite
handle unavailable' while the container reports Up.

Emit HERMES_UID/HERMES_GID in the plain and VPN generators' environment
blocks and in the deploy path's generated .env (env_file reaches the
container environment, so stage2 reads it there too), taken from the
Swarm Map process uid/gid with a 10000 fallback. Also reserve the two
names in RESERVED_EXTRA_ENV_NAMES so extraEnv cannot clobber them.

Fixes #274.

* fix(state-init): chown /state to the agent's runtime uid, not the bind mount's owner

state-init set /state's owner by copying /opt/data's apparent owner. On
macOS (VirtioFS, OrbStack/Docker Desktop) that isn't the gateway's uid,
so every container recreate left /state root-owned and SQLite failed
with "attempt to write a readonly database". On Linux a fresh data dir
belongs to the host user until hermes's first boot, so new agents could
hit the same thing.

Resolve the owner the way the image's stage2 does instead: HERMES_UID /
HERMES_GID (or the PUID/PGID aliases) from extraEnv, else the agent .env
(read with sed, never sourced), else the image's hermes user, else
10000. Chown recursively and after migration, so migrated DBs and their
-wal/-shm siblings are covered. A failed chown warns but stays non-fatal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit d151175d4497f26c195819d1c19e3f3e30eea941)

* fix(state-init): chown /state to the uid the gateway is remapped to

With HERMES_UID/HERMES_GID now set on the hermes service, the
state-init service must see the same values, or it falls back to the
image's baked uid and leaves /state owned by a different user than the
gateway runs as. Pass the generated remap lines to the init service in
both generators, and give the new real-sh ownership tests the same 30s
timeout as the other real-sh block.

Co-authored-by: Miles Thompson <utunga@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Agent <agent@lorentz.is>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): keep the uid range and extraEnv in step with the image

The image's stage2 hook remaps the gateway only to ids 1-65534. The
init script accepted any non-zero id, and the generators wrote the
host id whatever it was, so a host id above that range left /state
owned by a user the gateway does not run as. Both now use the same
range and fall back to the image default outside it.

HERMES_UID/HERMES_GID are written by Swarm Map now. An agent whose
extraEnv already holds the same values keeps regenerating; a different
value is refused with a message that says to remove it.

feat(door): put one door agent in more than one Discord channel (#363)

* feat(policy): let a room hear anyone and narrow tools per room

A policy can now give one room rules of its own. A room rule may set
`anyone`: anyone who can post there is heard as a guest, always by

hears anyone and whether it keeps the agent's tools, the web only, or
none. Admins, the people heard and the monthly budget stay shared.

Each channel becomes a room in the policy, the connector may post only
in the listed channels, and notes stay per room. The dashboard's Rules

hits.message:
harness: dry-run backfill for compose mounts that extraMounts does not record (#224)

16 bind mounts across 8 fleet agents live only in their generated compose
files. Nothing in harnesses.json records them, so the only thing standing
between them and a silent disappearance is isDeployBornCompose() — a substring
test for 'google-multiplayer-mcp' / '/opt/google/tokens' / 'read_only: true',
consulted at exactly ONE call site (the settings PUT, and only when the VPN
toggle or the resource limits change). Any other regeneration path, any rename
of a container path, or any relaxation of that 409 drops them, and the container
comes back healthy with a capability gone. That is how the iris gate-intake
mounts were lost once already (#222).

Per agent (all 8 the same shape: the google-mcp checkout ro, the token dir rw):

  cryptids, cyborg, mare, matilde, nimbleco, osint, personal
      /Users/juni/Documents/GitHub/google-mcp -> /opt/google-multiplayer-mcp:ro
      <agent data dir>/google-tokens          -> /opt/google/tokens:rw
  egregore
      /Users/juni/Documents/GitHub/google-mcp -> /opt/google-mcp:ro   (different target)
      /Users/juni/.hermes-egregore/google-tokens -> /opt/google/tokens:rw

Adds scripts/backfill-extra-mounts.mjs. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: it prints the
per-agent plan and an LCS diff of harnesses.json and exits without writing.
--apply is the only thing that writes, and it backs up first, verifies the
backup byte-for-byte, and replaces the file by atomic rename. It touches no
compose file and no container.

Three decisions worth naming:

  The mode trap. Docker's short-syntax default for `- /host:/container` is rw;
  ExtraMount.mode's default is ro. A backfill that copies a mount without an
  explicit mode therefore flips /opt/google/tokens to read-only on the next
  regeneration, and OAuth refresh starts failing for reasons nobody connects
  back to the backfill. The script always writes mode explicitly and says so
  whenever the mode came from docker's default rather than the file.

  Refuse, never skip. Anything the compose reader will not vouch for — long
  syntax, a stray key inside volumes:, an unparseable spec, an overlay that
  disagrees with the compose, an overlay already targeting /opt/data or /state —
  is a refusal that stops the whole run. A mount quietly ignored by a tool whose
  job is to stop mounts being quietly ignored would be the same bug again.

  It never invents an overlay entry. The three seraph agents have unbacked
  mounts and no harnesses.json entry at all; they are reported and skipped. An
  id that matches no discovered agent is inert, and a wrong one attaches
  another agent's host paths.

The tests check the load-bearing claim by content, not by shape: they feed the
planner's own output to the real generateStandaloneCompose and assert each
mount renders — and assert that without the backfill the same regeneration
drops both. One test exists purely to record what this does NOT fix:
extraMounts carries mounts and only mounts, so read_only/tmpfs, security_opt,
extra published ports and the environment: block of a deploy-born compose are
still lost on regeneration. Backfilling is not a licence to relax the 409.

Runbook (plan / apply / three-way verify / one-line rollback) is in the file
header. Nothing has been run against the live host.

hits.message:
harness: extraMounts/extraEnv survive compose regeneration (#222)

## What

- `extraMounts` / `extraEnv` survive compose regeneration, so hand-added mounts are no longer silently severed by an unrelated settings change.
- Carries them through the **discovered-container** projection, not just the overlay-only path — without this the fix did not reach any running agent, which is every agent it was written for.
- Duplicating an agent no longer copies the source's `extraMounts` onto the duplicate.
- Settings validation moved to the top of the handler: a bad mount path is a 400 with nothing written, instead of a 500 after the `.env` and overlay had already landed.
- Adds tilde expansion for host paths, a reserved-name denylist for `extraEnv`, and excludes stale nested `.wt-*` worktrees from vitest.

## Why

The Iris approval-gate mounts were hand-added to a *generated* compose file, so any settings change would silently sever the agent from the gate that decides what it is allowed to publish. That already happened once.

The first version of this change did not actually close it. `services.harness.get(id)` for a running agent returned `extraMounts: undefined`, because only the undiscovered path carried them — so the next VPN or resources PUT regenerated a compose without the mounts, which is the original bug. Nothing caught it: the unit test exercised the pure function, and the route test mocked the generator away.

It also opened a worse hole. `duplicateOverlay` generated the duplicate's compose without extras and then spread `{...source}`, handing the duplicate rw access to the **source's** host paths. For iris that is the approval-gate spool — a duplicate could write into the gate that decides what gets published, with no UI surfacing it.

## Verification

- 101 files, 1166 tests, green. `npx vitest run`. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Each fix was proven load-bearing by reverting just its hunk and confirming the new test goes red — including the discovered-projection fix, which fails with `expected undefined to deeply equal [ { …(4) } ]` and a regenerated compose missing the spool mount.
- The hollow tests were repaired at the source, not patched around: `settings/route.test.ts` previously replaced the whole `harness-compose` module, so deleting the two forwarding lines left the suite green. It now uses `importActual` and asserts on the options object actually reaching the generator.
- The stale-worktree claim was verified by reverting the vitest exclude: 33 failures, all inside `.wt-*` directories, none in this tree.

## Risk

**Observable behavior change:** pre-write validation is unconditional, so an agent whose persisted `extraMounts` are malformed now gets a 400 on *every* settings PUT, where before a non-regenerating PUT succeeded. Deliberate — 400-with-nothing-written beats 500-with-half-written — but reviewers should see it stated.

**No migration exists.** `extraMounts` is only ever read from the `harnesses.json` overlay. Mounts that live only in a hand-edited compose file are still dropped on the next PUT until someone writes them into the overlay. That is a deployment step, not a code gap.

## Links

Root cause context in `memory/handoffs/2026-08/06-juniper-iris-gate-intake-publish-plan.md`.

Follow-ups deliberately out of scope: no collision/dedupe rule between `extraMounts` and the generated `/opt/data` and `/state` targets; `generateAgentCompose` has no `extraMounts` parameter, so deploy-born agents cannot receive them at all.

hits.message:
feat(runtime): add door agents from a form, and run Letta Code behind a door (#350)

* feat(runtime): let the door launcher run Letta Code as well as Pi

The launcher put Pi in the cell and nothing else. The harness is now a
setting of the config: `"harness": "letta-code"` picks Letta Code's
shim, its cell image and what it declares about itself. A config with
no `harness` key is a Pi config, read and rendered as before, so the
command, the config keys and the state folder are unchanged for an
agent that already runs from it.

The dry run names the harness, the one version that is pinned and
what it cannot do. Letta Code keeps one memory for the whole agent,
so it has one room only; the door already enforces that, and the dry
run now says it.

Letta Code is told what Pi is told, in place of its own system
prompt. It adds starting notes of its own after that text, so the
text ends by saying what those notes are.

A start no longer depends on the cell dialling after the door is
listening: a cell that dialled too early is started again once, by
name, and looked at again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(runtime): make Letta Code door agents from the dashboard

Creating a door agent now takes a harness and one line about what
the agent is for, and Letta Code is accepted. The record's harness
is fixed when the agent is made: the launcher's config is rendered
with it, an edit of the rules cannot change it, and a Pi agent's
config is written exactly as before.

The name rule moves to one plain function that the server and the
create form both call, so the form can say a name is taken while it
is typed. The server's answer is still the one that counts.

The agent view now carries which harness is in the cell, the one
version that is pinned and what it cannot do, and who started the
door that is running: this page, a supervisor, or something else.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(ui): add door agents from a form, and say more on their page

"Add door agent" opened the browser's own prompt. It is now a small
dialog: a name checked while it is typed, a choice of Pi or Letta
Code with what each cannot do, one line of description, and what
has to be done by hand with a link to the runbook. A new agent's
page opens on its Rules tab.

Remove and Stop for a door agent ask in the app's confirm dialog,
on the fleet page and on the agent's page. Nothing in the door
agent pages uses a browser pop-up.

The Overview names the harness and its pinned version, says when
the cell's seal was last checked or that it never was, and says who
started a running door. For Letta Code the Rules tab says, beside
the channel, that it has that one room only. The sidebar no longer
names one harness under the app's name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): start the cell again when it has not reached the door

The launcher starts the cell before the door is listening, so the
cell can be looked at from outside first. The relay takes the cell's
dial whether or not the door is there yet, and a cell that said
hello to nobody does not dial again. Which came first was a matter
of milliseconds.

A cell that has not reached the door three seconds after the door is
up is now stopped, the door is given time to drop any link it held,
and the cell is started again and checked from outside again. Both
launcher suites start a door this way on purpose.

The dashboard also forgets which process it started once that door
is stopped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): fail a start whose door still holds a stopped cell's link

When a cell is started again, the door is given up to five seconds
to see the stopped cell's link close. If it had not, the start went
on, and the wait that followed read the old link as the cell that
came back: a start with no cell behind it could be called live.
That start now fails, and nothing is left running.

The step is now one function that is handed the door, Docker and
the clock, so its waits are tested to the millisecond with no
sleeping: once and no more, the seal looked at again before the
wait, and every way it can fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): read a door agent written before the harness setting

The fixtures are the record, config, start script, fleet row, dry
run and run on record of a Pi door agent, written by the code as it
was before a harness could be named. The test shows nothing needs
migrating: the agent is listed and reported as it was, the old
config is still a Pi config with the same policy hash, and what is
rendered from the old record is byte for byte what was rendered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ui): say only what is known about who started a door

A running door that Swarm Map has no note of starting was said to be
started by "not this page". A door the page started before that note
was kept is shown the same way, so the flat statement could be
false. It now says there is no note and that no supervisor was seen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): stop the cell with the flag every Docker takes

The cell is stopped with `docker stop --time 1` before it is started
again. Docker no longer lists `--time`, only `-t` and `--timeout`,
and a Docker that drops the old spelling would fail every start
that needs the cell started again. It now uses `-t`.

fix(backfill): make the unreadable-service-key path actually refuse

The comment on the service-depth branch claimed that clearing `service` was
enough because "the agent simply fails to resolve and buildPlan refuses out
loud". It does not. Clearing only stops the MIS-attribution; the volumes under
the unreadable key are then dropped by `if (!service) continue`, and if the
agent's own service key parsed fine, buildPlan() resolves it, finds no anomaly,
and returns zero refusals. The operator gets "nothing to back up" and exit 0
for a compose file that visibly had a second service full of mounts.

That is the same silent-skip class this script exists to end, sitting behind a
comment asserting the opposite.

- Record an unreadable service-depth key as a file-level anomaly
  (`services.fileAnomalies`), carried as a property so `[...services.keys()]`
  stays a clean service-name list for buildPlan's candidate search.
- Raise it as a refusal in buildPlan() BEFORE the service search, so it is
  reported even when the agent's own service resolves cleanly.
- The existing test's comment already promised "refusing out loud is the only
  acceptable outcome" while asserting only non-attribution. Assert the refusal,
  so the promise cannot rot away again.

Verified the new assertion is non-vacuous: with the fileAnomalies push disabled
the test fails; restored, 19/19 pass.

feat(compose): split shared vpn into trust groups (#281)

* feat(compose): split shared vpn into trust groups

A shared namespace exposes each agent's localhost servers to every
other agent in it, so VPN'd agents must be split by trust. sharedVpn
is now a group name (or null for off) instead of a boolean. Each group
gets its own gluetun container (gluetun-<group>), compose project,
WireGuard key file (<dataDir>/vpn/<group>/gluetun.env) and deny-all
control-server lockdown.

A group is any name matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}$, not a fixed list.
The trust split is the owner's policy, and a group only works once
its key file exists, so a typo is refused for the missing key rather
than silently creating a namespace.

Moving an agent between groups judges the agent's own off-state
networking, starts the target group's gluetun first, then rewrites the
compose and recreates the agent. A move to a group without a key
refuses and leaves the agent where it was. The #280 boolean shape is
rejected with 400; that layout was never deployed, so there is no
migration shim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): verify group gluetun compose, report failed moves

- An existing vpn/<group>/docker-compose.yml must name this group's
  project, container and key file, and mount the lockdown. Otherwise
  the change is refused before anything is written. A copied
  vpn/private would otherwise start a second container on the private
  key and leave the agent pointing at a container that never exists.
- A group change whose agent recreate fails now returns 502 with
  restarted:false instead of success. The running agent is still in
  its old namespace.
- sharedVpn: false is rejected like true. Off is spelled null.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compose): gate group moves on gluetun health, exact compose

- After `up`, wait for the group's gluetun to report Docker-healthy
  before moving the agent. A bad key crash-loops gluetun, and `up`
  returns as soon as the container exists. If it never becomes
  healthy, the agent is not moved and nothing in its compose changes.
- An existing group compose must equal the generated one exactly. A
  line-based check was bypassable (an extra service on another key, a
  network_mode into another group, a second env_file, an env override
  of the lockdown path). A differing file is refused, never
  overwritten.
- The 502 text for a recreate that cannot be started no longer claims
  the old networking is certain. The UI adopts the fresh version token
  from failure responses too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docker): stop waiting early on a gluetun that cannot get healthy

waitHealthy now returns false at once when the container is missing or
has no healthcheck, and after 20s of not running (a crash loop). The
request no longer blocks the server for the full 90s.

feat(artifacts): POST /api/harnesses/:id/artifacts/sync — install missing artifacts onto existing agents (#82)

installBaselineTemplates only runs at agent create/duplicate, so existing
agents never receive artifacts added to infra/artifacts.json later (e.g.
#81's captcha_cascade never reaches already-created agents via rebuild).

New endpoint syncs an agent's data dir against the manifest with a
two-layer no-clobber model:
- additive floor (no history needed): install MISSING artifacts, never
  touch existing — solves the driving case with zero clobber risk
- pristine-update: an .artifacts-lock.json records shipped content hashes
  at install; an existing artifact is updated only if its on-disk hash
  still matches (unmodified). user-modified or untracked → skipped. force
  overrides.
Newly-installed enabled plugins are added to config.yaml plugins.enabled
(text-based, no YAML dep); container recreated only if something changed;
dryRun returns the plan without writing.

Pure logic in lib/services/artifacts-sync.ts (13 tests) + service method
+ route (4 tests). Create path untouched (additive, low-risk): the lock
writes on first sync. Full suite green (317), tsc + eslint clean.

Closes #82.

  rewrote the on-disk allowlist with values the operator never typed.
  Display data stays in the separate resolvedUsers field.

  resource change) skips the write and the recreate — a plain re-save
  no longer kills in-flight agent work.

hits.message:
harness: the backfill reader must not fold YAML comments into containerPath

`scripts/backfill-extra-mounts.mjs` split each `volumes:` list item on ':'
without first ending the scalar at a YAML comment. A hand-annotated mount —
and these compose files are hand-edited by definition, which is the premise of
the whole script — parsed with the comment inside containerPath, and nothing
downstream caught it. validateMount() only rejects newlines, non-absolute
paths and ':'.

The consequence is not cosmetic. GENERATED_TARGETS is an exact-match Set, so

    - /home/u/.hermes-x:/opt/data   # agent state, do not move

classified as 'extra' rather than 'generated' and would have been copied into
extraMounts — making the next regeneration render /opt/data TWICE, which
docker refuses. That is exactly the breakage the script's own header says it
exists to prevent.

Two adjacent silent-skip paths, found while confirming the first:

  - `volumes:   # hand-maintained` did not match the key test, so inVolumes
    stayed false and EVERY mount in the block was dropped without a word —
    zero additions, exit 0, and a human concluding there was nothing to back up.
  - an unreadable key at service depth left `service` pointing at the PREVIOUS
    service, attributing one agent's mounts to another. Recording another
    container's mounts is the one mistake this script must never make; it now
    clears the service and refuses out loud instead.

readMountScalar() honours quoting before stripping (a '#' inside quotes is
literal, and `/a#1:/b` has no comment at all) and returns null on malformed
quoting, which surfaces as a refusal rather than a skip — the reader's stated
contract.

Verified against the live fleet's harnesses.json and compose files: the plan
is byte-identical before and after this change (16 additions, 0 refusals), so
this fixes a latent trap without moving the pending backfill.

6 new tests, each confirmed failing against the pre-fix reader.

fix(surfaces): recreate container on connect/disconnect so env changes apply

Connecting or disconnecting a surface wrote the agent .env but never
recreated the container, so the running gateway kept the OLD environment
(e.g. a stale Signal account/token) and silently held a broken receive
connection. This is exactly how seraph-generalist ended up locked to a
dead number after its surface was 'reconnected'.

Add a lightweight 'recreate' RestartMode (up -d --force-recreate, no image
build) and fire it from the connect/disconnect routes after writing .env.
force-recreate reloads the env_file without the cost of a full rebuild.
Recreate failures (no compose file, e.g. undeployed harness) are swallowed
so the .env write still succeeds.

disconnect routes invoke harness.restart(id, 'recreate').

* fix(door): refuse a provider redirect instead of following it

The model route sent its calls with the HTTP client's default, which

wherever it points: unlike Authorization, that header is not dropped

in its place) that replied 307 had the real key delivered to another
host, and a redirect to another path of the provider reached a call
the route does not meter.

and the key goes nowhere else. This holds for both wire formats.

The SDK has no write tool in its minimal mode: a shell, a read and an
edit are all it has there. The shim listed `Write` in its tool map and
the fake SDK had one, so a policy that allowed writing files had the
door offer it, the session reported other tools than it was started
with, and every turn ended in an error. `Write` is gone from the map

tools, and C4m drives each mapped tool with every class allowed.

nothing. The shim kept no deadline, so a room's later messages queued
behind a turn the door had given up on. It now keeps the turn's own
deadline, stops the session there, and does not start a turn whose
deadline passed while it waited. C1t drives a silent model.

Asked to pick up a transcript that is gone, the SDK ends the turn
without saying it started, and the shim asked for the same transcript
on every later turn. It now forgets one that cannot be picked up. A

feat(door): add an ACP shim, with OpenCode as its first agent (#370)

* feat(door): add an ACP shim, with OpenCode as its first agent

The door gets one shim for any agent that speaks the Agent Client
Protocol over stdio. The shim is the ACP client: every permission
request goes to decide() as a tool_request, the door's yes must carry
the hash of the call asked about, only once-options are ever picked,
unmapped tool kinds and paths outside the scratch folder are refused
without asking, and no file or terminal client methods are offered.
Because ACP permission is advisory, the shim watches the agent's tool
updates: a call that ran without a yes ends the turn as an error and
drops the agent's process and session.

OpenCode 1.19.5 runs behind it as `--harness opencode`, with the door
as its only provider, its rules written by the shim, and a sealed cell
image built like the others. Conformance covers the shared suite and
the ask flow on a fake and on the real program, plus broken agents
and shims (ignores a reject, picks always, asks nobody).

fix(models): fully replace config sections incl. column-0 list items (#126)

PUT /harnesses/:id/models rewrites the model: and fallback_providers:
sections of config.yaml. The old replacer only skipped INDENTED old body
lines, so a fallback_providers block whose entries were written with the
dash at column 0 (valid YAML) was only half-replaced: the freshly-written
block landed, but the old `- provider:` items survived after it as a bare
sequence beside top-level keys → invalid YAML → the agent can't load config.

Treat a section as spanning up to the next top-level mapping key, skipping
indented lines, blank lines, AND column-0 block-sequence items alike.

feat(surfaces): default discord and signal dms to admins only (#285)

* feat(surfaces): default discord and signal dms to admins only

New agents now start with DMs limited to their admins, or closed when
they have none, on both creation paths.

Discord gets DISCORD_DM_ALLOWED_USERS (hermes-agent-mt#200), registered
as an admission var so disconnect and duplicate strip it and extraEnv
cannot shadow it. Changing the admin list writes it and recreates the
container. A settings save moves it only on a real allowlist change,
and only if it matched the allowlist before, so a hand-set list is never
blanked or widened. Swarm Map never writes "*".

Signal already uses SIGNAL_ALLOWED_USERS as its DM list. The adapter
reads unset as "*" and empty as open mode, which accepts a stranger's
group invite, so new agents get a "0" deny value that matches no sender.
Admin changes do not rewrite this list, because it can hold DM users who
are not admins.

The DM policy toggle was already inert and its help text claimed it let
anyone DM, so the wording now says what really decides.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(surfaces): stop dm lists following the allowlist

An audit of the admins-only default found the DM list could widen or
lose people without anyone choosing that.

Allowlist edits no longer move DISCORD_DM_ALLOWED_USERS, and connect no
longer seeds it from the whole allowlist, because the allowlist also
holds channel users. An explicit admin change now moves the list only if
it equalled the previous explicit admins; otherwise it stays and the
response says so. Empty counts as matching when there was no earlier
explicit list, or a new agent could never open.

The admin and connect routes now warn about a listed admin who is not on
DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS, since the runtime refuses them. The help text
points at the DM list instead of saying admins can DM.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(surfaces): stop treating empty lists as a reason to write

A second audit found paths that read an empty or unset Discord or Signal
list as permission to write one.

Sending the GET admins back no longer opens a closed agent's DMs to the
whole allowlist: a first admin list that matches it is left alone with a
warning. Connect now changes these lists only on a first connect, so
rotating a credential keeps them as they are, including an unset channel
list, which seeding would have turned into a deny. A first connect
replaces the empty lines page saves leave behind, which kept Signal in
open mode and Discord answering in every channel.

Same pattern elsewhere: page saves add no empty Signal list, a Signal key
closes the list on an agent new to Signal, and removing the last Discord
channel through the policy route denies instead of opening every channel.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(surfaces): show connect warnings and correct Signal setup text

Connect warnings never reached a person: the UI only showed success, so
an admin the runtime would refuse looked fine. The Signal setup script
also said an empty DM list means nobody, when empty is open mode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(signal): correct the group list note in setup output

The script said an empty group list means no groups, but people on the
DM list can still add the agent to groups. Notes now print on their own
lines, because python-dotenv read an inline note as the empty value.

A turn whose model call was refused or failed ended with nothing in

looked the same as a model still thinking.

The model route now writes a receipt with the reason for every call

past its deadline, the door posts one short line saying so, with the

The Claude SDK shim gives up at the same deadline as the door, so
the line the door posts for a turn the model never answered can be
the error or no-reply one, not only the timeout one. C1t now asks
for exactly one line, and that it is the door's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): tell no bot, name only fixed reasons, say what a timeout is

A turn a bot started now ends with a receipt and no line in the room.

A model call refused by the rules for any reason but the budget is

feat(door): give a door agent its first tools, with an admin's yes in the room (#352)

* docs(lab): design the tools slice before building it

A door agent's first tools: file read, file write and a shell, all
inside the sealed cell, with a mode per class (never, ask, allow) and
an approval step in the chat room for ask. Says what is a wall and
what is a guardrail, how a later fetch-through-the-door tool would
work, and what is left out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(door): hold a tool for an admin's yes in the room

A class of tool on the ask list no longer makes decide() refuse the
whole record. It answers ask, and the door holds the call: it posts
the exact call in the room, written so nothing in it can hide or ping,
and waits for an admin. Only a reply to that request or a reaction on
it, from a user id on the admin list, is an answer. A bot, a named
bot, a role-holder and the agent itself are refused. No answer in time
is a no, and a yes is checked against the rules as they are when it
lands.

The yes that goes back to the cell carries a hash of the tool name and
input. Pi's gate now runs a call only on a yes that names that call's
hash, so a yes meant for another call does not fit. The gate also keeps
file tools in a scratch folder, links followed, puts a time limit on a
shell call before it asks, and cuts a tool's output before the model
sees it. The door counts tool calls per conversation per hour.

Ten harness-neutral tool checks go with it, each with a gate or a rig
broken on purpose that must turn it red, and they run for Pi as a
process and in the Docker cell. Letta Code's shim takes a plain yes or
no, so its adapter says why the checks are not run for it and its
matrix lists them as not run. All four matrices are regenerated from
real runs, because the list of known checks grew.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(lab): tools in the launcher's config, in a capped scratch folder

The launcher's config gains a tools section: the classes that are
switched on (file_read, file_write, shell) and a mode for each. None is
on by default, and a shell that is switched on asks an admin unless the
config says otherwise. The lists in the rules record are written from
it. A config that hears anyone in the channel now makes a public
record, and is refused outright if it also switches a tool on.

The folder the harness is started in becomes a mount in memory with a
size, owned by the user the cell runs as, and the dry run checks it:
as written, as Docker made it, and by filling it. Where a tool waits
for an admin, the cell is told to wait a little longer than the door,
and Discord is asked for reactions. The agent is told which tools it
has and which wait for an admin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(ui): a Tools card on a door agent's rules, and approvals in its receipts

The Rules tab gets a Tools card: read files, write files and shell,
each Off, Ask an admin or Allow, all Off to start with. It edits the
tools part of the same rules record, so the launcher's parser still
decides whether a choice is sound, and it is switched off for an agent
that hears anyone in the channel. The Receipts tab gets an Approvals
only box and shows who answered a request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(lab): what the tools slice runs showed, and where the other pages point

A note written beside them in the file was carried into the rules

The dry run printed 'tools: none' whatever the config asked for. It now
names each class that is switched on and how it is decided.

The door refused a request longer than one chat message, but a request
is a fixed frame around a name and a call that are both capped, so the

* fix(door): a tool request that cannot be decided does not move its turn's deadline

The turn's clock is stopped while a call waits for an admin and started

harness that kept asking could keep its turn open. Only the call that

* feat(ui): switch the Tools card off for a harness that has no tools

* feat(door): route rooms with fewer tools to a second cell

The door can now hold a second cell for rooms with fewer tools than
the agent's own. Turns from those rooms (and their threads) go to it
only. It is taken at hello only if every tool it declares is web,
search or notes, and it may ask for nothing else (tools.cell).

turn was sent to, so neither cell can act under the other's turn

never starts Pi with any other; the cell entry reads SMLAB_TOOLS.

When a listed channel has web-only or no tools and the agent's own
channel has shell or file tools, the launcher starts a second sealed
cell built with web, search and notes only, on its own networks,
token and port, sharing the door, budget and notes. Single-channel
configs keep their policy hash and one-cell layout unchanged.

Dry run checks both cells (S0t for the second), status and stop
cover both, and the dashboard Status card shows the cell count.
Unit tests cover routing, cross-cell refusal and the seal checks.

hits.message:
fix(discord): manage the vars that actually gate a Discord agent (#186)

* fix(discord): manage the vars that actually gate a Discord agent

HSM managed two DISCORD_* vars while the adapter decides whether to execute a
message using four. The two it did manage were reported with inverted semantics,
so the console could not show — let alone control — who can command an agent.
Found while auditing HSM as the control surface ahead of a community migration.

- DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES, DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS and DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS are now
  first-class settings. Roles are the only "admin class" primitive the runtime
  has; ignored-channels is the only channel deny that binds a bot holding
  Administrator; allow-bots is evaluated BEFORE the human allowlist and skips it,
  so a permissive value was a fourth authorization class invisible here.
  Each is written only when the client sends the field, so an older client cannot
  blank a hand-hardened value.

- Never write an empty DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS. The adapter gates on
  `if allowed_channels_raw:`, so empty skipped the channel check entirely and
  "no channels approved" meant "respond in EVERY channel". Writes a sentinel that
  no snowflake can match, mapped back to an empty list on read.

- GET reports an absent channel allowlist as unscoped rather than as a lockdown,
  so wide-open and locked-down stop rendering identically.

- Reject non-numeric role/channel IDs and unrecognized allowBots values. Both
  failure modes are silent AND fail-open at runtime: the adapter drops
  non-numeric roles with no log, and only compares against 'none' first, so a
  typo lands in the permissive branch.

- buildSettingsEnvValue no longer derives '*' from dmPolicy. These vars are the
  general allowlist, not a DM-only one, so a toggle labelled "DM Access Policy"
  granted every server member command access whenever a surface had no users.

- Regenerate the compose only when the VPN toggle actually changed. GET always
  emits vpnEnabled and both clients PUT the whole document back, so regeneration
  fired on every save, including permissions-only edits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(discord): close a fail-open found by independent review

Independent adversarial review of the first cut found that its most visible
change was itself a regression. Fixes all three blockers.

1. GET must not fold "unscoped" into allowAllGroups. Empty and '*' are DIFFERENT
   runtime states: _discord_channel_ids_allowed returns False on empty but True
   on '*', and _is_allowed_user uses it as the channel bypass for agents with no
   user/role allowlist. Both clients PUT back the document GET returns, so
   reporting an empty allowlist as allowAllGroups materialized a literal '*' and
   would have turned a fail-closed agent into one every guild member can command.
   Now reported as its own read-only `groupsUnscoped` field that PUT ignores.

2. DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS='*' is no longer erased. parseCommaList maps '*' to
   [], which wrote back empty — silently removing a guild-wide mute, the only
   kill switch that binds a bot holding Administrator.

3. Channel validation no longer requires numeric IDs. The adapter builds its gate
   keys from the snowflake, the bare name AND '#name', so configuring by name is
   supported; rejecting it 400'd the entire save, including every other
   platform's settings. Now rejects only values that would corrupt the env line
   (comma, whitespace, newline). The roles rule stays numeric — that one is
   correctly grounded in the adapter's .isdigit() filter.

Also: an unrecognized DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS is reported as permissive rather than
flattered to 'none' (the adapter compares 'none' then 'mentions' and lets
everything else fall through), and new Discord agents are seeded with a
deny-sentinel channel scope plus an explicit ALLOW_BOTS=none instead of being
born in the exact state that triggers the fail-open above.

Adds a round-trip suite — GET the document, PUT it back verbatim, assert access
never widens — which is the class of test that would have caught the original bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(discord): narrow the deny sentinel; stop validation deadlocking the page

Second independent review confirmed the three original blockers closed but found
the fix had inverted one of them and added a save-deadlock.

- The sentinel now applies ONLY when the operator actually clears a scoped agent.
  Every agent HSM deployed before this change carries an empty
  DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS, so echoing the GET document back was writing the
  sentinel and silently taking them offline in every channel. It also suppressed
  the adapter's config.yaml `discord.allowed_channels` fallback, which applies
  only when the env var is falsy — a live regression for YAML-scoped agents.
  When the operator really did clear a non-empty list, the var was already truthy,
  so YAML was already inactive and the sentinel changes nothing there.

- Validation now grandfathers values already on disk and checks only entries the
  operator introduces. GET emits what is on disk and both clients PUT the whole
  document back, so a hand-configured `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES=moderators` made the
  settings page permanently unsaveable for EVERY platform, with no console path to
  repair it.

- Channel names may contain spaces — voice, stage, forum and category names allow
  them and the adapter matches the name verbatim. Only commas and newlines are
  rejected now, since those corrupt the list format and the file respectively.

- The groups write uses the callback form of String.replace. A literal '$&' or
  '$`' in a channel name would otherwise splice surrounding file content —
  including DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN — into the written value. The adjacent users path
  and this repo's surface-admins.ts already model this.

Adds coverage for the previously untested hunks: the fail-closed new-agent seed
and its explicit ALLOW_BOTS=none.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(discord): derive the sentinel from disk; reject space-then-# in channels

Third review round. Both findings were real.

- The sentinel decision no longer trusts the client's `groupsUnscoped`. Neither
  client refetches after a save, so an operator who scoped an agent and then
  cleared it again in the same page session was still echoing
  groupsUnscoped:true — suppressing the sentinel and leaving the agent answering
  in every channel while the console showed "no channels approved". That is the
  original fail-open, reintroduced through a client contract. The previous value
  is now read from the .env, which makes the invariant structural. It also closes
  the two paths where the sentinel could still land on a previously-falsy var and
  suppress config.yaml's discord.allowed_channels fallback.

- Channel entries containing whitespace-then-# are rejected. This .env is consumed
  as a compose env_file and Docker treats that as an inline comment: verified
  against the compose CLI, `A=mute #2` reaches the container as `mute`. On
  DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS that silently un-mutes the channel the operator muted —
  a fail-open on the one deny that binds a bot holding Administrator — while HSM's
  own parseEnvFile does no comment handling and would keep displaying the full
  value. Bare `#name` and internal spaces remain legal.

- Group values are trimmed before joining so the written value matches what
  validation inspected.

Adds the test that distinguishes a server-derived sentinel from a client-trusting
one — its absence is why the previous round's regression passed review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(discord): trim ignored-channel entries before writing

Validation inspects String(c).trim(), so an untrimmed write could smuggle past
it: ' #b' validates as '#b' (legal) but landed in the file as 'a, #b', and
Docker's env_f

hits.message:
fleet: make "this agent is running old code" impossible to miss (#223)

Detection only — read-only observability, no update/apply machinery.

The gap: nothing on the host pulls or rebuilds. Agent code moves only when
a human runs a per-agent `docker compose build` + `up -d --force-recreate`.
On 2026-08-10, 11 agents ran four-day-old code carrying a bug that silently
deleted tool results, for days, with nothing anywhere saying "behind".

hermes-agent-mt's Dockerfile already declared `ARG HERMES_GIT_SHA` and wrote
/opt/hermes/.hermes_build_sha, but swarm-map never passed the build-arg — so
the file exists in no running container and no agent can say what it was
built from. Verified on the Mini before writing any of this.

- docker.ts: syncBuildSource also returns the FULL sha, and the rebuild/purge
  build steps pass `--build-arg HERMES_GIT_SHA=<full sha>`. Adds diffContainer
  (`docker diff`) as an async seam.
- drift.ts: containerBuildSha (reads the baked sha out of the RUNNING
  container via the existing exec helper), buildSourceHead (HEAD + how far
  behind its own upstream, never fetching), hotPatched (files copied into
  /opt/hermes/agent — the next recreate silently reverts them; this really
  happened). States: current | behind | unknown-no-provenance |
  unknown-not-running. Nothing renders green by default; unknown is not
  current, and an unknown gap is null, never 0.
- Agents are enumerated from the harness registry unioned with the compose
  dirs, not `docker ps | grep hermes-`: three services are keyed seraph-*,
  and a never-started agent has no container to grep at all.
- GET /api/fleet/drift returns it per agent.
- Dashboard: per-agent chip showing an AGE DELTA ("11 commits / 4d behind"),
  not a boolean, plus a banner while any agent is not current.

Tests are mutation-checked: 11 mutations (short sha instead of full, dropped
build-arg, no-provenance reading as current, dropped compose-dir enumeration,
unknown gap reported as 0, loosened hot-patch path match, unknown rendered
green, hot-patch ignored, label collapsed to a boolean, banner only firing on
"behind", missing row hidden) each turned the suite red and were reverted.

hits.message:
Validate provider-credential presence before pushing model cascade to live agents (PUT /harnesses/:id/models) (#91)

* Validate model cascade against catalog in PUT /harnesses/:id/models

The PUT /api/harnesses/:id/models route wrote any model string into a
live agent's config.yaml and restarted it, with no validation. A bad /
unknown / empty model id could crash-loop a production agent.

Add validateCascadeEntries() in lib/model-catalog (catalog-as-truth) and
call it in the PUT route before any config write. Rejects with 400 +
the offending model id(s) when a catalogued, non-free-form provider
(anthropic / openai / google / bedrock) is given a model not in the
catalog, or when a model id is empty.

Leniency mirrors /suggest: free-form providers (ollama / openrouter /
custom) and any non-catalogued provider accept arbitrary model ids,
since the catalog is not authoritative for them and the UI offers a
free-text model field for exactly that case.

Covers both request shapes (legacy cascade+provider, and
fallback_providers[]). Adds unit tests for the validator and route
integration tests (valid passes, unknown rejected 400, free-form
allowed, empty rejected).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Validate provider-credential presence (not catalog membership) in PUT /models

Review rejected the catalog-membership approach: MODEL_CATALOG is a tiny
2-per-provider *suggestions* list, not an allowlist, so strict membership
would 400 legitimate in-use models (e.g. claude-opus-4-8, newer gemini/gpt).

What actually crash-loops an agent is pushing a model whose provider has no
configured credential for that agent (e.g. openrouter without OPENROUTER_API_KEY).
So validate provider-credential PRESENCE instead.

- KEEP the empty/missing model-id guard (the unambiguous crash case).
- DROP the strict MODEL_CATALOG membership check entirely.
- ADD readAgentEnvVarNames(dataDir) — reads the agent's .env var NAMES (never
  values) using the same parse semantics as keys.ts parseEnvFile.
- validateCascadeEntries now takes the agent's present env-var set and rejects
  an entry ONLY when its provider is DEFINITIVELY un-serviceable: provider needs
  a known single key, we know which env var, and it is absent. Enforced set is
  conservative: anthropic (API_KEY|TOKEN), openai, openrouter.
- FAIL OPEN on all uncertainty: ollama/custom need no key (always allowed);
  google/gemini have ambiguous auth modes (allowed); bedrock uses AWS multi-var
  creds / instance roles (allowed); unknown providers (nous, etc.) allowed.

Tests: replaced catalog-membership tests with credential-presence tests
(provider-with-key passes; provider-without-key 400s; ollama/custom pass;
unknown provider fails open; empty id 400s). Full suite green except the 4
pre-existing better-sqlite3 ABI failures in usage.test.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* models validation: fail open on empty env-set (missing/unreadable .env)

A missing/unreadable agent .env yields an empty env-var set. The credential
check must NOT treat that as 'no credentials' and reject every enforced-provider
model — that's a worse false-reject than the bug being fixed. When the set is
empty, skip credential validation entirely (fail open); the empty-id guard
remains the floor. Verified guessDataDir co-locates .env with the config.yaml
the route already reads, so a non-empty set reliably reflects real keys.

hits.message:
Named-volume DB migration + snapshot export (#204 PR2) (#208)

* compose: named-volume DB migration via one-shot state-init service (#204 PR2)

All three generators (standalone plain, standalone VPN, deploy-born) now emit:
- a named volume hermes-state-<name> (explicit name: so the project prefix
  can never fork the volume identity between compose locations)
- a one-shot state-init-<name> service (reuses the hermes image/build source,
  bypasses s6 via entrypoint override) that moves state.db/response_store.db/
  kanban.db (+ -wal/-shm) off the VirtioFS bind mount onto the volume and
  leaves symlinks in /opt/data — idempotent, crash-safe (tmp+rename, db-first
  delete), and self-healing after `hermes import` (regular file wins)
- a service_completed_successfully depends_on gate on the hermes service
  (map form everywhere — VPN list form can't mix with the condition entry)
- a /state mount on the hermes service so the symlink targets resolve

Shell $ are compose-escaped ($$) on embed; the raw script is exported as
STATE_INIT_SCRIPT and exercised directly under /bin/sh in tests with real
WAL-mode SQLite files. setComposeImage now rewrites the init service's source
block too, so a CD image pin can't strand init on a stale ref.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* host readers: lstat-aware state.db resolution — no silent zeros post-migration

After migration the host-side <dataDir>/state.db is a symlink whose target
exists only in-container; fs.existsSync follows it and returns false, so every
existsSync-gated reader silently reported no-db/zero (usage → \$0, monthly
budget enforcement OFF, memory scope hidden). New lib/services/db-path.ts
classifies the four states via lstat:

  live | snapshot | migrated-pending | none

Adopted in usage.ts (getCostToday/getCostMonth/getInvocationsToday/
getUsageSummary — migrated harnesses read the host-visible state.db.snapshot
export, ≤ ~5 min stale) and memory.ts (existence check). migrated-pending
(symlink up, first snapshot not yet exported) is an explicit UNKNOWN: the
usage functions return null, Harness.costToday/invocations are now
number|null, the UI renders '—' instead of \$0, and the budget check responds
costUnknown:true / exceeded:false instead of silently disabling enforcement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* snapshot exporter: periodic state.db export for volume-migrated harnesses

New async DockerService.execInContainer (promisified execFile, argv array, no
shell) so multi-hundred-MB DB work never blocks the single pm2 fork — the
better-sqlite3 sync-blocking problem #204 set out to fix.

lib/services/db-snapshot.ts sweeps container harnesses, detects migration by

feat(artifacts): git-sourced artifacts behind a security trust gate (#96)

* feat(artifacts): parse + validate git:<org>/<repo>#<tag> artifact sources

First step of git-sourced (third-party) artifact support. parseGitSource is the
security front door: returns null for non-git sources, and throws loudly on any
git-prefixed source that is unpinned (pinning to a tag is mandatory — an
unpinned ref can silently drift to malicious code), malformed, or carries unsafe
characters / path traversal (the ref later feeds a git command). Pure function,
no network — to be wired into installArtifacts behind the capability + injection
trust gate.

TDD: 9 new tests; existing loader tests still pass.

Faithful TS port of the image-side tools/threat_patterns.py library (prompt
injection / promptware / exfiltration) with the same all/context/strict scope
semantics and invisible-unicode detection. HSM uses scanForThreats as the EARLY
gate when installing git-sourced artifacts; the Python scanner in the agent
image remains the authoritative runtime backstop (defense in depth). Keep the
two in sync when upstream patterns change.

gateArtifactDir() walks a fetched git-sourced artifact directory and scans every
text file with the TS threat-pattern scanner (context scope) before install.

findings so the caller can refuse a poisoned artifact (loud failure) instead of
copying it onto disk.

(fetchGitArtifact), running the content-scan gate (gateArtifactDir), and

The Phase-1 "git is unsupported" contract test now asserts a genuinely

* fix(security): reject newlines at .env/compose write sinks (F8–F11)

A CR/LF in a value spliced onto a single line of a generated file lets an
attacker inject additional `KEY=value` env lines (policy override) or
additional docker-compose YAML keys. The worst case (F8): `PUT
/api/harnesses/:id/image` with a newline in `imageRef` injects
`privileged: true` + a `/:/host` bind under the hermes service, and the
immediate recreate brings the container up as host root — container
breakout from one request.

Adds a shared `assertNoNewline(value, field)` in lib/env-helpers.ts and
wires it into the four generated-file sinks:
- mergeEnvVars (shared env sink: settings + surface connect) — F11
- upsertEnvVar (keys → agent .env; now exported for direct test) — F9
- generateEnvContent (create-new deploy template) — F10
- setComposeImage (compose YAML → image ref) — F8

Values that legitimately live on one line (secrets, tokens, URLs, image
refs) never contain a newline, so we reject rather than escape.

Tests: lib/services/__tests__/injection-newline.test.ts proves each sink
refuses an injecting value and still accepts a clean one (RED→GREEN).
Full suite: 693 passing, no regressions.

hits.message:
fix(deploy): correct the Google MCP wiring for newly created agents (#189)

* fix(deploy): make Google MCP actually work for newly created agents

A newly created agent's Google MCP could not start, for three independent
reasons. All three had to be wrong for the outage to be invisible, and all
three were.

1. GOOGLE_MCP_DIR defaulted only to ~/Documents/GitHub/google-multiplayer-mcp.
   The repo is commonly cloned as `google-mcp`, so the existsSync probe failed,
   googleMcpDir became undefined, and an operator who ticked "Google" in the
   wizard silently got no Google at all — no mount, no mcp_servers entry, no
   error. Now probes both names, and probes dist/index.js rather than the
   directory so an unbuilt checkout is caught too. When Google is enabled and
   nothing is found, the deploy now FAILS with the paths it looked at instead
   of shipping an agent whose integration does not exist.

2. The generated config pointed --config at /opt/google/config.yaml. Only
   /opt/google/tokens is bind-mounted, so that path never existed and the
   server exited 1 on readFileSync. Now points at
   /opt/data/google-permissions.yaml, inside the agent data dir mount.

3. Nothing wrote a Google permission config anywhere. HSM now generates one.

On (3), a security constraint shapes the default: in google-multiplayer-mcp an
EMPTY `folders` list means NO RESTRICTION (permissions.ts getAllowedFolders),
so emitting e.g. `drive: {access: write, folders: []}` would hand a brand-new
agent unscoped read/write over an entire Google account. The wizard collects no
folder IDs, so every service is generated at access: none, with a header
explaining that granting access requires listing folder IDs and how to run the
one-time OAuth flow. An optional googleIdentity in the request body lets an API
caller match an existing token file; it defaults to the agent slug.

Also creates the google-tokens dir at deploy time so it is owned by the
invoking user — letting Docker create the missing bind-mount source can leave
it root-owned, and the OAuth flow needs to write token JSON into it.

Separately, config.yaml now pins web.search_backend: brave-free. Leaving it
unset makes the runtime auto-detect from whichever API key happens to be
present, so the provider an agent searches with was a side effect of .env
contents rather than a decision — and it changed silently when a key was
added. Both creation paths share generateDefaultConfig, so the wizard and the
harness service both get it.

Tests: 12 new route-level integration tests running the real deploy logic and
its real fs writes against temp dirs — including that Google-off writes no
Google artifacts, and that every generated service defaults to none. Verified
non-vacuous: 9 of 12 fail against origin/main. 905 tests pass, typecheck clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address independent audit — no side effects on reject, and the
credentials/paths the server actually reads

BLOCKING (B1): the Google preflight ran AFTER mkdirSync(agentDataDir) and the
.env write, and returned from inside the try — so the catch's cleanup was
unreachable. Rejecting a deploy left a half-created agent dir containing the
resolved PLAINTEXT LLM key, and then 409'd every retry of that name forever;
recovery needed `rm -rf ~/.hermes-<slug>` from a shell with nothing in the UI
saying so. On the letta runtime it also orphaned an already-created brain agent,
which then 409'd by name too.

Moved the whole preflight above every side effect — above the LLM key
resolution and the letta branch, not merely above mkdir — which is the rule the
letta branch itself states ("before a single door byte is written"). A new test
asserts no dir, no docker start, no key-registry writes, and that the same name
is still deployable afterwards.

Three more from the audit, each the same class of bug this PR set out to fix —
a path or name that nothing on the other side reads:

- S4: GOOGLE_TOKEN_DIR was set nowhere, so the server fell back to
  $HOME/.nimbleco-google/tokens. With HOME=/opt/data the tokens landed
  somewhere the compose file never mounts deliberately, making the
  /opt/google/tokens mount dead weight. Now set explicitly.
- S2: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET were never provisioned, and HSM
  never writes ~/.nimbleco-google/config.json, so loadGlobalConfig() always
  threw and the OAuth flow was impossible regardless of scoping. Now written to
  the agent .env (from the request, else inherited from HSM's own env) and
  referenced from the mcp_servers env block.
- S5: googleIdentity was interpolated into YAML unvalidated. "a: b" broke the
  parse (MCP exits 1 — the exact regression this fixes) and a newline could
  inject permission entries past the deny-by-default. Now `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`.

Found while fixing the above, not in the audit: generateEnvContent wrote a
wizard-supplied Brave key as BRAVE_API_KEY only. The runtime reads exclusively
BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY (plugins/web/brave_free/provider.py, and the auto-detect
table in tools/web_tools.py); nothing reads BRAVE_API_KEY. So the key was
invisible to the agent, brave-free reported itself unavailable, and the
search_backend pin added in this PR would have fallen straight through to
auto-detect — inert. Both names are now written.

Also: N1 the probe now requires node_modules as well as dist/index.js (the
bundle imports bare googleapis/js-yaml, so a pruned checkout passed and exited
1 at runtime); N2 non-absolute GOOGLE_MCP_DIR is rejected (Docker reads a
relative volume source as a named volume, mounting an empty dir over the
bundle); N4 the 400 now carries ok: false like its neighbours; S3 the generated
OAuth runbook now passes GOOGLE_TOKEN_DIR and the client creds, without which
it hit EROFS on the read_only container.

Tests: 18 (was 12). Verified by mutation — reverting each of the six fixes
individually fails a test. 911 pass on the real tree, typecheck clean.

hits.message:
fix(deploy): new agents boot (run:exec) + clean up scaffold on failure (#98)

* fix(deploy): mount /run exec so new agents boot under read-only rootfs

The create-new compose hardens agents with `read_only: true` + a bare
`tmpfs: - /run`. Docker mounts short-form tmpfs noexec, but s6-overlay
execs /run/s6/basedir/bin/init at boot — so init fails with EACCES
(exit 126) and every newly-created agent restart-loops.

Existing fleet agents predate this hardening, so the regression stayed
latent until the first real create-new (a live Matilde use-case-template
E2E on the Mini). Mounting /run exec lets s6 boot while keeping the
read-only rootfs + dropped caps. Verified live: container reaches
`running exit=0` and the use-case plugin loads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deploy): remove scaffolded agent dir when a deploy fails

A failed create-new (e.g. the trust gate refusing a poisoned use-case
template, or container start timing out) returned 500 but left the
half-written agent dir on disk — including its .env, which holds the
resolved API key. Track the dir once created and rm it on both the
container-start failure path and the outer catch, so a failed deploy
leaves no secret-bearing leftovers. Never removes a pre-existing agent
(the var is only set after we mkdir a fresh one).

Makes the existing P2 cleanup test green (was red on main).

x-ai/grok-4.20 (released 2026-03) was the "successor" of grok-4.7

feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable (#265)

* feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable

Per-repo copies of check_sanitization.py drifted apart, each missing a
protection another copy had. swarm-map becomes the one home: the
script, the union of every copy's self-tests, and a reusable workflow
(sanitization-gate.yml) other repos call pinned to a
sanitization-gate-v* tag. Each repo keeps only sanitize.config.json.

The canonical script merges the Matilde/osint-engine base (fail-closed
semantic layer, fork-PR honesty, match-scoped allowlist, broadest
detector set) with swarm-map's --diff scope, separated international
phones, public-IP and fiction-phone filters (now opt-in config), and
ASG's per-content verdict cache. It adds --check-config and
--require-config. The swarm-map-specific reviewer prompt moves out of
the script into swarm-map's own sanitize.config.json.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close audit bypasses in the gate

An audit of the canonical gate found silent skips that let a real
token pass. git C-quoted non-ASCII paths, so docs/café.md was never
found on disk; one non-UTF-8 byte made layer 1 skip a whole file; an
allow_substrings entry of "" or a skip_paths entry of "."/"**"
disabled layer 1 and was only checked under --check-config; and the
reusable workflow accepted pull_request_target, which scans the base
with the key exposed.

Paths now come from git with -z, a listed path missing from disk is a
hard failure (deletions are excluded from --diff), binaries are judged
by NUL bytes and text is decoded with replacement, structural config
validation runs on every gate run, and pull_request_target is refused.
The workflow docs now say consumers must make the check required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): stop config and encodings from disabling layer 1

A re-audit found the PR under review controlled its own rules and that
some files escaped layer 1 entirely. sanitize.config.json was read from
the PR head and could set deterministic.enabled false, narrow scope,
skip any path, or allow "sk-ant-" as a substring; and one NUL byte or
UTF-16 encoding skipped a file in both layers.

On pull_request the reusable workflow now scans with the base commit's
config (SANITIZE_CONFIG) and notices a config change. Layer 1 cannot be
disabled or narrowed, skip_paths accepts only test-fixture paths, and
allow entries match exactly (plus email-domain and /24 forms). Layer 1
decodes UTF-16/32, reads other NUL-bearing files as latin-1, and scans
symlink target strings. swarm-map's config drops scope and lists its
fixture files and exact known values instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): judge home-repo PRs with the base gate

In swarm-map the gate judged a PR with the PR's own script, so a PR
could weaken the gate that judged it. On pull_request the reusable
workflow now runs the judging steps with the base commit's script; the
PR's script is still exercised by the self-tests, and a notice says when
the script changed. The garden guild id leaves the allowlist: #266
moves it out of source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close round-3 audit gaps

Threat model, now written down: the gate stops accidental leaks by
trusted committers and their agents; required checks and CODEOWNERS
cover a malicious committer.

Layer 1 scans the union of the decoded text and the raw latin-1 bytes,
so a stray BOM cannot hide an ASCII token. skip_paths match by path
segment, never as bare string prefixes; inside them provider tokens and
private keys are still reported, and .env/.pem/.key/id_* files are
never skipped. The workflow no longer runs git fetch (it failed in
private repos without persisted credentials), refuses a gate_ref that
is not a release tag or full SHA, and swarm-map's caller drops its
paths filter so the check reports on every PR. Adds CODEOWNERS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): ship the workflow to consumers' self-tests

The self-tests now check the reusable workflow itself, but consumers'
sparse checkout of the gate left it out, so their self-test step
failed. Also drop a personal name from the threat model wording.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): catch JSON assignments and fleet provider tokens

Round-4 audit. Credential-assignment patterns required the separator
right after the key, so JSON ("api_key": "...") never matched; they
now allow a closing quote on the key, while template words, env-var
names and lowercase slugs stay quiet. Adds high-confidence patterns for
