feat(runtime): put the Claude Agent SDK behind the door (#351)

* feat(runtime): teach the model route the Anthropic Messages format

The model route swapped the key, metered and capped only for a harness
that spoke the OpenAI chat format. It now has a second wire format,
Anthropic Messages, which is what the Claude Agent SDK speaks.

The placeholder is read from x-api-key and the real key goes out there.
Usage is read from the two events a stream reports it in, with cache
reads counted in full and cache writes counted twice, so the figure is
never less than the bill. A call for a tool the provider runs and bills
by the use is refused, since its cost is not in the usage figure. The
token-count call is answered by the route itself, as an estimate.

The scripted model speaks the same format when told to, and the shared
key check reads the key from whichever header the format puts it in.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(runtime): add a Claude Agent SDK shim behind the door

A third harness adapter. The shim drives one SDK session per door
session, starts it with exactly the tools the door offered, and puts
every tool call to the door first. The SDK runs some calls unasked by
default, so it is told to ask about each tool by name.

The SDK is not a dependency of the repo. It is handed to the shim as a
value, so CI runs the shared checks against a fake and a local run
points at a pinned install. Four checks are its own: a call it would
run unasked still waits, no built-in tool runs when none is offered,
rooms keep separate threads, and a direct message is not delivered.

Its traffic is watched by a proxy it is told to use, since no tripwire
can be loaded into a compiled program. The credential guard accepts a
placeholder and a local route under the two fixed names the SDK reads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): put the Claude Agent SDK in the sealed Docker cell

A third cell image holds the pinned SDK, installed from a lock file
with no install script run. The rig, the probe and the broken rigs are
the ones Pi and Letta Code use. The rig's entry now picks the adapter
by the harness it is told, and the probe knows which files of this
harness must not be writable.

The two checks that need a file in the cell have the harness make it,
so they run where the lab's side cannot write. The scripted model's
Anthropic side and the fake SDK each have tests of their own, which
pin the ways the real SDK is not careful: it runs some calls unasked,
and writes a failed model call where a reply goes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(lab): say what the Claude Agent SDK slice proves, and what it does not

The write-up for the third harness: what was built, each check and
its result, what about the real SDK needed special handling, what it
declares, the model route's second format, what its install pulls in,
and a paragraph on Anthropic's terms with what was not verified.

A one-turn run against a real provider is written for the day there is
a key. It needs an SDK folder and a key file. CI runs the same code
with a stand-in at each end. It has not been run for real.

The route also refuses a call that asks for the same model at another
price. Dependabot's update pull requests are switched off for the
folder that pins the SDK, as for Letta Code's. Tests were added for
the gaps a mutation run found.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): keep credential-shaped strings out of the new tests

The sanitize gate reads a URL with an @ in it as a login, and a quoted
value after a key header as a key. The guard tests that need such
strings now put them together from parts, as the older ones do. Lint
warnings in the new test files and the broken SDK wrapper are cleared.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): re-run Pi and Letta Code after the shared changes

Both were run again as a plain process and in the sealed Docker cell,
after the model route, the credential guard, the scripted model and
the shared key check changed. Pi passes 14 and 20, Letta Code 16 and
22, as before. Their four matrix files are from those runs.

The doc's row on what the cell sends is from the capture taken during
the final Docker run of the third harness.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): refuse a provider redirect instead of following it

The model route sent its calls with the HTTP client's default, which
follows a redirect. A client that follows one sends x-api-key on to
wherever it points: unlike Authorization, that header is not dropped
when a redirect leaves the host. So a provider (or anything answering
in its place) that replied 307 had the real key delivered to another
host, and a redirect to another path of the provider reached a call
the route does not meter.

A redirect is now refused with 502 and a receipt, nothing is charged,
and the key goes nowhere else. This holds for both wire formats.

A second test pins which request headers reach the provider: the ones
the format names and no other. A route that passed every header on
was not caught by any test before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): three ways the Claude SDK shim could leave a room mute

An audit of the adapter against the real SDK 0.3.325 found three, none
of them unsafe and none seen by a check.

The SDK has no write tool in its minimal mode: a shell, a read and an
edit are all it has there. The shim listed `Write` in its tool map and
the fake SDK had one, so a policy that allowed writing files had the
door offer it, the session reported other tools than it was started
with, and every turn ended in an error. `Write` is gone from the map
(the edit tool makes a new file), the fake has the real one's three
tools, and C4m drives each mapped tool with every class allowed.

The SDK waits far longer than the door: about three minutes of retries
on a refused model call, and more than nine on a model that says
nothing. The shim kept no deadline, so a room's later messages queued
behind a turn the door had given up on. It now keeps the turn's own
deadline, stops the session there, and does not start a turn whose
deadline passed while it waited. C1t drives a silent model.

Asked to pick up a transcript that is gone, the SDK ends the turn
without saying it started, and the shim asked for the same transcript
on every later turn. It now forgets one that cannot be picked up. A
turn that ends before the session said what it is gives no reply.

Two broken shims turn the two new checks red. The matrix files are
made again in the next commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): catch a Claude SDK missing a tool it claims

Three gaps a mutation pass on the Claude SDK slice left open, each
now with a test that fails on the mutated code.

- lacks-a-tool: an SDK that starts without its edit tool and says it

- A lab that never asked the credential guard passed every check.

- A turn that ends with empty text is settled with no reply.

* fix(runtime): stop a Claude SDK session that runs a tool unasked

The pump now keeps the id of every call the door was asked about. A

to the door, means the SDK ran it on

test(sanitization): add property-based discovery suite (#303)

* test(sanitization): add property-based discovery suite

A hypothesis suite that plants synthetic credential and PII shapes in
the wrappings an honest committer produces by accident: JSON, YAML,
URLs, unspaced non-English prose, CRLF, UTF-16/32, BOMs, latin-1,
NUL-prefixed binaries, large files and odd file names, including

fix(models): read and write the hermes "new format" model: forms

readModelBlock only recognised model.default. A scalar `model: <id>` (the
hermes "new format", cli.py:487) or a block with model.model and no default
(promoted at cli.py:498) read as primary=null, so the chain was the rows
alone and any save promoted fallbacks[0] to a brand-new model.default and
emptied fallback_providers — 200 OK, primary silently changed.

Reader: a scalar after `model:` is the default; model.model is the default
when `default:` is absent (default wins when both are present, as at
runtime). Writer: the primary is written under the key the file uses
(model.model stays model.model, no `default:` added beside it); the scalar
form stays scalar while the block would hold nothing else, and upgrades to
block form when the primary carries a provider or base_url. A no-op save
over either shape is byte-identical.

Validate provider-credential presence before pushing model cascade to live agents (PUT /harnesses/:id/models) (#91)

* Validate model cascade against catalog in PUT /harnesses/:id/models

The PUT /api/harnesses/:id/models route wrote any model string into a
live agent's config.yaml and restarted it, with no validation. A bad /
unknown / empty model id could crash-loop a production agent.

Add validateCascadeEntries() in lib/model-catalog (catalog-as-truth) and
call it in the PUT route before any config write. Rejects with 400 +
the offending model id(s) when a catalogued, non-free-form provider
(anthropic / openai / google / bedrock) is given a model not in the
catalog, or when a model id is empty.

Leniency mirrors /suggest: free-form providers (ollama / openrouter /
custom) and any non-catalogued provider accept arbitrary model ids,
since the catalog is not authoritative for them and the UI offers a
free-text model field for exactly that case.

Covers both request shapes (legacy cascade+provider, and
fallback_providers[]). Adds unit tests for the validator and route
integration tests (valid passes, unknown rejected 400, free-form
allowed, empty rejected).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Validate provider-credential presence (not catalog membership) in PUT /models

Review rejected the catalog-membership approach: MODEL_CATALOG is a tiny
2-per-provider *suggestions* list, not an allowlist, so strict membership
would 400 legitimate in-use models (e.g. claude-opus-4-8, newer gemini/gpt).

What actually crash-loops an agent is pushing a model whose provider has no
configured credential for that agent (e.g. openrouter without OPENROUTER_API_KEY).
So validate provider-credential PRESENCE instead.

- KEEP the empty/missing model-id guard (the unambiguous crash case).
- DROP the strict MODEL_CATALOG membership check entirely.
- ADD readAgentEnvVarNames(dataDir) — reads the agent's .env var NAMES (never
  values) using the same parse semantics as keys.ts parseEnvFile.
- validateCascadeEntries now takes the agent's present env-var set and rejects
  an entry ONLY when its provider is DEFINITIVELY un-serviceable: provider needs
  a known single key, we know which env var, and it is absent. Enforced set is
  conservative: anthropic (API_KEY|TOKEN), openai, openrouter.
- FAIL OPEN on all uncertainty: ollama/custom need no key (always allowed);
  google/gemini have ambiguous auth modes (allowed); bedrock uses AWS multi-var
  creds / instance roles (allowed); unknown providers (nous, etc.) allowed.

Tests: replaced catalog-membership tests with credential-presence tests
(provider-with-key passes; provider-without-key 400s; ollama/custom pass;
unknown provider fails open; empty id 400s). Full suite green except the 4
pre-existing better-sqlite3 ABI failures in usage.test.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* models validation: fail open on empty env-set (missing/unreadable .env)

A missing/unreadable agent .env yields an empty env-var set. The credential
check must NOT treat that as 'no credentials' and reject every enforced-provider
model — that's a worse false-reject than the bug being fixed. When the set is
empty, skip credential validation entirely (fail open); the empty-id guard
remains the floor. Verified guessDataDir co-locates .env with the config.yaml
the route already reads, so a non-empty set reliably reflects real keys.

sessions folder showed other people's conversations. A file tool

installBaselineTemplates only runs at agent create/duplicate, so existing
agents never receive artifacts added to infra/artifacts.json later (e.g.

  touch existing — solves the driving case with zero clobber risk
- pristine-update: an .artifacts-lock.json records shipped content hashes

Newly-installed enabled plugins are added to config.yaml plugins.enabled
(text-based, no YAML dep); container recreated only if something changed;
dryRun returns the plan without writing.

+ route (4 tests). Create path untouched (additive, low-risk): the lock
writes on first sync. Full suite green (317), tsc + eslint clean.

hits.message:
feat(door): add an ACP shim, with OpenCode as its first agent (#370)

* feat(door): add an ACP shim, with OpenCode as its first agent

The door gets one shim for any agent that speaks the Agent Client
Protocol over stdio. The shim is the ACP client: every permission
request goes to decide() as a tool_request, the door's yes must carry
the hash of the call asked about, only once-options are ever picked,
unmapped tool kinds and paths outside the scratch folder are refused
without asking, and no file or terminal client methods are offered.
Because ACP permission is advisory, the shim watches the agent's tool
updates: a call that ran without a yes ends the turn as an error and
drops the agent's process and session.

OpenCode 1.19.5 runs behind it as `--harness opencode`, with the door
as its only provider, its rules written by the shim, and a sealed cell
image built like the others. Conformance covers the shared suite and
the ask flow on a fake and on the real program, plus broken agents
and shims (ignores a reject, picks always, asks nobody).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): close the audit findings on the ACP shim

Give every OpenCode process a new, empty global config folder
(XDG_CONFIG_HOME, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR), so instructions, plugins or
rules a shell call wrote there are never read by a later process.
Checked on the real 1.19.5: a planted ~/.config AGENTS.md reached the
model before and does not now.

Catch a call reported finished between turns that was never given a
yes: the process is stopped and its session dropped. After a yes, a
call moved to a folder outside the scratch folder is a breach too, and
an edit that asks without a diff is refused.

Keep OpenCode out of the launcher until its Docker matrix is
committed, and say in the doc that the cell checks are not yet run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(door): keep the ACP transport loadable by plain Node

The cell and the rig run the lab's TypeScript with no build step, and
Node only strips types. A parameter property in the JSON-RPC error
class stopped both containers at import, before the cell reached the
door. Write the field out, and add a test that loads the shim, the ACP
client and the harness adapter under plain Node.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(door): remove the whole ACP gate for the cell's wall check

C10 tests the wall with the gate removed. For OpenCode the gate is
two things, the shim's veto and its watch on what the agent reports.
With only OpenCode's rules set to allow, the watch still ended the
turn, so the check could not show that the reply still comes from the
model. The cell now uses a wrapper that answers every permission
request itself and shows the shim no tool call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(door): commit the Docker matrix for OpenCode in the sealed cell

OpenCode 1.19.5 was run in the sealed cell on a machine with Docker:

fix(models): never pick a successor released before the current row

findSuccessor ranked dotted version segments numerically, so live
x-ai/grok-4.20 (released 2026-03) was the "successor" of grok-4.7
(2026-09) and an apply-mode scheduler would have downgraded a tracked
agent six months. Snapshot keys also mixed three domains (YYYYMMDD,
raw MMDD tokens, epoch strings) so deepseek-r1 (Jan 2025) sorted as the
newer snapshot of deepseek-r1-0528.

date in the id, else `created`); a version bump dated before the
current row is a near miss, never a successor; a snapshot bump must be
strictly newer.

fix(sanitization): fail closed on empty replies with the real cause (#286)

* fix(sanitization): fail closed on empty replies with the real cause

kimi-k3 reasons before it answers. On game-maker PR #3 a 70 KB test
file used the whole 4096-token budget on reasoning, so OpenRouter
returned 200 with empty content and finish_reason "length". The client
dropped finish_reason, usage and provider, and the gate failed with
"no verdict object in model reply: ''" and a hint to fix the extractor.

Raise the first budget to 16384 and retry an empty reply once at 65536.
A reply that is still empty fails closed as EmptyModelReply, naming the
file, finish_reason, token counts and provider. An error body inside a
200 reply is now a ModelReplyError. Reasoning text is never parsed for a
verdict. Bump the gate to 1.0.1.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4bKdY6Zp1z5ApBhPoJ

* fix(sanitization): close three false-green paths in the reply parser

The PR #286 audit found three ways a reply could pass that should not.

Content parts were joined whatever their type, so a reasoning part
holding {"flagged": false} could outrank the real flagged answer. Only
"text" parts (and plain strings) are now the answer.

A non-boolean "flagged" (null, "false", 0) went through bool() and read
as clean. Anything but a JSON boolean is now a fail-closed parse error.

The 180 s socket timeout is too short for a non-streamed 16k-65k token
reasoning reply. It is now 600 s, still bounded. A timeout raises
ModelTimeout naming the file and fails the layer closed.

fix: HSM create-new + Signal first-run correctness (6 bugs) (#134)

* fix(wizard): remove redundant inline Signal phone field (double-ask)

The create-new wizard asked for the Signal number twice: an inline
Phone field in the Platforms step AND again in the register/connect
dialog. Worse, the inline field was non-functional — the actual bond
only fires when signalCaptured is set (by the dialog), so a number
typed only inline never connected. Drop the inline field so the number
is entered once, in the dialog (which already handles the
already-registered case). Review step now shows the captured number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(config): derive compression summary_model from provider catalog

The template hardcoded summary_model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview for
every agent regardless of provider — an invalid, provider-agnostic model
that crash-loops compression on non-Google agents. Derive it instead from
MODEL_CATALOG: the provider's fallback-tier entry, else its local-tier
entry, else the caller's fallbackModel/primaryModel, emitted in litellm
provider/model form keyed by the provider itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deploy): deliver github token as literal GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

The agent .env only wrote GITHUB_TOKEN, but the github MCP server reads
GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN. The compose sets that var via ${GITHUB_TOKEN}
interpolation, which resolves from the (empty) process env rather than the
env_file — so the token never reached the server. Also emit the token as a
literal GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN line, mirroring how the llm key is
written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tools): discover platform_toolsets + fix empty-tools discovery guard

Two causes of 'No tools found' for a freshly created agent:

1. harness.ts seeded overlay.tools:[] and used `overlay.tools ?? auto`;
   since [] ?? x === [], auto-discovery never ran. Mirror the models guard:
   use overlay.tools only when non-empty, else auto-discover.

2. tools.ts discovery read a top-level toolsets:/mcp_servers: block, but a
   generated config.yaml writes platform_toolsets: — so a plain agent
   surfaced nothing. Parse platform_toolsets and flatten its per-platform
   arrays into toolset entries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(signal): place host-proxy.conf before compose up (first-run mount bug)

The signal deploy route runs docker compose with cwd=~/.hermes-swarm, so
the compose's ./host-proxy.conf bind-mount resolves there — but the route
never copied the conf, so Docker auto-created it as an empty DIRECTORY and
the nginx mount failed ('not a directory') on every first-time setup.
Copy infra/signal-cli/host-proxy.conf into ~/.hermes-swarm before 'up',
and self-heal a previously auto-created directory. Guards that the conf
source ships and the compose mounts it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(signal): default bot's Signal profile name to the harness name on bond

Fresh registration via the wizard already sets the profile to the bot
name (harnessName -> defaultDisplayName -> verify). But bonding an
already-registered number kept its old/generic profile ('Hermes Agent').
Set the Signal profile given-name to the harness name during connect
(best-effort, doesn't fail the bond) so the agent shows up under the name
it was created with regardless of registration path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(review): deliver github token via env_file only + fix ollama summary prefix

Addresses independent-audit blockers:
- github: the compose 'environment: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=${GITHUB_TOKEN}'
  override takes precedence over env_file and resolves from the empty process
  env, blanking the token. Remove the override entirely; the literal in the
  agent .env (env_file) is now the sole, working source. Inverted the test that
  had enshrined the buggy override.
- ollama summary_model: emitted 'ollama/<id>' but the model block declares
  provider 'custom' (with base_url), so 'ollama/' has no declared provider and
  won't resolve. Local providers now emit 'custom/<primaryModel>' (matches the
  declared provider, reuses the actually-served model). Cloud paths unchanged.

fix(keys): unify the provider list so the harness add-key menu offers custom (#185)

The "add key" dropdown existed twice: KEY_PROVIDERS in app/(dashboard)/keys/page.tsx
and a second, unrelated const of the same name in harnesses/[id]/page.tsx. Nothing
linked them, so they drifted in both directions — the harness-scoped menu lacked
`google` and `custom`, while the global menu lacked the twelve service providers
(zai, signal, mattermost, aws-bedrock, google-cloud, helius, coingecko, dehashed,
opencorporates, capsolver, open-measures, pexels).

The reported symptom was the missing `custom`: a harness could not be given a key
for any provider HSM doesn't know by name. Nothing server-side was stopping it —
POST /api/keys does no provider validation and KeyInput.provider is a plain string
— the option simply was not in that array.

Extract both into lib/key-providers.ts as the single list, plus providerOptions()
carrying over the unknown-provider escape hatch the keys page had (a ?request=
prefill would otherwise vanish from the harness dropdown).

`custom` also needs the env-var field, which the harness form never had: with no
PROVIDER_TO_VAR entry, resolveEnvVar falls back to the key's name and then to a
useless CUSTOM_API_KEY, so a custom key added from a harness would have landed in
the wrong variable. The field now renders there too, clears when the provider
changes away from custom, and is only sent for custom.

MODEL_PROVIDERS is deliberately untouched — that drives the model cascade editor,
not credential storage.

Tests pin the parity itself, since a redeclared local list is how this broke:
they fail if either page declares its own KEY_PROVIDERS, stops importing the
shared module, or drops the custom env-var field. Verified red against a
reintroduced local const. Full suite green (874).

fix(api): resolve every agent id through one shared step (#332)

* fix(surface-admins): match an id to exactly one agent

The surface admin store looked an agent up two ways: the stored row by
id, and the agent's data dir by a looser rule that accepts several
spellings of the same name. The two could disagree about which agent an
id meant, and a write for an id with no stored row added a new row for
it.

Every function now resolves the id once, to one agent, and uses that
agent's id for everything after: the admin list, the .env, the audit
entry and the container recreate. An id names an agent by its stored id
or its bare slug. Any other id is treated as no agent: reads return no
admins and no allowed groups, setAdmins and approveGroupInvite return
404, and nothing is written.

setAdmins no longer adds rows itself. An agent with no stored row yet
(a discovered container) is saved through HarnessService, and only when
HarnessService lists that id. The admins and groups routes recreate the
resolved agent instead of the id from the URL.

Tests cover each function and each route against the real service, with
the actor check asserted before any write.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* fix(harness): check a new agent's name before writing anything

Import and deploy make a new agent from a name. Both found out the name
was already a stored agent's only at the last step, when the row is
registered, after the data dir had been copied or scaffolded and the
.env patched.

HarnessService.nameTaken(name) answers from the stored rows whether a
name (as its slug, or the id built from it) is in use. importFromDir
asks it before the copy, the import route answers 409 from it, and the
deploy route answers 409 from it before its first write. The import
route also refuses a name or dataDir that is not a string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* fix(api): resolve every agent id through one shared step

Routes that take an agent id each did their own thing with it. Some
looked the agent up, some turned the id straight into a data dir, and
the routes that take ids in a request body (a key's assignedTo) did
neither.

lib/harness-ref.ts is now the one step. invalidHarnessId() checks the
shape (400). requireHarness() also resolves the id to the agent listed
under exactly that id (404). refuseUnknownHarnesses() does the same for
a list from a request body, keeping ids the record already holds.

- Every handler under /api/harnesses/[id] calls it first: the shape
  check on reads, the full resolve on anything that changes something.
- /api/keys POST and PUT resolve assignedTo before a key is stored or a
  .env is written. KeysService also checks the shape of every agent
  reference at add, setAssignment, rotateValue and writeKeyToEnv.
- Cascade apply and model-update apply resolve the body's harnessId
  first. The Signal PIN routes check its shape.
- Pairing DELETE accepts only a known platform name.

app/api/harness-id-sweep.test.ts walks every route file. Each must be
classified (id in the URL, id in the body, new-agent name, or no agent
id), and each one that takes an id must refuse a malformed or unknown
one before any service call or file write. A new route fails the sweep
until it is classified.

The three surfaces/[platform] routes keep resolving through
SurfaceAdminService, which accepts the bare slug agents send and reads
only the stored rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* fix(surface-admins): resolve the agent before a group invite is saved

approveGroupInvite appends a group to an agent's .env. For an id with a
stored row that agent is the row. For an id with no row it now has to be
an agent HarnessService lists (a discovered container), the rule
setAdmins already applies; otherwise the answer is 404 and nothing is
written. The lookup runs only after the invite has passed the policy
and admin check, so a refused invite costs no Docker discovery.

Tests also pin the agent shapes found on a running fleet, each called
by slug and by stored id: a stored row with a name, a stored row whose
name is null, and a running agent with no stored row. All keep their
admins, their group checks and their group-invite approval.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* test(api): cross-check the body fields each route reads

The route sweep knew which body fields carry an agent id only from its
own table, so a handler could start reading an id under a new field
name without the sweep noticing.

The sweep now reads every handler's source for the fields it takes from
a parsed JSON body or the query string, and each route's set must equal
what is declared for it: the id fields in BODY_ID (each swept on its
own) plus OTHER_FIELDS. A new field fails the sweep until it is
declared one way or the other. Handlers that pass the body on whole are
listed with where it goes, and id-like names declared as something else
each carry a reason.

Also: the key resync route checks the shape of the ids in `harnesses`
and joins the swept routes, and nameTaken's match on a stored name
(a row whose id was built from an earlier name) has its own tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y9VM4cL7LUkbCykWmcvDDi

* test(api): keep route bodies to the one form the sweep reads

The sweep's field reader follows `body = await request.json()` and a
destructuring of the same call. A handler that took its body any other
way (a clone, text, form data, the raw stream, or a parsed body under
another variable name) was not followed, so its fields were not
compared with the declared set.

The sweep now fails for a route file that reads the request body in
any form other than those two.

A door agent's first tools: file read, file write and a shell, all
inside the sealed cell, with a mode per class (never, ask, allow) and
an approval step in the chat room for ask. Says what is a wall and
what is a guardrail, how a later fetch-through-the-door tool would
work, and what is left out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(door): hold a tool for an admin's yes in the room

A class of tool on the ask list no longer makes decide() refuse the
whole record. It answers ask, and the door holds the call: it posts
the exact call in the room, written so nothing in it can hide or ping,
and waits for an admin. Only a reply to that request or a reaction on
it, from a user id on the admin list, is an answer. A bot, a named
bot, a role-holder and the agent itself are refused. No answer in time
is a no, and a yes is checked against the rules as they are when it
lands.

The yes that goes back to the cell carries a hash of the tool name and
input. Pi's gate now runs a call only on a yes that names that call's
hash, so a yes meant for another call does not fit. The gate also keeps
file tools in a scratch folder, links followed, puts a time limit on a
shell call before it asks, and cuts a tool's output before the model
sees it. The door counts tool calls per conversation per hour.

Ten harness-neutral tool checks go with it, each with a gate or a rig
broken on purpose that must turn it red, and they run for Pi as a
process and in the Docker cell. Letta Code's shim takes a plain yes or
no, so its adapter says why the checks are not run for it and its
matrix lists them as not run. All four matrices are regenerated from
real runs, because the list of known checks grew.

on by default, and a shell that is switched on asks an admin unless the
config says otherwise. The lists in the rules record are written from
it. A config that hears anyone in the channel now makes a public
record, and is refused outright if it also switches a tool on.

The folder the harness is started in becomes a mount in memory with a
size, owned by the user the cell runs as, and the dry run checks it:
as written, as Docker made it, and by filling it. Where a tool waits
for an admin, the cell is told to wait a little longer than the door,
and Discord is asked for reactions. The agent is told which tools it

fix(correctness): Batch D — operator-facing data-loss & integrity bugs (D1,D2,D3,D5,D6) (#158)

* fix(correctness): personal data dir, key discovery, decrypt-failure (D1,D2,D5)

Three operator-triggered data-integrity bugs (no attacker required).

D1 — personal harness wrong data dir. personal's data lives at ~/.hermes
(guessDataDir special-cases it), but duplicateOverlay() and remove()
hardcoded ~/.hermes-${name} → ~/.hermes-personal, which doesn't exist.
Duplicating personal produced an empty clone; deleting it targeted the
wrong dir. (Reachable once personal is persisted as an overlay, e.g. after
setting its model cascade — a routine dashboard action.) Both now resolve
through a shared `agentDataDirForName` helper. remove() additionally
guards the personal base ~/.hermes from dashboard deletion — it's the root
install, not a disposable overlay.

D2 — key discovery only scanned a hardcoded 8-name list, so harnesses
created via the app's own Create/Duplicate/Import UI (persisted in
harnesses.json) showed zero keys/tools/memory permanently. `list()` and
`getDecryptedValue()` now union in the overlay names via `allHarnessNames`.

D5 — getDecryptedValue returned the raw `iv:tag:ciphertext` string when
decryption failed (rotated/lost .key), handing a garbage credential to the
agent instead of failing loud. It now fails closed (undefined) for values
in our ciphertext format, while still returning genuine legacy plaintext
(pre-encryption values, which have no such shape) as-is.

Tests (RED→GREEN): keys-dataloss.test.ts (rotation → undefined, legacy
plaintext preserved, UI-harness key discovered), harness-personal-datadir
.test.ts (personal duplicate copies ~/.hermes; remove deletes normal dirs
but never ~/.hermes). Full suite: 688 passing; tsc clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ui): recreate on key assign/unassign; key ModelCascadeEditor (D3, D6)

D3 — assign/unassign key handlers issued a `quick` restart
(docker compose restart), which does NOT reload env_file. So a newly
assigned key never reached the running process, and a "removed" key stayed
live despite the success toast — a silent-failed revoke. Both now use
`recreate`, matching the add-key handler that already documents this exact
env_file-reload requirement.

D6 — ModelCascadeEditor had no `key`, so React reused the instance across
an in-app harness A→B navigation. The editor seeds its cascade into local
state once, so B's Models tab could render (and save) A's cascade. Added
`key={id}` to force a per-harness remount.

Note: these are client-side handlers with no unit-test seam in the current
vitest setup — verified by inspection against the sibling add-key handler
(D3) and standard React remount semantics (D6). tsc clean; no new lint.
Behavior confirmation belongs in the browser once deployed.

hits.message:
fix(discord): manage the vars that actually gate a Discord agent (#186)

* fix(discord): manage the vars that actually gate a Discord agent

HSM managed two DISCORD_* vars while the adapter decides whether to execute a
message using four. The two it did manage were reported with inverted semantics,
so the console could not show — let alone control — who can command an agent.
Found while auditing HSM as the control surface ahead of a community migration.

- DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES, DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS and DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS are now
  first-class settings. Roles are the only "admin class" primitive the runtime
  has; ignored-channels is the only channel deny that binds a bot holding
  Administrator; allow-bots is evaluated BEFORE the human allowlist and skips it,
  so a permissive value was a fourth authorization class invisible here.
  Each is written only when the client sends the field, so an older client cannot
  blank a hand-hardened value.

- Never write an empty DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS. The adapter gates on
  `if allowed_channels_raw:`, so empty skipped the channel check entirely and
  "no channels approved" meant "respond in EVERY channel". Writes a sentinel that
  no snowflake can match, mapped back to an empty list on read.

- GET reports an absent channel allowlist as unscoped rather than as a lockdown,
  so wide-open and locked-down stop rendering identically.

- Reject non-numeric role/channel IDs and unrecognized allowBots values. Both
  failure modes are silent AND fail-open at runtime: the adapter drops
  non-numeric roles with no log, and only compares against 'none' first, so a
  typo lands in the permissive branch.

- buildSettingsEnvValue no longer derives '*' from dmPolicy. These vars are the
  general allowlist, not a DM-only one, so a toggle labelled "DM Access Policy"
  granted every server member command access whenever a surface had no users.

- Regenerate the compose only when the VPN toggle actually changed. GET always
  emits vpnEnabled and both clients PUT the whole document back, so regeneration
  fired on every save, including permissions-only edits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(discord): close a fail-open found by independent review

Independent adversarial review of the first cut found that its most visible
change was itself a regression. Fixes all three blockers.

1. GET must not fold "unscoped" into allowAllGroups. Empty and '*' are DIFFERENT
   runtime states: _discord_channel_ids_allowed returns False on empty but True
   on '*', and _is_allowed_user uses it as the channel bypass for agents with no
   user/role allowlist. Both clients PUT back the document GET returns, so
   reporting an empty allowlist as allowAllGroups materialized a literal '*' and
   would have turned a fail-closed agent into one every guild member can command.
   Now reported as its own read-only `groupsUnscoped` field that PUT ignores.

2. DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS='*' is no longer erased. parseCommaList maps '*' to
   [], which wrote back empty — silently removing a guild-wide mute, the only
   kill switch that binds a bot holding Administrator.

3. Channel validation no longer requires numeric IDs. The adapter builds its gate
   keys from the snowflake, the bare name AND '#name', so configuring by name is
   supported; rejecting it 400'd the entire save, including every other
   platform's settings. Now rejects only values that would corrupt the env line
   (comma, whitespace, newline). The roles rule stays numeric — that one is
   correctly grounded in the adapter's .isdigit() filter.

Also: an unrecognized DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS is reported as permissive rather than
flattered to 'none' (the adapter compares 'none' then 'mentions' and lets
everything else fall through), and new Discord agents are seeded with a
deny-sentinel channel scope plus an explicit ALLOW_BOTS=none instead of being
born in the exact state that triggers the fail-open above.

Adds a round-trip suite — GET the document, PUT it back verbatim, assert access
never widens — which is the class of test that would have caught the original bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(discord): narrow the deny sentinel; stop validation deadlocking the page

Second independent review confirmed the three original blockers closed but found
the fix had inverted one of them and added a save-deadlock.

- The sentinel now applies ONLY when the operator actually clears a scoped agent.
  Every agent HSM deployed before this change carries an empty
  DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS, so echoing the GET document back was writing the
  sentinel and silently taking them offline in every channel. It also suppressed
  the adapter's config.yaml `discord.allowed_channels` fallback, which applies
  only when the env var is falsy — a live regression for YAML-scoped agents.
  When the operator really did clear a non-empty list, the var was already truthy,
  so YAML was already inactive and the sentinel changes nothing there.

- Validation now grandfathers values already on disk and checks only entries the
  operator introduces. GET emits what is on disk and both clients PUT the whole
  document back, so a hand-configured `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES=moderators` made the
  settings page permanently unsaveable for EVERY platform, with no console path to
  repair it.

- Channel names may contain spaces — voice, stage, forum and category names allow
  them and the adapter matches the name verbatim. Only commas and newlines are
  rejected now, since those corrupt the list format and the file respectively.

- The groups write uses the callback form of String.replace. A literal '$&' or
  '$`' in a channel name would otherwise splice surrounding file content —
  including DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN — into the written value. The adjacent users path
  and this repo's surface-admins.ts already model this.

Adds coverage for the previously untested hunks: the fail-closed new-agent seed
and its explicit ALLOW_BOTS=none.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(discord): derive the sentinel from disk; reject space-then-# in channels

Third review round. Both findings were real.

- The sentinel decision no longer trusts the client's `groupsUnscoped`. Neither
  client refetches after a save, so an operator who scoped an agent and then
  cleared it again in the same page session was still echoing
  groupsUnscoped:true — suppressing the sentinel and leaving the agent answering
  in every channel while the console showed "no channels approved". That is the
  original fail-open, reintroduced through a client contract. The previous value
  is now read from the .env, which makes the invariant structural. It also closes
  the two paths where the sentinel could still land on a previously-falsy var and
  suppress config.yaml's discord.allowed_channels fallback.

- Channel entries containing whitespace-then-# are rejected. This .env is consumed
  as a compose env_file and Docker treats that as an inline comment: verified
  against the compose CLI, `A=mute #2` reaches the container as `mute`. On

feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable (#265)

* feat(sanitization): make the gate canonical and reusable

Per-repo copies of check_sanitization.py drifted apart, each missing a
protection another copy had. swarm-map becomes the one home: the
script, the union of every copy's self-tests, and a reusable workflow
(sanitization-gate.yml) other repos call pinned to a
sanitization-gate-v* tag. Each repo keeps only sanitize.config.json.

The canonical script merges the Matilde/osint-engine base (fail-closed
semantic layer, fork-PR honesty, match-scoped allowlist, broadest
detector set) with swarm-map's --diff scope, separated international
phones, public-IP and fiction-phone filters (now opt-in config), and
ASG's per-content verdict cache. It adds --check-config and
--require-config. The swarm-map-specific reviewer prompt moves out of
the script into swarm-map's own sanitize.config.json.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close audit bypasses in the gate

An audit of the canonical gate found silent skips that let a real
token pass. git C-quoted non-ASCII paths, so docs/café.md was never
found on disk; one non-UTF-8 byte made layer 1 skip a whole file; an
allow_substrings entry of "" or a skip_paths entry of "."/"**"
disabled layer 1 and was only checked under --check-config; and the
reusable workflow accepted pull_request_target, which scans the base
with the key exposed.

Paths now come from git with -z, a listed path missing from disk is a
hard failure (deletions are excluded from --diff), binaries are judged
by NUL bytes and text is decoded with replacement, structural config
validation runs on every gate run, and pull_request_target is refused.
The workflow docs now say consumers must make the check required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): stop config and encodings from disabling layer 1

A re-audit found the PR under review controlled its own rules and that
some files escaped layer 1 entirely. sanitize.config.json was read from
the PR head and could set deterministic.enabled false, narrow scope,
skip any path, or allow "sk-ant-" as a substring; and one NUL byte or
UTF-16 encoding skipped a file in both layers.

On pull_request the reusable workflow now scans with the base commit's
config (SANITIZE_CONFIG) and notices a config change. Layer 1 cannot be
disabled or narrowed, skip_paths accepts only test-fixture paths, and
allow entries match exactly (plus email-domain and /24 forms). Layer 1
decodes UTF-16/32, reads other NUL-bearing files as latin-1, and scans
symlink target strings. swarm-map's config drops scope and lists its
fixture files and exact known values instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): judge home-repo PRs with the base gate

In swarm-map the gate judged a PR with the PR's own script, so a PR
could weaken the gate that judged it. On pull_request the reusable
workflow now runs the judging steps with the base commit's script; the
PR's script is still exercised by the self-tests, and a notice says when
the script changed. The garden guild id leaves the allowlist: #266
moves it out of source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): close round-3 audit gaps

Threat model, now written down: the gate stops accidental leaks by
trusted committers and their agents; required checks and CODEOWNERS
cover a malicious committer.

Layer 1 scans the union of the decoded text and the raw latin-1 bytes,
so a stray BOM cannot hide an ASCII token. skip_paths match by path
segment, never as bare string prefixes; inside them provider tokens and
private keys are still reported, and .env/.pem/.key/id_* files are
never skipped. The workflow no longer runs git fetch (it failed in
private repos without persisted credentials), refuses a gate_ref that
is not a release tag or full SHA, and swarm-map's caller drops its
paths filter so the check reports on every PR. Adds CODEOWNERS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): ship the workflow to consumers' self-tests

The self-tests now check the reusable workflow itself, but consumers'
sparse checkout of the gate left it out, so their self-test step
failed. Also drop a personal name from the threat model wording.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): catch JSON assignments and fleet provider tokens

Round-4 audit. Credential-assignment patterns required the separator
right after the key, so JSON ("api_key": "...") never matched; they
now allow a closing quote on the key, while template words, env-var
names and lowercase slugs stay quiet. Adds high-confidence patterns for
the fleet's providers (OpenRouter, Discord bot tokens and webhooks,
Telegram, Hugging Face, npm, GitLab, OpenAI project and service-account
keys), also reported inside fixture paths, as are JWTs. Card detection
now needs a real issuer prefix and length, so Discord snowflakes no
longer read as card numbers.

hits.message:
feat(runtime): add door agents from a form, and run Letta Code behind a door (#350)

* feat(runtime): let the door launcher run Letta Code as well as Pi

The launcher put Pi in the cell and nothing else. The harness is now a
setting of the config: `"harness": "letta-code"` picks Letta Code's
shim, its cell image and what it declares about itself. A config with
no `harness` key is a Pi config, read and rendered as before, so the
command, the config keys and the state folder are unchanged for an
agent that already runs from it.

The dry run names the harness, the one version that is pinned and
what it cannot do. Letta Code keeps one memory for the whole agent,
so it has one room only; the door already enforces that, and the dry
run now says it.

Letta Code is told what Pi is told, in place of its own system
prompt. It adds starting notes of its own after that text, so the
text ends by saying what those notes are.

A start no longer depends on the cell dialling after the door is
listening: a cell that dialled too early is started again once, by
name, and looked at again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(runtime): make Letta Code door agents from the dashboard

Creating a door agent now takes a harness and one line about what
the agent is for, and Letta Code is accepted. The record's harness
is fixed when the agent is made: the launcher's config is rendered
with it, an edit of the rules cannot change it, and a Pi agent's
config is written exactly as before.

The name rule moves to one plain function that the server and the
create form both call, so the form can say a name is taken while it
is typed. The server's answer is still the one that counts.

The agent view now carries which harness is in the cell, the one
version that is pinned and what it cannot do, and who started the
door that is running: this page, a supervisor, or something else.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(ui): add door agents from a form, and say more on their page

"Add door agent" opened the browser's own prompt. It is now a small
dialog: a name checked while it is typed, a choice of Pi or Letta
Code with what each cannot do, one line of description, and what
has to be done by hand with a link to the runbook. A new agent's
page opens on its Rules tab.

Remove and Stop for a door agent ask in the app's confirm dialog,
on the fleet page and on the agent's page. Nothing in the door
agent pages uses a browser pop-up.

The Overview names the harness and its pinned version, says when
the cell's seal was last checked or that it never was, and says who
started a running door. For Letta Code the Rules tab says, beside
the channel, that it has that one room only. The sidebar no longer
names one harness under the app's name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): start the cell again when it has not reached the door

The launcher starts the cell before the door is listening, so the
cell can be looked at from outside first. The relay takes the cell's
dial whether or not the door is there yet, and a cell that said
hello to nobody does not dial again. Which came first was a matter
of milliseconds.

A cell that has not reached the door three seconds after the door is
up is now stopped, the door is given time to drop any link it held,
and the cell is started again and checked from outside again. Both
launcher suites start a door this way on purpose.

The dashboard also forgets which process it started once that door
is stopped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): fail a start whose door still holds a stopped cell's link

When a cell is started again, the door is given up to five seconds
to see the stopped cell's link close. If it had not, the start went
on, and the wait that followed read the old link as the cell that
came back: a start with no cell behind it could be called live.
That start now fails, and nothing is left running.

The step is now one function that is handed the door, Docker and
the clock, so its waits are tested to the millisecond with no
sleeping: once and no more, the seal looked at again before the
wait, and every way it can fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(runtime): read a door agent written before the harness setting

The fixtures are the record, config, start script, fleet row, dry
run and run on record of a Pi door agent, written by the code as it
was before a harness could be named. The test shows nothing needs
migrating: the agent is listed and reported as it was, the old
config is still a Pi config with the same policy hash, and what is
rendered from the old record is byte for byte what was rendered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ui): say only what is known about who started a door

A running door that Swarm Map has no note of starting was said to be
started by "not this page". A door the page started before that note
was kept is shown the same way, so the flat statement could be
false. It now says there is no note and that no supervisor was seen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): stop the cell with the flag every Docker takes

The cell is stopped with `docker stop --time 1` before it is started
again. Docker no longer lists `--time`, only `-t` and `--timeout`,
and a Docker that drops the old spelling would fail every start
that needs the cell started again. It now uses `-t`.

feat(ci): sanitization gate for the base package (#65)

* feat(ci): sanitization gate for the base package

The base package (infra/templates/**, docs, base skills/soul) ships to every
agent, so it must never contain secrets, PII, or use-case-specific particulars —
even from an automated contribution. Adds a layered, fail-closed gate:

- scripts/check_sanitization.py — deterministic layer (secret/API keys, private
  keys, JWTs, quoted hardcoded creds, real emails, phones; placeholder-aware, no
  API key needed) + an LLM particulars layer (use-case-specific names/orgs/IDs/
  case details). Full-tree (--all) so a pre-existing leak can't hide in an
  untouched file. Both must pass; a missing LLM key fails closed.
- .github/workflows/sanitization.yml — runs the scanner's own tests + the
  full-tree base scan on every PR.
- Sanitized a real pre-existing leak (operator SSH target) from a base doc.

TDD: 18 scanner tests; the base now scans clean (deterministic layer).

NOTE: set the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repo secret to enable the semantic layer; the
deterministic layer enforces without it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* harden(sanitization): close adversarial-audit holes

Independent audit found a critical bypass + coverage gaps. Fixes:
- CRITICAL: placeholder check no longer skips a finding on an internal char run
  (an attacker could pad a real secret with `0000000…` to hide it). Now only a
  WHOLLY low-entropy body counts as a placeholder.
- Added key families: Stripe, Twilio, SendGrid, Slack webhook, Bearer, Basic
  auth, and credential connection strings (scheme://user:pass@host).
- Unquoted hardcoded credentials (YAML/.env) now caught, entropy-gated so code
  identifiers / function calls (token = foo()) are not false-positived.
- PII: international phones, SSNs, Luhn-validated card numbers, and public IPv4
  (private/CGNAT/doc/loopback excluded as examples, not leaks). Reserved 555
  phone range treated as a placeholder.
- Semantic layer hardened against prompt injection: scanned content fenced with
  a random nonce + system prompt marks it untrusted, never instructions.
- gather_base_files / select_sensitive_files / workflow paths reconciled to cover
  top-level SOUL* so a leak there can't dodge the full-tree run.

TDD: 36 tests (incl. every audit hole as a regression). Base scans clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* harden(sanitization): tighten RFC5737 doc-IP range to /24; document the unquoted-all-letter gap

Re-audit follow-ups (both non-blocking): public IPs in 192.0/16, 198.51/16,
203.0/16 outside the actual /24 doc ranges are now flagged; the accepted
unquoted-all-letter-secret gap is documented (closing it would false-positive on
code identifiers).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sanitization): clean fail-closed message on empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

feat(artifacts): git-sourced artifacts behind a security trust gate (#96)

* feat(artifacts): parse + validate git:<org>/<repo>#<tag> artifact sources

First step of git-sourced (third-party) artifact support. parseGitSource is the
security front door: returns null for non-git sources, and throws loudly on any
git-prefixed source that is unpinned (pinning to a tag is mandatory — an
unpinned ref can silently drift to malicious code), malformed, or carries unsafe
characters / path traversal (the ref later feeds a git command). Pure function,
no network — to be wired into installArtifacts behind the capability + injection
trust gate.

TDD: 9 new tests; existing loader tests still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(artifacts): TS port of the threat-pattern scanner (pre-install gate)

Faithful TS port of the image-side tools/threat_patterns.py library (prompt
injection / promptware / exfiltration) with the same all/context/strict scope
semantics and invisible-unicode detection. HSM uses scanForThreats as the EARLY
gate when installing git-sourced artifacts; the Python scanner in the agent
image remains the authoritative runtime backstop (defense in depth). Keep the
two in sync when upstream patterns change.

TDD: 8 new tests; git-source + loader suites still pass (28 total).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(artifacts): pre-install content-scan gate for fetched artifacts

gateArtifactDir() walks a fetched git-sourced artifact directory and scans every
text file with the TS threat-pattern scanner (context scope) before install.
Binary/oversized files and .git are skipped. Returns ok=false with per-file
findings so the caller can refuse a poisoned artifact (loud failure) instead of
copying it onto disk.

TDD: 4 new tests; full lib/services suite 32 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(artifacts): install git-sourced artifacts behind the trust gate

Wires parse -> fetch -> gate -> install. installArtifacts now handles
git:<org>/<repo>#<tag> sources by shallow-cloning at the pinned tag
(fetchGitArtifact), running the content-scan gate (gateArtifactDir), and
REFUSING (throwing) when injection / promptware is found instead of copying a
poisoned artifact onto disk. The fetcher is injectable for hermetic testing.
Local sources are unchanged.

The Phase-1 "git is unsupported" contract test now asserts a genuinely
unsupported scheme, since git is first-class.

TDD: 5 new tests (real git clone via a local fixture + gate wiring via an
injected fetcher); full lib/services suite 192 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(artifacts): wire git build-time token into install + align design docs

installBaselineTemplates now reads the git build-time token from the HSM-server
env (ARTIFACT_GIT_TOKEN, fallback GITHUB_TOKEN) and passes it to installArtifacts
— distinct from the per-agent runtime token, the agent never sees it. No call-site
changes (all three creation paths route through this wrapper) and a no-op for
today's local-only manifest, so git-sourced artifacts become reachable from the
real agent-create/deploy path without changing local behaviour.

Docs aligned with the implementation:
- artifact-commons-design.md: Phase 2 records the implemented git: fetch and the
  install-time trust gate (new vs the original design); status + risk #5 updated.
- image-vs-hsm-boundary.md: adds a "third-party / git-sourced artifact" example —
  HSM early pre-install scan + image runtime backstop (defense in depth).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* security(artifacts): keep build-time token out of argv/URL/errors + runbook

The git build-time token was embedded in the clone URL, so a failed clone
printed it (process args + error). Now the token is delivered via GIT_ASKPASS
with an x-access-token username — never in the URL or argv — and any clone error
is run through redactSecrets() (scrubs the known value + GitHub token shapes +
user:secret@ URLs). Also fixes auth for ghu_/fine-grained tokens (token-as-
username didn't authenticate).

Adds docs/runbooks/git-sourced-artifacts.md documenting the end-to-end process
(private repo -> tag -> manifest -> ARTIFACT_GIT_TOKEN [PAT w/ contents:read] ->
fetch+gate+install -> flip visibility to publish).

TDD: redact-secrets tests; git-fetch fixture + full lib/services suite green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(runbook): manifest must reference the artifact subdir (#tag:<subdir>)

Verified live: a single repo holds a co-located plugin+skill; each manifest
entry points at its own subdir (hermes-plugin / hermes-skill) so plugin.yaml
lands at plugins/<name>/plugin.yaml. Without the subdir the repo root is copied
and the runtime can't find the plugin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* security(artifacts): close trust-gate audit findings (pinning, symlinks, scanner evasions)

Independent adversarial audit of the git-artifact trust gate found three
exploitable gaps; all now closed (TDD), re-audited CLOSED-ALL.

- Pinning: reject mutable refs. parseGitSource fast-fails HEAD/main/master/
  develop; fetchGitArtifact runs an authoritative `git ls-remote --heads`
  BEFORE clone and refuses any ref that resolves to a branch (catches arbitrary
  branch names, incl. SHA-shaped ones).
- Symlinks: the gate walk now flags symlinks as a finding instead of silently
  skipping them (cp copies symlinks verbatim) — refusal happens before any copy.
- Scanner evasions: oversized files (>MAX_SCAN_BYTES) are refused not skipped;
  NUL-byte files are scanned with NULs stripped instead of being treated as
  binary and skipped.

No shell introduced; new ls-remote uses execFileSync + -- guard + GIT_ASKPASS
token delivery + error redaction.

Follow-ups (pre-existing, non-blocking): raw commit-SHA pins need fetch-then-
checkout (clone --branch can't take a SHA; currently fails closed); consider
'strict' scan scope for git-sourced skill installs.

feat(hsm): person_memory default + first-class observe-unmentioned toggle (#217)

* feat(hsm): person_memory as a provisioning default (repo-homed, manifest bug fixed)

Repo-homes the person_memory plugin under infra/templates/plugins/ (it lived
only in agent data dirs) and enables it by default in infra/artifacts.json, so
every HSM-provisioned agent gets per-person adaptive context.

- Manifest name fixed to 'person_memory' (underscore). It shipped as
  'person-memory' (dash) while configs enable the underscore form; the loader
  matches on manifest name (hermes_cli/plugins.py), so it was silently
  discovered-but-never-enabled on every agent. This is the whole fix.
- Read-only, fail-open, never touches the system prompt (cache-safe).
- Boundary review clears: reads only its own memory_dir/people; the injected
  directive is behavioral (display_name/role/tech-level/comm-style), never raw
  identifiers — manifest carries a note to keep raw IDs out of Notable context,
  which matters given shared group sessions are the HSM default.

Resolves #213.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(hsm): first-class observe-unmentioned toggle, decoupled from mention-gating

Observe-unmentioned becomes a proper harness setting instead of a hidden
derivative of mention-gating. Agents ingest unmentioned channel messages as
context (they still only respond per the mention gate) — input and output are
now orthogonal.

- Settings API: add observeUnmentioned to SettingsResponse; GET derives it from
  the observe env vars (default ON, matching the deploy template); PUT writes it
  from body.observeUnmentioned instead of body.mentionGating (the decoupling).
- UI: dedicated 'Observe Unmentioned Messages' toggle; removed the stale
  'observes silently' clause from the mention-gating copy.
- Registry: add the Slack + Discord observe seam (SLACK_/DISCORD_OBSERVE_
  UNMENTIONED) now that hermes-agent-mt#142 ships the adapter support; harmless
  no-op env on agents whose image predates it, activates once rebuilt.
- Tests: registry golden counts (+2 vars), orthogonality cases (observe stays
  true when mention-gating off; observe can be turned off independently),
  byte-identical fixtures updated. 80 pass, tsc clean.

Resolves #214.

Changelog

Sourced from react-router's changelog.

v8.4.0

Minor Changes

  • Deprecate the createStaticRouter({ branches }) option (#15297)
    • createStaticRouter now caches route branches internally, ignores branches, and logs a deprecation warning when the option is provided
    • The deprecated EntryContext.branches property remains available for compatibility but is always an empty array

Patch Changes

  • Prevent stale route discovery during manifest version-mismatch recovery (#15489)
    • Keep concurrent manifest responses pending while a document reload is in progress
    • Report a discovery error when a previous reload failed to resolve a version mismatch instead of loading a stale route or reloading repeatedly
    • Fail pending requests if a document reload does not complete within five seconds or the document is restored from the back-forward cache, allowing subsequent requests to recover
  • Preserve lazy route module import errors during SPA navigations instead of replacing them with a missing dataStrategy result error (#15464)
  • Switch to more granular internal router contexts to avoid unnecessary route component re-renders when unrelated data router state changes (#15376)
    • ⚠️ This contains some breaking changes to exported UNSAFE_ contexts, so please review carefully if you are using those unsafe exports
  • Correctly escape streamed RSC redirect locations in meta tag attributes (#15491)
  • Avoid unintended document.startViewTransition calls during initial hydration and router.revalidate() calls (#15484)
  • Fix SingleFetchNoResultError thrown when a fetcher revalidates against a splat route during lazy route discovery (#15395)
    • Track discovery per fetcher load so revalidation waits for the current load's discovery, even when the fetcher key is reused, while still restarting interrupted loaders after discovery completes
  • Preserve the underlying decode failure as the cause of the Unable to decode turbo-stream response error (#15450)

Unstable Changes

⚠️ Unstable features are not recommended for production use

  • Add a Data Mode future.unstable_routePatternMatching flag for more efficient route matching powered by @remix-run/route-pattern (#15298)
    • Add an unstable_validateParams route field to reject invalid parameter values and continue matching
  • Document access control requirements for RSC Server Functions (#15490)
    • Treat every Server Function as a public endpoint that must perform all of its own access control checks
    • Recommend route actions when access control should be provided by route middleware

v8.3.1

Patch Changes

  • Fix Expected fetcher: <key> error thrown on navigation when a fetcher is aborted during its post-action revalidation (#15365)
  • Fix lazy route discovery caching a path as discovered when the triggering navigation was aborted after the manifest response settled but before the route tree was patched, which permanently (for the session) shadowed the real route behind a catch-all or produced 404s on every subsequent visit (#15399)
  • Improve route matching performance for long paths (#15417)
  • Improve validation of action request origins (#15419)
  • Fix <ScrollRestoration> leaving history.scrollRestoration set to "auto" after a bfcache restore, which let the browser restore scroll on subsequent history traversals before the destination route had rendered (#15397)
  • Properly respect the relative option in useSubmit/fetcher.submit when resolivng the action path (#15400)
  • Add additional URL validation on client side navigations/redirects (#15445)

v8.3.0

Patch Changes

  • Encode path params in href/generatePath

4.0.37

  • c70adf6: Fix TypeSafe decision requests with primitive JSON state by serializing those values as text, reject empty criteria and null or undefined Score levels before sending a request, and expose structured Score legends in provider metadata. Allow omitted or null Box instructions and null Boolean criteria in experimental decision question types.

4.0.36

Patch Changes

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

  • e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.

  • 892af4d: feat (provider): add server-side realtime extensions to the experimental RealtimeModelV4 spec

    Extends the existing optional getServerWebSocketConfig() method and a normalized usage field so a trusted server/proxy can drive realtime providers the way it drives HTTP language models:

    • getServerWebSocketConfig({ intent? }) returns the upstream WebSocket { url, headers, protocols? } for a server-initiated connection (header auth with the long-lived credential). Providers fail fast for unsupported endpoint intents instead of silently falling back. It is the server-side sibling of the browser-only getWebSocketConfig.
    • serializeClientEvent and buildSessionConfig now accept the same optional intent so server-side callers can keep endpoint selection and session serialization aligned.
    • New RealtimeModelV4Usage type and optional usage on response-done, input-transcription-completed, and provider custom snapshot events. Gross totals and known modality buckets remain separate, and duration is reported as seconds. Counts are gross (cache-inclusive) with cached portions reported separately so consumers can apply their own billing split without re-parsing raw.
    • New RealtimeModelV4ServerConnection and RealtimeModelV4SessionIntent types, exported with the Experimental_ prefix.

OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.

Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new ping union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.

The stable SpeechModelV4 is unchanged.

4.0.32

Patch Changes

  • 10026d1: Add the interrupted finish reason for provider streams that end without a completion signal. Preserve partial output without introducing an error solely for interruption, and stop tool execution, agent continuation, and automatic UI follow-ups for interrupted responses, including late tool results and approvals. Provider detection and emission will be added separately.

    Compatibility notice: Adding interrupted to the public finish-reason types can break type checking after upgrading, even though this is a patch release. Exhaustive switches (for example, using an assertNever fallback) and mappings such as Record<FinishReason, string> must handle the new value. Update any custom validation or application logic that assumes the existing set of finish reasons is exhaustive.

    When providers begin emitting interrupted, a stream ending without a completion signal will preserve partial output and report this finish reason without emitting an error solely for the interruption. Applications that need to detect incomplete responses should check finishReason === 'interrupted' as well as their existing error handling.

v2.14.3 (2026-11-04)

Packaging

This is now fixed: starting in v2.14.3, we no longer publish GraalPy 3.11 wheels, and GraalPy 3.13 wheels are now published together with the existing 3.12 one.

  • Skip annotation handler setup when annotations are empty by @​alexmojaki in #14149
  • Fix quadratic serialization time with per-index include/exclude on sequences by @​Viicos in #14160
  • Avoid type lookups when checking for None during serialization by @​Viicos in #14167
  • Improve performance of model serialization by @​Viicos in #14171

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. python/v1.21.0

Major Features

Custom HTTP Client Support for OpenAI and Gemini - PR#1366

The OpenAI and Gemini model providers now accept a pre-configured client via the client parameter, enabling connection pooling, proxy configuration, custom timeouts, and centralized observability across all model requests. The client is reused for all requests and its lifecycle is managed by the caller, not the model provider.

from strands.models.openai import OpenAIModel
import httpx

Create custom client with proxy and timeout configuration


custom_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
proxy="http://proxy.example.com:8080",
timeout=60.0
)


model = OpenAIModel(model_id="gpt-4o-mini", client=custom_client)

4.0.35

Patch Changes

  • dcd2f8d: Introduce a model entry contract with named capability sections and request configuration. Consolidate the OpenAI and Anthropic model catalogs so existing request behavior and generated capability documentation use the same source of truth. Catalogs also declare the provider options each provider accepts and which models support them.

4.0.34

Patch Changes

  • 5475347: Fix non-streaming Responses API structured output failing when multiple assistant messages contain JSON. Providers can supply separate structured-output text for parsing, allowing OpenAI and Azure Responses models to select the last final_answer while preserving all generated content, annotations, conversation history, and token usage.
  • e729d58: chore(docs): update README.md for consistent format and to avoid duplication

4.0.33

Patch Changes

  • 85d84a1: feat(provider): add experimental streaming speech model spec

    Adds Experimental_StreamingSpeechModelV4, a SpeechModelV4 extension with doStream() that takes the input text as a stream of text parts (each with an optional per-part voice and providerOptions) and returns a stream of audio parts, plus Experimental_-prefixed stream option, text part, part, result, and usage types. The stable SpeechModelV4 is unchanged.

4.0.32

Patch Changes

  • 10026d1: Add the interrupted finish reason for provider streams that end without a completion signal. Preserve partial output without introducing an error solely for interruption, and stop tool execution, agent continuation, and automatic UI follow-ups for interrupted responses, including late tool results and approvals. Provider detection and emission will be added separately.

    Compatibility notice: Adding interrupted to the public finish-reason types can break type checking after upgrading, even though this is a patch release. Exhaustive switches (for example, using an assertNever fallback) and mappings such as Record<FinishReason, string> must handle the new value. Update any custom validation or application logic that assumes the existing set of finish reasons is exhaustive.

    When providers begin emitting interrupted, a stream ending without a completion signal will preserve partial output and report this finish reason without emitting an error solely for the interruption. Applications that need to detect incomplete responses should check finishReason === 'interrupted' as well as their existing error handling.

4.0.31

Patch Changes

  • 0c2a9de: Add maxOutputTokens and reasoning to experimental decision calls and forward them to language-model-backed decisions. Language-model adapters keep reasoning disabled when omitted. Native decision providers warn when either setting is unsupported.

4.0.30

Patch Changes

  • 60cc252: feat(perplexity): add decisions api support

4.0.29

Patch Changes

  • 0957554: Add box decision question type with image bounds for TypeSafe AI.
