Updates `@ai-sdk/provider` from 4.0.13 to 4.0.37
Changelog

Sourced from @​ai-sdk/provider's changelog.

4.0.37

Patch Changes

  • c70adf6: Fix TypeSafe decision requests with primitive JSON state by serializing those values as text, reject empty criteria and null or undefined Score levels before sending a request, and expose structured Score legends in provider metadata. Allow omitted or null Box instructions and null Boolean criteria in experimental decision question types.

4.0.36

Patch Changes

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

  • e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.

  • 892af4d: feat (provider): add server-side realtime extensions to the experimental RealtimeModelV4 spec

    Extends the existing optional getServerWebSocketConfig() method and a normalized usage field so a trusted server/proxy can drive realtime providers the way it drives HTTP language models:

    • getServerWebSocketConfig({ intent? }) returns the upstream WebSocket { url, headers, protocols? } for a server-initiated connection (header auth with the long-lived credential). Providers fail fast for unsupported endpoint intents instead of silently falling back. It is the server-side sibling of the browser-only getWebSocketConfig.
    • serializeClientEvent and buildSessionConfig now accept the same optional intent so server-side callers can keep endpoint selection and session serialization aligned.
    • New RealtimeModelV4Usage type and optional usage on response-done, input-transcription-completed, and provider custom snapshot events. Gross totals and known modality buckets remain separate, and duration is reported as seconds. Counts are gross (cache-inclusive) with cached portions reported separately so consumers can apply their own billing split without re-parsing raw.
    • New RealtimeModelV4ServerConnection and RealtimeModelV4SessionIntent types, exported with the Experimental_ prefix.

  • 41465fd: Expose optional transcription word timings separately from segments and accept shared timestampGranularities. Explicit provider timing settings take precedence. OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.

  • 9754014: Add typed streaming heartbeat parts. Anthropic emits them only with includePings: true (disabled by default), without requiring raw chunks. Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new ping union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.

  • 4bb73b0: Add optional video, reranking and decision sections to model capability catalogs, including support for declaring provider options for these operations.

  • 2e44144: Represent videos delivered directly to caller-managed storage with an explicit uploaded outcome. Video generation reports uploadedVideos without downloading or synthesizing video bytes; access video only when videos is nonempty.

  • dcd2f8d: Introduce a model entry contract with named capability sections and request configuration. Consolidate the OpenAI and Anthropic model catalogs so existing request behavior and generated capability documentation use the same source of truth. Catalogs also declare the provider options each provider accepts and which models support them.

v2.14.2 2026-10-29

v2.14.2 (2026-10-29)

This release addresses 2 security issues, https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-qpmf-fgh3-ff25 and https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-3r8g-cqwr-jr29.

Packaging

  • Bump PyO3 to 0.30.1, jiter to 0.18.0, use PyFrozenDict by @​Viicos in #14003
  • Bump speedate to v0.18.0 by @​Viicos in #14007
  • Publish pydantic-core wheels for PyPy 8.0 (pp80 ABI) by @​Viicos in #14083

Performance

  • Avoid Python tuple allocation during model fields validation by @​Viicos in #13955
  • Lazily call repr of values during nested union serialization by @​Viicos in #14082
  • Skip decorator field checks when no field decorators exist by @​alexmojaki in #14111
  • Avoid heap allocation for small JSON model field buffers by @​alexmojaki in #14113

Fixes

  • Make JSON validation by iteration consistent with Python approach by @​davidhewitt in #13275.

    JSON validation now handles field lookup and extra data the same way as Python validation. In particular, keys that only match an unused alias or field name are now treated as extra data, instead of being silently dropped:

    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel

    class Page(BaseModel):
    
model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid', alias_generator=to_camel)
    

    page_size: int = 10

    

    Page.model_validate_json('{"page_size": 50}')
    

    Before: Page(page_size=10)
    

    After: ValidationError (extra_forbidden)

    See the pull request for the full list of behavior changes. This change addresses https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-qpmf-fgh3-ff25.

  • Ignore extra data matching a field name in TypedDict and dataclasses with extra=allow by @​Viicos in #14090. Addresses https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-3r8g-cqwr-jr29.

  • Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module by @​Viicos in #13994

  • Support explicit by_alias overriding validate_by_alias in validation JSON schemas by @​Viicos in #13997

  • Fix mypy plugin crash on deferred empty model by @​ilevkivskyi in #14027

  • Fix infinite recursion when validating an invalid default with PydanticUseDefault by @​Viicos in #14028

  • Implement recursion guard for validate_strings() by @​Viicos in #14029

v1.106.0

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

4.0.38

4.0.37

Patch Changes

  • c70adf6: Fix TypeSafe decision requests with primitive JSON state by serializing those values as text, reject empty criteria and null or undefined Score levels before sending a request, and expose structured Score legends in provider metadata. Allow omitted or null Box instructions and null Boolean criteria in experimental decision question types.

4.0.36

Patch Changes

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

  • e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.

  • 892af4d: feat (provider): add server-side realtime extensions to the experimental RealtimeModelV4 spec

    Extends the existing optional getServerWebSocketConfig() method and a normalized usage field so a trusted server/proxy can drive realtime providers the way it drives HTTP language models:

    • getServerWebSocketConfig({ intent? }) returns the upstream WebSocket { url, headers, protocols? } for a server-initiated connection (header auth with the long-lived credential). Providers fail fast for unsupported endpoint intents instead of silently falling back. It is the server-side sibling of the browser-only getWebSocketConfig.
    • serializeClientEvent and buildSessionConfig now accept the same optional intent so server-side callers can keep endpoint selection and session serialization aligned.
    • New RealtimeModelV4Usage type and optional usage on response-done, input-transcription-completed, and provider custom snapshot events. Gross totals and known modality buckets remain separate, and duration is reported as seconds. Counts are gross (cache-inclusive) with cached portions reported separately so consumers can apply their own billing split without re-parsing raw.
    • New RealtimeModelV4ServerConnection and RealtimeModelV4SessionIntent types, exported with the Experimental_ prefix.

  • 41465fd: Expose optional transcription word timings separately from segments and accept shared timestampGranularities. Explicit provider timing settings take precedence. OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.

  • 9754014: Add typed streaming heartbeat parts. Anthropic emits them only with includePings: true (disabled by default), without requiring raw chunks. Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new ping union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.

  • 4bb73b0: Add optional video, reranking and decision sections to model capability catalogs, including support for declaring provider options for these operations.

  • 2e44144: Represent videos delivered directly to caller-managed storage with an explicit uploaded outcome. Video generation reports uploadedVideos without downloading or synthesizing video bytes; access video only when videos is nonempty.

4.0.35

Patch Changes

  • dcd2f8d: Introduce a model entry contract with named capability sections and request configuration. Consolidate the OpenAI and Anthropic model catalogs so existing request behavior and generated capability documentation use the same source of truth. Catalogs also declare the provider options each provider accepts and which models support them.

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

v2.14.2 (2026-10-29)

This release addresses 2 security issues, https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-qpmf-fgh3-ff25 and https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-3r8g-cqwr-jr29.

Packaging

  • Bump PyO3 to 0.30.1, jiter to 0.18.0, use PyFrozenDict by @​Viicos in #14003
  • Bump speedate to v0.18.0 by @​Viicos in #14007
  • Publish pydantic-core wheels for PyPy 8.0 (pp80 ABI) by @​Viicos in #14083

Performance

  • Avoid Python tuple allocation during model fields validation by @​Viicos in #13955
  • Lazily call repr of values during nested union serialization by @​Viicos in #14082
  • Skip decorator field checks when no field decorators exist by @​alexmojaki in #14111
  • Avoid heap allocation for small JSON model field buffers by @​alexmojaki in #14113

Fixes

  • Make JSON validation by iteration consistent with Python approach by @​davidhewitt in #13275.

    JSON validation now handles field lookup and extra data the same way as Python validation. In particular, keys that only match an unused alias or field name are now treated as extra data, instead of being silently dropped:

    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel

    class Page(BaseModel):
    
model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid', alias_generator=to_camel)
    

    page_size: int = 10

    

    Page.model_validate_json('{"page_size": 50}')
    

    Before: Page(page_size=10)
    

    After: ValidationError (extra_forbidden)

    See the pull request for the full list of behavior changes. This change addresses https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-qpmf-fgh3-ff25.

  • Ignore extra data matching a field name in TypedDict and dataclasses with extra=allow by @​Viicos in #14090. Addresses https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-3r8g-cqwr-jr29.

  • Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module by @​Viicos in #13994

  • Support explicit by_alias overriding validate_by_alias in validation JSON schemas by @​Viicos in #13997

  • Fix mypy plugin crash on deferred empty model by @​ilevkivskyi in #14027

  • Fix infinite recursion when validating an invalid default with PydanticUseDefault by @​Viicos in #14028

  • Implement recursion guard for validate_strings() by @​Viicos in #14029

hits.body: The current memory pipeline should be reviewed for at least four concerns: inconsistent ranking across sources, lack of explicit pruning for duplicate nodes, missing confidence calibration, and weak handling of stale graph state. These issues may appear as noisy memory retrieval, repeated context injection, or the agent over-weighting older observations. The consequence is not only degraded recall quality but also harder debugging, because the root cause may be buried inside multiple memory sources rather than a single failure point. I recommend a consolidated retrieval policy that combines recency, relevance, source trust, and conflict resolution, along with a small set of audits for duplicate edges, expired entries, and inconsistent graph labels.

python/v1.21.0

Major Features

Custom HTTP Client Support for OpenAI and Gemini - PR#1366

The OpenAI and Gemini model providers now accept a pre-configured client via the client parameter, enabling connection pooling, proxy configuration, custom timeouts, and centralized observability across all model requests. The client is reused for all requests and its lifecycle is managed by the caller, not the model provider.

from strands.models.openai import OpenAIModel
import httpx

Create custom client with proxy and timeout configuration


custom_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
proxy="http://proxy.example.com:8080",
timeout=60.0
)


model = OpenAIModel(model_id="gpt-4o-mini", client=custom_client)

Gemini Built-in Tools (Google Search, Code Execution) - PR#1050

Gemini models now support native Google tools like GoogleSearch and CodeExecution through the gemini_tools parameter. These tools integrate directly with Gemini's API without requiring custom function implementations, enabling agents to search the web and execute code natively.

from google.genai import types

model = GeminiModel(
model_id="gemini-2.0-flash-exp",
gemini_tools=[types.Tool(google_search=types.GoogleSearch())]

Release notes

Sourced from astral-sh/setup-uv's releases.

v7.0.0 🌈 node24 and a lot of bugfixes

Changes

This release comes with a load of bug fixes and a speed up. Because of switching from node20 to node24 it is also a breaking change. If you are running on GitHub hosted runners this will just work, if you are using self-hosted runners make sure, that your runners are up to date. If you followed the normal installation instructions your self-hosted runner will keep itself updated.

This release also removes the deprecated input server-url which was used to download uv releases from a different server. The manifest-file input supersedes that functionality by adding a flexible way to define available versions and where they should be downloaded from.

Fixes

  • The action now respects when the environment variable UV_CACHE_DIR is already set and does not overwrite it. It now also finds cache-dir settings in config files if you set them.
  • Some users encountered problems that cache pruning took forever because they had some uv processes running in the background. Starting with uv version 0.8.24 this action uses uv cache prune --ci --force to ignore the running processes
  • If you just want to install uv but not have it available in path, this action now respects UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH
  • Some other actions also set the env var UV_CACHE_DIR. This action can now deal with that but as this could lead to unwanted behavior in some edgecases a warning is now displayed.

Improvements

If you are using minimum version specifiers for the version of uv to install for example

[tool.uv]
required-version = ">=0.8.17"

This action now detects that and directly uses the latest version. Previously it would download all available releases from the uv repo to determine the highest matching candidate for the version specifier, which took much more time.

If you are using other specifiers like 0.8.x this action still needs to download all available releases because the specifier defines an upper bound (not 0.9.0 or later) and "latest" would possibly not satisfy that.

🚨 Breaking changes

  • Use node24 instead of node20 @​eifinger (#608)
  • Remove deprecated input server-url @​eifinger (#607)

🐛 Bug fixes

  • Respect UV_CACHE_DIR and cache-dir @​eifinger (#612)
  • Use --force when pruning cache @​eifinger (#611)
  • Respect UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH @​eifinger (#603)
  • Warn when UV_CACHE_DIR has changed @​jamesbraza (#601)

🚀 Enhancements

🧰 Maintenance

Release notes

Sourced from litellm's releases.

v1.106.0

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

hits.body: **content**: The retrieval path may silently degrade when prompt context exceeds the graph window, causing stale or partial memory recall during agent sessions. **file**: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/graph_store.py **code**: ```python result = session.query("MATCH (m:Memory) RETURN m LIMIT $limit") ``` **description**: The risk is that a large conversation can create fragmented memory entries, but the query does not consistently enforce recency, relevance, or deduplication across overlapping facts. In a graph memory system, stale nodes can overshadow recent observations, which may distort planning, summary generation, or tool selection. The fix should add ordering by time, a confidence score, and explicit similarity thresholds before returning candidates. A small regression test covering repeated updates, duplicate entities, and stale memory invalidation would reduce the risk of silent reasoning drift in long-running agents.

Updates `@ai-sdk/provider` from 4.0.13 to 4.0.37
Changelog

Sourced from @​ai-sdk/provider's changelog.

4.0.37

Patch Changes

  • c70adf6: Fix TypeSafe decision requests with primitive JSON state by serializing those values as text, reject empty criteria and null or undefined Score levels before sending a request, and expose structured Score legends in provider metadata. Allow omitted or null Box instructions and null Boolean criteria in experimental decision question types.

4.0.36

Patch Changes

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

  • e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.

  • 892af4d: feat (provider): add server-side realtime extensions to the experimental RealtimeModelV4 spec

    Extends the existing optional getServerWebSocketConfig() method and a normalized usage field so a trusted server/proxy can drive realtime providers the way it drives HTTP language models:

    • getServerWebSocketConfig({ intent? }) returns the upstream WebSocket { url, headers, protocols? } for a server-initiated connection (header auth with the long-lived credential). Providers fail fast for unsupported endpoint intents instead of silently falling back. It is the server-side sibling of the browser-only getWebSocketConfig.
    • serializeClientEvent and buildSessionConfig now accept the same optional intent so server-side callers can keep endpoint selection and session serialization aligned.
    • New RealtimeModelV4Usage type and optional usage on response-done, input-transcription-completed, and provider custom snapshot events. Gross totals and known modality buckets remain separate, and duration is reported as seconds. Counts are gross (cache-inclusive) with cached portions reported separately so consumers can apply their own billing split without re-parsing raw.
    • New RealtimeModelV4ServerConnection and RealtimeModelV4SessionIntent types, exported with the Experimental_ prefix.

  • 41465fd: Expose optional transcription word timings separately from segments and accept shared timestampGranularities. Explicit provider timing settings take precedence. OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.

  • 9754014: Add typed streaming heartbeat parts. Anthropic emits them only with includePings: true (disabled by default), without requiring raw chunks. Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new ping union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.

  • 4bb73b0: Add optional video, reranking and decision sections to model capability catalogs, including support for declaring provider options for these operations.

  • 2e44144: Represent videos delivered directly to caller-managed storage with an explicit uploaded outcome. Video generation reports uploadedVideos without downloading or synthesizing video bytes; access video only when videos is nonempty.

4.0.35

Patch Changes

  • dcd2f8d: Introduce a model entry contract with named capability sections and request configuration. Consolidate the OpenAI and Anthropic model catalogs so existing request behavior and generated capability documentation use the same source of truth. Catalogs also declare the provider options each provider accepts and which models support them.

4.0.34

Patch Changes

  • 5475347: Fix non-streaming Responses API structured output failing when multiple assistant messages contain JSON. Providers can supply separate structured-output text for parsing, allowing OpenAI and Azure Responses models to select the last final_answer while preserving all generated content, annotations, conversation history, and token usage.

4.0.38

Patch Changes

4.0.37

Patch Changes

  • c70adf6: Fix TypeSafe decision requests with primitive JSON state by serializing those values as text, reject empty criteria and null or undefined Score levels before sending a request, and expose structured Score legends in provider metadata. Allow omitted or null Box instructions and null Boolean criteria in experimental decision question types.

4.0.36

Patch Changes

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

  • e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.

  • 892af4d: feat (provider): add server-side realtime extensions to the experimental RealtimeModelV4 spec

    Extends the existing optional getServerWebSocketConfig() method and a normalized usage field so a trusted server/proxy can drive realtime providers the way it drives HTTP language models:

    • getServerWebSocketConfig({ intent? }) returns the upstream WebSocket { url, headers, protocols? } for a server-initiated connection (header auth with the long-lived credential). Providers fail fast for unsupported endpoint intents instead of silently falling back. It is the server-side sibling of the browser-only getWebSocketConfig.
    • serializeClientEvent and buildSessionConfig now accept the same optional intent so server-side callers can keep endpoint selection and session serialization aligned.
    • New RealtimeModelV4Usage type and optional usage on response-done, input-transcription-completed, and provider custom snapshot events. Gross totals and known modality buckets remain separate, and duration is reported as seconds. Counts are gross (cache-inclusive) with cached portions reported separately so consumers can apply their own billing split without re-parsing raw.
    • New RealtimeModelV4ServerConnection and RealtimeModelV4SessionIntent types, exported with the Experimental_ prefix.

OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.

  • 9754014: Add typed streaming heartbeat parts. Anthropic emits them only with includePings: true (disabled by default), without requiring raw chunks. Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new ping union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.

  • 4bb73b0: Add optional video, reranking and decision sections to model capability catalogs, including support for declaring provider options for these operations.

  • 2e44144: Represent videos delivered directly to caller-managed storage with an explicit uploaded outcome. Video generation reports uploadedVideos without downloading or synthesizing video bytes; access video only when videos is nonempty.

Patch Changes

Consolidate the OpenAI and Anthropic model catalogs so existing request behavior and generated capability documentation use the same source of truth. hits.body: The project would benefit from centralizing validation logic for memory schema, timestamps, and node lifecycle checks so that the Python SDK and TypeScript SDK do not drift apart. This is especially relevant because both packages share the same memory model but are released independently. A common validation contract could reduce inconsistencies in graph creation, edge constraints, and deletion semantics, while also improving test parity. The expected benefit is fewer silent incompatibilities during runtime, faster onboarding for contributors, and easier maintenance when introducing new memory types or provider adapters. I would suggest a single shared specification and a minimal cross-language conformance test for core memory operations.

    from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

Updates `@strands-agents/sdk` from 1.17.0 to 1.21.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​strands-agents/sdk's releases.

python/v1.21.0

Major Features

Custom HTTP Client Support for OpenAI and Gemini - PR#1366

The OpenAI and Gemini model providers now accept a pre-configured client via the client parameter, enabling connection pooling, proxy configuration, custom timeouts, and centralized observability across all model requests. The client is reused for all requests and its lifecycle is managed by the caller, not the model provider.

from strands.models.openai import OpenAIModel
import httpx

Create custom client with proxy and timeout configuration


custom_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
proxy="http://proxy.example.com:8080",
timeout=60.0
)


model = OpenAIModel(model_id="gpt-4o-mini", client=custom_client)

Gemini Built-in Tools (Google Search, Code Execution) - PR#1050

Gemini models now support native Google tools like GoogleSearch and CodeExecution through the gemini_tools parameter. These tools integrate directly with Gemini's API without requiring custom function implementations, enabling agents to search the web and execute code natively.

from strands.models.gemini import GeminiModel
from google.genai import types

model = GeminiModel(
model_id="gemini-2.0-flash-exp",
gemini_tools=[types.Tool(google_search=types.GoogleSearch())]
)

Patch Changes

Provider detection and emission will be added separately.

Exhaustive switches (for example, using an assertNever fallback) and mappings such as Record<FinishReason, string> must handle the new value. Update any custom validation or application logic that assumes the existing set of finish reasons is exhaustive.

    When providers begin emitting interrupted, a stream ending without a completion signal will preserve partial output and report this finish reason without emitting an error solely for the interruption. Applications that need to detect incomplete responses should check finishReason === 'interrupted' as well as their existing error handling.

Release notes

Sourced from litellm's releases.

v1.106.0

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

4.0.37

Patch Changes

  • c70adf6: Fix TypeSafe decision requests with primitive JSON state by serializing those values as text, reject empty criteria and null or undefined Score levels before sending a request, and expose structured Score legends in provider metadata. Allow omitted or null Box instructions and null Boolean criteria in experimental decision question types.

4.0.36

Patch Changes

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

  • e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.

  • 892af4d: feat (provider): add server-side realtime extensions to the experimental RealtimeModelV4 spec

    Extends the existing optional getServerWebSocketConfig() method and a normalized usage field so a trusted server/proxy can drive realtime providers the way it drives HTTP language models:

    • getServerWebSocketConfig({ intent? }) returns the upstream WebSocket { url, headers, protocols? } for a server-initiated connection (header auth with the long-lived credential). Providers fail fast for unsupported endpoint intents instead of silently falling back. It is the server-side sibling of the browser-only getWebSocketConfig.
    • serializeClientEvent and buildSessionConfig now accept the same optional intent so server-side callers can keep endpoint selection and session serialization aligned.
    • New RealtimeModelV4Usage type and optional usage on response-done, input-transcription-completed, and provider custom snapshot events. Gross totals and known modality buckets remain separate, and duration is reported as seconds. Counts are gross (cache-inclusive) with cached portions reported separately so consumers can apply their own billing split without re-parsing raw.
    • New RealtimeModelV4ServerConnection and RealtimeModelV4SessionIntent types, exported with the Experimental_ prefix.

  • 41465fd: Expose optional transcription word timings separately from segments and accept shared timestampGranularities. Explicit provider timing settings take precedence. OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.

Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new ping union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.

  • 2e44144: Represent videos delivered directly to caller-managed storage with an explicit uploaded outcome. Video generation reports uploadedVideos without downloading or synthesizing video bytes; access video only when videos is nonempty.

hits.body: This project demonstrates a thoughtful balance between graph-based memory and multi-SDK delivery. The separation between the Python package and the TypeScript package is clear, and the shared memory model plus NAMS backend suggests a disciplined architecture that can scale without forcing the ecosystem to choose a single language. I especially appreciate the explicit naming conventions and release tagging strategy, which reduce confusion between the Python and TypeScript packages and make operational ownership clearer. The repository also appears to emphasize documentation, examples, and deployments, which is important for agent-based systems where usage patterns are rarely obvious. From a product perspective, the combination of memory graph semantics and language-specific clients is a strong foundation for cross-tool recall, task continuity, and context assembly. I would encourage the team to keep the public contract stable and document the integration boundaries carefully as the system grows.

hits.title: Strong Graph Memory Layer for Multi-Agent Coordination

hits.body: **content**: The retrieval path may silently degrade when prompt context exceeds the graph window, causing stale or partial memory recall during agent sessions. **file**: src/neo4j_agent_memory/memory/graph_store.py **code**: ```python result = session.query("MATCH (m:Memory) RETURN m LIMIT $limit") ``` **description**: The risk is that a large conversation can create fragmented memory entries, but the query does not consistently enforce recency, relevance, or deduplication across overlapping facts. In a graph memory system, stale nodes can overshadow recent observations, which may distort planning, summary generation, or tool selection. The fix should add ordering by time, a confidence score, and explicit similarity thresholds before returning candidates. A small regression test covering repeated updates, duplicate entities, and stale memory invalidation would reduce the risk of silent reasoning drift in long-running agents.

Updates `@strands-agents/sdk` from 1.17.0 to 1.21.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​strands-agents/sdk's releases.

python/v1.21.0

Major Features

Custom HTTP Client Support for OpenAI and Gemini - PR#1366

The OpenAI and Gemini model providers now accept a pre-configured client via the client parameter, enabling connection pooling, proxy configuration, custom timeouts, and centralized observability across all model requests. The client is reused for all requests and its lifecycle is managed by the caller, not the model provider.

from strands.models.openai import OpenAIModel
import httpx

Create custom client with proxy and timeout configuration


custom_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
proxy="http://proxy.example.com:8080",
timeout=60.0
)


model = OpenAIModel(model_id="gpt-4o-mini", client=custom_client)

Gemini Built-in Tools (Google Search, Code Execution) - PR#1050

Gemini models now support native Google tools like GoogleSearch and CodeExecution through the gemini_tools parameter. These tools integrate directly with Gemini's API without requiring custom function implementations, enabling agents to search the web and execute code natively.

from strands.models.gemini import GeminiModel
from google.genai import types

model = GeminiModel(
model_id="gemini-2.0-flash-exp",
gemini_tools=[types.Tool(google_search=types.GoogleSearch())]
)

Changelog

Sourced from @​ai-sdk/provider's changelog.

4.0.38

Patch Changes

  • cb4fa52: add experimental extract api and extraction model spec

4.0.37

Patch Changes

  • c70adf6: Fix TypeSafe decision requests with primitive JSON state by serializing those values as text, reject empty criteria and null or undefined Score levels before sending a request, and expose structured Score legends in provider metadata. Allow omitted or null Box instructions and null Boolean criteria in experimental decision question types.

4.0.36

Patch Changes

  • 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its url parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom download function retains local download behavior.

    For telemetry integrations, TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength and audio.mediaType can now be undefined when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

    Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

  • e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

    Add an optional createTransport interface and provider connection capability.

  • 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.

  • 892af4d: feat (provider): add server-side realtime extensions to the experimental RealtimeModelV4 spec

    Extends the existing optional getServerWebSocketConfig() method and a normalized usage field so a trusted server/proxy can drive realtime providers the way it drives HTTP language models:

    • getServerWebSocketConfig({ intent? }) returns the upstream WebSocket { url, headers, protocols? } for a server-initiated connection (header auth with the long-lived credential). Providers fail fast for unsupported endpoint intents instead of silently falling back. It is the server-side sibling of the browser-only getWebSocketConfig.
    • serializeClientEvent and buildSessionConfig now accept the same optional intent so server-side callers can keep endpoint selection and session serialization aligned.
    • New RealtimeModelV4Usage type and optional usage on response-done, input-transcription-completed, and provider custom snapshot events. Gross totals and known modality buckets remain separate, and duration is reported as seconds. Counts are gross (cache-inclusive) with cached portions reported separately so consumers can apply their own billing split without re-parsing raw.
    • New RealtimeModelV4ServerConnection and RealtimeModelV4SessionIntent types, exported with the Experimental_ prefix.

  • 41465fd: Expose optional transcription word timings separately from segments and accept shared timestampGranularities. Explicit provider timing settings take precedence. OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.

  • 9754014: Add typed streaming heartbeat parts. Anthropic emits them only with includePings: true (disabled by default), without requiring raw chunks. Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new ping union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.

  • 4bb73b0: Add optional video, reranking and decision sections to model capability catalogs, including support for declaring provider options for these operations.

  • 2e44144: Represent videos delivered directly to caller-managed storage with an explicit uploaded outcome. Video generation reports uploadedVideos without downloading or synthesizing video bytes; access video only when videos is nonempty.

4.0.35

Patch Changes

  • dcd2f8d: Introduce a model entry contract with named capability sections and request configuration. Consolidate the OpenAI and Anthropic model catalogs so existing request behavior and generated capability documentation use the same source of truth. Catalogs also declare the provider options each provider accepts and which models support them.

Release notes

Sourced from litellm's releases.

v1.106.0

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

ci: cache Hugging Face model dir to fix flaky integration-test-matrix (#168)

The integration/example jobs use a sentence-transformers embedder
(all-MiniLM-L6-v2). With no caching, every run re-downloads the model from
Hugging Face, and test_no_openai_import_with_llm_none caps its subprocess at
120s — a cold/slow HF pull blows that cap and fails integration-test-matrix
intermittently (observed red on a feature branch while main was green, purely
on download-timing variance).

- Cache ~/.cache/huggingface in each job that pulls a model
  (integration-test, integration-test-matrix, integration-test-testcontainers,
  example-tests, example-tests-quick). Model-agnostic: rotating
  `key: hf-cache-<os>-<sha>` + `restore-keys: hf-cache-<os>-` restores the
  newest prior cache and re-saves whatever models the run pulled, so new models
  are picked up without maintaining per-model keys.
- Raise the no-llm subprocess timeout 120s -> 300s so the first
  (cache-populating) run tolerates a cold download.

fix(short-term): stop CREATE_MESSAGE fanning out over a forked chain

CREATE_MESSAGE read the conversation tail with an OPTIONAL MATCH that can
bind more than one row. Every clause after it runs once per row, so the
CREATE ran once per tail with the same $id and breached the uniqueness
constraint on Message.id.

Two concurrent appends produced that state: both read the same tail, both
linked to it, and left two messages with no outgoing NEXT_MESSAGE. The
next append then fanned out. This is not flakiness -- once a conversation
has two tails, every later append to it fails, sequential or not.

Write to the conversation before reading the tail so SET takes a write
lock that serializes concurrent appends, and collapse the tail candidates
to the newest so a chain already forked by an earlier write stays
appendable; migrate_message_links() remains the repair path for the fork
itself. GET_LAST_MESSAGE gets the matching ORDER BY -- it had LIMIT 1 but
no ordering, so the batch path picked an arbitrary tail.

The concurrency test blamed "UUID collisions" and staggered itself with a
sleep that hid the bug. It now runs unstaggered and asserts the invariant
that was actually broken: one head, one tail, one unbroken chain. A new
TestForkedChainRecovery builds the forked state directly, so the guard no
longer depends on winning a race.

Known gap, deliberately not addressed here: _ensure_conversation is a
read-then-create race, so concurrent first writes to one session can still
mint several conversations. session_id is deliberately not unique, so a
MERGE-plus-constraint fix is a data-model decision rather than a query
one; the test establishes the conversation first and says so.

Validation: verified against Neo4j 2026.07. Reverting the query change
fails both the concurrency test and the new deterministic one; with it,
tests/integration is 505 passed, 92 skipped (skips are NAMS-sandbox and
cloud-credential gates), and tests/unit is 1819 passed.

fix(tests): make the unit suite pass without optional extras

The CI `test` job installs no extras, which exposed two gaps the local

hits.message:
fix(ontology,resolution): fix the 0.7 code-review findings

Fixes the 15 defects a review of the gliner-2.5 branch found, plus its
convention and cleanup notes. Each fix has a regression test.

Extraction
- The client's resolved ontology now uses extraction.gliner_schema when
  the client builds a gliner or pipeline extractor, as the factory does.
  Before, ingest-time validation dropped every relation the template's
  extractor decoded.
- The pipeline merge carries GLiNER2.5 mention ids onto the copy of an
  entity that survives (spaCy's or the LLM's), so the confidence floor
  keeps the relations that point at it.
- spaCy under a subtyped ontology maps a label only onto spaCy's own
  subtype, the label as the subtype, or the bare POLE+O type, and drops
  anything else (drop_unmapped). Before, every label went to the first
  ontology label of its type, so amounts became diseases under medical.
- Relationship types declared for several endpoint pairs get a decoding
  constraint that admits exactly those pairs, not heads x tails.

Resolution and storage
- Blocking matches stored lookup keys (name_key, surface_keys) through
  three new indexes instead of scanning every entity of the type per
  message. Every entity write keeps the keys current
  (queries.entity_keys_set_clause), and a one-time entity_keys_backfill
  fills them on existing graphs. The queries carry no index hints: a
  hint errors while its index is still populating.
- Vector blocking skips merged-away entities.
- add_entity deduplicates through the ontology resolver without an
  embedding. An exact re-add falls through to the MERGE, so the new
  description, aliases and location are applied.
- An intra-message merge links to the anchor of its own type; a
  name-only relation endpoint shared by two types is picked by the
  ontology. The two SAME_AS blocks are now one.
- Explicit mentions: a typed EntityRef goes through _persist_entities
  (strict-mode check, resolution). A name-only one links a single
  existing entity and never creates one.
- Re-running MERGE_ENTITIES on the same pair no longer re-adds support.
- add_relationship stores the ontology's spelling of the type.

Ontology
- from_entity_schema maps custom type names (PATIENT) onto POLE+O
  instead of emitting a document validate_structure rejects.
- BoltOntology.migrate removes the old type and built-in subtype labels,
  judged per node from its stored type/subtype, and adds the target's.
- ontology_node_label re-cases all-caps parts (INDIVIDUAL -> Individual).
- BoltOntology.create/update reject an unknown validation_mode; a stored
  mode is read case-insensitively.
- NAMS: a malformed active document or version schema_json raises
  ValueError instead of reading as "nothing bound" / document=None.

Conventions and cleanups
- The keys() guards that only avoided UNRECOGNIZED warnings are gone
  (CLAUDE.md item 23), including in GET_ACTIVE_ONTOLOGY_VERSION.
- core.metrics.normalize_name reuses the resolver's key, so scoring now
  also folds punctuation.
- The explicit-mention and alias query comments are in the right place;
  build_merge_entity_reference_query and MERGE_ENTITY_REFERENCE_BY_NAME
  are removed (unused).

Docs: CHANGELOG (Unreleased), CLAUDE.md, schema-objects,
configuration-providers, extractor-classes, ontology-api,
short-term-messages, ontology-driven-extraction and migrate-to-gliner2.

feat(extraction): adopt GLiNER2.5 with ontology-driven extraction and resolution

Replace the gliner v1 + GLiREL extraction stage with GLiNER2.5 (the `gliner2`
package) and make a first-class ontology drive extraction, relation
validation, storage and entity resolution on the bolt backend. Release 0.7.0.

Extraction
- New `GLiNER2Extractor`: loads `fastino/gliner2.5-base-v1` via
  `AutoExtractor`, decodes entities and relations in one JointIE pass with
  typed endpoints, windows long input at 384 library-counted words, and
  offers an opt-in span-attribute pass. Relations carry mention ids and
  `derived` flags; entities carry ids and offsets.
- Remove `GLiNEREntityExtractor`, `GLiRELExtractor`,
  `GLiNERWithRelationsExtractor` and `gliner_extractor.py`; the old names
  raise an `ImportError` with a migration hint. Domain catalogs move to
  `domain_schemas.py`, label mapping to `label_mapping.py`.
- Extras: new `[gliner2]` (`[gliner]` stays as a deprecated alias);
  `[extraction]` and `[full]` carry gliner2. Relock moves transformers to
  4.57.x and drops gliner/glirel. New `ExtractionConfig` fields for
  thresholds, windowing, overlap policy, attributes, quantize/compile.

Ontology (both backends)
- New `neo4j_agent_memory.ontology` package: the NAMS document model
  promoted and extended (descriptions, aliases, per-type resolution
  thresholds, relationship constraints), built-in POLE+O and domain
  templates, compiler to JointIE schemas and LLM prompt fragments,
  converters for `EntitySchemaConfig`, domain catalogs and arrows files,
  structural validation and diff.
- `client.ontology` now works on bolt (`BoltOntology`): versioned
  `:Ontology`/`:OntologyVersion` storage, activate, clone, import, diff
  and a synchronous migrate. `MemoryClient(ontology=...)`,
  `SchemaConfig.ontology_path`, `use_active_ontology` and
  `validation_mode` select the effective ontology; strict mode rejects
  undeclared types and forbidden relationship pairs.
- `ExtractionResult.validate_relations()` runs as a pipeline stage and on
  ingestion; the LLM extractor prompt carries the relationship catalogue.

Storage and resolution
- Typed relations merge on `RELATED_TO {type}` with `support`, `derived`,
  `extractor`, `source_message_ids` and `evidence`; `r.type` is canonical
  and a one-time backfill (`SchemaConfig.backfill_relation_types`) migrates
  legacy edges. Relationship readers now return real properties instead of
  defaults (they previously mis-parsed driver tuples).
- New `OntologyResolver` on the ingestion path by default
  (`resolution.resolve_on_ingest=False` opts out): normalisation,
  type-constrained blocking in Cypher, alias gazetteer, weighted scoring
  with review band -> pending `SAME_AS`, two-pass episode clustering,
  tenant scoping. Dedup thresholds are single-sourced from
  `ResolutionConfig` (auto-merge 0.90, review 0.85).

Evaluation, examples, docs
- Relation precision/recall/F1, `MatchPolicy`, B-cubed and gold data in
  `core/metrics.py` + `benchmarks/`; `benchmarks/compare_extractors.py`;
  `extraction` and `resolution` eval dimensions.
- New keyless `examples/ontology-extraction`; lennys-memory backend
  relocked onto gliner2.
- Docs: migration guide, ontology-driven extraction and resolution tuning
  how-tos, ~40 pages updated with the GLiNER/GLiNER2.5 naming glossary;
  CHANGELOG 0.7.0; version bump.

BREAKING CHANGE: gliner v1 and GLiREL extractors are removed; the default
GLiNER model id changes; `RELATED_TO` edges merge on `{type}` (legacy edges
are backfilled on first connect); ingestion resolves entities by default.

  timestamps. In 0.6.0 untimed batch messages share one timestamp, so
  the order assertion failed at random.
- nams_first_write.py creates the conversation, writes to the ID NAMS
  returns, reads the message back and deletes the conversation. It used
  to post to a client-chosen ID that NAMS never created.
- cloud_embeddings_recipe.py builds Bedrock and Vertex embedding
  providers. MemorySettings rejects the legacy embedder objects it
  passed with a TypeError.
- anthropic_local_memory.py checks extracted entities with a graph read.
  In 0.6.0 auto-extracted entities have no vectors, so search_entities
  returned nothing and the tutorial always stopped.

  instead of GLiREL. Its documented install could not load GLiREL, and
  0.6.0 passes GLiREL the wrong spans. It sends temperature=1.0 because
  GPT-5 and o-series models reject the SDK's default of 0.

  copies, and 'npm run build' failed.

ci: run the docs programs and guard section ids; fix docs tooling

CI and Makefile
- ci-python runs the maintained tutorial and how-to programs
  (tests/docs/test_tutorial_examples.py, test_howto_examples.py) against
  the integration job's Neo4j. Nothing ran them before, so mocked
  contract tests passed while the programs failed on a live database.
- ci-python adds test_nav_labels.py to the link-validation step, and
  runs 'scripts/check_docs.py --build' as its own step.
- ci-typescript builds the vercel-ai-provider package for every example
  whose package.json links it. nextjs-memory-chat started depending on
  it, but only the nams-ai-provider leg built it, so the nextjs leg
  failed type-checking. 'make ts-test-examples' now builds it too.
- 'make docs-render-check' sets DOCS_RENDER_CHECK_REQUIRED=1, so a
  missing Playwright install fails the gate instead of skipping every
  rendered check. The new 'make docs-render-install' target installs
  Playwright and Chromium, which 'make docs-install' never did.
- 'make test-docs-framework-contracts' installs the extras and the
  agent-framework-openai client that the framework recipe contracts
  need. 'make test-docs' now skips that module, so it passes in the
  documented dev environment.
- 'make example-*' exports NEO4J_URI and NEO4J_USERNAME with the
  password when it starts the local Docker Neo4j. The examples read all
  three, so 'make examples' crashed with KeyError on a clean checkout.
- tck-conformance.yml no longer claims that ci-typescript runs the
  in-tree TCK suite. .gitignore adds .cursor/mcp.json.

Docs tooling
- check_docs.py records rendered section ids in
  scripts/docs_section_ids.json (seeded from the 531bae1 site) and fails
  when a recorded id stops resolving, so a renamed section must keep its
  old id as an anchor. --record-section-ids extends the baseline from a
  clean build. Image attribute lists are split as Asciidoctor splits
  them, so a quoted alt text containing a comma is not cut in two.
- manage_diagrams.py fails when a manifest record's referring_pages
  differ from the pages that embed the image. add-refs writes a
  captioned SVG embed.
- export_diagrams.mjs writes only the SVG unless the manifest tracks a
  PNG or --png is passed, and --all re-exports only the SVGs the
  manifest records. Before, --all left 23 untracked PNGs that the
  orphan check then rejected.
- The tutorial copy button stays in the tab order: the theme hid its
  container with display:none until hover, so keyboard users could not
  reach it. It now stays rendered but transparent, and shows on hover
  or focus-within.
- The docs snippet syntax check compiles snippets instead of only
  parsing them, so compile-phase errors (await in a plain def, return
  outside a function) fail again. Reference signature stubs are now
  checked as well.
- test_rendered_site.py registers its 'rendered' marker in
  pyproject.toml. test_docs_checker.py, test_nav_labels.py and
  test_rendered_site.py now pass ruff format, which CI enforces.
- The docs-excalidraw and docs-diataxis skills describe the SVG-first
  export, the manifest step and the captioned embed.

Depends on the docs commit that follows. Against this commit's docs,
check_docs.py --build reports 49 recorded section ids that no longer
resolve, and manage_diagrams.py reports one stale referring_pages entry
for memory-architecture.svg. That commit restores the anchors and
updates the manifest.

workflow YAML parses, 'make -n' resolves every new or changed target,
and 422 tests pass across test_docs_checker.py, test_nav_labels.py,
test_code_snippets.py and test_links.py. With the docs changes applied
as well, every gate passes, including the rendered-site checks under
Playwright.

Type-safety Phase 3: mypy-strict + ty clean integrations (#163)

Brings the entire `integrations/` tree (plus `integrations/base.py`) to zero
`mypy --strict` errors and zero `ty` diagnostics, and lowers the type-check
ratchet accordingly: mypy 102 -> 13, ty 85 -> 26. The remaining mypy errors are
confined to `testing/mocks.py` (a later workstream). Budget updated in
`scripts/typecheck-budget.txt` so CI enforces the new floor.

Integrations cleaned: langchain, crewai, agentcore, pydantic_ai, google_adk,
openai_agents, strands, llamaindex, microsoft_agent. `run_sync` in
`integrations/base.py` is now `ParamSpec`-generic; the per-integration
`_run_async` sync bridges are `TypeVar`-generic over `Coroutine`.

Runtime bugs surfaced by the type checkers (fixed):

- Microsoft Agent GDS never used the GDS library. `GDSIntegration` called
  `Neo4jClient.session()`, which did not exist, so every algorithm query threw
  `AttributeError`, was swallowed by the surrounding try/except, and silently
  fell back to basic Cypher even with GDS installed. The unit-test mock had
  drifted to expose a `.session` attribute the real object lacked, masking it.
  Added a public `Neo4jClient.session()` and routed GDS through it.
- Strands `context_graph_tools()` raised `ValidationError` on every client
  cache-miss: it built `Neo4jConfig(user=..., password=<str>)` but the field is
  `username` with a `SecretStr` password and `extra="forbid"`. Now
  `username=...` + `password=SecretStr(...)`.
- CrewAI `Neo4jCrewMemory` never subclassed the real base class — the import
  `from crewai.memory import Memory` raised `ImportError` (the class lives at
  `crewai.memory.memory.Memory`), so it silently fell back to the stub.

Public-API typing changes (recorded in CHANGELOG):

- New public `Neo4jClient.session()` accessor for raw Cypher/session control.
- Strands `transport_mode` narrowed from `str` to
  `Literal["auto", "rest", "bridge"]` on `nams_context_graph_tools()`.
- `GDSIntegration.find_shortest_path()` return type corrected to
  `dict[str, Any] | None` (it always returned a dict, never a list).
- Pydantic AI `record_agent_trace(result=...)` typed `AgentRunResult`
  (`RunResult` moved to `pydantic_ai.agent`).

Other notes:

- `google.adk.*` and `nest_asyncio` (no py.typed, used at a typed boundary in
  one/two files each) are suppressed per-module via `ignore_missing_imports`.
- Modernized `datetime.utcnow()` -> `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` in
  `agentcore/types.py`.
- The `client.short_term` -> `ShortTermProtocol` widening is intentionally NOT
  included here; it is a breaking return-type change that will land separately.

All unit tests pass (1444); lint, format, mypy, ty, and the ratchet are green.

ci: cache Hugging Face model dir to fix flaky integration-test-matrix (#168)

The integration/example jobs use a sentence-transformers embedder
(all-MiniLM-L6-v2). With no caching, every run re-downloads the model from
Hugging Face, and test_no_openai_import_with_llm_none caps its subprocess at
120s — a cold/slow HF pull blows that cap and fails integration-test-matrix
intermittently (observed red on a feature branch while main was green, purely
on download-timing variance).

- Cache ~/.cache/huggingface in each job that pulls a model
  (integration-test, integration-test-matrix, integration-test-testcontainers,
  example-tests, example-tests-quick). Model-agnostic: rotating
  `key: hf-cache-<os>-<sha>` + `restore-keys: hf-cache-<os>-` restores the
  newest prior cache and re-saves whatever models the run pulled, so new models
  are picked up without maintaining per-model keys.
- Raise the no-llm subprocess timeout 120s -> 300s so the first
  (cache-populating) run tolerates a cold download.

dimensions). The NAMS trio showcases workspace addressing, bulk_add_messages,
wait_for_extraction/get_extraction_status, observations/reflections and
expand_graph.

FSA loader); the Microsoft backend validates relationship types instead of
interpolating them into Cypher; the chat backend's read-only guard is fixed.

parametrized runner with thin wrappers; shared examples/_env.py and
examples/.env.example replace copy-pasted env loading; retired model ids
(gpt-4o, claude-3-*, text-embedding-004) replaced by env-driven ids with

both bolt and NAMS classes and additionally rejects private client
reach-through and adapter phantoms. READMEs carry Labs badges, disclaimer,

test(strands): drive a real Agent against live NAMS on the synchronous path

Every existing test of Neo4jMemoryStore drives the store directly, on one
event loop -- the blind spot that let a Critical through review. Strands'
synchronous entry point runs Agent.__init__ on one throwaway loop and each
Agent.__call__ on another, so a settings=-constructed store connected its
client on the construction loop and then raised "attached to a different
loop" on the first call. initialize() now rebinds an owned client; nothing
exercised that end-to-end.

tests/e2e/test_strands_agent_nams_e2e.py constructs a real Agent over
hosted NAMS and a local tool-calling Ollama model, calls it twice
synchronously (construction-loop -> call-loop, then call-loop ->
call-loop), and asserts the memory landed in the sink conversation, comes
back out of store.search(), that the store's graph tool is registered
under its namespaced name while get_user_preferences is absent on NAMS,
and that MemoryManager's <memory> block reached the model (read off a
RecordingModel subclass overriding the public Model.stream -- no privates).

A sync test on purpose: asyncio_mode="auto" would otherwise run the body
inside a loop, and the fresh-loop-per-call entry point is the thing under
test. Extraction is awaited via wait_for_extraction/get_extraction_status,
never a sleep, and every live call is bounded by asyncio.wait_for.

Gated so it never breaks anyone's CI: skips unless MEMORY_API_KEY is in
the process environment and the Ollama endpoint answers a 5s probe. New
`e2e` marker, deliberately not `integration` (the root conftest ties that
marker to Neo4j reachability). Teardown deletes every conversation the run
created and asserts they are gone; NAMS_E2E_KEEP=1 leaves them for
inspection in the web UI.

Type-safety Phase 3: mypy-strict + ty clean integrations (#163)

Brings the entire `integrations/` tree (plus `integrations/base.py`) to zero
`mypy --strict` errors and zero `ty` diagnostics, and lowers the type-check
ratchet accordingly: mypy 102 -> 13, ty 85 -> 26. The remaining mypy errors are
confined to `testing/mocks.py` (a later workstream). Budget updated in
`scripts/typecheck-budget.txt` so CI enforces the new floor.

Integrations cleaned: langchain, crewai, agentcore, pydantic_ai, google_adk,
openai_agents, strands, llamaindex, microsoft_agent. `run_sync` in
`integrations/base.py` is now `ParamSpec`-generic; the per-integration
`_run_async` sync bridges are `TypeVar`-generic over `Coroutine`.

Runtime bugs surfaced by the type checkers (fixed):

- Microsoft Agent GDS never used the GDS library. `GDSIntegration` called
  `Neo4jClient.session()`, which did not exist, so every algorithm query threw
  `AttributeError`, was swallowed by the surrounding try/except, and silently
  fell back to basic Cypher even with GDS installed. The unit-test mock had
  drifted to expose a `.session` attribute the real object lacked, masking it.
  Added a public `Neo4jClient.session()` and routed GDS through it.
- Strands `context_graph_tools()` raised `ValidationError` on every client
  cache-miss: it built `Neo4jConfig(user=..., password=<str>)` but the field is
  `username` with a `SecretStr` password and `extra="forbid"`. Now
  `username=...` + `password=SecretStr(...)`.
- CrewAI `Neo4jCrewMemory` never subclassed the real base class — the import
  `from crewai.memory import Memory` raised `ImportError` (the class lives at
  `crewai.memory.memory.Memory`), so it silently fell back to the stub.

Public-API typing changes (recorded in CHANGELOG):

- New public `Neo4jClient.session()` accessor for raw Cypher/session control.
- Strands `transport_mode` narrowed from `str` to
  `Literal["auto", "rest", "bridge"]` on `nams_context_graph_tools()`.
- `GDSIntegration.find_shortest_path()` return type corrected to
  `dict[str, Any] | None` (it always returned a dict, never a list).
- Pydantic AI `record_agent_trace(result=...)` typed `AgentRunResult`
  (`RunResult` moved to `pydantic_ai.agent`).

Other notes:

- `google.adk.*` and `nest_asyncio` (no py.typed, used at a typed boundary in
  one/two files each) are suppressed per-module via `ignore_missing_imports`.
- Modernized `datetime.utcnow()` -> `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` in
  `agentcore/types.py`.
- The `client.short_term` -> `ShortTermProtocol` widening is intentionally NOT
  included here; it is a breaking return-type change that will land separately.

All unit tests pass (1444); lint, format, mypy, ty, and the ratchet are green.

fix(ts/strands): scope the memory-store dedupe to the agent run

- addMessages: sequence numbers reset to 0 each agent run, so a store
  shared across runs collided with its own banked tokens and silently
  skipped the new run's first turns. Detect the reset (lowest incoming
  number <= highest banked) and re-mint the generation — but only when
  the previous call returned cleanly, so a retry, which repeats the same
  numbers after a throw, is still deduped rather than duplicated.
- resolveSink: memoize the in-flight promise before the first await.
  Concurrent tool calls and a programmatic add overlapping a background
  save each minted their own sink, and metadata is not settable after
  creation. A rejection clears the memo.
- Scan for the sink under the same userId the create path records, so
  the unscoped case no longer pages through arbitrary conversations.
- Accept either spelling of the sink metadata key on read: the
  snake/camel round trip only closes if the service echoes the key, and
  a miss would mint another sink per process.
- get_entity_graph: validate entityName before connecting, and flag
  truncated: true when the 50-element cap actually dropped something.
- Correct two comments: close() clears a flag rather than reconnecting;
  the double-extraction guard throws at initAgent, not at construction.
- Drop a dead role fallback and cast — MessageData.role is a required
  'user' | 'assistant', a subset of MessageRole.

docs: align the documentation with the released SDKs and rebuild the rendered site

This branch brings the Antora documentation into line with the released SDKs (`neo4j-agent-memory` 0.6.0 on PyPI, `@neo4j-labs/agent-memory` 0.4.1 on npm) and with what a reader actually sees in the browser. It started as an alignment pass for guides and examples that referenced unsupported APIs or overstated backend capabilities, then absorbed three further reviews: a multi-persona review of every page against the four repository skills, a plan built from headless renders of the whole site, and a diagram-focused polish of the rendered result. Every finding was independently verified before it was fixed, and the review evidence lives under `docs/audit-evidence/`.

The site grows from 111 to 138 pages: 27 new pages, most of them subpages split out of the longest reference pages, plus concept pages for the context tiers and the v0.2 operational primitives. 51 editable diagram scenes back 42 tracked exports.

**Accuracy against the released SDKs**
- Pages describe 0.6.0 behaviour, verified against `origin/main` rather than the branch's older source: `add_entity` returns the stored id on a merge match, `add_relationship` raises `NotFoundError` on a missing endpoint, `merge_duplicate_entities` copies the seven edge types the docstring lists.
- Broken code samples fixed: the hosted connection check, the batch-processing schema name, the PydanticAI dependency field, the graph-architecture Cypher property, the Strands peer-dependency version.
- Backend scope is declared on every how-to through shared partials, and the capability matrix, REST tables and deployment options fit a phone.
- Every entry page carries the Labs disclaimer through one partial; the Next.js guide builds the SDK from source until the middleware it needs ships on npm.

**Structure and navigation**
- Sidebar labels, index text and page titles agree, in sentence case, enforced by a new nav-label test; the "How to:" prefixes and Title Case remnants are gone.
- Closing sections are "See also" on task and reference pages and "Next steps" on tutorials, always last.
- The how-to, reference and concepts indexes group and describe their pages; the integrations index lists all eleven guides once.
- Leftover migration scaffolding ("Earlier section links") is removed from ten reference pages with every old anchor kept resolvable and a checker rule against regressions.
- The six longest reference pages are hubs with subpages that preserve every section id; the FAQ is grouped; the environment-variables page has real tables.

**Diagrams**
- Six new diagrams (Bolt versus NAMS data flow, hosted memory flow, multi-agent boundaries, entity relationship recipe, tutorial routes, TypeScript MCP architecture) and a real `HAS_STEP` and `TOUCHED` graph on the audit page.
- One house style recorded in `docs/MAINTAINING.md`: Helvetica text, semantic palette, ellipses for graph nodes, canvases composed for the 648px column, a caption on every image, SVG exports.
- The rendered polish pass fixed hidden branch labels, swapped layer colours, crossing arrows, clipped footnotes and an orphaned export, and re-exported the README-referenced PNGs from current scenes.

**Tooling**
- `scripts/render_docs.mjs` and `tests/docs/test_rendered_site.py` render the built site with Playwright and fail on body tables of contents, undersized images, phone overflow, uncaptioned diagrams, Title Case headings and scaffolding headings; wired into `make docs-lint`, skipped cleanly where Playwright is absent.

- The TypeScript MCP example test assembles its lesson from both the tutorial and the how-to after the tutorial was trimmed to one path.

**Process**
- `docs/MAINTAINING.md` records release verification against the released tree, the diagram rules, the non-published directories under `docs/`, and treats hosted-only preview claims as release-verification items.
- READMEs state that the Python and TypeScript packages are versioned independently.

1. A twelve-group, three-persona review (Diataxis editor, accuracy verifier against `src/` and `typescript/src/`, target reader) plus seven corpus-wide lenses; 173 candidate findings, 152 confirmed after independent verification, all implemented and re-checked.
2. Every page rendered headlessly at 1280px and 390px with each diagram cropped at its rendered size; four reviewers by quadrant produced the plan in `docs/audit-evidence/2026-09-17/rendered-site-review-plan.md`, implemented in phases A to D with a reviewer on each task.
