docs(examples): add support-desk-agent full-stack app

A FastAPI + PydanticAI 2.x agent and a Next.js 16 + Chakra UI v3 app on the
support-desk ontology of the ontology-lifecycle examples: the same Arrows
diagram (byte-identical), the same transcript as the first of eight seeded
conversations (34 messages), on bolt with keyless GLiNER2.5 extraction.

Reasoning memory both ways: each chat turn stores the user message, starts a
trace linked to it (INITIATED_BY), records every tool call as a step with its
ToolCall (TRIGGERED_BY) and TOUCHED audit edges, and completes the trace with
a TraceOutcome; the agent's recall_similar_tasks tool reads earlier traces via
get_similar_traces, and the seed adds three traces of earlier work (marked
seeded) so recall works on the first chat.

Backend (examples/support-desk-agent/backend): SSE chat, threads, memory
context and SAME_AS review, NVL graph, ontology overview / diff / rename +
migrate / activate (reconnecting the memory client, since a bolt client
resolves its ontology at connect), traces, similar traces and tool stats;
`python -m src.seed [--reset]`. AGENT_MODEL defaults to openai:gpt-5-mini;
AGENT_MODEL=test runs PydanticAI's TestModel for smoke tests and CI.

Frontend (examples/support-desk-agent/frontend): threads sidebar, streaming
chat with tool-call cards and per-turn trace chips, and Memory, Graph,
Ontology and Reasoning panels.

Wiring: Makefile and docker-compose for the example, a frontend-build matrix

tests/examples/test_support_desk_agent_example.py: structure, pins, parity

construction on TestModel, and an end-to-end run against Neo4j (seed, chat

hits.message:
fix(py/strands): address PR review findings

- search() and session-manager injection scoped preference recall to the
  store's user_id. search_preferences applies no :User filter, so a scoped
  construct could surface another tenant's preferences; get_preferences_for
  is the only user-scoped primitive, so a scoped lookup lists the user's
  active preferences instead of searching all of them.
- initialize()'s loop guard keys on the recorded loop, not _initialized:
  aclose() leaves a borrowed client connected, so an aclose/re-enter cycle
  on a new loop fell through to the already-connected path and produced the
  driver's opaque error instead of the named one.
- Store tools route through store.initialize() instead of a captured
  client: with injection disabled a tool call can be the store's first
  operation on a new loop.
- add_messages banks retry tokens per chunk, not after the whole batch, so
  a batch failing on chunk 2 is not re-written from chunk 1 on retry.
- _tool_prefix is 1:1. Sanitisation alone maps team/graph and team graph to
  the same prefix, and ToolRegistry overwrites duplicate @tool names
  silently; names that need rewriting now carry a digest of the original.
- Quick Start configures extraction. extraction defaults off and
  MemoryManager disables add_memory by default, so the documented
  agent("Remember ...") persisted nothing; extraction=True alone is every
  fifth turn, hence the explicit InvocationTrigger.
- The doc field-drift guard resolves a class by its import, not by name
  alone: strands.memory.ExtractionConfig and our config.settings one share
  a name and no fields.

feat(python): move adapters and extras to current framework majors; fix example-blocking bugs

Library prerequisites for the examples modernization (Phase 1 of the
examples review). Every framework adapter now targets the major that is
current in September 2026, and four bugs the examples tripped over are
fixed. All changes are covered by the unit suite (1794 passing) and the
integration suites for each adapter.

Framework adapters and extras
- PydanticAI 2.x: `[pydantic-ai]` is now `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]>=2.0,<3`
  (the meta package conflicts with the fastmcp pin). MemoryDependency,
  create_memory_tools, nams_memory_tools and record_agent_trace use the
  2.x toolset/RunContext API; trace outcomes were always "Completed".
- Google ADK 2.x: `google-adk>=2.0,<3` + `google-genai>=1.0`.
  Neo4jMemoryService implements the 2.x BaseMemoryService contract
  (SearchMemoryResponse of MemoryEntry with types.Content); agent turns
  are no longer dropped on ingest. NAMS compatibility from #130 kept.
- Microsoft Agent Framework GA: `[microsoft-agent]` is
  `agent-framework-core>=1.13,<2`; BaseContextProvider/BaseHistoryProvider
  renamed to ContextProvider/HistoryProvider; MIN_VERSION bumped.
- LangChain 1.x: `langchain-core>=1.0,<2` plus a new `[langchain-agents]`
  extra (`langchain>=1.0,<2`). Neo4jAgentMemory previously imitated a
  BaseMemory class that langchain-core 1.x does not ship; it is now a
  real BaseChatMessageHistory, Neo4jMemoryRetriever a real BaseRetriever,
  and a create_agent middleware (before_model/after_model) is added.
  Two async deadlocks in the adapters are fixed; NotSupportedError is
  tolerated on NAMS.
- Strands 1.52+: `strands-agents>=1.52,<2`; session manager re-verified
  against the multi-agent/bidi hooks; Bedrock model ids in
  integrations/strands/config.py moved to inference-profile ids.
- FastMCP 4 / MCP Python SDK 2: `[mcp]` is `fastmcp>=4.0,<5`. Server,
  tools, resources and prompts ported (keyword-only constructor,
  snake_case ToolAnnotations keys, Streamable HTTP). `mcp serve
  --transport sse` remains as a deprecated alias for streamable-http.
- OpenAI `>=2.0,<4`, Anthropic `>=1.0,<2` (temperature/top_p/top_k are
  no longer sent; structured output kept), sentence-transformers
  `>=3.0,<7`, crewai `>=1.0,<2`, llama-index-core `>=0.14,<1`,
  google-cloud-aiplatform `>=2.0,<3` + google-genai `>=1.66`.

Bug fixes
- Vertex AI embeddings: `text-embedding-004` was shut down on 2026-01-14
  and was still the default. Default is now `gemini-embedding-001` with
  `output_dimensionality` defaulting to 768 so existing vector indexes
  keep their dimensions; retired models raise a clear error
  (embeddings/vertex_models.py). Docs, tests and the examples README
  convention updated.
- Enrichment results never reached `entity.metadata`; the enrichment
  node properties and JSON blob are now folded into metadata
  (enriched_description, wikipedia_url, wikidata_id, image_url,
  enriched_at) and BackgroundEnrichmentService also SETs the URL
  properties it previously only selected.
- ExactMatchResolver reported match_type="exact" on its no-match path;
  it now reports "none".
- LongTermProtocol.wait_for_extraction accepts the NAMS keyword
  signature so client.long_term type-checks on both backends.

Docs: how-to and tutorial pages for each adapter, the MCP tutorial and
tool reference, the CLI and configuration references, and the TypeScript
how-to pages updated to the new APIs.

Dev dependency group gains python-dotenv and respx (used by the example
smoke tests that follow in later commits).

BREAKING: extras floors above; VertexAIEmbedder default model and
dimension behaviour; LangChain adapter base classes; MCP transport names

feat(support-desk-agent): seed the demo from STATE-Bench customer support

Replace the eight hand-written support-desk conversations with 24
curated trajectories from Microsoft's STATE-Bench customer-support
dataset (MIT, pinned at commit 5644b1838d96). They cover every task type
and all five customers, with 129 turns and 140 tool calls.

Data and ontology
- data/state-bench/ holds the trajectories, tasks and task environments
  plus the licence, copied unchanged.
- data/customer-support.ontology.yaml replaces the Arrows support-desk
  ontology: Customer, Order, OrderLine, Product and Warranty, with
  PLACED, CONTAINS, OF_PRODUCT, COVERS and REPLACED_BY. The header records
  the measured label choices: "Item" pulled product nouns, so the type is
  OrderLine; a declared Policy type caught every "return"/"refund", so
  policies are records without an extraction label.
- The demo no longer shares data with examples/ontology-lifecycle-bolt,
  so the parity test is gone.

Backend
- src/statebench/vendor/ copies the benchmark's environment, policies,
  schemas and tool definitions, changing only import lines. Each file
  names its source. It is excluded from ruff and strict mypy.
- src/statebench/world.py stores the task records as typed entities with
  RELATED_TO links, runs the vendored environment against the graph, and
  writes the changes of confirmed returns, refunds, exchanges and
  cancellations back. Each order is evaluated at its own task date
  (`today` in tool results). Policy gates and previews persist per
  session.
- The seed loads the records and policies, stores each conversation, and
  repairs ID mentions that extraction typed wrongly. It records every
  assistant turn's tool calls as a reasoning trace with TOUCHED edges:
  38 traces and 140 tool calls.
- The agent has the eleven STATE-Bench tools under their own names and
  schemas (writes run sequentially), plus recall_similar_tasks,
  find_customer, search_support_history and get_ontology. The
  instructions require a preview, then confirmation, for every change.

  mentions. Tool steps get readable thoughts (agent/thoughts.py).

Frontend
- New suggestions, OrderLine/Policy colours and grouping, and the
  one-click rename demo is now Warranty -> WarrantyCoverage.

Tests and docs
- The example test checks provenance and coverage, and replays all 140
  recorded tool calls against the vendored environment. The end-to-end
  test seeds, chats on TestModel, runs a real return through the graph,
  and renames and migrates Warranty.

hits.message:
fix(strands): rebind an owned client when Strands changes the event loop

Agent.__init__ initializes the store through strands._async.run_async
(asyncio.run in a throwaway thread) and every Agent.__call__ uses a
different loop. The neo4j async driver and the NAMS transport bind to the
loop that opened them, and initialize() returned early on _initialized,
so the guide's Quick Start raised "Task ... attached to a different loop"
from inside the driver on the first real call.

initialize() now records the running loop and, on a change:

  - owned client (settings=): close and reconnect on the current loop.
    One reconnect per synchronous Agent(...) invocation.
  - borrowed client (client=): raise, naming the problem and both
    remedies. Closing or reconnecting someone else's client is not ours
    to do.

aclose() resets the initialization state so re-entering the async context
manager reconnects, and tolerates a client whose loop has already gone.

Also drops the write-only _conversation_id attribute (_sink_key carries
the value) and trims the config docstring's argument against the
rejected TypedDict design, which belongs in the spec.

docs(spec): design for Strands MemoryStore integration

Neo4jMemoryStore implementing Strands' long-term-memory MemoryStore
protocol in both SDKs. Both Strands reviewers asked for it unprompted in
harness-sdk#3871, where they also asked us to keep the session manager
and the memory store apart as constructs.

Verified against strands-agents 1.52.0 and @strands-agents/sdk 1.13.0:
MemoryManager now ships its own per-model-call injection, and
first-party vended stores exist to copy the idiom from.

Notable outcomes:

- One store class per SDK defining both write sinks, so extraction is
  server-side by default while add stays live for the manager's tools.
- search() is an LTM fan-out over entities/preferences/facts, auto-gated
  per backend; add() writes a message into a deterministic sink
  conversation with extraction, with metadata["kind"] routing typed
  writes.
- The store stays free of Strands internals: both coexistence guards
  live in the session manager, which is the side that gets an agent.
- Store is positioned as the preferred memory construct; the session
  manager keeps transcript duties and gains no memory framing.

hits.message:
test(nams): gate live-NAMS tests on a throwaway workspace; stop resolver noise

The SDK cannot clean up what these two tests create. clear_session deletes a
conversation but not the entities NAMS extracted from it, and
NamsLongTermMemory declares _SPEC_DELETE_ENTITY while exposing no
delete_entity() -- so entities, and the pending fuzzy-merge candidates the
resolver files against them, accumulate permanently in whatever workspace the
credentials point at. A live run is a one-way write. Our own runs already left
the owner a review backlog to clear by hand.

So both tests now refuse to run unless NAMS_E2E_WORKSPACE_ID names a workspace
that is not MEMORY_WORKSPACE_ID (nor its NAMS_SANDBOX_WORKSPACE_ID alias):
unset and equal each skip with a reason that states why the variable is
separate. The gate is new tests/nams_live.py, called at module scope before
every other gate -- nams_credentials is session-scoped and would otherwise
report a missing key first, hiding whether the gate is wired at all. Both
docstrings now record that the opik pytest plugin loads .env into os.environ
regardless of the shell, so skips must be verified with `-p no:opik`; two
agents lost an hour to that.

The workspace is wired in explicitly rather than inherited: the integration
test overrides conftest's nams_config fixture, and build_nams_settings gains a
keyword-only workspace_id forwarded to NamsConfig -- the only missing link,
since without it MemorySettings falls back to MEMORY_WORKSPACE_ID and the gate
would be theatre. Default None keeps every existing caller unchanged.

Second fix: the e2e fixture's entity name was one stem plus a hex run suffix
(Zorbium89980F486C, Zorbium868C72705A, ...). Those are ~85% similar to each
other, so every run handed the resolver a fresh merge candidate against every
previous run. TOKEN is now one word drawn from a 128-word pool of pronounceable
nonsense, built by greedy rejection sampling that admitted a candidate only at
<= 55 against every incumbent under all four of rapidfuzz's ratio, WRatio,
partial_ratio and token_sort_ratio. Measured worst case over all 8128 pairs:
54.5, with no word a substring of another. Distinct runs cannot reach the
threshold; identical draws (1 in 128) are exact matches that merge and queue
nothing. One word, not two concatenated: a shared 8-char half measured 81.5
under partial_ratio, and a three-syllable scheme measured 90.9 -- only
whole-word distinctness holds substring-flavoured scorers down. RUN_ID still
namespaces the store name, user id and sink metadata, so runs stay traceable;
the run banner prints the codename since it is no longer derivable from RUN_ID.

Third: the aws-strands guide claimed user_id scopes writes via ":User edges",
which is bolt-only. NAMS stores tenancy as a plain userId property on the
conversation -- no node, no edge -- and filters the conversation listing on it;
_link_user_to_conversation exists only in memory/short_term.py. Guide and
design spec now state one clause per backend.

feat(strands): add Neo4jSessionManager — push-based conversation persistence for Strands agents (#136)

Adds `Neo4jSessionManager`, a Strands Agents `SessionManager` backed by
`MemoryClient` (self-hosted bolt and hosted NAMS). Complements the existing
pull-based `@tool` integration with the push-based half: every turn is persisted
automatically, history is restored on agent restart, and relevant long-term
memories can be injected per user message.

- `Neo4jSessionManager` — direct `SessionManager` implementation: lifecycle,
  hook wiring, write-behind buffer for guardrail redaction, `for_nams()` factory.
- `_retrieval.py` — `Neo4jRetrievalConfig` + concurrent long-term search and
  `<user_context>` block formatting (opt-in per-turn injection).
- `_messages.py` — pure Strands <-> Memory message mapping.
- `AsyncBridge` (`integrations/base.py`) — shared persistent-event-loop bridge
  for sync code driving loop-bound async transports.
- Shared NAMS settings-from-env helpers in `integrations/strands/config.py`.
- Restructured `aws-strands.adoc` (both modes as one integration) and a runnable
  shared-brain example (no API keys required).

Design notes: one Strands session maps to one `Conversation` (no Strands-specific
node types); persistence is memory-grade (text turns stored, tool-use blocks and
`agent.state` are not); redaction rewrites the buffer before the original reaches
the backend; injection never contaminates storage.

Programs that failed when a reader ran them
- core_memory_recipes.py gives its batch explicit, increasing
  timestamps. In 0.6.0 untimed batch messages share one timestamp, so
  the order assertion failed at random.
- nams_first_write.py creates the conversation, writes to the ID NAMS
  returns, reads the message back and deletes the conversation. It used

  passed with a TypeError.

hits.message:
feat(support-desk-agent): resizable columns and a readable graph layout

Resizable side columns
- Drag the edge between either side column and the chat to resize it, or
  focus the edge and use the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps, Home and
  End for the limits); double-click resets. The handle is a WAI-ARIA window
  splitter with pointer capture, so dragging over the graph canvas works.
- Widths are remembered per browser (useResizableWidth, read through
  useSyncExternalStore so hydration renders the default first) and clamped
  so the chat stays at least 420 px wide.
- The memory panel is a CSS size container: below 430 px the tab icons are
  dropped instead of squeezed, and the tool stats table wraps long tool
  names so its columns fit.

Graph layout and sizing
- Positions come from our own d3-force run (graphLayout.ts) rendered with
  NVL's "free" layout, because NVL's d3Force layout takes no options and
  pulled busy messages into a hairball. Springs are tuned per edge kind:
  typed RELATED_TO / SAME_AS short and stiff, MENTIONS medium and loose,
  conversation structure long and weak; collision padding leaves room for
  captions, and capped repulsion keeps the "All seeded" pieces together.
- An expanded graph pins the original nodes and places only the new
  neighbours; the view re-fits when positions change and after the panel
  is resized. Dragged nodes stay put when another node is selected.
- Smaller nodes (entities 36 px, conversations 42, messages 20) with
  captionSize 2, the largest that keeps ids like TK-2210 on one line (NVL
  accepts only 1, 2 or 3; other values render no caption). Relationship
  captions are 1.8x, and MENTIONS / HAS_MESSAGE labels are shown only
  around the selected node.

d3-force (already installed through @neo4j-nvl/base) is now a direct
dependency, with @types/d3-force for type-checking.

hits.message:
fix: drop type-name mentions and quiet the library's schema warnings

Two issues the support-desk app surfaced.

Type-name mentions. Span extractors type the class noun along with the
instances: in "which tickets does Grace have?" GLiNER2.5 returns `tickets` as
a Ticket, and sharper type descriptions did not stop it. Such a mention names
the type, not an entity. ExtractionResult.filter_invalid_entities() now also
drops a mention whose whole name - ignoring case, a leading article or
possessive ("my ticket", "open tickets") and regular plurals - is its POLE+O
type, its subtype, its extractor label (attributes["gliner2_label"]) or, via
the new optional `ontology` argument, the label the ontology declares for its
pair ("support cases" under SupportCase). Relations to a dropped mention go
with it, and message ingestion passes the client's ontology. "TK-2210" and
"Acme Company" are kept. Against real GLiNER2.5 output the generic "ticket(s)"
mentions are gone and every TK-/SO- reference, product and customer stays.

Schema warnings. On a fresh database Neo4j logged "label / relationship type
/ property key does not exist" for correct library queries - `e.aliases` in
entity resolution once per ingested message, plus :SchemaMigration and
HAS_VERSION at connect: 18 warnings for one ontology-lifecycle-bolt run. A
`keys()` guard or e['aliases'] does not prevent them; the planner resolves
both statically. Neo4jClient.execute_read/execute_write now open sessions with
the UNRECOGNIZED notification classification disabled (report_unrecognized=
False by default; driver < 5.22 spells it as a category). The read-only
client.query.cypher accessor passes report_unrecognized=True and
Neo4jClient.session() applies no filter, so user-written Cypher still warns.
The same run now logs none. CLAUDE.md item 23's keys()-guard advice is
corrected, and support-desk-agent no longer silences neo4j.notifications.

Tests: unit (2710), docs (1049), integration + docs programs (603) and
requires_neo4j examples (22) pass; a fresh support-desk seed gives the same
counts with no warnings.

test(strands): drive a real Agent against live NAMS on the synchronous path

Every existing test of Neo4jMemoryStore drives the store directly, on one
event loop -- the blind spot that let a Critical through review. Strands'
synchronous entry point runs Agent.__init__ on one throwaway loop and each
Agent.__call__ on another, so a settings=-constructed store connected its
client on the construction loop and then raised "attached to a different
loop" on the first call. initialize() now rebinds an owned client; nothing
exercised that end-to-end.

tests/e2e/test_strands_agent_nams_e2e.py constructs a real Agent over
hosted NAMS and a local tool-calling Ollama model, calls it twice
synchronously (construction-loop -> call-loop, then call-loop ->
call-loop), and asserts the memory landed in the sink conversation, comes
back out of store.search(), that the store's graph tool is registered
under its namespaced name while get_user_preferences is absent on NAMS,
and that MemoryManager's <memory> block reached the model (read off a
RecordingModel subclass overriding the public Model.stream -- no privates).

A sync test on purpose: asyncio_mode="auto" would otherwise run the body
inside a loop, and the fresh-loop-per-call entry point is the thing under
test. Extraction is awaited via wait_for_extraction/get_extraction_status,
never a sleep, and every live call is bounded by asyncio.wait_for.

Gated so it never breaks anyone's CI: skips unless MEMORY_API_KEY is in
the process environment and the Ollama endpoint answers a 5s probe. New
`e2e` marker, deliberately not `integration` (the root conftest ties that
marker to Neo4j reachability). Teardown deletes every conversation the run
created and asserts they are gone; NAMS_E2E_KEEP=1 leaves them for
inspection in the web UI.

hits.message:
fix(short-term): stop CREATE_MESSAGE fanning out over a forked chain

CREATE_MESSAGE read the conversation tail with an OPTIONAL MATCH that can
bind more than one row. Every clause after it runs once per row, so the
CREATE ran once per tail with the same $id and breached the uniqueness
constraint on Message.id.

Two concurrent appends produced that state: both read the same tail, both
linked to it, and left two messages with no outgoing NEXT_MESSAGE. The
next append then fanned out. This is not flakiness -- once a conversation
has two tails, every later append to it fails, sequential or not.

Write to the conversation before reading the tail so SET takes a write
lock that serializes concurrent appends, and collapse the tail candidates
to the newest so a chain already forked by an earlier write stays
appendable; migrate_message_links() remains the repair path for the fork
itself. GET_LAST_MESSAGE gets the matching ORDER BY -- it had LIMIT 1 but
no ordering, so the batch path picked an arbitrary tail.

The concurrency test blamed "UUID collisions" and staggered itself with a
sleep that hid the bug. It now runs unstaggered and asserts the invariant
that was actually broken: one head, one tail, one unbroken chain. A new
TestForkedChainRecovery builds the forked state directly, so the guard no
longer depends on winning a race.

Known gap, deliberately not addressed here: _ensure_conversation is a
read-then-create race, so concurrent first writes to one session can still
mint several conversations. session_id is deliberately not unique, so a
MERGE-plus-constraint fix is a data-model decision rather than a query
one; the test establishes the conversation first and says so.

Validation: verified against Neo4j 2026.07. Reverting the query change
fails both the concurrency test and the new deterministic one; with it,
tests/integration is 505 passed, 92 skipped (skips are NAMS-sandbox and
cloud-credential gates), and tests/unit is 1819 passed.

ci: cache Hugging Face model dir to fix flaky integration-test-matrix (#168)

The integration/example jobs use a sentence-transformers embedder
(all-MiniLM-L6-v2). With no caching, every run re-downloads the model from
Hugging Face, and test_no_openai_import_with_llm_none caps its subprocess at
120s — a cold/slow HF pull blows that cap and fails integration-test-matrix
intermittently (observed red on a feature branch while main was green, purely
on download-timing variance).

- Cache ~/.cache/huggingface in each job that pulls a model
  (integration-test, integration-test-matrix, integration-test-testcontainers,
  example-tests, example-tests-quick). Model-agnostic: rotating
  `key: hf-cache-<os>-<sha>` + `restore-keys: hf-cache-<os>-` restores the
  newest prior cache and re-saves whatever models the run pulled, so new models
  are picked up without maintaining per-model keys.
- Raise the no-llm subprocess timeout 120s -> 300s so the first
  (cache-populating) run tolerates a cold download.

fix(strands): store-tool naming, search budget, tenant-scoped writes, docs

Findings from the whole-branch review, other than the loop rebinding and
the formatting gate.

get_entity_graph reported every bolt edge as an invented
`relationship_type` attribute that the real Relationship model does not
have (it carries `.type`), and inverted the direction the library
reports. Now reads `.type` and orients edges by the relationship's own
source_id/target_id. The fake returned an invented relationship shape,
so the unit test asserted "WORKS_AT" — unreachable in production: the
bolt path cannot report a relationship's own type at all, because
execute_read's result.data() flattens a relationship to
(start, type, end) and drops its properties. The fake now returns real
Relationship objects shaped the way the bolt path really shapes them, the
unit test asserts that, and a new integration test pins it against a real
Neo4j so a library-side fix surfaces as a failing assertion. The library
defect itself is left for a separate change.

get_tools' names are now prefixed with the store's name. ToolRegistry
skips its duplicate-name check for @tool functions (supports_hot_reload
is always true there) and silently overwrites, so the store's
get_entity_graph / get_user_preferences were replacing
context_graph_tools' identically-named tools — which take different
arguments — in the guide's own combined snippet. Prefixing by store name
also lets several stores (the documented personal / team / org shape)
coexist.

search() applied its limit per kind, so max_search_results=5 returned up
to 15 rows, entity-first; Strands caps per store and then slices the
concatenation, so five entity hits starved preferences and facts
entirely. The budget is now handed out round-robin across the enabled
kinds, capped at the requested total.

add(kind="preference") passes user_identifier, so the write gets its
(:User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE] edge — which is exactly what the store's own
get_user_preferences reads — and does not raise under multi_tenant=True.

The unit-test CI job installs the `strands` extra. Without it every
strands test file's `pytest.importorskip("strands")` skipped, hiding 136
tests including the tripwire for a strands rename of
MemoryManager._stores. Verified the extra resolves and the tests run on
both 3.10 and 3.13.

Docs and spec: user_id scopes writes, not reads; the three spec-mandated
store limitations are now in the guide (separate sink, in-process retry
dedupe, conversation_id pointed at the chat history); the row-3 pairing
exception said "neither side extracts" where the store owns extraction;
the spec's "one private attribute" limitation now names both
(_stores and _injection_config) and its Testing table no longer promises
a NAMS integration suite that was not shipped. Plus: _row() is
keyword-only, the get_preferences_for docstring's stated reason for its
cast was wrong (it is on the protocol, with a different calling
convention), two short_term docstrings named MemorySettings.multi_tenant
instead of MemorySettings.memory.multi_tenant, and the CHANGELOG's Fixed
entry now states the observable break.

hits.message:
fix(embeddings): serialize sentence-transformers encode calls

SentenceTransformerEmbedder ran model.encode on the default executor with
nothing serializing it, so concurrent embed()/embed_batch() calls ran it
on several threads at once. The sentence-transformers/... provider
string picks the mps device on Apple Silicon, and PyTorch's MPS backend
is not thread-safe: two threads compiling a Metal kernel race on its
kernel cache and the process segfaults (EXC_BAD_ACCESS in
MetalShaderLibrary::exec_unary_kernel on both threads). The support-desk
demo backend hit this when the Reasoning panel requested similar traces
twice at once (React StrictMode).

encode now runs under one process-wide lock. A single encode already
uses every CPU core, so serializing costs little off the GPU.

The new unit test fails without the lock (overlapping encode calls) and
passes with it.

hits.message:
feat(extraction): adopt GLiNER2.5 with ontology-driven extraction and resolution

Replace the gliner v1 + GLiREL extraction stage with GLiNER2.5 (the `gliner2`
package) and make a first-class ontology drive extraction, relation
validation, storage and entity resolution on the bolt backend. Release 0.7.0.

Extraction
- New `GLiNER2Extractor`: loads `fastino/gliner2.5-base-v1` via
  `AutoExtractor`, decodes entities and relations in one JointIE pass with
  typed endpoints, windows long input at 384 library-counted words, and
  offers an opt-in span-attribute pass. Relations carry mention ids and
  `derived` flags; entities carry ids and offsets.
- Remove `GLiNEREntityExtractor`, `GLiRELExtractor`,
  `GLiNERWithRelationsExtractor` and `gliner_extractor.py`; the old names
  raise an `ImportError` with a migration hint. Domain catalogs move to
  `domain_schemas.py`, label mapping to `label_mapping.py`.
- Extras: new `[gliner2]` (`[gliner]` stays as a deprecated alias);
  `[extraction]` and `[full]` carry gliner2. Relock moves transformers to
  4.57.x and drops gliner/glirel. New `ExtractionConfig` fields for
  thresholds, windowing, overlap policy, attributes, quantize/compile.

Ontology (both backends)
- New `neo4j_agent_memory.ontology` package: the NAMS document model
  promoted and extended (descriptions, aliases, per-type resolution
  thresholds, relationship constraints), built-in POLE+O and domain
  templates, compiler to JointIE schemas and LLM prompt fragments,
  converters for `EntitySchemaConfig`, domain catalogs and arrows files,
  structural validation and diff.
- `client.ontology` now works on bolt (`BoltOntology`): versioned
  `:Ontology`/`:OntologyVersion` storage, activate, clone, import, diff
  and a synchronous migrate. `MemoryClient(ontology=...)`,
  `SchemaConfig.ontology_path`, `use_active_ontology` and
  `validation_mode` select the effective ontology; strict mode rejects
  undeclared types and forbidden relationship pairs.
- `ExtractionResult.validate_relations()` runs as a pipeline stage and on
  ingestion; the LLM extractor prompt carries the relationship catalogue.

Storage and resolution
- Typed relations merge on `RELATED_TO {type}` with `support`, `derived`,
  `extractor`, `source_message_ids` and `evidence`; `r.type` is canonical
  and a one-time backfill (`SchemaConfig.backfill_relation_types`) migrates
  legacy edges. Relationship readers now return real properties instead of
  defaults (they previously mis-parsed driver tuples).
- New `OntologyResolver` on the ingestion path by default
  (`resolution.resolve_on_ingest=False` opts out): normalisation,
  type-constrained blocking in Cypher, alias gazetteer, weighted scoring
  with review band -> pending `SAME_AS`, two-pass episode clustering,
  tenant scoping. Dedup thresholds are single-sourced from
  `ResolutionConfig` (auto-merge 0.90, review 0.85).

Evaluation, examples, docs
- Relation precision/recall/F1, `MatchPolicy`, B-cubed and gold data in
  `core/metrics.py` + `benchmarks/`; `benchmarks/compare_extractors.py`;
  `extraction` and `resolution` eval dimensions.
- New keyless `examples/ontology-extraction`; lennys-memory backend
  relocked onto gliner2.
- Docs: migration guide, ontology-driven extraction and resolution tuning
  how-tos, ~40 pages updated with the GLiNER/GLiNER2.5 naming glossary;
  CHANGELOG 0.7.0; version bump.

BREAKING CHANGE: gliner v1 and GLiREL extractors are removed; the default
GLiNER model id changes; `RELATED_TO` edges merge on `{type}` (legacy edges
are backfilled on first connect); ingestion resolves entities by default.

docs(spec): design for Strands MemoryStore integration

Neo4jMemoryStore implementing Strands' long-term-memory MemoryStore
protocol in both SDKs. Both Strands reviewers asked for it unprompted in
harness-sdk#3871, where they also asked us to keep the session manager
and the memory store apart as constructs.

Verified against strands-agents 1.52.0 and @strands-agents/sdk 1.13.0:
MemoryManager now ships its own per-model-call injection, and
first-party vended stores exist to copy the idiom from.

Notable outcomes:

- One store class per SDK defining both write sinks, so extraction is
  server-side by default while add stays live for the manager's tools.
- search() is an LTM fan-out over entities/preferences/facts, auto-gated
  per backend; add() writes a message into a deterministic sink
  conversation with extraction, with metadata["kind"] routing typed
  writes.
- The store stays free of Strands internals: both coexistence guards
  live in the session manager, which is the side that gets an agent.
- Store is positioned as the preferred memory construct; the session
  manager keeps transcript duties and gains no memory framing.

feat(extraction): adopt GLiNER2.5 with ontology-driven extraction and resolution

Replace the gliner v1 + GLiREL extraction stage with GLiNER2.5 (the `gliner2`
package) and make a first-class ontology drive extraction, relation
validation, storage and entity resolution on the bolt backend. Release 0.7.0.

Extraction
- New `GLiNER2Extractor`: loads `fastino/gliner2.5-base-v1` via
  `AutoExtractor`, decodes entities and relations in one JointIE pass with
  typed endpoints, windows long input at 384 library-counted words, and
  offers an opt-in span-attribute pass. Relations carry mention ids and
  `derived` flags; entities carry ids and offsets.
- Remove `GLiNEREntityExtractor`, `GLiRELExtractor`,
  `GLiNERWithRelationsExtractor` and `gliner_extractor.py`; the old names
  raise an `ImportError` with a migration hint. Domain catalogs move to
  `domain_schemas.py`, label mapping to `label_mapping.py`.
- Extras: new `[gliner2]` (`[gliner]` stays as a deprecated alias);
  `[extraction]` and `[full]` carry gliner2. Relock moves transformers to
  4.57.x and drops gliner/glirel. New `ExtractionConfig` fields for
  thresholds, windowing, overlap policy, attributes, quantize/compile.

Ontology (both backends)
- New `neo4j_agent_memory.ontology` package: the NAMS document model
  promoted and extended (descriptions, aliases, per-type resolution
  thresholds, relationship constraints), built-in POLE+O and domain
  templates, compiler to JointIE schemas and LLM prompt fragments,
  converters for `EntitySchemaConfig`, domain catalogs and arrows files,
  structural validation and diff.
- `client.ontology` now works on bolt (`BoltOntology`): versioned
  `:Ontology`/`:OntologyVersion` storage, activate, clone, import, diff
  and a synchronous migrate. `MemoryClient(ontology=...)`,
  `SchemaConfig.ontology_path`, `use_active_ontology` and
  `validation_mode` select the effective ontology; strict mode rejects
  undeclared types and forbidden relationship pairs.
- `ExtractionResult.validate_relations()` runs as a pipeline stage and on
  ingestion; the LLM extractor prompt carries the relationship catalogue.

Storage and resolution
- Typed relations merge on `RELATED_TO {type}` with `support`, `derived`,
  `extractor`, `source_message_ids` and `evidence`; `r.type` is canonical
  and a one-time backfill (`SchemaConfig.backfill_relation_types`) migrates
  legacy edges. Relationship readers now return real properties instead of
  defaults (they previously mis-parsed driver tuples).
- New `OntologyResolver` on the ingestion path by default
  (`resolution.resolve_on_ingest=False` opts out): normalisation,
  type-constrained blocking in Cypher, alias gazetteer, weighted scoring
  with review band -> pending `SAME_AS`, two-pass episode clustering,
  tenant scoping. Dedup thresholds are single-sourced from
  `ResolutionConfig` (auto-merge 0.90, review 0.85).

Evaluation, examples, docs
- Relation precision/recall/F1, `MatchPolicy`, B-cubed and gold data in
  `core/metrics.py` + `benchmarks/`; `benchmarks/compare_extractors.py`;
  `extraction` and `resolution` eval dimensions.
- New keyless `examples/ontology-extraction`; lennys-memory backend
  relocked onto gliner2.
- Docs: migration guide, ontology-driven extraction and resolution tuning
  how-tos, ~40 pages updated with the GLiNER/GLiNER2.5 naming glossary;
  CHANGELOG 0.7.0; version bump.

BREAKING CHANGE: gliner v1 and GLiREL extractors are removed; the default
GLiNER model id changes; `RELATED_TO` edges merge on `{type}` (legacy edges
are backfilled on first connect); ingestion resolves entities by default.

Branch: `fix/asset-summarize-unparsed-recovery` — see [branch naming](.github/BRANCH_NAMING.md)

## What & why

Asset **Regenerate** intermittently returned `400 summarize_failed`. OpenRouter load-balances `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` across upstreams, and some (observed: Phala — not excluded even by `require_parameters: true`) ignore `response_format: json_schema` and answer with plain prose, which `Output.object()` cannot parse.

Recover the description from the raw reply instead of failing, and share the trim/cap normalization between both paths.

```diff
 summarizeLinkedDocContent
   generateText(output: Output.object(...))
-    result.output.description -> normalize
+    result.output.description -> normalize
   catch (error)
-    return { ok: false, message: "Could not summarize file." }
+    error.text
+      -> recoverDescriptionFromUnparsedOutput()  # prose | fenced JSON | embedded JSON
+      -> normalize (raw JSON without a description is rejected)
+    return { ok: true, description } | existing failure
```

## Checklist

- [x] **User impact:** describe: Regenerate and Add-asset AI descriptions succeed when an upstream skips strict JSON formatting; unrecoverable failures behave as before. No cost change — same formatter model, no upstream pinning. Runs that used the fallback log `recovered=unparsed_response`.
- [x] **Migration:** none
- [x] **Tests:** unit — `backend/src/services/linked-docs-summarize.test.ts` +4 cases (prose recovery, fenced-JSON recovery, parse error without text, unparsed JSON without description); 11/11 pass
- [x] **README:** N/A

## How to verify

1. `cd backend && npx vitest run src/services/linked-docs-summarize.test.ts` → 11 passed
2. `npm run build` from repo root → clean
3. Click **Regenerate** on a workspace asset; runs served by a non-conforming upstream log `Success: ... recovered=unparsed_response` and return a draft description instead of a 400.

Deploy (backend only): `docker compose build backend && docker compose up -d backend`

## Evidence

- **Before:** forcing Phala routing (healing plugin on or off) → `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError`, response text is prose (`startsJson=false`), `POST .../assets/:assetId/summarize` → `400`. Production logs: `savor_pizza.jpeg`, `Event Space Brochure_compressed.pdf`.
- **After:** the same error shape fed to the service returns `{ ok: true, description: "This file is a compressed PDF brochure about event spaces." }` (test: “recovers the description from plain prose…”), with fenced-JSON recovery covered by a second test.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — reverting restores previous behavior; no schema or data changes.

**Blast Radius:** single service (`linked-docs-summarize.ts`) used by the asset summarize routes and the Add-asset AI description flow.

v2.1.8

What's Changed

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.7...v2.1.8

v2.1.7

Security fixes

This release includes a fix for the following security issue:

serveStatic with allowPercentInPath still allows the double-decode middleware bypass

Affects: serveStatic with allowPercentInPath: true. The fix for GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f rejects a path containing %, but the allowPercentInPath option skipped that check entirely. A malformed percent sequence such as /static/%%36%31dmin/secret.txt was routed as /static/%61dmin/secret.txt, so middleware on /static/admin/* did not run, and serveStatic then decoded %61 to a and served static/admin/secret.txt. The default configuration was already fixed in 2.1.3. GHSA-fj57-4f93-cfw6

serveStatic now accepts the second decode only when its result equals the routed path with %25 replaced by %. File names containing a literal %, requested as %25, are served as before.

The same fix ships in hono v4.13.18 (GHSA-74fm-fwc7-3fwp).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.6...v2.1.7

v2.1.6

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Backslash in the request path is parsed as a path separator, bypassing path-based access control at a reverse proxy

Affects: all requests. The raw request-target was passed to the WHATWG URL parser, which treats a backslash in the path as / and resolves .. segments, so /admin\secret reached the application as /admin/secret. A reverse proxy that forwards the backslash unchanged applied its path-based rules to the original path. GHSA-jpvv-r467-5p4w

A request whose path contains a raw backslash is now rejected with 400 Bad Request, for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and WebSocket upgrades. A percent-encoded backslash (%5C) and a backslash in the query string are still accepted.

WebSocket upgrade request-target starting with // replaces the host in c.req.url, bypassing Origin checks

Affects: upgradeWebSocket. The URL of an upgrade request was built by resolving the request-target against the Host header, so a request-target such as //attacker.example/ws set the host of c.req.url to a client-chosen value while routing still saw /ws. An application that compared Origin with the origin of c.req.url could be bypassed by a page on another site. GHSA-7v5p-43qr-wch5

The host of upgrade requests now comes from the Host header, as for ordinary requests.

Unhandled ECONNRESET on the socket during an asynchronous WebSocket upgrade crashes the process

Affects: upgradeWebSocket. While the application handled an upgrade request, the socket had no error listener. A client that reset the connection during asynchronous middleware caused an unhandled 'error' event and terminated the process. GHSA-qv5m-9pm6-hqp3

Error and close events on the socket are now handled while the application runs, and a pending upgrade is released when the socket closes.

## Summary
When a WhatsApp channel is inactive, the agent should still generate and record a **shadow reply** for every incoming message — but not send it to the user.

## Why
- Users can see how the agent would reply before going live.
- Builds trust in the agent quality before switching the channel on.
- Zero-risk testing: no real customer receives anything while the channel is inactive.

## Behavior
- Channel inactive → incoming messages still run through the agent pipeline.
- Agent reply is captured as a shadow reply (visible in the conversation view, clearly marked as a preview/draft).
- Nothing is delivered to the WhatsApp user.
- When the channel goes live, existing behavior continues as normal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Incoming messages on inactive channels produce a visible shadow reply in the UI
- [ ] Shadow reply is labeled/clearly distinguished from a real sent reply
- [ ] No outbound message is sent to the WhatsApp user
- [ ] Shadow replies are recorded so they can be reviewed before going live

  • 43ad966: Report interrupted when a stream ends cleanly without its provider completion signal, preserving partial output without emitting an error solely for the interruption.

    This applies to OpenAI (Chat, Responses, and Completions), Anthropic, Google (Generate Content and Interactions), Alibaba, Amazon Bedrock Converse, Cohere, DeepSeek, Groq, Hugging Face Responses, Mistral Chat, Moonshot AI, Open Responses, Perplexity, and xAI Responses. It also covers cutoffs in later Anthropic messages and Google automatic continuations.

    Compatibility notice: These streams previously fell back to other or omitted the finish part. Applications must now handle interrupted in finish-reason switches, mappings, and custom validation. ## Summary
When a WhatsApp channel is inactive, the agent should still generate and record a **shadow reply** for every incoming message — but not send it to the user.

## Why
- Users can see how the agent would reply before going live.
- Builds trust in the agent quality before switching the channel on.
- Zero-risk testing: no real customer receives anything while the channel is inactive.

## Behavior
- Channel inactive → incoming messages still run through the agent pipeline.
- Agent reply is captured as a shadow reply (visible in the conversation view, clearly marked as a preview/draft).
- Nothing is delivered to the WhatsApp user.
- When the channel goes live, existing behavior continues as normal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Incoming messages on inactive channels produce a visible shadow reply in the UI
- [ ] Shadow reply is labeled/clearly distinguished from a real sent reply
- [ ] No outbound message is sent to the WhatsApp user
- [ ] Shadow replies are recorded so they can be reviewed before going live

Branch: `fix/agent-stale-media-urls`

## What & why

Agent transcripts persisted inbound media as presigned URLs (1-hour TTL). Every later run replayed history and let the AI SDK re-download the stored URL, so once it expired Supabase Storage answered `400 Bad Request` and the whole run failed (`Failed to download …: 400 Bad Request`) — conversations stayed broken until the URL left history (see #23 example thread). Transcripts now persist stable storage references (`media_ref`: bucket + path) and mint a fresh signed URL on every run; legacy signed URLs already stored are re-signed during history resolution (and dropped only when unresolvable, so one missing attachment cannot fail a run). Eval turns sign from their stored path instead of the persisted `signedUrl`.

## Checklist

- [x] **User impact:** AI no longer gets permanently stuck on a conversation after a media URL expires; already-affected conversations recover on their next run (no migration).
- [x] **Migration:** none — stored `agent_messages` content is JSONB; legacy signed URLs are handled at read time.
- [x] **Tests:** unit/integration — new `storageParseSignedUrlKey` and history-media resolver suites, plus updated agent runtime, inbound debounce, outbound mirror, and eval subject tests. Full backend suite: 784 passing.
- [x] **README:** N/A

## How to verify

1. `cd backend && npm test` (784 pass) and `npm run build` from the repo root.
2. Send an image to a dry-run/live line, wait >1 hour, then send another message: the run should no longer fail with `Failed to download …: 400 Bad Request`, and the earlier image is still visible to the model (re-signed from storage).
3. Deploy note: normal VPS image rebuild (`docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build`); no migrations.

## Security finding S-01 — CRITICAL

**Category:** OWASP A01 Broken Access Control / A07 Auth Failures
**Evidence:** static code review + **confirmed by live dynamic test (2026-10-14)**

`POST /api/whatsapp/events` (backend/src/routes/whatsapp.ts:722) has **no authentication**:
- `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION` is required at startup (`lib/env.ts:47`) but **never validated anywhere** in backend code
- No auth middleware on the route
- Rate limiter explicitly *skips* this path

**Live proof (single request, zero credentials):**
```
POST /api/whatsapp/events
{"type":"message.inbound","connectionId":"<known-id>","messageId":"forge-…",
 "chatId":"15559990001@s.whatsapp.net","sender":"15559990001@s.whatsapp.net",
 "senderName":"Attacker","wid":"15550001111@s.whatsapp.net",
 "messageType":"textMessage","text":"INJECTED-FORGED-MESSAGE-PWNED",…}
→ 200 {"received":true,"message":"processed: 1 event(s)"}
```
Verified in DB after the request: conversation created (`Attacker - WhatsApp`), message row persisted (`role=user, content=INJECTED-FORGED-MESSAGE-PWNED`), attacker contact record created. Also unauthenticated `connection.state` manipulation accepted (200).

**Impact:** anyone with network reach to the backend (or via the nginx `/api` proxy) can forge WhatsApp inbound messages, poison AI agent history, pollute the shared inbox/CRM, and flip connection state.

## Fix
1. Enforce shared secret: `timingSafeEqual` on an `x-webhook-token` header vs `env.whatsappWebhookAuthorization` at the top of `/events` (mirror the pattern already used in `resolveConnection` for `/send`)
2. Whatsapp service must send it as a header, not URL query (see companion issue: token leaks into logs)
3. Regression test: 401 without token / with wrong token

*From the 2026-10-14 security study (static + dynamic). Full report: Senqo Security Study — Business Readiness Report.*

hits.body:
## Problem

Admins currently manage the platform by clicking through separate pages: Agent profiles, Knowledge base, Analytics, Reports, Conversations, Integrations, Settings. There is no single place where an admin can simply **ask a question in natural language** ("How many handoffs did we have this week?", "What knowledge sources are attached to the Sales agent?", "Which conversations were reported lately?") and get an answer — let alone **perform management actions** through that same chat.

This means:
- Admins must know where each feature lives in the UI to use it.
- Getting answers requires manually navigating and reading tables/charts.
- There is no conversational, AI-assisted way to manage the platform.

## Proposed solution

Add an **Admin AI Chat** — a dedicated admin-only AI assistant inside the platform that admins can use to:

1. **Ask about the platform** — natural-language questions answered from live platform data (e.g. conversation stats, handoff counts, reported errors, agent performance, knowledge base contents, integration status).
2. **Manage stuff through chat** — perform common management actions conversationally, e.g.:
   - Update agent profile / settings
   - Add, edit, or review knowledge entries
   - Look up a conversation and summarize it
   - Change channel/integration settings
   - Trigger common workflows (e.g. create an eval case from a conversation)

## Suggested implementation approach

- Build on the existing agent infrastructure (agent runtime, tool/function-calling) rather than a separate stack.
- Expose platform management operations to the agent as **admin-scoped tools**, mirroring the existing backend APIs.
- Enforce **role-based access**: this chat is only available to admin users; the AI's tool calls must respect the same permission checks as the UI/API.
- For destructive or high-impact actions (e.g. changing agent behavior, deleting knowledge), require an explicit **confirmation step** in the chat before execution.
- Surface which tools/actions the AI used to answer, so admins can verify the response.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admin sees an "AI Chat" entry point (e.g. in the dashboard sidebar) that opens a chat interface.
- [ ] Admin can ask questions about platform data and receive accurate, data-grounded answers (not hallucinated numbers).
- [ ] Admin can perform at least the core management actions through chat (agent settings, knowledge entries).
- [ ] Non-admin users cannot access the admin chat or its underlying tools.
- [ ] Destructive/impactful actions require explicit confirmation in-chat before being applied.
- [ ] The chat shows which tool calls/actions were used to produce each answer.

## Out of scope (for this issue)

- End-user/customer-facing chat changes (this is admin-only).
- The customer-service agent behavior itself.

## Notes

- Relates to #13 (user satisfaction collection) and #12 (reply/handoff metrics confusion) — the admin chat could also serve as a natural surface for asking "why did the bot reply/hand off here?", but that is optional for this issue.

Branch: `fix/connection-delete-guard`

## What & why

Deleting a connection failed with `connection_delete_failed` whenever any scheduled task still referenced it (the `tasks` FK uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` and nothing ever cleaned it up); the same blocked delete also left unlinked devices showing as Authorized. Branch: `fix/asset-summarize-unparsed-recovery` — see [branch naming](.github/BRANCH_NAMING.md)

## What & why

Asset **Regenerate** intermittently returned `400 summarize_failed`. OpenRouter load-balances `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` across upstreams, and some (observed: Phala — not excluded even by `require_parameters: true`) ignore `response_format: json_schema` and answer with plain prose, which `Output.object()` cannot parse.

Recover the description from the raw reply instead of failing, and share the trim/cap normalization between both paths.

```diff
 summarizeLinkedDocContent
   generateText(output: Output.object(...))
-    result.output.description -> normalize
+    result.output.description -> normalize
   catch (error)
-    return { ok: false, message: "Could not summarize file." }
+    error.text
+      -> recoverDescriptionFromUnparsedOutput()  # prose | fenced JSON | embedded JSON
+      -> normalize (raw JSON without a description is rejected)
+    return { ok: true, description } | existing failure
```

## Checklist

- [x] **User impact:** describe: Regenerate and Add-asset AI descriptions succeed when an upstream skips strict JSON formatting; unrecoverable failures behave as before. No cost change — same formatter model, no upstream pinning. Runs that used the fallback log `recovered=unparsed_response`.
- [x] **Migration:** none
- [x] **Tests:** unit — `backend/src/services/linked-docs-summarize.test.ts` +4 cases (prose recovery, fenced-JSON recovery, parse error without text, unparsed JSON without description); 11/11 pass
- [x] **README:** N/A

## How to verify

1. `cd backend && npx vitest run src/services/linked-docs-summarize.test.ts` → 11 passed
2. `npm run build` from repo root → clean
3. Click **Regenerate** on a workspace asset; runs served by a non-conforming upstream log `Success: ... recovered=unparsed_response` and return a draft description instead of a 400.

Deploy (backend only): `docker compose build backend && docker compose up -d backend`

## Evidence

- **Before:** forcing Phala routing (healing plugin on or off) → `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError`, response text is prose (`startsJson=false`), `POST .../assets/:assetId/summarize` → `400`. Production logs: `savor_pizza.jpeg`, `Event Space Brochure_compressed.pdf`.
- **After:** the same error shape fed to the service returns `{ ok: true, description: "This file is a compressed PDF brochure about event spaces." }` (test: “recovers the description from plain prose…”), with fenced-JSON recovery covered by a second test.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — reverting restores previous behavior; no schema or data changes.

**Blast Radius:** single service (`linked-docs-summarize.ts`) used by the asset summarize routes and the Add-asset AI description flow.

## What & why

Instance admins had no way to use AI to inspect or manage platform-level state. This adds an administrative AI chat on the Instance admin page: admins can ask questions about the instance (settings, workspaces, users) and have the public registration setting changed for them, backed by admin-scoped tools over existing repositories.

## Checklist

- [x] **User impact:** Instance admins get an "AI assistant" card on /admin — chat persists per admin, with clear-chat and error states.
- [x] **Migration:** added (`database/migrations/0029_admin_chat_messages.sql`) — new `admin_chat_messages` table (per-admin chat history).
- [x] **Tests:** unit (backend routes/agent/repository, frontend hook/component) + e2e `e2e/admin-ai-chat.spec.ts` (3 tests, passing locally).
- [x] **README:** N/A (feature documented in code; no README admin section today).

## How to verify

1. Sign in as an instance admin → `/admin` → "AI assistant" card at the top.
2. Ask "How many workspaces do I have?" — the model calls the platform-state tool and answers from live data.
3. Ask "Turn off public registration." — the assistant flips the registration toggle (the Public registration card reflects it on reload).
4. Clear chat wipes the stored conversation (`DELETE /api/admin/ai/messages`).

Branch: `fix/agent-stale-media-urls`

## What & why

Agent transcripts persisted inbound media as presigned URLs (1-hour TTL). Every later run replayed history and let the AI SDK re-download the stored URL, so once it expired Supabase Storage answered `400 Bad Request` and the whole run failed (`Failed to download …: 400 Bad Request`) — conversations stayed broken until the URL left history (see #23 example thread). Transcripts now persist stable storage references (`media_ref`: bucket + path) and mint a fresh signed URL on every run; legacy signed URLs already stored are re-signed during history resolution (and dropped only when unresolvable, so one missing attachment cannot fail a run). Eval turns sign from their stored path instead of the persisted `signedUrl`.

## Checklist

- [x] **User impact:** AI no longer gets permanently stuck on a conversation after a media URL expires; already-affected conversations recover on their next run (no migration).
- [x] **Migration:** none — stored `agent_messages` content is JSONB; legacy signed URLs are handled at read time.
- [x] **Tests:** unit/integration — new `storageParseSignedUrlKey` and history-media resolver suites, plus updated agent runtime, inbound debounce, outbound mirror, and eval subject tests. Full backend suite: 784 passing.
- [x] **README:** N/A

## How to verify

1. `cd backend && npm test` (784 pass) and `npm run build` from the repo root.
2. Send an image to a dry-run/live line, wait >1 hour, then send another message: the run should no longer fail with `Failed to download …: 400 Bad Request`, and the earlier image is still visible to the model (re-signed from storage).
3. Deploy note: normal VPS image rebuild (`docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build`); no migrations.

## Summary
When a WhatsApp channel is inactive, the agent should still generate and record a **shadow reply** for every incoming message — but not send it to the user.

## Why
- Users can see how the agent would reply before going live.
- Builds trust in the agent quality before switching the channel on.
- Zero-risk testing: no real customer receives anything while the channel is inactive.

## Behavior
- Channel inactive → incoming messages still run through the agent pipeline.
- Agent reply is captured as a shadow reply (visible in the conversation view, clearly marked as a preview/draft).
- Nothing is delivered to the WhatsApp user.
- When the channel goes live, existing behavior continues as normal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Incoming messages on inactive channels produce a visible shadow reply in the UI
- [ ] Shadow reply is labeled/clearly distinguished from a real sent reply
- [ ] No outbound message is sent to the WhatsApp user
- [ ] Shadow replies are recorded so they can be reviewed before going live

hits.body:
Implements the two features promised on the [agent observability page](https://www.chiranjeevthomas.com/projects/agent-observability): per-step tracing of every agent run, and a golden-set eval that runs on every prompt or model change.

## Tracing
- Every run (chat, escalation, decision, client reply, CLI) records its steps: model calls (the prompt, tools offered, tokens, latency), tool calls, refused tools, approval cards, the human decision (an edited approval is labelled `approved_with_edits`) and the email send.
- Runs go to new `agent_runs` and `agent_trace_steps` tables.
- Text is redacted and capped. Traces are kept for 30 days (`pg_cron` purge), with RLS on.
- Tracing is fail-open: a trace write times out after 3 s, and dropped traces are counted in `/api/health`.
- Responses carry `X-Trace-Id`. `GET /api/invoices/{id}/traces` serves the invoice's owner, and a new **Trace** tab in the invoice page shows the runs.

## Golden-set eval
- 18 disputes across levels 0–3, including prompt injection through client replies.
- Cases run through the real API and graph, offline, and are graded from their traces: tool choice, no send or approval-gated action without an approval, tone rules, and an LLM judge.
- Tier 1 replays scripted runs inside `pytest`. Tier 2 (`python -m evals.run`) runs the live model, and `.github/workflows/evals.yml` posts its scorecard on PRs that touch the agent.
- `python -m evals.promote` turns a bad trace into a case.
- Baseline: 94% tool choice, approval rule 100% (18/18), judge 4.33/5.

## Bugs it found and fixed
- **Escalation gating was advisory.** Above-level tools still ran, and above-level drafts reached the approval card. `enforce_tool_gate` now refuses them.
- **Injected client replies could escalate or rewrite the client's email**, using tools with no approval step. Runs started by a reply can no longer use those tools.
- **Opening a chat erased a waiting approval card** proposed by a client reply. The cause: `None` vs `''` in the state sync, plus `/history` writing state while a card was waiting.
- **The CLI crashed after approving**, because it resumed without the freelancer context.
- **Two leaks in the new redaction**, both caught by review (bounded regexes, merged overlapping spans).

## Not in scope
Deferred items are in `TODOS.md`. The P1s: putting `escalate_dispute` behind an approval card, and the empty reply to small-claims questions that the eval flags.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest`: 400 passed
- [x] `npx vitest run`: 133 passed; `tsc -b` and `npm run build` pass
- [x] Live `python -m evals.run` passes its gates
- [x] Schema validated on a local Postgres 16 (idempotent re-run, retention, cascades)
- [ ] Production smoke test after deploy

## Summary

Follow-up to #3. Hardens the invoice PDF/DOCX parser so a single transient Groq hiccup no longer dumps the user into the weak heuristic fallback (which grabs the wrong email + jurisdiction).

The retry loop previously only re-tried on `429`/rate_limit and bailed instantly on anything else (timeout, 5xx, dropped connection, one-off structured-output glitch). Now:
- **Transient** signals (429, 5xx, timeout, connection, overloaded/unavailable) → all 3 attempts
- **Permanent** errors (401 bad key, 400 bad request) → fail fast
- **Unknown** one-off errors → get a 2nd attempt before falling back

This matches the resilience the chase path already has.

## Test plan

- [x] Both sample invoices (PDF + DOCX) parse with full LLM extraction — correct client email + jurisdiction, confidence 1.0, zero warnings
- [x] Verified live via `POST /api/invoices/parse` across repeated runs

## Summary

Capture runtime failures in dedicated Sentry projects and post Sentry links to Slack using the free Web API.

```text
FastAPI / React / handled API failures → Sentry issues → grouped email alerts
                                      ↘ Slack bot → #invoicechaser-alerts
```

- Capture all error events and sample production traces at 10%. Scrub request data, invoice IDs, arbitrary exception messages, locals and user identity.
- Report caught summary failures without changing their responses. Drain telemetry at the end of Vercel invocations.
- Upload hidden frontend source maps and remove them before publication.
- Browser Slack reporting sends only an event ID to an origin-checked, size-limited and rate-limited route. Credentials stay server-side.
- Slack uses a bounded queue, duplicate suppression, serialized sends and Retry-After cooldowns. Sentry email covers grouped new issues and regressions.
- Resolve names and omit unresolved date-field labels in final inbound-analysis replies using the existing domain formatter; preserve concrete dates. Clarify that a reported payment promise prepares the existing owner approval card with its stated date. Tool implementations, approval rules and raw model traces stay intact.
- Preserve the branch's README architecture/documentation update.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no Sentry/Slack reporting, unresolved names in inbound analysis, and a live dated-payment-promise case returned prose without its review card.
  **After:** 1,023 backend tests passed (13 skipped), 190 frontend tests passed; lint/build passed. Real graph/API placeholder regressions and unresolved-date tests failed before the fixes and passed afterward; concrete bracketed date facts are preserved. Independent reviews found no actionable issues.
- Real local FastAPI and actual React entry-point/lifecycle errors reached Sentry:
  - [Backend issue](https://referfee.sentry.io/issues/INVOICE-DISPUTE-AGENT-SERVER-1)
  - [Frontend issue](https://referfee.sentry.io/issues/INVOICE-DISPUTE-AGENT-FRONTEND-3)
- Slack acknowledged both deliveries in Software-Factory / #invoicechaser-alerts:
  - [Backend message](https://software-factoryorg.slack.com/archives/C0CJJPTLWM9/p1794995980865289)
  - [Frontend message](https://software-factoryorg.slack.com/archives/C0CJJPTLWM9/p1794995967206069)
- Temporary triggers removed; tests/evals disable real telemetry. Backend logs/traces verified through Sentry MCP. Source-map upload succeeded with zero `.map` files left in output.
- Dedicated projects, email workflow 6360535, Slack app/channel and Vercel Production settings are configured outside Git. They take effect on the next production release.
- All required CI gates passed on bf74b18: 36/36 live agent cases with 100% tool/approval/tone checks; summary evaluation 27/28 positive (96.4%), with 95% single-case, 100% sequence and 100% sequence-step results against the unchanged 85% minimum. The summary missed-promise attribution case remains the single negative result. [Live evaluation](https://github.com/code0monkey1/invoice-dispute-agent/actions/runs/44434566787) and [backend/frontend CI](https://github.com/code0monkey1/invoice-dispute-agent/actions/runs/44434566845) passed. Testing credentials remain separate from production.
- Preview builds pass, but Preview API has no app credentials and cannot start. Production configuration is separate. Production symbolication and delivery remain post-release checks.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

## Why
The golden-set eval failed on almost every run, each time on different cases. I measured it: most failures weren't agent mistakes.

1. **Throttling graded as wrong answers.** Groq's free tier allows 8,000 tokens/min per model per key, and one agent turn uses ~4–6k. When a *client-reply* case was rate-limited, `handle_client_reply` logged and swallowed the error (correct for a webhook), so the eval saw "the agent didn't call the tool". `l3-client-pays` scored 0/3 under load, then passed on its own.
2. **Placeholders.** The agent wrote `[date]` / `[Client Name]` (tone-rule failures). It had no date to work with, since the product stores only `days_overdue`, and no person's name for a company client.

## Changes
- **Agent context:** adds `Today's date: YYYY-MM-DD` to the current-invoice block.
- **Prompts (all levels):** "If you don't know a contact person's name, greet the company by its name. Write real dates, counted from today's date in the invoice details, or leave the date out." Deliberately no bracketed example, per the existing `test_no_prompt_shows_a_placeholder_to_copy`.
- **Harness:** after a client reply, a failed `inbound_reply` trace raises `client reply failed: …`, so the runner retries a 429 as "provider busy" instead of grading it.
- **CI:** `--pace 20` between cases, timeout 30 min. The judge can use its own key (`EVAL_JUDGE_GROQ_API_KEY`, now set as a repo secret).
- No thresholds or baseline changed.

## Tried and dropped
An extra prompt line forbidding `update_invoice_details` / `escalate_dispute` on client replies: an A/B on the affected cases showed no difference (the recipient-change case was 3/3 either way), and the tool gate already refuses those calls.

## Testing
- `pytest`: 430 passed (new: today's date in the context, judge key, and a rate-limited client reply surfaced as a retryable error).

## Problem
At level 3 the prompt tells the agent to answer small-claims questions *"using the jurisdiction in the invoice details"*, and final notices must name it. But `build_user_invoice_context`, which builds the "Current invoice" block the model sees, **never included the jurisdiction**. When a *client-reply* case was rate-limited, `handle_client_reply` logged and swallowed the error (correct for a webhook), so the eval saw "the agent didn't call the tool". `l3-client-pays` scored 0/3 under load, then passed on its own.
2. **Placeholders.** The agent wrote `[date]` / `[Client Name]` (tone-rule failures). It had no date to work with, since the product stores only `days_overdue`, and no person's name for a company client.

## Changes
- **Agent context:** adds `Today's date: YYYY-MM-DD` to the current-invoice block.
- **Prompts (all levels):** "If you don't know a contact person's name, greet the company by its name. Write real dates, counted from today's date in the invoice details, or leave the date out." Deliberately no bracketed example, per the existing `test_no_prompt_shows_a_placeholder_to_copy`.
- **Harness:** after a client reply, a failed `inbound_reply` trace raises `client reply failed: …`, so the runner retries a 429 as "provider busy" instead of grading it.
- **CI:** `--pace 20` between cases, timeout 30 min. The judge can use its own key (`EVAL_JUDGE_GROQ_API_KEY`, now set as a repo secret).
- No thresholds or baseline changed.

## Tried and dropped
An extra prompt line forbidding `update_invoice_details` / `escalate_dispute` on client replies: an A/B on the affected cases showed no difference (the recipient-change case was 3/3 either way), and the tool gate already refuses those calls.

- `pytest`: 430 passed (new: today's date in the context, judge key, and a rate-limited client reply surfaced as a retryable error).

## Problem
Production runs on `InMemorySaver` (`/api/health`: `"checkpointer": "InMemorySaver"`), so every redeploy or new Vercel instance forgets each invoice's chat and any draft waiting for approval.

The old Postgres path couldn't have fixed it. Its connection had no `autocommit`, so nothing `PostgresSaver` wrote was ever committed: it looked fine on one warm instance and was lost when the instance was recycled. Its never-committed `CREATE TABLE` also held locks with no timeout, so a second instance's cold start could hang.

## What changes
- **`src/checkpointer.py`**: a pooled `PostgresSaver` on Supabase's transaction pooler (6543), with autocommit, prepared statements off, `dict_row`, health-checked connections and `min_size=0`. Startup makes one direct connection and checks the tables are at the installed library's migration version. If not, it falls back to memory with a reason (`not_configured`, `tables_missing`, `migrations_behind`, or a redacted connection error).
- **`/api/health`**: `checkpointer` is now `{store, reason}`. `status` is `degraded` when production is on memory, or when a configured database failed. The old `checkpointer_error` and `database_url_set` fields are removed; nothing in the repo read them.
- **`python -m src.checkpoint_setup`**: creates and upgrades the tables, locks them down (RLS on, no anon/authenticated access), and fails on a broken index left by an interrupted migration. Nothing does DDL at import any more.
- **`supabase/schema.sql`**: adds the dedicated `langgraph_checkpointer` role (only its own tables, statement 15 s / idle-in-transaction 30 s timeouts, no password in the file) and an idempotent lockdown block.
- **Tests**: `conftest` forces `DATABASE_URL=""`. Unit tests cover the store choice, secret redaction, the schema check and health. Opt-in `tests/test_checkpointer_postgres.py` (`TEST_DATABASE_URL`, local hosts only) checks that history and a pending draft survive a simulated restart, and that two invoices chatted with at once stay separate.

## Rollout (code first, credential second)
Merging this is safe without `DATABASE_URL`: behaviour is unchanged and health reports `degraded`. After the deploy:
1. run `python -m src.checkpoint_setup` against production as `langgraph_checkpointer`
2. add `DATABASE_URL` (sensitive, through stdin) and redeploy
3. check that `/api/health` shows `checkpointer.store == "postgres"`

## Testing
- `pytest`: 421 passed, 15 skipped (5 opt-in Postgres tests, 10 needing a built frontend).
- Opt-in Postgres tests: 5/5 against local Postgres 16, as the restricted role, as the superuser, and on a brand-new empty database.
- The production role was checked through the real Supavisor transaction pooler: repeated queries, pipeline mode, pool health checks, no access to `invoices`/`users`/`auth`.

## Why

When a client says "I'll pay on the 15th", the agent proposes `mark_invoice_pending` and you approve it. Until now that approval **saved nothing**: the promise and its date were lost, the dashboard never showed them, and the agent forgot them on the next turn.

Fixing that showed that invoice data was written from several routes in `api/index.py`. The escalation level had three writers, one of which rewrote it after every approval. Payment changes were reconciled inside `/resume`. So invoice writes now go through a single module.

We also considered giving the agent an open-source CRM to work through, and decided against it. The README explains why (AGPL licences; no invoice model; the wrong tool shape for an agent).

## What changed

- **`src/services/invoice_service.py`**: the only writer of invoice data (status, payments, promise to pay, escalation level, settling, client details). Routes call it, and tools still only propose changes in agent state. Approving a tool commits only that tool's allowed fields (`COMMITTABLE_BY_TOOL`).
- **Promise to pay:** `mark_invoice_pending` validates the date and proposes `status=pending` + `follow_up_date`. Approval saves both; the agent sees the date in its context.
- **Dashboard:** "Promised to pay by Nov 15, 2026" / "Promise missed (…)" status, a Promised filter, and the date in the chat side panel.
- **README:** reasons, an animated flow (`docs/promise-to-pay.svg`), and 3 sequence diagrams.
- Removed the unused mock MCP server and a dead DB helper; exposed `build_agent()` for tests.

## Fixed by adversarial testing (including against the real LangGraph graph)

| Attack | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Approve an email draft while agent state says `paid` | Invoice marked paid, chasing stopped | Email approvals commit no invoice changes |
| Model records a payment of `inf` | Invoice marked paid | Rejected by the tool and the service |
| `inf`/`NaN` in any tool call | Chat and history 500 on every load | Responses replace them with `null` |
| Late approval racing a settle | Could reopen the invoice | Writes carry `status != paid` |
| `/details` with a recipient list or a 5,000-char name | Saved | 422 |
| Ungated tool resets the level to 1 | Written back on the next approval | The level only goes up |

## Migration

`ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS follow_up_date TEXT;` is **already applied** to the production Supabase project, and is also in `supabase/schema.sql`.

## Tests

- `pytest`: 220 passed. New files: `test_invoice_service.py`, `test_promise_to_pay.py`, `test_pentest_invoice_writes.py`, `test_real_graph_payments.py`.

## Why

`invoices.user_id` had no index; Postgres doesn't index foreign keys automatically. `get_invoices_by_user` (`user_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC`) runs on every dashboard load and twice per chat message (agent context + on-topic check), and read every user's invoices each time.

## Change

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_invoices_user_created ON invoices (user_id, created_at DESC);
```

It serves both the filter and the newest-first sort, plus the guest → account migration's `user_id` filter. `created_at` is `YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS` text, which sorts in time order.

**Cost:** a few µs per insert and about 80 bytes per invoice. Status, payment and escalation updates don't touch indexed columns. **Benefit:** not visible at today's size (Postgres rightly still scans a tiny table), but lookups stay proportional to one user's invoices as the table grows.

## Production

Already applied in the Supabase SQL editor. `pg_indexes` lists it, and `EXPLAIN` (with seq scans disabled to force the choice) shows **Index Scan using idx_invoices_user_created** with no Sort node.

## Tests
No app code changes. `pytest`: 239 passed.
