### Problem

Streaming dropped `redacted_thinking` blocks. They arrive as a complete block in `content_block_start` with no deltas, but the streaming switch only handled tool-use blocks, so they fell through and were discarded. The non-streaming path already handled them.

Because the encrypted `data` never reached the caller, it couldn't be replayed on the next turn, and Anthropic can reject follow-up requests with missing thinking blocks.

### Fix

Added a `redacted_thinking` case to the streaming switch that emits the block as a `ChunkReasoning` with `redactedData` metadata, matching what the request serializer reads back.

### Tests

- New `TestChat_Stream_RedactedThinking`.
- `go build`, `go vet`, and the anthropic streaming suite pass.

#### Summary

The Google serializer maps each GoAI `RoleTool` message to a separate Gemini
`role: "user"` content and does not normalize consecutive tool messages.
Parallel tool execution therefore produces consecutive user contents instead
of one user content containing all function responses.

The same path also drops Gemini function-call IDs in both directions:

- parsed provider IDs are replaced with synthetic `call_<name>_<index>` IDs;
- serialized `functionCall` and `functionResponse` objects omit their `id`.

Google's Gemini 3 examples group parallel responses into one user block, and
the current function-calling guide requires returning the provider's matching
function-call ID:

- https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/gemini-3#parallel-function-calling

## What this PR adds

AWS Bedrock support for `provider.EmbeddingModel`, covering all text embedding models available on Bedrock today:

| Model | Batch | ProviderOptions |
|---|---|---|
| `amazon.titan-embed-text-v1` | 1 | — |
| `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` | 1 | `dimensions` (256/512/1024), `normalize`, `embeddingTypes` |
| `amazon.titan-embed-image-v1` | 1 | `outputEmbeddingLength` (256/384/1024) |
| `amazon.nova-2-multimodal-embeddings-v1:0` | 1 | `embeddingPurpose`, `embeddingDimension`, `truncationMode` |
| `cohere.embed-english-v3` | 96 | `input_type`, `truncate` |
| `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3` | 96 | `input_type`, `truncate` |
| `cohere.embed-v4:0` | 96 | `input_type`, `truncate`, `output_dimension`, `embedding_types` |
| `twelvelabs.marengo-embed-2-7-v1:0` | 1 | `textTruncate` |
| `twelvelabs.marengo-embed-3-0-v1:0` | 1 | — |

## Design notes

- Reuses existing SigV4 signing, `options`, and credential resolution from the `Chat` provider — no new deps
- `MaxValuesPerCall()` is model-aware: 96 for Cohere (AWS-confirmed limit), 1 for everything else
- Cohere v3 and v4 have different response shapes (`embeddings: [][]float64` vs `embeddings: {float: [][]float64}`) — handled transparently
- Titan v1 only accepts `inputText`; sending `normalize`/`dimensions` to it causes an API error, so those fields are gated behind a `isTitanV2()` check
- `EmbedMany` auto-chunking and parallel calls work out of the box via the core `goai.EmbedMany` function

```go
// Titan V2
model := bedrock.Embedding("amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0")
result, err := goai.Embed(ctx, model, "hello world")

// with options
result, err := goai.Embed(ctx, model, "hello world",
    goai.WithEmbeddingProviderOptions(map[string]any{"dimensions": 512}),
)

// Cohere — EmbedMany batches automatically up to 96/call
model := bedrock.Embedding("cohere.embed-english-v3")
result, err := goai.EmbedMany(ctx, model, texts)
```

Follow-up to #88 (zenflow review finding, responses.go:814).

## Problem

The Responses API `error` event handler overwrote the flat `message`/`code` with the nested `error` object unconditionally:

```go
if ev.Error != nil {
    msg, code = ev.Error.Message, ev.Error.Code
}
```

A partial nested object (e.g. a nested `code` with no `message`) clobbered a flat `message` with an empty string, losing the detail and falling back to the generic "stream error".

## Fix

Per-field fallback with `cmp.Or`: prefer the nested value when set, otherwise keep the flat value.

```go
if ev.Error != nil {
    msg = cmp.Or(ev.Error.Message, msg)
    code = cmp.Or(ev.Error.Code, code)
}
```

## Scope

Isolated to `provider/openai/responses.go` (Responses API streaming). Affects OpenAI Responses mode and Azure (delegates to openai for Responses-only models); no effect on Chat Completions, openaicompat providers, or the shared `errors.go`.

## Tests

New `TestStreamResponses_ErrorEventPartialNested` (flat message + nested code with empty nested message) asserts the flat message is preserved and the nested code still drives 429/retryable classification.

## Summary

Native structured-output mode (`structuredOutputMode: "outputFormat"`, or `"auto"` with a supported model) sent the JSON schema as the **top-level `output_format`** request field. The Anthropic Messages API has deprecated that field, so every native-output-format request now fails with `400: output_format: This field is deprecated. Use 'output_config.format' instead.` This nests the schema under `output_config.format` instead.

## Changes

- `buildRequest` (`provider/anthropic/anthropic.go`): nest the native structured-output schema under `output_config.format`, merging into the same `output_config` object that `effort` writes so the two coexist. (The merge lives here, not in `injectNativeOutputFormat`, because `buildRequest` runs after the wire body exists and is the only place `output_config` is assembled.)
- Add `output_format` to `anthropicHandledKeys` so the provider-options passthrough loop no longer copies it to the top level of the body.
- Update the doc comment on `injectNativeOutputFormat` to describe the nesting.
- Update `TestDoGenerate_NativeOutputFormat` and `TestDoStream_NativeOutputFormat` to assert the `output_config.format` wire shape; their httptest handlers now use only non-fatal assertions so a missing field can no longer panic the handler goroutine into a client-side `EOF`.
- Add `TestBuildRequest_NativeOutputFormat`: asserts the body carries `output_config.format` (type `json_schema`, correct schema), carries no top-level `output_format`, and that `format` coexists with `effort`. Verified failing before the fix.

# HTTP 400 "No tool output found for function call call_" with OpenAI provider and (default) store: true

**Provider**: openai (Responses API, automatic stored-response continuation)

**Go version**: go1.27.3

**GoAI version**: v0.11.0

**Description**

When the OpenAI Responses API is used with automatic stored-response continuation (the default: `store: true`, no request-side `store` option), `setPreviousResponseID` sets `previousResponseId` on the first tool-call step and then **refuses to refresh it on subsequent steps**, because the guard treats caller-supplied and auto-set values identically:

```go
// generate.go — setPreviousResponseID()
if store, ok := response.ProviderMetadata["store"].(bool); ok && !store {
    if auto, _ := params.ProviderOptions["goaiAutoPreviousResponseID"].(bool); auto {
        delete(params.ProviderOptions, "previousResponseId")
        delete(params.ProviderOptions, "goaiAutoPreviousResponseID")
    }
    return
}
...
if _, ok := params.ProviderOptions["previousResponseId"]; ok {
    return
}
```

The only code path that removes the key runs when the response reports `store: false`. OpenAI reports `store: true`, so the id set at step 1 stays pinned for the entire turn — and since only the trailing tool outputs are sent as input (per `convertAutoContinuationInput`), OpenAI prepends only the *first* response's output, producing a `function_call` / `function_call_output` pair with mismatched tool call ids.

**Code to reproduce**

```go
model := openai.Chat("gpt-5.1", openai.WithAPIKey(os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")))

weatherTool := goai.NewTool("get_weather", "Get the current weather for a city.",
	func(ctx context.Context, args struct {
		City string `json:"city" jsonschema:"description=City name"`
	}) (string, error) {
		return "22°C and sunny", nil
	})

// Any prompt that forces two or more tool rounds:
result, err := goai.GenerateText(context.Background(), model,
	goai.WithPrompt("Check the weather in Tokyo, then Paris, then New York — one city at a time."),
	goai.WithProviderOptions(map[string]any{"useResponsesAPI": true}), // store defaults to true
	goai.WithTools(weatherTool),
	goai.WithMaxSteps(5),
)
```

**Expected behavior**

When `goaiAutoPreviousResponseID` is already set (i.e. goai owns the id), each completed step should advance `previousResponseId` to the latest response so the chain grows with the loop:

```go
if auto, _ := params.ProviderOptions["goaiAutoPreviousResponseID"].(bool); auto {
    delete(params.ProviderOptions, "previousResponseId")
    delete(params.ProviderOptions, "goaiAutoPreviousResponseID")
}
if _, ok := params.ProviderOptions["previousResponseId"]; ok {
    return
}
```

Caller-supplied `previousResponseId` must remain pinned as it is today.

**Actual behavior**

For a tool loop that needs two or more tool rounds (`MaxSteps >= 3`):

- **Step 1** → `resp_1`, output ends with `function_call(call_1)`. Tools execute.
- **Step 2** → request: `previous_response_id=resp_1`, input `[function_call_output(call_1)]`. Valid; `resp_2` created. Tools execute again.
- **Step 3** → request: `previous_response_id=resp_1` **(stale)**, input `[function_call_output(call_2)]`.

OpenAI prepends only `resp_1`'s output, so the merged sequence is `function_call(call_1)` followed by `function_call_output(call_2)` — a mismatched pairing. The API rejects with:

```
400 invalid_request_error: No tool output found for function call call_1
```

Even if the request were accepted, the context would be corrupted: step 3 never sees `resp_2`'s assistant message or round 1's tool output. Every request after the second tool round of a turn fails, so any OpenAI turn requiring ≥ 2 tool rounds cannot complete.

**Additional context**

- Observed on a production agent platform (Go, goai v0.11.0, OpenAI provider, Responses API default). Sessions consistently fail mid-tool-loop with `No tool output found for function call call_...`, where the reported `call_id` is the first tool call of the failing turn. Anthropic/OpenRouter providers on the same platform are unaffected (they don't use stored-response continuation). Matching error semantics are documented in openai/openai-agents-python#3620.
- Existing coverage doesn't catch it: `TestResponsesStorageContinuation` and `TestGenerateText_ToolLoopPropagatesPreviousResponseID` only run a 2-step loop, where the stale id happens to be correct. `TestSetPreviousResponseID` asserts the non-refresh behavior for caller-supplied ids but has no case for a *second auto-set* on an auto continuation.
- Workaround: request-side `store: false` (documented as disabling automatic continuation) avoids the bug entirely — every step sends the full history statelessly, and reasoning round-trips via `reasoning.encrypted_content`. We've applied that as a mitigation.

## Summary

Gemini's `cachedContents` API allows callers to upload an immutable prefix once — system instructions and tool definitions — and reference it across subsequent requests. This provides significant latency and token-cost savings for agentic workloads that resend large tool catalogs or extensive system prompts every turn.

While `goai` already supported referencing an existing cache via `cachedContent`, there was no mechanism to create or renew cached contents, forcing consumers to hand-roll custom API clients and duplicative serializers for tool definitions and system instructions.

This PR adds `google.CacheClient`:
- Reuses `buildToolsAndConfig` and `buildSystemInstruction` to guarantee the cached prefix is byte-for-byte identical to generate requests (preventing cache-miss drift).
- Exposes `goai.ToolDefinitions` to permit high-level `goai.Tool` to `provider.ToolDefinition` conversion without breaking encapsulation.
- Supports both the Gemini Developer API (`cachedContents/<id>`) and Google Cloud Vertex AI (`projects/.../locations/.../cachedContents/<id>`) through existing auth and endpoint helpers.
- Adds `Create` and `Renew` operations with TTL support.

## Verification

- Tested against mock servers for create, renew, prefix matching, and Vertex routing.
- Package test coverage in `provider/google`: 98.5%.
- `go test ./...` passes across all packages.

**Is this about a specific provider?**

Core SDK, `mcp` package.

**Description**

Rebuild `goai/mcp` on top of the official MCP Go SDK (`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`, v1.8.0) and keep in GoAI only what GoAI uniquely provides: the bridge between MCP and GoAI concepts.

Today `goai/mcp` is its own implementation of the protocol (JSON-RPC, stdio/Streamable HTTP/SSE transports, negotiation, OAuth). It targets the 2024-11-05 and 2025-03-26 revisions and a subset of the client features (no elicitation, completions, progress or subscriptions).

The current spec, **2026-07-28**, changed the protocol's foundations: no handshake and no sessions (each request carries its version and capabilities in `_meta`), `server/discover`, Multi Round-Trip Requests instead of server-initiated requests, `subscriptions/listen`, a required `resultType`, `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers, cacheable list results, and new OAuth rules (RFC 9207 `iss` validation, Client ID Metadata Documents, issuer-bound credentials). Keeping a parallel implementation means chasing every revision. The official SDK (Tier 1, maintained with Google) already implements 2026-07-28 and negotiates down to 2024-11-05.

**Use case**

Applications connecting to third-party MCP servers expect the full standard: resources and templates, prompts, completions, progress, cancellation, structured tool output, elicitation (form and URL), OAuth for protected remote servers, and graceful behavior with servers that implement only part of the spec.

**Proposed API**

```go
import (
    sdk "github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
    "github.com/zendev-sh/goai/mcp"
)

session, err := mcp.Connect(ctx, &sdk.CommandTransport{Command: exec.Command("my-server")},
    mcp.WithElicitationHandler(askUser), // capabilities derived from the handlers you pass
)
defer session.Close()

tools, err := mcp.ConvertTools(ctx, session) // paginated, keeps structuredContent
result, err := goai.GenerateText(ctx, model, goai.WithPrompt("..."), goai.WithTools(tools...))

msgs, err := mcp.PromptMessages(ctx, session, "code-review", args) // prompt -> []provider.Message
```

Design points:

- **The official SDK owns the protocol.** GoAI deletes its own JSON-RPC, transports and OAuth, and does not re-wrap SDK types (that would be another parallel implementation). The public API exposes `*sdk.ClientSession`.
- **`goai/mcp` keeps the bridges:** MCP tools → `goai.Tool` (without dropping `structuredContent` or non-text content), prompts → GoAI messages, resource contents → GoAI parts, OAuth integration with `provider.TokenSource`.
- **Separate Go module (`mcp/go.mod`)**, like `observability/langfuse` and `observability/otel`. The SDK brings about eight dependencies, so the root module stays minimal and users who don't need MCP don't pay for them. `release.yml` already tags submodules.
- **Standard only.** Everything the SDK implements from the core spec is available. Deprecated features (roots, sampling, logging, HTTP+SSE transport, dynamic client registration) keep working because the SDK supports them for compatibility, but they are documented as deprecated and no new GoAI helper builds on them. Extensions such as MCP Apps or tasks are out of scope.
- **No capabilities the application didn't configure.** The SDK advertises `roots` by default; GoAI's helpers build the client with explicit capabilities.

**Breaking change**

The current `goai/mcp` API changes. The PR includes a migration guide (before → after), migrated examples and a rewritten `docs/concepts/mcp.md` with a capability matrix (spec feature → SDK API → GoAI bridge → test).

**Alternatives considered**

- Upgrading the in-house implementation to 2026-07-28: large rewrite (stateless core, MRTR, subscriptions, new auth rules) that would keep diverging from the reference SDK.
- Adding the SDK to the root module: imposes its dependencies on every GoAI user.

## Motivation

Anthropic's prompt caching accepts a `ttl` on the ephemeral `cache_control` marker, selecting a **5-minute** or **1-hour** cache lifetime. The SDK always emitted the bare marker:

```json
{"type": "ephemeral"}
```

so callers were pinned to the 5m default with no way to opt into 1h — the better trade for long-lived system prompts and agentic loops whose turns outlive a 5-minute window.

## API

```go
result, err := goai.GenerateText(ctx, model,
    goai.WithSystem(bigSystemPrompt),
    goai.WithPromptCaching(true),
    goai.WithCacheTTL("1h"),   // "5m" | "1h"; empty = provider default (5m)
)
```

Surfaced on the provider layer as:

- `GenerateParams.CacheTTL` — request-wide, applied to every ephemeral marker the request emits.
- `Part.CacheControlTTL` — per-breakpoint, for callers building parts directly.

Both the system block and message breakpoints honour it, including the file/document parts added in #115 — uploaded documents inherit the configured TTL rather than silently falling back to 5m.

## Backward compatibility

Additive and non-breaking. An empty TTL emits **exactly** the previous payload — `{"type":"ephemeral"}` with no `ttl` key — so existing behaviour is preserved byte-for-byte. `TestBuildRequest_SystemCacheControl` asserts the key is absent by default.

Two internal signatures gain a parameter (`applyCacheControl`, `applyCaching`); both are unexported.

The 1h TTL is GA and requires no beta opt-in — the wire test asserts the `anthropic-beta` header is unchanged.

## Tests

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| `TestBuildRequest_SystemCacheControlTTL` | TTL on the system block |
| `TestBuildRequest_SystemCacheControl` | default omits `ttl` (no behaviour change) |
| `TestBuildRequest_CacheTTLWithoutPromptCaching` | TTL inert when caching is off |
| `TestConvertMessages_PartLevelCacheTTL` | per-part breakpoint, set and empty |
| `TestConvertMessages_MessageLevelCacheControlIgnoresPartTTL` | message-level marker must not absorb a part TTL |
| `TestEphemeralCacheControl` | helper, both branches |
| `TestApplyCaching_TTLPropagatedToMarker` | propagation + no caller mutation |
| `TestBuildParams_CacheTTL` / `...DefaultsEmpty` | option → params plumbing |
| `TestDoGenerate_CacheTTLOnWire` | end-to-end mock server: TTL on wire, beta header unchanged |

**Patch coverage: 100%** (27/27 added statement lines). Package coverage unchanged vs. base — root 97.6%, `provider/anthropic` 98.0%, project total 97.9%.

`go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass (34 packages, 0 failures).

hits.body:
First, this project looks really cool!

We’re considering using it to replace the corresponding functionality in one of our internal apps, but I’d like to know how far GoAI is from a 1.0 release. Is the current version considered a stable, official release, and should we expect any major changes in the future?

I performed a read-only API compatibility audit of GoAI, covering all 27 provider packages and the shared compatibility layer.

`go test ./...` passes, but most tests use mocked responses and do not validate the latest official provider schemas. The basic text-generation paths generally look fine, but I found the following confirmed compatibility issues:

### Confirmed issues

- **OpenAI GPT Image 2**: `response_format: "b64_json"` is sent even though GPT Image models do not support this parameter.  
  `provider/openai/image.go`

- **OpenAI file inputs**: external file URLs are sent as `file_data` instead of `file_url`; uploaded raw bytes may also be treated as base64 incorrectly.  
  `internal/openaicompat/messages.go`, `provider/openai/responses.go`

- **OpenAI Chat audio inputs**: unsupported formats such as AAC, OGG, FLAC, and M4A may be sent; the current API documents WAV and MP3.  
  `internal/openaicompat/messages.go`

- **Anthropic Files API**: `created_at` is parsed as `int64`, while the current API returns an RFC3339 string.  
  `provider/anthropic/file.go`

- **Anthropic/Vertex/Bedrock file uploads**: Vertex and Bedrock Anthropic models expose a Files uploader even though Anthropic Files API is not supported on those platforms.

- **Anthropic RemoteRef images**: uploaded image references are silently dropped.  
  `provider/anthropic/anthropic.go`

- **Anthropic manual thinking + forced tool choice**: `thinking.type="enabled"` combined with `tool_choice="any"` or a specific tool is rejected by the current API.

- **Bedrock native Anthropic server tools**: Web Search and Code Execution are exposed even though they are not available on Amazon Bedrock.  
  `provider/bedrock/anthropic.go`

- **Bedrock TwelveLabs Marengo embeddings**: Marengo 2.7/3.0 use `InvokeModel`, but AWS requires `StartAsyncInvoke`.  
  `provider/bedrock/embed.go`

- **Bedrock embeddings**: binary/non-float embedding modes are exposed, but the response parser only handles float embeddings.  
  `provider/bedrock/embed.go`

- **Bedrock stop-sequence metadata**: `/delta/stop_sequence` is used instead of the documented `/stop_sequence`.  
  `provider/bedrock/converse.go`

- **Vertex API-key embeddings**: Gemini API endpoint is combined with a Vertex-style `:predict` request body.  
  `provider/vertex/vertex.go`, `provider/vertex/embedding.go`

- **Google Gemini 3**: default `thinkingLevel` is sent as lowercase `"high"` instead of the documented uppercase enum `"HIGH"`.  
  `provider/google/google.go`

- **Google Gemini image generation**: `numberOfImages` is sent inside `generationConfig`, although it is not part of the Gemini `generateContent` schema.  
  `provider/google/image.go`

- **Google Files API**: file upload does not follow the current resumable upload protocol.  
  `provider/google/file.go`

- **Google Imagen**: Imagen support is still advertised even though the official documentation lists Imagen as deprecated and scheduled for shutdown on 2026-08-17.

- **Google RemoteRef images and server-tool responses**: uploaded images and fields such as `executableCode`, `codeExecutionResult`, and URL-context metadata may be dropped.

- **Cohere `tool_choice`**: GoAI sends lowercase OpenAI-style values, while Cohere v2 documents `REQUIRED` and `NONE`.

- **Cohere structured outputs**: the `json_schema` request shape is incompatible with the current Cohere v2 API.

- **Cohere parameters**: `seed`, `k`, `frequency_penalty`, and `presence_penalty` are silently ignored.

- **MiniMax Anthropic compatibility**: `tool_choice="required"` and forced tool names are not supported by MiniMax.

- **MiniMax image input**: HTTPS image URLs are silently dropped by the Anthropic adapter.

- **xAI Web Search/X Search**: these server-side tools are sent to Chat Completions, but the current xAI API requires the Responses API.

- **Cerebras**: `MaxOutputTokens` is sent as `max_tokens`; current Cerebras models require `max_completion_tokens`.  
  `internal/openaicompat/openaicompat.go`

- **llama.cpp**: default base URL is missing `/v1`, causing default chat and embedding requests to use incorrect paths.  
  `provider/llamacpp/llamacpp.go`

- **Ollama tool loop**: tool results omit the required `tool_name` field.

- **Ollama thinking**: string thinking levels such as `"high"` and `"medium"` are reduced to `false`.

- **Perplexity Sonar**: the provider advertises custom tool calling although Sonar does not support registering custom tools.

- **Perplexity structured output**: schema-less requests send `json_object`, which is not part of the current Sonar schema.

- **Requesty PDF input**: GoAI sends nested `type="file"` content, while Requesty requires flat `type="input_file"` content.

- **Fireworks**: tool-call arguments may be string/object/null, while the shared parser only accepts strings.

- **Mistral**: `seed` is sent as `seed` instead of Mistral's `random_seed`; reasoning content is also not fully preserved by the shared parser.

- **DeepSeek**: cache usage fields such as `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` are not parsed.

**Provider:** Cloudflare Workers AI (`cloudflare.Chat`)

**Go version:** v1.25.5

**GoAI version:** v0.7.10

## Description

We are observing a schema compatibility issue when using native tool calling with Cloudflare Workers AI.

When `goai.WithTools()` is enabled, the request message content is automatically transformed into an OpenAI-style content array. However, Cloudflare's API expects the message content to remain a plain string.

As a result, requests fail before reaching the model with a `400 Bad Request` validation error.

## Error Output

```text
400 Bad Request: {"errors":[{"message":"AiError: Bad input: Error: oneOf at '/' not met, 0 matches: required properties at '/' are 'prompt', Type mismatch of '/messages/0/content', 'array' not in 'string'..."}]}
```

## Example

When tools are enabled, the request payload contains:

```text
content: [{"type":"text","text":"Hello"}]
```

However, Cloudflare expects:

```text
content: "Hello"
```

## Additional Context

This issue occurs only when tool calling is enabled via `goai.WithTools()`.

Cloudflare appears to require its native message schema, while the request is being normalized into an OpenAI-style content format.

## Question

Is there a recommended approach to:

* preserve the original string content format when using the Cloudflare provider, or
* disable the automatic OpenAI-style content transformation for providers that require native message schemas?

I'd be happy to help test a fix or provide additional logs if needed.

Thanks again for the great library!

Round-trips provider-executed tool calls (Anthropic `web_search`, `code_execution`, `web_fetch`, `mcp`; OpenAI Responses `web_search_call`, `file_search_call`, `code_interpreter_call`, `image_generation_call`, `local_shell_call`, `mcp_call`, `computer_call`) so multi-turn conversations with these tools no longer drop the inline result.

Related to #59 (does **not** close — leaving open until end-to-end verified against direct Anthropic API on a regular API key; verification so far is mock-based for direct Anthropic + real-LLM for OpenAI Responses via Azure and Google Gemini).

## Bug class

- **Hard (Anthropic, HTTP 400)**: API requires `tool_use` paired with its `tool_result` in the same assistant turn. Dropping `web_search_tool_result` on parse produces an orphan `tool_use`; the next request is rejected with `tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after`.
- **Soft (OpenAI Responses, lost context)**: server tool items dropped → re-send loses search/grounding history. Not rejected, but the model loses memory across turns.

## Approach

- Capture server-tool payload in non-streaming (`parseResponse` / `parseResponsesResult`) and streaming (`parseSSE` / `parseResponsesStream`) paths via a side-channel raw parse + deferred `ChunkToolCall` emission.
- Attach to `ToolCall.Metadata` (`resultBlock` for Anthropic, `rawItem` + `providerExecuted` for OpenAI Responses). The metadata flows through `buildFinalAssistantMessages` / `appendToolRoundTrip` into `ResponseMessages` via `Part.ProviderOptions`.
- Re-emit verbatim when the assistant turn is serialized back to the API.
- Shared core (`isProviderExecuted`, `executeToolsParallel`, `buildToolMessages`, `ensureToolResultPairing`) skips unknown-tool synthesis and orphan `tool_result` injection for these calls — so mixing server + client tools no longer fabricates fake `tool_result` messages with the server tool's id.

## New: `bedrock.AnthropicChat`

Routes Anthropic models through Bedrock's InvokeModel / InvokeModelWithResponseStream (rather than Converse) so the anthropic provider's parsing applies on Bedrock. Wraps `anthropic.Chat` with a SigV4-signing transport, EventStream-to-SSE byte translator, body-shape adjustments (`anthropic_version`, strip `stream`/`model`), and a beta-flag filter for Bedrock's accepted set. Inherits the server-tool fix automatically.

Note: AWS Bedrock does not yet execute Anthropic server tools (`web_search_20250305` etc. — verified across Converse + InvokeModel and multiple model IDs/regions). Infrastructure is ready for when AWS adds support; in the meantime regular usage (text, custom tools, extended thinking, prompt caching) works.

## Provider audit

| Provider | Status |
|---|---|
| Anthropic direct | Fixed (parse + serialize, non-streaming + streaming) |
| Vertex AnthropicChat | Inherits via `anthropic.Chat` delegation |
| MiniMax | Inherits via `anthropic.Chat` delegation |
| Bedrock Anthropic | New `AnthropicChat` constructor; goai-side ready, AWS-side blocking server tools |
| OpenAI Responses | Fixed (parse + serialize, non-streaming + streaming) |
| Azure OpenAI | Inherits via `openai.Chat` delegation |
| Google Gemini | No fix needed — grounding via `groundingMetadata` → `Sources`, not a tool_call cycle |
| xAI / Groq / Cohere / Perplexity | No fix needed — search inline as text + sources |

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` (all packages green)
- [x] Anthropic non-streaming + streaming round-trip unit tests (mock SSE, exact wire format)
- [x] OpenAI Responses non-streaming + streaming round-trip unit tests
- [x] Bedrock AnthropicChat: URL builder, body transformer, EventStream→SSE translator, beta filter, full generate + stream round-trip (with server tool result block)
- [x] Convert-message round-trip tests for both providers (server_tool_use + result_block adjacency, web_search_call shape preservation)
- [x] Orphan-injection regression test (`ensureToolResultPairing` skips inline results)
- [x] User's exact reproduction code (StreamText + append ResponseMessages loop) verified against an Anthropic wire-format mock that asserts `server_tool_use → web_search_tool_result` adjacency on each re-send turn
- [x] Azure OpenAI Responses with `web_search` across 3 multi-turn rounds — `web_search_call` round-trip preserved, model retains search context
- [x] Google Gemini with `google_search` — multi-turn passes (no roundtrip needed structurally)
- [x] Bedrock AnthropicChat basic streaming + custom function tool — works end-to-end via SigV4 + EventStream translator

func toolsFromDef(def provider.ToolDefinition) []goai.Tool {

I thought response messages was supposed to automatically append tool result ids etc in message history

tool result not being returned in response messages.

## Summary

When an OpenRouter **server tool** (e.g. `openrouter:web_search`) is used, the agentic loop in `StreamText`/`GenerateText` **terminates after the first response instead of continuing**, returning an empty result — even though the tool ran and the model is mid-loop.

OpenRouter executes server tools upstream and, when the model wants to keep going, returns `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` with **`message.tool_calls: null`** (there is nothing for the *client* to execute — the tool already ran server-side). goai's loop looks for client-executable tool calls, finds none, and stops. The model's `reasoning` and the tool's results (`annotations`) are discarded and no final answer is ever produced.

## Version

`github.com/zendev-sh/goai v0.8.5` (latest).

## What goai sends (correct)

Verified with a logging `http.RoundTripper` wired via `openrouter.WithHTTPClient`:

```json
{"messages":[...],"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash","stream":true,
 "tools":[{"type":"openrouter:web_search"}],"usage":{"include":true}}
```

The provider-defined tool is serialized correctly.

## What OpenRouter returns (rich, but goai drops it)

```jsonc
"choices":[{
  "finish_reason":"tool_calls",
  "native_finish_reason":"tool_calls",
  "message":{
    "role":"assistant",
    "content":null,                 // no final answer YET — model is mid-loop
    "tool_calls":null,              // nothing for the CLIENT to run (server tool already executed)
    "reasoning":"...1245 chars of analysis, incl. the actual data...",
    "annotations":[ /* 20–40 url_citation objects, each with an 877-char `content` field of scraped page text */ ]
  }
}],
"usage":{"prompt_tokens":20208, ...}   // ~20k tokens of search results were injected
```

## What goai produces

| path | result |
|---|---|
| `StreamText` | **`steps=0`, empty text, empty reasoning** — entire turn discarded |
| `GenerateText` | `steps=1`, empty text |

goai makes **exactly one HTTP request** and never continues.

## Reliability

Same request, repeated: **~1/3** of the time OpenRouter completes the search inline and returns `finish_reason: "stop"` with the full cited answer — goai handles that correctly. **~2/3** of the time it returns `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` (as above) and goai bails with an empty result. Manually continuing (append the assistant turn, re-request) yields *another* `tool_calls` round, so it is a genuine **multi-round** server-tool loop that goai currently drives **zero** rounds of.

## Root cause (hypothesis)

The loop's continuation is gated on the presence of *client-executable* `tool_calls`. A server/provider-executed tool returns `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` with `tool_calls: null`, so the loop finds nothing to execute and exits.

## Suggested fix

When `finish_reason == "tool_calls"` (or a provider-defined/server tool is in the request) **and there are no client-executable tool calls**, continue the loop by re-requesting with the accumulated messages, up to `MaxSteps`, instead of terminating. That is exactly the continuation OpenRouter's server tools (`openrouter:web_search`, `openrouter:web_fetch`, …) expect.

## Related

- #111 — reasoning here arrives in `message.reasoning` (streamed as `delta.reasoning`), which the openaicompat parser also drops (reads only `reasoning_content`). So even the mid-loop reasoning above is lost independently of this loop bug.
- The `annotations[].content` payload (the actual tool results) is likewise not surfaced on `TextResult`.

## Repro

~30-line program: `openrouter.Chat("deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", WithHTTPClient(loggingClient))`, then `StreamText(..., WithTools(goai.Tool{Name:"web_search", ProviderDefinedType:"openrouter:web_search"}), WithMaxSteps(60))` with a query needing current data (e.g. "current weather in Singapore"). Drain `Stream()`, inspect `Result()` → `steps=0`, empty. The logging RoundTripper shows the single request + the `finish_reason:"tool_calls"` / `tool_calls:null` response.

## Summary
- New comment-triggered workflow that runs two AI reviewers (Go idiomatics, security) and posts a single synthesised summary comment back to the PR.
- Powered by [zenflow](https://github.com/zendev-sh/zenflow) v0.1.5 + FPT Smart Cloud Qwen3.6-27B (262K context).
- Files: `.zenflow/pr-review.yaml` (workflow spec), `.github/workflows/zenflow-review.yml` (GH Action), `.gitignore` (per-run artifacts).

## How to use
A repo OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR posts a comment containing `/zenflow-review` on the PR. The action acknowledges with an eyes reaction, runs the review, posts the result comment, and uploads the event stream as an artifact.

## What it checks
1. **Go idiomatics + repo standards**: errors.As vs type assertion, no input mutation, lock-free I/O, provider option conventions, compile-time interface checks, dependency minimality, ctx propagation, goroutine lifecycle.
2. **Security**: secret handling, log/error leak of API keys, TLS, SSRF on user-supplied URLs, HTTP timeouts, prompt injection in tool defs, race conditions.

Lead agent merges both into a markdown comment with severity-bucketed findings, drops duplicates, and tags each finding with the originating reviewer.

## Required org secret
- `FPT_API_KEY`: FPT Smart Cloud marketplace API key (JP region).

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is auto-provided by Actions and is sufficient for diff fetch + PR comment posting on same-repo PRs.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge this PR.
- [ ] Open a follow-up trivial PR and post `/zenflow-review`. Expect: eyes reaction, then a summary comment within ~3-5 min.
- [ ] Open a PR with a deliberate violation (e.g. type assertion instead of errors.As) and verify it gets flagged.

**Provider**:  google (Gemini via google.Chat)

**Go version**: v1.25.5

**GoAI version**: v0.5.8

**Description**
We are observing inconsistent tool re-execution behavior in multi-turn conversations when using WithMessages(...) along with WithTools() and WithMaxSteps().

In some cases, the model repeats previously executed tool actions from earlier turns, even when the current user input is unrelated. This behavior is intermittent — sometimes the flow works correctly, and sometimes prior tool steps are replayed.

A clear description of the bug.

**Code to reproduce**

```go
messages = append(messages, goai.UserMessage(userInput))

result, err := goai.GenerateText(
		ctx,
		model,
		goai.WithMessages(chatMessages...),
		goai.WithPrompt(userMessage),
		goai.WithMaxSteps(10),
		goai.WithTools(weatherTool),
		goai.WithToolChoice(goai.ToolChoiceAuto),
	)

messages = append(messages, goai.AssistantMessage(result.Text))
```
Example Scenario

Turn 1:
User: What is the weather condition of Mumbai, India?
→ Tool gives the weather

Turn 2:
User: Hi
→ Expected: simple greeting
→ Actual (intermittent): excetues weather tool in backend + greeting as response

**Expected behavior**

- Tool execution should be scoped to the current user intent
- Previously executed tool steps should not be repeated unless explicitly required

**Actual behavior**

- Prior tool actions are sometimes re-triggered in later turns
- Behavior is not deterministic (works correctly in some runs, repeats in others)

**Additional context**

- This occurs when passing full conversation history via WithMessages(...)
- Observed mainly with tool-heavy workflows
- No explicit errors returned — behavior issue at model/tool interaction level
- We will add detailed logs and reproducible traces shortly to help diagnose further

**Is there a recommended approach to:**

- isolate tool-heavy execution per turn, or
- prevent re-execution of previously completed tool steps in multi-turn flows?

* fix(anthropic,openai,bedrock,core): round-trip server-executed tool calls

Provider-executed tools (Anthropic web_search/code_execution/web_fetch/mcp,
OpenAI Responses web_search_call/file_search_call/code_interpreter_call/
image_generation_call/local_shell_call/mcp_call/computer_call) deliver their
result inline on the assistant turn. The providers previously dropped these
result blocks/items, so appending result.ResponseMessages to the conversation
produced an orphan tool_use that Anthropic rejected with HTTP 400 (and silently
lost OpenAI Responses search context across turns).

Changes:

- anthropic: capture web_search_tool_result and other server result blocks
  in DoGenerate (side-channel raw parse) and DoStream (defer ChunkToolCall
  emission until the matching result block is observed). Attach the raw
  payload to ToolCall.Metadata["resultBlock"] and re-emit verbatim alongside
  server_tool_use when the assistant turn is serialized back. Vertex
  AnthropicChat and MiniMax inherit automatically.

- openai/responses: capture server-executed item types into ToolCall.Metadata
  with providerExecuted + rawItem; the request serializer re-emits them
  verbatim instead of reshaping as function_call. Verified end-to-end on
  Azure OpenAI Responses with web_search across three multi-turn rounds.

- bedrock: new bedrock.AnthropicChat constructor that routes Anthropic
  models through Bedrock's InvokeModel / InvokeModelWithResponseStream
  endpoints (rather than Converse) so the anthropic provider's parsing
  applies. Includes SigV4 signing transport, EventStream-to-SSE translator,
  body shape adjustments (anthropic_version, strip stream/model fields),
  and a beta-flag filter for Bedrock's accepted set. Note: as of this
  writing AWS does not yet execute Anthropic server tools regardless of
  endpoint; the infrastructure is ready for when they do.

- generate: isProviderExecuted helper centralises the "skip server-executed
  tool calls" rule for executeToolsParallel and buildToolMessages, so a
  mixed client+server tool config does not synthesize spurious
  unknown-tool error tool_result messages for server tool ids.

- normalize: ensureToolResultPairing skips orphan-result injection for
  tool calls that already carry an inline resultBlock or rawItem.

Tests: full unit coverage for both parse and serialize paths on Anthropic,
OpenAI Responses, and Bedrock Anthropic (URL builder, body transformer,
EventStream-to-SSE, beta filter, server-tool round-trip non-streaming +
streaming). go test ./... passes.

References issue #59.

* test: cover new helpers and bedrock-anthropic transport branches

Lift diff coverage on the server-tool round-trip change to ≥90%:

- isProviderExecuted: 22.2% → 100% (table test for nil/empty/typed/
  resultBlock/rawItem branches).
- bedrock.AnthropicChat: bearer-auth path, HTTP-error surfacing,
  custom header passthrough.
- eventStreamSSEReader: exception frame branch + Close propagation.

* test: cover skip-server-tool branches in tool loop and orphan-pairing

Direct unit tests for the two shared-core branches that the prior
end-to-end mock tests covered indirectly:

- executeToolsParallel skips server-executed tool calls (no toolMap
  lookup, no ErrUnknownTool synthesis, no tool message emitted) while
  still executing concurrent client tools normally.
- ensureToolResultPairing skips orphan tool_result injection for tool
  calls carrying ProviderOptions["resultBlock"] (server-executed).

Plus extra branches in bedrock.AnthropicChat:

- Default base URL when WithBaseURL is omitted.
- Cross-region inference profile region override.
- base.RoundTrip error propagation.
- Body sent without anthropic_beta when no betas are present.

marks every 404 retryable to absorb OpenAI's transient model 404s. Hosts

fix(openai): read raw reasoning from Responses reasoning_text (#183)

* fix(openai): read raw reasoning from Responses reasoning_text

The Responses API carries reasoning either as summaries or as raw
reasoning_text content parts, streamed as response.reasoning_text.delta.
Only summaries were read, so providers that return the raw form lost
their reasoning: DeepSeek's Responses API streams its whole chain of
thought this way and generates no summaries.

Stream reasoning_text deltas as ChunkReasoning, keyed by the reasoning
item's canonical ID and content_index, and collect reasoning_text parts
when parsing a non-streaming result. Replay is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(openai): cover reasoning_text delta schema checks

Add response.reasoning_text.delta to the recognized-event schema table:
a mistyped field, and null item_id, content_index and delta.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(openai): cover cancellation while sending a reasoning_text delta

A reasoning_text delta that is waiting to be received when the caller
cancels is dropped, and the stream ends without delivering it.

Introduce `decodeResponsesEvent` to centralize and validate JSON

fix(openaicompat): let the caller decide max_completion_tokens

The max_tokens -> max_completion_tokens rename is keyed on the model id via
IsReasoningModel. That works when the id names the model, but Azure OpenAI puts
the user-chosen deployment name in the wire id: a GPT-5 deployment called
"prod-gpt5" fails the prefix check, gets max_tokens, and Azure rejects the
request with "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens'". The reverse also happens
for a non-reasoning deployment named after a reasoning model.

Add ChatModelConfig.UsesCompletionTokens (and the matching RequestConfig field)
so a provider that knows the answer can state it. Nil keeps the id heuristic, so
every existing provider behaves exactly as before. compat exposes it as
WithCompletionTokens.

hits.message:
fix(openai,cohere): forward ChunkToolCallDelta during tool-call streaming (#57)

The openai-responses and cohere streaming adapters buffered tool-call
argument fragments internally and only emitted ChunkToolCall once the
accumulated buffer parsed as JSON (or at done/end). Consumers wanting
progressive rendering of large tool inputs (e.g. write/edit content)
saw a long silence between ToolCallStreamStart and the final ToolCall.

Forward each upstream argument fragment as ChunkToolCallDelta while
keeping the existing buffer + final ChunkToolCall behavior intact, so
existing consumers are unaffected and new ones can render progress.

Aligns these two adapters with anthropic, bedrock-converse, and the
shared openaicompat codec, which already forward deltas. Closes #56.

hits.message:
fix(openai): emit a Responses tool call once, not per valid buffer

response.function_call_arguments.delta finalized the call as soon as the
accumulated buffer parsed as JSON, and then reset that buffer. This assumes
the delta that completes the object is the last one for the call. It usually
is, but nothing guarantees it: any delta that follows -- down to a trailing
newline -- stays in the buffer, and response.function_call_arguments.done
emits it as a second tool call carrying garbage arguments under the same call
id. A client that executes tool calls then runs the same call twice, the
second time with an unparseable payload.

Resolve the call on the explicit done signal instead, which is what the
Anthropic provider already does by waiting for content_block_stop rather than
validating mid-stream. response.output_item.done keeps a flush for the case
where the done event never arrives, so an item closed early still emits its
call instead of being dropped.

The added test drives a delta after the arguments already parse: it emitted
two calls before this change and one after, plus the cancellation path of the
flush. Package coverage 98.8%.

hits.message:
fix(openai): keep the boundary between reasoning summaries

Responses can return several summary segments under one reasoning item,
told apart by summary_index. The deltas of each segment carry no separator:
the boundary exists only in that index. Concatenating them therefore runs two
summaries together, and since each one tends to open with a bold title, the
seam produces "**A****B**" -- markdown that no longer renders as two spans.

The streaming path now prefixes a delta with a blank line when its
summary_index differs from the previous one on the same item, and the
non-streaming parser joins the summary entries the same way instead of
relying on each string to bring its own trailing whitespace.

Deltas that share a summary_index are still concatenated bare, which is the
common case: one summary arrives as many deltas. The reasoningId metadata
keeps carrying the index, so a consumer that prefers to split on it still can.

Reported in #125.

Tests cover the reported case, several deltas within one summary, a lone
summary, a second reasoning item starting clean, a first index that is not
zero, deltas with no reasoning item to track, and that reasoningId still
reports the index. Package coverage 98.8%.

feat(google): add CacheClient for explicit context caching

Gemini's cachedContents lets a caller upload a prefix once -- system
instruction plus tool declarations -- and reference it across turns, which is
where the savings are for an agent that resends the same tools every request.
The provider could reference an existing cache through the cachedContent
field, but there was no way to create or renew one, so the caller had to hand
roll the API and, with it, a second serializer for the prefix.

That second serializer is the real hazard: a cache only hits if the prefix is
byte-identical to what the request sends. CacheClient avoids it by reusing the
request path -- buildToolsAndConfig and buildSystemInstruction, extracted from
buildRequest -- so the cached prefix is produced by the same code that builds
a chat request. It also reuses the existing auth and routing, so caching works
against both the direct API and Vertex.

Supporting changes: goai.ToolDefinitions exposes the Tool to ToolDefinition
conversion that was already there but unexported, and the HTTP helpers become
free functions (doGoogleJSON, resolveOptions) so both the chat model and the
cache client share them instead of duplicating request plumbing.

Additive: a caller that never constructs a CacheClient sends exactly the same
requests as before. Tests cover create and renew against a mock server, the
prefix matching a chat request, Vertex routing, and the error paths. Package
coverage 96.5%.

feat(anthropic): configurable ephemeral cache TTL (5m/1h)

Anthropic's prompt caching accepts a `ttl` on the ephemeral cache_control
marker, selecting a 5-minute or 1-hour cache lifetime. The SDK always
emitted the bare marker, so callers were pinned to the 5m default and had
no way to opt into the 1h TTL, which is the better trade for long-lived
system prompts and agentic loops that outlive a 5-minute window.

Adds a `WithCacheTTL("5m"|"1h")` option, surfaced on the provider layer as
`GenerateParams.CacheTTL` (request-wide) and `Part.CacheControlTTL`
(per-breakpoint). Both the system block and message breakpoints honour it,
including the file/document parts added in #115, so uploaded documents
inherit the configured TTL.

The change is additive and backward compatible: an empty TTL emits exactly
the previous payload — `{"type":"ephemeral"}` with no `ttl` key — so the
provider default (5m) is preserved. The 1h TTL is GA and needs no beta
header, which the wire test asserts.

Tests cover the system block, part-level breakpoints, message-level
markers (which must not absorb a part TTL), the caching.go propagation,
the option-to-params plumbing, and an end-to-end mock-server check that
the TTL reaches the wire. Patch coverage 100%; package coverage unchanged
(root 97.6%, anthropic 98.0%).

feat: surface hook and predicate panics instead of swallowing them (#85)

* feat: surface hook and predicate panics instead of swallowing them

Lifecycle hooks and the StopWhen predicate previously ran inside a
recover that printed the panic to stderr and discarded it, so callers
could not intercept it and observability handlers never saw it.

Add an OnPanic observability hook (WithOnPanic, PanicInfo) that fires
for every panicking callback, and a PanicError type. Panics in the
propagate-fatal callbacks (OnRequest, OnResponse, OnStepFinish,
OnFinish, OnBeforeStep, StopWhen) are now surfaced as a *PanicError:
returned by GenerateText/GenerateObject, or via stream.Err() for
StreamText/StreamObject. The tool path (tool Execute, OnToolCallStart,
OnToolCall, OnBeforeToolExecute, OnAfterToolExecute) stays resilient,
converting panics to tool errors so a single bad tool does not abort
the agent loop, while still reporting them to OnPanic.

Closes #82

* fix: surface step-1 StreamText hook panics + document panic-value type checks

Address zenflow review findings on the streaming step-1 path: OnRequest
and OnResponse hooks fired synchronously before the consume goroutine
(single-step StreamText and streamWithToolLoop step 1) ran raw, so a
panic crashed the caller's goroutine instead of surfacing as a
*PanicError and was not reported to OnPanic. Wrap them in callHook and
add defer recoverToError to both entry points.

The recover-value type assertions (any -> *PanicError) are intentional,
not errors.As: they detect the exact sentinel we re-panic, not a wrapped
error chain. Documented inline.

* refactor: use errors.As for panic-value *PanicError detection

Replace the recover()-value type assertions with an asPanicError helper
backed by errors.As, per the repo's errors.As-over-type-assertion rule
(zenflow review). A non-error panic value (e.g. a string) yields nil and
is wrapped fresh.

* security: keep raw panic values out of error messages

Address zenflow security review: PanicError.Error() and the tool-path
panic errors no longer embed the raw panic value, so a panic carrying
sensitive data (tokens, captured args) is not leaked into logged error
strings or echoed to the model. The full value and stack remain on
PanicError.Value/Stack and PanicInfo for deliberate, sanitizable
observability access, now documented as potentially sensitive.

* security: recoverToError converts all panics to errors (no crash dump)

Make the synchronous entry-point recovery a catch-all consistent with
recoverToStreamErr: a non-*PanicError panic is wrapped as
*PanicError(phase="internal") and reported to OnPanic instead of being
re-raised as an uncaught panic, so a panic carrying sensitive data is not
printed to stderr as a crash dump. Threads o.OnPanic through the five
call sites.

  server_tool_use when the assistant turn is serialized back. Vertex
  AnthropicChat and MiniMax inherit automatically.

  with providerExecuted + rawItem; the request serializer re-emits them
  verbatim instead of reshaping as function_call. Verified end-to-end on
  Azure OpenAI Responses with web_search across three multi-turn rounds.

  models through Bedrock's InvokeModel / InvokeModelWithResponseStream
  endpoints (rather than Converse) so the anthropic provider's parsing
  applies. Includes SigV4 signing transport, EventStream-to-SSE translator,

fix(anthropic): derive model capabilities from version, not literal lists (#164)

* fix(anthropic): derive model capabilities from version, not literal lists

`supportsThinking` and `supportsNativeOutputFormat` each matched a
hardcoded list of model-id substrings. Both lists have gone stale, so
current models are reported as lacking capabilities they have:

    model                      thinking  nativeOutputFormat
    claude-opus-4-7            true      false
    claude-opus-4-8            true      false
    claude-haiku-4-5           false     false
    claude-opus-5              false     false
    claude-sonnet-5            false     false
    claude-fable-5             false     false

`supportsThinking` feeds `Capabilities().Reasoning`, so callers that gate
on reported capabilities skip thinking on models that support it.

`supportsNativeOutputFormat` decides `structuredOutputMode: "auto"`. When
it returns false, "auto" falls back to the tool-trick path, which sets
`tool_choice` to force the synthetic `json_response` tool. The Messages
API rejects a forced `tool_choice` when thinking is enabled ("Thinking
may not be enabled when tool_choice forces tool use"), and thinking is on
by default on claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, and claude-fable-5. So on
"auto", structured output combined with thinking is broken on every model
shipped since 4.6.

Replace both literal lists with a shared `anthropicModelVersion` helper
that parses the major/minor generation out of the id, and express each
capability as a version range: thinking is Claude 4 and later (plus
legacy claude-3-7-sonnet), native structured output is 4.1 and later.

Two details the helper has to get right, both covered by tests:

  - The pattern is unanchored. Bedrock reuses this provider through
    bedrock.AnthropicChat with a prefixed id ("anthropic.claude-opus-5",
    "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"), and Vertex appends an "@date"
    suffix. Anchoring at the start would regress those.
  - A trailing numeric run is a minor version only when it is one or two
    digits. "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" is the 4.0 release with a release
    date, not minor 20250514, and 4.0 predates structured output.

Legacy family-last ids ("claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022") carry no parseable
version and are reported unversioned, preserving today's behaviour.

Sanitise schemas on the native path
===================================

Widening `supportsNativeOutputFormat` alone would trade one breakage for
another, because native `output_config.format` is not a superset of the
tool trick. Its validator rejects JSON Schema keywords the tool trick
tolerates, since a tool's `input_schema` is advisory without
`strict:true`:

    output_config.format.schema: For 'number' type, properties maximum,
    minimum are not supported

Without this half, a caller on "auto" with a constrained schema would
regress: claude-opus-4-8 with thinking omitted currently works on the
tool trick and would start failing on native. Hence one commit, not two.

`injectNativeOutputFormat` now strips the unsupported keywords (numeric
constraints, string-length constraints, and the complex array
constraints) recursively before the schema reaches the wire. Supported
constructs — basic types, enum/const, anyOf/allOf, $ref/$defs, string
formats, additionalProperties:false — are left untouched, and callers
who stay on the tool trick keep full validation. Follows the
non-mutating, fresh-allocation contract of the sibling sanitiser in
internal/gemini; kept unexported in provider/anthropic because, unlike
the Gemini one, only this package needs it (Bedrock and Vertex reach it
through anthropic.Chat).

Tests
=====

Table-driven coverage for the version parser (including the
Bedrock/Vertex id shapes and the date-vs-minor distinction) and for both
predicates, with the previously-matched ids kept as regression cases.
For the sanitiser: keyword removal at every depth including inside
anyOf and array items, survival of every supported construct,
non-mutation of the input, and a buildRequest-level assertion that a
constrained schema reaches output_config.format usable rather than
rejected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(anthropic): address review on capability detection and schema transform

- Use an explicit documented model compatibility list for native structured
  output instead of a version threshold (Opus 4.1 is not supported; the
  non-versioned claude-mythos-preview is). Add WithNativeOutputFormatSupport
  so platform adapters select their own documented set: Bedrock uses the
  narrower subset, MiniMax opts out, Vertex/Azure keep the direct set.
- Handle claude-mythos-preview as a thinking-capable alias.
- Replace the global keyword-denylist sanitizer with a type-aware schema
  transform mirroring Anthropic's documented SDK behavior: preserve
  minItems 0/1, filter unsupported string formats, convert oneOf to anyOf,
  add additionalProperties:false on objects, and record unsupported
  constraints in the description instead of silently dropping them.
- Surface an error for an invalid response-format schema instead of silently
  falling back to the tool trick.

The max_tokens -> max_completion_tokens rename is keyed on the model id via
IsReasoningModel. That works when the id names the model, but Azure OpenAI puts
the user-chosen deployment name in the wire id: a GPT-5 deployment called
"prod-gpt5" fails the prefix check, gets max_tokens, and Azure rejects the
request with "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens'". The reverse also happens
for a non-reasoning deployment named after a reasoning model.

Add ChatModelConfig.UsesCompletionTokens (and the matching RequestConfig field)
so a provider that knows the answer can state it. Nil keeps the id heuristic, so
every existing provider behaves exactly as before. compat exposes it as
WithCompletionTokens.

hits.message:
fix(anthropic): stream long-running DoGenerate requests (#165)

* fix(anthropic): stream long-running DoGenerate requests

A non-streaming Messages call holds an HTTP response open with no bytes
flowing until the model has finished everything it intends to do. For a
request that thinks for minutes that invites idle-timeout enforcement,
from the client and from any proxy or load balancer in between —
Anthropic's own guidance is to stream long-running requests for exactly
this reason.

The combination that makes this acute is native structured output plus
tools plus a thinking model. GenerateObject is the only structured-output
entry point that runs a tool loop (StreamObject is single-step by
design), and it drives every step through DoGenerate, so that
combination was reachable only over the non-streaming transport. Observed
as a thinking model investigating for twenty minutes across twenty tool
calls and then never delivering a response, the request dying on a
stalled POST rather than any API error.

DoGenerate now issues stream:true and reassembles the events into the
Message document they describe, when the request is expected to think:
a "thinking" or "effort" provider option, or a model from the 5.x
generation, which thinks with no thinking parameter sent at all. Opus
4.7/4.8 support adaptive thinking only on request, so they qualify via
the option. Callers can force the decision either way with
ProviderOptions["streamingTransport"].

Reassembling the wire document rather than mapping events onto
provider.GenerateResult directly is deliberate. parseResponse is the one
place that knows how to interpret a Message, and it reads several things
provider.StreamChunk has no field for: thinking-block signatures, which
must be replayed verbatim on the next turn, redacted_thinking payloads,
server tool result blocks, citations, and container / context_management
metadata. Going through the document keeps the two transports identical
in everything but transport; mapping events would fork that logic and
silently drop whatever a chunk cannot carry. An "error" event is handed
to parseResponse unchanged so error classification also stays in one
place.

doHTTP already derives streaming from body["stream"], so Bedrock's and
Vertex's URL builders pick the streaming endpoint without further
change.

Tests assert the property that matters: the same Message delivered as an
event stream and as a single response parses to identical results, across
text, thinking-with-signature, fragmented tool input, redacted_thinking,
and usage iterations with context_management. Plus end-to-end coverage
that a thinking model's DoGenerate requests stream:true and still
surfaces the thinking signature, that a non-thinking model stays
non-streaming, that streamingTransport never reaches the wire, and that
truncated, malformed and unparseable-tool-input streams degrade rather
than fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(anthropic): harden streamed DoGenerate transport per review

- Strict SSE lifecycle in accumulateStreamedMessage: require message_start and
  message_stop, track open content blocks, and return a protocol error on
  premature EOF, malformed frames, duplicate starts, or deltas/stops for
  unopened blocks. A truncated stream is no longer reported as a successful
  generation.
- Consume complete SSE events (NextEvent) so Bedrock's event:error with AWS
  exception payloads is surfaced as an error instead of becoming partial
  success.
- Validate and bound content block indexes (reject negative, fractional,
  overflowing, or over-limit values) so a hostile index cannot force
  unbounded allocation.
- Make auto-streaming provider-aware: add WithAutoStreaming, enabled by
  default for the direct API, disabled for Bedrock whose
  InvokeModelWithResponseStream needs a different IAM permission.
- Reject non-boolean streamingTransport values instead of silently ignoring
  them.
- Add parity tests for citations and server tool use + result blocks.

---------

fix(bedrock): sign SigV4 over the URI-encoded path, not the raw wire path

AWS SigV4 requires the canonical URI to be the RFC 3986 URI-encoded
absolute path. Go leaves reserved chars such as ':' unescaped in
url.URL.EscapedPath() for model IDs like 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0',
so signing that raw path produces a signature AWS rejects (broken since
#168 switched to EscapedPath()).

Restore uriEncodePath(req.URL.Path), which yields the canonical '%3A0'
AWS computes from the received path. Rewrite TestSigV4_SignsWirePath so
it no longer recomputes the signature from the same buggy function
(tautology): it now asserts the shipped signature matches the encoded
canonical URI and does NOT match the raw wire path.

fix(anthropic): replay thinking blocks in place around tool_use (#178)

Claude 5.x models (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1) return a progress-update thinking
block right before each tool_use, so thinking blocks interleave with text
and tool_use in one turn. The API requires them back in order within a
tool-use turn and binds each block to everything before it. parseResponse
now builds ordered Content, but two paths still reorder the turn:

- parseSSE sets no ChunkFinish.Content, so streamed turns fall back to the
  aggregate fields and appendToolRoundTrip hoists all reasoning to the front.
  An orderedContent helper keyed by stream block ID now rebuilds it.
- convertMessages' ReorderAssistantParts moves every tool_use to the end of
  the turn, past the thinking blocks that follow it. Assistant turns carrying
  signed or redacted thinking now keep their original interleaving; other
  turns are reordered as before.

TestOrderedThinkingReplay now expects the turn back exactly as produced, on
every transport, including streaming.

hits.message:
fix(anthropic): mark streamed reasoning chunks with their content block

Claude models can return several consecutive thinking blocks in one turn,
each with its own signature and often with empty text (display "omitted").
DoStream's reasoning chunks carried no block boundary, and a chunk that has
only a signature does not trigger the accumulator's split rule, so
[thinking "" sigA, thinking "" sigB] was replayed as one block with sigB, a
partly dropped sequence the API rejects. Redacted thinking followed by
thinking text merged the same way.

Every ChunkReasoning from parseSSE (thinking_delta, signature_delta,
redacted_thinking) now carries Metadata["blockId"], the stream block index.
reasoningBoundaryKey already recognizes that key, so the accumulator and
raw-stream consumers split at real block boundaries.

hits.message:
fix(gemini): rewrite schema "const" to a single-value "enum"

Gemini's function_declarations validator rejects "const", so it was dropped
along with the other unsupported keywords. Dropping it also drops the
constraint: a schema that pinned a field to one value now accepts anything of
that type, and the model is free to fill it in wrongly.

"const" has an exact equivalent Gemini does accept -- an "enum" with a single
member -- so rewrite it instead of deleting it. An existing "enum" wins, and a
const without a type gets "string", which Gemini requires alongside an enum.

This shows up with MCP tool schemas and discriminated unions, where a const
tag is what tells the model which variant it is filling in.

hits.message:
feat(google): add WithVertex for native Vertex AI endpoints

The Google provider only talks to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with an
API key. The same Gemini models are also served through Vertex AI, which many
users are required to use -- it is where GCP billing, IAM, VPC controls and
data residency apply -- and there was no way to reach it.

WithVertex(project, location) switches the request URL to
aiplatform.googleapis.com and authenticates with a Bearer token instead of the
x-goog-api-key header. Everything else is reused as is: the same wire format,
SSE parsing, thinking and grounding paths, since Vertex serves the same native
Gemini API.

The URL construction is centralized in endpointURL, which also handles the
"global" location, whose hostname has no region prefix. project and location
are validated before they reach the URL: they come from the caller and are
interpolated into a hostname and path, so a malformed value would otherwise
redirect the request elsewhere.

Additive: without WithVertex the provider behaves exactly as before, down to
the same URLs and the same header.

Tests cover the endpoint construction, the "global" special case, the
validation guard, and that Vertex mode authenticates with Bearer instead of
the API key header. Package coverage 98.1%.

hits.message:
feat: surface hook and predicate panics instead of swallowing them (#85)

* feat: surface hook and predicate panics instead of swallowing them

Lifecycle hooks and the StopWhen predicate previously ran inside a
recover that printed the panic to stderr and discarded it, so callers
could not intercept it and observability handlers never saw it.

Add an OnPanic observability hook (WithOnPanic, PanicInfo) that fires
for every panicking callback, and a PanicError type. Panics in the
propagate-fatal callbacks (OnRequest, OnResponse, OnStepFinish,
OnFinish, OnBeforeStep, StopWhen) are now surfaced as a *PanicError:
returned by GenerateText/GenerateObject, or via stream.Err() for
StreamText/StreamObject. The tool path (tool Execute, OnToolCallStart,
OnToolCall, OnBeforeToolExecute, OnAfterToolExecute) stays resilient,
converting panics to tool errors so a single bad tool does not abort
the agent loop, while still reporting them to OnPanic.

Closes #82

* fix: surface step-1 StreamText hook panics + document panic-value type checks

Address zenflow review findings on the streaming step-1 path: OnRequest
and OnResponse hooks fired synchronously before the consume goroutine
(single-step StreamText and streamWithToolLoop step 1) ran raw, so a
panic crashed the caller's goroutine instead of surfacing as a
*PanicError and was not reported to OnPanic. Wrap them in callHook and
add defer recoverToError to both entry points.

The recover-value type assertions (any -> *PanicError) are intentional,
not errors.As: they detect the exact sentinel we re-panic, not a wrapped
error chain. Documented inline.

* refactor: use errors.As for panic-value *PanicError detection

Replace the recover()-value type assertions with an asPanicError helper
backed by errors.As, per the repo's errors.As-over-type-assertion rule
(zenflow review). A non-error panic value (e.g. a string) yields nil and
is wrapped fresh.

* security: keep raw panic values out of error messages

Address zenflow security review: PanicError.Error() and the tool-path
panic errors no longer embed the raw panic value, so a panic carrying
sensitive data (tokens, captured args) is not leaked into logged error
strings or echoed to the model. The full value and stack remain on
PanicError.Value/Stack and PanicInfo for deliberate, sanitizable
observability access, now documented as potentially sensitive.

* security: recoverToError converts all panics to errors (no crash dump)

Make the synchronous entry-point recovery a catch-all consistent with
recoverToStreamErr: a non-*PanicError panic is wrapped as
*PanicError(phase="internal") and reported to OnPanic instead of being
re-raised as an uncaught panic, so a panic carrying sensitive data is not
printed to stderr as a crash dump. Threads o.OnPanic through the five
call sites.

hits.message:
feat(anthropic): configurable ephemeral cache TTL (5m/1h)

Anthropic's prompt caching accepts a `ttl` on the ephemeral cache_control
marker, selecting a 5-minute or 1-hour cache lifetime. The SDK always
emitted the bare marker, so callers were pinned to the 5m default and had
no way to opt into the 1h TTL, which is the better trade for long-lived
system prompts and agentic loops that outlive a 5-minute window.

Adds a `WithCacheTTL("5m"|"1h")` option, surfaced on the provider layer as
`GenerateParams.CacheTTL` (request-wide) and `Part.CacheControlTTL`
(per-breakpoint). Both the system block and message breakpoints honour it,
including the file/document parts added in #115, so uploaded documents
inherit the configured TTL.

The change is additive and backward compatible: an empty TTL emits exactly
the previous payload — `{"type":"ephemeral"}` with no `ttl` key — so the
provider default (5m) is preserved. The 1h TTL is GA and needs no beta
header, which the wire test asserts.

Tests cover the system block, part-level breakpoints, message-level
markers (which must not absorb a part TTL), the caching.go propagation,
the option-to-params plumbing, and an end-to-end mock-server check that
the TTL reaches the wire. Patch coverage 100%; package coverage unchanged
(root 97.6%, anthropic 98.0%).

fix(google): count output tokens as candidatesTokenCount

The Gemini API reports thinking separately in thoughtsTokenCount, and
totalTokenCount is prompt + candidates + thoughts. Subtracting thoughts from
candidatesTokenCount double-counts them: once thoughts outgrow the answer the
subtraction goes negative and OutputTokens clamps to 0, so a reasoning-heavy
turn reports no output at all.

Output now maps to candidatesTokenCount directly. ReasoningTokens already
carries thoughtsTokenCount, so nothing is lost.

### [`v0.99.2`](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/HEAD/packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md#0992---2026-09-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/v0.99.1...v0.99.2)

##### New Features

- MCP servers stay out of the way: servers with the default `codemode` exposure are no longer listed in the `codemode` description and no longer block the first prompt. They appear in a short system prompt section, and scripts find their tools with `searchTools()` and `describeNamespace()`. See [Control tool exposure](docs/mcp.md#control-tool-exposure).
- More MCP authentication options: `oauth.clientName` for servers that only accept known OAuth clients, and `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` to authenticate HTTP servers with a provider's `/login` token. See [Authenticate with OAuth](docs/mcp.md#authenticate-with-oauth).
- Anthropic workload identity federation from the Anthropic SDK environment variables. See [Use an API key from the environment](docs/providers.md#use-an-api-key-from-the-environment).
- `/reload` enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. See [Tools](docs/settings.md#tools).

##### Added

- Added a `description` field for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --description`), shown with the server in the system prompt and used to rank its tools in tool search, and a `describeNamespace(name)` codemode helper that returns a namespace's instructions and tool names. `describeNamespace()` and `searchTools()` accept a namespace as `mcp__dev-radius`, `mcp__dev_radius`, `dev-radius`, or `dev_radius`.
- Added an `oauth.clientName` setting for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --oauth-client-name`) to change the client name sent during OAuth client registration, for servers that only accept known clients ([#​10226](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10226)).
- Added `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` for HTTP MCP servers to send a provider's current `/login` token as the bearer token instead of using MCP OAuth. The token is read on every request, so provider refreshes apply. Only allowed in the global `mcp.json` and from extensions, and requires https except on loopback hosts.
- Added Anthropic workload identity federation from the `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variables (see [Providers](docs/providers.md)) ([#​10177](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10177), [#​10242](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10242) by [@​philfreo](https://redirect.github.com/philfreo)).
- `/reload` now enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. Tools removed from it stay enabled, tools turned off during the session stay off unless newly added, and `--tools`, `--no-tools`, and `--no-builtin-tools` still override the setting ([#​10245](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10245)).

##### Changed

- MCP servers with the default `codemode` exposure no longer appear in the `codemode` description; scripts find them with `searchTools()`. `codemode-deferred` is now an alias for `codemode`. Use `direct` exposure for tools the model should see without searching ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The `codemode` description no longer includes deferred tools, tool counts, or MCP server instructions, so it no longer changes when MCP servers connect or change their tools. The `tool_search` description no longer lists the servers whose tools it can load, for the same reason. Servers are listed instead in an `mcp_servers` system prompt section with a one-line summary, updated at the start of each prompt; a changed section is appended to the conversation. Scripts read server instructions with `describeNamespace()` ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The first prompt no longer waits for MCP servers without `direct` tools. They connect in the background and are waited for when a codemode script names them, a script searches tools, or `tool_search` runs ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).

##### Fixed

- Fixed new sessions intermittently ignoring the saved default model, or warning that no models are available, when it belongs to an extension-registered native provider with a stored credential ([#​9962](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9962), [#​10190](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10190) by [@​davidbrai](https://redirect.github.com/davidbrai)).
- Fixed the `/mcp` sign-in URL not being clickable when it wraps across lines, by emitting it as a terminal hyperlink with a `Cmd/Ctrl+click to open` line like `/login` ([#​10186](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10186)).
- Fixed codemode `image()` accepting malformed base64 data or unsupported image types, which persisted an invalid image block that made every later provider request fail with HTTP 400 ([#​10215](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10215)).
- Fixed codemode failing to start its script worker from the standalone Windows executable ([#​10204](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10204)).
- Fixed prompt submission slowing down with session length, because resolving the session's model selection looked up the model catalog once per assistant message ([#​10198](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10198)).
- Fixed model lookups slowing down for providers with a refreshed pi.dev catalog, because merging remote catalog models took quadratic time.
- Fixed the `built-in-tool-renderer.ts` and `minimal-mode.ts` extension examples removing the built-in tools' summaries and guidelines from the system prompt ([#​10072](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10072), [#​10193](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10193) by [@​christianklotz](https://redirect.github.com/christianklotz)).
- Fixed context overflow detection for Z.AI CN endpoint `Prompt exceeds max length` errors ([#​10208](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10208)).
- Fixed Anthropic requests failing when a tool schema uses keywords Anthropic strict tool use rejects, such as `minimum`/`maximum`; such tools are now sent non-strict ([#​9953](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9953)).
- Fixed provider retries firing immediately when a `Retry-After` header contains an unparseable date; they now use exponential backoff ([#​9571](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9571)).
- Fixed extension commands registered without a string name or handler crashing pi when typing `/`; the extension now fails to load with an error instead ([#​10054](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10054)).
- Fixed collapsed `codemode` and MCP tool results filling the screen when the output is one long line, such as minified JSON. Like bash output, the preview is now limited to wrapped line
