Composer dev versions come in two flavors: `dev-*` prefix (`dev-master`, `dev-main`) and `*-dev` suffix (`v12.x-dev`, `1.x-dev`). `findLatestVersion` only filtered the prefix form.

A package like `laravel/framework` with versions `["v12.x-dev", "v11.5.1", "v11.5.0"]` would pick `v12.x-dev` as latest because `parseInt("12")` sorts above `parseInt("11")` and the suffix variant passed the filter. `fetchPackage` then returns a dev branch as `latestVersion`.

One-line fix in the filter, two test cases covering both the mixed scenario and the all-dev fallback path.

hits.body:
The `Retry-After` handler in `Client.getJSON` runs `Number.parseInt` on the raw header value. Numeric strings like `"120"` work fine, but RFC 7231 also allows HTTP-date values (`"Wed, 21 Oct 2025 07:28:00 GMT"`), and parseInt returns NaN for those. That NaN ends up in `RateLimitError.retryAfter`, which breaks the error message and any consumer code that reads the field.

Extracted a `parseRetryAfter()` function that tries numeric first, then `Date.parse` for HTTP-date, and falls back to 60s when neither works. The registries regxa targets all use numeric values today, but the NaN fallthrough was still a bug waiting to happen.

Addresses item 3 from #18.

hits.body:
Concurrent cache misses for the same key each ran their own upstream `fetcher()` call. With `Promise.all` on a cold cache, upstream requests scaled linearly with caller count instead of one fetch plus shared await.

Added a per-key in-flight `Map` to `CachedRegistry.cached()` so the first caller fetches and subsequent callers await the same promise. The map entry is cleaned up in a `finally` block, so the next call after completion fetches fresh if needed. Errors propagate to all waiters.

Closes #29

## Test plan
- [x] 3 new tests covering coalescing, post-flight re-fetch, and error propagation
- [x] All 346 tests passing

## Summary

Two agent skills following the [agentskills.io spec](https://github.com/mgechev/skills-best-practices) for [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/):

- **regxa** - teaches agents how to query package registries using regxa's CLI and library API. Covers all 6 ecosystems, PURL format, caching, helpers.
- **regxa-ai-tool** - teaches agents how to integrate regxa's `packageTool` into Vercel AI SDK applications. Covers all 5 operations (package, versions, dependencies, maintainers, bulk).

Both skills use progressive disclosure - lean SKILL.md files with JiT-loaded references for detailed type contracts, PURL encoding rules, and common mistakes.

## Test plan

- [x] Skill directory names match frontmatter `name` fields
- [x] SKILL.md files under 500 lines (main skill: ~120, ai-tool: ~100)
- [x] References are flat (one level deep)
- [x] Instructions use third-person imperative
- [x] No human-centric files (README, CHANGELOG)

### [`v0.99.2`](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/HEAD/packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md#0992---2026-09-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/v0.99.1...v0.99.2)

##### New Features

- MCP servers stay out of the way: servers with the default `codemode` exposure are no longer listed in the `codemode` description and no longer block the first prompt. They appear in a short system prompt section, and scripts find their tools with `searchTools()` and `describeNamespace()`. See [Control tool exposure](docs/mcp.md#control-tool-exposure).
- More MCP authentication options: `oauth.clientName` for servers that only accept known OAuth clients, and `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` to authenticate HTTP servers with a provider's `/login` token. See [Authenticate with OAuth](docs/mcp.md#authenticate-with-oauth).
- Anthropic workload identity federation from the Anthropic SDK environment variables. See [Use an API key from the environment](docs/providers.md#use-an-api-key-from-the-environment).
- `/reload` enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. See [Tools](docs/settings.md#tools).

##### Added

- Added a `description` field for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --description`), shown with the server in the system prompt and used to rank its tools in tool search, and a `describeNamespace(name)` codemode helper that returns a namespace's instructions and tool names. `describeNamespace()` and `searchTools()` accept a namespace as `mcp__dev-radius`, `mcp__dev_radius`, `dev-radius`, or `dev_radius`.
- Added an `oauth.clientName` setting for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --oauth-client-name`) to change the client name sent during OAuth client registration, for servers that only accept known clients ([#​10226](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10226)).
- Added `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` for HTTP MCP servers to send a provider's current `/login` token as the bearer token instead of using MCP OAuth. The token is read on every request, so provider refreshes apply. Only allowed in the global `mcp.json` and from extensions, and requires https except on loopback hosts.
- Added Anthropic workload identity federation from the `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variables (see [Providers](docs/providers.md)) ([#​10177](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10177), [#​10242](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10242) by [@​philfreo](https://redirect.github.com/philfreo)).
- `/reload` now enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. Tools removed from it stay enabled, tools turned off during the session stay off unless newly added, and `--tools`, `--no-tools`, and `--no-builtin-tools` still override the setting ([#​10245](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10245)).

##### Changed

- MCP servers with the default `codemode` exposure no longer appear in the `codemode` description; scripts find them with `searchTools()`. `codemode-deferred` is now an alias for `codemode`. Use `direct` exposure for tools the model should see without searching ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The `codemode` description no longer includes deferred tools, tool counts, or MCP server instructions, so it no longer changes when MCP servers connect or change their tools. The `tool_search` description no longer lists the servers whose tools it can load, for the same reason. Servers are listed instead in an `mcp_servers` system prompt section with a one-line summary, updated at the start of each prompt; a changed section is appended to the conversation. Scripts read server instructions with `describeNamespace()` ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The first prompt no longer waits for MCP servers without `direct` tools. They connect in the background and are waited for when a codemode script names them, a script searches tools, or `tool_search` runs ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).

##### Fixed

- Fixed new sessions intermittently ignoring the saved default model, or warning that no models are available, when it belongs to an extension-registered native provider with a stored credential ([#​9962](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9962), [#​10190](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10190) by [@​davidbrai](https://redirect.github.com/davidbrai)).
- Fixed the `/mcp` sign-in URL not being clickable when it wraps across lines, by emitting it as a terminal hyperlink with a `Cmd/Ctrl+click to open` line like `/login` ([#​10186](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10186)).
- Fixed codemode `image()` accepting malformed base64 data or unsupported image types, which persisted an invalid image block that made every later provider request fail with HTTP 400 ([#​10215](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10215)).
- Fixed codemode failing to start its script worker from the standalone Windows executable ([#​10204](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10204)).
- Fixed prompt submission slowing down with session length, because resolving the session's model selection looked up the model catalog once per assistant message ([#​10198](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10198)).
- Fixed model lookups slowing down for providers with a refreshed pi.dev catalog, because merging remote catalog models took quadratic time.
- Fixed the `built-in-tool-renderer.ts` and `minimal-mode.ts` extension examples removing the built-in tools' summaries and guidelines from the system prompt ([#​10072](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10072), [#​10193](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10193) by [@​christianklotz](https://redirect.github.com/christianklotz)).
- Fixed context overflow detection for Z.AI CN endpoint `Prompt exceeds max length` errors ([#​10208](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10208)).
- Fixed Anthropic requests failing when a tool schema uses keywords Anthropic strict tool use rejects, such as `minimum`/`maximum`; such tools are now sent non-strict ([#​9953](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9953)).
- Fixed provider retries firing immediately when a `Retry-After` header contains an unparseable date; they now use exponential backoff ([#​9571](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9571)).
- Fixed extension commands registered without a string name or handler crashing pi when typing `/`; the extension now fails to load with an error instead ([#​10054](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10054)).
- Fixed collapsed `codemode` and MCP tool results filling the screen when the output is one long line, such as minified JSON. Like bash output, the preview is now limited to wrapped line

##### New Features

- **Terminal capability overrides** — Override detected terminal hyperlink, image, and truecolor support. See [Capability Overrides](docs/terminal-setup.md#capability-overrides).
- **Extension UI prompt events** — Integrations can distinguish active agent work from time spent waiting for `ctx.ui` prompts. See [Extension UI prompt events](docs/extensions.md#ui_prompt_start--ui_prompt_end).
- **RPC queue clearing** — Retrieve and clear queued steering and follow-up messages with `clear_queue`. See [RPC `clear_queue`](docs/rpc.md#clear_queue).
- **Fullscreen selection copy controls** — Disable automatic selection copying in fullscreen mode and use Ctrl+X to copy the active selection. See [UI & Display](docs/settings.md#ui--display).
- **DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision (experimental)** — Use the vision-capable model through the built-in DeepSeek provider. See [API Keys](docs/providers.md#api-keys).

##### Added

- Added `supportsMidConvoEffort` to custom Anthropic Messages model compatibility settings.
- Added transcript notices for Anthropic thinking blocks dropped during provider recovery when cache miss notices are enabled.
- Added `ui_prompt_start` and `ui_prompt_end` extension events so host integrations can distinguish active agent work from waiting on user-facing `ctx.ui` prompts ([#​8355](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8355) by [@​cristinaponcela](https://redirect.github.com/cristinaponcela)).
- Added `detectSupportedImageMimeTypeFromFile()` to the public library exports ([#​8600](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8600) by [@​xl0](https://redirect.github.com/xl0)).
- Added inherited experimental vision-capable `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` model support.
- Added transcript usage notices for compaction and branch summaries when cache miss notices are enabled.
- Added RPC `clear_queue` to retrieve and remove queued steering and follow-up messages ([#​8432](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8432)).
- Added environment variables and advanced settings for overriding auto-detected terminal hyperlink, image, and truecolor capabilities ([#​8665](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8665)).
- Added `fullscreenCopyOnSelect` to disable automatic fullscreen selection copy; when disabled, `Ctrl+X` copies the active text selection before falling back to the last assistant message, while `/tree` still copies the selected message ([#​7720](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7720)).

##### Changed

- Changed fullscreen scrollbars to reveal on pointer entry, support optional `scrollbarTrack` and `scrollbarThumb` theme colors with muted and text fallbacks, keep one thumb color across normal and expanded states, and support track-click jumping.
- Changed fullscreen transcript search arrows to underline on hover and capitalized the search placeholder.
- Changed selectors in `/thinking`, `/model`, `/scoped-models`, `/trust`, per-model thinking settings, and theme settings to keep active options marked while browsing. `/scoped-models` now uses consistent per-item toggles and strikes through unavailable models ([#​8900](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8900)).

The `Retry-After` handler in `Client.getJSON` runs `Number.parseInt` on the raw header value. Numeric strings like `"120"` work fine, but RFC 7231 also allows HTTP-date values (`"Wed, 21 Oct 2025 07:28:00 GMT"`), and parseInt returns NaN for those. That NaN ends up in `RateLimitError.retryAfter`, which breaks the error message and any consumer code that reads the field.

Extracted a `parseRetryAfter()` function that tries numeric first, then `Date.parse` for HTTP-date, and falls back to 60s when neither works. The registries regxa targets all use numeric values today, but the NaN fallthrough was still a bug waiting to happen.

Addresses item 3 from #18.

### [`v0.99.2`](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/HEAD/packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md#0992---2026-09-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/v0.99.1...v0.99.2)

##### New Features

- MCP servers stay out of the way: servers with the default `codemode` exposure are no longer listed in the `codemode` description and no longer block the first prompt. They appear in a short system prompt section, and scripts find their tools with `searchTools()` and `describeNamespace()`. See [Control tool exposure](docs/mcp.md#control-tool-exposure).
- More MCP authentication options: `oauth.clientName` for servers that only accept known OAuth clients, and `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` to authenticate HTTP servers with a provider's `/login` token. See [Authenticate with OAuth](docs/mcp.md#authenticate-with-oauth).
- Anthropic workload identity federation from the Anthropic SDK environment variables. See [Use an API key from the environment](docs/providers.md#use-an-api-key-from-the-environment).
- `/reload` enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. See [Tools](docs/settings.md#tools).

##### Added

- Added a `description` field for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --description`), shown with the server in the system prompt and used to rank its tools in tool search, and a `describeNamespace(name)` codemode helper that returns a namespace's instructions and tool names. `describeNamespace()` and `searchTools()` accept a namespace as `mcp__dev-radius`, `mcp__dev_radius`, `dev-radius`, or `dev_radius`.
- Added an `oauth.clientName` setting for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --oauth-client-name`) to change the client name sent during OAuth client registration, for servers that only accept known clients ([#​10226](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10226)).
- Added `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` for HTTP MCP servers to send a provider's current `/login` token as the bearer token instead of using MCP OAuth. The token is read on every request, so provider refreshes apply. Only allowed in the global `mcp.json` and from extensions, and requires https except on loopback hosts.
- Added Anthropic workload identity federation from the `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variables (see [Providers](docs/providers.md)) ([#​10177](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10177), [#​10242](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10242) by [@​philfreo](https://redirect.github.com/philfreo)).
- `/reload` now enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. Tools removed from it stay enabled, tools turned off during the session stay off unless newly added, and `--tools`, `--no-tools`, and `--no-builtin-tools` still override the setting ([#​10245](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10245)).

##### Changed

- MCP servers with the default `codemode` exposure no longer appear in the `codemode` description; scripts find them with `searchTools()`. `codemode-deferred` is now an alias for `codemode`. Use `direct` exposure for tools the model should see without searching ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The `codemode` description no longer includes deferred tools, tool counts, or MCP server instructions, so it no longer changes when MCP servers connect or change their tools. The `tool_search` description no longer lists the servers whose tools it can load, for the same reason. Servers are listed instead in an `mcp_servers` system prompt section with a one-line summary, updated at the start of each prompt; a changed section is appended to the conversation. Scripts read server instructions with `describeNamespace()` ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The first prompt no longer waits for MCP servers without `direct` tools. They connect in the background and are waited for when a codemode script names them, a script searches tools, or `tool_search` runs ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).

##### Fixed

- Fixed new sessions intermittently ignoring the saved default model, or warning that no models are available, when it belongs to an extension-registered native provider with a stored credential ([#​9962](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9962), [#​10190](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10190) by [@​davidbrai](https://redirect.github.com/davidbrai)).
- Fixed the `/mcp` sign-in URL not being clickable when it wraps across lines, by emitting it as a terminal hyperlink with a `Cmd/Ctrl+click to open` line like `/login` ([#​10186](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10186)).
- Fixed codemode `image()` accepting malformed base64 data or unsupported image types, which persisted an invalid image block that made every later provider request fail with HTTP 400 ([#​10215](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10215)).
- Fixed codemode failing to start its script worker from the standalone Windows executable ([#​10204](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10204)).
- Fixed prompt submission slowing down with session length, because resolving the session's model selection looked up the model catalog once per assistant message ([#​10198](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10198)).
- Fixed model lookups slowing down for providers with a refreshed pi.dev catalog, because merging remote catalog models took quadratic time.
- Fixed the `built-in-tool-renderer.ts` and `minimal-mode.ts` extension examples removing the built-in tools' summaries and guidelines from the system prompt ([#​10072](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10072), [#​10193](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10193) by [@​christianklotz](https://redirect.github.com/christianklotz)).
- Fixed context overflow detection for Z.AI CN endpoint `Prompt exceeds max length` errors ([#​10208](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10208)).
- Fixed Anthropic requests failing when a tool schema uses keywords Anthropic strict tool use rejects, such as `minimum`/`maximum`; such tools are now sent non-strict ([#​9953](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9953)).
- Fixed provider retries firing immediately when a `Retry-After` header contains an unparseable date; they now use exponential backoff ([#​9571](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9571)).
- Fixed extension commands registered without a string name or handler crashing pi when typing `/`; the extension now fails to load with an error instead ([#​10054](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10054)).
- Fixed collapsed `codemode` and MCP tool results filling the screen when the output is one long line, such as minified JSON. Like bash output, the preview is now limited to wrapped line

hits.body:
`registries_dependencies` is the only surface that refuses a PURL without a version. The CLI and the docs API pick the latest release, but an agent needs a second call just to find a version.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Call the MCP tool:

   ```json
   {"purl":"pkg:npm/lodash"}
   ```

2. Run the CLI:

   ```sh
   registries deps npm/lodash
   ```

## Actual

The tool answers `registries_dependencies failed: Invalid PURL "pkg:npm/lodash": must include a version for dependency lookup`.

The CLI prints `No version specified, using latest: 4.18.1` and then the dependency list. The docs API route `docs/server/api/dependencies.get.ts` resolves the latest version first as well and returns the version it used.

That's the wrong way round. The terminal gets the convenient default, the agent gets a lecture about its PURL.

## Proposal

In `dependenciesOperation` in `src/tool-operations.ts`, resolve `latestVersion` from the package when the PURL has no version. Name the version used in the text the model reads and in the details, which are `{ dependencies }` today.

`fetchDependenciesFromPURL` in `src/helpers.ts` keeps throwing `InvalidPURLError`. The library docs say a version is required there, and that's fine for library callers.

## Notes

Resolving latest costs one more registry request. On the hosted `/mcp` worker that's a second query against the budget of 30 a minute, and `queryCost` in `docs/server/utils/registries-mcp.ts` would need to count it.

Open question: resolve latest in the tool, or keep refusing and put the latest version into the error message?

[src/core/client.ts](https://github.com/agntn/registries/blob/4c06e3e4fe5ccbe7f690e3c3e68a14202082f3e7/src/core/client.ts) uses `ofetch.create()`, `$Fetch`, `FetchOptions` and `FetchError`. Native `fetch` is available in the supported Node runtime. Remove this extra transport dependency without changing registry error handling.

## Proposal

- Replace the configured client with native requests and explicit response parsing, including the existing handling of empty responses. Failed HTTP responses must still become `HTTPError`, and exhausted 429 responses must keep their `RateLimitError` metadata.
- Keep the rate limiter, configurable retries, exponential backoff with jitter, `Retry-After` handling and timer overflow checks. Cancellation must interrupt requests and backoff, and every attempt needs a fresh timeout.
- Retain header overrides and the identifying User-Agent. Update the client tests and the build configuration regression test.
- Remove `ofetch` from [package.json](https://github.com/agntn/registries/blob/4c06e3e4fe5ccbe7f690e3c3e68a14202082f3e7/package.json) and `docs/package.json`, regenerate both lockfiles and update the transport notes in `AGENTS.md`.

Exercise the existing client tests against mocked native responses, including 404, 429, retry exhaustion and abort during a wait. Do not remove transitive copies still required by Nuxt or unstorage.

hits.body:
`registries_versions` sends every release back to the agent. On v0.4.1, `pkg:pypi/requests` produced about 30,000 characters for one result. That's a lot of context for checking recent releases. Pi, OMP, MCP and the AI SDK version operation only accept a PURL, while the CLI already limits its output to 20 versions by default.

Add a bounded recent-version view to the agent operations, with an explicit way to request more or all releases. Sort before limiting and report how many releases were omitted, so older history does not silently disappear. Acceptance: a normal lookup returns a bounded, newest-first result across the four agent integrations; an explicit history request can still retrieve all releases; dates and status remain available. This limits the answer sent to the model, not necessarily the registry fetch.

hits.body:
Every request this library makes announces itself as `registries/0.1.0`. The package is 0.4.1 (5d2107a), and `src/version.ts` already exports the real version, so the header has been wrong through four minor releases:

```ts
// src/core/client.ts:9
const DEFAULT_USER_AGENT = "registries/0.1.0";
```

npm, PyPI and crates.io all read the User-Agent for traffic attribution and rate-limit decisions, so a frozen version makes it impossible to tell which release is behind a request when one of them starts throttling us. The sibling packages already do this right: `agntn-web/${version}` in web, `agntn-books/${version} (+https://github.com/agntn/books)` in books. Registries is the odd one out, and it also drops the `agntn-` prefix the others share.

Scope I would take: build the default from `version` in `src/version.ts` and match the sibling shape, `agntn-registries/${version}`, with the repository URL if the convention there is worth keeping. A caller-supplied `userAgent` still wins as it does now. Accepting it: the default header carries the installed version and moves on its own with a release, an explicit `userAgent` option is unchanged, and no registry adapter hardcodes a version string of its own.

Closes #33

`cached()` fetches registry data, then persists it to storage and updates the lockfile. If either write throws (disk full, permissions, remote driver timeout on something like Cloudflare KV), the exception bubbles up and the caller never gets the data that was already sitting in memory.

The fix wraps only the two storage I/O calls in try-catch. Pure computation (entry construction, integrity hashing) stays outside the catch so programming errors there still surface normally. On storage failure, the caller gets fresh data and next request just refetches.

`readLockfile()` already had this resilience pattern (try-catch with empty-lockfile fallback). The write side was missing it.

Raise the minimum Node.js to 26 and test on 26 only. The package declares `engines.node` `>=22.6.0`.

## Proposal

- `package.json`: set `engines.node` to `>=26`.
- CI: `test.yml` uses `node-version: lts/*`, which is 24 until 2026-10-28. Test and release on 26.
- CI: `publish.yml` pins `node-version: 24.21.0`. Test and release on 26.
- Docs: README.md:26 and README.md:34 still say Node.js 22.6 or newer.

## Why

- Node.js 24 goes into maintenance on 2026-10-20 and Node.js 26 becomes LTS on 2026-10-28 ([release schedule](https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-schedule)).
- These packages are built for our own agents and tooling, and development already happens on 26. Keeping older majors costs a CI job and caps the APIs we can use. It doesn't keep a user we need.
- 26 has what 24 lacks: OpenSSL 3.6 in `node:crypto` (`keccak-256` among others) and native `Uint8Array` hex and base64 (`fromHex`, `toHex`, `fromBase64`, `toBase64`). Checked on 26.10.0 against 24.21.0.
- agntn/hashes#31 made the switch first and replaced its own Keccak with OpenSSL's.

The `Retry-After` handler in `Client.getJSON` runs `Number.parseInt` on the raw header value. Numeric strings like `"120"` work fine, but RFC 7231 also allows HTTP-date values (`"Wed, 21 Oct 2025 07:28:00 GMT"`), and parseInt returns NaN for those. That NaN ends up in `RateLimitError.retryAfter`, which breaks the error message and any consumer code that reads the field.

Extracted a `parseRetryAfter()` function that tries numeric first, then `Date.parse` for HTTP-date, and falls back to 60s when neither works. The registries regxa targets all use numeric values today, but the NaN fallthrough was still a bug waiting to happen.

Addresses item 3 from #18.

hits.body:
Pi 0.99.0 warns about extension packages that list host-provided modules in `dependencies`, and `typebox` is on that list ([check](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.99.0/packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts#L53-L97)). `package.json` has `"typebox": "1.3.34"` there, so Pi shows an extension warning whenever it loads this package. Pi's point is that a physical copy can dodge its module mapping and end up as a second TypeBox next to the host's. There's no peer entry for it yet.

## Proposal

Take `typebox` out of `dependencies`, declare it as a required peer with the `"*"` range [Pi's docs](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.99.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/packages.md#declare-dependencies) ask for, and keep an exact pin in `devDependencies`. `src/mcp.ts` imports TypeBox at runtime, so the CLI and MCP server still need it installed: npm and pnpm install required peers by default, while Pi's own managed installs switch peer installs off and supply the host copy. If leaning on peer auto-install feels too loose for the CLI, bundling TypeBox into `dist` is the other option.

The Pi dev pin (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 0.84.2) goes to 0.99.x in the same change, or rides along with Renovate's grouped `earendil-works` PR.

Release: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v0.99.0

The `storageKey` in `CachedRegistry.cached()` didn't include the ecosystem, so it was built as `lodash:package` while the lockfile key was correctly `npm:lodash:package`. With default storage this was masked by `getEcosystemStorage()` wrapping the storage in `prefixStorage`, but when passing custom storage (Cloudflare KV, Redis, etc.), two registries caching the same package name would silently overwrite each other's data.

I hit this while testing a shared Cloudflare KV setup where both npm and PyPI registries used the same storage instance. Fetching `json` from npm, then `json` from PyPI, returned the PyPI result for both.

The fix reuses the lockfile's `cacheKey` (which already includes the ecosystem) as the storage key, and drops the ecosystem-prefixed storage wrapper since the key itself now provides the namespace. Existing caches will miss once and rebuild on the next fetch.

Partially addresses #18 (item 2: cache storageKey not namespaced by ecosystem).

**Changes:**
- `storageKey` now equals `cacheKey(eco, name, type, version)` instead of omitting the ecosystem
- Constructor uses `getStorage()` directly instead of `getEcosystemStorage()` (no double-prefixing)
- Added test verifying two ecosystems with the same package name don't collide

hits.body:
`combineLicenses` was joining multiple licenses with `" AND "`, which in SPDX means "you must comply with all of them". When a registry returns an array of licenses (RubyGems `licenses: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]`, Packagist `license: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]`), the semantics are disjunctive - the user picks one. Composer docs say this explicitly: "array = disjunctive license".

So `["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]` should produce `"MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, not `"MIT AND Apache-2.0"`. One-word fix, but gets the SPDX expression right for every multi-licensed package coming through RubyGems and Packagist adapters.

hits.body:
`fetchPackage` was picking the license from `data.versions[0]` - the first element in the crates.io API response array. The API returns versions newest-first, so this grabs whatever was published most recently, not the version that `latestVersion` actually points to.

When a crate has a pre-release newer than the latest stable (e.g. `2.0.0-alpha.1` after `1.0.0`), the license would come from the pre-release instead of the stable version. If the author changed or simplified the license for the alpha, `fetchPackage` would report the wrong license for the crate.

The fix finds the version entry matching `latestVersion` and uses its license, falling back to `versions[0]` only if the match isn't found. This matches how the npm registry already does it - keying into `data.versions[latestVersion]` rather than blindly using the first array element.

Added a test with a crate where `max_stable_version` differs from the newest version and each has a different license.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>earendil-works/pi (@​earendil-works/pi-coding-agent)</summary>

### [`v0.99.2`](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/HEAD/packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md#0992---2026-09-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/v0.99.1...v0.99.2)

##### New Features

- MCP servers stay out of the way: servers with the default `codemode` exposure are no longer listed in the `codemode` description and no longer block the first prompt. They appear in a short system prompt section, and scripts find their tools with `searchTools()` and `describeNamespace()`. See [Control tool exposure](docs/mcp.md#control-tool-exposure).
- More MCP authentication options: `oauth.clientName` for servers that only accept known OAuth clients, and `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` to authenticate HTTP servers with a provider's `/login` token. See [Authenticate with OAuth](docs/mcp.md#authenticate-with-oauth).
- Anthropic workload identity federation from the Anthropic SDK environment variables. See [Use an API key from the environment](docs/providers.md#use-an-api-key-from-the-environment).
- `/reload` enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. See [Tools](docs/settings.md#tools).

##### Added

- Added a `description` field for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --description`), shown with the server in the system prompt and used to rank its tools in tool search, and a `describeNamespace(name)` codemode helper that returns a namespace's instructions and tool names. `describeNamespace()` and `searchTools()` accept a namespace as `mcp__dev-radius`, `mcp__dev_radius`, `dev-radius`, or `dev_radius`.
- Added an `oauth.clientName` setting for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --oauth-client-name`) to change the client name sent during OAuth client registration, for servers that only accept known clients ([#​10226](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10226)).
- Added `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` for HTTP MCP servers to send a provider's current `/login` token as the bearer token instead of using MCP OAuth. The token is read on every request, so provider refreshes apply. Only allowed in the global `mcp.json` and from extensions, and requires https except on loopback hosts.
- Added Anthropic workload identity federation from the `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variables (see [Providers](docs/providers.md)) ([#​10177](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10177), [#​10242](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10242) by [@​philfreo](https://redirect.github.com/philfreo)).
- `/reload` now enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. Tools removed from it stay enabled, tools turned off during the session stay off unless newly added, and `--tools`, `--no-tools`, and `--no-builtin-tools` still override the setting ([#​10245](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10245)).

##### Changed

- MCP servers with the default `codemode` exposure no longer appear in the `codemode` description; scripts find them with `searchTools()`. `codemode-deferred` is now an alias for `codemode`. Use `direct` exposure for tools the model should see without searching ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The `codemode` description no longer includes deferred tools, tool counts, or MCP server instructions, so it no longer changes when MCP servers connect or change their tools. The `tool_search` description no longer lists the servers whose tools it can load, for the same reason. Servers are listed instead in an `mcp_servers` system prompt section with a one-line summary, updated at the start of each prompt; a changed section is appended to the conversation. Scripts read server instructions with `describeNamespace()` ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The first prompt no longer waits for MCP servers without `direct` tools. They connect in the background and are waited for when a codemode script names them, a script searches tools, or `tool_search` runs ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).

##### Fixed

- Fixed new sessions intermittently ignoring the saved default model, or warning that no models are available, when it belongs to an extension-registered native provider with a stored credential ([#​9962](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9962), [#​10190](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10190) by [@​davidbrai](https://redirect.github.com/davidbrai)).
- Fixed the `/mcp` sign-in URL not being clickable when it wraps across lines, by emitting it as a terminal hyperlink with a `Cmd/Ctrl+click to open` line like `/login` ([#​10186](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10186)).
- Fixed codemode `image()` accepting malformed base64 data or unsupported image types, which persisted an invalid image block that made every later provider request fail with HTTP 400 ([#​10215](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10215)).
- Fixed codemode failing to start its script worker from the standalone Windows executable ([#​10204](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10204)).
- Fixed prompt submission slowing down with session length, because resolving the session's model selection looked up the model catalog once per assistant message ([#​10198](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10198)).
- Fixed model lookups slowing down for providers with a refreshed pi.dev catalog, because merging remote catalog models took quadratic time.
- Fixed the `built-in-tool-renderer.ts` and `minimal-mode.ts` extension examples removing the built-in tools' summaries and guidelines from the system prompt ([#​10072](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10072), [#​10193](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10193) by [@​christianklotz](https://redirect.github.com/christianklotz)).
- Fixed context overflow detection for Z.AI CN endpoint `Prompt exceeds max length` errors ([#​10208](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10208)).
- Fixed Anthropic requests failing when a tool schema uses keywords Anthropic strict tool use rejects, such as `minimum`/`maximum`; such tools are now sent non-strict ([#​9953](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9953)).
- Fixed provider retries firing immediately when a `Retry-After` header contains an unparseable date; they now use exponential backoff ([#​9571](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9571)).
- Fixed extension commands registered without a string name or handler crashing pi when typing `/`; the extension now fails to load with an error instead ([#​10054](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10054)).
- Fixed collapsed `codemode` and MCP tool results filling the screen when the output is one long line, such as minified JSON. Like bash output, the preview is now limited to wrapped line

- **DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision (experimental)** — Use the vision-capable model through the built-in DeepSeek provider. See [API Keys](docs/providers.md#api-keys).

- Added `supportsMidConvoEffort` to custom Anthropic Messages model compatibility settings.
- Added transcript notices for Anthropic thinking blocks dropped during provider recovery when cache miss notices are enabled.

- Added RPC `clear_queue` to retrieve and remove queued steering and follow-up messages ([#​8432](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8432)).
- Added environment variables and advanced settings for overriding auto-detected terminal hyperlink, image, and truecolor capabilities ([#​8665](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8665)).
- Added `fullscreenCopyOnSelect` to disable automatic fullscreen selection copy; when disabled, `Ctrl+X` copies the active text selection before falling back to the last assistant message, while `/tree` still copies the selected message ([#​7720](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7720)).

##### Changed

- Changed fullscreen scrollbars to reveal on pointer entry, support optional `scrollbarTrack` and `scrollbarThumb` theme colors with muted and text fallbacks, keep one thumb color across normal and expanded states, and support track-click jumping.
- Changed fullscreen transcript search arrows to underline on hover and capitalized the search placeholder.
- Changed selectors in `/thinking`, `/model`, `/scoped-models`, `/trust`, per-model thinking settings, and theme settings to keep active options marked while browsing. `/scoped-models` now uses consistent per-item toggles and strikes through unavailable models ([#​8900](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8900)).

- Fixed compaction and branch summaries forcing `toolChoice: "none"` ([#​8649](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8649), [#​8638](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8638)).
- Fixed large tool results crossing the auto-compaction threshold being sent to the provider before compaction. - Fixed Google Vertex requests failing with `HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor` when the bundled Node.js runtime uses an HTTP(S) proxy ([#​8610](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8610)).
- Fixed saving a default model from a non-empty model scope so it remains available in that scope.

hits.body:
`registries_dependencies` is the only surface that refuses a PURL without a version. The CLI and the docs API pick the latest release, but an agent needs a second call just to find a version.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Call the MCP tool:

   ```json
   {"purl":"pkg:npm/lodash"}
   ```

2. Run the CLI:

   ```sh
   registries deps npm/lodash
   ```

## Actual

The tool answers `registries_dependencies failed: Invalid PURL "pkg:npm/lodash": must include a version for dependency lookup`.

The CLI prints `No version specified, using latest: 4.18.1` and then the dependency list. The docs API route `docs/server/api/dependencies.get.ts` resolves the latest version first as well and returns the version it used.

That's the wrong way round. The terminal gets the convenient default, the agent gets a lecture about its PURL.

## Proposal

In `dependenciesOperation` in `src/tool-operations.ts`, resolve `latestVersion` from the package when the PURL has no version. Name the version used in the text the model reads and in the details, which are `{ dependencies }` today.

`fetchDependenciesFromPURL` in `src/helpers.ts` keeps throwing `InvalidPURLError`. The library docs say a version is required there, and that's fine for library callers.

## Notes

Resolving latest costs one more registry request. On the hosted `/mcp` worker that's a second query against the budget of 30 a minute, and `queryCost` in `docs/server/utils/registries-mcp.ts` would need to count it.

Open question: resolve latest in the tool, or keep refusing and put the latest version into the error message?

hits.body:
The MCP server, the Pi extension, the OMP extension and `src/ai.ts` each wire up the tools on their own: schema handling, validation, error text and sanitizing, four times over. Every tool change has to land in all of them, and so does every fix to how a failure reads. `@agntn/tools` takes one definition per tool and hands it to every surface, with validation in the core, so there's only one copy left to get wrong.

## Proposal

- One `defineTool` per tool, schemas built with `Type` from `@agntn/tools`. Never from `typebox` directly: OMP rewrites that bare import to its own facade and `Value.Check` then quietly accepts anything.
- Wire the surfaces through the adapters: `createMcpServer` in `src/mcp.ts`, `registerPiTools` and `registerOmpTools` in the extensions, `toAiTools` in `src/ai.ts`.
- Keep executors behind a cached dynamic import, so the extensions register tools without loading the library.
- Drop what the adapters replace: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.x (the MCP adapter runs on `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.x), zod and the direct `typebox` dependency where nothing else needs them, plus the local validation and sanitizing helpers.

## Notes

- archives, books, ciphers, hashes, keys, puzzles, wiki and `_template` are already on it. On hashes the production install dropped from 95 packages to 7 and the MCP cold start from 330 ms to 184 ms, all 208 tests unchanged. Numbers and the reasoning behind each adapter are in the agntn/tools `AGENTS.md`.
- Check the result in compiled OMP and Pi from a packed tarball, not only against the test doubles. books had a dead OMP extension that its mocked test never noticed.

## CLI

The command line moves too. It's still its own citty app in `src/cli.ts` and `src/commands/`, with every argument written there a second time. `runCli` from `@agntn/tools/cli` (since 0.1.0) takes the same tool list and builds one command per tool from its schema, `mcp: true` replaces the hand written `mcp` command, and `citty` goes away.

- Command names, aliases and positionals the current CLI has go into the `cli` hint on `defineTool`, so the usual invocations keep working.
- Commands today: `cache`, `deps`, `info`, `maintainers`, `versions`, plus `mcp`. Each one with a tool behind it becomes a generated command, the rest become package `commands` (tool definitions too, which only the CLI gets).
- Output changes a bit: the text is the tool's model text, `--json` prints `details`, object and array arguments come in as JSON, and stdin is strict UTF-8, one argument per call. A command that needs binary stdin stays a package command whose `execute` reads `-` itself.
- Guide: https://tools.agntn.dev/guide/cli

### [`v2.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/%40modelcontextprotocol/client%402.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/compare/@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.3.1...@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.4.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​3085](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3085) [`a633756`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/a63375661399956a744ff8b34d03d36e3d09e98a) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - Add an opt-in for sending `scope` on refresh-token requests, for authorization servers that reject a refresh without it (Microsoft Entra ID answers `AADSTS90009` when the client and the resource are the same app registration, [#​2718](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/issues/2718)). `OAuthClientProvider` gains an optional `scopeForRefresh(tokens)`: `auth()`, and so the transports and `withOAuth`, sends the string it returns. `refreshAuthorization()` gains an optional `scope`. When a scope is sent and the response has none, the sent scope is kept on the returned tokens. Without either option the refresh request and the saved tokens are unchanged.

- [#​3047](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3047) [`46d9c99`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/46d9c9921b6542e813c1ecc5f9fc964085e8e3bb) Thanks [@​KKonstantinov](https://redirect.github.com/KKonstantinov), [@​tobi-oye](https://redirect.github.com/tobi-oye), [@​mattzcarey](https://redirect.github.com/mattzcarey)! - Add the Skills extension (SEP-2640), reachable through new `ext/skills` subpaths; package root exports are unchanged.

  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills`: `SkillsExtension` (`attach(server)` serves `skills/list`, `skills/get`, `resources/directory/read` and a `skill://{+path}` resource template), `SkillsExtension.load(files)` returning a `SkillCatalog` with `entries` and `reload()`, the `SkillFiles` storage adapter with `memorySkillFiles`, `SkillSource` for generated catalogs, `skillEntry`, and `SkillCatalogError`. Invalid skills are skipped with a warning (`onWarning`), or fail under `strict`. A file whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is served as `text`, whatever its MIME type; any other file as a base64 `blob`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills/node`: `loadSkills(folder)` and `nodeSkillFiles(folder)`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills`: `SkillsClient` with `list()` (throws on an invalid entry; `skipInvalid: true` keeps the valid ones and returns the rest in `invalid`), `get()`, `read(skill, path?)` (size, digest and `SKILL.md` frontmatter verified, `SkillVerificationError` on a mismatch; a copy from the response cache that fails a check is fetched once more with `cacheMode: 'refresh'` first) and `readDirectory()`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/core/ext/skills`: schemas, types and constants, including `SKILL_LIMITS`. The result schemas follow the stable spec, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are required.

  `SkillsExtension.attach` is `@experimental`: how an extension is wired to a server may change in a minor release. The rest of the Skills API is stable.

  Works on 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. On 2026-07-28 only, the server sends the caching fields (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope`), and `SkillsClient` requires them and returns them from `list()`, `get()` and `readDirectory()`.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​3083](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3083) [`ef38c67`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/ef38c6765a15ee29030340dfea28b013893fa0a2) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - The bundled Ajv validator is now built with fast-uri 3.1.8 (was 3.1.0). fast-uri 3.1.6 and later reject a `$id` or `$ref` whose text before the first colon is not a valid URI scheme (`my_tool:output`), or whose URN namespace is not valid (`urn:my_tool:output`): a schema that uses one no longer compiles, and a tool that carries it fails with an invalid-schema error. An underscore without a colon (`my_tool_output`) and a `$ref` into `#/$defs/...` or `#/definitions/...` are not affected.

`cached()` fetches registry data, then persists it to storage and updates the lockfile. If either write throws (disk full, permissions, remote driver timeout on something like Cloudflare KV), the exception bubbles up and the caller never gets the data that was already sitting in memory.

The fix wraps only the two storage I/O calls in try-catch. Pure computation (entry construction, integrity hashing) stays outside the catch so programming errors there still surface normally. On storage failure, the caller gets fresh data and next request just refetches.

`readLockfile()` already had this resilience pattern (try-catch with empty-lockfile fallback). The write side was missing it.

The PEP 508 parser was using substring matching on environment markers to guess dependency scope. `extra == "latest"` got classified as test scope because the marker string contains "test". Platform markers like `sys_platform == "win32"` were also incorrectly affecting scope since "win32" doesn't contain "dev" or "test" but other platform values could.

The fix switches to proper `extra == "..."` marker extraction so only the extra name itself determines scope. Platform and python version markers are left alone - they don't change whether something is a dev or test dependency.

While in there, version specs now get their parentheses stripped (`(<4,>=2)` becomes `<4,>=2`) for consistency with how the other registries store version constraints, and `[extras]` bracket groups in package names are handled instead of leaking into the version spec.

hits.body:
The `storageKey` in `CachedRegistry.cached()` didn't include the ecosystem, so it was built as `lodash:package` while the lockfile key was correctly `npm:lodash:package`. With default storage this was masked by `getEcosystemStorage()` wrapping the storage in `prefixStorage`, but when passing custom storage (Cloudflare KV, Redis, etc.), two registries caching the same package name would silently overwrite each other's data.

I hit this while testing a shared Cloudflare KV setup where both npm and PyPI registries used the same storage instance. Fetching `json` from npm, then `json` from PyPI, returned the PyPI result for both.

The fix reuses the lockfile's `cacheKey` (which already includes the ecosystem) as the storage key, and drops the ecosystem-prefixed storage wrapper since the key itself now provides the namespace. Existing caches will miss once and rebuild on the next fetch.

Partially addresses #18 (item 2: cache storageKey not namespaced by ecosystem).

**Changes:**
- `storageKey` now equals `cacheKey(eco, name, type, version)` instead of omitting the ecosystem
- Constructor uses `getStorage()` directly instead of `getEcosystemStorage()` (no double-prefixing)
- Added test verifying two ecosystems with the same package name don't collide

`Version.publishedAt` is typed as `Date | null`, but `unstorage` serializes through JSON under the hood. `JSON.parse` doesn't revive ISO date strings back to Date objects, so after a cache hit, `publishedAt` is silently a plain string. Any downstream code calling `.getTime()` or `.toISOString()` on it (like `selectVersion` in helpers.ts, or the `versions` CLI command) would blow up with a TypeError.

Added a revive step in `CachedRegistry.fetchVersions` that wraps `publishedAt` with `new Date()`. Safe for both paths - `new Date(date)` copies a Date, `new Date(isoString)` parses a string.

`fetchPackage` was picking the license from `data.versions[0]` - the first element in the crates.io API response array. The API returns versions newest-first, so this grabs whatever was published most recently, not the version that `latestVersion` actually points to.

When a crate has a pre-release newer than the latest stable (e.g. `2.0.0-alpha.1` after `1.0.0`), the license would come from the pre-release instead of the stable version. If the author changed or simplified the license for the alpha, `fetchPackage` would report the wrong license for the crate.

The fix finds the version entry matching `latestVersion` and uses its license, falling back to `versions[0]` only if the match isn't found. This matches how the npm registry already does it - keying into `data.versions[latestVersion]` rather than blindly using the first array element.

Added a test with a crate where `max_stable_version` differs from the newest version and each has a different license.

`combineLicenses` was joining multiple licenses with `" AND "`, which in SPDX means "you must comply with all of them". When a registry returns an array of licenses (RubyGems `licenses: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]`, Packagist `license: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]`), the semantics are disjunctive - the user picks one. Composer docs say this explicitly: "array = disjunctive license".

So `["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]` should produce `"MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, not `"MIT AND Apache-2.0"`. One-word fix, but gets the SPDX expression right for every multi-licensed package coming through RubyGems and Packagist adapters.

The `Retry-After` handler in `Client.getJSON` runs `Number.parseInt` on the raw header value. Numeric strings like `"120"` work fine, but RFC 7231 also allows HTTP-date values (`"Wed, 21 Oct 2025 07:28:00 GMT"`), and parseInt returns NaN for those. That NaN ends up in `RateLimitError.retryAfter`, which breaks the error message and any consumer code that reads the field.

Extracted a `parseRetryAfter()` function that tries numeric first, then `Date.parse` for HTTP-date, and falls back to 60s when neither works. The registries regxa targets all use numeric values today, but the NaN fallthrough was still a bug waiting to happen.

Addresses item 3 from #18.

## Summary
PyPI's `/pypi/<project>/json` endpoint still works but the `releases` field is deprecated - the Simple API (`/simple/<project>/`, PEP 691) is the intended way to enumerate versions now. `fetchVersions` was the only method touching `releases`, so only that one moved.

`Client.getJSON()` picked up an optional `headers` parameter to support content negotiation (`application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json`). The other PyPI methods (`fetchPackage`, `fetchDependencies`, `fetchMaintainers`) stay on the project JSON endpoint since they only need package metadata, not version lists.

Files in the Simple API response aren't grouped by version, so there's a `matchFileVersion` helper that maps filenames back to their versions. Not the prettiest API design on PyPI's part, but it works.

`parsePURL` calls `decodeURIComponent` in six places (name, namespace, version, qualifiers, subpath) but never catches the `URIError` it throws on broken sequences like `%ZZ` or a trailing `%`. That means malformed input bypasses the typed error hierarchy - consumers catching `InvalidPURLError` won't see it, and the error message is a raw V8 `URIError: URI malformed` instead of something useful.

Adds a `decodePURLComponent` helper that catches decode failures and re-throws as `InvalidPURLError` with the original PURL string. Six new tests cover each component position.

hits.body:
Version extraction in `parsePURL` used `indexOf("@")` on the full remainder, so `pkg:npm/@vue/core` hit the scope `@` first and treated `@vue/core` as the version string. Every CLI command (`info`, `versions`, `deps`, `maintainers`) threw `InvalidPURLError` on scoped shorthand that wasn't percent-encoded.

Switched to `lastIndexOf("@")` with a positional guard - the `@` only counts as a version separator if it sits after the last `/`. Scoped `@` always comes before a `/`, so it's left alone now.

Existing tests still pass (percent-encoded scopes were fine before). Two new tests cover the literal `@` path: `pkg:npm/@vue/core` without version and `pkg:npm/@vue/core@3.4.0` with one.

Closes #25

hits.body:
Package name normalization only replaced underscores with hyphens, but PEP 503 specifies collapsing any run of `[-_.]` into a single hyphen. A package like `zope.interface` or `my--package` would pass through with dots and double hyphens intact, which breaks cache key consistency and can cause duplicate entries for the same package.

The regex in both `purl.ts` and `pypi.ts` now matches the reference implementation from PEP 503: `re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()`. Also normalized dependency names coming out of `parsePEP508`, so `requires_dist` entries like `zope.interface>=5.0` produce `zope-interface` instead of the raw dotted form.

## Test plan

- [x] New test: dots, double-dots, double-hyphens, mixed separators (`my_-_package`) all collapse to single hyphen
- [x] Full test suite (320 tests) passes
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean

`withErrorHandling` only caught three error types - `NotFoundError`, `UnknownEcosystemError`, and `InvalidPURLError`. When a registry returned 500/503 after exhausting retries, or rate-limited with 429, the CLI dumped a raw stack trace instead of something useful.

Added handlers for `HTTPError` (shows status code and URL, suggests retrying for 5xx) and `RateLimitError` (shows the retry-after window). Also switched existing handlers from bare `process.exit(1)` to `return process.exit(1)` so the function actually terminates when `process.exit` is mocked in tests.

Partially addresses #18 - items 2 (storageKey namespacing) and 3 (Retry-After parsing) were already fixed in prior work, this covers the remaining gap in CLI error handling.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/v0.99.1...v0.99.2)

##### New Features

- MCP servers stay out of the way: servers with the default `codemode` exposure are no longer listed in the `codemode` description and no longer block the first prompt. They appear in a short system prompt section, and scripts find their tools with `searchTools()` and `describeNamespace()`. See [Control tool exposure](docs/mcp.md#control-tool-exposure).
- More MCP authentication options: `oauth.clientName` for servers that only accept known OAuth clients, and `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` to authenticate HTTP servers with a provider's `/login` token. See [Authenticate with OAuth](docs/mcp.md#authenticate-with-oauth).
- Anthropic workload identity federation from the Anthropic SDK environment variables. See [Use an API key from the environment](docs/providers.md#use-an-api-key-from-the-environment).
- `/reload` enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. See [Tools](docs/settings.md#tools).

##### Added

- Added a `description` field for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --description`), shown with the server in the system prompt and used to rank its tools in tool search, and a `describeNamespace(name)` codemode helper that returns a namespace's instructions and tool names. `describeNamespace()` and `searchTools()` accept a namespace as `mcp__dev-radius`, `mcp__dev_radius`, `dev-radius`, or `dev_radius`.
- Added an `oauth.clientName` setting for MCP servers (`pi mcp add --oauth-client-name`) to change the client name sent during OAuth client registration, for servers that only accept known clients ([#​10226](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10226)).
- Added `"auth": { "provider": "<provider>" }` for HTTP MCP servers to send a provider's current `/login` token as the bearer token instead of using MCP OAuth. The token is read on every request, so provider refreshes apply. Only allowed in the global `mcp.json` and from extensions, and requires https except on loopback hosts.
- Added Anthropic workload identity federation from the `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variables (see [Providers](docs/providers.md)) ([#​10177](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10177), [#​10242](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10242) by [@​philfreo](https://redirect.github.com/philfreo)).
- `/reload` now enables tools newly added to the `defaultTools` setting. Tools removed from it stay enabled, tools turned off during the session stay off unless newly added, and `--tools`, `--no-tools`, and `--no-builtin-tools` still override the setting ([#​10245](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10245)).

##### Changed

- MCP servers with the default `codemode` exposure no longer appear in the `codemode` description; scripts find them with `searchTools()`. `codemode-deferred` is now an alias for `codemode`. Use `direct` exposure for tools the model should see without searching ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The `codemode` description no longer includes deferred tools, tool counts, or MCP server instructions, so it no longer changes when MCP servers connect or change their tools. The `tool_search` description no longer lists the servers whose tools it can load, for the same reason. Servers are listed instead in an `mcp_servers` system prompt section with a one-line summary, updated at the start of each prompt; a changed section is appended to the conversation. Scripts read server instructions with `describeNamespace()` ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).
- The first prompt no longer waits for MCP servers without `direct` tools. They connect in the background and are waited for when a codemode script names them, a script searches tools, or `tool_search` runs ([#​10212](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212)).

##### Fixed

- Fixed new sessions intermittently ignoring the saved default model, or warning that no models are available, when it belongs to an extension-registered native provider with a stored credential ([#​9962](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9962), [#​10190](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10190) by [@​davidbrai](https://redirect.github.com/davidbrai)).
- Fixed the `/mcp` sign-in URL not being clickable when it wraps across lines, by emitting it as a terminal hyperlink with a `Cmd/Ctrl+click to open` line like `/login` ([#​10186](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10186)).
- Fixed codemode `image()` accepting malformed base64 data or unsupported image types, which persisted an invalid image block that made every later provider request fail with HTTP 400 ([#​10215](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10215)).
- Fixed codemode failing to start its script worker from the standalone Windows executable ([#​10204](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10204)).
- Fixed prompt submission slowing down with session length, because resolving the session's model selection looked up the model catalog once per assistant message ([#​10198](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10198)).
- Fixed model lookups slowing down for providers with a refreshed pi.dev catalog, because merging remote catalog models took quadratic time.
- Fixed the `built-in-tool-renderer.ts` and `minimal-mode.ts` extension examples removing the built-in tools' summaries and guidelines from the system prompt ([#​10072](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10072), [#​10193](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10193) by [@​christianklotz](https://redirect.github.com/christianklotz)).
- Fixed context overflow detection for Z.AI CN endpoint `Prompt exceeds max length` errors ([#​10208](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10208)).
- Fixed Anthropic requests failing when a tool schema uses keywords Anthropic strict tool use rejects, such as `minimum`/`maximum`; such tools are now sent non-strict ([#​9953](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9953)).
- Fixed provider retries firing immediately when a `Retry-After` header contains an unparseable date; they now use exponential backoff ([#​9571](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9571)).
- Fixed extension commands registered without a string name or handler crashing pi when typing `/`; the extension now fails to load with an error instead ([#​10054](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10054)).
- Fixed collapsed `codemode` and MCP tool results filling the screen when the output is one long line, such as minified JSON. Like bash output, the preview is now limited to wrapped line

- Changed fullscreen transcript search arrows to underline on hover and capitalized the search placeholder.
- Changed selectors in `/thinking`, `/model`, `/scoped-models`, `/trust`, per-model thinking settings, and theme settings to keep active options marked while browsing. `/scoped-models` now uses consistent per-item toggles and strikes through unavailable models ([#​8900](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8900)).

They are now appended once the turn's tool results are in ([#​8537](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8537)).
- Fixed compaction and branch summaries forcing `toolChoice: "none"` ([#​8649](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8649), [#​8638](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8638)).
- Fixed large tool results crossing the auto-compaction threshold being sent to the provider before compaction. Pi now compacts between tool execution and the next assistant response in the same run, and restores interactive progress when that run resumes ([#​6879](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6879)).
- Fixed Google Vertex requests failing with `HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor` when the bundled Node.js runtime uses an HTTP(S) proxy ([#​8610](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8610)).
- Fixed saving a default model from a non-empty model scope so it remains available in that scope.
- Fixed inherited `@` file autocomplete ranking to prefer direct and shallower matches over similarly ranked nested paths ([#​8669](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8669)).
- Fixed inherited OpenAI-compatible streams serializing thinking signatures repeatedly during streaming ([#​8671](https://redirect.github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8671)).

- Fixed inherited OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions ignoring an explicitly requested `toolChoice` when no tools are defined.

Closes #33

`cached()` fetches registry data, then persists it to storage and updates the lockfile. If either write throws (disk full, permissions, remote driver timeout on something like Cloudflare KV), the exception bubbles up and the caller never gets the data that was already sitting in memory.

The fix wraps only the two storage I/O calls in try-catch. Pure computation (entry construction, integrity hashing) stays outside the catch so programming errors there still surface normally. On storage failure, the caller gets fresh data and next request just refetches.

`readLockfile()` already had this resilience pattern (try-catch with empty-lockfile fallback). The write side was missing it.

hits.body:
The `Retry-After` handler in `Client.getJSON` runs `Number.parseInt` on the raw header value. Numeric strings like `"120"` work fine, but RFC 7231 also allows HTTP-date values (`"Wed, 21 Oct 2025 07:28:00 GMT"`), and parseInt returns NaN for those. That NaN ends up in `RateLimitError.retryAfter`, which breaks the error message and any consumer code that reads the field.

Extracted a `parseRetryAfter()` function that tries numeric first, then `Date.parse` for HTTP-date, and falls back to 60s when neither works. The registries regxa targets all use numeric values today, but the NaN fallthrough was still a bug waiting to happen.

Addresses item 3 from #18.

hits.body:
## Problem

`matchFileVersion` in `src/registries/pypi.ts` normalizes the package name to underscores per PEP 427/625, then checks if the filename starts with that prefix. This works for spec-compliant builds but silently drops files from maintainers who upload non-normalized filenames (dashes or dots in the distribution segment).

The result is `publishedAt: null` and empty `integrity` for those versions, which is graceful but hides data.

## Context

PyPI doesn't enforce filename normalization on upload. PEP 427 (wheels) and PEP 625 (sdists) define the spec, but older or non-compliant tooling can produce filenames that don't follow it.

Flagged in PR #56 review threads by both CodeRabbit and Cubic.

## Suggested approach

Try both the underscore-normalized prefix and a dash-based variant. Return the first match.

The `storageKey` in `CachedRegistry.cached()` didn't include the ecosystem, so it was built as `lodash:package` while the lockfile key was correctly `npm:lodash:package`. With default storage this was masked by `getEcosystemStorage()` wrapping the storage in `prefixStorage`, but when passing custom storage (Cloudflare KV, Redis, etc.), two registries caching the same package name would silently overwrite each other's data.

I hit this while testing a shared Cloudflare KV setup where both npm and PyPI registries used the same storage instance. Fetching `json` from npm, then `json` from PyPI, returned the PyPI result for both.

The fix reuses the lockfile's `cacheKey` (which already includes the ecosystem) as the storage key, and drops the ecosystem-prefixed storage wrapper since the key itself now provides the namespace. Existing caches will miss once and rebuild on the next fetch.

Partially addresses #18 (item 2: cache storageKey not namespaced by ecosystem).

**Changes:**
- `storageKey` now equals `cacheKey(eco, name, type, version)` instead of omitting the ecosystem
- Constructor uses `getStorage()` directly instead of `getEcosystemStorage()` (no double-prefixing)
- Added test verifying two ecosystems with the same package name don't collide

hits.body:
`combineLicenses` was joining multiple licenses with `" AND "`, which in SPDX means "you must comply with all of them". When a registry returns an array of licenses (RubyGems `licenses: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]`, Packagist `license: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]`), the semantics are disjunctive - the user picks one. Composer docs say this explicitly: "array = disjunctive license".

So `["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]` should produce `"MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, not `"MIT AND Apache-2.0"`. One-word fix, but gets the SPDX expression right for every multi-licensed package coming through RubyGems and Packagist adapters.

`fetchPackage` was picking the license from `data.versions[0]` - the first element in the crates.io API response array. The API returns versions newest-first, so this grabs whatever was published most recently, not the version that `latestVersion` actually points to.

When a crate has a pre-release newer than the latest stable (e.g. `2.0.0-alpha.1` after `1.0.0`), the license would come from the pre-release instead of the stable version. If the author changed or simplified the license for the alpha, `fetchPackage` would report the wrong license for the crate.

The fix finds the version entry matching `latestVersion` and uses its license, falling back to `versions[0]` only if the match isn't found. This matches how the npm registry already does it - keying into `data.versions[latestVersion]` rather than blindly using the first array element.

Added a test with a crate where `max_stable_version` differs from the newest version and each has a different license.

Three issues surfaced during the #17 review that predate the PR. Worth addressing separately.

**1. `sideEffects: false` conflicts with registry side-effect imports**
`src/registries/index.ts` is purely side-effect imports (each registry calls `register()` at top level). With `sideEffects: false` in package.json, bundlers like Webpack/Vite can tree-shake the entire registries barrel, meaning registrations never execute for consumers using `import "regxa/registries"`.

Either remove `sideEffects: false` or switch to an allowlist like `"sideEffects": ["dist/registries/index.mjs"]`.

**2. Cache `storageKey` not namespaced by ecosystem**
In `src/cache/cached-registry.ts`, the lockfile key (`cacheKey`) includes the ecosystem but `storageKey` does not. If someone shares one `Storage` instance across multiple registries, two ecosystems with the same package name overwrite each other's cached payload.

**3. `Retry-After` header only handles numeric format**
`src/core/client.ts` parses `Retry-After` with `Number.parseInt()`, which returns `NaN` for HTTP-date values like `"Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT"`. The registries we target all use numeric values today, but the fallback to `NaN` is still a latent bug.

Additionally, 5 more test files import from `vitest` despite `globals: true` being set:
- `test/unit/ai-tool.test.ts`
- `test/unit/alpm.test.ts`
- `test/unit/cached-registry.test.ts`
- `test/unit/registries.test.ts`
- `test/unit/lockfile.test.ts`

Sourced from anyio's releases.

4.14.2

  • Changed ByteReceiveStream.receive() implementations to raise a ValueError when max_bytes is not a positive integer (#1191)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting float("inf") when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop. The adapter setter checked for infinity by identity (value is math.inf), so only the exact math.inf singleton was accepted, while every backend setter (using math.isinf()) accepts any positive infinity (#1189; PR by @​greymoth-jp).
  • Fixed to_process.run_sync() deadlocking when the worker function writes enough data to sys.stderr to fill the (undrained) pipe buffer. The worker process now redirects sys.stderr to os.devnull as well, matching the documented behavior
  • Fixed TLSStream.wrap() matching an internationalized (unicode) host name against the peer certificate using IDNA 2003 (via the standard library) instead of IDNA 2008, which could cause the host name to be matched against the wrong certificate (#1208)
  • Fixed anyio.open_process() (and run_process()) ignoring the extra_groups argument, as it mistakenly passed the value of the group argument instead (#1209)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait() and CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait_on_behalf_of() raising trio.WouldBlock instead of anyio.WouldBlock on the trio backend when there are no tokens available (#1218)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter on the asyncio backend over-granting tokens (borrowed_tokens exceeding total_tokens and available_tokens going negative) when a non-blocking acquire was made in the window between a token being released and the notified waiter resuming. The freed token is now reserved for the woken waiter right away, so the non-blocking acquire correctly raises WouldBlock (#1170; PR by @​gaoflow)
  • Fixed unnecessary CPU spin when delivering cancellation from CancelScope on asyncio under certain conditions, including improper cancel scope nesting (#1111)

  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting a value of 0 when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop, contradicting the documented behavior of allowing 0 total tokens (#1183; PR by @​nyxst4ck)

4.14.0

## Summary

Adds support for Azure AI Foundry **project endpoints** (`https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}`), which fail with classic `AzureChatOpenAI` (e.g. `API version not supported`).

**Closes #41**

- New `AzureFoundryProvider` using `AzureAIOpenAIApiChatModel` (`langchain-azure-ai`)
- `ProviderType` split: `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure` → classic OpenAI-on-Azure; `MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry` → Foundry project API
- Shared `azure_deployments.py` for deployment env map and helpers used by both Azure providers
- Documentation and unit tests

No URL auto-detection — use `MODEL_PROVIDER` or `LLMConfig(provider=...)`.

## Breaking change

| Before | After |
|--------|--------|
| `azure` and `foundry` aliases both used classic `AzureProvider` | `azure` → `AzureProvider` (`AzureChatOpenAI`) |
| `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure_ai_foundry` selected classic Azure | `azure_ai_foundry` / `foundry` → `AzureFoundryProvider` |

Classic `*.openai.azure.com` deployments: keep `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure`.  
Foundry project URLs: use `MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry`.

## Usage

```bash
MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry
AZURE_FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT=https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}
AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY=...
AZURE_GPT_4O_DEPLOYMENT=your-deployment-name
DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-4o
```

API key auth uses the resource OpenAI-compatible `/openai/v1` endpoint (derived from the project URL). Deployment env vars match classic Azure.

For Entra ID, pass `AzureFoundryProvider` via `LLMConfig` — see `packages/agent-sdk/README.md`.

- [x] `make lint-fix && make typecheck && make test-unit` in `packages/agent-sdk`
- [x] Unit tests in `test_azure_foundry_provider.py`
- [ ] Manual: Foundry project with `MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry`
- [ ] Manual: Classic Azure still works with `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure`
