Bumps [pyjwt](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt) from 2.10.1 to 2.15.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pyjwt's releases.

2.15.0

See the 2.15.0 changelog for complete release details.

2.14.0

See the 2.14.0 changelog for the complete release details and related security advisories.

2.13.0

PyJWT 2.13.0 — Security Release

This release bundles five security fixes plus three additional hardening / spec-compliance changes. We recommend all users upgrade.

Security

  • GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx — JWK JSON accepted as HMAC secret (algorithm confusion). HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key previously rejected PEM- and SSH-formatted asymmetric keys but did not catch a JWK passed as a raw JSON string. In a verifier configured with both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms in algorithms=[…] and a raw-JSON JWK as the key, an attacker could forge HS256 tokens using the JWK text as the HMAC secret. The guard has been extended to reject any JWK-shaped JSON. Reported by @​aradona91.

  • GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f — Algorithm allow-list bypass with PyJWK / PyJWKClient. When verifying with a PyJWK, the caller's algorithms=[…] allow-list was checked against the token header alg as a string only; actual verification used the algorithm bound to the PyJWK. An attacker who controlled a registered JWKS key could sign with one algorithm and advertise another on the header. PyJWT now requires the token header alg to match the PyJWK's algorithm before verification. Reported by @​sushi-gif.

  • GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39 — DoS via base64 decode of unused payload segment when b64=false. For detached-payload JWS (b64=false), the compact-form payload segment was base64-decoded before being discarded in favor of the caller-supplied detached_payload. An attacker could inflate the unused segment to force CPU + memory cost without holding a valid signature. The segment is now required to be empty per RFC 7515 Appendix F, and is no longer decoded. Reported by @​thesmartshadow.

  • GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4 — PyJWKClient accepts non-HTTP(S) URIs. PyJWKClient.fetch_data passed its URI to urllib.request.urlopen, which by default also handles file://, ftp://, and data: schemes. An application that fed an attacker-influenced URI into PyJWKClient could be coerced into reading local files or reaching other unintended schemes. PyJWKClient now rejects any URI whose scheme isn't http or https. Reported by @​KEIJOT.

  • GHSA-fhv5-28vv-h8m8 — PyJWKClient cache wiped on fetch error. A finally-block put(jwk_set=None) cleared the JWK Set cache whenever a fetch raised, turning a transient JWKS-endpoint outage into application-wide auth failure. The cache write was moved into the success path; transient errors no longer evict valid cached keys. Reported by @​eddieran.

Fixed

  • Reject empty HMAC keys outright in HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key with InvalidKeyError instead of accepting them with only a warning. Defends against the os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "") footgun. Thanks to @​SnailSploit and @​spartan8806 for the reports.
  • Forward per-call options (including enforce_minimum_key_length) from PyJWT.decode through to PyJWS._verify_signature. The option was previously silently dropped between the two layers, so it only took effect when set on the PyJWT instance. Thanks to @​WLUB for the report.
  • RFC 7797 §3 compliance for b64=false: the encoder now auto-adds "b64" to crit, and the decoder rejects tokens that set b64=false without listing it in crit. Thanks to @​MachineLearning-Nerd for the report.

Changed

  • Migrate the dev, docs, and tests package extras to dependency groups, by @​kurtmckee in #1152.

Upgrade notes

Most fixes are invisible to correctly-configured callers. A few behavioral changes you may encounter:

  • Empty HMAC keys now raise. If your app passed "" or b"" as a secret (often via a missing env var, e.g. os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "")), encode/decode will now raise InvalidKeyError. This is the intended behavior — fix the configuration.
  • PyJWK decoding now requires the token's alg to match the JWK's algorithm. Previously a mismatch was silently honored if the header alg appeared in the allow-list. Tokens that relied on this mismatch will now fail with InvalidAlgorithmError.
  • PyJWKClient now rejects non-HTTP(S) URIs at construction time. Tests or dev environments that fetched JWKS from file:// URIs need to switch to a local HTTP server or load the JWKS by other means (e.g. construct PyJWKSet.from_dict(...) directly).
  • b64=false tokens are now strictly RFC 7515 / 7797 compliant. Tokens with a non-empty compact-form payload segment, or that omit "b64" from crit, will be rejected. PyJWT-produced tokens always satisfy both invariants, so round-trips through PyJWT are unaffected.
  • enforce_minimum_key_length set per-call now takes effect. Callers who passed options={"enforce_minimum_key_length": True} to jwt.decode() previously got no enforcement; they will now get InvalidKeyError on undersized keys, as documented.

Full changelog: https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/compare/2.12.1...2.13.0

Bumps [mcp](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk) from 1.30.0 to 2.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from mcp's releases.

v2.3.0

pip install -U mcp. Docs: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/

Mostly fixes, plus three new options. A few things behave differently, so skim these first:

Behaviour changes

httpx2>=2.10.0 is now required (#3600)

  • It was >=2.5.0. The new max_sse_event_size option needs it.
  • Nothing to do unless you pin httpx2 below 2.10.

A tool with an invalid x-mcp-header annotation fails at registration (#3620)

  • @mcp.tool(), add_tool and Tool.from_function raise InvalidSignature, naming the tool and the problem.
  • Until now the server started, and 2026-07-28 clients silently dropped the tool from their listing.
  • Refused: anything other than a plain str, int or bool parameter (so also str | None, float, lists and enums), a header name that isn't a valid token, and two names that differ only by case.
  • For an optional header parameter, give the schema directly: Annotated[str | None, WithJsonSchema({"type": "string", "x-mcp-header": "Region"})] = None.

Empty _meta and params are no longer sent (#3628)

  • On 2025-11-25 and earlier connections, 2.x sent "_meta": {} on every request. Some servers reject that. It is now left out, as in v1.
  • ping and list requests without a cursor go out with no params member.
  • On the receiving side ctx.meta is None rather than {}, and middleware sees ctx.params as None for a request without params.
  • 2026-07-28 connections are unchanged.

initialize leaves out experimental when none is configured (#3614)

  • It used to send "experimental": {}. server/discover already left it out.
  • Client code reading capabilities.experimental on a legacy connection should handle None.

Mcp-Param-* validation looks the tool up by name (#3630)

  • MCPServer no longer runs tools/list for every tools/call, so middleware no longer sees that extra request.
  • The registered schema is what gets checked. Middleware that filters or rewrites tools/list no longer affects it.

An interactive OAuth login no longer counts against request timeouts (#3635)

  • The timeout pauses while OAuthClientProvider waits on redirect_handler and callback_handler.
  • This fixes Client(mode="auto") settling on 2025-11-25 when the login took longer than 10 seconds.
  • A request timeout no longer ends a login nobody finishes. Put a limit inside callback_handler if you need one.

New

  • max_sse_event_size= on streamable_http_client and StreamableHttpParameters. The default stays 1 MiB per SSE event; raise it, or pass None, for larger tool results (#3600).
  • MCPServer(subscriptions=False) stops serving subscriptions/listen and advertises listChanged and subscribe as false (#3626).
  • Server(get_tool_input_schema=...) lets a low-level server supply a tool's schema for header validation without running its tools/list handler (#3630).
  • Client.call_tool re-lists the tools and retries once after a HeaderMismatch (-32020) rejection (#3627).

Fixes

  • ctx: Context[AppState] works on prompts and resource templates, not only on tools (#3624).
  • An explicit "structuredContent": null is checked against the output schema instead of being treated as missing (#3621).
  • A progress_callback that raises no longer fails the call on an in-process Client(server) (#3623).
  • Client OpenTelemetry spans record JSON-RPC error responses. With mode="auto", connecting to a server without server/discover now shows one ERROR span for the probe (#3629).
  • stdio_client resolves the executable off the event loop on Windows (#3510).

Changelog

Sourced from cryptography's changelog.

50.0.0 - 2026-07-31


* **SECURITY ISSUE**:
  :func:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.pkcs7.pkcs7_decrypt_der`
  and its PEM and S/MIME variants no longer expose distinguishable errors or
  timing when unwrapping a ``RecipientInfo``'s ``encryptedKey``, which could
  act as a Bleichenbacher oracle for callers that decrypt untrusted messages.
  A random key is now substituted on failure, as described in :rfc:`3218`.
  Credit to **@X1AOxiang** for reporting the issue. **CVE-2026-69247**
* Deprecated Diffie-Hellman key exchange over finite fields (FFDH).
  Everything FFDH is deprecated, including the types in
  ``cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.dh`` and loading FFDH keys or
  parameters with the key loading APIs. Users should migrate to a more
  modern key exchange algorithm.
* Added ``xof()`` class methods to
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE128` and
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE256` for constructing
  algorithm instances configured for use with
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash`.
* The :mod:`X.509 verification <cryptography.x509.verification>` APIs are now
  considered stable and are subject to our API stability policy.
* Added the :doc:`/cobblestone` recipe, an implementation of the
  Cobblestone-128 and Cobblestone-256 instantiations of the `C2SP
  chunked-encryption specification
  <https://c2sp.org/chunked-encryption>`_ for streaming authenticated
  encryption of large messages.
* Parsing a Signed Certificate Timestamp list now rejects encodings that
  carry trailing bytes after the list or after an individual SCT, instead of
  silently ignoring them.
* Added support for using :class:`~cryptography.x509.Name` as a field type in
  the :doc:`/hazmat/asn1/index` module.
* Loading a public key or an EC private key now rejects DER where the
  ``subjectPublicKey`` (or EC ``publicKey``) ``BIT STRING`` declares a non-zero
  number of unused bits, instead of silently ignoring it.
* Parsing a CRL entry's ``InvalidityDate`` extension now rejects a
  ``GeneralizedTime`` that carries fractional seconds or another non-DER form,
  matching the strict encoding already required for every other X.509 time
  field.
* :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_request` and
  :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_response` now reject a request
  or response whose ``version`` field is not ``v1``, the only version defined
  by RFC 6960, matching the version validation already performed when loading
  certificates, CSRs and CRLs.
* :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash` is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
* HMAC (and therefore PBKDF2-HMAC) with SHA-3 hashes is now supported when
  building against AWS-LC.
* Diffie-Hellman (:doc:`/hazmat/primitives/asymmetric/dh`) is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.

Sourced from pyasn1's releases.

Release 0.6.4

This is a security release.

  • CVE-2026-59885 (GHSA-8ppf-4f7h-5ppj): Fixed quadratic time complexity in the OBJECT IDENTIFIER and RELATIVE-OID decoders. A small crafted substrate encoding many arcs could consume excessive CPU.

  • Pinned PyPI publish GitHub Action to an immutable commit.

All changes are noted in the CHANGELOG.

Release 0.6.3

It's a minor release.

  • Added nesting depth limit to ASN.1 decoder to prevent stack overflow from deeply nested structures (CVE-2026-30922).
  • Fixed OverflowError from oversized BER length field.
  • Fixed DeprecationWarning stacklevel for deprecated attributes.
  • Fixed asDateTime incorrect fractional seconds parsing.

All changes are noted in the CHANGELOG.

Release 0.6.2

It's a minor release.

  • Fixed continuation octet limits in OID/RELATIVE-OID decoder (CVE-2026-23490).

Arcs are now accumulated in linear time; decoded values are unchanged (thanks for reporting, tynus2)
  • CVE-2026-59884 (GHSA-m4p7-r5rc-7g4j): Limited BER long-form tag IDs to 20 octets (140 bits), matching the OID arc limit introduced in 0.6.2. Unbounded tag IDs allowed a crafted substrate to consume excessive CPU and memory; longer tag IDs are now rejected with PyAsn1Error. Also fixed Tag and TagSet repr() failing on huge tag (thanks for reporting, mikeappsec) IDs due to the integer-to-string conversion limit (Python 3.11+)

Conversion no longer materializes huge intermediate integers; values too large to represent as a Python float raise OverflowError promptly, and prettyPrint() renders them as '' as before. Also fixed base-10 mantissa normalization to use exact integer arithmetic; mantissas larger than 2**53 could previously lose precision through float division (thanks for reporting, gvozdila)

Release notes

Sourced from anyio's releases.

4.14.2

  • Changed ByteReceiveStream.receive() implementations to raise a ValueError when max_bytes is not a positive integer (#1191)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting float("inf") when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop. The adapter setter checked for infinity by identity (value is math.inf), so only the exact math.inf singleton was accepted, while every backend setter (using math.isinf()) accepts any positive infinity (#1189; PR by @​greymoth-jp).
  • Fixed to_process.run_sync() deadlocking when the worker function writes enough data to sys.stderr to fill the (undrained) pipe buffer. The worker process now redirects sys.stderr to os.devnull as well, matching the documented behavior
  • Fixed TLSStream.wrap() matching an internationalized (unicode) host name against the peer certificate using IDNA 2003 (via the standard library) instead of IDNA 2008, which could cause the host name to be matched against the wrong certificate (#1208)

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Both jobs in the scheduled Security Audit run on main failed on 2026-10-26 because of advisories published against the unchanged lockfiles. This branch fixes all of them and applies Dependabot #105, which it supersedes, so the audit passes again before the 1.0 release. No Dependabot security alerts are currently open.

## JavaScript: zod override

GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (high) affects all zod versions below 4.6.6. Hooks already uses zod 4.6.7, but `@ag-ui/client` and `@ag-ui/proto` 1.0.3 (the latest release; the canary too) declare `zod ^3.25.76`, which pulled a nested 3.25.76. No 3.x release is patched.

The root `package.json` now overrides zod to `^4.6.6`. All `@ag-ui/*` runtime imports are `zod/v4`, which zod 4 exports with the same API, so the lock resolves a single zod 4.6.7. Applications that install `spaik-sdk-react` get zod 3 from `@ag-ui/client` until upstream moves to zod 4. They can add the same override.

## Python (`packages/agent-sdk/uv.lock`)

- fastmcp 4.1.0 → 4.1.4 for GHSA-7xgj-8392-5q4r and GHSA-vqqp-x5qm-5qp4 (both medium; the Python audit fails on any finding). The keyring tree leaves the lock with it.
- filelock 4.2.0 → 4.2.4 for six CVEs fixed in 4.2.1.
- From #105: fastapi 0.162.0, langchain-azure-ai 1.2.12 and pytest-mock 3.17.0.

fastapi 0.147–0.151 changed request-parameter handling. Spaik's routers are affected in two places, and both are fine: in the audio router, an empty `language`/`prompt` form field now arrives as `None` (already `Optional`), and a request with no file selected now gets a 422 response on the file and audio upload endpoints.

## langchain-azure-ai and anthropic

This reverses the hold from #104. langchain-azure-ai 1.2.10+ requires `anthropic<1.0` and pre-release Azure packages, so the lock now has:

- anthropic 1.14.0 → 0.125.0
- azure-ai-contentsafety 1.1.0b1
- azure-ai-contentunderstanding 1.2.0b3

Spaik only uses `AzureAIOpenAIApiChatModel` from it and never imports `anthropic` directly. langchain-anthropic 1.7.x accepts `>=0.120.0`. Anyone who installs `[azure]` together with `[anthropic]` gets the 0.x Anthropic SDK.

The lock was generated with uv 0.13.5, the version CI and Dependabot use. uv 0.11 won't pick the transitive betas, so a local `uv lock` on an old uv will fail for the azure extra.

## Verification

- `bun audit` (bun 1.4.4) and `pip-audit` on the exported lock, run as in `audit.yml`: no vulnerabilities.
- `uv lock --check`, ruff, ty and `pytest tests` (185 passed) on anthropic 0.125.0.
- `build:packages`, lint and type-check for hooks and Material, the example build, the AG-UI contract fixture with `bun test packages/agent-sdk-hooks/tests`, and Playwright (3 passed) with zod 4 inside `@ag-ui/client`.

hits.body:
# Spaik 1.0: AG-UI threads and UI, arbitrary models, reported costs, and removal of deprecated legacy packages

Spaik's frontend and backend spoke a custom block/event protocol, and the SDK kept its own price tables, model eligibility lists and per-model Azure maps. This PR makes official AG-UI the transcript and wire protocol, lets the SDK use any provider model ID, and removes code that duplicated upstream libraries. It is a breaking 1.0 release. Merging does not publish anything: committed versions stay at main's, and the per-package release workflows publish release candidates and then 1.0.0.

## Python SDK

- `get_response()` returns AG-UI assistant messages and streaming yields official AG-UI events. Use `.content` or `message_text(message)` in place of `.blocks`/`.get_text_content()`.
- Server: `/messages/stream` becomes `POST /threads/{id}/runs` (`RunAgentInput`, SSE) plus `/threads/{id}/cancel`. Threads have owners from creation; stored history is authoritative, so conflicting IDs, edited history and overlapping runs are rejected. Cancellation or disconnect saves partial output.
- Models: every model is an `LLMModel` (preset, custom or plain ID with a provider). Presets carry per-model limits; each family's current reasoning API applies to presets and new models alike. Older generations such as Claude 4.5 use `reasoning=False` or `provider_kwargs`, and `reasoning_budget_tokens` is removed. Reasoning summaries stream from OpenAI and Claude.
- Costs: `get_cost()` returns `CostSummary | None` from provider-reported charges, per currency, with a completeness flag.
- Storage: versioned JSON. Application repositories load legacy 0.x JSON with `load_thread_data`, converted in memory; local pickle stores are exported under 0.11.x and imported.
- Python 3.11+ is required.
- Provider SDKs, server, audio and MCP are optional extras. Mandatory dependencies go from 33 to 8. Tavily, Azure Functions queue and SignalR helpers are removed.

## React and Material

Hooks wrap the official AG-UI client (`HttpAgent`), so `AgentChat` works with any AG-UI backend. Spaik thread management is an optional `ThreadRepository`; the sidebar requires one.

Both packages accept React 18 or 19. Material takes `@mui/material` (5.15+, 6, 7 or 9) and emotion as peers, so applications install them (#72). The example app and templates consume the shared kit and show realistic agents and tools.

## Legacy packages and release

- `packages/coding-agents` and `packages/agent-workflows` are removed. Their final releases, coding agents 0.2.3 and workflows 0.3.2 (pinned to SDK 0.11.1), are published and tagged from main, and the earlier unpinned versions are yanked.
- The release workflows gain a *Pre-release* checkbox: ticked gives `1.0.0rc1` (npm `1.0.0-rc.1` under `next`) and then the next RC; unticked on an RC publishes the final version.
- Material peer-depends on `spaik-sdk-react ^1.0.0-rc.1`, so release hooks before Material. Templates accept the RCs.

## Testing

- The SDK test suite: 182 tests on Python 3.13. CI repeats it on 3.11.
- Python-to-TypeScript contract tests against SSE from the real endpoint.
- Chromium tests on React 19 and MUI 9 for the thread lifecycle, cancel and re-run, an independent AG-UI backend, uploads and speech.
- Installation of the minimal and full wheel, and of the npm tarballs into a new Vite app with strict peers: React 18 with MUI 5.15, and React 19 with MUI 6, 7 and 9.
- Migration of a real 0.11.1 store, including `export_thread` output loaded by `load_thread_data`.
- Live on OpenAI, Anthropic and Azure OpenAI (Entra ID): text, tools across turns, structured output, streaming and reasoning. Gemini 3.8 Flash answered text.

## Before stable 1.0

- After merging, release all three packages as `major` RCs, validate them in staging, then publish 1.0.0.
- The built-in runner is single-process; multi-worker deployments need application-owned coordination.

Updates `axios` from 1.20.0 to 1.21.0
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.21.0 — October 21, 2026

This release adds response timing and opt-in UTF-8 Basic authentication, improves request handling across runtimes, and changes how header defaults are recognized.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Header Defaults: Only plain objects, null-prototype maps, and compatible AxiosHeaders instances are treated as common or method-specific defaults; literal headers such as Link are now preserved. Applications using custom class instances as defaults must convert them to plain maps, for example { post: { ...customDefaults } }, or compatible AxiosHeaders. Otherwise, those instances become literal header values, including on requests using other methods. (#11156)

🚀 New Features

  • Response Timing: Added response.duration, in milliseconds, including on error.response when present. Timing measures adapter execution and excludes interceptors and transforms; streamed responses stop timing when the stream becomes available. Axios replaces any existing duration value supplied by a custom adapter. (#11214)
  • UTF-8 Basic Authentication: Added transitional.encodeBasicAuthUsername: true to support Unicode usernames in XHR and Fetch requests. The option defaults to false, preserving existing authentication behavior; applications opting in should supply the original Unicode username and remove manual pre-encoding workarounds. (#11159)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Fetch Compatibility: Restored requests in runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers that reject the implicit cache: 'default', while preserving explicit caller settings. Response-size failures now retain their original ERR_BAD_RESPONSE and request context when runtime wrappers replace the underlying stream error. (#11194, #11179)
  • Runtime Consistency: Aligned encoded-byte size accounting, multipart uploads, proxy routing, same-origin resolution, parameter merging, and form serialization across adapters. Circular parameters now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and sparse or non-index numeric form fields serialize as keyed objects. With proxy: false, native proxyEnv agents using unsupported pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle overrides now reject with ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE; construct those agents without proxyEnv. (#11242)
  • Header Handling: Preserved headers named __proto__ using safe casing without changing the AxiosHeaders instance prototype. Function matchers in has(), delete(), and clear() now receive the headers instance as this, matching their declared contract. (#11134, #11216)
  • URL and Data URL Parsing: Accepted case-insensitive supported URL schemes and Base64 markers, and corrected decoding of percent-encoded Base64 data URLs. Node data URL allocation estimates remain aligned with decoding so configured size limits apply before allocation. (#11138, #11163, #11294)
  • Error Diagnostics: Preserved short reconstructed request stacks and appended wrapped error stacks under Caused by: so tooling that reads only error.stack retains the original failure context. (#11132, #11142)
  • Interceptor Removal: Restored removal through canonical numeric-string interceptor IDs, including after registry compaction. (#11139)
  • Proxy TLS: HTTPS CONNECT tunnels now apply current origin TLS options from an explicit httpsAgent, or from https.globalAgent when no explicit agent is supplied. This preserves process-wide custom CA settings through proxy tunnels. (#11178)
  • XHR Lifecycle: Used asynchronous Cookie Store reads for XSRF tokens where supported, preserving cookie fallback, timeout accounting, and cancellation. Upload and download progress listeners are now removed on completion, failure, timeout, and cancellation. (#11166, #11225)
  • HTTP/2 Sessions: Stopped reusing sessions immediately after GOAWAY and prevented draining sessions from scheduling idle timers that could delay process exit. (#11210)
  • TypeScript Declarations: Exposed the response-default marker as a public type to resolve TS2527 when consumers emit declarations involving unresolved response generics, covering both ESM and CommonJS. (#11125)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Configuration Performance: Reduced request configuration merge overhead, particularly for requests with many headers, while preserving merge semantics and prototype-pollution guards. (#11208)
  • Same-Origin Checks: Removed obsolete Internet Explorer detection without changing origin decisions in supported environments. (#11174)
  • Dependencies: Updated follow-redirects to 1.16.1 and refreshed development, documentation, test, and GitHub Actions dependencies. Removed unused dayjs from the docs package, root chalk, and chai from CJS module tests. (#11169, #11188,

Spaik 1.0 removes `spaik-coding-agents` and `spaik-agent-workflows`. The published versions of both declare `spaik-sdk>=0.2.0` with no upper bound, so once SDK 1.0 is on PyPI a fresh install can pair them with an SDK they cannot import. This PR prepares the last 0.x releases from main: an SDK catalog patch (0.11.2), and final coding-agents 0.2.3 and workflows 0.3.2 releases pinned to SDK 0.11.1 that warn they are deprecated. The 1.0 migration itself lives in a separate PR that must not merge until these releases are published.

## SDK catalog (ships as 0.11.2)

- New presets, verified against provider docs on 2026-10-13: `CLAUDE_SONNET_5_5`, `CLAUDE_OPUS_5_5`, `CLAUDE_HAIKU_5_5`, `CLAUDE_FABLE_5_1`, `GPT_6_1_SOL`, `GPT_6_ASTRA`, `GPT_6_LUNA`, `GEMINI_3_8_FLASH`.
- **Behaviour change for alias users:** the bare aliases `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, `claude` and `gemini flash` now resolve to the newest model in each family. Versioned aliases such as `sonnet 5` are unchanged.
- In the Anthropic factory, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 raise `ValueError` when reasoning is disabled, because they require adaptive thinking. With reasoning off, Sonnet 5.5 uses `between_tools`; the other models still use `disabled`.
- GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra declare a minimum reasoning effort of `low`.

## Final coding-agents 0.2.3

- Requires exactly `spaik-sdk==0.11.1` and raises a `FutureWarning` on import. The README is marked deprecated and gives the pinned install command.
- `release-coding-agents.yml` publishes the committed 0.2.3 without a version bump, after installing it against the released SDK with `--no-sources`. It then tags `spaik-coding-agents-v0.2.3`.

## Final agent-workflows 0.3.2

- Requires exactly `spaik-sdk==0.11.1` and `spaik-coding-agents==0.2.3`, warns on import (which also covers CLI use), and is classified `Development Status :: 7 - Inactive`.
- `release-agent-workflows.yml` follows the same fixed-version pattern. Before publishing it runs `ruff check --no-fix`, the test suite and `spaik-agent-workflows --list` against PyPI dependencies. Its install step fails until coding-agents 0.2.3 is on PyPI, which enforces the release order.
- Fixes one import-order lint error in `claude_code.py` so the `--no-fix` check passes.

## Testing

- SDK: Ruff, `ty`, and 378 unit tests pass with `DEFAULT_MODEL` set as in the release workflow.
- Both final packages were built and installed into a fresh Python 3.11 environment alongside SDK 0.11.1 from PyPI. The resolver selected SDK 0.11.1. In that environment, coding-agents imports passed, the 38 workflows tests passed, the CLI listed the bundled workflows, and both deprecation warnings appeared.

## After merging

- Use **Create a merge commit**. The 1.0 branch already contains these commits, so a squash or rebase would make the 1.0 PR conflict.
- Run the manual workflows from main in this order, waiting for each version to appear on PyPI before starting the next:
  1. Release agent-sdk (`patch`, publishes 0.11.2)
  2. Final legacy coding-agent release
  3. Final legacy agent-workflows release
- On PyPI, yank coding-agents 0.2.0–0.2.2 and workflows 0.3.1 and earlier. Existing exact pins keep working.
- Release details: `docs/MODEL_REFRESH_2026_10.md`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added model presets for Claude 5.1/5.5, GPT-6, and Gemini 3.8, with updated aliases for Sonnet, Opus, Haiku, Fable, and Gemini Flash.
  * Updated reasoning behavior for selected Claude models.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated model guidance and optional preset availability notes.
  * Clarified that the legacy agent packages are deprecated, limited to the legacy protocol, and not compatible with Spaik 1.0.

* **Chores**
  * Set final legacy package versions and fixed compatibility requirements; importing these packages now displays a deprecation warning.

The scheduled Security Audit on 2026-11-02 failed in both jobs ([run](https://github.com/siilisolutions/spaik-sdk/actions/runs/41398554737)). This fixes it, then runs the weekly model refresh.

## Security audit

| Package | From → To | Advisory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| joserfc (py) | 1.7.5 → 1.7.7 | CVE-2026-119284 |
| pyasn1 (py) | 0.6.4 → 0.6.5 | CVE-2026-119194, -119195, -119196, -119197 |
| follow-redirects (js, via axios) | 1.16.1 → 1.16.2 | GHSA-mrwp-f3q8-3g9p (high) |

Lockfile-only changes. `pip-audit` reports no vulnerabilities. `bun audit --audit-level=high` passes (bun 1.4.4, the CI version). `uv lock --check` passes with uv 0.13.6.

**Not fixed:** minimatch 10.2.6 (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, moderate). It is reachable only through eslint and typescript-eslint, which are dev tools. The fix is minimatch 11, but eslint 10 pins `^10`, so it is blocked until eslint widens its range. It is below the `high` threshold, so it does not fail the audit.

## Model presets

Checked against the Anthropic, OpenAI and Google model docs, following `.agents/skills/model-update`.

- `GPT_6_1_TERRA` (`gpt-6.1-terra`): reasoning model. Lowest effort is `none`, which is the preset default. Supports prompt caching. [docs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-terra)
- `GEMINI_4_ARGON` (`gemini-4-argon`): GA on 2026-10-13. Thinking levels are low, medium and high (no `minimal`), so the preset sets `reasoning_min_effort="low"`. Implicit caching only. [docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-4-argon)
- The Claude lineup is unchanged: Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5.
- No presets were retired; none are deprecated in their providers' current lists. No alias changes.

## Dependabot PRs rolled in

Dependabot opened #112, #113 and #114 while this PR was open. All three failed the Security Audit only because they are based on main, which lacks the fixes above. Their bumps are folded in here, re-resolved on top of this branch:

- #113, python-minor-patch: langchain-core 1.7.6, langgraph 1.2.20, pydantic 2.14.3, langchain-openai 1.7.4, langchain-anthropic 1.7.10, ruff 0.17.4, pytest 9.2.0, pytest-asyncio 1.4.1.post1, ty 0.0.95 (`ty` pin bumped in `pyproject.toml`). Some of these are newer patches than the PR proposed, because they were released after it.
- #112, js-minor-patch: axios ^1.21.0, @eslint-react/eslint-plugin ^5.28.8, eslint ^10.14.0, typescript-eslint ^8.72.1.
- #114, pyasn1 0.6.5: already covered above.

Once this merges, Dependabot should close all three as up to date.

The CodeRabbit review had no actionable comments.

## Checks

`pip-audit` and `bun audit --audit-level=high` are clean after the roll-up. `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test-unit` (178 passed), `bun test packages/agent-sdk-hooks/tests`, `bun run build:packages`, and package lint and `tsc` for hooks, material and the example frontend. I did not run the live provider smoke test because no API keys were available locally.

# chore(deps): apply Dependabot #101 and #102 and clear certifi and follow-redirects advisories

Dependabot PRs #98, #101 and #102 were all red. #98 and #101 failed validation because they were opened against the old MCP 1 code and ty 0.0.13, and #99 has since moved main to MCP SDK 2 (`mcp` 2.3.0). #102's bumps were fine, but its audit jobs failed on two new advisories that hit main as well. This branch applies what those PRs still add on top of main and fixes both advisories, so the audit passes for the 1.0.0rc2 release.

## Python (`packages/agent-sdk`)

From #101: langchain-core 1.6.12, langgraph 1.2.16, fastapi 0.143.3, ruff 0.17.1 and ty 0.0.89. ty 0.0.89 is pinned in both `dev` lists in `pyproject.toml`, and it type-checks the current code cleanly.

`certifi` moves to 2026.10.19 for PYSEC-2026-4320 (compromised emSign intermediates).

`langchain-azure-ai` stays at 1.2.3. Version 1.2.10 needs `azure-ai-contentunderstanding>=1.2.0b2`, which only exists as a pre-release, and the lock doesn't allow pre-releases.

## JavaScript

From #102:
- `@ag-ui/client` and `@ag-ui/core` 1.0.3 in hooks
- eslint 10.13, typescript-eslint 8.72 and `@eslint-react/eslint-plugin` 5.28 in hooks and Material, plus eslint and typescript-eslint in the example

The frontend template gets the same eslint and typescript-eslint ranges as the example.

`follow-redirects` moves to 1.16.1 in `bun.lock` for GHSA-q3jh-wrc6-jgq8 and GHSA-8r9p-f939-6h3c (both high). It stays a transitive dependency of axios and 1.16.1 is within axios's `^1.16.0` range, so it needs no manifest entry or override.

## Verification

- `bun audit` (bun 1.4.4) and `pip-audit` on the exported lock, run the same way as `audit.yml`: no vulnerabilities found.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test-unit` (175 passed), `make test-integration` (10 passed), `ruff format --check`.
- `bun run build:packages`, type-check and lint for hooks and Material, lint for the example, `bun test packages/agent-sdk-hooks/tests`, and the example frontend build.

The Playwright suite was not run locally because port 8000 was in use. CI runs it.

## After merge

Close #98, #101 and #102. None of these changes affect the public API, so the migration guide is unchanged. Then run the release workflows with *prerelease* ticked: hooks first, then Material, then agent-sdk.

## Summary

Verified model refresh for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google based on official provider docs (August 2026).

- Add Claude Opus 4.8, Fable 5, Opus 5, and Sonnet 5
- Add OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna
- Add Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
- Update default aliases: `opus` → Opus 5, `sonnet`/`claude` → Sonnet 5, `gpt 5.6` → Sol, `gemini flash` → 3.6 Flash
- Retain legacy/shut-down model entries (no removals)
- Anthropic factory: adaptive thinking for 4.8/5.x; clear error when disabling thinking on Fable 5
- Azure: GPT-5.6 deployment env vars; `env.example` bumped to `2025-03-01-preview` for Responses API support
- Pricing added for all new models (Sonnet 5 uses intro rate through Aug 31, 2026)

## New models

| Provider | Registry constant | API ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | `CLAUDE_4_8_OPUS` | `claude-opus-4-8` | Adaptive thinking |
| Anthropic | `CLAUDE_FABLE_5` | `claude-fable-5` | Thinking always on |
| Anthropic | `CLAUDE_OPUS_5` | `claude-opus-5` | Default `opus` alias |
| Anthropic | `CLAUDE_SONNET_5` | `claude-sonnet-5` | Default `sonnet`/`claude` alias |
| OpenAI | `GPT_5_6_SOL` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-5.6` alias |
| OpenAI | `GPT_5_6_TERRA` | `gpt-5.6-terra` | Balanced tier |
| OpenAI | `GPT_5_6_LUNA` | `gpt-5.6-luna` | Low-cost tier |
| Google | `GEMINI_3_6_FLASH` | `gemini-3.6-flash` | Default `gemini flash` alias |
| Google | `GEMINI_3_5_FLASH_LITE` | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | GA July 2026 |

## Not added

- **Claude Mythos 5** — invitation-only (Project Glasswing), not GA in public API
- **New Claude Azure deployments** — no explicit Microsoft Foundry availability documented for 4.8/5.x yet

## Azure testing notes

GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna are already deployable on Azure OpenAI. Verified on `fndry-orion-leevi-test-001`:

- Chat Completions works with `AZURE_API_VERSION=2024-02-15-preview`

- Set deployment env vars (deployment names often match model IDs):

- `gemini-3-pro-preview` — deprecated on Google API March 9, 2026
- `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` — shut down May 25, 2026
- `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` — replacement is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`

This applies the ten open Dependabot PRs (#89–#98) and the remaining updates their next run would open, so main starts the 1.0 release candidates with nothing outdated. Two changes are breaking for SDK users, and both are in the migration guide: Zustand 5 in `spaik-sdk-react`, and MCP SDK 2 behind the `mcp` extra. `bun audit`, `npm audit` on the template and pip-audit across all extras each report 0.

## Runtime dependencies

`spaik-sdk-react` moves to ag-ui 1.0.2, zod 4 and Zustand 5. zod 4 stays internal, because the schemas are not exported; `BaseApiClient` adopts its `ZodType<Output, Input>` signature. Material moves to react-markdown 10, whose only breaking change is a `className` prop that Material does not pass.

## MCP

`langchain-mcp-adapters` caps `mcp` below 2 and is superseded upstream by `langchain.mcp`. The `mcp` extra now installs `langchain[mcp]` (fastmcp 4, mcp 2), and `McpToolProvider` builds on `MCPAdapter`. Its public API is unchanged. One adapter per server keeps tool names unprefixed, and tools from `load_from_stdio` stay callable after loading. `langchain.mcp` is beta upstream; the provider suppresses its beta warning, since users never import it directly. The integration tests run a local MCP SDK 2 echo server over stdio and streamable HTTP and cover env passing and multi-server tool names.

## Python

The lock is upgraded within `pyproject.toml`, covering the python-minor-patch group, and `ty` is pinned to 0.0.87. The stricter `ty` found type errors, fixed in `efd19dc`. All four lint setups (hooks, Material, example and template) move to ESLint 10 flat config. eslint-plugin-react stops at ESLint 9, so hooks and Material use `@eslint-react` instead. The example and template move to Vite 8 and plugin-react 6, and the template README now gives the Node versions Vite 8 needs. GitHub Actions move to checkout, setup-uv and setup-node v7.

## Checks

Locally on Python 3.13, ruff, ty, 175 unit and 10 integration tests pass. The full suite also passes on Python 3.11. For the frontend, lint, type-check and builds pass for every package, and so do the hooks tests. The template also passes lint, build and `npm audit` when installed outside the repo. The Playwright tests passed after each runtime change up to react-markdown. The final TypeScript commit was checked by type-check and builds only, because local ports were taken, so CI's browser run covers it.

## Follow-ups

`dependabot.yml` skips TypeScript 6.1 and later until typescript-eslint supports it; TypeScript 7 is out. Dependabot should close #89–#98 once this merges.

The security audit workflow only ran by hand, and its last run was nine months ago. On main, `bun audit` reports 83 vulnerabilities (47 high), and pip-audit finds known vulnerabilities in the SDK's base dependencies and in its server, MCP and provider extras. This PR clears all of them and makes the audit run on its own.

## JavaScript

`bun.lock` was out of sync with the 1.0 version bumps of hooks and Material, so it is regenerated first. In-range upgrades fix most findings, including vite 6.4.3, rollup, postcss and axios. `@typescript-eslint` moves from v6 to v8 (`^8.71.2`), because v6 pins a vulnerable `minimatch` and pulls in `braces` through globby. ESLint stays on 8, with its floor raised to `^8.57.1` as v8 requires, and the existing `.eslintrc.cjs` configs lint cleanly. The minimum axios version in hooks and the minimum vite version in the example and template move to the fixed releases, so npm installs that ignore our lockfile still get them. `npm audit` on the frontend template reports 0.

## Python

The affected packages are upgraded in `uv.lock`. Several jumps are large: openai 2 → 3, anthropic 0.76 → 1.14, starlette 0.48 → 1.8, fastapi 0.117 → 0.143 and pytest 9.

langchain-anthropic 1.4.1 added its own `output_config` setting, and it warns whenever `output_config` is passed through `model_kwargs`. `family_settings.py` now sets Claude's effort through `output_config` directly, and the `anthropic` extra requires `langchain-anthropic>=1.4.6`. The override in the migration guide for older Claude models changes with it: callers now pass `"output_config": None` instead of `"model_kwargs": {}`.

## Audit workflow

`audit.yml` runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC, on PRs to main that touch a lockfile, a `package.json`, `pyproject.toml` or the workflow, and by hand. Running only on those PRs keeps a newly published advisory from failing unrelated PRs. The bun job fails based on `bun audit --audit-level` instead of grepping the output text; against main's lockfile, the `high` threshold fails it and `critical` passes it. The Python job audits every shipped extra except `dev`, and it now uses Python 3.13, because the 3.10 it installed is below the SDK's `requires-python`.

`.github/dependabot.yml` sets up weekly version updates for bun, uv and GitHub Actions. Minor and patch bumps are grouped into one PR per ecosystem.

## Checks

Lint, type-check, 175 unit tests and 7 integration tests pass for Python. Lint, type-check, both package builds, the example build and the hooks tests pass for the frontend. None of these call real model APIs, so a live run against Anthropic and OpenAI is worth doing before the next release, given the major SDK bumps.

## After merge

This supersedes the open Dependabot PRs for aiohttp, cryptography, pyasn1 and anyio. GitHub sends scheduled-run failures to whoever last changed the cron line.

## Summary

Adds support for Azure AI Foundry **project endpoints** (`https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}`), which fail with classic `AzureChatOpenAI` (e.g. `API version not supported`).

**Closes #41**

- New `AzureFoundryProvider` using `AzureAIOpenAIApiChatModel` (`langchain-azure-ai`)
- `ProviderType` split: `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure` → classic OpenAI-on-Azure; `MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry` → Foundry project API
- Shared `azure_deployments.py` for deployment env map and helpers used by both Azure providers
- Documentation and unit tests

No URL auto-detection — use `MODEL_PROVIDER` or `LLMConfig(provider=...)`.

## Breaking change

| Before | After |
|--------|--------|
| `azure` and `foundry` aliases both used classic `AzureProvider` | `azure` → `AzureProvider` (`AzureChatOpenAI`) |
| `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure_ai_foundry` selected classic Azure | `azure_ai_foundry` / `foundry` → `AzureFoundryProvider` |

Classic `*.openai.azure.com` deployments: keep `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure`.  
Foundry project URLs: use `MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry`.

```bash
MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry
AZURE_FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT=https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}
AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY=...
AZURE_GPT_4O_DEPLOYMENT=your-deployment-name
DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-4o
```

API key auth uses the resource OpenAI-compatible `/openai/v1` endpoint (derived from the project URL). Deployment env vars match classic Azure.

For Entra ID, pass `AzureFoundryProvider` via `LLMConfig` — see `packages/agent-sdk/README.md`.

## Summary

- Adds proxy mode (`LLM_AUTH_MODE=proxy`) allowing all LLM provider traffic to route through a single proxy endpoint, configured via `LLM_PROXY_BASE_URL`, `LLM_PROXY_API_KEY`, and `LLM_PROXY_HEADERS` environment variables.
- Introduces `_get_proxy_config()` in `BaseProvider` that maps proxy settings to each provider's LangChain-specific parameter names (e.g. `anthropic_api_key`, `google_api_key`, `xai_api_base`).
- All 9 providers (Anthropic, Azure, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Ollama, OpenAI, XAI) support proxy mode with graceful fallback — direct mode remains the default and API keys are now optional when absent.
- Includes 32 unit tests covering `EnvConfig` proxy methods and proxy/direct mode behavior across all providers.

## Motivation

In enterprise and self-hosted deployments, it's common to route all LLM API calls through a centralized proxy (e.g. LiteLLM, custom gateway) for auth, rate limiting, cost tracking, or compliance. Today each provider requires its own API key and base URL, making proxy setups require per-provider env var overrides. This change introduces a single, unified proxy configuration that works across all providers.

## Changes

| Area | Files | What |
|------|-------|------|
| Config | `config/env.py`, `config/credentials_provider.py` | New proxy env methods (`is_proxy_mode`, `get_proxy_base_url`, `get_proxy_api_key`, `get_proxy_headers`); provider key no longer required |
| Base | `providers/base_provider.py` | `_get_proxy_config()` helper mapping proxy env to provider-specific LangChain kwargs |
| Providers | All 9 provider files | `get_model_config()` checks proxy mode first; direct mode now tolerates missing API keys |
| Tests | `tests/.../config/test_env_proxy.py` | 13 tests for `EnvConfig` proxy methods (defaults, parsing, edge cases) |
| Tests | `tests/.../providers/test_proxy_support.py` | 19 tests for proxy/direct mode across all providers |

## Configuration

| Env Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LLM_AUTH_MODE` | `direct` | Set to `proxy` to enable proxy routing |
| `LLM_PROXY_BASE_URL` | _(empty)_ | Proxy endpoint URL |
| `LLM_PROXY_API_KEY` | _(empty)_ | Auth key sent to proxy |
| `LLM_PROXY_HEADERS` | _(empty)_ | Comma-separated `Key:Value` pairs for extra headers |

## Test plan

- [x] All 32 new unit tests pass

## feat: incremental thread checkpointing during streaming

### Problem

`ThreadJobProcessor` only persisted the thread to storage after the entire streaming run completed. Any interruption mid-run — server restart, hot-reload, crash, timeout — wiped the full response. A 90-minute multi-tool run killed at 89 minutes lost everything.

### Solution

Checkpoint the thread to storage after each completed tool result and each completed message, so in-progress state survives interruptions.

### Changes

**`server/response/response_generator.py`**  
Added `OnCheckpoint` type alias and `on_checkpoint` optional parameter to the `ResponseGenerator` ABC.

**`server/response/agent_response_generator.py`**  
After each event from the agent stream, fires `on_checkpoint` if the event is a `ToolResponseReceivedEvent` or `MessageFullyAddedEvent` — the two natural "durable state" boundaries: tool result just landed, or a full message was finalized.

**`server/job_processor/thread_job_processor.py`**  
Wires a local `on_checkpoint` coroutine that calls `update_thread` into `stream_response`. The final `update_thread` after the loop is kept for clean-completion saves.

### Tests

- **5 unit tests** (`test_agent_response_generator.py`) — checkpoint fires on the right event types, once per event, silent when `None`
- **4 unit tests** (`test_thread_job_processor.py`) — `update_thread` call count, `on_complete` wiring, 404 handling
- **1 integration test** (`test_thread_checkpointing.py`) — runs a real recorded tool-calling agent through the full stack and asserts `save_thread` is called ≥ 2 times (at least one mid-run checkpoint + the final save)

hits.body:
## Problem

When a tool spawns a nested `BaseAgent` using `asyncio.run()`, the subagent inherits the calling coroutine's `contextvars` context. LangChain stores its active callback handlers there, so the subagent's tool calls get routed through the parent's `MessageHandler` and bleed into the parent thread — cluttering the UI and breaking the "subagent in a box" pattern.

## Solution

Two new methods on `BaseAgent`:

- **`spawn(task, attachments=None) → ThreadMessage`** — the primary API. Runs the subagent as an isolated call, preventing callback context from leaking. Drop-in replacement for `asyncio.run(sub.get_response_async(task))` inside a tool.
- **`BaseAgent.run_isolated(coro) → Any`** — static helper for the rare case where you need to isolate an arbitrary coroutine rather than a full agent response.

The fix works by running the coroutine in a fresh OS thread with a blank `contextvars.Context()`. A blank context has no inherited `ContextVar` values, so LangChain's callbacks are absent and the subagent's events stay inside its own `ThreadContainer`.

## Changes

- `spaik_sdk/agent/base_agent.py` — `spawn()` + `run_isolated()` added
- `examples/agents/subagent_example.py` — runnable demo: MainAgent → tool → SubAgent with echo tool, asserts only `spawn_sub` appears in parent thread
- `tests/unit/spaik_sdk/agent/test_base_agent.py` — `TestRunIsolated` class with 5 tests:
  - ContextVar set in parent is not visible inside `run_isolated`
  - Return value passes through correctly
  - Exceptions propagate out of the isolated run
  - `spawn()` doesn't leak parent ContextVar into the subagent (the exact bug scenario)
  - Concurrent `run_isolated` calls don't interfere
- `packages/agent-sdk/README.md` — new Subagents section
- `AGENTS.md` — `spawn()` added to Agent Methods list

## Usage

```python
class ResearchTools(ToolProvider):
    def get_tools(self) -> list[BaseTool]:
        @tool
        def research(topic: str) -> str:
            """Delegate to a specialist subagent."""
            sub = ResearchAgent(system_prompt="You are a research specialist.")
            return sub.spawn(topic).get_text_content()
        return [research]
```

# Issue: Subagents freeze indefinitely and never wake up

## Summary

Subagents occasionally get completely stuck — no tool calls, no findings, no
exit — and the orchestrator waits forever. Two separate bugs in spaik-sdk
interact. The primary cause is an unbounded LLM API hang that is never
interrupted. A secondary bug then adds 60 seconds of frozen event loop on top
of any error that does escape. Together they produce what looks like a permanent
freeze.

---

## Observed Behaviour

- Subagent starts (frontend shows "Running…"), never makes a single tool call.
- Orchestrator stalls indefinitely — no forward progress, no error reported.
- Restarting the backend is the only recovery path.

---

## Root Cause

### Bug 1 (primary) — LLM API hang is never interrupted

`spawn_subagent` calls `subagent.spawn(task)` which lands in
`BaseAgent.run_isolated()`:

```python
# spaik_sdk/agent/base_agent.py
t = threading.Thread(target=_thread)
t.start()
t.join()           # ← no timeout, ever
```

`_thread` calls `asyncio.run(get_response_async())`. If the HTTP connection to
the LLM API goes silent mid-stream (stale TCP connection, transient server
issue, etc.), `httpx` waits up to its `read` timeout per chunk — **600 seconds
by default** in the OpenAI SDK. The default `max_retries=2` means the SDK
silently retries up to twice:

```
3 attempts × 600 s read timeout = up to 30 minutes
```

Nothing in the spaik-sdk call chain can interrupt this. `t.join()` has no
timeout. The orchestrator's executor thread is held for the entire duration.
From the user's perspective: the subagent freezes and **never wakes up**.

This is the case where no tool calls appear — the agent dies before the first
LLM response is even received.

### Bug 2 (secondary) — `SyncAdapter.wait_for_completion_async()` CPU-spins for 60 s after any error

When the agent stream dies early (whether from a tool exception, an API
timeout, or any other error), blocks that were started with `streaming=True`
are never finalized. `SyncAdapter` is then called:

```python
# spaik_sdk/thread/adapters/sync_adapter.py
async def wait_for_completion_async(self, timeout: float = 30.0):
    start_time = time.time()
    while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
        if self._streaming_ended or not self.container.is_streaming_active():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
        # ← NO await in the else-branch
        # ← event loop is fully seized, nothing can happen for up to 30 s
    return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
```

It is called **twice** in the normal flow — once in `run_async()` (30 s) and
once in `get_response_async()` (30 s) — adding exactly **60 seconds** of dead
time on top of any upstream error.

### Bug 3 (contributing) — LangGraph `ToolNode` default handler re-raises all runtime tool exceptions

`LangChainService.create_executor()` uses `create_react_agent` without setting
`handle_tool_errors`, so `ToolNode` is created with the library default
`_default_handle_tool_errors`:

```python
# langgraph/prebuilt/tool_node.py  (LangGraph 1.1.3)
def _default_handle_tool_errors(e: Exception) -> str:
    if isinstance(e, ToolInvocationError):   # only arg-validation errors
        return e.message
    raise e                                  # everything else re-raised
```

Any runtime tool exception (`urllib.error.HTTPError`, `OSError`,
`ConnectionError`, HTTP 4xx from the LLM API itself such as a content filter
response, …) propagates out of LangGraph and crashes the agent loop.
The LLM never gets a chance to see the error and recover. Combined with Bug 2,
this turns a recoverable tool failure into a 60-second frozen subagent.

This bug affects both the subagent executor and the **main agent's** executor.
When a subagent spawn fails (raising `ValueError("No response received")`), that
exception escapes the main agent's ToolNode too — killing the entire
orchestration rather than letting the main LLM decide to retry or skip the step.

---

## Evidence from diagnostic run (`diagnose_subagents.py`)

Subagent 6 hit a 403 from DuckDuckGo, demonstrating Bug 2 + Bug 3 together:

```
[+409s]  SUBAGENT 6 starts
[+429s]  ERROR - langchain_service.py:210 - Error executing agent: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden
                ↑ Bug 3: exception escapes ToolNode instead of returning to LLM
[+429s–487s]  ← 58 s of SyncAdapter busy-wait (Bug 2: 30 s + 30 s)
[+487s]  SUBAGENT 6 OK  tool_calls=0  text_blocks=0
```

The truly indefinite freeze (Bug 1) was not hit in this run because the LLM API
responded promptly. It manifests when a connection stalls mid-stream, most
often on the first LLM call — which is why users see "no tool calls at all."

---

## Impact

| Scenario | Duration | Visible symptom |
|---|---|---|
| LLM API stalls (Bug 1) | 10–30 min (httpx timeout × retries) | frozen, no tool calls, no exit |
| Tool raises exception (Bug 3 + Bug 2) | ~60 s | frozen 60 s, then empty result |
| Both combined | 30 min + 60 s | effectively permanent freeze |

---

## Proposed Fixes

All fixes belong in **spaik-sdk**.

### Fix 1 — `base_agent.py` / `sync_adapter.py`: bound the LLM API call

The `t.join()` in `run_isolated()` must be bounded. The right lever is a
per-API-call `timeout` on `ChatOpenAI`/`ChatAnthropic`, not a blanket subagent
timeout (which would penalise legitimate long-running work). Setting the httpx
`read` timeout to something like 120 s on the `ChatOpenAI` instance means a
single hanging API call errors out quickly, while a complex subagent that makes
many calls can still run for as long as it needs.

```python
# openai_provider.py (or AnthropicProvider equivalent)
return ChatOpenAI(**full_config, timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=5.0))
```

Additionally, `max_retries` should be reduced for streaming requests — three
attempts at 120 s each is 6 minutes, which is still a long freeze.

### Fix 2 — `sync_adapter.py`: add `await asyncio.sleep()` in the polling loop

```python
async def wait_for_completion_async(self, timeout: float = 30.0):
    start_time = time.time()
    while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
        if self._streaming_ended or not self.container.is_streaming_active():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)   # ← yield to event loop between checks
    return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
```

Without this, every error that does slip through (including timeouts from Fix 1)
adds another 60 s of seized event loop.

### Fix 3 — `langchain_service.py`: use `handle_tool_errors=True`

```python
from langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node import ToolNode

def create_executor(self, tools: list[BaseTool]):
    tool_node = ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)
    return create_react_agent(self._get_model(), tool_node)
```

With `handle_tool_errors=True`, all runtime tool exceptions become
`ToolMessage(status="error")` objects. The LLM sees the error and can retry,
skip, or report rather than the agent crashing entirely.

---

## Files to Change

| File | Location | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `openai_provider.py` / `anthropic_provider.py` | spaik-sdk | add `timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=5.0)` to model creation |
| `sync_adapter.py` | spaik-sdk | `wait_for_completion_async` — add `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` in loop |
| `langchain_service.py` | spaik-sdk | `create_executor` — use `ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)` |

# fix(streaming): prevent duplicate tool_use events from overwriting tool_call_args

## Problem

`tool_call_args` was always `{}` in `BlockAdded` SSE events, even when tools clearly ran with arguments. This made the UI unable to show what parameters the agent called tools with.

## Root Cause

`on_chain_end` calls `_collect_final_tool_calls` and re-emits `TOOL_USE` events for every tool — including ones already processed during streaming. These duplicate emissions use `message.tool_calls`, which often has empty args `{}` at that point. The empty args then overwrote the correct args that were set during the initial streaming phase via `_handle_ai_message`.

PR #56 addressed a related symptom (preserving `tool_call_response`/`tool_call_error` during block upserts in `thread_container.py`) but did not stop the duplicate emissions themselves.

## Fix

Track which tool IDs and their args have been processed during streaming. In `on_chain_end`, only re-emit `TOOL_USE` for a tool if:

1. It was not seen during streaming at all (tool call only in final message), OR
2. It was seen during streaming but with empty args `{}`, and `on_chain_end` has non-empty args (upgrade scenario)

This preserves the legitimate use-case where `on_chain_end` provides complete args that streaming didn't have, while preventing empty args from clobbering correct ones.

## Changes

- **`streaming_event_handler.py`**: Added `_processed_tool_ids` and `_tool_args_by_id` tracking; logic in `on_chain_end` to skip or allow re-emission based on whether args are an upgrade
- **`examples/backend/main.py`**: Added `search_web(query, limit)` tool to `DemoTool` for easy manual verification

## Testing

- All 247 unit tests pass
- Manually verified with spaik-sdk example backend: `search_web` consistently shows `{"query": "...", "limit": N}` in all `BlockAdded` events
- Verified in consumer project (was the original reporter): `tool_call_args` now shows full query strings and limit values instead of `{}`

## Related

Closes #53  
Builds on #56 (block upsert logic in `thread_container.py` is preserved and complementary)

# Fix subagent silent-death from tool errors and event-loop starvation (#61)

Closes #61 (partial — bugs 2 and 3 only; see "Out of scope" below).

## Summary

Two independent bugs in `spaik-sdk` combined to make subagents look frozen
when anything went wrong during a run. Both are fixed here; both have
regression tests that would fail against the old code.

### Bug — runtime tool exceptions escape the agent loop

`LangChainService.create_executor` used `create_react_agent(model, tools)`
with no `ToolNode` configuration, which picks up LangGraph's default error
handler. That handler only catches argument-validation errors and
re-raises everything else — a content-filter 4xx, `urllib.error.HTTPError`,
`ConnectionError`, or any raised exception from a tool propagates out of
the graph and kills the agent loop. The LLM never sees the error and
never gets a chance to retry or recover. On a subagent this also means
the parent agent's `spawn` call dies with `ValueError("No response
received")` and no useful diagnostics.

Wrap tools in `ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)` so runtime tool
exceptions become `ToolMessage(status="error")` the LLM can react to.

Reproduction (minimal LangGraph, no LLM call needed):

```
Default ToolNode          : raised ConnectionError: boom: 1
handle_tool_errors=True   : ToolMessage status=error content="Error: ConnectionError('boom: 1')\n Please fix your mistakes."
```

### Bug — `SyncAdapter.wait_for_completion_async` seizes the event loop

The polling loop had no `await` on the not-ready branch, so while
streaming was still active the coroutine spun on `time.time()` without
yielding. Because `get_response_async` calls this method twice (once
from `run_async`, once directly) this added up to 60s of frozen event
loop on top of any upstream error that ended streaming early.

Adding `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` in the loop lets other coroutines
(including the one watching for cancellation) make progress while we
wait.

Reproduction — a sibling coroutine ticking every 5ms alongside a
0.5s `wait_for_completion_async`:

```
Before fix: elapsed=0.500s ticks_during_wait=0    (event loop starved)
After  fix: elapsed=0.507s ticks_during_wait=92   (event loop free)
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `spaik_sdk/llm/langchain_service.py` | Wrap tools in `ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)` before passing to `create_react_agent`. |
| `spaik_sdk/thread/adapters/sync_adapter.py` | `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` at the end of the polling loop body. |
| `tests/unit/spaik_sdk/llm/test_langchain_service_tool_errors.py` | New — asserts `create_executor` wires `ToolNode` with `handle_tool_errors=True`. |
| `tests/unit/spaik_sdk/thread/adapters/test_sync_adapter.py` | New — asserts the poll yields to the event loop while streaming is active, and returns promptly once streaming ends. |

## Out of scope (deliberately not in this PR)

The reporter's "Bug 1" (unbounded `t.join()` in `BaseAgent.run_isolated`
combined with a 600s httpx read timeout and 2 retries) is real but
**not** fixed here. The proposed mitigation — setting a 120s request
timeout on `ChatOpenAI`/`ChatAnthropic` — would be measured per-chunk,
not per-call, and while that's enough for the streaming agent path it
caps `get_structured_response` (which uses `.invoke()`) at 120s total.
More importantly, a blanket HTTP-layer timeout conflates "stalled
socket" with "model is taking its time on a hard task." The right
layer for that fix is `run_isolated` itself (e.g. a bounded
`t.join(timeout=...)` with a generous wall clock), which will be
handled separately.

## Verification

- `make lint` — clean
- `make typecheck` — clean
- `make test-unit` — 265 passed
- Bug 2 reproducer: 0 ticks (before) vs 92 ticks (after) during a 0.5s poll
- Bug 3 reproducer: `ConnectionError` escapes graph (before) vs `ToolMessage(status="error")` (after)

## Risk

Low. Both changes are narrowly scoped:

- `ToolNode(handle_tool_errors=True)` changes the format the LLM sees
  when a tool raises — the LLM is now told about the error instead of
  the stream dying. Existing tests for the tool-call happy path are
  unaffected (all 265 unit tests still pass).
- The extra `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` only adds up to ~10ms of
  latency before `wait_for_completion_async` notices that streaming
  has ended; the existing 100ms "finalize" sleep in the ready branch
  is unchanged.

# fix(thread): emit BlockFullyAddedEvent for tool-use blocks

## Problem

Local traces silently dropped every tool call. A run with three `calculator` invocations only showed reasoning and the final assistant message — no `🔧: calculator {...}` lines. This also affected any other `BlockFullyAddedEvent` subscriber, not just `AgentTrace`.

## Root cause

Four different call sites in `ThreadContainer` were independently responsible for the "block finishes streaming" transition, and they disagreed on the contract:

| Site | Flipped `streaming=False`? | Emitted `BlockFullyAddedEvent`? |
|---|---|---|
| `finalize_streaming_blocks` | yes (guarded on `streaming=True`) | yes |
| `add_tool_call_response` | yes (direct mutation) | **no** |
| `update_tool_use_block_with_response` | yes (redundant duplicate of the above) | no |
| `cancel_generation` | yes (direct mutation) | yes (but also for already-completed blocks) |

Because the tool-response path flipped the flag eagerly without emitting the event, the later `COMPLETE` → `finalize_streaming_blocks` saw `streaming=False` and skipped the block. The invariant "streaming → done = exactly one `BlockFullyAddedEvent`" was implicit and unenforced, which is why this regressed silently.

## Fix

Introduce a single private helper `_mark_block_complete(message_id, block)` that owns the transition — idempotent, flushes `streaming_content`, emits `BlockFullyAddedEvent` exactly once. Every call site now goes through it. `update_tool_use_block_with_response` collapses into a thin wrapper over `add_tool_call_response` since the extra mutation loop was pure duplication.

Second commit is a boyscout pass on the same file to strip narrative comments and thin docstrings, aligned with the repo's own style rules.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit: `add_tool_call_response` emits `BlockFullyAddedEvent` with response data on the block

# OpenAI 400: `parallel_tool_calls` sent without `tools` (breaks `gpt-4.1-mini` structured outputs)

## Summary
When using OpenAI models (observed with `gpt-4.1-mini`) the request can fail with:

> Error code: 400 - `{'error': {'message': "Invalid value for 'parallel_tool_calls': 'parallel_tool_calls' is only allowed when 'tools' are specified.", ...}}`

This happens when the SDK config enables tool usage globally, but the specific request path does **not** include `tools` (e.g. structured output / schema validation flows).

## Where this comes from in the SDK
`OpenAIModelFactory.get_model_specific_config()` sets `model_kwargs={"parallel_tool_calls": True}` whenever `LLMConfig.tool_usage` is true:

- File: `packages/agent-sdk/spaik_sdk/models/factories/openai_factory.py`
- Logic: `if config.tool_usage: model_config["model_kwargs"] = {"parallel_tool_calls": True}`

This is applied at model construction time, not at call time.

## Why it fails
Some LangChain call paths (notably structured output via `with_structured_output(...)`) invoke the model without passing `tools` in the request. OpenAI rejects `parallel_tool_calls` unless the request also includes `tools`.

So the SDK ends up sending:
- `parallel_tool_calls=true`
- `tools` omitted

…which is invalid per OpenAI API validation.

## Reproduction (minimal)
Any app using `spaik-sdk` where:

- The agent has tools (so `LLMConfig.tool_usage` becomes true), and
- A request is made via structured output (`with_structured_output` / schema validation) that does not attach tools.

Observed downstream:
- Availability Scout “shortage agent”
- Model: `gpt-4.1-mini`
- Failure observed during structured output / schema validation calls.

## Expected behavior
Requests without `tools` should succeed and must not include tool-only parameters like `parallel_tool_calls`.

## Actual behavior
OpenAI returns 400 and the agent run fails.

## Suggested fix (minimal)
Ensure `parallel_tool_calls` is only set when **tools are actually specified on the request**.

Options (pick one):
- **Option A (factory-side guard)**: Don’t set `parallel_tool_calls` for structured output calls (or other non-tool requests).
- **Option B (call-site behavior)**: Only add `parallel_tool_calls` when tools are bound / present (e.g. when using `model.bind_tools(...)` or equivalent).
- **Option C (config contract)**: Ensure “structured response config” disables tool usage so tool-only kwargs aren’t added.

## Notes
- This is not model-specific in principle; `gpt-4.1-mini` is just where it was observed first.
- The error message is returned by OpenAI request validation and is consistent with the API requirement that `parallel_tool_calls` is only allowed with `tools`.

## Summary

When using a reasoning-capable OpenAI model (e.g. `gpt-5.2`) via the Responses API, reasoning summary blocks are silently dropped — they never appear in traces or the frontend UI.

## Root cause

In `spaik_sdk/llm/streaming/streaming_event_handler.py`, `_handle_ai_message` extracts reasoning text like this:

```python
elif block_type in ("reasoning", "thinking", "reasoning_summary"):
    reasoning = block.get("reasoning", "") or block.get("thinking", "") or block.get("text", "")
```

OpenAI's Responses API streaming emits reasoning blocks in this shape:

```json
{
  "type": "reasoning",
  "id": "rs_...",
  "summary": [{ "type": "summary_text", "text": "actual reasoning text" }]
}
```

None of `block["reasoning"]`, `block["thinking"]`, or `block["text"]` exist on this dict — the text is nested under `summary[0]["text"]`. The extraction silently returns `""`, so no reasoning block content is ever stored or traced.

PR #68 (`fix(agent-sdk): stream OpenAI reasoning summaries`, merged 2026-04-30) added `"reasoning_summary"` to the recognized types and added `block.get("text", "")` as a fallback, but this only covers a flat `{"type": "reasoning_summary", "text": "..."}` shape. The actual streaming shape OpenAI emits is the nested `summary[]` structure above — so the bug persists in `0.9.3`.

## Impact

- Traces contain no `🧠:` entries for reasoning models
- Frontend shows no reasoning content (it would render as empty markdown)

## Fix

In `streaming_event_handler.py`, add extraction from the nested `summary` list:

```python
elif block_type in ("reasoning", "thinking", "reasoning_summary"):
    reasoning = (
        block.get("reasoning", "")
        or block.get("thinking", "")
        or block.get("text", "")
        or "".join(
            s.get("text", "")
            for s in (block.get("summary") or [])
            if isinstance(s, dict)
        )
    )
```

## Environment

- `spaik-sdk` version: `0.9.3`
- Model: `gpt-5.2` (any OpenAI reasoning model using Responses API)
