This applies the ten open Dependabot PRs (#89–#98) and the remaining updates their next run would open, so main starts the 1.0 release candidates with nothing outdated. Two changes are breaking for SDK users, and both are in the migration guide: Zustand 5 in `spaik-sdk-react`, and MCP SDK 2 behind the `mcp` extra. `bun audit`, `npm audit` on the template and pip-audit across all extras each report 0.

## Runtime dependencies

`spaik-sdk-react` moves to ag-ui 1.0.2, zod 4 and Zustand 5. zod 4 stays internal, because the schemas are not exported; `BaseApiClient` adopts its `ZodType<Output, Input>` signature. Material moves to react-markdown 10, whose only breaking change is a `className` prop that Material does not pass.

## MCP

`langchain-mcp-adapters` caps `mcp` below 2 and is superseded upstream by `langchain.mcp`. The `mcp` extra now installs `langchain[mcp]` (fastmcp 4, mcp 2), and `McpToolProvider` builds on `MCPAdapter`. Its public API is unchanged. One adapter per server keeps tool names unprefixed, and tools from `load_from_stdio` stay callable after loading. `langchain.mcp` is beta upstream; the provider suppresses its beta warning, since users never import it directly. The integration tests run a local MCP SDK 2 echo server over stdio and streamable HTTP and cover env passing and multi-server tool names.

## Python

The lock is upgraded within `pyproject.toml`, covering the python-minor-patch group, and `ty` is pinned to 0.0.87. The stricter `ty` found type errors, fixed in `efd19dc`. One was real: `BaseOrchestrator.step()` was typed with the state type, so the documented pattern of re-yielding its events from `run()` failed type checking. It now yields `OrchestratorEvent[Any]`, like the event factory methods.

## Frontend toolchain

All four lint setups (hooks, Material, example and template) move to ESLint 10 flat config. eslint-plugin-react stops at ESLint 9, so hooks and Material use `@eslint-react` instead. Its React 19-only rules are off because both packages support React 18, and Material keeps index keys for its positional lists. react-hooks 7 flagged three effects that set state synchronously. `useThread` and `useThreadList` now set state only when the request settles, and `AgentThemeProvider` reads the colour scheme through `useSyncExternalStore`. TypeScript moves to 6.0, and hooks switches `moduleResolution` from `node` to `bundler`, matching Material. The example and template move to Vite 8 and plugin-react 6, and the template README now gives the Node versions Vite 8 needs. GitHub Actions move to checkout, setup-uv and setup-node v7.

## Checks

Locally on Python 3.13, ruff, ty, 175 unit and 10 integration tests pass. The full suite also passes on Python 3.11. For the frontend, lint, type-check and builds pass for every package, and so do the hooks tests. The template also passes lint, build and `npm audit` when installed outside the repo. The Playwright tests passed after each runtime change up to react-markdown. The final TypeScript commit was checked by type-check and builds only, because local ports were taken, so CI's browser run covers it.

## Follow-ups

`dependabot.yml` skips TypeScript 6.1 and later until typescript-eslint supports it; TypeScript 7 is out. Dependabot should close #89–#98 once this merges.

* **New Features**
  * MCP tool providers support both stdio and streamable HTTP servers, including optional headers and environment settings.
  * Orchestration steps support any awaitable result, not just coroutine results.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Thread and thread-list loading now handle stale requests and errors more reliably.
  * Streamed tool-call updates are matched to assistant messages.

* **Documentation**

## Summary

- Adds proxy mode (`LLM_AUTH_MODE=proxy`) allowing all LLM provider traffic to route through a single proxy endpoint, configured via `LLM_PROXY_BASE_URL`, `LLM_PROXY_API_KEY`, and `LLM_PROXY_HEADERS` environment variables.
- Introduces `_get_proxy_config()` in `BaseProvider` that maps proxy settings to each provider's LangChain-specific parameter names (e.g. `anthropic_api_key`, `google_api_key`, `xai_api_base`).
- All 9 providers (Anthropic, Azure, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Ollama, OpenAI, XAI) support proxy mode with graceful fallback — direct mode remains the default and API keys are now optional when absent.
- Includes 32 unit tests covering `EnvConfig` proxy methods and proxy/direct mode behavior across all providers.

## Motivation

In enterprise and self-hosted deployments, it's common to route all LLM API calls through a centralized proxy (e.g. LiteLLM, custom gateway) for auth, rate limiting, cost tracking, or compliance. Today each provider requires its own API key and base URL, making proxy setups require per-provider env var overrides. This change introduces a single, unified proxy configuration that works across all providers.

## Changes

| Area | Files | What |
|------|-------|------|
| Config | `config/env.py`, `config/credentials_provider.py` | New proxy env methods (`is_proxy_mode`, `get_proxy_base_url`, `get_proxy_api_key`, `get_proxy_headers`); provider key no longer required |
| Base | `providers/base_provider.py` | `_get_proxy_config()` helper mapping proxy env to provider-specific LangChain kwargs |
| Providers | All 9 provider files | `get_model_config()` checks proxy mode first; direct mode now tolerates missing API keys |
| Tests | `tests/.../config/test_env_proxy.py` | 13 tests for `EnvConfig` proxy methods (defaults, parsing, edge cases) |
| Tests | `tests/.../providers/test_proxy_support.py` | 19 tests for proxy/direct mode across all providers |

## Configuration

| Env Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LLM_AUTH_MODE` | `direct` | Set to `proxy` to enable proxy routing |
| `LLM_PROXY_BASE_URL` | _(empty)_ | Proxy endpoint URL |
| `LLM_PROXY_API_KEY` | _(empty)_ | Auth key sent to proxy |
| `LLM_PROXY_HEADERS` | _(empty)_ | Comma-separated `Key:Value` pairs for extra headers |

## Test plan

- [x] All 32 new unit tests pass

## Summary

Adds support for Azure AI Foundry **project endpoints** (`https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}`), which fail with classic `AzureChatOpenAI` (e.g. `API version not supported`).

**Closes #41**

- New `AzureFoundryProvider` using `AzureAIOpenAIApiChatModel` (`langchain-azure-ai`)
- `ProviderType` split: `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure` → classic OpenAI-on-Azure; `MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry` → Foundry project API
- Shared `azure_deployments.py` for deployment env map and helpers used by both Azure providers
- Documentation and unit tests

No URL auto-detection — use `MODEL_PROVIDER` or `LLMConfig(provider=...)`.

## Breaking change

| Before | After |
|--------|--------|
| `azure` and `foundry` aliases both used classic `AzureProvider` | `azure` → `AzureProvider` (`AzureChatOpenAI`) |
| `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure_ai_foundry` selected classic Azure | `azure_ai_foundry` / `foundry` → `AzureFoundryProvider` |

Classic `*.openai.azure.com` deployments: keep `MODEL_PROVIDER=azure`.  
Foundry project URLs: use `MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry`.

## Usage

```bash
MODEL_PROVIDER=foundry
AZURE_FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT=https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}

## feat: incremental thread checkpointing during streaming

### Problem

`ThreadJobProcessor` only persisted the thread to storage after the entire streaming run completed. Any interruption mid-run — server restart, hot-reload, crash, timeout — wiped the full response. A 90-minute multi-tool run killed at 89 minutes lost everything.

### Solution

Checkpoint the thread to storage after each completed tool result and each completed message, so in-progress state survives interruptions.

### Changes

**`server/response/response_generator.py`**  
Added `OnCheckpoint` type alias and `on_checkpoint` optional parameter to the `ResponseGenerator` ABC.

**`server/response/agent_response_generator.py`**  
After each event from the agent stream, fires `on_checkpoint` if the event is a `ToolResponseReceivedEvent` or `MessageFullyAddedEvent` — the two natural "durable state" boundaries: tool result just landed, or a full message was finalized.

**`server/job_processor/thread_job_processor.py`**  
Wires a local `on_checkpoint` coroutine that calls `update_thread` into `stream_response`. The final `update_thread` after the loop is kept for clean-completion saves.

### Tests

- **5 unit tests** (`test_agent_response_generator.py`) — checkpoint fires on the right event types, once per event, silent when `None`
- **4 unit tests** (`test_thread_job_processor.py`) — `update_thread` call count, `on_complete` wiring, 404 handling
- **1 integration test** (`test_thread_checkpointing.py`) — runs a real recorded tool-calling agent through the full stack and asserts `save_thread` is called ≥ 2 times (at least one mid-run checkpoint + the final save)

# fix(streaming): prevent duplicate tool_use events from overwriting tool_call_args

## Problem

`tool_call_args` was always `{}` in `BlockAdded` SSE events, even when tools clearly ran with arguments. This made the UI unable to show what parameters the agent called tools with.

## Root Cause

`on_chain_end` calls `_collect_final_tool_calls` and re-emits `TOOL_USE` events for every tool — including ones already processed during streaming. These duplicate emissions use `message.tool_calls`, which often has empty args `{}` at that point. The empty args then overwrote the correct args that were set during the initial streaming phase via `_handle_ai_message`.

PR #56 addressed a related symptom (preserving `tool_call_response`/`tool_call_error` during block upserts in `thread_container.py`) but did not stop the duplicate emissions themselves.

## Fix

Track which tool IDs and their args have been processed during streaming. In `on_chain_end`, only re-emit `TOOL_USE` for a tool if:

1. It was not seen during streaming at all (tool call only in final message), OR
2. It was seen during streaming but with empty args `{}`, and `on_chain_end` has non-empty args (upgrade scenario)

This preserves the legitimate use-case where `on_chain_end` provides complete args that streaming didn't have, while preventing empty args from clobbering correct ones.

## Changes

- **`streaming_event_handler.py`**: Added `_processed_tool_ids` and `_tool_args_by_id` tracking; logic in `on_chain_end` to skip or allow re-emission based on whether args are an upgrade
- **`examples/backend/main.py`**: Added `search_web(query, limit)` tool to `DemoTool` for easy manual verification

## Testing

- All 247 unit tests pass
- Manually verified with spaik-sdk example backend: `search_web` consistently shows `{"query": "...", "limit": N}` in all `BlockAdded` events
- Verified in consumer project (was the original reporter): `tool_call_args` now shows full query strings and limit values instead of `{}`

## Related

Closes #53  
Builds on #56 (block upsert logic in `thread_container.py` is preserved and complementary)

# Fix subagent silent-death from tool errors and event-loop starvation (#61)

Closes #61 (partial — bugs 2 and 3 only; see "Out of scope" below).

## Summary

Two independent bugs in `spaik-sdk` combined to make subagents look frozen
when anything went wrong during a run. Both are fixed here; both have
regression tests that would fail against the old code.

### Bug — runtime tool exceptions escape the agent loop

`LangChainService.create_executor` used `create_react_agent(model, tools)`
with no `ToolNode` configuration, which picks up LangGraph's default error
handler. That handler only catches argument-validation errors and
re-raises everything else — a content-filter 4xx, `urllib.error.HTTPError`,
`ConnectionError`, or any raised exception from a tool propagates out of
the graph and kills the agent loop. The LLM never sees the error and
never gets a chance to retry or recover. On a subagent this also means
the parent agent's `spawn` call dies with `ValueError("No response
received")` and no useful diagnostics.

Wrap tools in `ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)` so runtime tool
exceptions become `ToolMessage(status="error")` the LLM can react to.

Reproduction (minimal LangGraph, no LLM call needed):

```
Default ToolNode          : raised ConnectionError: boom: 1
handle_tool_errors=True   : ToolMessage status=error content="Error: ConnectionError('boom: 1')\n Please fix your mistakes."
```

### Bug — `SyncAdapter.wait_for_completion_async` seizes the event loop

The polling loop had no `await` on the not-ready branch, so while
streaming was still active the coroutine spun on `time.time()` without
yielding. Because `get_response_async` calls this method twice (once
from `run_async`, once directly) this added up to 60s of frozen event
loop on top of any upstream error that ended streaming early.

Adding `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` in the loop lets other coroutines
(including the one watching for cancellation) make progress while we
wait.

Reproduction — a sibling coroutine ticking every 5ms alongside a
0.5s `wait_for_completion_async`:

```
Before fix: elapsed=0.500s ticks_during_wait=0    (event loop starved)
After  fix: elapsed=0.507s ticks_during_wait=92   (event loop free)
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `spaik_sdk/llm/langchain_service.py` | Wrap tools in `ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)` before passing to `create_react_agent`. |
| `spaik_sdk/thread/adapters/sync_adapter.py` | `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` at the end of the polling loop body. |
| `tests/unit/spaik_sdk/llm/test_langchain_service_tool_errors.py` | New — asserts `create_executor` wires `ToolNode` with `handle_tool_errors=True`. |
| `tests/unit/spaik_sdk/thread/adapters/test_sync_adapter.py` | New — asserts the poll yields to the event loop while streaming is active, and returns promptly once streaming ends. |

## Out of scope (deliberately not in this PR)

The reporter's "Bug 1" (unbounded `t.join()` in `BaseAgent.run_isolated`
combined with a 600s httpx read timeout and 2 retries) is real but
**not** fixed here. The proposed mitigation — setting a 120s request
timeout on `ChatOpenAI`/`ChatAnthropic` — would be measured per-chunk,
not per-call, and while that's enough for the streaming agent path it
caps `get_structured_response` (which uses `.invoke()`) at 120s total.
More importantly, a blanket HTTP-layer timeout conflates "stalled
socket" with "model is taking its time on a hard task." The right
layer for that fix is `run_isolated` itself (e.g. a bounded
`t.join(timeout=...)` with a generous wall clock), which will be
handled separately.

## Verification

- `make lint` — clean
- `make typecheck` — clean
- `make test-unit` — 265 passed
- Bug 2 reproducer: 0 ticks (before) vs 92 ticks (after) during a 0.5s poll
- Bug 3 reproducer: `ConnectionError` escapes graph (before) vs `ToolMessage(status="error")` (after)

## Risk

Low. Both changes are narrowly scoped:

- `ToolNode(handle_tool_errors=True)` changes the format the LLM sees
  when a tool raises — the LLM is now told about the error instead of
  the stream dying. Existing tests for the tool-call happy path are
  unaffected (all 265 unit tests still pass).
- The extra `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` only adds up to ~10ms of
  latency before `wait_for_completion_async` notices that streaming
  has ended; the existing 100ms "finalize" sleep in the ready branch
  is unchanged.

# fix(thread): emit BlockFullyAddedEvent for tool-use blocks

## Problem

Local traces silently dropped every tool call. A run with three `calculator` invocations only showed reasoning and the final assistant message — no `🔧: calculator {...}` lines. This also affected any other `BlockFullyAddedEvent` subscriber, not just `AgentTrace`.

## Root cause

Four different call sites in `ThreadContainer` were independently responsible for the "block finishes streaming" transition, and they disagreed on the contract:

| Site | Flipped `streaming=False`? | Emitted `BlockFullyAddedEvent`? |
|---|---|---|
| `finalize_streaming_blocks` | yes (guarded on `streaming=True`) | yes |
| `add_tool_call_response` | yes (direct mutation) | **no** |
| `update_tool_use_block_with_response` | yes (redundant duplicate of the above) | no |
| `cancel_generation` | yes (direct mutation) | yes (but also for already-completed blocks) |

Because the tool-response path flipped the flag eagerly without emitting the event, the later `COMPLETE` → `finalize_streaming_blocks` saw `streaming=False` and skipped the block. The invariant "streaming → done = exactly one `BlockFullyAddedEvent`" was implicit and unenforced, which is why this regressed silently.

## Fix

Introduce a single private helper `_mark_block_complete(message_id, block)` that owns the transition — idempotent, flushes `streaming_content`, emits `BlockFullyAddedEvent` exactly once. Every call site now goes through it. `update_tool_use_block_with_response` collapses into a thin wrapper over `add_tool_call_response` since the extra mutation loop was pure duplication.

Second commit is a boyscout pass on the same file to strip narrative comments and thin docstrings, aligned with the repo's own style rules.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit: `add_tool_call_response` emits `BlockFullyAddedEvent` with response data on the block
- [x] New unit: `finalize_streaming_blocks` is idempotent for already-completed tool blocks (no double emit)
- [x] New unit: end-to-end — drive a tool-call lifecycle through `ThreadContainer` into an `AgentTrace` subscriber and assert `🔧: calculator {...}` shows up in the rendered trace
- [x] `make lint-fix && make typecheck && make test-unit` — 268 passed, 0 failed

## Scope / risk

- `thread_container.py` internal refactor, no public API changes beyond `update_tool_use_block_with_response` now delegating (same signature, same semantics)
- `BlockFullyAddedEvent` now fires for tool-use blocks for the first time. Any subscriber that previously relied on never receiving it for tool blocks would be affected — none found in repo (trace + UI hooks were already the intended consumers)

## Problem

When a tool spawns a nested `BaseAgent` using `asyncio.run()`, the subagent inherits the calling coroutine's `contextvars` context. LangChain stores its active callback handlers there, so the subagent's tool calls get routed through the parent's `MessageHandler` and bleed into the parent thread — cluttering the UI and breaking the "subagent in a box" pattern.

## Solution

Two new methods on `BaseAgent`:

- **`spawn(task, attachments=None) → ThreadMessage`** — the primary API. Runs the subagent as an isolated call, preventing callback context from leaking. Drop-in replacement for `asyncio.run(sub.get_response_async(task))` inside a tool.
- **`BaseAgent.run_isolated(coro) → Any`** — static helper for the rare case where you need to isolate an arbitrary coroutine rather than a full agent response.

The fix works by running the coroutine in a fresh OS thread with a blank `contextvars.Context()`. A blank context has no inherited `ContextVar` values, so LangChain's callbacks are absent and the subagent's events stay inside its own `ThreadContainer`.

## Changes

- `spaik_sdk/agent/base_agent.py` — `spawn()` + `run_isolated()` added
- `examples/agents/subagent_example.py` — runnable demo: MainAgent → tool → SubAgent with echo tool, asserts only `spawn_sub` appears in parent thread
- `tests/unit/spaik_sdk/agent/test_base_agent.py` — `TestRunIsolated` class with 5 tests:
  - ContextVar set in parent is not visible inside `run_isolated`
  - Return value passes through correctly
  - Exceptions propagate out of the isolated run
  - `spawn()` doesn't leak parent ContextVar into the subagent (the exact bug scenario)
  - Concurrent `run_isolated` calls don't interfere
- `packages/agent-sdk/README.md` — new Subagents section
- `AGENTS.md` — `spawn()` added to Agent Methods list

## Usage

```python
class ResearchTools(ToolProvider):
    def get_tools(self) -> list[BaseTool]:
        @tool
        def research(topic: str) -> str:
            """Delegate to a specialist subagent."""
            sub = ResearchAgent(system_prompt="You are a research specialist.")
            return sub.spawn(topic).get_text_content()
        return [research]
```

# Issue: Subagents freeze indefinitely and never wake up

## Summary

Subagents occasionally get completely stuck — no tool calls, no findings, no
exit — and the orchestrator waits forever. Two separate bugs in spaik-sdk
interact. The primary cause is an unbounded LLM API hang that is never
interrupted. A secondary bug then adds 60 seconds of frozen event loop on top
of any error that does escape. Together they produce what looks like a permanent
freeze.

---

## Observed Behaviour

- Subagent starts (frontend shows "Running…"), never makes a single tool call.
- Orchestrator stalls indefinitely — no forward progress, no error reported.
- Restarting the backend is the only recovery path.

---

## Root Cause

### Bug 1 (primary) — LLM API hang is never interrupted

`spawn_subagent` calls `subagent.spawn(task)` which lands in
`BaseAgent.run_isolated()`:

```python
# spaik_sdk/agent/base_agent.py
t = threading.Thread(target=_thread)
t.start()
t.join()           # ← no timeout, ever
```

`_thread` calls `asyncio.run(get_response_async())`. If the HTTP connection to
the LLM API goes silent mid-stream (stale TCP connection, transient server
issue, etc.), `httpx` waits up to its `read` timeout per chunk — **600 seconds
by default** in the OpenAI SDK. The default `max_retries=2` means the SDK
silently retries up to twice:

```
3 attempts × 600 s read timeout = up to 30 minutes
```

Nothing in the spaik-sdk call chain can interrupt this. `t.join()` has no
timeout. The orchestrator's executor thread is held for the entire duration.
From the user's perspective: the subagent freezes and **never wakes up**.

This is the case where no tool calls appear — the agent dies before the first
LLM response is even received.

### Bug 2 (secondary) — `SyncAdapter.wait_for_completion_async()` CPU-spins for 60 s after any error

When the agent stream dies early (whether from a tool exception, an API
timeout, or any other error), blocks that were started with `streaming=True`
are never finalized. `SyncAdapter` is then called:

```python
# spaik_sdk/thread/adapters/sync_adapter.py
async def wait_for_completion_async(self, timeout: float = 30.0):
    start_time = time.time()
    while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
        if self._streaming_ended or not self.container.is_streaming_active():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
        # ← NO await in the else-branch
        # ← event loop is fully seized, nothing can happen for up to 30 s
    return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
```

It is called **twice** in the normal flow — once in `run_async()` (30 s) and
once in `get_response_async()` (30 s) — adding exactly **60 seconds** of dead
time on top of any upstream error.

### Bug 3 (contributing) — LangGraph `ToolNode` default handler re-raises all runtime tool exceptions

`LangChainService.create_executor()` uses `create_react_agent` without setting
`handle_tool_errors`, so `ToolNode` is created with the library default
`_default_handle_tool_errors`:

```python
# langgraph/prebuilt/tool_node.py  (LangGraph 1.1.3)
def _default_handle_tool_errors(e: Exception) -> str:
    if isinstance(e, ToolInvocationError):   # only arg-validation errors
        return e.message
    raise e                                  # everything else re-raised
```

Any runtime tool exception (`urllib.error.HTTPError`, `OSError`,
`ConnectionError`, HTTP 4xx from the LLM API itself such as a content filter
response, …) propagates out of LangGraph and crashes the agent loop.
The LLM never gets a chance to see the error and recover. Combined with Bug 2,
this turns a recoverable tool failure into a 60-second frozen subagent.

This bug affects both the subagent executor and the **main agent's** executor.
When a subagent spawn fails (raising `ValueError("No response received")`), that
exception escapes the main agent's ToolNode too — killing the entire
orchestration rather than letting the main LLM decide to retry or skip the step.

---

## Evidence from diagnostic run (`diagnose_subagents.py`)

Subagent 6 hit a 403 from DuckDuckGo, demonstrating Bug 2 + Bug 3 together:

```
[+409s]  SUBAGENT 6 starts
[+429s]  ERROR - langchain_service.py:210 - Error executing agent: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden
                ↑ Bug 3: exception escapes ToolNode instead of returning to LLM
[+429s–487s]  ← 58 s of SyncAdapter busy-wait (Bug 2: 30 s + 30 s)
[+487s]  SUBAGENT 6 OK  tool_calls=0  text_blocks=0
```

The truly indefinite freeze (Bug 1) was not hit in this run because the LLM API
responded promptly. It manifests when a connection stalls mid-stream, most
often on the first LLM call — which is why users see "no tool calls at all."

---

## Impact

| Scenario | Duration | Visible symptom |
|---|---|---|
| LLM API stalls (Bug 1) | 10–30 min (httpx timeout × retries) | frozen, no tool calls, no exit |
| Tool raises exception (Bug 3 + Bug 2) | ~60 s | frozen 60 s, then empty result |
| Both combined | 30 min + 60 s | effectively permanent freeze |

---

## Proposed Fixes

All fixes belong in **spaik-sdk**.

### Fix 1 — `base_agent.py` / `sync_adapter.py`: bound the LLM API call

The `t.join()` in `run_isolated()` must be bounded. The right lever is a
per-API-call `timeout` on `ChatOpenAI`/`ChatAnthropic`, not a blanket subagent
timeout (which would penalise legitimate long-running work). Setting the httpx
`read` timeout to something like 120 s on the `ChatOpenAI` instance means a
single hanging API call errors out quickly, while a complex subagent that makes
many calls can still run for as long as it needs.

```python
# openai_provider.py (or AnthropicProvider equivalent)
return ChatOpenAI(**full_config, timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=5.0))
```

Additionally, `max_retries` should be reduced for streaming requests — three
attempts at 120 s each is 6 minutes, which is still a long freeze.

### Fix 2 — `sync_adapter.py`: add `await asyncio.sleep()` in the polling loop

```python
async def wait_for_completion_async(self, timeout: float = 30.0):
    start_time = time.time()
    while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
        if self._streaming_ended or not self.container.is_streaming_active():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)   # ← yield to event loop between checks
    return self.container.get_latest_ai_message()
```

Without this, every error that does slip through (including timeouts from Fix 1)
adds another 60 s of seized event loop.

### Fix 3 — `langchain_service.py`: use `handle_tool_errors=True`

```python
from langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node import ToolNode

def create_executor(self, tools: list[BaseTool]):
    tool_node = ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)
    return create_react_agent(self._get_model(), tool_node)
```

With `handle_tool_errors=True`, all runtime tool exceptions become
`ToolMessage(status="error")` objects. The LLM sees the error and can retry,
skip, or report rather than the agent crashing entirely.

---

## Files to Change

| File | Location | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `openai_provider.py` / `anthropic_provider.py` | spaik-sdk | add `timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=5.0)` to model creation |
| `sync_adapter.py` | spaik-sdk | `wait_for_completion_async` — add `await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` in loop |
| `langchain_service.py` | spaik-sdk | `create_executor` — use `ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)` |

## Bug

Overriding `get_system_prompt()` in a `BaseAgent` subclass does nothing. The SDK always tries to load from `prompts/agent/{ClassName}/system.md`.

```python
class TestAgent(BaseAgent):
    def get_system_prompt(self) -> str:
        return "You are a helpful assistant."  # Never called

agent = TestAgent(llm_model=ModelRegistry.CLAUDE_4_SONNET)
# FileNotFoundError: Prompt file prompts/agent/TestAgent/system.md not found
```

## Cause

`BaseAgent.__init__` calls `_get_system_prompt()` which uses `prompt_loader` directly, bypassing the overrideable `get_system_prompt()` method entirely.

## Workaround

```python
agent = TestAgent(llm_model=..., system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant.")
```

## Fix

Call `self.get_system_prompt()` in `__init__` before falling back to file-based loading.

## Summary

- Add `--provenance` flag to `npm publish` in both npm release workflows, closing #33
- Replace `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `RELEASE_TOKEN` (PAT) in the checkout step of all 5 release workflows so that version bump commits and tags can be pushed back to protected `main`

## Changes

### npm provenance attestation (`release-hooks.yml`, `release-material.yml`)

```diff
- run: npm publish --access public
+ run: npm publish --provenance --access public
```

Provenance creates a cryptographic attestation linking the published package to its source commit and CI build, showing a verified badge on npmjs.com.

### RELEASE_TOKEN for checkout (all 5 release workflows)

```diff
- token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+ token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_TOKEN }}
```

The default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is blocked from pushing to protected branches. Using a PAT stored as `RELEASE_TOKEN` allows the workflow to push version bump commits and tags back to `main` after a successful release.

## Prerequisites

- `RELEASE_TOKEN` secret must be added to the `release` environment in repo settings before running any release workflow
- Repository must be public for npm provenance to work (npm requirement)

Fix subagent silent-death from tool errors and event-loop starvation (#61) (#62)

* Fix SyncAdapter busy-wait in wait_for_completion_async

The polling loop never awaited anything on the not-ready branch, so a
single wait_for_completion call could seize the event loop for the full
30s timeout. Combined with the two call sites in run_async and
get_response_async this added ~60s of dead time on top of any upstream
agent error (issue #61, bug 2).

Yield to the loop each iteration so other coroutines can make progress
while we wait for streaming to end.

Made-with: Cursor

* Handle runtime tool exceptions in create_executor

LangGraph's default ToolNode error handler only catches arg-validation
errors and re-raises everything else, so a network failure, HTTP error
or any other runtime tool exception crashes the agent loop before the
LLM can react. When a subagent spawn fails this also kills the parent
agent's orchestration instead of letting it retry or move on.

Wrap tools in ToolNode(handle_tool_errors=True) so errors surface as
ToolMessage(status="error") the LLM can recover from (issue #61, bug 3).

Made-with: Cursor

* Trim verbose comments on #61 changes

Keep single-line references to the bug for context; drop the
multi-paragraph explanations that just restate what the code and
test names already say.

Made-with: Cursor

* Strengthen #61 regression tests and annotate create_executor

- test_yields_to_event_loop_while_waiting now runs tick() as a background
  task so its ticks only land while the adapter is inside the poll;
  the old gather/wait_for form passed even when the loop was seized.
- test_returns_promptly_once_streaming_ends now uses a streaming-active
  container so it actually exercises the polling branch rather than the
  immediate-return branch.
- Annotate LangChainService.create_executor return type.

Verified by reverting the sync_adapter fix and observing both tests fail
(0 ticks; 5s hang) before reapplying it.

* docs: record Spaik 1.0 migration and release gates

* feat: use official AG-UI client state in hooks and shared Material chat

Pin spaik-sdk==0.11.1 and spaik-coding-agents==0.2.3, warn on import,
mark the package inactive and replace the bump-and-publish workflow with

Earlier releases accept any SDK >=0.2.0 and could resolve against 1.0.

* chore: deprecate and remove legacy coding-agents and agent-workflows from 1.0

Both packages target the legacy block protocol. Final pinned releases

and must be published from main before this line merges. Remove their
source, release workflows, CI and audit jobs, cancel workflows 0.4.0rc1

* docs: record published final legacy releases and yanks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Remove the release plan, validation log and catalog refresh notes; the
migration guide keeps the compatibility table. Replace .cursor rules with
nested AGENTS.md files (root CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md), move the model
update runbook to .agents/skills rewritten for 1.0, and give templates
self-contained AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md in place of stale block-protocol rules.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: restore per-package release workflows for 1.0

Replace the unified release-1.yml with the existing per-package workflows.
Committed versions return to main's (SDK 0.11.2, hooks 0.2.0, Material
0.1.2) so a major bump in each releases 1.0.0. The SDK workflow now uses
Python 3.11 and installs all extras, as 1.0 requires.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: add pre-release option to release workflows

Ticking prerelease publishes an RC (1.0.0rc1 / 1.0.0-rc.1, npm tag next)
and increments it on repeat runs; unticked on an RC publishes the final
version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* build: accept 1.0 release candidates in Material peer and template ranges

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(agent-sdk): build every model through LLMModel family settings and Spaik providers

Reasoning settings were applied only to registry presets, so the same
model ID behaved differently as a preset, an LLMModel or a string, and
temperature, streaming and structured-response settings were ignored.

- family_settings.py applies per-family settings by model.family.
- A string ID that matches a preset uses that preset; other strings
  use provider defaults.
- Known providers always build through Spaik providers; init_chat_model
  is only for provider names Spaik does not wrap.
- temperature is sent only when set, streaming=False disables
  streaming, structured responses use the minimum thinking, and Gemini 3
  minimal thinking is restored. tool_usage is removed.
- Docs lead with presets and LLMModel; chat_model is a last resort.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(agent-sdk): load legacy 0.x thread data from application databases

The 1.0 migration only covered the local pickle store. Applications
that keep threads in their own database need to read legacy rows
without a separate migration environment or downtime.

- migration.load_thread_data loads 1.0 JSON and converts legacy JSON
  (ThreadMessage.to_dict() messages) in memory, with a fallback owner.
- ThreadContainer.from_dict points legacy data to load_thread_data.
- scripts/export_legacy_threads.py exposes export_thread for 0.11 jobs
  that convert pickles stored in a database.
- The migration guide describes reading both formats, writing 1.0 data
  to a new column for rollback, and optional up-front conversion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(agent-sdk): make structured response reasoning effort configurable

Structured responses use each model's minimum reasoning by default,
now consistently across families (OpenAI previously used the full
reasoning effort). The effort can be raised per call with
get_structured_response(..., reasoning_effort=...) or for every call
with LLMConfig.structured_reasoning_effort. Models that require
thinking default to low effort.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(react,material): publish ESM that Node can resolve

The compiled packages imported relative modules without extensions and
Material imported the @mui/material/styles subpath, which MUI 5 does not
export. Bundlers accepted both; Node's ESM loader, used by Vitest and

feat(tracing): improve global tracing configuration and fix reasoning params (#38)

* spec(0001-global-tracing-and-reasoning-fixes): create task specifications

* feat(tracing): add NoOpTraceSink and global tracing configuration

- Add NoOpTraceSink class that silently discards traces
- Add NOOP to TraceSinkMode enum for explicit no-op via env var
- Add configure_tracing() function for global trace sink configuration
- Update get_trace_sink() resolution order:
  1. TRACE_SINK_MODE=local env var → LocalTraceSink
  2. TRACE_SINK_MODE=noop env var → NoOpTraceSink
  3. Global sink via configure_tracing() → that sink
  4. No config → NoOpTraceSink (silent default)
- Update env.py to return None when TRACE_SINK_MODE is unset
- TraceSinkMode.from_name now returns None for invalid/empty values
- Export configure_tracing and NoOpTraceSink from tracing module
- Add comprehensive unit tests for all resolution scenarios

This changes the default behavior from writing traces to filesystem
to silently discarding them (no-op). Users must explicitly enable
tracing via TRACE_SINK_MODE=local or configure_tracing().

* docs: mark step 001 as completed in task documentation

- Update acceptance criteria checkboxes in 001.md (all marked [x])
- Update overview.md to show step 001 as done [x]

* feat(tracing): add agent instance ID for trace correlation

- BaseAgent generates a UUID (agent_instance_id) on construction
- AgentTrace accepts and stores agent_instance_id, passes to TraceSink
- TraceSink.save_trace signature updated with agent_instance_id parameter
- LocalTraceSink accepts but ignores instance ID (file naming unchanged)
- NoOpTraceSink accepts the new parameter
- AgentTrace generates its own UUID if not provided (backward compatibility)
- Added comprehensive unit tests for instance ID generation and propagation

This enables correlation of traces in observability backends (Datadog,
OpenTelemetry) when multiple agent instances exist or when an agent
makes multiple calls.

* docs: mark step 002 as complete in task spec

Update acceptance criteria in 002.md and mark step as done in overview.md

* fix(models): disable Gemini reasoning when reasoning=False

When users set reasoning=False on an agent using a Google Gemini model,
the thinking/reasoning was not actually disabled because Gemini models
have thinking enabled by default.

This change explicitly sets thinking_budget=0 and include_thoughts=False
when reasoning is disabled, as required by the Gemini API to disable
thinking (simply omitting the parameter doesn't work).

- Add else branch to handle reasoning=False case in GoogleModelFactory
- Set thinking_budget=0 to explicitly disable thinking
- Set include_thoughts=False for consistency
- Add comprehensive unit tests for both reasoning=True and reasoning=False

* fix(models): check user reasoning preference in OpenAI factory

The OpenAI factory was checking config.model.reasoning (model capability)
instead of config.reasoning (user preference). This meant that setting
reasoning=False on a reasoning-capable model like GPT-5.1 would be ignored.

Changes:
- Check config.reasoning (user preference) instead of config.model.reasoning
- Add _supports_full_reasoning_disable() helper to detect model version
- When reasoning=False on GPT-5.1+ models, set effort='none' (full disable)

__init__ now calls self.get_system_prompt() (overrideable, returns None
by default) before falling back to file-based prompt loading.  This lets
subclasses supply a system prompt without passing system_prompt= kwarg
and without needing a prompt file on disk.

* fix: don't send parallel_tool_calls without tools on OpenAI (#44)

Two changes:

1. as_structured_response_config() now sets tool_usage=False so
   tool-only kwargs like parallel_tool_calls are not included in
   requests that omit tools (e.g. structured output).

2. OpenAI factory now merges into model_kwargs instead of replacing it,
   so parallel_tool_calls is no longer silently dropped when reasoning

feat(tracing): improve global tracing configuration and fix reasoning params (#38)

* spec(0001-global-tracing-and-reasoning-fixes): create task specifications

* feat(tracing): add NoOpTraceSink and global tracing configuration

- Add NoOpTraceSink class that silently discards traces
- Add NOOP to TraceSinkMode enum for explicit no-op via env var
- Add configure_tracing() function for global trace sink configuration
- Update get_trace_sink() resolution order:
  1. TRACE_SINK_MODE=local env var → LocalTraceSink
  2. TRACE_SINK_MODE=noop env var → NoOpTraceSink
  3. Global sink via configure_tracing() → that sink
  4. No config → NoOpTraceSink (silent default)
- Update env.py to return None when TRACE_SINK_MODE is unset
- TraceSinkMode.from_name now returns None for invalid/empty values
- Export configure_tracing and NoOpTraceSink from tracing module
- Add comprehensive unit tests for all resolution scenarios

This changes the default behavior from writing traces to filesystem
to silently discarding them (no-op). Users must explicitly enable
tracing via TRACE_SINK_MODE=local or configure_tracing().

* docs: mark step 001 as completed in task documentation

- Update acceptance criteria checkboxes in 001.md (all marked [x])
- Update overview.md to show step 001 as done [x]

* feat(tracing): add agent instance ID for trace correlation

- BaseAgent generates a UUID (agent_instance_id) on construction
- AgentTrace accepts and stores agent_instance_id, passes to TraceSink
- TraceSink.save_trace signature updated with agent_instance_id parameter
- LocalTraceSink accepts but ignores instance ID (file naming unchanged)
- NoOpTraceSink accepts the new parameter
- AgentTrace generates its own UUID if not provided (backward compatibility)
- Added comprehensive unit tests for instance ID generation and propagation

This enables correlation of traces in observability backends (Datadog,
OpenTelemetry) when multiple agent instances exist or when an agent
makes multiple calls.

* docs: mark step 002 as complete in task spec

Update acceptance criteria in 002.md and mark step as done in overview.md

* fix(models): disable Gemini reasoning when reasoning=False

When users set reasoning=False on an agent using a Google Gemini model,
the thinking/reasoning was not actually disabled because Gemini models
have thinking enabled by default.

This change explicitly sets thinking_budget=0 and include_thoughts=False
when reasoning is disabled, as required by the Gemini API to disable
thinking (simply omitting the parameter doesn't work).

- Add else branch to handle reasoning=False case in GoogleModelFactory
- Set thinking_budget=0 to explicitly disable thinking
- Set include_thoughts=False for consistency
- Add comprehensive unit tests for both reasoning=True and reasoning=False

* fix(models): check user reasoning preference in OpenAI factory

The OpenAI factory was checking config.model.reasoning (model capability)
instead of config.reasoning (user preference). This meant that setting
reasoning=False on a reasoning-capable model like GPT-5.1 would be ignored.

Changes:
- Check config.reasoning (user preference) instead of config.model.reasoning
- Add _supports_full_reasoning_disable() helper to detect model version
- When reasoning=False on GPT-5.1+ models, set effort='none' (full disable)
- When reasoning=False on GPT-5 base models, set effort='minimal' (lowest available)
- Add comprehensive unit tests for all model variants

* test(tracing): add unit tests for EnvConfig.get_trace_sink_mode

Add dedicated test class TestEnvConfigGetTraceSinkMode to verify:
- Returns None when TRACE_SINK_MODE env var is not set
- Returns None when env var is empty string
- Returns TraceSinkMode.LOCAL when env var is "local"
- Returns TraceSinkMode.NOOP when env var is "noop"
- Returns None for invalid values (no error)
- Case insensitive handling (LOCAL, Local, NOOP, NoOp)

These tests complete step 005 of the global tracing configuration task,
ensuring the env config default behavior change from "local" to unset
is properly tested.

* docs: mark step 005 as complete in task tracking

Update acceptance criteria in 005.md (all items marked [x]) and
mark the step as complete [x] in overview.md.

* fix(api): fix URL construction in postStream to preserve base path

The new URL() API treats paths starting with '/' as absolute, which
discards the path portion of the baseURL. This caused streaming
requests to go to /threads/... instead of /api/chat/threads/...

Changes:
- Use string concatenation instead of new URL() for fullUrl
- Include all axios headers (including custom headers like X-Project-Id)
- Add credentials: 'include' for cookie-based authentication

* chore: remove tasks folder

Remove development planning documents as requested in PR review.

* chore: add tasks folder to gitignore

Prevent development planning documents from being committed in future.

* feat(models): add reasoning_min_effort attribute to LLMModel

Introduce a new attribute, reasoning_min_effort, to the LLMModel class to specify the minimum reasoning effort level. Update GPT-5 model variants in ModelRegistry to utilize this new attribute, ensuring consistent reasoning behavior across models. Adjust OpenAIModelFactory to use the model's minimum reasoning effort when reasoning is disabled.

* refactor(tests): remove unused helper function tests from OpenAIModelFactory tests

Eliminate tests for the _supports_full_reasoning_disable helper function, as they are no longer necessary following recent changes to reasoning handling in the OpenAIModelFactory. This streamlines the test suite and focuses on relevant functionality.

* chore: bump spaik-sdk version to 0.6.4

hits.message:
Fix subagent silent-death from tool errors and event-loop starvation (#61) (#62)

* Fix SyncAdapter busy-wait in wait_for_completion_async

The polling loop never awaited anything on the not-ready branch, so a
single wait_for_completion call could seize the event loop for the full
30s timeout. Combined with the two call sites in run_async and
get_response_async this added ~60s of dead time on top of any upstream
agent error (issue #61, bug 2).

Yield to the loop each iteration so other coroutines can make progress
while we wait for streaming to end.

Made-with: Cursor

* Handle runtime tool exceptions in create_executor

LangGraph's default ToolNode error handler only catches arg-validation
errors and re-raises everything else, so a network failure, HTTP error
or any other runtime tool exception crashes the agent loop before the
LLM can react. When a subagent spawn fails this also kills the parent
agent's orchestration instead of letting it retry or move on.

Wrap tools in ToolNode(handle_tool_errors=True) so errors surface as
ToolMessage(status="error") the LLM can recover from (issue #61, bug 3).

Made-with: Cursor

* Trim verbose comments on #61 changes

Keep single-line references to the bug for context; drop the
multi-paragraph explanations that just restate what the code and
test names already say.

Made-with: Cursor

* Strengthen #61 regression tests and annotate create_executor

- test_yields_to_event_loop_while_waiting now runs tick() as a background
  task so its ticks only land while the adapter is inside the poll;
  the old gather/wait_for form passed even when the loop was seized.
- test_returns_promptly_once_streaming_ends now uses a streaming-active
  container so it actually exercises the polling branch rather than the
  immediate-return branch.
- Annotate LangChainService.create_executor return type.

Verified by reverting the sync_adapter fix and observing both tests fail
(0 ticks; 5s hang) before reapplying it.

hits.message:
feat: incremental thread checkpointing during streaming (#58)

* fix(streaming): prevent duplicate tool_use events from overwriting tool_call_args

Resolves issue where tool_call_args would be empty in BlockAdded events even when tools had arguments.

Root cause: on_chain_end was re-emitting TOOL_USE events for tools already processed during streaming, and these re-emissions often had empty args (from message.tool_calls) that would overwrite the correct args from the initial streaming.

Solution:
- Track which tool IDs have been processed during streaming
- Track the args seen for each tool
- In on_chain_end, only re-emit TOOL_USE if:
  1. Tool wasn't seen during streaming, OR
  2. Streaming had empty args but on_chain_end has non-empty args (upgrade scenario)

This preserves the PR #56 fix for upserting blocks while preventing the duplicate emissions that caused empty args to overwrite correct ones.

Added search_web tool with arguments to examples/backend for testing.

Made-with: Cursor

* fix(lint): wrap long line in streaming_event_handler

Made-with: Cursor

* feat(examples): add subagent_example.py with isolation helper

Shows how to spawn a nested BaseAgent from inside a tool call without
leaking the subagent's tool_use blocks into the main thread stream.
Includes the run_isolated() helper and an inline explanation of why
asyncio.run() alone causes ContextVar leakage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: checkpoint thread after each tool call and completed message

Persists the thread to storage after every ToolResponseReceivedEvent and
MessageFullyAddedEvent during streaming, so long-running multi-tool runs
survive server restarts or crashes mid-run.

Made-with: Cursor

* test: add unit and integration tests for thread checkpointing

Unit tests verify that AgentResponseGenerator fires on_checkpoint only
on ToolResponseReceivedEvent and MessageFullyAddedEvent, and that
ThreadJobProcessor wires the callback to update_thread correctly.

Integration test runs a real recorded tool-calling agent through the
full stack and asserts save_thread is called mid-run (not only at end).

Made-with: Cursor

* fix: swallow checkpoint errors so a storage failure does not abort the stream

If on_checkpoint raises (e.g. IO error, network blip), the exception is
logged and the stream continues. The final update_thread call in
ThreadJobProcessor is unaffected and still runs on clean completion.

Made-with: Cursor

OllamaProvider.create_langchain_model() passed model= explicitly while

"got multiple values for keyword argument 'model'" on every Ollama call.
Align with other providers that just spread full_config.

* fix: allow get_system_prompt() override in BaseAgent subclasses (#34)

__init__ now calls self.get_system_prompt() (overrideable, returns None
by default) before falling back to file-based prompt loading.  This lets
subclasses supply a system prompt without passing system_prompt= kwarg
and without needing a prompt file on disk.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: don't send parallel_tool_calls without tools on OpenAI (#44)

Two changes:

1. as_structured_response_config() now sets tool_usage=False so
   tool-only kwargs like parallel_tool_calls are not included in
   requests that omit tools (e.g. structured output).

2. OpenAI factory now merges into model_kwargs instead of replacing it,
   so parallel_tool_calls is no longer silently dropped when reasoning
   config is also set.

feat(tracing): improve global tracing configuration and fix reasoning params (#38)

* spec(0001-global-tracing-and-reasoning-fixes): create task specifications

* feat(tracing): add NoOpTraceSink and global tracing configuration

- Add NoOpTraceSink class that silently discards traces
- Add NOOP to TraceSinkMode enum for explicit no-op via env var
- Add configure_tracing() function for global trace sink configuration
- Update get_trace_sink() resolution order:
  1. TRACE_SINK_MODE=local env var → LocalTraceSink
  2. TRACE_SINK_MODE=noop env var → NoOpTraceSink
  3. Global sink via configure_tracing() → that sink
  4. No config → NoOpTraceSink (silent default)
- Update env.py to return None when TRACE_SINK_MODE is unset
- TraceSinkMode.from_name now returns None for invalid/empty values
- Export configure_tracing and NoOpTraceSink from tracing module
- Add comprehensive unit tests for all resolution scenarios

This changes the default behavior from writing traces to filesystem
to silently discarding them (no-op). Users must explicitly enable
tracing via TRACE_SINK_MODE=local or configure_tracing().

* docs: mark step 001 as completed in task documentation

- Update acceptance criteria checkboxes in 001.md (all marked [x])
- Update overview.md to show step 001 as done [x]

* feat(tracing): add agent instance ID for trace correlation

- BaseAgent generates a UUID (agent_instance_id) on construction
- AgentTrace accepts and stores agent_instance_id, passes to TraceSink
- TraceSink.save_trace signature updated with agent_instance_id parameter
- LocalTraceSink accepts but ignores instance ID (file naming unchanged)
- NoOpTraceSink accepts the new parameter
- AgentTrace generates its own UUID if not provided (backward compatibility)
- Added comprehensive unit tests for instance ID generation and propagation

This enables correlation of traces in observability backends (Datadog,
OpenTelemetry) when multiple agent instances exist or when an agent
makes multiple calls.

* docs: mark step 002 as complete in task spec

Update acceptance criteria in 002.md and mark step as done in overview.md

* fix(models): disable Gemini reasoning when reasoning=False

When users set reasoning=False on an agent using a Google Gemini model,
the thinking/reasoning was not actually disabled because Gemini models
have thinking enabled by default.

This change explicitly sets thinking_budget=0 and include_thoughts=False
when reasoning is disabled, as required by the Gemini API to disable
thinking (simply omitting the parameter doesn't work).

- Add else branch to handle reasoning=False case in GoogleModelFactory
- Set thinking_budget=0 to explicitly disable thinking
- Set include_thoughts=False for consistency
- Add comprehensive unit tests for both reasoning=True and reasoning=False

* fix(models): check user reasoning preference in OpenAI factory

The OpenAI factory was checking config.model.reasoning (model capability)
instead of config.reasoning (user preference). This meant that setting
reasoning=False on a reasoning-capable model like GPT-5.1 would be ignored.

Changes:
- Check config.reasoning (user preference) instead of config.model.reasoning
- Add _supports_full_reasoning_disable() helper to detect model version
- When reasoning=False on GPT-5.1+ models, set effort='none' (full disable)
- When reasoning=False on GPT-5 base models, set effort='minimal' (lowest available)
- Add comprehensive unit tests for all model variants

* test(tracing): add unit tests for EnvConfig.get_trace_sink_mode

Add dedicated test class TestEnvConfigGetTraceSinkMode to verify:
- Returns None when TRACE_SINK_MODE env var is not set
- Returns None when env var is empty string
- Returns TraceSinkMode.LOCAL when env var is "local"
- Returns TraceSinkMode.NOOP when env var is "noop"
- Returns None for invalid values (no error)
- Case insensitive handling (LOCAL, Local, NOOP, NoOp)

These tests complete step 005 of the global tracing configuration task,
ensuring the env config default behavior change from "local" to unset
is properly tested.

* docs: mark step 005 as complete in task tracking

Update acceptance criteria in 005.md (all items marked [x]) and
mark the step as complete [x] in overview.md.

* fix(api): fix URL construction in postStream to preserve base path

The new URL() API treats paths starting with '/' as absolute, which
discards the path portion of the baseURL. This caused streaming
requests to go to /threads/... instead of /api/chat/threads/...

Changes:
- Use string concatenation instead of new URL() for fullUrl
- Include all axios headers (including custom headers like X-Project-Id)
- Add credentials: 'include' for cookie-based authentication

* chore: remove tasks folder

Remove development planning documents as requested in PR review.

* chore: add tasks folder to gitignore

Prevent development planning documents from being committed in future.

* feat(models): add reasoning_min_effort attribute to LLMModel

Introduce a new attribute, reasoning_min_effort, to the LLMModel class to specify the minimum reasoning effort level. Update GPT-5 model variants in ModelRegistry to utilize this new attribute, ensuring consistent reasoning behavior across models. Adjust OpenAIModelFactory to use the model's minimum reasoning effort when reasoning is disabled.

* refactor(tests): remove unused helper function tests from OpenAIModelFactory tests

Eliminate tests for the _supports_full_reasoning_disable helper function, as they are no longer necessary following recent changes to reasoning handling in the OpenAIModelFactory. This streamlines the test suite and focuses on relevant functionality.

* chore: bump spaik-sdk version to 0.6.4

Fix/agent-sdk runtime bugs (#45)

* fix: add missing python-multipart dependency (#32)

FastAPI file router requires python-multipart for form data parsing,
but it was not declared as a dependency, causing startup failures.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: remove duplicate model kwarg in OllamaProvider (#31)

OllamaProvider.create_langchain_model() passed model= explicitly while
full_config already contained the key from the factory, causing
"got multiple values for keyword argument 'model'" on every Ollama call.
Align with other providers that just spread full_config.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: allow get_system_prompt() override in BaseAgent subclasses (#34)

__init__ now calls self.get_system_prompt() (overrideable, returns None
by default) before falling back to file-based prompt loading.  This lets
subclasses supply a system prompt without passing system_prompt= kwarg
and without needing a prompt file on disk.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: don't send parallel_tool_calls without tools on OpenAI (#44)

Two changes:

1. as_structured_response_config() now sets tool_usage=False so
   tool-only kwargs like parallel_tool_calls are not included in
   requests that omit tools (e.g. structured output).

2. OpenAI factory now merges into model_kwargs instead of replacing it,
   so parallel_tool_calls is no longer silently dropped when reasoning
   config is also set.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* style: apply ruff formatting

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Revert "fix: allow get_system_prompt() override in BaseAgent subclasses (#34)"

This reverts commit 5e193d794a7055ef40027f2e25b34c7dd10796bb.

* fix: resolve provider type from model family when MODEL_PROVIDER env is not set

Previously, provider type was always resolved via env config (MODEL_PROVIDER
env var or DEFAULT_MODEL name prefix matching), ignoring the model's family
field. This broke dynamically created models like Ollama where the family
is the correct source for provider resolution.

Now BaseAgent resolves provider type by checking MODEL_PROVIDER env first
(for cross-provider hosting like Claude-on-Azure), then falling back to
the model's own family field.

* fix(agent-sdk): build every model through LLMModel family settings and Spaik providers

Reasoning settings were applied only to registry presets, so the same
model ID behaved differently as a preset, an LLMModel or a string, and
temperature, streaming and structured-response settings were ignored.

- family_settings.py applies per-family settings by model.family.
- A string ID that matches a preset uses that preset; other strings
  use provider defaults.
- Known providers always build through Spaik providers; init_chat_model
  is only for provider names Spaik does not wrap.
- temperature is sent only when set, streaming=False disables
  streaming, structured responses use the minimum thinking, and Gemini 3
  minimal thinking is restored. tool_usage is removed.
- Docs lead with presets and LLMModel; chat_model is a last resort.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(agent-sdk): load legacy 0.x thread data from application databases

The 1.0 migration only covered the local pickle store. Applications
that keep threads in their own database need to read legacy rows
without a separate migration environment or downtime.

- migration.load_thread_data loads 1.0 JSON and converts legacy JSON
  (ThreadMessage.to_dict() messages) in memory, with a fallback owner.
- ThreadContainer.from_dict points legacy data to load_thread_data.
- scripts/export_legacy_threads.py exposes export_thread for 0.11 jobs
  that convert pickles stored in a database.
- The migration guide describes reading both formats, writing 1.0 data
  to a new column for rollback, and optional up-front conversion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(agent-sdk): make structured response reasoning effort configurable

Fix/agent-sdk runtime bugs (#45)

* fix: add missing python-multipart dependency (#32)

FastAPI file router requires python-multipart for form data parsing,
but it was not declared as a dependency, causing startup failures.

* fix: remove duplicate model kwarg in OllamaProvider (#31)

OllamaProvider.create_langchain_model() passed model= explicitly while
full_config already contained the key from the factory, causing
"got multiple values for keyword argument 'model'" on every Ollama call.
Align with other providers that just spread full_config.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: allow get_system_prompt() override in BaseAgent subclasses (#34)

__init__ now calls self.get_system_prompt() (overrideable, returns None
by default) before falling back to file-based prompt loading.  This lets
subclasses supply a system prompt without passing system_prompt= kwarg
and without needing a prompt file on disk.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: don't send parallel_tool_calls without tools on OpenAI (#44)

Two changes:

1. as_structured_response_config() now sets tool_usage=False so
   tool-only kwargs like parallel_tool_calls are not included in
   requests that omit tools (e.g. structured output).

2. OpenAI factory now merges into model_kwargs instead of replacing it,
   so parallel_tool_calls is no longer silently dropped when reasoning
   config is also set.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* style: apply ruff formatting

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Revert "fix: allow get_system_prompt() override in BaseAgent subclasses (#34)"

This reverts commit 5e193d794a7055ef40027f2e25b34c7dd10796bb.

* fix: resolve provider type from model family when MODEL_PROVIDER env is not set

Previously, provider type was always resolved via env config (MODEL_PROVIDER
env var or DEFAULT_MODEL name prefix matching), ignoring the model's family
field. This broke dynamically created models like Ollama where the family
is the correct source for provider resolution.

Now BaseAgent resolves provider type by checking MODEL_PROVIDER env first
(for cross-provider hosting like Claude-on-Azure), then falling back to
the model's own family field.

Release notes

Sourced from aiosmtplib's releases.

v5.1.2

What's Changed

  • Security: Discard any buffered server data before the STARTTLS handshake, preventing a response-injection attack where a man-in-the-middle pre-stages plaintext that would otherwise be read as part of the encrypted session. More details: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/security/advisories/GHSA-vxj7-4xrp-5vr4
  • Bugfix: Corrected SMTPResponse __repr__ result
  • Bugfix: Calling connect() on an already-connected client now raises SMTPException instead of deadlocking on the connection lock
  • Feature: Poe command runner for dev tasks
  • Bugfix: Timeout ignored during CRAM-MD5 verification
  • Bugfix: Only parse EHLO response after validating success
  • Bugfix: return None from extract_sender when address list is empty
  • Bugfix: Enforce a maximum total response size, preventing unbounded memory use if a server streams data with no line ending or endless multiline continuation lines
  • Bugfix: Use the invalid_response status code (-1) instead of 500 when a server response line exceeds the maximum length
  • Bugfix: A read timeout now closes the connection instead of leaving it in a desynced state, where a late server response could be mispaired with a subsequent command
  • Bugfix: Correctly parse old-style AUTH= extension advertisements; all advertised methods are now kept (e.g. both PLAIN and LOGIN from AUTH=PLAIN LOGIN)
  • Bugfix: ESMTP extension lines with leading whitespace are no longer ignored

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/compare/v5.1.1...v5.1.2

5.1.1

What's Changed

  • Security: Reject control characters (the C0 range 0x00-0x1F and DEL 0x7F, including CR, LF, and NUL) in SMTP command arguments, preventing command injection via input passed to mail(), rcpt(), vrfy(), expn() or sendmail(). Such input now raises ValueError before anything is written to the connection. More details: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/security/advisories/GHSA-v3q9-hj7j-63hq Thanks to @​tonghuaroot for the report.
  • Bugfix: SMTP.quit() no longer hangs until the read timeout when the peer drops the transport with an exception after QUIT is sent but before the 221 reply is parsed (e.g. AWS SES closing TLS without close_notify). Contributed by @​yamaaaaaa31

8.3.3

This is the Click 8.3.3 fix release, which fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes compared to the latest feature release.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/click/8.3.3/ Changes: https://click.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-8-3-3 Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/click/milestone/30

  • Use :func:shlex.split to split pager and editor commands into argv lists for :class:subprocess.Popen, removing shell=True. #1026 #1477 #2775
  • Fix TypeError when rendering help for an option whose default value is an object that doesn't support equality comparison with strings, such as semver.Version. #3298 #3299
  • Fix pager test pollution under parallel execution by using pytest's tmp_path fixture instead of a shared temporary file path. #3238
  • Treat Sentinel.UNSET values in a default_map as absent, so they fall through to the next default source instead of being used as the value. #3224 #3240
  • Patch pdb.Pdb in CliRunner isolation so pdb.set_trace(), breakpoint(), and debuggers subclassing pdb.Pdb (ipdb, pdbpp) can interact with the real terminal instead of the captured I/O streams. #654 #824 #843 #951 #3235
  • Add optional randomized parallel test execution using pytest-randomly and pytest-xdist to detect test pollution and race conditions. #3151
  • Add contributor documentation for running stress tests, randomized parallel tests, and Flask smoke tests. #3151 #3177
  • Show custom show_default string in prompts, matching the existing help text behavior. #2836 #2837 #3165 #3262 #3280 #3328
  • Fix default=True with boolean flag_value always returning the flag_value instead of True. The default=True to flag_value substitution now only applies to non-boolean flags, where True acts as a sentinel meaning "activate this flag by default". For boolean flags, default=True is returned as a literal value. #3111 #3239
  • Mark make_default_short_help as private API.

Sourced from aiosmtplib's releases.

v5.1.2

What's Changed

  • Security: Discard any buffered server data before the STARTTLS handshake, preventing a response-injection attack where a man-in-the-middle pre-stages plaintext that would otherwise be read as part of the encrypted session. More details: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/security/advisories/GHSA-vxj7-4xrp-5vr4
  • Bugfix: Corrected SMTPResponse __repr__ result
  • Bugfix: Calling connect() on an already-connected client now raises SMTPException instead of deadlocking on the connection lock
  • Feature: Poe command runner for dev tasks
  • Bugfix: Timeout ignored during CRAM-MD5 verification
  • Bugfix: Only parse EHLO response after validating success
  • Bugfix: return None from extract_sender when address list is empty
  • Bugfix: Enforce a maximum total response size, preventing unbounded memory use if a server streams data with no line ending or endless multiline continuation lines
  • Bugfix: Use the invalid_response status code (-1) instead of 500 when a server response line exceeds the maximum length

  • Bugfix: Correctly parse old-style AUTH= extension advertisements; all advertised methods are now kept (e.g. both PLAIN and LOGIN from AUTH=PLAIN LOGIN)

Release notes

Sourced from aiosmtplib's releases.

v5.1.2

What's Changed

  • Security: Discard any buffered server data before the STARTTLS handshake, preventing a response-injection attack where a man-in-the-middle pre-stages plaintext that would otherwise be read as part of the encrypted session. More details: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/security/advisories/GHSA-vxj7-4xrp-5vr4
  • Bugfix: Corrected SMTPResponse __repr__ result
  • Bugfix: Calling connect() on an already-connected client now raises SMTPException instead of deadlocking on the connection lock
  • Feature: Poe command runner for dev tasks
  • Bugfix: Timeout ignored during CRAM-MD5 verification
  • Bugfix: Only parse EHLO response after validating success
  • Bugfix: return None from extract_sender when address list is empty
  • Bugfix: Enforce a maximum total response size, preventing unbounded memory use if a server streams data with no line ending or endless multiline continuation lines
  • Bugfix: Use the invalid_response status code (-1) instead of 500 when a server response line exceeds the maximum length
  • Bugfix: A read timeout now closes the connection instead of leaving it in a desynced state, where a late server response could be mispaired with a subsequent command
  • Bugfix: Correctly parse old-style AUTH= extension advertisements; all advertised methods are now kept (e.g. both PLAIN and LOGIN from AUTH=PLAIN LOGIN)
  • Bugfix: ESMTP extension lines with leading whitespace are no longer ignored

Release notes

Sourced from click's releases.

8.3.3

This is the Click 8.3.3 fix release, which fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes compared to the latest feature release.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/click/8.3.3/ Changes: https://click.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-8-3-3 Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/click/milestone/30

  • Use :func:shlex.split to split pager and editor commands into argv lists for :class:subprocess.Popen, removing shell=True. #1026 #1477 #2775
  • Fix TypeError when rendering help for an option whose default value is an object that doesn't support equality comparison with strings, such as semver.Version. #3298 #3299
  • Fix pager test pollution under parallel execution by using pytest's tmp_path fixture instead of a shared temporary file path. #3238
  • Treat Sentinel.UNSET values in a default_map as absent, so they fall through to the next default source instead of being used as the value. #3224 #3240
  • Patch pdb.Pdb in CliRunner isolation so pdb.set_trace(), breakpoint(), and debuggers subclassing pdb.Pdb (ipdb, pdbpp) can interact with the real terminal instead of the captured I/O streams. #654 #824 #843 #951 #3235
  • Add optional randomized parallel test execution using pytest-randomly and pytest-xdist to detect test pollution and race conditions. #3151
  • Add contributor documentation for running stress tests, randomized parallel tests, and Flask smoke tests. #3151 #3177
  • Show custom show_default string in prompts, matching the existing help text behavior. #2836 #2837 #3165 #3262 #3280 #3328

Updates `click` from 8.3.2 to 8.3.3
Release notes

Sourced from click's releases.

8.3.3

This is the Click 8.3.3 fix release, which fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes compared to the latest feature release.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/click/8.3.3/ Changes: https://click.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-8-3-3 Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/click/milestone/30

  • Use :func:shlex.split to split pager and editor commands into argv lists for :class:subprocess.Popen, removing shell=True. #1026 #1477 #2775
  • Fix TypeError when rendering help for an option whose default value is an object that doesn't support equality comparison with strings, such as semver.Version. #3298 #3299
  • Fix pager test pollution under parallel execution by using pytest's tmp_path fixture instead of a shared temporary file path. #3238
  • Treat Sentinel.UNSET values in a default_map as absent, so they fall through to the next default source instead of being used as the value. #3224 #3240
  • Patch pdb.Pdb in CliRunner isolation so pdb.set_trace(), breakpoint(), and debuggers subclassing pdb.Pdb (ipdb, pdbpp) can interact with the real terminal instead of the captured I/O streams. #654 #824 #843 #951 #3235
  • Add optional randomized parallel test execution using pytest-randomly and pytest-xdist to detect test pollution and race conditions. #3151
  • Add contributor documentation for running stress tests, randomized parallel tests, and Flask smoke tests. #3151 #3177
  • Show custom show_default string in prompts, matching the existing help text behavior. #2836 #2837 #3165 #3262 #3280 #3328
  • Fix default=True with boolean flag_value always returning the flag_value instead of True. The default=True to flag_value substitution now only applies to non-boolean flags, where True acts as a sentinel meaning "activate this flag by default". For boolean flags, default=True is returned as a literal value. #3111 #3239
  • Mark make_default_short_help as private API.

Updates `aiosmtplib` from 5.1.0 to 5.1.2
Release notes

Sourced from aiosmtplib's releases.

v5.1.2

What's Changed

  • Security: Discard any buffered server data before the STARTTLS handshake, preventing a response-injection attack where a man-in-the-middle pre-stages plaintext that would otherwise be read as part of the encrypted session. More details: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/security/advisories/GHSA-vxj7-4xrp-5vr4
  • Bugfix: Corrected SMTPResponse __repr__ result
  • Bugfix: Calling connect() on an already-connected client now raises SMTPException instead of deadlocking on the connection lock
  • Feature: Poe command runner for dev tasks
  • Bugfix: Timeout ignored during CRAM-MD5 verification
  • Bugfix: Only parse EHLO response after validating success
  • Bugfix: return None from extract_sender when address list is empty
  • Bugfix: Enforce a maximum total response size, preventing unbounded memory use if a server streams data with no line ending or endless multiline continuation lines
  • Bugfix: Use the invalid_response status code (-1) instead of 500 when a server response line exceeds the maximum length
  • Bugfix: A read timeout now closes the connection instead of leaving it in a desynced state, where a late server response could be mispaired with a subsequent command
  • Bugfix: Correctly parse old-style AUTH= extension advertisements; all advertised methods are now kept (e.g. both PLAIN and LOGIN from AUTH=PLAIN LOGIN)
  • Bugfix: ESMTP extension lines with leading whitespace are no longer ignored

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/compare/v5.1.1...v5.1.2

5.1.1

What's Changed

  • Security: Reject control characters (the C0 range 0x00-0x1F and DEL 0x7F, including CR, LF, and NUL) in SMTP command arguments, preventing command injection via input passed to mail(), rcpt(), vrfy(), expn() or sendmail(). Such input now raises ValueError before anything is written to the connection. More details: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/security/advisories/GHSA-v3q9-hj7j-63hq Thanks to @​tonghuaroot for the report.
  • Bugfix: SMTP.quit() no longer hangs until the read timeout when the peer drops the transport with an exception after QUIT is sent but before the 221 reply is parsed (e.g. AWS SES closing TLS without close_notify). Contributed by @​yamaaaaaa31

New Contributors

  • @​yamaaaaaa31 made their first contribution in cole/aiosmtplib#346

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/compare/v5.1.0...v5.1.1

Updates `aiosmtplib` from 5.1.0 to 5.1.1
Release notes

Sourced from aiosmtplib's releases.

5.1.1

What's Changed

  • Security: Reject control characters (the C0 range 0x00-0x1F and DEL 0x7F, including CR, LF, and NUL) in SMTP command arguments, preventing command injection via input passed to mail(), rcpt(), vrfy(), expn() or sendmail(). Such input now raises ValueError before anything is written to the connection. More details: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/security/advisories/GHSA-v3q9-hj7j-63hq Thanks to @​tonghuaroot for the report.
  • Bugfix: SMTP.quit() no longer hangs until the read timeout when the peer drops the transport with an exception after QUIT is sent but before the 221 reply is parsed (e.g. AWS SES closing TLS without close_notify). Contributed by @​yamaaaaaa31

New Contributors

  • @​yamaaaaaa31 made their first contribution in cole/aiosmtplib#346

Full Changelog: https://github.com/cole/aiosmtplib/compare/v5.1.0...v5.1.1

Updates `click` from 8.3.2 to 8.3.3
Release notes

Sourced from click's releases.

8.3.3

This is the Click 8.3.3 fix release, which fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes compared to the latest feature release.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/click/8.3.3/ Changes: https://click.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-8-3-3 Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/click/milestone/30

  • Use :func:shlex.split to split pager and editor commands into argv lists for :class:subprocess.Popen, removing shell=True. #1026 #1477 #2775
  • Fix TypeError when rendering help for an option whose default value is an object that doesn't support equality comparison with strings, such as semver.Version. #3298 #3299
  • Fix pager test pollution under parallel execution by using pytest's tmp_path fixture instead of a shared temporary file path. #3238
  • Treat Sentinel.UNSET values in a default_map as absent, so they fall through to the next default source instead of being used as the value. #3224 #3240
  • Patch pdb.Pdb in CliRunner isolation so pdb.set_trace(), breakpoint(), and debuggers subclassing pdb.Pdb (ipdb, pdbpp) can interact with the real terminal instead of the captured I/O streams. #654 #824 #843 #951 #3235
  • Add optional randomized parallel test execution using pytest-randomly and pytest-xdist to detect test pollution and race conditions. #3151
  • Add contributor documentation for running stress tests, randomized parallel tests, and Flask smoke tests. #3151 #3177
  • Show custom show_default string in prompts, matching the existing help text behavior. #2836 #2837 #3165 #3262 #3280 #3328
  • Fix default=True with boolean flag_value always returning the flag_value instead of True. The default=True to flag_value substitution now only applies to non-boolean flags, where True acts as a sentinel meaning "activate this flag by default". For boolean flags, default=True is returned as a literal value. #3111 #3239
  • Mark make_default_short_help as private API.
