He approved that proposal in full and asked for it to be built by Opus and PR'd. Decisions: two pages per Bot, identical on desktop (380 right panel) and phone (pushed page). The Bot page is activity: header avatar 28 + name + gear + close; Computer card first with an always-present status row (Live/Ready/captured) and Open; Routines = last three runs as rows opening the run log + an All Routines row carrying the unacknowledged badge; Applets running + All Applets; More = Package doors. Card grammar everywhere (FrockRowGroup/FrockRow 46/58, icon column 22, divider indent 48). Routines and Plugins ViewDocuments render through one shared renderer (ViewSwitchRows) rather than a fork: Plugins is one card of switch rows with 'Built in' as a group label; the Routines projection files Routines under Scheduled/Webhooks with a pause switch per row, moves Run now / Run log / keys / Delete onto the editor a row opens, empty state is a card, Completions stays as the last card because acknowledging has no other home. ## What Changed

## Intent

Get the realtime voice session on the Flutter Android app working well. Tim asked for three things: (1) the standard mobile audio setup — with Bluetooth it did not respond, without it the reply came out quietly like a phone-call earpiece; (2) a snappy, optimistic start — the footer and the voice button should react instantly on press even though the call takes seconds to open; (3) better, non-laggy animations that show it can hear him and when the Bot is talking, built the right way for Flutter. Decisions made with him during the session: adopt the VoIP model used by WebRTC/LiveKit (communication mode, transient voice-communication focus, route priority Bluetooth headset > wired > loudspeaker, never earpiece on its own; earpiece route only if a headset is chosen; A2DP-only speakers cannot be a communication device and fall back to the loudspeaker — accepted, an output picker is a later step); the record plugin is told to leave the session alone for the call profile (modeNormal, manageBluetooth false, no focus request) while dictation keeps the plugin's own handling; the speaker AudioTrack uses USAGE_VOICE_COMMUNICATION; because that track sits on Pixel's VoIP output path it must be pumped continuously (silence when idle) or it underruns while the Bot thinks and the playback head never advances — verified on Tim's Pixel 9a with logcat — so PcmSpeaker was rewritten as a pump thread and the Dart player keeps 15 chunks (500 ms) in flight against a 100 ms device buffer to avoid mid-sentence padding (Tim heard choppy audio at 6 chunks/200 ms). All AudioManager calls run on a HandlerThread because setCommunicationDevice took ~480 ms on the main thread and froze the footer entrance. Start path: footer shown in the press frame before any await, capability probe read once at sign-in (a press proceeds when the probe is unknown), socket connect concurrent with route.begin + mic open, hello/start_call deferred until both welcome and an open mic (no billing during the permission prompt); the sidebar voice button paints active colour on pointer-down and, at Tim's request, also ends the call while the footer is up (tooltip 'End voice session' on both). Meter: replaced the three-ribbon path painter with five pills (Gemini-style), one Ticker → ChangeNotifier → CustomPainter repaint, no per-frame allocation, modes connecting/listening/thinking/speaking/asleep/muted from AssistantSessionController.meterMode; VoiceEnvelope attack shortened to ~20 ms (test expectation deliberately changed); capture streamBufferSize = max(platform minimum, one frame). Focus loss: transient → hold mic + interrupt reply (reuses the dictation hold), permanent → call ends with a sentence. Server-side, also at Tim's request: the bridge filler 'One second.' was spoken unconditionally before any tool step — now only the acknowledgment timer speaks it, raised from 1 s to 2.5 s because the meter's thinking state carries an ordinary turn, and it rotates through six phrases never repeating the last (pickVoiceBridgeV1); tests updated accordingly (fast tool turns no longer bridged; the abort-after-ack test now uses a slow model). A Bot answering a voice request wrote the answer as a send_to_user message (push notification) and then spoke it: the voice prompt now says say it once and never also write it, and sends from a voice-origin Turn carry notify:false while still landing in the thread and counting unread. docs/voice.md updated for all of it. A test in voice_footer_test pumps twice after delivering a frame because the new connecting ticker changed frame parity. Kotlin changed, so a full Shorebird release is owed after merge; Worker changes reach production through the release pipeline. Bluetooth headset path is unverified on a real headset (none paired); everything else was verified on the Pixel with dumpsys audio, logcat and screen recordings.

## What Changed

- **Android audio (VoIP model):** the new `VoiceAudioRoute.kt` and `route.dart` put the call in communication mode with transient voice-communication focus. Output goes to a Bluetooth headset first, then a wired headset, then the loudspeaker, and never falls back to the earpiece. All AudioManager calls run on a HandlerThread. `PcmSpeaker` is now a pump thread on a `USAGE_VOICE_COMMUNICATION` track that writes silence when idle, so playback doesn't underrun while the Bot is thinking. The Dart player keeps 15 chunks (500 ms) in flight. The call profile tells the record plugin to leave the audio session alone; dictation still uses the plugin's own handling. If focus is lost briefly, the mic is held and the reply is interrupted; if focus is lost for good, the call ends.
- **Instant start and meter:** the footer appears as soon as the button is pressed. The socket connects while the route and mic are opening, and `hello`/`start_call` wait until both the server's welcome and an open mic have arrived. The sidebar voice button turns active on pointer-down and ends the call while the footer is up (tooltip "End voice session"). The old three-ribbon waveform is replaced by a five-pill meter driven by a single Ticker. It has connecting, listening, thinking, speaking, asleep and muted modes. The envelope attack is shorter, and the capture stream buffer is at least one frame.
- **Server:** the "One second." filler no longer plays before every tool step. Only the acknowledgment timer speaks it, now after 2.5 s instead of 1 s, and it rotates through six phrases without repeating the last one (`pickVoiceBridgeV1`). The voice prompt now tells the Bot to say an answer once and not also write it. Sends from a voice-origin Turn carry `notify:false`, so there's no push notification, but they still land in the thread and count as unread. Tests and `docs/voice.md` / `docs/notifications.md` are updated to match.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Both fixes are correct and tightly scoped. The start timer now waits for both the socket and the mic. Thinking mode ignores mic sound below speech level. Native audio-session work is still risky, though: dictating during a call can end the call, and that needs your decision.

## Testing

The baseline `bun test` had already passed. I then ran the four changed Flutter voice test files and the workerd voice-assistant test file, and all passed, including the rotating bridge-phrase acknowledgment test. These are fakes-based tests, not live runs. No scenario was driven against the running app. A call needs a debug build of this branch installed over the dev app on Tim's own Pixel, a signed-in account that gets billed, and someone speaking. I did not do that without permission. As a result there are no screenshots or recordings of the footer or meter, and the verdict is inconclusive.

| Pressing the sidebar voice button on Android shows the footer and the active colour at once; pressing it again ends the call | ⏸️ untested | no | Needs a debug build of this branch installed on the Pixel, and a signed-in account. Installing over Tim's dev app was not authorized. |

## Intent

Implement task 3 in FrockBot: hiding a Bot from the sidebar must also turn off that Bot's Notifications setting. When Notifications is on and the user turns on Hidden from sidebar, show an explicit confirmation that hiding turns off notifications; cancel changes neither setting; confirm immediately predicts Hidden on and Notifications off, then saves. If notifications are already off, show no redundant warning. A hidden Bot cannot enable Notifications and the control must be disabled with explanatory text. Showing the Bot again leaves Notifications off until explicitly enabled. Enforce hidden implies notifications disabled atomically in the authoritative Bot configuration transaction for all writers, including agent-authored changes and other clients. Avoid two writes or revisions when native changes both together. Normalize existing hidden Bots that still notify under disposable pre-user cleanup rules. Keep muted Bots unread; this changes alert eligibility only. Test backend atomic enforcement, idempotency and conflicts; test native confirm, cancel, prediction, save failure, disabled state and unhide behavior; update current-state docs. Do not merge.

## What Changed

- The Bot configuration transaction (`app/settings/bot.ts`) now enforces hidden-implies-muted for every writer: any write that leaves `profile.hiddenFromSidebar` true also sets `notifications.enabled` false in the same revision, and `bot/update-notifications` enabling alerts on a hidden Bot returns a stored `rejected` receipt without moving the revision. The `bot_update` agent tool refuses `notify_on_updates: true` for a hidden Bot before writing anything, reports the mute hiding caused, and its schema text documents the coupling.
- Native Bot settings (`apps/native/lib/settings/bot_settings.dart`) confirm before hiding a notifying Bot ("Hide and turn off" / "Cancel"), predict both switches locally and send a single `bot/set-profile`; the Notifications switch is disabled with explanatory copy while hidden, unhiding leaves notifications off, and a failed save re-reads the authoritative settings to reconcile a hide that may have landed unanswered.
- Added the one-time `hidden-bot-notifications-cleanup.ts` pass, run as each Bot loads in `BotState`, that mutes already-hidden Bots still set to notify; added backend unit, workerd, integration and e2e coverage plus native widget tests, and updated `docs/notifications.md` and `docs/grokbot-parity.md`. ## Intent

Tim's decision after tonight's voice incident, in his words: 'I don't think the old answers thing needs to be so complicated. I think each voice session should be fresh but just with memory. And I think the agent can decide to read an answer or not when a bot returns a result. I think if the voice chat stops while the bot has a task in flight then the bot should simply not be able to send it to the voice agent and that's that. I agree on never opening a call with a read out.' Then: 'do it. PR and merge when done.' So: (1) No cross-call queue of Bot answers. A call that ends (end_call, stale/abandoned alarm, superseded by another device or a new call after the rejoin window) cancels its admitted and settled delegations in the ledger itself, so every end path is covered; a Bot still working answers into its own conversation (the reply_to_request already lands in the Bot thread as the exchange view) and nothing carries to the next call. onCallStart reads nothing out. (2) A Bot answer that arrives during the call is handed to the assistant as an event turn (admitted and metered like a spoken turn, record.event = {kind: bot-answer}, transcript = a '[Bot answer] ...' message carrying the request in the person's own words from the retained turn), run through runVoiceTurnV1 with acknowledge:false (no bridge), spoken once whole, aborted if the person starts talking or interrupts; the assistant decides what to say and may say nothing (an empty answer is settled as answered:'' and traced outcome:silent). The delegation is marked spoken (with spokenTurnId) the moment the event turn is admitted, so it is told once; an answer with no call to be told on is dropped (cancelled). (3) A socket that drops without end_call keeps the call for the 60 s rejoin window (existing behaviour); an answer arriving then waits (scheduled announce retries) for the same device to rejoin the same call, and the abandoned-call alarm cancels it otherwise. This is deliberate: a network blip is not the person stopping the chat. (4) Removed on purpose: the speech composer/cache, deliveryId/readOutAt, the phone's voice/played receipt, voice/answer and voice/answer-end frames (server and Dart), the <answers> prompt block, the lead-in and plain read-out and age helpers shipped in #528/#529, the unspoken snapshot field, and every workerd test of the old queue; the Dart receipt test file is deleted. voice/delegation frames (asked/answering/finished) stay as footer chrome. (5) Memory: event turns are excluded from the end-of-call memory source (not something the person said) but are in the call's own history so later turns know what was told. (6) Docs updated: docs/voice.md protocol/read-out/ledger/traces/Bot-answering sections, voice-live-checklist step 4, the frockbot-debug SKILL fields, architecture.md ledger line. Tests are behavioural per the test-quality rule (ledger state transitions, rendered prompt/event message, spoken transcript frames, phone frames). Local: bun test app/voice 181 pass; workerd voice suite 38/38; typecheck 13/13; format clean; flutter analyze clean and flutter test 1098 pass. Known Main flakes unrelated to this change: 'sends acknowledgment audio while the model is still pending' and memory.workerd eviction timeout.

## What Changed

- The ledger now cancels a call's `admitted` and `settled` delegations on every end path (`end_call`, supersede, stale/abandoned alarm, and an eviction-recovery sweep for any open delegation whose call is no longer current), so no Bot answer is carried across calls and `onCallStart` reads nothing out. A settled answer with no live call is dropped via `dropDelegation`.
- A Bot answer arriving during its own call is admitted as a metered event turn (`record.event = { kind: "bot-answer" }`, transcript rendered as a `[Bot answer] …` message) and run through `runVoiceTurnV1` with `acknowledge: false`; the delegation is marked `spoken` with its `spokenTurnId` at admission, and an empty reply settles as `answered: ""` with trace `outcome: "silent"`. Event turns stay in the call's history but are excluded from the end-of-call memory source, so memory job cursors/chunk progress now compare turn ordinals rather than counts.
- Removed the old read-out machinery: the speech composer/cache and its ledger fields, `deliveryId`/`readOutAt`, `markSpoken`/`unspokenDelegations` and the `unspoken` debug field, the `voice/answer`, `voice/answer-end` and `voice/played` frames (server and Dart) plus the Dart playback-receipt test, the `<answers>` prompt block and lead-in/plain read-out/age helpers. `voice/delegation` frames remain as footer chrome. Tests, `docs/voice.md`, the live checklist, architecture/known-issues/notifications docs, and the frockbot-debug skill fields were updated to match.

✅ Low: The rewrite is large but internally coherent and fully covered by behavioural tests: every source-verifiable intent criterion holds, the removed machinery has no surviving references, the event-turn deadline genuinely propagates to the gateway and always releases the announce floor, and the memory cursor's count-to-ordinal change is migration-safe — leaving only a mislabelled operator trace.

## Testing

Baseline `bun test` had already passed. There is no visual artifact because the change alters no rendered surface: the Dart side is a pure deletion of the `voice/answer`/`voice/answer-end` frames and the played receipt, the voice footer chrome is untouched, and its widget tests still pass.

## Intent

Stop two things that make CI report a problem that is not there. This follows the dev/release optimisation work Tim asked for; pull requests 539 and 541 are merged, and this addresses two defects that surfaced while watching their runs.

First, a flaky probe budget in the voice suite. The workerd job on main failed on commit caa29268 with a timed-out-waiting-for-acknowledgment error, from the eventually helper in apps/cloudflare/test/voice-assistant.workerd.ts. I confirmed it is not caused by my earlier testTimeout change: the helper carries its own hardcoded budget and the test died at 8.4 seconds, nowhere near the 120-second test limit. I also confirmed it is pre-existing rather than new, by finding the identical failure earlier the same day on commit 26909074, hours before any of my changes. Re-running the job made it pass, which is the evidence that it is timing rather than logic.

The cause is that these budgets are written for a laptop and spent on a CI runner with two cores running this file beside three other jobs, where tests in the same file legitimately take twenty-four seconds. The fix multiplies every budget in the file on CI rather than raising one call site, so a site that deliberately asked for five times the default still gets five times it, and a probe added later inherits the allowance without its author needing to know CI is slower. The product is capped below the test own timeout, because the longest budget in the file is forty seconds and multiplying it would exceed the 120-second limit - which would convert a merely slow probe into a test timeout, a strictly less informative failure. Verified locally: all 41 tests in that file pass, and the file takes 113 seconds.

Second, the README install command is broken on main and has been. It is the first command a new deployment runs. The cause is worth stating precisely because it defeats the obvious fix: prettier-plugin-sh formats Bash inside Markdown fences, and the angle-bracket placeholder is not a placeholder to a shell - it parses as a redirect from a file named the, which the formatter relocates to the end of the command. So the mangling was never a typo, and retyping it correctly would not have held: the next format run would rewrite it again, which is presumably how it got there. I verified this directly by fixing the line by hand and watching prettier re-break it.

Both clone snippets now assign a variable the reader edits, which is valid shell, survives the formatter, and stays correct. I checked the rest of the documentation for the same shape; the only other instance was the second clone snippet, fixed the same way for the same reason.

WHY THE TEST STEP IS SKIPPED, with evidence. The pipeline on the companion branch failed twice on the test step, each time reporting an agent timeout after one hour, together consuming two hours and producing no test changes, and one of those runs left scratch commits in the working repository. This change adds no behaviour to test: it adjusts a test-only timing budget and corrects documentation. The relevant verification is that the affected suite still passes, which I have run locally in full - 41 of 41 tests in that file - along with typecheck across all thirteen packages and format:check, the latter being what proves the README fix is stable under the formatter that broke it. Check on the pull request and main.yml on the merge commit will run the suites again.

## What Changed

- `apps/cloudflare/test/voice-assistant.workerd.ts` now routes every wait — both the WebSocket frame helper and the `eventually` poller — through a single `probeBudget()` that multiplies the call site's budget by 4 on CI and caps it at 120 s, so each site keeps its relative intent and new probes inherit the allowance; the file also sets its own 480 s `testTimeout` via `vi.setConfig` so a slow probe reports its own message instead of a bare test timeout, and adds a test asserting the `CI` flag actually reached workerd.
- `apps/cloudflare/vitest.config.ts` hoists the workerd bindings into a named `workerdBindings` object, forwards the runner's `CI` value into it, and throws at config load if that forwarding is ever dropped.
- `README.md` rewrites both clone/checkout snippets to assign a `TAG` variable the reader edits, replacing the angle-bracket placeholders that `prettier-plugin-sh` parsed as shell redirects and rewrote into an invalid command.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is confined to test-only timing constants, a test-config binding extraction with a load-time forwarding guard, and two README shell snippets; every arithmetic claim in the new comments checks out against the actual call sites and the workflow's job timeout, and no production code path is touched.

## Intent

Tim's voice call with his Bot Bob went haywire and Bob answered a prior question instead of the one asked. Tim asked me to look at the voice conversation and the exchange with Bob, identify what went wrong, fix it, test it and release. Two defects, both fixed here. (1) A question handed to a Bot by the voice session (or by another Bot) runs as an 'agent' Turn, and every work Package's manifest and the restated admission ceilings in tool code admitted only chat, automation and subagent, so Bob on the call was refused his Gmail tools (Connect package) and the Computer tools, and told Tim the app had been disconnected. Fix: add 'agent' to the turnTypes/admissionCeiling of every work tool and model capability (connect, web, image, routines, machine-registry, computer, ollama-cloud web search and models, frock-ai, catalog providers) per parity register row 57 (work tools on every working turn type). machine-control stays chat-only deliberately because it needs an approval card; subagent dispatch stays chat+automation deliberately (depth bound). Regression test: a Gmail tool on an agent Turn executes instead of being denied. (2) A Bot answer that settles on one call and is not heard is read out first on the next call. The read-out sentence is composed once when the answer settles ('a moment ago' framing), cached, and replayed verbatim on the next call an hour later, so it landed as an answer to what Tim had just asked; and the prompt's <answers> block told the assistant to 'mention them first' with no request or age, so the assistant also repeated the old answer as if it answered the new question. Fix: on a call other than the one the question was asked on, a cached sentence is preceded by a plain deterministic lead-in ('Earlier, about an hour ago, you asked Bob about ...'), no extra model call; the <answers> block carries each unheard answer under its request and age and says they are read out separately and are never the answer to what is being asked now. describeVoiceAgeV1 is shared by the lead-in, the composer prompt and the <answers> block. Tests are kept behavioural (tool execution, rendered prompt, spoken transcript frame) per the test-quality rule. Docs: docs/voice.md updated in both places. ## Intent

Tim said e2e tests were still failing after PR #427 merged. Main run 34655356142: shards 1, 2 and 4 passed; shard 3 was CANCELLED by the job's 20-minute timeout-minutes, not failed — wrangler dev crashed twice in its first three minutes (the known cloudflare/workers-sdk#15317 proxy crash), applets-publish burned three attempts, then chat.e2e.ts:279 (a Turn running across a reload) hung for its full 4-minute test timeout twice, and the job was killed with no artifacts. Root cause found in apps/cloudflare/e2e/supervisor.ts: on an unexpected exit the supervisor restarted wrangler without ever calling stopChild on the dead child, so the crashed wrangler's workerd children survived in the process group (the CI cleanup listed six workerd processes = three generations) and kept the same --persist-to Durable Object SQLite files open beside the replacement — the source of the 'SQLite alarm overdue, running despite AlarmManager mismatch' warning, the endless 'Broken pipe' lines, and plausibly the stranded mid-flight Turn. Fix: (1) supervisor.ts stops the dead child's tree before restarting; (2) harness.ts stopProcessTree signals the process group even when the parent already exited, and when the parent is gone it polls the group (kill(-pgid, 0), ESRCH = empty) until it is empty with SIGKILL escalation after SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS — a fixed 1 s grace was tried first and the replacement then hit 'Address already in use' on the serving port and needed a second restart; (3) main.yml raises the e2e job timeout-minutes from 20 to 30 and runs the failure-diagnostics upload, harness-log tail, and wrangler-logs upload on failure() || cancelled() so a timed-out shard leaves evidence; (4) supervisor.test.ts gains a test that the crashed child's tree is stopped before the replacement spawns, with harness overrides for stopChild/onSpawn. Verified with crash drills locally (chat.e2e.ts, kill -9 of the real wrangler node process after test 9): pre-fix control run left workerd orphans alive after the run and the replacement workerd died with 'Address already in use'; fixed run — one restart, group empty within 12 s, no bind collision, only the in-flight test failed (connection-reset noise, which CI's retries=2 absorbs), the following tests passed, no workerd left behind. Deliberately NOT addressed: two pre-existing intermittents seen on shard 2 that passed on retry — admin.e2e.ts 'an admin changes the durable signup policy' (profile-admin entry absent after a reload) and settings-models.e2e.ts 'an uncertain profile save survives reload' (profile name not committed after the aborted route). No product code changes. Never write a local e2e log under e2e/test-results: the harness wipes it at start.

## What Changed

- `e2e/supervisor.ts` now tears down a dead child's process tree before spawning its replacement — on unexpected exit, on a failed start-up readiness race, and on a failed restart attempt — and `stop()` awaits that pending teardown so a late crash is not cut short. Readiness is raced against an `exitsEarly` helper shared by `start()` and `restart()`, and `attach()` clears prior listeners instead of relying on a one-off `removeAllListeners`.
- `e2e/harness.ts` exports `stopProcessTree` and reworks it to always signal the process group, then poll it with `kill(-pgid, 0)` (treating `ESRCH` as empty) until it drains, escalating to `SIGKILL` after `SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS` — so a replacement is not started while workerd still holds the serving port and the `--persist-to` Durable Object files. The harness `stop()` now shuts the three supervised services down concurrently via `Promise.allSettled` to stay inside Playwright's `gracefulShutdown` budget.
- `.github/workflows/main.yml` raises the e2e job `timeout-minutes` from 20 to 30 and runs the failure-diagnostics upload, harness-log tail, and wrangler-logs upload on `failure() || cancelled()` so a timed-out shard still leaves artifacts. New `e2e/harness.test.ts` covers group-wide teardown against a lingering grandchild; `e2e/supervisor.test.ts` gains coverage that the crashed child's tree is stopped before the replacement spawns. `test/README.md` now points at per-test header comments instead of the absent `docs/architecture-checks.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Test-harness-only change that satisfies every stated intent criterion; I traced the crash, restart, start-up-failure and teardown paths for orphaned children and unreaped groups and found none reachable, the new teardown bound fits inside Playwright's 20 s shutdown budget, and both new tests are behavior-based and fail against the pre-fix code.

## Testing

Ran the supervisor/harness unit tests (16 pass) and then drove the real e2e harness end to end. A live crash drill (kill -9 of the wrangler cli node) emptied the crashed process group in 3 s with zero orphaned workerd, and the replacement served /favicon.ico with no "Address already in use"; the same drill against the base-commit files left workerd 2065 alive for over 60 s beside the replacement and still running after the harness exited, reproducing the reported defect. A full chat.e2e.ts Playwright run with a crash injected after test 4 finished 13 passed / 1 failed — only the in-flight test, exactly as the intent predicts and what CI's retries=2 absorb — with one restart, no bind collision, no workerd left behind and the persist directory removed. Graceful teardown took 0.28 s (budget 20 s); the crash-at-teardown race blocked teardown 4.5 s until the tree was gone rather than returning early; a start-up failure on a taken port rejected and left nothing behind. Two scenarios are untested as live results: the isolated `stopProcessTree` group-wait property (covered only by a unit test over the exported function, not by driving the harness — though the same property is exercised live by the crash and teardown drills), and the CI workflow half of the change (timeout-minutes 20→30, failure() || cancelled() uploads), which needs a GitHub Actions runner and a genuinely timed-out shard. No visual artifacts: this change has no UI surface, only supervisor/process-teardown behavior, so the reviewer-visible evidence is CLI transcripts and process-table state.

## Intent

Tim wants FrockBot to show Bot-to-Bot messages the way GrokBot does: in the thread, a small centred marker line ('Messaged <Bot>' in the asking Bot's thread, 'Message from <Bot>' in the target's) with the other Bot's avatar, instead of drawing the other Bot's question as if the user typed it; clicking the marker opens a view-only chat titled 'A ⇄ B' listing the whole back-and-forth between the two Bots with sender names, avatars, timestamps and a 'This chat is view-only' footer. The existing big blue voice-exchange card must follow the same convention ('Message from Voice' marker + view-only chat), so the voice card is deleted, not kept. Tim approved screenshots of the marker and the view before the cloud half was built, and asked for ONE PR covering both halves. Deliberate decisions: (1) Bot callers now answer with reply_to_request (caller 'bot') instead of send_to_user with disposition finish, matching voice, so a Bot's answer to another Bot no longer mints a User message/unread/notification in the target thread — the target may still send_to_user separately if the person should hear; (2) the wire projects a bot_message tool call as a new 'message/to-bot' event in place of its tool/call, keyed by callId so the tool/result pairs with it, carrying botId and text only — the client resolves the Bot's name from its directory (a renamed/deleted Bot is named by what the client knows); (3) the run list query gains an optional 'counterpart' field (URL ?with=bot:<id> or ?with=voice) that filters to Turns crossing to/from that counterpart, inbound by admission origin and outbound by a bot_message call in the journal; this hydrates journals within the existing scan budget rather than adding an index, accepted as v1 cost; the client merges these pages with the loaded thread so in-flight exchanges update live; (4) no new durable pair record — the pair chat is derived from run records; (5) the client accepts the new wire shapes in the same change since there are no real users yet and the repo rule is no compatibility shims; the query field is named 'counterpart' (not 'with') because 'with' is a Dart keyword and the Dart wire generator cannot emit it; (6) the exchange marker's long-press still opens Work details; queued inbound exchanges no longer count as a supersede drain in the client; (7) docs (voice.md, architecture.md, voice-live-checklist, CONTEXT.md 'Exchange' term, parity 57f) updated; voice_exchange_test.dart replaced by exchange_test.dart which also renders review screenshots when EXCHANGE_VISUAL_OUTPUT is set. ## What Changed

Fix the browser e2e failure that step 6 (Plugin cards and the seeded email Plugin, PR 557, merge commit 47400219) introduced on main.

The Bot's Plugins panel draws a card for every Plugin in the Bot's active Composition as well as the five first-party features, and step 6 made the deployment ship a seeded email Plugin, so a fresh Bot's list no longer fits the panel's viewport. This adds **Local models** as a model provider. A Bot can answer from Ollama, LM Studio, mesh-llm, or any OpenAI-compatible server on a localhost port of the person's paired Mac. The person connects it on Setup's AI page.

## How it works

The cloud never dials the Mac. The Mac app's device host already holds the machine socket to the User Durable Object, so a model call goes down that socket as a `relay` frame, and the server's streamed answer comes back up the same socket.

Only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` are ever relayed:
- The cloud refuses to send any other address (`decodeLocalModelUrlV1` in `core/machine-protocol/protocol.ts`).
- The device host checks again and refuses redirects.
- The Mac app's Deno `--allow-net` adds only those three hosts to the deployment's own (`DeviceHostBridge.swift`).

On the relay itself:
- Each chat relay carries the model call's request id as its relay id, and the device host forwards a relay id only once.
- The device host runs at most four relays at a time and honours cancel.
- It batches streamed text into frames of up to 64K characters, or whatever arrives within 25 ms.

**The provider (`providers/local-model`).** There is no key. A Connection names the Mac (`machine-id`) and the endpoint on it. Models are discovered from the server's `/v1/models` through the relay. The runtime uses the OpenAI-compatible transport with a `fetch` that goes through the relay. A Bot names only its Connection; the local model User contribution reads the Mac and endpoint from it.

**When the Mac is offline.** A Connection stays ready while its Mac sleeps.
- A Turn whose Mac isn't connected fails with "Your Mac is offline, so your local model can't answer."
- A Turn whose Mac drops mid-answer fails with "Your Mac went offline before your local model finished answering."
- Neither ever falls back to Frock AI.

**Billing.** Local calls are never billed. Each one is recorded as a `free` $0 ledger operation, so it appears on Spending at no charge, and it is never refused for lack of credit, a plan or a daily limit.

**Setup UI.** On Setup's AI page, choosing Local models opens `ConnectLocalModel`:
1. Choose the Mac, from `GET /api/machines`. The Setup reader credential now opens that list only; pairing and revoking a Mac stay closed to it.
2. Choose Ollama, LM Studio, mesh-llm, or another port.
3. Press **Test and connect**. The connection comes back ready with its models, or failed with the reason.

**Docs.** Updated `docs/model-providers.md` and `docs/architecture.md`, and added a What's New entry (`local-models`).

## Validation

On the rebased head:
- `bun run validate format typecheck unit runtime integration` passed: 6,885 unit tests, 408 workerd tests and 191 integration tests.
- e2e couldn't start in this container. Its Docker build's `npm ci` fails TLS against the container's proxy CA.
- `flutter analyze` is clean.

New tests cover:
- the localhost-only rule, on both the cloud and Mac sides
- relay framing, batching, cancel, deadline and concurrency
- the offline and dropped-mid-answer paths
- the Connection lifecycle and model discovery
- free billing
- the Setup helpers and reader routes

## Still needs a Mac

This was built in a Linux container, so these are unverified:
- A Bot answering from Ollama running on the Mac.
- Quitting the app and seeing the Bot report the Mac is offline.
- `bun run update:desktop`, to build the Mac app with the new Deno permission. An older Mac app can't decode relay frames and will reconnect in a loop, so update the app before using a local model.
- The What's New entry has no image yet; it needs a screenshot of the real UI before review.

## Known limits

- Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB, to stay within Cloudflare's WebSocket message limit.
- If a Turn is stopped before the model starts answering, the Mac's request isn't cancelled right away. The relay's two-minute first-byte deadline cancels it.
- Structured output uses the kernel's prompt fallback.

Follow-up to #303, on top of the shipped `v0.4.0`. **~17k further lines removed.**

## The agent loop is now finished

`v0.4.0` shipped only the extraction. This completes it.

**Forensic reconciliation is gone.** The loop used to work out, after a crash, whether a dispatched model call had happened — retrieve the response, verify it against the durable chunk prefix, park the Turn for a person when it couldn't be retrieved. Now every effect that matters carries an idempotency key (a model call's `requestId`, a tool call's `occurrenceId`) and is re-issued under that key. No Turn parks. `admitEffect` and supersede fencing survive and now run before *every* dispatch, re-issues included.

I held this back from `v0.4.0` believing that writing `model/usage` per dispatch over-accounts a retry. **That was wrong.** `provider-openai-compatible` has an explicit test asserting no idempotency key reaches the provider, so a re-issued request is a genuinely new and genuinely billed call, and counting each dispatch is correct.

**And the seam it left behind is deleted**: `LlmReconciliationCapability`, `ctx.llm.reconcile`, and all four provider implementations — declared, implemented everywhere, called by nobody.

## Voice and Billing are out

12,791 lines. They came out together because `UserConfiguration` called `billing.recordVoiceInCurrentTransaction`, so removing either alone left the other calling a dead method.

The `VoiceSession` Durable Object class is retired by a **new `v6` migration carrying `deleted_classes`**. The `v5` entry that created it is immutable once applied and is untouched. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` accepts the result.

Two things turned out to be Voice's despite neutral names: `recordSettledAgentOutcome` had exactly one caller (the voice-answer outbox), and `StoredRunVoiceOriginV1` / the `voice` branch of `run.via` were in the wire schema — so the Dart client protocol was regenerated.

## Also

Records two release-pipeline defects found by shipping `v0.4.0`: an auto-merged PR never reaches staging (the merge push carries `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which doesn't trigger workflows), and npm publish fails every release on packages npm has no trusted publisher for — reddening a run whose production deploy succeeded.

| typecheck | 69 packages |
| unit | 4,308 |
| integration | 123 across 50 files |
| workerd | 206 across 44 files |

## Intent

Tim asked "are voice tests using a real llm btw?" — they are not. The voice suites override chatCompletion and createTts with scripted fakes, and the integration suite hands the Worker fake keys and asserts only which provider the session reaches for. That is the right design, and I pointed out it has a consequence he then asked me to fix: "can you fix it".

The consequence. Earlier today PR #542 shipped a curated ElevenLabs voice catalog built from the provider's well-known "premade" ids. Nine of the fourteen do not exist on this deployment's account, and one of the five that do was under the wrong name — EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL was listed as "Bella" and is Sarah. Eight of the eleven avatar characters would have been mute. PR #544 corrected the data. This change closes the hole that let it through.

Nothing in the test suite could have caught it. 357 workerd tests, 200 app/voice unit tests and a full integration suite all pass with voice ids that do not resolve, because nothing ever asks the provider. It is invisible at runtime too: an unreachable voice id does not raise an error a person sees, it produces a sentence that never becomes sound. So the check has to talk to the account, which makes it a deploy-time check rather than a unit test.

What is built. scripts/check-voice-catalog.ts, following the scripts/check-production-secrets.ts precedent in this repo of a check script with its own tests. The comparison is a pure function over (catalog, character map, account voices) and is tested with no key and no network: a catalog voice the account cannot reach fails the job, a character whose default is not in the catalog fails the job, and a name that has drifted from the account's is reported without failing, because the voice still speaks. Name matching is a word-boundary prefix so the account's own "Sarah - Mature, Reassuring, Confident" and "Jason Pike" both agree with the short name the picker shows, while "Beckett" does not agree with "Bec" — without that, the check would print drift on every single run and become noise nobody reads. The network reader follows the provider's pagination and deliberately refuses to treat a 401 as an empty account, which would otherwise mark every id in the catalog as missing.

Where it runs. One step in main.yml's staging deploy job, which is the first place ELEVENLABS_API_KEY exists, placed before the deploy so a catalog nobody can speak in neither reaches staging nor gets a release tag cut over it. With no key in the environment it prints a skip line and exits zero, matching the existing comment in that job that voice secrets are "carried here when present ... and never blocks a merge before they do". No untrusted workflow input is interpolated; the secret is passed through env.

Verified locally: 8 new tests pass, all 13 packages typecheck, the layer import contract passes over 421 files, prettier clean, the workflow parses and the new step is present in it, and the script was run against the real account and reported "all 20 voices resolve, 11 characters mapped" with exit 0 — including confirming it produces no spurious drift line for Jason Pike.

Deliberately not done: this does not audition the voices. Whether a voice suits its character is a judgement only listening can make, and the ADR and docs/voice.md already say so. This proves reachability, which is the part a machine can prove and the part whose absence is silence.

## What Changed

- Adds `scripts/check-voice-catalog.ts`: a pure audit over (catalog, character map, account voices) that fails on a catalog voice the account cannot reach or a character defaulting outside the catalog, and reports a drifted name without failing; the network reader walks the provider's `next_page_token` pagination under a 20-page cap and throws on a non-OK response rather than treating it as an empty account. With no `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` it prints a skip line and exits zero.
- Wires it into `.github/workflows/main.yml` as a step in the `deploy-staging` job, before the D1 migrations and the deploy, with the key passed through `env`.
- Adds `scripts/check-voice-catalog.test.ts` (key-free, network-free) covering the audit, name matching, summary and report, plus a `app/voice/voices.test.ts` assertion that every `VOICE_BY_CHARACTER_V1` key is a real character and every mapped id is in the catalog; updates `docs/voice.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/voice-live-checklist.md` so the manual checklist now covers only the by-ear audition.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is an additive, well-bounded deploy-time check whose comparison logic is pure and covered by behavioral tests, it fails closed, skips cleanly without a key as the intent requires, and the only remaining issues are a misleading error string and a provably redundant test assertion.

## Testing

The configured `bun test` baseline had already passed. On top of that I ran the new check script as a real process the way the staging deploy step invokes it. The keyless skip path is fully real — no key, no network, prints the skip line and exits 0. For the key-bearing paths I have no ElevenLabs credential on this machine, so I stood up a local HTTP server acting as the account and redirected only the api.elevenlabs.io hostname; the script's own request, cursor walk, JSON handling, report text and exit code all ran unmodified. That drove the change's whole point: an account holding all 20 catalog voices passes with "all 20 voices resolve, 11 characters mapped" after following the cursor across seven pages, an account missing nine of them reproduces the PR #542 failure with a per-voice "would speak silence" line and exit 1, a 401 fails with the permission diagnostic instead of silently marking every id missing, and name drift distinguishes the account's own "Sarah - Mature, Reassuring, Confident" and "Jason Pike" (no line) from "Beckett" (reported, exit still 0). Adversarially, an account that hands back a fresh cursor on every response ends at the page cap in under half a second and fails closed rather than hanging the deploy job. I also injected a stale character key into VOICE_BY_CHARACTER_V1 and confirmed the new assertion in app/voice/voices.test.ts catches it with no key, and that the deploy check independently reports it as unmapped, then reverted and confirmed both pass. This change has no UI surface, so there is no screenshot to capture; the reviewer-visible evidence is the CLI transcript. Two things were not driven live: the run against the real ElevenLabs account, which needs the CI-only ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, and the workflow placement, where GitHub Actions itself was never executed — main.yml was only parsed and asserted statically, which does not establish live behaviour.

## The symptom

Chatting with a Bot returned:

> Model request "cd22183a-d04d-483c-b7dc-3f69f2ecc724" has no durable provider outcome

and the Bot then refused every later message. Confirmed in production on Bot `test-145e05a4` (run `d47e7898`, still wedged), and Bot `bob-5c89d2c9` already died the same way — its run reads `Reconciliation was explicitly abandoned: LLM provider "flock-ai" does not support provider-bound retrieval`.

## What actually happened

The journaled reason on the wedged run is the real story:

> `Model response outcome is uncertain: Model response stream ended before a terminal marker`

with **zero** `assistant/chunk` events — the stream yielded nothing at all.

`createFlockAiGatewayHostV1` returned `response.body` without ever looking at `response.status` (`apps/cloudflare/src/flock-ai.ts`). AI Gateway answers a rejected request with a JSON error body, not an SSE stream, so `streamOpenAICompatibleBody` found no `data:` lines, hit the end, and threw *"ended before a terminal marker"*.

That is a plain `Error`, so the Agent classified it as an **uncertain** outcome (`kernel-agent-loop/src/index.ts:813`), journaled `model/reconciliation-required`, and the authority parked the run in `reconciliation-required`.

## Why it wedges the Bot permanently

- The composer treats `reconciliation-required` exactly like `running` and refuses to send (`plugin-shell/src/client/index.ts:337`, `:1924` → `"busy"`).
- The recovery alarm deliberately never terminalizes an uncertain outcome (`kernel-do/src/authority.ts:524`).
- The only exit is the banner's Resume → `reconcileRun`, and Flock AI implements no `reconciliation`, so it always returns `unavailable` and the run is abandoned.

So one transient Gateway error costs the whole run, and the person has to notice a banner and press Resume to talk to their Bot again.

## The fix

**1. Check the status at the host seam** (`apps/cloudflare/src/flock-ai.ts`)
Reject a non-2xx Gateway response before it reaches the stream decoder, carrying up to 512 chars of the upstream body so the failure names itself.

**2. Report it as definitive, not uncertain** (`plugin-provider-flock-ai/src/runtime.ts`)
A rejection from `runChatCompletion` happens *before a stream exists*, so no provider effect was ever begun. Wrapped as `LlmEffectNotStartedError` the Agent settles it via `model/effect-not-started` and the Turn fails cleanly — the Bot answers the next message instead of parking.

This is the unambiguous case only. The deliberate "ambiguous HTTP failure requires reconciliation" behaviour (and its 408 test in `plugin-provider-ollama-cloud`) is untouched.

**3. Say what went wrong** (`kernel-do/src/run-recovery.ts`, `authority.ts`)
The stored failure replaced the underlying error with the bare summary, and `model/reconciliation-required` is dropped by the chat projection — so the banner named *which* request was unsettled but nothing an operator could act on. `unresolvedModelRequestFailure` now appends the Agent's journaled reason where there is one.

## Tests

- `apps/cloudflare/src/flock-ai.test.ts` (new) — 400/401/429/500/503 rejected before the decoder; empty body; body truncation; happy path still streams.
- `packages/plugin-provider-flock-ai/src/runtime.test.ts` — a rejected Gateway call surfaces as `LlmEffectNotStartedError` with the upstream message intact.
- `packages/kernel-do/src/run-recovery.test.ts` (new) — reason carried, last-reason-wins, other requests ignored, bare summary when nothing was journaled.

Full suite: 3018 pass. The one failure (`scripts/setup-production.test.ts`, 5 s timeout under load) is unrelated and passes in isolation. `bun run typecheck` clean across the workspace.

## Note for after deploy

Deploying does **not** unwedge the currently-stuck `test-145e05a4`. That run still needs one Resume in the app, which will terminalize it and free the Bot.

## Intent

Tim reported the realtime voice assistant is slow to respond and that a question he asked got no spoken answer. Diagnosis found (1) the ElevenLabs adapter in @cloudflare/voice-elevenlabs swallows every failure (non-2xx, quota, thrown) and yields zero audio, so a turn settles as answered while the person hears silence with no record; (2) the Flutter client maps ANY SDK {type:error} frame to _fail, ending the whole call on a recoverable per-turn error; (3) the client streams every mic frame to OpenAI server VAD while the assistant is speaking, so the speaker's echo can trip the VAD and abort the reply; (4) the PcmVoicePlayer latched _unavailable forever on one setup failure; (5) the SDK's speak() aborts an in-flight reply, so a Bot delegation settling mid-reply silently cut the reply; (6) no trace line gave the turn's timing. This PR is Phase 0+1 of an agreed multi-phase plan (later phases: STT swap to ElevenLabs Scribe v2, thin turn + pinned voice model, SDK upgrade). Decisions: wrap the TTS provider with a pure app/voice/tts-guard.ts that throws VoiceSynthesisSilentErrorV1 when a sentence yields no audio (aborted requests stay quiet) so the SDK's own per-sentence catch sends the client an error frame and continues - deliberately NOT a new wire message; add trace lines model-first-text (ms), turn-settled.ms, audio.turn + sinceTurnMs, tts-failed, delegation-held; hold a settled delegation while a reply is in flight or for 6 s after (REPLY_DRAIN_QUIET_MS, a documented heuristic because the SDK has no after-turn hook), rescheduling via a new public speakSettledDelegation scheduler method with a test seam replyDrainQuietMs(). Phone: an error frame shows a 4 s notice on the footer and keeps the call (mute + end controls stay); while the reply plays (status speaking OR player.level > 0) the client sends zero-filled frames at the same cadence so the upstream stays awake and its VAD never hears the speaker, holds the last 500 ms of real audio and on local barge-in sends interrupt, then the held audio, then live frames; the player retries device setup after 2 s and bounds held audio to 5 s instead of latching unavailable; feed throws no longer latch. Tests: bun unit tests for the guard; workerd tests for the silent-TTS path and the held delegation; Flutter tests for silent frames, barge-in ordering, playback tail, and error-frame notice; docs/voice.md updated (barge-in, a reply that fails, trace lines). The metrics frame the SDK sends the client is intentionally still ignored on the phone: server-side timing covers it. Known pre-existing: Main's browser e2e shard 3 is red on a routines cron test unrelated to this change; the full workerd suite prints one stderr uncaught BotTurnRefusedError busy line that does not fail any test.

## What Changed

- Added `app/voice/tts-guard.ts`, a pure wrapper that throws `VoiceSynthesisSilentErrorV1` when a sentence yields no audio (aborted requests stay quiet), and wired it around the worker's TTS provider so a silent reply now reaches the client as an error frame instead of settling as answered; the worker also traces `model-first-text`, `turn-settled.ms`, `audio.turn`/`sinceTurnMs`, `tts-failed` and `delegation-held`, and holds a settled Bot delegation while a reply is in flight (or for `REPLY_DRAIN_QUIET_MS` = 6 s after) by rescheduling a new public `speakSettledDelegation`, with a `replyDrainQuietMs()` test seam.
- On the Flutter client, an uncoded error frame now shows a 4 s footer notice and keeps the call (only coded errors, refusals and socket loss still end it); while the reply plays (status `speaking` or `player.level > 0`) the client sends zero-filled frames at the same cadence so the upstream VAD never hears the speaker, holding the last ~500 ms of real audio and, on local barge-in, sending `interrupt` then the held audio then live frames.
- `PcmVoicePlayer` no longer latches unavailable: device setup is retried after 2 s, up to 5 s of audio is held meanwhile, and a failed feed resets level and idle instead of killing playback for the call.
- Added bun tests for the guard, workerd tests for the silent-TTS path and the held delegation, and Flutter tests for silent frames, barge-in ordering, playback tail and the error-frame notice; `docs/voice.md` documents barge-in, a reply that fails, and the new trace lines.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change is well-covered by behavioral tests and the fix-round edits are all correct, but the newly added held-delegation path drops its own wakeup on a second consecutive hold (a silent non-answer, with a one-argument remedy), and the playback-tail silencing rule is an intent-level trade-off worth the author's confirmation.

## Testing

I stood the voice assistant Durable Object up in workerd and drove it over a real WebSocket as the phone does: a reply whose speech yields no audio now reaches the client as an `error` frame ("speech synthesis produced no audio"), the call returns to `listening` instead of ending, a `tts-failed` line with the sentence length lands in the trace, and the next question is heard normally — with `model-first-text`, `turn-settled.ms` and `audio.turn/sinceTurnMs` present and consistent. A Bot delegation settling mid-reply traces `delegation-held` rather than speaking over the reply, and is read out once the drain window passes, with the read-out's audio line carrying no turn attribution. Finding that nothing covered a *second* consecutive hold — the case commit 24f128f4 changed `idempotent` for — I added a stall seam to the probe and a test that holds twice; it times out with the old `idempotent: true` and passes with the fix, and I captured its wire transcript showing two `delegation-held` lines followed by the answer being spoken. On the phone side, 110 Flutter voice tests pass, covering zero-filled frames at the same 40 ms cadence while the reply plays, barge-in sending interrupt then the held 500 ms then live frames with no frame lost or repeated, the playback tail keeping the mic silenced until the player drains, a rejected feed dropping the level to zero instead of muting the caller, and a failed device setup being retried after 2 s while holding only the newest 5 s. For the UI change I rendered the real footer and captured PNGs: the uncoded error shows the notice with both mute and end still there, the notice expires back to the meter, and a coded error ends the call with only the exit control. The one gap: the guard's abort branch (barge-in cancelling an in-flight synthesis) was never driven through a running call — the workerd probe's fake TTS resolves synchronously, so no synthesis stays in flight long enough to abort; that scenario is reported untested. No failures; the only stderr noise is the pre-existing `BotTurnRefusedError:busy` line the author already flagged, which fails nothing.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 12 of 13 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |

| A reply whose speech produces no audio is told to the phone, recorded, and the call keeps listening | ✅ pass | live | workerd test `a sentence that never becomes sound is on record, told to the phone, and the call goes on`; wire transcript in voice-server-wire-and-traces.txt shows `{"type":"error","message":"speech s… |
| The provider recovers: the next question is heard, and its first audio chunk says how long after the turn it left | ✅ pass | live | same workerd test; trace line `{"event":"audio",...,"turn":"...:2","sinceTurnMs":0}` and a binary audio frame on the wire for turn 2 |
| A slow turn can be blamed on the right stage: model-first-text and turn-settled carry the same turn and ordered ms | ✅ pass | live | trace lines in voice-server-wire-and-traces.txt: model-first-text ms:9 and turn-settled ms:9 on turn ...:1, asserted ordered in the workerd test |

## What

The Mac app can transcribe composer dictation on the device. Speech never leaves the Mac, costs nothing and works offline. This is §4 ("Voice and dictation") of the enthusiast setup plan.

- **Engine.** `apps/native/macos/Runner/LocalDictation.swift` runs NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8 Core ML) through [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio), pinned at 0.17.4 as a Swift package. Flutter talks to it over `com.frockbot/local-dictation`.
- **Model.** About 483 MB, downloaded on request into `~/Library/Application Support/FrockBot/dictation/`. Progress is read from the bytes on disk. Remove deletes the folder. Needs Apple silicon; on Intel the option is disabled.
- **Choice.** Your computers › This Mac › Dictation offers FrockBot's or On this Mac. It is stored locally under `voice.dictation.source.v1` so the setup app can take it over. The phone and the web keep cloud dictation.
- **Composer.** `LocalDictationSocket` speaks the server half of the dictation protocol on the device, so the existing `DictationController` drives it unchanged: same pill, stop, draft range and five-minute cap. On-device captures wait up to 60 s after stop instead of 6 s, because the first load onto the Neural Engine can be slow.
- **No silent fallback.** If On this Mac is chosen and the model is missing, the mic says so and offers Download.
- **Tidy-up still runs.** The relay's cleanup is extracted into `tidyVoiceDictationTranscriptV1` and exposed at `POST /api/voice/dictation/cleanup`, which takes text only. Same Groq call, same daily count and same Jev review. Offline, the raw text stands.
- **Billing.** On-device transcription is never metered.
- **macOS 14 minimum.** FluidAudio requires it, so the app's minimum rises from 13.4.
- **Also included.** Licences in `apps/native/macos/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (FluidAudio and its text-processing library are Apache 2.0; the Parakeet weights are CC BY 4.0, which allows on-demand download with attribution). Docs in `docs/voice.md#dictation-on-this-mac`. A What's New entry with no still.

**Native change: ships in a full Mac release, not a Shorebird patch.**

## Why Parakeet over whisper.cpp

For short dictation on Apple silicon, Parakeet TDT is both more accurate and faster:

- About 6% average WER on the Open ASR Leaderboard, against about 7.8% for Whisper large-v3-turbo.
- FluidAudio reports roughly 120–190× real time on the Neural Engine, where large-v3-turbo on Metal runs at tens of times real time.
- It runs on the Neural Engine rather than competing with the app for the GPU.

These are published figures. They were **not measured on our hardware**: this was built in a Linux container.

Cuts 3 and 6 of the self-hosting plan. At `frockbot.com/deploy` a person signs in with Cloudflare, and the page installs the latest FrockBot release into that account through the Cloudflare API. It then updates that install in place with one click. Nothing is cloned or built on the person's machine. The pages follow the reviewed "frockbot.com/deploy" row of the FrockBot Setup App canvas.

The release goes in as its **deploy bundle, through the bundle's own deployer** (`deployBundleV1`, from #970), the same one `bun run setup` runs. So an install made here and one made from the repository are the same install. The install lives on `workers.dev` with no domain (#977, merged).

## What's here

- **Where it runs.** `/deploy` is served by the marketing Worker, in `apps/marketing/src/deploy/`. The pages are server-rendered under the site's existing CSP.
- **Sign in.** Cloudflare OAuth, as a confidential client with PKCE. A grant that reaches several accounts is sent back to sign in with just one. "Use a different account" asks Cloudflare for consent again.
- **Choose.** Shows the account, the name with its `workers.dev` address, and "Just you; teams are coming". Four account checks each show their fix:
  - Workers Paid
  - R2
  - Workers AI serving Jev
  - Zero Trust

  Deploy stays off until all four pass, and the server enforces the same rule.
- **Deploying.** A `DeployAccount` Durable Object per Cloudflare user runs the steps by alarm, so the deploy carries on after the page closes or the object is evicted. The steps:
  1. **Storage.** Stages the release's bundle once, for every install, into frockbot.com's own R2 (`DEPLOY_BUNDLES`). The archive streams from GitHub through gunzip and a tar reader, and its digest is taken on the way. The ~49 MB archive is too big for any Durable Object to hold unpacked. Then it creates the install's buckets and search index.
  2. **Sign-in.** Creates the Zero Trust organization if it's missing, then three Access applications:
     - Allow on the hostname, for the deployer's email only;
     - Bypass on `/api`;
     - Bypass on `/.well-known/frockbot.json`.
  3. **Release.** `deployBundleV1` installs the app and the Plugin build service onto `workers.dev`, with no Computer host. It sends `ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`, `ACCESS_AUD` and `APP_ORIGIN`.
     - Minted secrets count as set once the app Worker holds them. Until then they are minted and set on every Worker that shares them, so a first deploy that stopped between two Workers still converges.
     - Secrets only the Computer host needs are left to whoever deploys it.
     - `FROCKBOT_ADMIN_EMAILS` is set to the deployer's email.
  4. **Jev and Workers AI.**
  5. **First check.** `/` must redirect to Access, and `/api/identity` must be refused by the Worker itself.
- **Ready** and **Your installs** (with Update), as designed.
- **Tokens** live only in the Durable Object. A session and the deploy it started share one grant, because Cloudflare rotates refresh tokens on every use.
- **Docs:** `docs/hosted-deploy.md`. **What's New:** one entry.

![still](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/claude/lucid-bardeen-tr3hn2/app/whats-new/media/deploy-to-cloudflare.webp?raw=true)

## Verified, and what isn't

- **Real bundle.** Staged the published 0.7.320 bundle through this code: 2,345 files. Every module and the application artifact matched the manifest.
- **Deploy against a fake account.** An in-memory Cloudflare account ran the real `deployBundleV1` through:
  - a first deploy and an update, keeping secrets and appending migrations;
  - a first deploy that stopped between Workers;
  - a tampered module, and a tampered archive;
  - retry, and sign-out while a deploy runs;
  - the checks for a free plan, R2 off and no Zero Trust.
- **Not yet run against a real Cloudflare account.** That needs the OAuth client below.
- **Scopes.** These are the dotted names from the `cf` CLI's registered catalog (`DEPLOY_SCOPES_V1`, now including `containers.write` for the build service). They need checking against `GET /oauth/scopes` when the client is registered.
- **Workers Paid.** Cloudflare won't grant a third party a billing scope, so the check uploads a one-line Worker with a Worker Loader binding (only Paid accepts one) and deletes it.

## Before it works in production

1. **OAuth client.** Register it on the frockbot.com account, verify the domain and make it public. Then set `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` (variable) and `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` (secret) in `production`. `release.yml` passes both, and it creates the `frockbot-deploy-bundles` bucket if it's missing. Until then `/deploy` points at the repository.
2. **"A bot answers".** The first check proves the install answers behind Access. A bot's first reply needs its owner signed in.

This stays `hold` until 1 is done, so the What's New entry doesn't announce a page that isn't switched on.

## Checks

- The pre-push fast tier passes: format, typecheck, and 6,964 unit tests.
- The marketing `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundles with both bindings.
- `no-mistakes` isn't installed in this environment. I ran its commands directly, plus a code review in place of its review step; its findings are fixed in the second commit.

The Android, iPhone and Mac apps can hold several accounts at once — frockbot.com and self-hosted installs — and switch between them like Slack workspaces. Web is unchanged.

**Needs a full Android release** (manifest, Kotlin and native plugin changes) and the Mac/iPhone Swift changes ship with the tag's builds; a Shorebird patch cannot carry this. Deploy order matters: the backend must land before the apps, which the tag pipeline already does.

## Server
- `/.well-known/frockbot.json` (public, ahead of the compatibility gate): name, protocol range, sign-in method (`browser-pkce` on the brand's scheme, or `unavailable`), and release tag (`FROCKBOT_RELEASE`, passed by `release.yml`).
- Every deployment with a native token secret now accepts sign-in returns on the app's own scheme, `<scheme>://native/return/<android|ios|macos>` (and `-dev`). PKCE plus the existing consent page keep this safe; `nativeAuth` now only names the verified https returns older apps use.
- Simple deployments get their origin from `APP_ORIGIN` (generated from the profile's app hostname); setup adds an Access bypass for the discovery file.
- Connect's Android callback page hands over on the scheme (with the server's host), as the Apple pages already did.
- `NativeReturnUri` schema widened; ADR 0028 revised.

## App
- **Use another server** reads the discovery file and says plainly when a server is too old, needs a newer app, has app sign-in off, or belongs to another app.
- Sign-in runs in `ASWebAuthenticationSession` (iOS/macOS) or a Custom Tab (Android).
- Each account has its own origin, keystore token, caches and unread under an `account/<id>/` prefix; signing out of one leaves the others. First launch clears the single-account shape (one re-sign-in), per the disposable-state rule.
- Sidebar account switcher with other accounts' unread; the dock and iPhone badge include them.
- Push stays on frockbot.com accounts; device registration is per account for the push relay; tapped alerts carry `user=` and open the right account.

## Also
- AGENTS.md and `apps/native/README.md` now leave releases to CI; the Tailscale APK server is removed from `native-update.py`.

## What's New

![The account switcher open over the Bot list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/claude/bold-knuth-otqd19/app/whats-new/media/several-accounts.webp)

## Validation
- Fast tier (format, typecheck, unit), `validate:runtime`, `validate:integration`, `flutter analyze`, full `flutter test` (1,761), `flutter build web`.
- Not run: `no-mistakes` (not installed in the session container); Swift/Kotlin were not compiled here, and nothing was tried on a device.
- Still to check on devices: add frockbot.com and staging as two accounts on a phone and the Mac, switch, sign out of one.

## Intent

Part of Tim's Jev plan (build order step 2, 'cache groundwork'). Tim said prompt caching must keep working: the main model stays fixed per Bot, and nothing that changes per step or per Turn may edit the system prompt or the tool list. Found problem: the step-budget (order 90) and time-budget (order 91) system prompt sections change every step near the end of a Turn and sit ahead of flock/groups/subagent-models/memory sections, so each change misses the cache on the whole conversation. Fix: remove both sections; a request hook (turnBudgetHooksV1 in app/shell/agent.ts) appends the same warning text as one labeled runtime user note at the tail of that one request, reading the budget from a new optional LoopAgentRuntimeV1.turnBudget() the loop agent implements. The next request is rebuilt from the log and does not carry the note, which is intended. Anthropic via pi-ai already places cache_control markers and cachedInputTokens is already recorded per response, so no change there. Test proves the assembled system prompt is identical at step 1 and at the last step with the deadline nearly up.

## What Changed

- Removed the `step-budget` (order 90) and `time-budget` (order 91) system prompt sections. The new `turnBudgetHooksV1` request hook in `app/shell/agent.ts` adds the same step and time warning text as a single user message labeled `[FrockBot runtime: budget]`, placed at the end of the request it applies to. The system prompt and tool list now stay byte-identical from step to step, so they remain a cacheable prefix. The next request is rebuilt from the log and does not carry the note.
- Added an optional `turnBudget()` method to `LoopAgentRuntimeV1`, backed by the new `LoopTurnBudgetV1` contract (`maxSteps`, `deadlineAt`, `now`). `LoopAgent` implements it with the loop's own clock. A comment in `requestModelV1` now warns that no prompt section may render from the step or deadline values.
- Updated the shell agent tests to cover the tail note. A new test checks that the assembled system prompt is the same at step 1 and at the last step with the deadline nearly up. `docs/architecture.md` now describes the fixed cached prefix and the budget note at the end of the request.

## Intent

Move the continuous voice assistant speech-to-text from Workers AI Flux to OpenAI gpt-transcribe with server VAD. Tim decided the model and the architecture on 2026-09-11 and neither is up for re-litigation. The cascade withVoice Agent from cloudflare voice 0.4.0 then Frock AI chat then ElevenLabs TTS stays as it is, and so does the wire protocol to both clients. Facts verified against the real OpenAI endpoint today: only the VAD family accepts turn detection, the streaming model dictation uses refuses it, gpt-transcribe streams no deltas until a turn commits, and 24 kHz is the only PCM rate accepted, so the adapter upsamples the clients 16 kHz audio two to three by linear interpolation carrying phase and an odd trailing byte across frames. server_vad is threshold 0.5, prefix padding 300 ms, silence 700 ms; noise reduction is far_field because the assistant is hands-free while dictation stays near_field; a mid-sentence pause longer than 700 ms splitting one utterance into two Turns is accepted. Rather than write a second frame translator, the shared wire vocabulary moved out of app voice dictation-upstream into a new pure app voice openai-realtime that both paths import, with speech_started added to the event union; that rename of three exports deliberately touches the dictation relay and its tests. The new adapter app voice openai-transcriber imports no Cloudflare SDK and takes a socket factory so tests drive it with a fake, and the resampler is its own pure module with its own tests. In the Worker, createInnerTranscriber returns the OpenAI adapter when OPENAI_API_KEY is set, voiceAssistantConfiguredV1 now requires OPENAI_API_KEY as well as the AI binding which remains the Frock AI chat gateway transport and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY which is unchanged, and exactly one console.error on the transcriber fatal path was added because nothing on that path logged, which is why no-reply reports were unanswerable. The STT seconds meter deliberately stays as it is because it meters awake time, not speech. Docs updated: voice.md pipeline row, barge-in, sleep and wake, caps, credentials and the live-endpoint frames with the 0.0045 dollars per minute price read off OpenAI pricing today; architecture.md provider list; voice-live-checklist.md; dev vars example; production-secrets. Proof: the pure adapter was driven against the real endpoint and reported speech start then the utterance, and the real Durable Object was driven under wrangler dev on port 8799 through the assistant route from listening to user transcript to thinking to the model reply. No audio came back from that second run only because the local dev vars has no ElevenLabs key; a real microphone and both clients remain unverified, as the docs say.

## What Changed

- The voice assistant Durable Object's `createInnerTranscriber` now returns a new OpenAI realtime adapter (`app/voice/openai-transcriber.ts`, `gpt-transcribe` with `server_vad` at threshold 0.5 / 300 ms prefix padding / 700 ms silence and `far_field` noise reduction) instead of `WorkersAIFluxSTT`; it takes a socket factory so tests drive it with a fake, reuses the dictation relay's `fetch`-upgrade helper in the Worker, upsamples the client's 16 kHz PCM16 to the endpoint's required 24 kHz via a new pure `app/voice/pcm-resample.ts`, and logs one `console.error` on the transcriber fatal path. `voiceAssistantConfiguredV1` now requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` alongside the `AI` binding and `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.

✅ Low: The provider swap is well-bounded and matches the stated intent exactly — the new adapter and resampler are pure, independently tested modules with a socket-factory seam, the fatal/connect-timeout/send-guard paths were traced against the sleeping wrapper in both pre-ready and post-ready states and hold, the shared wire vocabulary is now defined once, and the only surviving item is a module-private-vs-exported constant with no behavioral consequence.

From `docs/enthusiast-setup-plan.md` §4: voice calls get their own provider, with Gemini Live today and OpenAI Realtime beside it.

## What changed

- **The seam.** `app/voice/provider.ts` defines `VoiceProviderV1`: where a session connects and with which key, its audio rates, whether it resumes, whether it searches, and a per-session codec that turns the object's four commands (setup, audio, text turn, tool answers) into frames and reads frames back as the object's events. The `VoiceAssistant` Durable Object now only knows the seam.
- **Gemini Live behind it, unchanged.** `geminiLiveProviderV1` writes exactly the frames the object wrote before. A unit test checks this frame by frame, and all 54 existing Gemini workerd scenarios pass unmodified.
- **OpenAI Realtime** (`app/voice/openai-realtime-voice.ts`, `gpt-realtime-2.1`, GA `session.type: "realtime"`):
  - Resamples the client's 16 kHz audio to 24 kHz.
  - Uses the server's `semantic_vad` with `interrupt_response`. The caller's speech is transcribed with `gpt-4o-transcribe`, because `gpt-live-transcribe` refuses turn detection.
  - Function calls arrive in `response.done`. The codec sends `response.create` only after every call in that response has an answer and no other response is running.
  - A `subagent`'s late result goes back as a turn.
  - Barge-in stops playback and truncates the model's item to what the listener could have heard.
  - `session_expired` is treated as `goAway`.
  - It has no resumption, so a wake reopens and carries the call's turns forward.
  - It has no built-in web search, so the prompt sends current-facts questions to `subagent` instead.
  - Each of Gemini's 30 voice names maps to one of OpenAI's 10.
- **Choosing a provider.** The profile gets a `voice.provider` setting, which becomes the `VOICE_PROVIDER` var. Gemini is the default. `chooseVoiceProviderV1` already accepts an account-level choice and key for the setup web app to supply later; nothing sets those yet. **`deployments/staging.json` runs `openai-realtime`.**
- **Pricing.** Voice isn't charged to credit today. It's limited by daily caps in `app/voice/ledger.ts`. Each provider now declares its audio rates, and the daily audio-seconds caps are worked out as a money limit against Gemini's rates. Gemini keeps its 240 minutes each way. OpenAI gets about 56 minutes each way, based on $32/$64 per million tokens at 10/20 tokens a second. No new money path, so no new idempotency keys.
- **Docs.** `docs/voice.md` has a new section, "Which model a call runs on", plus updated credentials and cost notes. `docs/voice-live-checklist.md` has a new section, "On OpenAI Realtime". Also updated: architecture, the deployment-config README and `.dev.vars.example`.

## Verification

- `bun run validate:format`, `validate:typecheck` and `validate:unit` all pass (6685 unit tests).
- Voice workerd suites pass: 87 tests, including 6 new OpenAI scenarios driven through `test/voice-openai-fake.ts`: setup, talk, tool call, barge-in with truncate, `end_call`, and wake with handover.
- The `voice-upstream` integration test passes: 7 tests, including the OpenAI upgrade carrying the key in `Authorization`, never in the URL.
- The full no-mistakes gate passed with every step run. Review fixed a stale comment and the document step updated `README.md` and `docs/plan.md`. The gate's PR and CI steps were skipped automatically because `gh` isn't installed in this environment.
- **Not done:** a live call against the real OpenAI endpoint on staging. There's no key here, and staging deploys only when `DEPLOY_STAGING` is set. Use `docs/voice-live-checklist.md` → "On OpenAI Realtime".
