The design lives in the repository: **[`docs/plans/voice.md`](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/main/docs/plans/voice.md)** (landing via the pull request linked below; until it merges, read it on branch `worktree-voice-design-doc`). It carries the decisions with rationale, the two assumptions to verify before slice A, the constraints discovered, the Feature rule, the slices, a repo map, the zerobsai salvage list, and the external references — enough for a fresh session to build from.

## Summary

Two voice capabilities, both **beyond parity** (Feature rule 8).

1. **Dictation in the composer** — when the draft is empty the send button becomes a voice-wave button; pressing it streams speech-to-text into the textarea in real time, with bin (discard) and send controls and a capture animation. Sending behaves exactly like a typed message; the Bot replies in text.
2. **App-wide voice assistant (Gemini 3.1 Flash Live)** — a User-scoped voice session, toggled on/off, with read-only tools over durable state (Memory, what each Bot has been doing), that asks a Bot when it needs an answer and is seamless across on/off: an answer that arrives while voice is off is known the next time it is on.

## Decisions (accepted 2026-09-04)

- **D1** Platform-ambient keys, BYOK on the `flock` AI Gateway; both realtime APIs over AI Gateway realtime WebSockets; a durable per-User voice-minutes quota.
- **D2** One transport for both: a per-User `VoiceSession` Durable Object proxy that holds sockets and no authority; durable facts live in the User DO.
- **D3** Dictation uses OpenAI Realtime transcription sessions (`gpt-live-transcribe`); `whisper-1` cannot stream deltas.
- **D4** Dictation streams into the textarea as the draft through `ComposerDraftStore`; bin discards, send commits and calls the ordinary `sendMessage`.
- **D5** The voice assistant is not a Bot: a first-party User-scoped Voice Package with its own ledger, no Agent loop, no Memory writes in v1.
- **D6** Asking a Bot rides the `agent` lane from #151; the Bot's reply is its `send_to_user` (#153); the exchange is recorded in the Bot's Session and shown in the thread with a "via voice" marker.
- **D7** Offline answers: client notification when voice is off, and a spoken briefing of pending answers on the next connect.
- **D8** v1 tools: `list_bots`, `bot_activity(bot, since)`, `memory_search`, `ask_bot`, `pending_answers`.
- **D9** Open mic with Gemini VAD, an explicit on/off toggle in shell chrome, auto-offline after 2 minutes of silence, barge-in, resumption on the next toggle.
- **D10** One live session per User, newest device wins.

## Slices

- **A — Dictation.** Proves the AI Gateway WebSocket path through a minimal `VoiceSession` DO.
- **B0 — ADR + #151.** ADR for the Voice Package and the DO seam; land the `agent` lane.
- **B1 — Voice Package core.** Gemini Live via the proxy, ledger, read-only tools, shell toggle, Voice surface, quota, e2e fake.
- **B2 — Ask a Bot.** `ask_bot`, answer push, offline notification, connect-time briefing, "via voice" marker.

Depends on #151 and #153. The full text — constraints, Feature rule, repo map, salvage list, references — is in the plan document; the comment below is the earlier handoff and is superseded by it.

Design doc for #179 plus a CI change so documentation-only pull requests stop running the full suite.

## `docs/plans/voice.md`

The accepted design for voice: composer dictation on OpenAI realtime transcription, and an app-wide assistant on Gemini 3.1 Flash Live. Decisions D1–D10 with rationale, the two assumptions to verify before slice A, the constraints discovered (no async tool calls on 3.1 Live, 15-minute sessions, intent-before-effect for `ask_bot`), the Feature rule, slices A / B0 / B1 / B2, a repo map, the zerobsai salvage list (`git show 86a86770:…`), and the external references. Written so a fresh session can build from it without redoing the discovery.

## `ci.yml`: docs-only changes run only the Prettier check

- A `Classify changes` job diffs the pull request (or the push range) and reports `docs-only` when every path is under `docs/` or is a root-level `.md`. Markdown elsewhere stays "code" because a Package may ship a Skill or a prompt as `.md`.
- `Validate` and the four browser shards carry `if: needs.changes.outputs.docs-only != 'true'`. This is a job-level skip, not a workflow `paths-ignore`: the `main` ruleset requires `Validate` and `Browser end-to-end` by name, and a check whose workflow never ran stays pending forever, while a skipped job reports `skipped`, which the ruleset accepts.
- The `Browser end-to-end` gate passes when its shards were skipped *and* the change was docs-only; any other skip still fails it.
- A `Check documentation` job runs `bun run format:check` on docs-only changes, so a plan that is not Prettier-clean fails its own pull request rather than the next code change's.
- `Deploy staging` is skipped with `Validate` on a docs-only push to `main`: nothing deployable changed.
- `workflow_dispatch`, a branch-creation push, and an empty diff all run the full suite.

## Local path: the pre-commit hook skips typecheck and tests for docs-only commits

`scripts/docs-only.sh` is the one definition of "documentation only" (paths on stdin; exit 0 when every one is `docs/**` or a root `.md`; an empty list is not documentation). The pre-commit hook pipes the staged paths through it and, on yes, runs Prettier (lint-staged) and stops; CI's `Classify changes` job pipes the diff through the same script. `scripts/docs-only.test.ts` covers the cases. README's testing section documents the path: a docs-only commit needs Prettier and nothing else, locally and in CI, and its pull request merges on the `Check documentation` job alone.

This pull request edits `.github/workflows/`, so auto-merge cannot queue it; it is merged by hand. Its own run is *not* docs-only (it changes the workflow), so the full suite runs here; the first docs-only pull request after this merges is what exercises the skip.

## Intent

Phase 2 of the voice latency plan Tim approved (Phase 0+1 merged as PR #450): swap the continuous voice assistant's speech-to-text from OpenAI gpt-transcribe (server VAD, 700 ms, no text before the commit) to ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime, which streams partial transcripts while the person speaks and commits the segment itself via VAD. Goal: cut ~0.7-1.2 s of time-to-first-word. Decisions: use the ElevenLabsSTT adapter that already ships in @cloudflare/voice-elevenlabs 0.1.0 (its Transcriber shape is structurally identical to app/voice/sleeping-transcriber's VoiceTranscriberV1, so it drops into the existing sleeping/gated wrapper; it opens its own socket with a fetch upgrade and xi-api-key); a new pure module app/voice/scribe-transcriber.ts holds the assistant's settings (pcm_16000 so nothing is resampled, vad_silence_threshold_secs 0.5, vad_threshold 0.4, min speech/silence 100 ms, enableLogging false because the account's words are not the provider's to keep) and the provider choice: VOICE_ASSISTANT_STT=openai keeps the OpenAI adapter reachable as a fallback, default is scribe; VOICE_ASSISTANT_STT is classified in the production secrets manifest as an optional var. voiceAssistantConfiguredV1 now requires the chosen provider's key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY for scribe) plus the ElevenLabs key for TTS, so OPENAI_API_KEY is no longer required for the assistant (dictation still needs it). No wire protocol change. Phone-side only comments changed to be provider-neutral (the 700 ms / OpenAI server VAD wording); the silent-frames-while-playing policy from Phase 1 stays. Docs: docs/voice.md table row, a new Ears section, barge-in and sleep wording, the OpenAI verification transcript marked as the fallback path; .dev.vars.example explains the key permission (the ElevenLabs key needs speech-to-text as well as text-to-speech permission - Tim is granting it). Tests: bun unit tests for the provider/key resolution and the Scribe options; the workerd suite is unchanged because the probe fakes the transcriber. Known: no local ElevenLabs key exists to probe the real endpoint, so the first real verification is in production via the voice assistant trace lines (an auth or permission failure shows as stt-failed). Do not re-litigate the choice of Scribe over Workers AI Nova-3 or OpenAI: Tim chose it.

## What Changed

- The continuous voice assistant now transcribes through ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime by default: a new pure module `app/voice/scribe-transcriber.ts` holds the Scribe options (`pcm_16000`, 0.5 s VAD silence threshold, VAD threshold 0.4, 100 ms min speech/silence, logging off) plus the provider and key resolution, and `VoiceAssistant.createInnerTranscriber` builds an `ElevenLabsSTT` from them. Setting `VOICE_ASSISTANT_STT=openai` keeps the existing OpenAI `gpt-transcribe` adapter reachable as a fallback; the wire protocol is unchanged.
- `voiceAssistantConfiguredV1` now requires the chosen provider's key (`ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` for Scribe) alongside the ElevenLabs TTS key, so `OPENAI_API_KEY` is no longer required for the assistant — only for dictation. `VOICE_ASSISTANT_STT` is declared on the Worker env and classified as an optional non-secret var in the production secrets manifest, and the `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` rationales were rewritten to match (the ElevenLabs key now needs speech-to-text permission as well as text-to-speech).
- Added bun unit tests for provider/key resolution and the Scribe options, plus a workerd integration suite that asserts which provider a session reaches via a new STT-upgrade recorder in the miniflare harness. Docs (`docs/voice.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `.dev.vars.example`) and the phone-side audio-policy comments were updated to describe the ~0.5 s server-side turn end in provider-neutral terms, with the OpenAI transcript marked as the fallback path.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The source change is well-bounded, intent-conformant and correct against the real adapter, with a working OpenAI fallback behind an env var, but it ships a provider path that has never been exercised live while the operator checklist that governs that live verification is now stale, and the fix round left a latent format/sample-rate coupling that no test can catch.

## Testing

Stood the deployed Worker up under workerd and drove the voice capability probe and the assistant WebSocket as a signed-in device, varying only the provider keys: the assistant is available and admits a call on ELEVENLABS_API_KEY alone (OpenAI no longer required), dictation still reports available on the OpenAI key while the assistant does not, VOICE_ASSISTANT_STT=openai reaches the OpenAI adapter, and the adversarial cases (" OpenAI " near-miss, blank key, fallback named without its key) all fall back to Scribe or refuse with `unconfigured`. Captured the outbound upgrade the live session attempted, which shows the Scribe realtime URL carrying every setting the intent specifies including enable_logging=false, and the OpenAI realtime URL with its Bearer key on the fallback path; the suite's sealed egress turns each into the `stt-failed` trace line that is the intent's stated production verification signal. Also ran the object's workerd suite, the gateway unit tests and the new bun unit tests as regression guards, and the operator deploy check to see the corrected secret rationales rendered. No UI surface changed (the Dart edits are comments only and Flutter is not installed on this host), so there is no screenshot; docs/voice.md is prose with no runtime surface. Everything driven passed; the only untested scenario is transcription against the real ElevenLabs endpoint, which needs a key with speech-to-text permission.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 10 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |

## Intent

Move the continuous voice assistant speech-to-text from Workers AI Flux to OpenAI gpt-transcribe with server VAD. Tim decided the model and the architecture on 2026-09-11 and neither is up for re-litigation. The cascade withVoice Agent from cloudflare voice 0.4.0 then Frock AI chat then ElevenLabs TTS stays as it is, and so does the wire protocol to both clients. Facts verified against the real OpenAI endpoint today: only the VAD family accepts turn detection, the streaming model dictation uses refuses it, gpt-transcribe streams no deltas until a turn commits, and 24 kHz is the only PCM rate accepted, so the adapter upsamples the clients 16 kHz audio two to three by linear interpolation carrying phase and an odd trailing byte across frames. server_vad is threshold 0.5, prefix padding 300 ms, silence 700 ms; noise reduction is far_field because the assistant is hands-free while dictation stays near_field; a mid-sentence pause longer than 700 ms splitting one utterance into two Turns is accepted. Cleanups after [timoconnellaus/frockbot#959](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/pull/959). Behaviour is unchanged.

- **Gemini's rates live in one place.** They were defined in two places; now the provider's own rates are `VOICE_REFERENCE_RATES_V1`, the figure the daily caps are measured against.
- **The OpenAI codec reuses existing helpers instead of its own copies:**
  - dictation's `voiceRealtimeAppendV1` to write the audio frame;
  - `VOICE_REALTIME_PCM_RATE_V1` and the client rates in `shared.ts`, instead of copied rate constants and a Gemini-named rate constant.
- **The upsampler allocates once per frame.** It works out the output length first and writes straight into the output buffer, where before it built a boxed `number[]` and ran a second pass.
- **The Durable Object reads the provider its call was opened on,** rather than re-resolving it from env. This covers the "handle forgotten" close code and the model recorded for resumption. It will matter once an account can choose its own provider.
- **The env keys go straight to the chooser.** Each provider's `keyName` does the lookup, so the object no longer names each key.
- **Removed:** the unused Gemini type aliases, the `model` parameter nobody passed, and a caps object that was rebuilt field by field.
- **`webSearch` is now always passed as a boolean,** instead of an optional flag checked with `=== false`.
- **The provider id list is a `const` tuple** and the id type is derived from it.
- **The test probe no longer needs an `instanceof` check** to read a fake's headers.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` passes.
- The pre-push fast tier passes (6695 unit tests).
- `app/voice` bun tests pass (281).

Minor Changes

  • #2249 ebab868 Thanks @​mattzcarey! - WebSockets speaks the Agent protocol for plain hosts, and gains a Cap'n Web transport.

    • A plain Durable Object composed with WebSockets now works with useAgent and AgentClient: the capability sends the identity frame on connect (protocol: false leaves the connect sequence to the host) and serves callables — an RpcTarget whose prototype methods are the host's remote interface.
    • useAgent({ transport }) and AgentClient({ transport }) pick the wire. "cf-websocket" (default) is the hibernating socket; call()/stub send JSON rpc frames. "capnweb" runs one Cap'n Web session that carries protocol frames and serves callables natively: call()/stub invoke them directly, an RpcTarget result is a live stub, a ReadableStream streams, calls pipeline.     • The experimental ?__agents_rpc=capnweb endpoint from 0.23.0 is removed.
    • LifecycleServices exposes name and className.

  • #2245 beff78a Thanks @​mattzcarey! - Add the Queue Lifecycle capability (agents/queue) for durable background work. Each pushed item is a job in the Lifecycle job queue, due immediately, run from the alarm loop one at a time in push order with Lifecycle's retry, deadman, and memory-limit policy. Callbacks are registered in the constructor and typed at declaration and push; push() accepts a stable id (upsert) and per-item retry.

    Agent.queue() and friends now delegate to the capability. Queued callbacks run from the alarm loop in a fresh invocation, so they no longer see the enqueuing request's connection or request through getCurrentAgent() (the agent itself is still available). The cf_agents_queues table and the in-isolate drain are gone; legacy rows migrate into the job queue on the next start. queue() accepts options.id; dequeue, dequeueAll, dequeueAllByCallback, getQueue, and getQueues are now asynchronous; and QueueItem.created_at is renamed createdAt. LifecycleServices.starting() is replaced by status(), which returns "zero" | "starting" | "started".

    Think's workflow-notification outbox and submission drain now run as queue items; the cf_think_workflow_notifications table migrates and is dropped on start.

    Both one-shot migrations (cf_agents_queues in Queue, cf_think_workflow_notifications in Think) are temporary upgrade paths and will be removed in the next minor release, by which point every started object has migrated. Deployments skipping this release should upgrade through it. Workflow-notification delivery retries with backoff capped at ten minutes (previously five) and gives up after twelve hours of continuous failure (previously never), reporting the failure through onError.

  initialState: { count: 0 },
  validateStateChange: (next, source) => validate(next, source),
  onChanged: (state, source) => notify(state, source),
});

Broadcast and the notification hook stay on Agent, and the onMessage state branch stays too; only its inner write delegates to the capability.

## Summary

Removes 12 model providers from the catalog. Each is a consumer subscription or coding plan whose terms rule out a hosted, general-purpose or scheduled client. In some cases FrockBot's adapter also presented itself to the provider as a different client.

| Removed | Why |
|---|---|
| OpenAI Codex (`openai-codex`) | OpenAI approves ChatGPT sign-in only for its own clients, pure open-source clients and its partners. On 2026-09-08 it told a hosted "bring your ChatGPT account" agent that this was "not an approved use of Sign in With ChatGPT". |
| GitHub Copilot (`github-copilot`) | Every request presented itself to GitHub as VS Code (`Editor-Version: vscode/…`, `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat`), and sign-in used GitHub's own client ID. |
| Kimi For Coding (`kimi-coding`) | Kimi Code is "for interactive use only", may not be resold as a service, and forbids spoofing the client. Sign-in used Kimi CLI's client ID. |
| Z.AI (`zai`, `zai-coding-cn`) | Both entries use the GLM Coding Plan endpoint, whose terms forbid using it from "bots, websites, SaaS products". |
| Qwen Token Plan (all three) | Not for application backends or scheduled background tasks. |
| Xiaomi Token Plan (all three) | Only for programming tools, not application backends. |
| OpenCode Go (`opencode-go`) | A subscription for OpenCode and other coding agents. |

Their pay-as-you-go routes stay where the catalog has one: OpenAI, Moonshot AI, Xiaomi and OpenCode Zen. The catalog goes from 40 providers to 28. Sign-in remains for OpenRouter, xAI and Radius.

## Changes

- **Catalog:** `providers/catalog/generate.ts` holds the exclusion list and keeps only API-key providers, so a pi-ai upgrade can't bring these back. `providers.json` is regenerated, and the `apiKey` flag and the Codex exception are gone because every remaining provider takes a key.

- **Docs:** `docs/model-providers.md` has a new "Excluded providers" section, next to the existing Claude subscription note. `docs/known-issues.md` has the new counts.
- **Marketing:** the provider list on the open page, the count on how-it-works, and `.agents/product-marketing.md`.
- **Icons:** the 12 icon map entries and PNGs are deleted. Deleting app assets means the next Android update has to be a full release instead of a Shorebird patch.
- **Unrelated flaky test:** `core/durable/session-flush-reads.test.ts` now waits for the earlier authority's drive to finish before the recorded flush. The cause is in [this comment](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/pull/722#issuecomment-5789267058). With the fix it passes 600 of 600 runs under the same load.

A Bot whose saved connection used one of these providers falls back to Frock AI, and its model line shows the chosen model as unavailable. Nothing crashes. The saved connection rows stay stored but hidden, and no cleanup is included.

- `validate:integration`: 167 of 169 pass. The two failures, `native-settings` and `web-tools` "a disabled Web Package", fail the same way on this branch's base, 5990a62. `main` has already fixed them in 82c9c46. Run with `main`'s versions of those files, this branch passes both, and `catalog-provider.integration.ts` passes too.

- `python3 scripts/sync-connector-icons.py --check` and `flutter analyze` pass.

## What and why

A Bot's reply used to appear only after the whole model step had finished and `send_to_user` had run: the visible reply is a tool call, and the OpenAI-compatible adapter dropped the AI SDK's `tool-input-*` parts, so nothing reached the person while the model wrote (known issue 34). This streams the `text` of the `send_to_user` being written to watching clients as a **reply draft**, which the Flutter client draws where the message will land and which the real message then replaces in place.

A draft is a preview and nothing else: nothing new is written to the durable log, nothing is published or replayed, an eviction or a dropped socket just loses it, and the Session still reconstructs every model request exactly.

## What changed

**Normalized stream vocabulary (`core/contracts`)**

- `LlmStreamEvent` gains `{ type: "tool-input-delta", id, name, delta }`: a fragment of a call's JSON arguments while the model writes them. The call still arrives whole as `tool-call`, and that is the only thing the loop acts on. The exact decoder accepts it, so a model-provider Plugin may send it too (bounded like `text-delta`; SDK types and ADR 0032 updated).
- The Plugin `ai` grant's stream is unchanged: the kernel filters `tool-input-delta` out before encoding for the isolate, whose exact decoder would refuse it.

**Providers**

- `providers/openai-compatible` (Frock AI included) yields `tool-input-delta` from the SDK's `tool-input-delta` parts, named with the joined name from the raw chunks. The catalog bridge maps pi-ai `toolcall_delta` the same way.
- Side effect, pinned by a deadline test: argument fragments are now stream events, so a long reply written as tool arguments no longer trips the first-byte or idle deadline.

**Billing (`app/billing/model.ts`)**

- `tool-input-delta` counts as partial data, like text: a provider failure part-way through a tool call keeps its reservation for reconciliation instead of settling at zero. Test added.

**Agent loop (`core/agent-loop`)**

- `AgentOptions.watchToolInput(dispatch)` returns a per-dispatch watcher (`delta`, `end`). `consumeStreamV1` hands it fragments and never journals them. A watcher that throws is ignored and costs the Turn nothing (tested).

**Shell (`app/shell/reply-draft.ts`, `turn.ts`)**

- A partial JSON reader pulls `payload.text` out of each `send_to_user` being written, alone or declared inside a `batch`, in the order the sends will land. A draft is `{runId, ordinal, parts}`: `ordinal` is the run's send count when the dispatch began, so part *i* lands at `ordinal + i`, and an empty part (a card, or text not begun) keeps its place.
- It redraws at most every 100 ms, plus once more when the dispatch ends. The next dispatch clears whatever the last one drew. Only chat and agent Turns in the Bot's own thread draw one; group, automation and subagent Turns do not.
- Past 256 KiB of argument text in one dispatch, the watcher stops reading and the draft stops growing.

**Bot Durable Object and state channel (`apps/cloudflare`)**

- `BotStateChannel.broadcastDraft` sends a `state/draft` frame only to sockets that asked with `drafts=1`. Those sockets carry a second hibernation tag, which survives eviction (workerd test).
- A draft appends nothing and has no cursor. A draft too large for one 64 KiB frame is not sent.

**Wire (`client-wire.schema.json`)**

- `StateFrame` gains `{schemaVersion, type: "state/draft", runId, ordinal, parts}`, with fixtures (valid and invalid) and regenerated TS and Dart. The protocol window stays `[2, 2]`.

**Installed apps (Android via Shorebird, macOS)**

- Their generated `StateFrame` decoder has no `state/draft`, and an unknown frame makes them drop and reopen the socket. So they must never be sent one, and they are not: they never ask with `drafts=1`.
- The opt-in is a query parameter because a browser cannot set `x-frockbot-client` on a WebSocket.
- Compatibility holds in both directions:
  - A new client on an older server: the parameter is ignored and no draft is drawn.
  - An old client on this server: nothing changes.
- There is no stored-shape change, so no cleanup is needed.

**Flutter client**

- The socket asks with `drafts=1`. `state/draft` bypasses the cursor but is queued with committed frames, so it can never be applied after the message that replaces it.
- `ChatController.replyDrafts` is in memory only. It is dropped when:
  - an empty frame arrives,
  - the run settles,
  - a snapshot arrives,
  - the socket drops.
- `projectRuns` draws each non-empty part as the line its message will be, under the same `<runId>:send:<ordinal>` id, so the message fills the same bubble.
- A message that landed mid-Turn is placed above the draft.
- A draft has no message actions and is never reported as read.

**Docs**

- Updated:
  - `architecture.md` (request path, stream consumption, a new "Reply drafts" section, client transport, stream events),
  - known issue 34,
  - `core/protocol-schemas/README.md` (also its stale 4,096-byte frame figure),
  - ADR 0032's event list,
  - the stale `chat.e2e.ts` note.
- `CONTEXT.md` gains **Reply draft**.

**What's New**

- `replies-as-written`: "Replies appear as they are written".
- The still is cut 16:9 from a 4× render of the chat shots harness, which uses the real Inter font. The harness gains a `writing` scene and a `CHAT_SHOTS_SCALE` define.

![A phone chat with Fox: under “Draft the investor update from those notes”, Fox’s reply stops mid-word at “bridge clo”, with Fox working below it.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/claude/charming-maxwell-r6nxhq-streaming/app/whats-new/media/replies-as-written.webp)

## Validation

- `bun run validate format` passed.
- `bun run validate typecheck` passed (all generators fresh, 13 packages).
- `bun run validate unit` passed: 5,607 tests.
- `bun run validate runtime` passed: cloudflare workerd (62 files, 355 tests), computer-host (6 tests) and applet-build (5 tests).
- The runtime run includes two new tests in `bot-state-channel.workerd.ts`.
  - A real Turn through the Bot Durable Object sends a `state/draft` before the message that replaces it.
  - A draft reaches only the tagged socket, and that holds across hibernation.
- `apps/native`: `flutter analyze` found no issues, and `flutter test` passed (1,549 passed, 25 skipped; the skipped ones are the review-still scenes, which run only with `CHAT_SHOTS` set).
- `no-mistakes` is not installed in this environment, so that gate was skipped.
- `bun run validate integration` passed: 65 files, 175 tests.
- The branch was rebased onto main at 0939fa40. The only conflicts were the two generated protocol files, and I regenerated both with `bun run generate:protocol`. After that, `check-client-protocol` passed, the protocol fixture tests passed (TS and Dart), `flutter analyze` and the touched Flutter suites passed, and the pre-push fast tier passed again (format, typecheck, and unit with 5,629 tests).
- Browser specs, run locally after the merge with the container's Chromium (`FROCKBOT_E2E_SUITE=core`): `chat`, `continuous-chat`, `unread-focus`, `mobile` and `errors`.
  - 19 of 20 passed.
  - `chat.e2e.ts` "a conversation opens at its end, and switching back to it does not reload it" failed in all three full-file runs on this code. It passes when run on its own.
  - The same file on the commit before this PR (8eee2960) passed that test in both runs. In the second run a different chat test failed instead, and that failure restarted the page, so this test ran on a fresh account.
  - The failure is in the harness's `expectBotOpen` for a newly created Bot, which could not read the page within 30 s. The machine's load average was about 15 on 4 cores, and the trace shows every page read taking 0.4 to 1.3 s.
  - The same file passed whole on main's CI for the merge commit (core shard 1/4, with this test at 58 s), and all four core browser shards passed there. I read this as load on the shared machine, not a regression.
- N

## Intent

Implement ADR 0028 (docs/adr/0028-open-deployment.md): FrockBot stays one public MIT repository holding the whole product and two deployment profiles. The hosted frockbot.com deployment (Tim's) is unchanged in behaviour: Google sign-in through better-auth, billing live, Shorebird/Sparkle releases, marketing site, GitHub environments and release.yml. A second 'simple' profile is added that anyone installs into their own Cloudflare account with 'bun run setup': Cloudflare Access sign-in, no billing, no release ceremony, the Fly Sprites Computer included, no customisation. A profile is which secrets exist, which workflows run and which auth Package is built in; nothing is gated and there is no private product code. Deliberate decisions: (1) Auth is a build-time Package with two implementations (app/auth/better-auth, app/auth/access) behind AuthPackageV1, chosen in apps/cloudflare/src/auth-package.ts (better-auth, the tracked default) or auth-package.access.ts, selected by a wrangler alias on the #auth-package subpath import that the deployment-config generator writes only for Access profiles; both variants typecheck (tsconfig.access.json) and the bundles were proven to exclude the other library. On the Access build admission short-circuits to admitted (the Access policy is the allowlist), native sign-in stays closed for now because the door is gated on BETTER_AUTH_URL as the origin, and NATIVE_TOKEN_SECRET is minted so opening it later rotates nothing. Existing hosted User ids, sessions and native bearers are untouched. (2) Administration leaves the app: AdminEntrypoint (WorkerEntrypoint RPC, service-binding only) and a hosted-only apps/admin-portal Worker behind Cloudflare Access; /api/admin routes and the client's Site administration page are deleted; a debug-token-gated POST /api/debug/users/:id/features replaces the admin write the e2e fixtures needed. (3) Deployment identity leaves the tracked wrangler files: deployments/hosted.json and staging.json, scripts/deployment-config.ts writes .deployment/<profile>/<worker>/wrangler.jsonc, placeholders named-by-deployment-config where wrangler insists on a value, byte-identical fixtures of the pre-change configs form an equivalence gate in bun test so the hosted deploy cannot drift; release.yml and main.yml deploy with -c and the D1 id regex rewrites are gone. hits.body:
Slice A of the voice plan (`docs/plans/voice.md`), issue #179.

## What a person sees

With an empty composer the send button is a waveform button. Pressing it starts capturing: a level-driven wave and a "Listening" line appear under the draft, and words arrive in the textarea as they are spoken. While it listens, two controls replace the one button — a bin and a send. Typing mid-dictation is allowed and survives the transcripts that arrive after it. Send commits the audio, waits for the finished transcript, then calls the ordinary `sendMessage`, so a dictated message supersedes, counts against the length limit, and is refused exactly like a typed one. Enter sends; Escape bins. Nothing about the composer moves for anyone who never presses the button.

## Shape

- **`VoiceSession` Durable Object**, one per User, holding the browser socket and the provider socket and **no authority** — the rule ADR 0017 already sets for Subagent objects. It asks `UserConfiguration` before opening a microphone and reports when it closes one.
- **A durable per-User voice budget**: 60 minutes of captured audio per UTC day, one constant, swept on the next day's first capture, with a plain-English refusal when it is spent.
- **A wire protocol of our own** (`@frockbot/protocol`) between the browser and the object. The provider's vocabulary stops at `voice-upstream.ts`, so a second provider is a change to one file and none in the client.
- **The upstream is selectable without a code change**: with an `OPENAI_API_KEY` Worker secret the object opens `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?intent=transcription` directly; without one it falls back to the AI Gateway's BYOK key and `cf-aig-authorization`.

## Key placement

- **`OPENAI_API_KEY`** — GitHub repository secret (added 2026-09-04), carried in the optional `--secrets-file` list in both `release.yml` (production) and `ci.yml` (staging); locally in `apps/cloudflare/.dev.vars`. This is the path production will take.
- **AI Gateway BYOK** — the fallback: the OpenAI provider key on the `flock` gateway in the Cloudflare dashboard, with the already-deployed `FROCK_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN`. Nothing new to place.
- **`GEMINI_API_KEY`** — added to both optional lists now so it survives the deploys before slice B reads it. Nothing reads it yet.

`--secrets-file` replaces the Worker's whole secret set, so an optional name that is not carried would be deleted on the next deploy (ADR 0025).

## One thing the plan did not anticipate

The app is served under `script-src 'self'`, and an `AudioWorklet` loaded from a `blob:` URL does not satisfy it. Rather than widen that policy for every script in the app to load one 40-line file, the worklet source is a string in `plugin-shell` and the application Worker answers `GET /voice-capture-worklet.js` with it. The Content-Security-Policy is unchanged.

## Tests

Unit tests for the budget (bound, idempotent charging, day sweep, receipt decode), for upstream selection and frame translation, and for the draft-tail and transcript logic. A new browser spec dictates with Chromium's fake microphone against a fake OpenAI realtime transcription service in the harness's auxiliary Worker: text arrives in the composer, the bin empties it, the next dictation sends, and the Bot replies. Full `bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint:ui-styles` and prettier are green; the voice spec and a regression subset of the browser layer were run locally.

## Still unverified

- **Assumption 1 of the plan is still open**: nobody has proved AI Gateway's OpenAI realtime path accepts a transcription-only session. That is exactly why the upstream is selectable and why the direct key wins — with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, the gateway branch does not run in production.
- Neither upstream has been reached from a deployed Worker; everything proved so far is against the fake.
- The worklet has been exercised in headless Chromium only. Safari, Capacitor and Electron are untested, and the native shells still need their microphone permission entries.
- The budget meters wall-clock seconds of an open capture, not audio the provider billed. It is a bound, not an invoice.

@​modelcontextprotocol/client@​2.1.0

Minor Changes

  • #2629 dcc0102 Thanks @​gbshankar! - Add DPoP (RFC 9449 / SEP-1932) sender-constrained access token support to the client.
    • Opt in by implementing OAuthClientProvider.dpop() returning a DpopSession (new, along with generateDpopKeyPair, accessTokenHash, isDpopNonceChallenge). auth() / exchangeAuthorization / refreshAuthorization / fetchToken then sign a DPoP proof into token requests (retrying once on an authorization-server use_dpop_nonce challenge, with client authentication re-applied per attempt), and StreamableHTTPClientTransport, SSEClientTransport and withOAuth present a token_type: "DPoP" access token as Authorization: DPoP <token> plus a fresh per-request proof, retry a resource-server use_dpop_nonce challenge once, and pick up a DPoP-Nonce delivered on any response. Tokens the AS issued as Bearer are still presented as Bearer.
    • DPoP is applied at the fetch layer: the transports wrap their resource-server fetch (including a caller-supplied fetch / eventSourceInit.fetch) with the new withDpopFromProvider(provider) middleware, so proofs are always bound to the request actually sent. withDpop(session, getToken) is exported for callers that manage tokens themselves (e.g. alongside a minimal AuthProvider); the AuthProvider interface itself is unchanged.

hits.body:
This adds **Local models** as a model provider. A Bot can answer from Ollama, LM Studio, mesh-llm, or any OpenAI-compatible server on a localhost port of the person's paired Mac. The person connects it on Setup's AI page.

## How it works

The cloud never dials the Mac. The Mac app's device host already holds the machine socket to the User Durable Object, so a model call goes down that socket as a `relay` frame, and the server's streamed answer comes back up the same socket.

Only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` are ever relayed:
- The cloud refuses to send any other address (`decodeLocalModelUrlV1` in `core/machine-protocol/protocol.ts`).
- The device host checks again and refuses redirects.
- The Mac app's Deno `--allow-net` adds only those three hosts to the deployment's own (`DeviceHostBridge.swift`).

On the relay itself:
- Each chat relay carries the model call's request id as its relay id, and the device host forwards a relay id only once.
- The device host runs at most four relays at a time and honours cancel.
- It batches streamed text into frames of up to 64K characters, or whatever arrives within 25 ms.

**The provider (`providers/local-model`).** There is no key. A Connection names the Mac (`machine-id`) and the endpoint on it. Models are discovered from the server's `/v1/models` through the relay. The runtime uses the OpenAI-compatible transport with a `fetch` that goes through the relay. A Bot names only its Connection; the local model User contribution reads the Mac and endpoint from it.

**When the Mac is offline.** A Connection stays ready while its Mac sleeps.
- A Turn whose Mac isn't connected fails with "Your Mac is offline, so your local model can't answer."
- A Turn whose Mac drops mid-answer fails with "Your Mac went offline before your local model finished answering."
- Neither ever falls back to Frock AI.

**Billing.** Local calls are never billed. Each one is recorded as a `free` $0 ledger operation, so it appears on Spending at no charge, and it is never refused for lack of credit, a plan or a daily limit.

**Setup UI.** On Setup's AI page, choosing Local models opens `ConnectLocalModel`:
1. Choose the Mac, from `GET /api/machines`. The Setup reader credential now opens that list only; pairing and revoking a Mac stay closed to it.
2. Choose Ollama, LM Studio, mesh-llm, or another port.
3. Press **Test and connect**. The connection comes back ready with its models, or failed with the reason.

**Docs.** Updated `docs/model-providers.md` and `docs/architecture.md`, and added a What's New entry (`local-models`).

## Validation

On the rebased head:
- `bun run validate format typecheck unit runtime integration` passed: 6,885 unit tests, 408 workerd tests and 191 integration tests.
- e2e couldn't start in this container. Its Docker build's `npm ci` fails TLS against the container's proxy CA.
- `flutter analyze` is clean.

New tests cover:
- the localhost-only rule, on both the cloud and Mac sides
- relay framing, batching, cancel, deadline and concurrency
- the offline and dropped-mid-answer paths
- the Connection lifecycle and model discovery
- free billing
- the Setup helpers and reader routes

## Still needs a Mac

This was built in a Linux container, so these are unverified:
- A Bot answering from Ollama running on the Mac.
- Quitting the app and seeing the Bot report the Mac is offline.
- `bun run update:desktop`, to build the Mac app with the new Deno permission. An older Mac app can't decode relay frames and will reconnect in a loop, so update the app before using a local model.
- The What's New entry has no image yet; it needs a screenshot of the real UI before review.

## Known limits

- Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB, to stay within Cloudflare's WebSocket message limit.
- If a Turn is stopped before the model starts answering, the Mac's request isn't cancelled right away. The relay's two-minute first-byte deadline cancels it.
- Structured output uses the kernel's prompt fallback.

## Summary

- classify pre-response provider failures as transient, permanent, or unknown with bounded reasons and optional Retry-After
- replace fixed immediate retrying with Turn-deadline-bounded equal-jitter exponential backoff and durable `model/retry` events
- fall back from a permanently rejected manual Frock AI model to Frock AI Auto for the rest of the Turn
- preserve reconciliation semantics after any provider response event and add plain total UI failure copy

## Transport classification

| Transport | Transient | Permanent | Unknown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI-compatible | HTTP 408, 429, 5xx; network/reset/timeout faults; first-byte deadline | HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 413; content/safety policy codes | other statuses or unmatched pre-response faults |
| Ollama Cloud | shared OpenAI-compatible mapping | invalid Connection authority/generation/authorization plus shared permanent HTTP failures | credential lease/open failures and unmatched faults |
| Frock AI Gateway / Workers AI | shared transient statuses and rate/overload/unavailable/timeout/gateway/reset envelopes | shared permanent statuses and invalid/auth/credential/model/content/safety/policy envelopes | unmatched native envelopes |
| Foundation | none declared by its local transport | none declared by its local transport | unexpected pre-response faults |
| Custom Models | delegates to the selected provider transport | delegates to the selected provider transport | delegates to the selected provider transport |

## Backoff

- base: 500 ms
- cap: 8,000 ms
- equal jitter: 50–100% of the exponential ceiling
- Retry-After is a floor and may exceed the cap
- transient failures retry only while the delay fits before the Turn deadline; unknown failures receive one retry; permanent failures do not retry the same model

## Validation

- `bun install --force`
- focused unit suites: 394 tests passed
- Cloudflare integration: 45 files / 119 tests passed
- root `bun run typecheck`: all 73 packages passed, including kernel/computer import checks and generated-artifact freshness
- Prettier check on all touched files

The v0.7.16 release run failed in "Build notarized macOS app". The Flutter SDK is checked out by immutable revision, and a shallow checkout without tags makes `flutter --version` report `0.0.0-unknown`, so `flutter pub get` rejected the app's `flutter: "3.47.0"` constraint:

```
The current Flutter SDK version is 0.0.0-unknown.
Because frockbot_native requires Flutter SDK version 3.47.0, version solving failed.
```

The 3.47.0 tag points at the pinned revision, so `fetch-tags: true` on that checkout is enough for `git describe` to name it. Verified with a shallow fetch of flutter/flutter at that revision: without tags describe fails, with tags it prints `3.47.0-0-g4cf241642`.

The other failed job in that run, "Deploy FrockBot app", is a missing-secrets stop (OPENAI_API_KEY and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY on the production environment), not a code change.

Builds §5 of the enthusiast setup plan: the setup chooser on frockbot.com, and the review screen that applies the carried-over choices after sign-up.

## frockbot.com
- **`/setup`**: starting points (Just works, Bring my keys, All mine, Self-hosted) and five questions: where FrockBot runs, the computer, AI per job, web search and connected apps. Each question's two choices are **Ready to wear** (FrockBot's) and **Dress it up** (yours). AI has searchable, grouped provider and model pickers covering every catalog provider. The rules are ported from the Setup Chooser canvas: self-hosting keeps AI on Frock AI; connected apps through FrockBot need BYO, self-hosted too; writing and the other chat jobs follow chat.
- **Result panel**: summary, who-runs-what diagram, suggested plan (Standard US$20 / BYO US$5 / none self-hosted), costs split into *From credit*, *Your accounts* and *Free*, what you gain, and steps. A coming-soon part is never a step: it is listed under **Not ready yet** with what covers it until then. A test walks every single-choice change from every preset to check this.
- **Honest statuses** live in `content/setup-options.json`, audited against main. Available today: frockbot.com, FrockBot's computer, Frock AI, chat on any catalog provider or Ollama Cloud, and FrockBot's search and apps. Everything else is coming soon. Model lists come from `providers/catalog`. `render-setup.ts --check` runs in the build, like capabilities. Later feature PRs flip their option to `available` there.
- **No JavaScript**: the default setup is rendered into the HTML. Runs under the existing CSP (no inline script or style).
- **Homepage**: a teaser section whose three cards open `/setup/#preset=…`. The pricing copy now says credit covers FrockBot's models and computer on Standard and Plus, and top-ups do on BYO.

## Carry-over
- **One shared, versioned format**: `core/setup-choices` (`v: 1`, no imports). The site serves an esbuild copy of it. Unknown or retired values fall back to FrockBot's version of that part, with a note.
- **Saved on the device** under `frockbot-setup-v1`: choices only, storage access guarded. Shows "Welcome back. Saved on this device · Start over".
- **Start with this setup** opens `bot.frockbot.com/setup/apply#setup=<base64url>`. The choices travel in the fragment, never the query string.

## In the app: `/setup/apply`
- The page moves the fragment into this origin's storage **before** any sign-in or checkout redirect, then clears it from the address bar.
- Signed out: Continue with Google, returning to `/setup/apply`.
- Signed in: **"Set up FrockBot the way you chose"** lists each part as Ready, Needs your key (inline field), Needs sign-in, or Coming soon with Frock AI or FrockBot's version for now. The plan row checks out on the suggested plan.
- Billing sends a successful checkout back while a setup is waiting.
- **Apply this setup** or **Start on Frock AI instead**. Nothing is applied silently. Apply uses the same Settings, Connections and Billing commands the app uses.
- Why `/setup/apply` and not `/setup`: the setup web app (`claude/eager-franklin-sy7ssj`, not yet opened as a PR) claims `/setup` and `/setup/{plan,computer,ai,search,apps,accounts}` in the gateway. A second `/setup` handler would be silently shadowed, whichever merged second. That app can adopt this screen by adding an `apply` page and deleting `app/setup/page.ts`.
- **Your Sprites** is named **Your Fly.io account** (id `fly`), because only the host may name Fly's Sprites (`check-computer-host-imports`).
- A What's New entry, `setup-review`, has a still of the review screen.

## Not in this PR
- **frockbot.com/deploy** (timoconnellaus/frockbot#964) should read `frockbot-setup-v1` with `readSavedSetupV1` / `normalizeSetupChoicesV1` from `@frockbot/core/setup-choices` and pass it to the install's first run. That belongs to that PR.

## Hold
Labelled `hold` until timoconnellaus/frockbot#962 (the BYO plan) merges. This PR suggests BYO and starts BYO checkout, and main's Stripe plan list doesn't have it yet. The chooser's price test in `stripe.test.ts` checks every plan the payments Package lists, so it covers BYO once #962 lands.

## Validation
- `bun run format:check`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (6,740 pass, 0 fail).
- `bun run build:marketing` passes. `validate:build` passes, including the white-label fixture and the Worker bundle.
- `validate:runtime`: all suites passed, including the app Worker's workerd suite (408/408). It recorded no success only because a path-only commit landed mid-run.
- Checked in Chromium on the local marketing Worker: desktop and 390px phone, no horizontal scroll, no CSP errors, reload restores the saved setup.
- Checked in Chromium against a mock of the app's APIs, using the real routes: fragment capture → sign-in → connect key → Apply → pending setup cleared.
- The `no-mistakes` CLI isn't installed in this environment, so that gate did not run.

Two batches of work land together on top of `main`, plus the merge that
puts them beside PRs 163–167.

## Providers never hang (models, connectors, settings)

- **F2** Every network call in the model path is bounded: the Ollama Cloud
  catalog read and inference probe, the OpenAI-compatible response headers
  (cleared the moment they arrive, so a live stream is never torn down) and
  each stream read, and the Flock AI Gateway request on both transports —
  which now also takes the caller's signal, so Stop reaches it.
- **F5, F6** An interrupted Turn settles instead of wedging the Bot. A new
  `not-retrievable` reconciliation outcome says the provider keeps no durable
  copy, so the loop settles the run as a model error with its partial text
  kept. Flock AI and Ollama Cloud declare it; a provider that declares none
  degrades to it. Ollama treats any failure before the first stream event as
  "not started", so a 429 or 502 fails cleanly and can be retried.
- **F1, F4, F7, F12** Connect shows a busy state and never hangs in
  `authorizing`: pending-command recovery has an attempt cap, an exhausted
  command abandons its Connection to `failed` with a reason and discards the
  staged credential, "Try again" reopens the form with the endpoint kept, and
  errors move off the single global slot into per-action state.
- **F8** A failed catalog refresh backs off from a minute rather than waiting
  the full hour.
- **F9, F10** The OAuth return is read at boot and rendered (and stripped from
  the URL); a browser callback failure redirects into the app instead of
  answering raw JSON as a page.
- **F3, F11, F12, F13** A settings refusal lands on the row that was clicked,
  in plain language and in the names the surface knows.

## A Bot can start a new conversation (memory, ADR 0027)

- **ADR 0027 / memory F6, robustness F4/F5** The Bot Durable Object owns which
  conversation its chat Session is on. The composer's "New conversation" puts
  the current one down and starts the next, keeping Memory; earlier
  conversations stay durable and readable Turn for Turn.
  `turnScopedMessagesV1` now carries a character budget (150k), evicting whole
  Turns so a tool result never outlives its call, with a plain notice where
  the dropped Turns were.
- **F8** A file at the size cap no longer takes its whole tier down: a month
  rolls to `log/YYYY-MM.pNN.md` and the cap is enforced at the commit.
- **F9** `forget` retracts the copies other Bots hold, not just my own line.
- **F10** A durable write whose ledger call fails reports `ok` with
  `ledgerPending` instead of claiming nothing was written.
- **F11** A listing that could not be read whole says so, and skips the index
  update rather than treating absent as deleted.
- **F12** Injection and the search index share one file selection.
- **F14** Every remote memory seam runs under a deadline and is retried; Memory
  that cannot be read records an omission and the Turn continues.
- **F32** A `project_create` whose membership call fails records the outcome.
- **F35** Memory and Skill writes are audited against the Workspace, not "This
  Computer" — they run while it is hibernated.
- **F36** Unreadable files are each named; a retraction is not measured against
  the fact cap; vector hits are keyed by document and hash; the injected block
  has a global 12k budget.
- **F40** `memory/injected` records a note as `note`.

## Merge

Four files conflicted with `main`; each keeps both behaviours (conversation
filter *and* degraded run projection; connection return *and* main's
"No model available — set one up in Models"; per-row refusals in main's
wording). Three fixes fall out of the combination: `package_author` reached
through `call_dynamic_tool` is audited against the Workspace; an Ollama Turn
that fails before its first stream event settles rather than parking; and a
read in flight when a new conversation starts no longer redraws the one that
just ended (the transcript keeps a conversation epoch).

## Tests

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- `bun test` — 3395 pass, 0 fail
- `test:workerd` — 40 files, 186 pass (1 skipped)
- `test:integration` — 40 files, 104 pass
- `bun run format:check` — clean
- e2e `chat`, `connect-ollama`, `first-run`, `new-conversation` (workers 1) —
  8 passed. The chat spec now restores the fake endpoint it switches to
  `unauthorized`; leaving it on was failing every later spec's Turn with a 401.

## Intent

Follow-up on PR #408, same branch. Tim ran the real-endpoint probe and found that gpt-live-transcribe REJECTS turn detection too: both server_vad and semantic_vad answer 'Turn detection is not supported for this transcription model.' OpenAI's actual rule is that the streaming transcription models (gpt-realtime-whisper, gpt-live-transcribe) take no VAD at all, while the models that do take VAD (gpt-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe) do not stream deltas. Tim's decision (2026-09-11, not to be re-litigated): dictation stays on gpt-live-transcribe with turn_detection: null, and the relay's existing commit-at-stop path is THE way a capture finalises. Proven live: with null, word deltas arrive 0.3-0.6 s behind speech all on a single item_id; input_audio_buffer.commit is answered by input_audio_buffer.committed then conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed within ~0.5 s; no completed ever arrives without the commit (a 73 s uncommitted capture produced nothing). The OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1 header must never be sent (beta shape retired, beta_api_shape_disabled); the relay already does not send it. So: voiceDictationSessionUpdateV1() now sends turn_detection: null explicitly (the server defaults the field to server_vad when it is absent, so the null has to be on the wire); the relay's stop path drops the redundant VAD-disabling session.update round trip and commits directly, since there is no automatic commit left to guard against; the workerd regression test encodes the real rule (the fake upstream refuses any non-null turn_detection for both streaming models, streams deltas against one item, and transcribes only what a client commit closes) and a second test puts server_vad back on the relay's own frame to reproduce the production failure end to end; the now-impossible 'automatic commit racing Stop' test in voice-dictation.workerd.ts was deleted along with its fake-upstream option rather than kept alive, since out-of-order and committed-order coverage still exists in two other tests. Docs rewritten to the new truth: one item per capture, deltas live, finalised at stop, plus why the model and the null are both forced. Real-endpoint proof was run this time and is recorded in docs/voice.md and the PR body: the probe against wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?intent=transcription, and the whole relay driven end to end through a local wrangler dev Worker with the real key and 5.5 s of synthesized 24 kHz speech, giving ready at +1.20s, growing deltas from +1.91s, stop at +5.75s, segment and final at +6.90s. Still not verified, deliberately: a real microphone, a browser client, and the Flutter client.

## What Changed

- `voiceDictationSessionUpdateV1()` now sends `turn_detection: null` explicitly instead of a `server_vad` block. The streaming transcription models (`gpt-live-transcribe`, `gpt-realtime-whisper`) answer any turn detection with "Turn detection is not supported for this transcription model." and the session dies there, which is why no production capture reached `ready`; the field has to be on the wire because the server defaults it to `server_vad` when absent.
- The relay's `stop` path drops the VAD-disabling `session.update` round trip and commits directly — with no upstream turn detection there is no automatic commit to guard against — and the five-minute cap now runs the same stop path (`capped` → `stop()` → commit → segment) before closing on the `limit` error in place of `final`, so a capped capture keeps its transcript.
- Tests and docs follow the new rule: the workerd model test's fake upstream refuses turn detection for both streaming models, streams deltas against a single item and transcribes only what a client commit closes, plus new cases for the cap and for putting `server_vad` back on the relay's own frame to reproduce the production failure; the now-impossible "automatic commit racing Stop" test and its `raceBeforeStopAck` option were deleted (out-of-order and committed-order coverage remain in two other tests). `docs/voice.md` records the real-endpoint run (probe against `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?intent=transcription`, then the whole relay through a local `wrangler dev` Worker with the real key and 5.5 s of synthesized 24 kHz speech: ready at +1.20s, deltas from +1.91s, stop at +5.75s, segment and final at +6.90s), and `docs/known-issues.md` / `docs/voice-live-checklist.md` are corrected to say a microphone, a browser client and the Flutter client are still unverified.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and matches the intent exactly — `turn_detection: null` is on the wire, the redundant VAD-disabling round trip is gone, the deleted race test and its fake-upstream option were removed together, and the fix-round cap path correctly commits, delivers the segment, and only then closes with the `limit` error (traced through the normal, empty-buffer, stop-before-ready, timeout, and socket-close paths with no state left wrong); the only residuals are informational and were already decided by the user.

## Testing

Everything user-facing was exercised against the real product: the relay running in a local wrangler dev Worker with the real OpenAI key, and the upstream contract probed directly at wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?intent=transcription. The session frame with turn_detection null is accepted and echoed back, deltas arrive ~0.3-0.6 s behind speech all on one item_id, and the transcript appears only after the relay's commit; putting server_vad or semantic_vad back on the same frame reproduces the production refusal verbatim. A full capture through the relay gave ready at +2.1s, growing deltas, and segment plus final ~0.7 s after stop. The five-minute cap was driven live with 315 s of continuous speech and no Stop: the segment carrying the whole five-minute transcript arrived at +303.04s immediately before the fatal limit error, which is what the round-2 decision asked for. A direct 5-minute probe confirmed OpenAI answers the commit in ~1.0 s with a 5151-character transcript, so the commit-at-stop design is not near an upstream bound. Stop-without-speaking still ends in a clean final. Two earlier five-minute attempts failed (client socket 1006 at +70 s; timeout at +307 s) but both ran on a wrangler dev process that afterwards refused connections entirely — a fresh dev server ran the same scenario cleanly and the direct probe never stalled, so that was local dev-server instability rather than relay behaviour. The targeted workerd suites also pass, but those run against a fake upstream, so they are reported as untested rather than as a live result. No screenshots: this change has no rendered UI surface — it is a WebSocket relay, and the user-visible frames are captured as CLI transcripts.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dictating through the composer relay produces live text and lands the transcript on Stop | ✅ pass | live | relay-live.log — local wrangler dev Worker with the real OPENAI_API_KEY: ready +2.08s, deltas from +2.93s, stop +4.93s, segment and final +5.66s |

## Intent Set up complete GitHub automation for FrockBot and merge it safely. Add Ubuntu-only CI on pushes to main and pull requests covering install, typecheck, tests, build, and the Cordis proof; weekly grouped Dependabot updates for Bun/npm and GitHub Actions; and tag-driven semantic-version releases that publish every reusable packages/* workspace publicly to the npmjs @frockbot scope while keeping root and app workspaces private, then create generated GitHub releases. The public repository should be timoconnellaus/frockbot. Add production Cloudflare backend deployment only after CI succeeds on a push to main, using pre-existing D1, R2, and Vectorize resources rather than provisioning resources automatically; apply remote D1 migrations, upload the immutable content-addressed application artifact to R2, and deploy the Worker using a protected GitHub production environment with documented variables and secrets. Preserve the repository's plugin convention that workspace package manifests remain private during development and transform them only in the release job for npm publication. Resolve the three CodeRabbit findings by content-addressing the R2 artifact, publishing prereleases under the npm next dist-tag, and strictly validating/documenting SemVer tags. Commit, push, validate CI and configured-bot feedback, and merge PR #1. ## What Changed - `ci.yml` now content-addresses the production application artifact: it computes the built bundle's SHA-256, uploads it to R2 under `applications/.mjs`, and rewrites the `foundation-v1` placeholder in `apps/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc` so the deployed Worker points at that digest. The D1 `database_id` substitution was rewritten as a Node heredoc that validates the id shape and targets the `frockbot-auth` production entry instead of rewriting the whole JSONC file, and the Cordis proof step now runs with `ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1` under xvfb. - `release.yml` validates the pushed tag against a strict SemVer regex (rejecting build metadata with an npm-specific message) and publishes prerelease versions under the `next` dist-tag instead of `latest`; Dependabot's root ecosystem changed from `npm` to `bun`. - Added `publishConfig.access: public` and `repository` metadata to the nine `packages/*` manifests that lacked it, and corrected `plugin-shell`'s repository `directory` from `packages/webui-shell` to `packages/plugin-shell`. README documents the content-addressed artifact flow, SemVer tag rules, prerelease dist-tag, and the Vectorize create command, replacing the stale production provisioning block. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix round's D1 substitution, content-addressed R2 key, SemVer/dist-tag logic, and package metadata all verify correct against the actual wrangler config and worker code, leaving only two informational items with no reachable production-breaking path. ## Testing I reproduced the Cloudflare deploy job's config steps verbatim against the real wrangler.jsonc and fed the result to real wrangler: the CLOUDFLARE_D1_DATABASE_ID production variable now rewrites the top-level frockbot-auth database_id (the env.development entry and the file's JSONC comments are untouched), and the built artifact's sha256 becomes both the R2 object key and DEFAULT_APPLICATION_HASH, matching the Worker's applications/<hash>.mjs lookup. I ran the release workflow's tag validator over a 13-tag matrix (SemVer accepted, build metadata and malformed tags rejected with the npm-specific message) and its dist-tag logic (prereleases route to `next`), then applied the release version transform and ran `npm publish --dry-run` for all 25 packages/* workspaces, each reporting public access under the `next` tag with correct repository.directory, while root and all apps/* manifests stayed private and the committed package manifests restored to private:true. Real CI run 33132707308 on PR #1 is green on ubuntu-latest through install, typecheck, test, build and the Cordis Electron proof under xvfb, with both deploy jobs correctly skipped for a pull_request event. Everything passed; no new findings. Two things are inherently unverifiable before merge and were already raised and accepted in earlier rounds: the dependabot.yml npm→bun ecosystem switch (only GitHub's Dependabot service consumes it, from main), and the live production deploy path itself, which requires the protected production environment's credentials. This change is workflow/config only with no user-facing UI surface, so no screenshot or rendered-UI artifact applies; the reviewer-visible evidence is the wrangler-resolved production config and the npm publish transcripts. ## Catalog provider: every Turn failed (product bug from #378)

`providers/catalog/runtime.ts` and `providers/catalog/bedrock.ts` spread the whole `ModelBindingSnapshot` into the model replay state. Fix: a `modelReplayBindingV1` helper in `providers/openai-compatible/index.ts` copies exactly the two permitted fields. Regression test in `providers/catalog/runtime.test.ts` asserts a binding carrying `catalogGeneration` still decodes with only the five allowed keys.

The spec got through every Turn. It failed only on the final phone leg because #381 moved the Applets entry off the conversation bar onto the Bot page, and after a reload at phone width the shell opens on the Bot list. The spec now walks the real shell: sidebar, Bot row, Bot panel toggle, then the chip. Phone screenshots regenerated.

hits.body:
## What and why

A message can now carry files. The person attaches up to five files of up to 20 MB each: pictures (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, and text, Markdown, JSON or code. Pictures reach a model that can see them. A document reaches the model as its text. Each file stays with the Bot. This is the first slice of parity items 1 and 2 (file upload and image understanding).

![What's New still: a message carrying a chart and a PDF, Fox's reply, and a spreadsheet in the composer tray](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/main/app/whats-new/media/attachments.webp?raw=true)

**How it works.** The app uploads a file as soon as it is attached, before Send. `POST /api/bots/:bot/uploads` admits the file durably: it checks the type from the bytes, extracts a document's text once, counts the file against the account's 5 GB, writes the bytes and the text to R2 under the Bot's own prefix, and records `upload:<sha256>` in the Bot Durable Object. Only then does it answer with the hash. Every step is idempotent by that hash. The Turn command names uploads by hash only, and the Bot resolves each one against its own records before admission. A message can therefore only carry a file its Bot holds. Through the run record, `input/queued`, `user/message`, the working context and the journaled `model/request`, an attachment is a reference with no bytes. `LlmRegistry` fills in the bytes and text after the request is journaled, through a new `ModelAttachmentResolverV1`. A re-dispatch after an eviction reads the same content-addressed objects again, and nothing resolved is ever written to the log.

## What changed

- **Kernel (`core/`)**: `MessageAttachmentV1` and its decoders (`core/contracts/message-attachments.ts`). User `LlmMessage.attachments`. `userMessagePartsV1`, the one way every provider draws a user message. `ModelAttachmentResolverV1` in `LlmRegistry`: a resolver failure is a call that never started. The agent loop takes a files-only message. The run record and admission store attachments. The fingerprint includes the upload ids, and a retry must carry the same ones.
- **App (`app/uploads/`)**: classification, extraction (Workers AI `toMarkdown` with image description off, plus a small Office XML reader for PowerPoint and as Word's fallback), the Bot-side upload records, the account quota ledger, and the per-Turn resolver. The resolver sends the files on the newest 3 attachment-bearing messages: at most 8 pictures of at most 8 MB, and 30,000 characters per document within 90,000 per request. Anything older is named in one line. `generate_image` now returns its picture as a tool attachment, so the Bot sees what it made.
- **Worker (`apps/cloudflare`)**: the upload route (`uploads.ts`) and `GET` for thumbnails (`private, immutable`; a non-image is served as a download under `sandbox`). Turn RPC carries refs only. `UploadNotFoundError` returns a 422. Deleting a Bot deletes its R2 objects and gives its quota back. Deleting the account (#808) deletes every Bot that way, and its file sweep now also covers the whole `uploads/<userId>/` prefix for a Bot lost before its teardown. The User object counts no new upload once deletion begins. Both ids in an upload key are URL-encoded, so one account's prefix never begins another's.
- **Providers**: OpenAI-compatible, Frock AI, the catalog runtime and Bedrock draw image parts or text notes. On the gateway route, Frock AI Auto accepts images (`vision: true`). A schema request, and Auto on the binding path, are told in words that a picture was attached.
- **Billing** (`apps/cloudflare/src/frock-ai.ts`, image rule only): the blanket `image_url` refusal is gone. When checking a request against its model's prepaid bound, each image counts as a fixed 6,000-token allowance in place of its base64. The charge still settles from the usage the model reports. Rebased onto #802: the allowance applies inside the rate table's per-model bounds, and settlement still prices the served model.
- **Protocol**: `UploadRef`, `UploadReceipt` and `Attachment`. A TurnCommand may carry `attachments` with empty `text`. A Run carries `attachments`. `protocolMax` is now 3 and `protocolMin` stays 2, so this is a grace period. The server leaves `attachments` off every Run sent to a protocol 2 client: pages, lookups, Stop receipts and state frames. The state socket sends its protocol as `?protocol=`. Installed 1.4 apps keep decoding every Run exactly. The socket also asks for #807's reply drafts (`drafts=1`); a draft carries no Run, so every socket that asked gets it whatever its protocol, and a reply being written is drawn under a message that carries files.
- **Flutter**: an attach button, drag-and-drop over the chat, ⌘V of copied files or pictures on desktop, and images from an Android keyboard. The tray above the field uploads each file as it is attached and supports retry and remove. Send waits for uploads to finish. Photos are downscaled to a 2,048 px long edge and HEIC is converted on the device. A sent message shows thumbnails and document tiles. New plugins: `file_picker`, `desktop_drop`, `pasteboard`. The macOS app also gets the `user-selected.read-only` entitlement.
- **Compaction is untouched.** Tool payloads are still pruned as before. The summariser reads a message's words, not its files, so a file older than the summary is known only by what the conversation said about it. The newest three messages' files still reach the model verbatim. This is recorded in known issue 49.
- **Stored shapes**: every new field is optional and nothing existing changed shape, so no cleanup is needed. Existing Bots reply as before.
- **Docs**: architecture §4 "Attachments", parity row 57j, known issues 49–50, protocol README. There is also a What's New entry, `attachments`, with the still above.

## Validation

Rebased onto `main` at #821:

- `bun run validate format`: pass
- `bun run validate typecheck`: all 13 packages pass
- `bun run validate unit`: 5890 pass, 0 fail (at #819; the pre-push hook re-ran the fast tier at #821)
- `bun run validate:runtime`: pass at #821 (cloudflare workerd: 63 files, 361 tests, including the account-deletion uploads assertions; computer-host 6; applet-build 5)
- `bun run validate:integration`: pass at #821 (67 files, 181 tests)
- `flutter analyze`: no issues. `flutter test --dart-define=FROCKBOT_ORIGIN=https://tests.invalid`: 1593 pass (the shots scenes skip without `CHAT_SHOTS`)
- Browser specs that exercise the composer (`chat`, `mobile`, `errors`, `defaults`), run before the later rebases: 18 of 19 passed. The one failure was `chat.e2e.ts:883` in `createBot`'s `expectBotOpen` on a heavily loaded machine, and it passed rerun alone. The full e2e category was not run.
- CI on `5ef9f45d`: `Check`, `Flutter`, `iOS build (advisory)` and `Qualify Mac desktop` passed.
- The still is rendered by the new `attachments desk` scene in `apps/native/test/chat_ui_shots_test.dart`, with Inter loaded.
- `no-mistakes` is not installed in this environment, so the gate was skipped.
- Not validated locally: the Android Gradle compile and the macOS and iOS builds (no SDKs here), and a real device. The new plugins carry native code, so this change needs a full APK release rather than a Shorebird patch, and `bun run update:desktop` for the Mac app.

## Deferred

- A tool that reads past a document's 30,000-character excerpt. The full text is already stored.
- The Computer reaching uploads.
- Pasting images in the web client, and HEIC in browsers that cannot decode it (known issue 50).
- The compaction summariser seeing files (owned by the compaction work).
- The seeded DeepSeek provider Plugin flattens user messages and ignores attachments.
- Audio and video, the share sheet, and deleting one file without deleting its Bot.

## Intent

Simplify provider, Package catalog, and computer identity contracts across the codebase: remove provider-specific connection lifecycle duplication, centralize catalog lookup and policy, preserve existing behavior, and publish a fully validated PR.

- Added `providers/catalog/registry.ts` as the single policy table for catalog providers (connection settings, runtime adapter, OAuth request auth, model source, settings validation, runtime environment names); `definition.ts`, `models.ts`, `runtime.ts` and the OAuth modules derive from it instead of per-provider `id === …` branches, and `catalogProviderV1` / `validateCatalogSettingsV1` / `catalogRuntimeEnvironmentV1` replace the loose provider-id arguments.

## What broke

Since #378 the user application artifact (`apps/cloudflare/dist/artifacts/foundation-v1.mjs`) fails to evaluate in the Worker Loader:

```
Failed to start Worker: Uncaught TypeError: The argument 'path' must be a file URL object, a file URL string, or an absolute path string. Received 'undefined'
  at node:module:34:15 in createRequire
  at index.js:1:854
```

`build-artifact.ts` builds the artifact with `Bun.build({ target: "node", packages: "bundle" })`. The provider catalog's `providers/catalog/runtime.ts` and `models.ts` import `@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/all`, which statically imports all 40 provider modules and with them `openai`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `google-auth-library` and their CommonJS dependencies. Bun then emits `createRequire(import.meta.url)` as the bundle's first statement, and a Worker Loader module has no file URL, so the statement throws before anything else runs. 38 of the 40 provider modules trigger the preamble, so importing fewer providers or making the map lazy does not help; the fix has to be at build level.

Every main pipeline run since b05924f2c failed Validate and all four browser shards on this.

## Change

- `apps/cloudflare/build-artifact.ts`: define `import.meta.url` as `file:///frockbot/foundation-v1.mjs` in the artifact build, naming the bundle the way a file-loaded module would be named. The `require` it produces is only reached from the lazy CommonJS wrappers of those SDKs' Node-only paths, and lands on the `nodejs_compat` built-ins like any other `require` in the Worker.
- Post-build assertion: the emitted artifact must not contain `import.meta.url`, so a bundler change surfaces at build time rather than hours later in the e2e job.

No feature removed; all 40 catalog providers still ship (the manifest lists 43 provider packages).

## Verification

- Reproduced before the change (HTTP 500 with the error above), HTTP 200 from `/app-manifest` after rebuild.
- `bun test providers/catalog`: 22 pass.
- `bun run --filter @frockbot/cloudflare test:workerd`: 46 files, 219 tests pass.
- `bun run --filter @frockbot/cloudflare typecheck` clean; prettier clean.
- Real e2e harness locally: `first-run` 1 passed; `settings-models` + `chat` 13 passed (one local-resource flake passes alone).

Follow-up worth a look: the catalog now adds about 3.5 MB of Node-only SDK weight to every user application artifact.

Follow-up to #303, on top of the shipped `v0.4.0`. **~17k further lines removed.**

## The agent loop is now finished

`v0.4.0` shipped only the extraction. This completes it.

**Forensic reconciliation is gone.** The loop used to work out, after a crash, whether a dispatched model call had happened — retrieve the response, verify it against the durable chunk prefix, park the Turn for a person when it couldn't be retrieved. Now every effect that matters carries an idempotency key (a model call's `requestId`, a tool call's `occurrenceId`) and is re-issued under that key. No Turn parks. `admitEffect` and supersede fencing survive and now run before *every* dispatch, re-issues included.

I held this back from `v0.4.0` believing that writing `model/usage` per dispatch over-accounts a retry. **That was wrong.** `provider-openai-compatible` has an explicit test asserting no idempotency key reaches the provider, so a re-issued request is a genuinely new and genuinely billed call, and counting each dispatch is correct.

**And the seam it left behind is deleted**: `LlmReconciliationCapability`, `ctx.llm.reconcile`, and all four provider implementations — declared, implemented everywhere, called by nobody.

## Voice and Billing are out

12,791 lines. They came out together because `UserConfiguration` called `billing.recordVoiceInCurrentTransaction`, so removing either alone left the other calling a dead method.

The `VoiceSession` Durable Object class is retired by a **new `v6` migration carrying `deleted_classes`**. The `v5` entry that created it is immutable once applied and is untouched. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` accepts the result.

Two things turned out to be Voice's despite neutral names: `recordSettledAgentOutcome` had exactly one caller (the voice-answer outbox), and `StoredRunVoiceOriginV1` / the `voice` branch of `run.via` were in the wire schema — so the Dart client protocol was regenerated.

## Also

Records two release-pipeline defects found by shipping `v0.4.0`: an auto-merged PR never reaches staging (the merge push carries `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which doesn't trigger workflows), and npm publish fails every release on packages npm has no trusted publisher for — reddening a run whose production deploy succeeded.

## Verification

Every suite, including the two that caught the last round's escapes:

| | |
|---|---|
| typecheck | 69 packages |
| unit | 4,308 |
| integration | 123 across 50 files |
| workerd | 206 across 44 files |
