## Intent

Switch FrockBot's real-time voice from the ElevenLabs cascade (Scribe STT + thin chat model + ElevenLabs Flash TTS through the Cloudflare voice SDK) to one Gemini 3.8 Live speech-to-speech session, per ADR 0031 (docs/adr/0031-voice-gemini-live.md). Tim's decisions: no ElevenLabs fallback at all (delete the cascade modules, both @cloudflare/voice packages, ELEVENLABS_*/VOICE_ASSISTANT_STT config, the voice catalog check); voice is a different mode of the Bot, not a layer over the chat model; voice does NOT share the thread (entering voice replaces the thread pane with a voice surface; the call reads thread+memory going in and writes to Memory only); the model chooses a single 'subagent' tool when it thinks a task will take a while (no fixed classification of long tools); subagents are Turns on the Bot's agent lane and keep running when the call is paused; Pause closes the Live socket (keeps the resumption handle) and starts nothing; the same 'subagent' hand-off tool exists in text Turns (app/flock/subagent.ts, capped 4 per Turn, depth 1); switch_bot is honoured only after the model's spoken turn completes so the sign-off and the tool call can come in either order, and 'ask <bot>' is a subagent not a switch; no captions on the voice surface; the voice UI must not shift between states (avatar and name fixed, activity slot fixed, Pause/meter/End); Paused just says 'Paused'; dictation stays on OpenAI (gpt-live-transcribe) for now; a Bot's voice is BotVoiceAppearanceV1 = one of Gemini's 30 prebuilt voiceNames + described delivery (accent with language pin in prose, attitude, pace, turn length, humour, disfluency, formality, custom text <=500 chars) stored as slugs and rendered into the system instruction at call start, with per-character default voices; Bot voice has its own revision and route (GET/POST /api/bots/:id/voice) and a Settings > Voice page in the Flutter app; ledger meters become audio seconds in/out (240 min each) instead of STT seconds/TTS characters; googleSearch is a built-in tool in the session; languageCode and enableAffectiveDialog are deliberately NOT sent (the probe showed affective dialog kills the socket on gemini-3.8-live; language is pinned in prose). ## Intent

Tim wants FrockBot to show Bot-to-Bot messages the way GrokBot does: in the thread, a small centred marker line ('Messaged <Bot>' in the asking Bot's thread, 'Message from <Bot>' in the target's) with the other Bot's avatar, instead of drawing the other Bot's question as if the user typed it; clicking the marker opens a view-only chat titled 'A ⇄ B' listing the whole back-and-forth between the two Bots with sender names, avatars, timestamps and a 'This chat is view-only' footer. The existing big blue voice-exchange card must follow the same convention ('Message from Voice' marker + view-only chat), so the voice card is deleted, not kept. Tim approved screenshots of the marker and the view before the cloud half was built, and asked for ONE PR covering both halves. Deliberate decisions: (1) Bot callers now answer with reply_to_request (caller 'bot') instead of send_to_user with disposition finish, matching voice, so a Bot's answer to another Bot no longer mints a User message/unread/notification in the target thread — the target may still send_to_user separately if the person should hear; (2) the wire projects a bot_message tool call as a new 'message/to-bot' event in place of its tool/call, keyed by callId so the tool/result pairs with it, carrying botId and text only — the client resolves the Bot's name from its directory (a renamed/deleted Bot is named by what the client knows); (3) the run list query gains an optional 'counterpart' field (URL ?with=bot:<id> or ?with=voice) that filters to Turns crossing to/from that counterpart, inbound by admission origin and outbound by a bot_message call in the journal; this hydrates journals within the existing scan budget rather than adding an index, accepted as v1 cost; the client merges these pages with the loaded thread so in-flight exchanges update live; (4) no new durable pair record — the pair chat is derived from run records; (5) the client accepts the new wire shapes in the same change since there are no real users yet and the repo rule is no compatibility shims; the query field is named 'counterpart' (not 'with') because 'with' is a Dart keyword and the Dart wire generator cannot emit it; (6) the exchange marker's long-press still opens Work details; queued inbound exchanges no longer count as a supersede drain in the client; (7) docs (voice.md, architecture.md, voice-live-checklist, CONTEXT.md 'Exchange' term, parity 57f) updated; voice_exchange_test.dart replaced by exchange_test.dart which also renders review screenshots when EXCHANGE_VISUAL_OUTPUT is set. `/setup` is now the one place to configure the account: Overview, Plan and credit, Computer, AI, Web search, Connected apps and Your accounts. It follows the reviewed "FrockBot Setup App" canvas in the Paper look, and in Ink when the account is on Ink.

The app's Setup door opens it signed in. The Flutter Models page and the Marketplace are gone.

![Setup's AI page](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/raw/claude/eager-franklin-sy7ssj/app/whats-new/media/setup.webp)

## What changed

**The page**
- A small Preact app in `apps/cloudflare/setup/`. `build-setup.ts` bundles it into the Worker's assets under `/_setup/`, and it runs after the Flutter build in `client:build`.
- `src/setup-page.ts` serves the document before auth, since it names no account.
- The document has its own CSP: `script-src 'self'`, `style-src 'self'`, `connect-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'self'`. It has no inline script or style.
- Every page is its own address: `/setup/ai`, `/setup/plan`, and so on.
- On a phone the layout is one column at 390px wide. Every control is at least 44px tall.

**Reading the account from a frame**
- `HostFrame` carries no session: the web iframe is `credentialless` and the phone's web view has its own store.
- So the app mints a reader credential (`POST /api/setup/frame`, `src/setup-reader.ts`): an HMAC over the User and a one-hour expiry, in its own key domain.
- It travels in the URL fragment. The page moves it to session storage and sends it as `Bearer frockbot-setup.…`.
- `identifyRequest` admits it the way it admits a cookie, but only on the account routes `setupReaderPathV1` names. That excludes Bot routes, saved secrets, deletion and the mint itself, so a page cannot renew itself.
- When the credential expires, the page asks the app for another.
- Sign-ins, payment pages and "Back to your bots" go to the app over `postMessage`. The app opens sign-ins with its own `openConnectionDoorV1`, so a phone comes back to itself.
- The app document's `frame-src` now names `/setup`.

**Real data, through routes that already exist**
- **AI:**
  - Frock AI / Custom. The chat model is set with `user/set-account-model`.
  - The provider picker is a searchable list of every model provider, grouped FrockBot / Popular / All providers / Your own.
  - Connecting a provider adds it, takes the key and any settings (Advanced holds the optional ones), and offers **Sign in** where the provider has it. It then lists the provider's models.
  - The Images model is set here too (the `image` Package setting).
  - A failed chat provider is shown, not hidden.
- **Plan and credit:** every plan the deployment sells, BYO included (#962). "Suits your setup" comes with one sentence of why. Also: credit, top-ups, plan changes, and what used credit, with "Jev: Included" and "Your own …: Paid to them".
- **Web search:** FrockBot's or the account's own Brave, Exa, Tavily or SearXNG, through `/api/web-search` (#960).
- **Connected apps:** a searchable app catalog with Connect and Remove, and MCP servers with add, sign in and remove.
- **Your accounts:** every provider key, app and server, with what uses each. Replace key and Remove warn about what stops. Keys are write-only.
- **Overview:** the "needs you" banner, the who-runs-what strip, and summary cards.

**Coming soon, drawn but inert**
- A different provider per job other than chat. That backend is still in progress.
- A Computer of the person's own: Fly.io, a server, or the Mac. #958 stores only FrockBot's today.
- Test a search.
- Composio of the person's own.

**Flutter**
- `lib/setup/page.dart` hosts the frame and answers its messages.
- The sidebar's Marketplace door, the You page's Models row and the Cmd+K entry all open Setup.
- Deleted: `lib/connections/page.dart` (the whole Marketplace; Setup now covers connectors and MCP) and `lib/settings/page.dart`.
- Personal details moves to `lib/settings/personal_details.dart`, with the Models code removed. The only per-account `package.*` section, Image generation, is now on Setup's AI page.
- `model_picker.dart` stays, because a Bot's own chat-model override still uses it.
- `connections/document.dart` keeps only the door and return-link requests.

**Server**
- Removed: `modelsSettingsFrame`, `modelsSettingsCommand`, the "Model in use" line, `/api/settings/models`, and the `home` parameter on the settings RPCs.
- Removed from the wire schema: the provider-section `credentialStatus` and `manage-provider` action, and `ConnectionsFrame.modelInUse`. TS and Dart were regenerated.
- The native settings hand-off lands on `/setup/ai` or `/setup/apps`.
- The unused `models` and `connections` settings-link surfaces are gone.

## Where this differs from the design
- **"Your Sprites" is labelled "Your Fly.io".** `check-computer-host-imports.ts` forbids Fly's own vocabulary outside the host code.
- **Silent fallback.** When the chosen chat provider fails, `resolveEffectiveBotModelV1` still lets the platform model stand in. The page says exactly that ("Until it's fixed, your bots answer with Frock AI, from your credit") rather than claiming bots stop. Removing that stand-in is a runtime change I left out of this PR.

## Validation
- **Fast tier:** `bun run validate format typecheck unit` is green.
- **Slow tiers:** `runtime` (402), `integration` (189) and `build` are green. They ran before the merge of `main`.
- **Browser suite:** the core corpus (`FROCKBOT_E2E_SUITE=core`) ran after the merge: 69 passed, 2 failed.
  - Both failures were re-run: all five Setup specs and `chat.e2e.ts:649` pass.
  - The publication lane could not run here: its container build cannot reach npm through this sandbox's proxy.
  - Before merging `main`, Bots in this sandbox couldn't reply ("AbortSignal serialization is not enabled"). #967 fixes that, and the merge brought it in.
- New e2e (`setup.e2e.ts`):
  - Setup changes chat and a Bot then answers with the person's model, and back.
  - The app opens Setup in its frame signed in by the reader credential.
  - Web search saves SearXNG and goes back to FrockBot's.
  - An MCP server form.
  - The phone layout.
- **Flutter:** `flutter analyze` is clean and `flutter test` passes (1,715).
- **Not run:** the `no-mistakes` gate isn't installed in this session.

## Shipping notes
- Dart-only client change, so the tag's Shorebird patch carries it. No native, asset or plugin change.
- No stored shape changes. The removed fields are wire projections only.
- What's New entry `setup`, with the still above.

Nine findings from the v3 verification wave (`findings-v3/chat.md`), plus the two the coordinator added after the stack came back up.

## The blocker

A Stop or supersede leaves a run terminal in intent before recovery ever looks at it. Recovery planned a resume for it anyway, reached `Model response outcome is uncertain after cancellation`, and `executeAdmittedRun` rethrew after recording the failure durably — into an alarm with no caller. The rejection was uncaught, wrangler exited, and the shared dev stack went down mid-run for every agent using it.

- `recoverActiveRun` settles a discarded run on the intent already durable. `failStoredRun` routes it to `cancelled`/`superseded` and closes the open turn on the way.
- `alarm()` records a failed recovery and re-arms in a `finally` — a failure is a logged fact, and the next firing is the retry.
- The User application's own `fetch` is an entry point in its own right (its own isolate, its own Request), and it was the remaining hole: it now answers 404/500 with a reason instead of dying. That is where the log's five uncaught `BotNotFoundError`s went. The Applet socket callbacks record what escapes them, and the Worker logs unhandled rejections no boundary caught. There is no `ctx.waitUntil` anywhere in the repo, so there were no detached promises to guard.

Note the `bot-state` entry-boundary work landed in `e8c99761`, after the tree the tester ran, so those points were already covered.

**Workerd regression** (`apps/cloudflare/test/interrupted-recovery.workerd.ts`): stop a Turn, evict, fire the alarm — no throw, the run stays terminal, and the next message is answered. Verified failing with the guard disabled.

## A refused send says why

The client treated every non-2xx from `POST /turns` as an uncertain admission, so a 120 KB message was rendered optimistically — a full screen of it — then answered with "Checking whether your message went through…" over a run lookup that 500'd. Any 4xx is the server having read the request and said no: the composer keeps the draft, shows the server's own sentence, and starts no reconciliation. The composer counts down to the same limit and stops before it.

This needed one change outside the client: the transport now carries the response status on the error it throws. Without it "what went wrong" and "is it settled" are the same question, and they are not.

## A backend this tab cannot reach

The placeholder sorted above the message it reported on, and `reconcileUncertainAdmission` retried for ever. It is now ordered after its message, bounded to six attempts with backoff, and settles to a line saying the app could not reach the Bot — with a Retry and the draft kept. The sentence appears once, in the bubble that carries the Retry, not again in the banner above it.

## A hung model request

PR 170's deadlines only ever applied to the OpenAI-compatible transport. Flock AI — the default, and the one the tester hit — bypassed them entirely and was bounded by nothing short of the fifteen-minute Turn deadline. That is the empty bubble.

Both transports now go through one seam that owns the clock, with an injectable timer so the deadlines are testable without waiting: 120 s to first byte, 60 s between chunks, each failing the step with plain-language copy. Cancellation was also audited for shared state a Stop could poison; none was found, and both transports gained a regression proving request B still completes after request A is aborted.

## The rest

- **F3** — a Turn the User stopped is an ordinary completion: the long-lived `POST /turns` answers 200 with the cancelled run instead of 500 beside a UI reading "You stopped this."
- **F10** — an abandoned reconciliation that settles the run returns that run rather than rethrowing, so "Try again" stops answering 409. A failure the authority composes from an error message is bounded on the way in, because nothing upstream bounds `error.message`: an oversized one was written anyway and then made every later read of that run throw.
- **F6** — a debug `limit` outside 1..20 is a 400 naming the range, refused at the gateway before it reaches the Bot's isolate.
- **F7** — the sidebar preview falls back to the transcript for a Bot with no stored preview record, instead of "No messages yet" over six messages.
- **F9** — a transcript read degrades an orphaned tool call to "no result recorded" rather than throwing. A read must never fail on data that is already durable.

## Verification

`bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (3470), `bun run format:check`, the workerd suite (188), the integration suite (110), and `chat.e2e.ts` (6, including two new specs) all pass, re-run after merging `origin/main` a second time.

Three merge conflicts, each two changes to one seam rather than two answers to one question — the Flock AI resolution keeps main's signal pass-through *and* the deadline seam, with the seam's derived signal going down to the gateway.

## Left alone

`Uncaught Error: Bot turn ended with outcome model-error` still appears in the Worker log when a Turn fails. It predates this branch and is now at least logged rather than silent. Fixing it properly means `executeAdmittedRun` no longer rethrowing once it has durably recorded the failure — the finding's own long-term suggestion — which changes what every caller expects and is too broad to land beside these fixes.

hits.body:
## What

The Mac app can transcribe composer dictation on the device. Speech never leaves the Mac, costs nothing and works offline. This is §4 ("Voice and dictation") of the enthusiast setup plan.

- **Engine.** `apps/native/macos/Runner/LocalDictation.swift` runs NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8 Core ML) through [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio), pinned at 0.17.4 as a Swift package. Flutter talks to it over `com.frockbot/local-dictation`.
- **Model.** About 483 MB, downloaded on request into `~/Library/Application Support/FrockBot/dictation/`. Progress is read from the bytes on disk. Remove deletes the folder. Needs Apple silicon; on Intel the option is disabled.
- **Choice.** Your computers › This Mac › Dictation offers FrockBot's or On this Mac. It is stored locally under `voice.dictation.source.v1` so the setup app can take it over. The phone and the web keep cloud dictation.
- **Composer.** `LocalDictationSocket` speaks the server half of the dictation protocol on the device, so the existing `DictationController` drives it unchanged: same pill, stop, draft range and five-minute cap. On-device captures wait up to 60 s after stop instead of 6 s, because the first load onto the Neural Engine can be slow.
- **No silent fallback.** If On this Mac is chosen and the model is missing, the mic says so and offers Download.
- **Tidy-up still runs.** The relay's cleanup is extracted into `tidyVoiceDictationTranscriptV1` and exposed at `POST /api/voice/dictation/cleanup`, which takes text only. Same Groq call, same daily count and same Jev review. Offline, the raw text stands.
- **Billing.** On-device transcription is never metered.
- **macOS 14 minimum.** FluidAudio requires it, so the app's minimum rises from 13.4.
- **Also included.** Licences in `apps/native/macos/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (FluidAudio and its text-processing library are Apache 2.0; the Parakeet weights are CC BY 4.0, which allows on-demand download with attribution). Docs in `docs/voice.md#dictation-on-this-mac`. A What's New entry with no still.

**Native change: ships in a full Mac release, not a Shorebird patch.**

## Why Parakeet over whisper.cpp

For short dictation on Apple silicon, Parakeet TDT is both more accurate and faster:

- About 6% average WER on the Open ASR Leaderboard, against about 7.8% for Whisper large-v3-turbo.
- FluidAudio reports roughly 120–190× real time on the Neural Engine, where large-v3-turbo on Metal runs at tens of times real time.
- It runs on the Neural Engine rather than competing with the app for the GPU.

These are published figures. They were **not measured on our hardware**: this was built in a Linux container.

## Validation

- `flutter analyze` is clean, and `flutter test` passes in full (1,751 tests, 10 new in `test/voice_local_dictation_test.dart`).
- `bun run validate format typecheck unit` passes, including the new gateway route test.
- `bun run validate runtime` passes (408/408 workerd tests, including the dictation relay).

## Not done (needs a Mac)

- **Swift is not compiled.** It was reviewed by hand against FluidAudio 0.17.4's source; the first real check is an Xcode build.
- **Mac-side checks:** `bun run update:desktop`, dictation with the network off, model download and removal, and switching back to FrockBot's dictation.
- **Benchmark:** the on-Mac Parakeet vs whisper.cpp measurement.
- **What's New still:** none yet.
- **no-mistakes gate:** not installed in the container, so it has not run.
- **Podfile.lock:** the `Podfile` platform changed; run `pod install` on a Mac to refresh the lock's checksum.

Cuts 3 and 6 of the self-hosting plan. At `frockbot.com/deploy` a person signs in with Cloudflare, and the page installs the latest FrockBot release into that account through the Cloudflare API. It then updates that install in place with one click. Nothing is cloned or built on the person's machine. The pages follow the reviewed "frockbot.com/deploy" row of the FrockBot Setup App canvas.

The release goes in as its **deploy bundle, through the bundle's own deployer** (`deployBundleV1`, from #970), the same one `bun run setup` runs. So an install made here and one made from the repository are the same install. The install lives on `workers.dev` with no domain (#977, merged).

## What's here

- **Where it runs.** `/deploy` is served by the marketing Worker, in `apps/marketing/src/deploy/`. The pages are server-rendered under the site's existing CSP.
- **Sign in.** Cloudflare OAuth, as a confidential client with PKCE. A grant that reaches several accounts is sent back to sign in with just one. "Use a different account" asks Cloudflare for consent again.
- **Choose.** Shows the account, the name with its `workers.dev` address, and "Just you; teams are coming". Four account checks each show their fix:
  - Workers Paid
  - R2
  - Workers AI serving Jev
  - Zero Trust

  Deploy stays off until all four pass, and the server enforces the same rule.
- **Deploying.** A `DeployAccount` Durable Object per Cloudflare user runs the steps by alarm, so the deploy carries on after the page closes or the object is evicted. The steps:
  1. **Storage.** Stages the release's bundle once, for every install, into frockbot.com's own R2 (`DEPLOY_BUNDLES`). The archive streams from GitHub through gunzip and a tar reader, and its digest is taken on the way. The ~49 MB archive is too big for any Durable Object to hold unpacked. Then it creates the install's buckets and search index.
  2. **Sign-in.** Creates the Zero Trust organization if it's missing, then three Access applications:
     - Allow on the hostname, for the deployer's email only;
     - Bypass on `/api`;
     - Bypass on `/.well-known/frockbot.json`.
  3. **Release.** `deployBundleV1` installs the app and the Plugin build service onto `workers.dev`, with no Computer host. It sends `ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`, `ACCESS_AUD` and `APP_ORIGIN`.
     - Minted secrets count as set once the app Worker holds them. Until then they are minted and set on every Worker that shares them, so a first deploy that stopped between two Workers still converges.
     - Secrets only the Computer host needs are left to whoever deploys it.
     - `FROCKBOT_ADMIN_EMAILS` is set to the deployer's email.
  4. **Jev and Workers AI.**
  5. **First check.** `/` must redirect to Access, and `/api/identity` must be refused by the Worker itself.
- **Ready** and **Your installs** (with Update), as designed.
- **Tokens** live only in the Durable Object. A session and the deploy it started share one grant, because Cloudflare rotates refresh tokens on every use.
- **Docs:** `docs/hosted-deploy.md`. **What's New:** one entry.

![still](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/claude/lucid-bardeen-tr3hn2/app/whats-new/media/deploy-to-cloudflare.webp?raw=true)

## Verified, and what isn't

- **Real bundle.** Staged the published 0.7.320 bundle through this code: 2,345 files. Every module and the application artifact matched the manifest.
- **Deploy against a fake account.** An in-memory Cloudflare account ran the real `deployBundleV1` through:
  - a first deploy and an update, keeping secrets and appending migrations;
  - a first deploy that stopped between Workers;
  - a tampered module, and a tampered archive;
  - retry, and sign-out while a deploy runs;
  - the checks for a free plan, R2 off and no Zero Trust.
- **Not yet run against a real Cloudflare account.** That needs the OAuth client below.
- **Scopes.** These are the dotted names from the `cf` CLI's registered catalog (`DEPLOY_SCOPES_V1`, now including `containers.write` for the build service). They need checking against `GET /oauth/scopes` when the client is registered.
- **Workers Paid.** Cloudflare won't grant a third party a billing scope, so the check uploads a one-line Worker with a Worker Loader binding (only Paid accepts one) and deletes it.

## Before it works in production

1. **OAuth client.** Register it on the frockbot.com account, verify the domain and make it public. Then set `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` (variable) and `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` (secret) in `production`. `release.yml` passes both, and it creates the `frockbot-deploy-bundles` bucket if it's missing. Until then `/deploy` points at the repository.
2. **"A bot answers".** The first check proves the install answers behind Access. A bot's first reply needs its owner signed in.

The web client can now tell you about a new Bot message with the tab closed, through the browser's own push service. Each deployment signs with its own VAPID key pair, so a self-hosted install gets browser notifications with no Firebase, relay or FrockBot account. It sits beside the push relay (#968), which it leaves unchanged.

## What changed

**Keys per deployment**
- New required secret `WEB_PUSH_VAPID_KEYS` (`{subject, publicKey, privateKey}`), classified in `production-secrets.ts` and forwarded by `main.yml` / `release.yml`.
- Minted by `bun run setup`, by deploy bundles (a `vapid` mint shape, subject = the install's hostname), and for hosted and staging by `bun scripts/web-push-keys.ts <profile>`, which `setup-production.sh` uses.
- `GET /api/push/web` hands the client the public key (`null` without one, and the client then offers nothing).

**Server** (`apps/cloudflare/src/web-push.ts`, `push.ts`)
- `/api/push/device` accepts `platform: "web"`, whose token is the browser's `PushSubscription` JSON; the endpoint must be HTTPS on Google's, Mozilla's, Apple's or Microsoft's push service.
- A web token is delivered through its own `web` sender beside FCM and the relay: an RFC 8292 VAPID token (signing key imported once per isolate) and the payload sealed with core's `sealPushV1` (RFC 8291 `aes128gcm`). Never through FCM or the relay.
- Same delivery rules as FCM: recorded before sending, 429/5xx retried by key, anything else recorded uncertain, 404/410 forgets the subscription. Presence defers web pushes like any other.
- A browser is sent only messages it is to be told about (a `userVisibleOnly` subscription must draw every push); the open client clears its notifications from the read cursors.

**Client**
- `push-worker.js`, staged at the origin root outside the content-addressed payload: one notification per conversation (tagged per Bot or group, like Android), and a click focuses an open tab on that Bot or opens one.
- Profile → Notifications: asks only from the Turn on notifications tap. An iPhone or iPad tab is told to add the app to the Home Screen; the document now links a `standalone` manifest so that copy is an app.
- The web client registers its subscription directly whatever the server answers about `delivery: "relay"`.

**Docs and What's New**: `docs/notifications.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/deploy-bundles.md`, README, and a What's New entry (no still: the surface is the OS notification).

## Deploy notes
- `WEB_PUSH_VAPID_KEYS` is set in the `production` and `staging` GitHub environments. It must never be regenerated: every browser subscription is bound to the public key.
- No stored-data change and no native build change; Android and iOS behave as before.

## Validation
- On the rebased head: `Check` and `Flutter` green; pre-push `format`, `typecheck`, `unit` pass; `flutter analyze` clean and all 1,715 Flutter tests pass locally.
- Browser e2e, core suite (before the rebase): passes. Two specs timed out under the full parallel run and passed when rerun alone.
- Not run here: the e2e publication lane, whose Docker build cannot trust the sandbox's HTTPS proxy.
- Not yet verified: real delivery in Chrome, Firefox, Safari and an iPhone Home Screen app. To check on staging after merge: Profile → Notifications → Turn on, close the tab, message a Bot, click the notification.

The Android, iPhone and Mac apps can hold several accounts at once — frockbot.com and self-hosted installs — and switch between them like Slack workspaces. Web is unchanged.

**Needs a full Android release** (manifest, Kotlin and native plugin changes) and the Mac/iPhone Swift changes ship with the tag's builds; a Shorebird patch cannot carry this. Deploy order matters: the backend must land before the apps, which the tag pipeline already does.

## Server
- `/.well-known/frockbot.json` (public, ahead of the compatibility gate): name, protocol range, sign-in method (`browser-pkce` on the brand's scheme, or `unavailable`), and release tag (`FROCKBOT_RELEASE`, passed by `release.yml`).
- Every deployment with a native token secret now accepts sign-in returns on the app's own scheme, `<scheme>://native/return/<android|ios|macos>` (and `-dev`). PKCE plus the existing consent page keep this safe; `nativeAuth` now only names the verified https returns older apps use.
- Simple deployments get their origin from `APP_ORIGIN` (generated from the profile's app hostname); setup adds an Access bypass for the discovery file.
- Connect's Android callback page hands over on the scheme (with the server's host), as the Apple pages already did.
- `NativeReturnUri` schema widened; ADR 0028 revised.

## App
- **Use another server** reads the discovery file and says plainly when a server is too old, needs a newer app, has app sign-in off, or belongs to another app.
- Sign-in runs in `ASWebAuthenticationSession` (iOS/macOS) or a Custom Tab (Android).
- Each account has its own origin, keystore token, caches and unread under an `account/<id>/` prefix; signing out of one leaves the others. First launch clears the single-account shape (one re-sign-in), per the disposable-state rule.
- Sidebar account switcher with other accounts' unread; the dock and iPhone badge include them.
- Push stays on frockbot.com accounts; device registration is per account for the push relay; tapped alerts carry `user=` and open the right account.

## Also
- AGENTS.md and `apps/native/README.md` now leave releases to CI; the Tailscale APK server is removed from `native-update.py`.

## What's New

![The account switcher open over the Bot list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/claude/bold-knuth-otqd19/app/whats-new/media/several-accounts.webp)

- Fast tier (format, typecheck, unit), `validate:runtime`, `validate:integration`, `flutter analyze`, full `flutter test` (1,761), `flutter build web`.
- Not run: `no-mistakes` (not installed in the session container); Swift/Kotlin were not compiled here, and nothing was tried on a device.

## Intent

Realtime voice on the phone stopped working: Tim starts a voice session, speaks, and hears no reply, with no message in the footer. A production tail showed two calls on 2026-09-12 that the VoiceAssistant Durable Object accepted, that streamed audio for 0.2 s and 6 s, and that the phone then closed cleanly (code 1005, no reason) with no server log, no refusal recorded, and no utterance ever transcribed. Tim asked for better telemetry so the next attempt is diagnosable from the server: 'Do you need to add some more tests or logging and deploy it so we have better telemetry?' The change deliberately adds observability only, no behavior change to the call itself: (1) the object logs one structured 'voice assistant {json}' line per step (connected, call-admitted, upstream state, listening, utterance with length only and never the words, turn, turn-settled, refused with code and message, stt-failed, call-ended, closed with the client's code/reason/wasClean), each carrying connection id, device key, call id and elapsed ms; refusals and closes log at warn/info respectively; transcript text is never logged by design. (2) The Flutter client now closes the socket with a code and reason naming the path that ended the call: 1000 with 'end-button', 'ended', or 'lifecycle:<state>' when the person or the app ended it, 4001 with the failure sentence when the controller failed on its own, 4002 'disposed' when the controller was torn down mid-call; the reason is truncated to 120 UTF-8 bytes to respect the 123-byte close-reason limit. The VoiceSocket interface gained optional code/reason parameters with defaults so the dictation controller is unchanged. Tests: the phone's assistant tests assert the close code and reason on the refusal, end and dispose paths (executing the controller, not grepping source). docs/voice.md documents the close codes and the trace lines. The tsgo-backed typescript fork could not narrow the settlement union via 'in', so the trace reads the fields through an explicit optional cast; that is intentional. Known but out of scope for this PR: the phone's Applet WebView was reconnecting its viewer socket about twice a second with a 401 for the whole observation window, and the app re-registered push once a second alongside it; that loop is suspected of ending voice via lifecycle churn and will be a separate fix once the new telemetry names the close path.

## What Changed

- `VoiceAssistant` (apps/cloudflare) now writes one structured `voice assistant {json}` line per step of a call — `connected`, `refused-identity`, `call-admitted`, `upstream`, `listening`, `listening-without-call`, `utterance`, `turn`, `turn-dropped`, `turn-settled`, `speech-suppressed`, `refused`, `stt-failed`, `call-ended` and `closed` (with the client's code, truncated reason and `wasClean`). Every line carries the connection id and device key, and once admitted the call id and elapsed ms; a small `#traced` map keeps the call id and start time alive past `releaseCall` so the `closed` line still names the call. Refusals and STT failures log at warn, the rest at info; transcript text is never logged, only lengths.
- The Flutter client closes its socket with a code and reason naming the path that ended the call: `1000` with `end-button` / `lifecycle:<state>` / `server-closed`, `4001` with the failure sentence, `4002` `disposed`, and `4003` `abandoned-connect` for a socket that arrives after the call ended or after the connect window expired (previously left unclosed). `VoiceSocket.close` gained optional `code`/`reason` with defaults so the dictation controller is untouched, and `voiceCloseReasonV1` truncates the reason to 120 UTF-8 bytes on a character boundary to fit the 123-byte wire limit.
- Tests: Dart tests drive the controller through the refusal, end, lifecycle, server-close, dispose and abandoned-connect paths and assert the resulting close code and reason, plus a new `voice_close_reason_test.dart` covering multibyte truncation; the workerd test asserts the closing trace still carries call id and a non-negative `elapsedMs` after `end_call`. `docs/voice.md` documents the close codes and a guide to reading the trace lines.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is observability-only and verified as such: the server-side traces log ids, lengths and enums but never transcript or answer text, the `#traced` correlation map and the UTF-8 close-reason truncation from prior fix rounds both hold under concrete traced sequences, teardown ordering sends the correct close reason, and the only open item is an inert redundant slice in a log path.

## Testing

`I stood the voice object up in workerd and opened real WebSockets to it, driving a whole call (connect, a grunt, an utterance, a spoken reply, End, close 1000/end-button), a socket presenting somebody else's identity, a day whose speech allowance runs out mid-call, and a transcript that arrives with no call — capturing the operator's trace tail exactly as the object emits it. The tail reads connected → call-admitted → upstream starting/awake → listening → utterance (chars only) → turn → turn-settled → call-ended → closed{code:1000,reason:"end-button",wasClean:true}, and the closing line still carries the call id and elapsedMs after end_call released the call record. Adversarially, I planted distinctive words in every transcript and asserted no trace line anywhere contains them; I drove two suppressed sentences and confirmed speech-suppressed is written each time while the quota refusal is still said once; and I reproduced the reported production symptom shape (a transcript that reaches the object with no call) and confirmed it now emits turn-dropped{reason:"no-call"} instead of nothing. On the client I drove the real ChannelVoiceSocket against a real WebSocket server and read the close frames off the server: all six named paths arrive intact, and a failure sentence of multibyte characters far over the limit arrives at 119 bytes, valid UTF-8 — while the same reason sent unguarded is rejected by the platform ("reason must be <= 123 bytes") and the server sees no reason at all, so the truncation is load-bearing. The controller-level close-code selection was exercised only through the Flutter suite's fake socket, which is not the live product, so it is reported untested here; the equivalent behaviour on the wire is covered by the live client-close-frames scenario. No screenshots: this change has no rendered surface — its user-visible output is server log lines and WebSocket close frames, both captured verbatim as artifacts. Warn-vs-info log level is not separately observable through the test probe (it intercepts both), and the stt-failed / listening-without-call traces have no external seam to force. Everything driven live passed.`

## Intent

Set up Composio as FrockBot's connection backend for external providers, as a proper integration rather than the Composio MCP: (1) new tools for Bots to call, and (2) later, new triggers for Routines. Tim's decisions: it is first-party app code (app/connect), not a plugin over the http grant, overriding the earlier plan note; Composio is invisible plumbing, no Composio vocabulary in copy, each toolkit is its own Connectors row; only apps the User actually connected appear in the prompt, and only Composio's 'important' tool subset; a curated toolkit list to start (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, GitHub, Slack, Notion) expanded later by editing the list; the consent-screen branding is understood and accepted; multiple accounts of one app (two Gmails) must work; COMPOSIO_API_KEY and COMPOSIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET are optional production secrets Tim set in the production environment, and the webhook URL https://bot.frockbot.com/api/connect/events is registered at Composio for cut 3 (Routine triggers), which is deliberately not in this change, so markAccountExpired and any webhook code are intentionally absent. Tim then said the generic document-rendered Connectors page looked bad, asked for icons, chose ONE generic Connectors page for every kind of connector (not a dedicated page), and after a second look asked for it to be compact like GrokBot's marketplace rows. So the Flutter Connectors page is host chrome over ConnectionsFrame: one compact row per provider (bundled icon from assets/connectors/<slug>.png rasterised from the provider's public logos, name, one truncated description line, a trailing Connect pill or the state pill), with the accounts, add-another and the inline name-and-key form shown below the row once it is tapped; two columns at 640px and up; the frame gained description and icon on provider rows and connectionTypeId on account rows; the Connectors document projection and its route branch were deleted (nothing is kept for compatibility); the e2e Ollama fixture's contract (connections-document id, provider card named by title, the Connect pill then 'Advanced - custom server', field labels, view-action-connect-<index>) is kept and the fixture updated for the pill's shorter label. Backend cuts 1 and 2: connections through the existing authorize press with a public return page that touches no Durable Object and settlement on the next settings read via a read bootstrap (a known, accepted trade-off: while a sign-in is outstanding, a Turn's settings read may make one throttled provider call); disconnect deletes upstream with revoke_on_delete; ModelOAuthCommandV1 gained optional connectionTypeId; one Tool Namespace per ready Connection (toolkit slug, first free -N suffix for another account) pinned per Turn via pinToolCatalog; execution uses the deployment key plus the account id from safe metadata, so no credential is leased; a transport failure after dispatch is reported as an unknown outcome and never retried because Composio has no idempotency key. API shapes verified against Composio's v3.1 OpenAPI on 2026-09-11. Harness stub at backend.composio.dev; connect-apps.integration.ts covers the flow end to end; Flutter connections_test covers the page.

## What Changed

- Adds a first-party `app/connect` package that backs a curated set of connectable apps (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, GitHub, Slack, Notion), each its own Connection Type with a hosted grant: `app/connect/user.ts` mints the sign-in link and writes the Connection in the User Durable Object, `app/connect/backend.ts` serves the start/revoke routes plus a public return page that touches no Durable Object, and the next settings read reconciles an outstanding sign-in to `ready` or `failed`. Disconnect deletes upstream with `revoke_on_delete`, multiple accounts per app are allowed, and `ModelOAuthCommandV1` gained an optional `connectionTypeId`.
- Mounts one Tool Namespace per ready Connection for every Bot (`app/connect/agent.ts`), named for the app with the first free `-N` suffix for a second account, carrying only the provider's "important" tool subset and pinned per Turn via `pinToolCatalog`; execution uses the deployment `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` plus the account id from safe metadata so no credential is leased, and a transport failure after dispatch is reported as an unknown outcome rather than retried.
- Rebuilds the Flutter Connectors page as host chrome over `ConnectionsFrame`: one compact row per provider with a bundled icon, name, truncated description and a trailing Connect or state pill, accounts and the inline add form revealed on tap, two columns at 640px and up; the frame gained `description`/`icon` on provider rows and `connectionTypeId` on account rows, and the old Connectors document projection and its gateway route branch were deleted.
- Adds `connect-apps.integration.ts` covering the flow end to end against a stubbed provider via a new Miniflare test harness, extends the Flutter `connections_test` for the new page, and documents the optional `COMPOSIO_API_KEY`/`COMPOSIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` secrets in the README, CI workflows and architecture docs.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change is large (a new first-party integration subsystem plus a full Connectors page rewrite) but is well covered by behavioural unit, Flutter widget and end-to-end gateway tests, satisfies the stated intent including the deliberate cut-3 omissions, and the surviving findings are unrequired components and one fail-closed decode edge that are safe to address as follow-ups rather than merge blockers.

I stood the product up twice — the SELF.fetch integration stack (production src/index.ts, real Durable Objects, real built application artifact, provider stubbed only at the outbound seam) and the browser e2e harness (wrangler dev serving the real Flutter web client) — and drove each scenario through them. The existing connect integration file covered the rows, the hand-off, the failure line, the namespaced tool call and the disconnect; I added three scenarios it lacked: two Gmail accounts taking gmail and gmail-2 with a Bot reaching the second by name, a retry after a failed sign-in retiring the dead row and keeping the app's own name, and a settings read that must not stall behind a hanging provider (the harness stub now hangs Notion's account read for 20s; the read returns in ~5.0s with Gmail settled and Notion left to be asked again). All eight pass. The Flutter page test and the connect unit tests pass. Visual evidence is from the running product in Chromium: the compact Connectors rows with bundled icons at two widths, the row opened onto the inline name-and-key form, a connect carried through to the Ready state pill and 'Add another account', and the public return page. One visual is missing and cannot be produced here — a connector row expanded over a genuinely connected app account needs a real Composio sign-in, which needs the production COMPOSIO_API_KEY and a live consent screen; the equivalent row-open, account-pill and add-another chrome is the same widget and is shown on the provider-account screenshot. Transient build outputs, harness logs and the temporary .dev.vars were removed; only the two intentional test-file changes remain in the worktree.

## Intent

Follow-up telemetry for the realtime voice bug. With PR #439's trace lines live, Tim's first traced call (2026-09-12 05:51Z) showed transcription, the turn and a 167-character model answer all succeeding, followed 0.3 s later by two SDK-logged 'ElevenLabs TTS stream failed: AbortError' lines, and Tim heard nothing. What is still unknown is who aborted the synthesis (the upstream's server VAD barge-in, the phone's local energy gate sending {type:'interrupt'}, or a pipeline replacement) and whether any synthesized audio ever left the object. Tim asked for more logging deployed rather than guessing ('Do you need to add some more tests or logging and deploy it so we have better telemetry?') and said 'PR and merge when done', so this is observability only, no behavior change: the object traces 'speech-started' when the upstream's own voice detector fires (wrapping onSpeechStart in the sleeping-transcriber session options), 'interrupted' from the SDK's onInterrupt hook (which fires for both detectors; the SDK consumes the client's 'interrupt' frame before onMessage, so a client interrupt is 'interrupted' with no preceding 'speech-started' and that reading is documented), 'audio' from afterSynthesize for the first chunk of each sentence (chars, bytes, running chunk count; the audio is passed through unchanged), and audioChunks/audioBytes/sentencesSpoken totals on 'call-ended'. LiveCall gained the counters. The workerd spoken-reply test asserts the audio line, the interrupted line after a client interrupt with no speech-started, and the call-ended totals, driving the object through the socket; the probe's VoiceTraceLine type gained the new optional fields. docs/voice.md enumerates the new lines and how to read them. Transcript text and provider error sentences are still never logged.

## What Changed

- `VoiceAssistant` now traces `speech-started` (wrapping `onSpeechStart` on the sleeping transcriber's session options, so the upstream's own voice detector is on record), `interrupted` from the SDK's `onInterrupt` hook, and an `audio` line from `afterSynthesize` for the first chunk of each sentence (characters, bytes, running chunk count) — the audio buffer is returned unchanged. The per-connection trace record gained `audioChunks`, `audioBytes`, `sentencesSpoken` and a per-sentence `awaitingFirstChunk` map, and `call-ended` now carries those three totals.
- The workerd tests drive the object through the socket to assert the `audio` line for a spoken reply, repeated identical sentences each getting their own line with a counted socket frame, an `interrupted` line after a client `interrupt` with no preceding `speech-started`, a `speech-started` line ordered before `interrupted` for the upstream detector, and the `call-ended` totals surviving a superseded call. The probe's `VoiceTraceLine` gained the new optional fields and `VoiceProbeScript` a `reply` override.
- `docs/voice.md` enumerates the new trace lines and how to read them, including that an `interrupted` without a preceding `speech-started` means the client sent the `interrupt` frame. Transcript text and provider error sentences are still never logged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: Observability-only change with no behavior change and a correct prior-round fix, but the counters and their documentation overclaim what they prove (synthesized vs. sent), and stale first-chunk marks after an aborted sentence can still over-count a repeated sentence - both wrong readings in the very failure the telemetry was added to diagnose.

## Testing

I stood the voice Durable Object up in workerd (miniflare, the way the app runs it) and drove it through the client WebSocket: start a call, speak an utterance, get a synthesized reply, interrupt from the phone, fire the upstream voice detector, and let a second device supersede the first. Evidence is the operator-facing artifact for this change — the literal trace lines the object logs — captured for three flows, showing `speech-started`, `audio {chars, bytes, chunk}`, `interrupted` and `call-ended {audioChunks, audioBytes, sentencesSpoken}` with the right values, and showing the phone's interrupt arriving with no `speech-started` before it. Two mutation checks prove the assertions actually bind: removing the speech-start hook and re-introducing the previous-chunk-text comparison each turn a test red. I added the one missing test (the `speech-started` line had no coverage) and an assertion that the counted chunks arrive as frames on the socket. No screenshot: this change has no UI surface — its entire product surface is the structured log tail, which is captured verbatim. The real ElevenLabs streaming path (several chunks per sentence) is the one thing I could not drive here.

## Intent

Tim reported the realtime voice assistant is slow to respond and that a question he asked got no spoken answer. Diagnosis found (1) the ElevenLabs adapter in @cloudflare/voice-elevenlabs swallows every failure (non-2xx, quota, thrown) and yields zero audio, so a turn settles as answered while the person hears silence with no record; (2) the Flutter client maps ANY SDK {type:error} frame to _fail, ending the whole call on a recoverable per-turn error; (3) the client streams every mic frame to OpenAI server VAD while the assistant is speaking, so the speaker's echo can trip the VAD and abort the reply; (4) the PcmVoicePlayer latched _unavailable forever on one setup failure; (5) the SDK's speak() aborts an in-flight reply, so a Bot delegation settling mid-reply silently cut the reply; (6) no trace line gave the turn's timing. This PR is Phase 0+1 of an agreed multi-phase plan (later phases: STT swap to ElevenLabs Scribe v2, thin turn + pinned voice model, SDK upgrade). Decisions: wrap the TTS provider with a pure app/voice/tts-guard.ts that throws VoiceSynthesisSilentErrorV1 when a sentence yields no audio (aborted requests stay quiet) so the SDK's own per-sentence catch sends the client an error frame and continues - deliberately NOT a new wire message; add trace lines model-first-text (ms), turn-settled.ms, audio.turn + sinceTurnMs, tts-failed, delegation-held; hold a settled delegation while a reply is in flight or for 6 s after (REPLY_DRAIN_QUIET_MS, a documented heuristic because the SDK has no after-turn hook), rescheduling via a new public speakSettledDelegation scheduler method with a test seam replyDrainQuietMs(). Phone: an error frame shows a 4 s notice on the footer and keeps the call (mute + end controls stay); while the reply plays (status speaking OR player.level > 0) the client sends zero-filled frames at the same cadence so the upstream stays awake and its VAD never hears the speaker, holds the last 500 ms of real audio and on local barge-in sends interrupt, then the held audio, then live frames; the player retries device setup after 2 s and bounds held audio to 5 s instead of latching unavailable; feed throws no longer latch. Tests: bun unit tests for the guard; workerd tests for the silent-TTS path and the held delegation; Flutter tests for silent frames, barge-in ordering, playback tail, and error-frame notice; docs/voice.md updated (barge-in, a reply that fails, trace lines). The metrics frame the SDK sends the client is intentionally still ignored on the phone: server-side timing covers it. Known pre-existing: Main's browser e2e shard 3 is red on a routines cron test unrelated to this change; the full workerd suite prints one stderr uncaught BotTurnRefusedError busy line that does not fail any test.

## What Changed

- Added `app/voice/tts-guard.ts`, a pure wrapper that throws `VoiceSynthesisSilentErrorV1` when a sentence yields no audio (aborted requests stay quiet), and wired it around the worker's TTS provider so a silent reply now reaches the client as an error frame instead of settling as answered; the worker also traces `model-first-text`, `turn-settled.ms`, `audio.turn`/`sinceTurnMs`, `tts-failed` and `delegation-held`, and holds a settled Bot delegation while a reply is in flight (or for `REPLY_DRAIN_QUIET_MS` = 6 s after) by rescheduling a new public `speakSettledDelegation`, with a `replyDrainQuietMs()` test seam.
- On the Flutter client, an uncoded error frame now shows a 4 s footer notice and keeps the call (only coded errors, refusals and socket loss still end it); while the reply plays (status `speaking` or `player.level > 0`) the client sends zero-filled frames at the same cadence so the upstream VAD never hears the speaker, holding the last ~500 ms of real audio and, on local barge-in, sending `interrupt` then the held audio then live frames.
- `PcmVoicePlayer` no longer latches unavailable: device setup is retried after 2 s, up to 5 s of audio is held meanwhile, and a failed feed resets level and idle instead of killing playback for the call.
- Added bun tests for the guard, workerd tests for the silent-TTS path and the held delegation, and Flutter tests for silent frames, barge-in ordering, playback tail and the error-frame notice; `docs/voice.md` documents barge-in, a reply that fails, and the new trace lines.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change is well-covered by behavioral tests and the fix-round edits are all correct, but the newly added held-delegation path drops its own wakeup on a second consecutive hold (a silent non-answer, with a one-argument remedy), and the playback-tail silencing rule is an intent-level trade-off worth the author's confirmation.

## Testing

I stood the voice assistant Durable Object up in workerd and drove it over a real WebSocket as the phone does: a reply whose speech yields no audio now reaches the client as an `error` frame ("speech synthesis produced no audio"), the call returns to `listening` instead of ending, a `tts-failed` line with the sentence length lands in the trace, and the next question is heard normally — with `model-first-text`, `turn-settled.ms` and `audio.turn/sinceTurnMs` present and consistent. A Bot delegation settling mid-reply traces `delegation-held` rather than speaking over the reply, and is read out once the drain window passes, with the read-out's audio line carrying no turn attribution. Finding that nothing covered a *second* consecutive hold — the case commit 24f128f4 changed `idempotent` for — I added a stall seam to the probe and a test that holds twice; it times out with the old `idempotent: true` and passes with the fix, and I captured its wire transcript showing two `delegation-held` lines followed by the answer being spoken. On the phone side, 110 Flutter voice tests pass, covering zero-filled frames at the same 40 ms cadence while the reply plays, barge-in sending interrupt then the held 500 ms then live frames with no frame lost or repeated, the playback tail keeping the mic silenced until the player drains, a rejected feed dropping the level to zero instead of muting the caller, and a failed device setup being retried after 2 s while holding only the newest 5 s. For the UI change I rendered the real footer and captured PNGs: the uncoded error shows the notice with both mute and end still there, the notice expires back to the meter, and a coded error ends the call with only the exit control. The one gap: the guard's abort branch (barge-in cancelling an in-flight synthesis) was never driven through a running call — the workerd probe's fake TTS resolves synchronously, so no synthesis stays in flight long enough to abort; that scenario is reported untested. No failures; the only stderr noise is the pre-existing `BotTurnRefusedError:busy` line the author already flagged, which fails nothing.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 12 of 13 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A reply whose speech produces no audio is told to the phone, recorded, and the call keeps listening | ✅ pass | live | workerd test `a sentence that never becomes sound is on record, told to the phone, and the call goes on`; wire transcript in voice-server-wire-and-traces.txt shows `{"type":"error","message":"speech s… |
| The provider recovers: the next question is heard, and its first audio chunk says how long after the turn it left | ✅ pass | live | same workerd test; trace line `{"event":"audio",...,"turn":"...:2","sinceTurnMs":0}` and a binary audio frame on the wire for turn 2 |
| A slow turn can be blamed on the right stage: model-first-text and turn-settled carry the same turn and ordered ms | ✅ pass | live | trace lines in voice-server-wire-and-traces.txt: model-first-text ms:9 and turn-settled ms:9 on turn ...:1, asserted ordered in the workerd test |
| A Bot answer settling mid-reply is held rather than cutting the reply

Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.6.0

Minor Changes

  • #1850 938d3f4 - Task functions like { title, task } can now use a logger function log() to emit output while the task runs. By default, the output will only be visible if the task fails, unless the --verbose option was used. Additionally, when the task rejects, the error will be shown in the output.

    import { defineConfig } from 'lint-staged/config'

    export default defineConfig({
'*': {
title: 'Fail if PDF files are committed',
task: async (filepaths, { log }) => {
const pdfFiles = filepaths.filter((f) => f.toLowerCase().endsWith('.pdf'))
if (pdfFiles.length > 0) {
log('PDF files should not be committed: %s', pdfFiles)
throw new Error('Failed')
}
},
},
})

  • #1854 30562bc - lint-staged now stages changes to all tracked files modified by tasks, including files that weren’t originally staged or didn’t match the configured globs. This can happen when your task has side-effects, or it's a function that ignores the staged files like () => "prettier --write .".

    If you have unstaged changes in a file and the task also edits that file, your unstaged changes will be staged too. Use --hide-unstaged to hide your changes while tasks run.

Patch Changes

  • #1860 4296532 - The assignment of staged files to lint-staged configuration files (when using multiple, for example in a monorepo) has been rewritten to be more efficient. As a reminder, each staged file is assigned to exactly one configuration (the closest one), even if that config doesn't match the file in its globs.

  • #1861 c45f28a - Fix running parallel tasks for a single glob, when tasks are created by a function. Nesting one level of arrays inside an array of tasks will result in the inner tasks running in parallel. This behavior should now be consistent when creating tasks using functions. In the following example eslint and prettier will run in parallel (for all files, when any JS files are staged):

    import { defineConfig } from 'lint-staged/config'

    export default defineConfig({
'*.js': () => [['eslint --max-warnings=0 .', 'prettier --list-different .']],
})

  • #1859 f0ea69d - Various performance improvements from skipping redundant internal Git calls.

  • #1856 69d7d17 - Partially staged changes are hidden in a uniquely-named patch file to avoid multiple invocations of lint-staged overwriting it. This makes it safer to run lint-staged in multiple worktrees at the same time.

## Intent

Phase 4 of the voice latency plan, which Tim approved as part of 'lets optimise what we have … with better model choices' and then confirmed with 'do it' after Phases 2 and 3 released: bump the voice SDK. @cloudflare/voice 0.4.0 -> 0.5.0 (now a re-export of agents/voice), @cloudflare/voice-elevenlabs 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0, and therefore agents 0.22.0 -> 0.23.0 (the 0.5.0 voice package requires it). Deliberate decisions: no application code changes — the assistant's scheduler use, Scribe options and the TTS guard are unchanged because the SDK keeps those public APIs (0.23 migrates cf_agents_schedules rows into its new cf_agents_jobs queue on first wake, which is the SDK's job); the TTS guard stays because voice-elevenlabs 0.2.0 still swallows synthesis failures; no TTS optimize_streaming_latency knob because neither adapter version exposes one and ElevenLabs deprecated it. docs/architecture.md version line updated. Only the Worker package pins these. Verified locally: Worker typecheck, 376 unit tests, full workerd suite 49 files / 270 tests pass on the bump.

## What Changed

- Bumped the Worker's pinned voice dependencies in `apps/cloudflare/package.json`: `@cloudflare/voice` 0.4.0 → 0.5.0 (now a re-export of `agents/voice`), `@cloudflare/voice-elevenlabs` 0.1.0 → 0.2.0, and `agents` 0.22.0 → 0.23.0, with `bun.lock` updated to match. No application code changed — the assistant's scheduler use, Scribe options and the TTS guard rely on public APIs the SDK keeps.
- Added a workerd test in `apps/cloudflare/test/voice-assistant.workerd.ts` that deletes the `cf_agents_jobs` rows and the alarm, evicts the object, and asserts the next call re-books `checkDelegation` from the ledger and settles the delegation through the real 0.23 scheduler.
- Updated the `VoiceAssistant` section of `docs/architecture.md` to the new package versions and documented that the delegation schedule is disposable across the one-way `cf_agents_schedules` → `cf_agents_jobs` migration.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A three-pin dependency bump plus one documentation sentence, where the entire public API surface the Worker consumes is byte-identical between the old and new packages, the voice wire protocol version and message sets are unchanged, and the only genuinely new SDK behavior (the one-way cf_agents_schedules → cf_agents_jobs migration) is bounded by the assistant's existing onStart/onCallStart recovery, which the added doc sentence accurately describes.

## Testing

Installed the bumped dependency tree and drove the voice assistant Durable Object end to end in local workerd — real Worker runtime, real DO, real Agents SDK 0.23 scheduler and voice mixin, with the STT/chat/TTS upstreams as the suite's scripted seams — covering calls over the wire protocol, sleep/wake, per-day metering caps, the TTS guard's silent-synthesis path, delegation across eviction, the mid-reply hold and the lost-dispatch retry; all 18 voice-assistant tests and both dictation suites pass on the bump, as do the 78 voice unit tests, and the Worker still bundles for deploy. I added one adversarial scenario for the migration claim this change documents: with a delegation in flight the cf_agents_jobs queue and the alarm are deleted under the object, it is evicted, and only a fresh call wakes it — onStart re-books checkDelegation from the ledger and 0.23's alarm settles the delegation and reads the answer out with nothing run by hand. There is no rendered UI in this change (a backend Durable Object and a dependency pin), so the evidence is CLI and runtime transcripts rather than screenshots. Not driven: a real ElevenLabs/OpenAI-credentialed call and an actual rollback to agents 0.22 against a migrated object, both reported untested.

## Intent

Tim asked for five Composio connector fixes in the FrockBot app: (1) after connecting a connector from the mobile or desktop app, the browser should hand the person back to the app instead of a page saying it is safe to close the browser; (2) that return page should be styled properly, using the desktop app's post-sign-in return page as prior art; (3) Composio supports multiple connections per account (e.g. two Gmail addresses) and the app should too; (4) the Connect button on the phone felt unbalanced (a phone screenshot over wireless adb showed the label sitting low in the pill); (5) pressing Connect disabled every Connect button on the phone, which looked odd — only the pressed one should indicate something is happening, the others may be inert but must not look disabled. Decisions made: the start command gained an optional returnClient (android|macos) that the gateway turns into a callbackUrl on the connection/oauth command; the User Durable Object keeps only that path and always uses its own callbackBaseUrl origin, falling back to the plain /api/connect/callback for any unrecognised path. Android's manifest now claims https://bot.frockbot.com/api/connect/callback/android as a verified App Link so the redirect opens the app; the Mac page hands over on the frockbot:// scheme via a nonce'd inline script, mirroring the sign-in return; a browser tab gets an Open FrockBot button. The connect return page and the native sign-in return page now share one template, app/return-page.ts (the inlined app icon moved to app/return-page-logo.ts); the sign-in page's CSP moved from script-src 'unsafe-inline' to a per-response nonce, and its test was updated for that. For (3): the server already allowed multiple accounts (allowMultiple with namespace suffixes; Composio's refusal of a second account is an SDK-side preflight, not a REST rule, and our raw client never hit it), so the fix is discoverability: a connected row now shows an expand chevron beside its state so 'Add another account' is visibly one tap away. For (4): the pill got a fixed 32px height with the label style at height 1.0 and even leading distribution, verified by a 3x render with the real Manrope font. For (5): the page tracks pendingRow instead of a page-wide boolean; the pressed pill stays enabled and pink with a spinner replacing its label (width preserved), other rows are untouched, and a press on another row while one is in flight is ignored by the page's send guard. The app also listens for the return link (app_links stream) and re-reads the connections frame on arrival, not just on lifecycle resume. Tests: core decoder, connect user/backend, native-auth, workerd integration, and Flutter widget tests were extended and all pass.

## What Changed

- Connector starts now carry an optional `returnClient` (`android` | `macos`) through the `connection/start` decoder and the gateway, which turns it into a `callbackUrl` on the `connection/oauth` command; the User Durable Object keeps only the callback path, always re-hosts it on its own `callbackBaseUrl` origin, and falls back to the plain `/api/connect/callback` for any unrecognised path. Android's manifest claims `/api/connect/callback/android` as a verified App Link, the macOS page hands over on the `frockbot://` scheme via a nonce'd inline script, and a plain browser tab gets an "Open FrockBot" button.
- The connect return page and the native sign-in return page now render from one shared template (`app/return-page.ts`, with the inlined icon in `app/return-page-logo.ts`); `native-auth.ts` drops its own markup and moves from `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` to a per-response nonce.
- On the native connections page: connected rows gained an expand chevron so "Add another account" is one tap away, the Connect pill is a fixed 32px with the label at height 1.0 and even leading, pending state is tracked per row (only the pressed pill swaps its label for a spinner, others stay untouched and presses on them are ignored while one is in flight), and the page reloads the connections frame on the `app_links` return stream as well as on lifecycle resume, coalescing a read that arrives mid-flight.
- Extended coverage across the core command decoder, connect user/backend, `native-auth`, the workerd connect-apps integration test, and Flutter widget tests; `docs/architecture.md` documents the return links and shared return page.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change is well-tested and its security-relevant parts are sound (the DO keeps only the callback path and always uses its own origin, the decoder rejects unknown returnClient values, and the return pages moved off 'unsafe-inline' to per-response nonces), but the return-link re-read cannot actually settle a Connection because of the 3 s poll throttle, and the per-row busy split introduces a silent api-key drop — both worth addressing as follow-ups rather than blocking.

## Testing

Stood the gateway up under wrangler dev and the production Worker under the integration project, and brought the Flutter app up on an Android emulator through the repo's own native-dev stack. All three branded return pages were fetched live and screenshotted in Chromium (dark and light): the Mac page shows "Opening FrockBot" plus an Open FrockBot button and hands over to frockbot://bot.frockbot.com/api/connect/callback/macos under a per-response nonce, Android's page says "Head back to the FrockBot app", the browser-tab page offers Open FrockBot, and none of them reflect the query. Adversarially, POST to a return page is 405, an unrecognised sub-path never reaches a page (401 at the gateway door), and a start naming returnClient "ios" is refused. On the emulator the Marketplace rendered with the Connect label centred in the 32px pill, pressing Connect left only that pill spinning while every other Connect stayed pink and enabled, and firing the production App Link into the foregrounded app re-read the connections frame. Five things were not driven against the running product and are reported untested: completing a real hosted OAuth on device (the local Composio key is rejected 401 by the provider, identically with and without returnClient, so it is an environment credential issue and not a regression); the native sign-in return page, which is only served on the bot.frockbot.com origin with native-auth configured; the connected-row chevron and "Add another account", which no connector could reach on device without a valid provider key and which rest on 3x widget renders; the in-flight-read race; and the return-link matcher's rejections — the last two are exercised only by `flutter test`, not on the emulator. Multi-account support was exercised live through the existing integration test that holds two Gmail accounts under separate namespaces.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 11 of 16 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A Mac user finishing a connector sign-in lands on a branded page that hands them back to the app on frockbot:// | ✅ pass | live | return-page-macos-dark.png / -light.png, served by `wrangler dev`; page contains frockbot://bot.frockbot.com/api/connect/callback/macos and an Open FrockBot button |
| A phone user finishing a connector sign-in gets the branded 'Head back to the FrockBot app' page, not 'safe to close the browser' | ✅ pass | live | return-page-android-dark.png; served HTML contains no <script> and the old copy is absent |
| A browser-tab user is given an Open FrockBot button back to the app origin | ✅ pass | live | return-page-browser-tab-light.png; href="https://bot.frockbot.com/" asserted in the integration test |
| Adversarial: the return pages never reflect the provider's query and the Mac hand-off script runs only under a per-response nonce | ✅ pass | live | curl with ?status=success&connectedAccountId=ca_42 — 'ca_42&#

These are **unverified leads**, not confirmed changes. A read-only scan on 2026-09-29 sent one Sonnet agent to each ~9k-line slice of the repo (56 slices, vendored code excluded), asking for reuse, simplification, dead-code, efficiency and altitude cleanups. Nothing below has had a second-pass check: before acting on one, re-read the code, grep for callers, and confirm it still applies on current `main`. The `apps/cloudflare` export cleanup from the same scan shipped in #990.

**Totals:** 242 findings, about 5,335 lines the agents estimated as removable · 108 dead-code · 68 simplification · 61 reuse · 5 efficiency · impact: 1 high / 45 medium / 196 low · safety: 202 safe / 40 needs-care (touches durable shapes, protocol, auth, billing or cross-module API).

Each line reads: **impact · safety · category** — `file:line` — what to change. Within each area, findings are sorted by impact, then safety.

### app/audit (4)
_The audit area is mostly clean and well documented. The real finding is one efficiency issue in the rebuild receipt, plus a little dead surface (an unused outbox method and an over-exported constant). The store's SQL and the decoders are consistent with the rest of the repo._

- **medium · safe · efficiency** — `app/audit/user.ts:219` — Count unknown outcomes with a `SELECT count(*) ... WHERE outcome = 'unknown'` on the store instead of loading and decoding every row through `all()`.
- **low · safe · dead-code** — `app/audit/bot.ts:437` — Remove `AuditOutboxV1.clearTruncation()`, which nothing in production calls, together with its test. (~8 lines)
- **low · safe · dead-code** — `app/audit/shared.ts:1` — Drop the `export` on `AUDIT_OUTCOMES_V1`, and consider un-exporting `AUDIT_KINDS_V1` if the client does not need it.
- **low · needs-care · simplification** — `app/audit/store.ts:213` — In `insertInto`, the per-entry `SELECT count(*)` existence check followed by `INSERT` can be a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, since the primary key is already (bot_id, run_id, occurrence_id).

### app/billing (8)
_app/billing is mostly tidy, and the real bugs are out of scope. ## What and why

`core/agent-loop/batch.test.ts` failed intermittently under load. Only one test flaked: **`batch ordering > ordering the sends does not serialise the rest of the batch`**.

### Root cause

The test measured the overlap with wall-clock sleeps. Each of the two ordered `send` calls slept 5 ms, and each of the two concurrent `read` calls slept 40 ms. The assertion needed both sends to land before either read ended. The second send's timer is set only after the first send lands and settles. If the process is descheduled for roughly 40 ms after that (a busy 4-CPU machine running several suites is enough), the reads' timers expire first and fire first. The timeline then read `…send:one, read:end:a, read:end:b, send:two`:

```
@@ -4,5 +4,5 @@
    "send:one",
-   "send:two",
    "read:end:a",
    "read:end:b",
+   "send:two",
```

The code under test is correct: the ordered chain and the concurrent group overlap as designed. Only the test depended on timing, so this PR changes the test alone.

### Fix

The calls now wait on each other instead of on the clock:
- A `send` doesn't land until both reads have started.
- A `read` doesn't finish until both sends have landed.

The whole path runs in-memory, so the asserted timeline (unchanged) holds by construction. A batch that serialised any of these calls would wait on itself. The test would then fail on its timeout instead of passing. I checked this by temporarily forcing every call into the ordered chain in `tool-execution.ts`: the test failed, and I reverted the change.

The `orderedEffect` fixture lost its `timeline` parameter, which only this test used.

The other tests that sleep ("ordered effects land in declared order", "a dynamic tool's own orderedEffect decides", "nothing outlives a batch whose concurrent call is fenced") didn't fail in any run. Their assertions hold by construction in the current code: the ordered chain is serial, and the send in the fenced test lands in microtasks, before any timer can fire. The sleeps only affect how well they would catch a regression, so I left them alone.

## Changed
- `core/agent-loop/batch.test.ts`: the test fix. There are no runtime changes.

## Validation

Each count is the number of runs of `bun test core/agent-loop/batch.test.ts` that failed, out of 100 back-to-back runs. The busy loops (`while :; do :; done`) were started for the run and killed by PID afterwards. The machine has 4 CPUs.

| Condition | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | 0 / 100 | 0 / 100 |
| 6 busy loops | 1 / 100 | 0 / 100 |
| 12 busy loops | **12 / 100** | **0 / 100** |

Every failure before the fix was the test named above.

- `bun run validate format typecheck unit`: format, typecheck and unit all passed. Unit ran 6144 tests with 0 failures.
- The `no-mistakes` CLI isn't installed in this environment, so I skipped that gate. The change touches tests only, so it would have run with `--skip test,document`.

## Left for later
Nothing.
