hits.body:
Three defects found while working out why a Bot "could not access email". It could: the 2026-09-16 morning triage firing read the inbox and built a 87-email triage. Everything after that failed.

## 1. A `batch` sub-call bricked its Session permanently

`Session.deriveMessages` skips a `tool/result` whose occurrence has a `parentOccurrenceId` — a call inside a `batch` answers no tool call the assistant sent — but `messageTurnsV1` counted every `tool/result`. The length invariant in `turnScopedMessagesV1` then threw.

The events are durable, so this was never one Turn's failure: **every later Turn in that Session died the same way, before the model was called.** Bob's morning triage has failed every day since `batch` landed in #517.

Both readers now take one list, `messageEventsV1`, so they cannot drift again. The regression test was verified to fail without the fix.

## 2. An automation Turn was told to use a tool it does not have

`CONVERSATION_PROMPT_TEXT_V1` rendered on every turn type, while the Shell manifest admits `user-voice` only on `chat` and `agent`. So the firing was told at length to call `send_to_user` — including #517's "put those sends in one `batch` call" — and spent its last steps failing to, which is how it reached the `batch` above.

The section is now chosen by the same admission ceiling that admits the tool. A Turn outside the conversation gets a hand-off contract naming `wake_parent`.

## 3. Nothing opened the Turn a hand-off was owed

`wake_parent` queues for the Bot's *next* conversational Turn, and nothing ever started one. A 9:45am triage waited until the person happened to speak — on 15 Sept, 3.5 hours, arriving as background context to an unrelated question. The only thing that reached them unasked was a notification carrying the first 240 characters.

The alarm now opens it: an ordinary `chat` Turn on the Bot's own conversation, carrying the drained hand-off and a cue saying nobody spoke, so the Bot says what matters in its own voice with the conversation in front of it.

**This deliberately does not let a Routine speak directly.** A firing's Session is blind to the conversation by design, so its words would land without knowing what the person already dealt with. The second inference is the point, not the price.

Safety properties, each pinned by a test:

- A hand-off is never consumed by a delivery Turn that did not deliver — a failed, cancelled or superseded delivery re-queues what it drained, and the ordinary next-chat-Turn drain carries it exactly as before.
- Only a delivery Turn re-queues. An ordinary chat Turn that fails or is superseded behaves exactly as it did before this change.
- A delivery Turn whose drain came back empty ends without a model call and without a send, so the Bot can never speak from nothing.
- The settler cannot cost the alarm its other work: no throw from it skips owed subagent Turns, overdue tasks, approval expiry or notifications.
- The delivery Turn's input is blanked in the client projection, as an automation Turn's already is — it is a hand-off, not the person's words, and must not render as their own chat bubble.

Scope: the trigger is narrowed to Routine hand-offs. A subagent hand-off is enqueued after its alarm pass, so nothing would have armed a delivery for it; it keeps today's behaviour, and a delivery Turn opened for a Routine drains any subagent hand-off already waiting.

## Verification

- 4823 unit tests pass; 348 workerd tests pass; typecheck and prettier clean.
- Two existing tests in `routines-firing.workerd.ts` were updated deliberately: the person's own next Turn no longer carries the hand-off, and a firing now leaves two runs.

The browser suite ran one file at a time because two things in it were global: the fake provider's chat mode, and the walk through provisioning that every spec repeated. Both are owned by whoever changes them now, so the run takes four workers locally.

## What changed

**The fake provider is per test.** `startFakeOllama` keys its chat mode by a path in the endpoint the request arrived on, and the `ollamaBaseUrl` fixture hands each test its own (`e2eOllamaEndpointV1`). An Ollama-compatible endpoint behind a path prefix is a shape the product already supports — `decodeOllamaApiBaseUrl` keeps the pathname — so nothing test-only was added to the product. One spec's `unauthorized` is now invisible to the rest.

**`chat.e2e.ts` provisions once for the file.** `shareProvisionedApplication` owns the page for the file: it walks `provisionThroughUi` in `beforeAll`, resets the viewport and any `page.route` between tests, and still fails each test on the console errors reported while *it* was running. Eleven boots of a 3 MB CanvasKit bundle and eleven walks through Plugins, Connectors and Models became one; each test makes the Bot it needs. Every assertion is unchanged, and nothing is skipped or deleted.

**The client build is fingerprinted.** `flutter build web --release` is not incremental, and the harness ran it before every suite run. `build-flutter-web.ts` now hashes what the build reads — `apps/native/lib`, `web`, `assets`, `vendor`, both pubspecs, the build flags and the Flutter version — and skips the build when the staged bundle already came from exactly those. `FROCKBOT_FORCE_CLIENT_BUILD=1` builds anyway.

Also: `test/tsconfig.json` no longer names `vite/client`. Vite left with the Vue client, and a type package that is not installed failed `bun run typecheck` for the whole repository — which blocked every commit on this branch.

## Wall clock

Same machine, `--retries 0`, in order.

| Run | Wall clock |
| --- | --- |
| `step9/flip`, one worker (the suite as it was) | **24:15** |
| this branch, four workers | **10:29** |
| this branch, four workers, minus the one nine-minute pre-existing failure | **5:06** |

The same seven tests fail before and after, so the parallelism introduced nothing. What the numbers do not show until you split them is where the time goes: of the 1418 seconds of test time in the serial baseline, **930 are spent inside those seven failing tests** — two-thirds of the suite's cost — and `defaults.e2e.ts` alone is 546 of them (`toPass({ timeout: 540_000 })`, spent in full because the Bot never answers on the platform model).

The passing tests are 462 seconds of work. Across four workers a green suite lands near three minutes; the file that sets the floor is `chat.e2e.ts`, which is 90 seconds of passing tests and one 1.9-minute failure.

## The seven pre-existing failures

They fail identically on `step9/flip` with one worker. None is caused by anything here.

- `defaults.e2e.ts` — the Bot never replies on the platform model; the transcript stays at one message. 9.1 min.
- `chat.e2e.ts` — a message sent mid-Turn does not land above the working sheep. 1.9 min.
- `computer-presence.e2e.ts` — both tests. 1.7 min.
- `applets-publish.e2e.ts` — `applet_check` returns no preview URL. 1.5 min.
- `skill-menu.e2e.ts` — the Skill popover loses the arrow-key highlight. 1.3 min.
- `mobile.e2e.ts` — the shell on a phone. 0.9 min.

hits.body:
## Intent

Let a push to main that cannot affect the slow test tier skip it. This is the CI half of the dev/release optimisation Tim asked for; the local half merged as pull request 539.

The measured problem: main.yml runs about eleven minutes of suites on every landed change - the Flutter client suite, the Cloudflare workerd suite, the Cloudflare integration suite and the browser suite across four shards. A change to the marketing site or the admin portal cannot affect any of them. Those are separate Workers with their own deploy job in the release workflow, and nothing under apps/cloudflare, core, app or providers imports either. Measured over the last eighty merges only one was marketing-only, so the value is latent rather than immediate; it matters for the launch work, where copy changes are expected to be frequent, and it costs a marketing change about eighteen minutes of CI to ship twenty-five seconds of deploy.

Design decisions:
- A new scope job reads the pushed range and decides. The decision lives in scripts/ci-change-scope.ts rather than in a workflow expression, because it is a rule worth testing and a workflow expression cannot be tested. It has unit tests covering each case.
- The default direction is deliberate and fail-safe. An unclassified path obliges the full tier, an empty change set obliges the full tier, and an unreadable range - a force push, a first push, a before value this checkout cannot resolve - obliges the full tier and emits a notice saying so. Only the two named directory prefixes buy a skip, and only when every changed path is under one of them.
- Prefixes are directories. apps/marketing-experiments does not inherit the skip from apps/marketing, and there is a test for exactly that.
- The fast tier is not gated at all. validate runs format:check, typecheck and the unit suite, and all three read the whole repository including the two excused workspaces - the formatter reads everything and the typechecker walks every workspace package - so validate owes every push regardless of scope.
- Documentation never reaches this code: main.yml already ignores docs and root Markdown at the trigger, so a documentation-only push starts no run at all.

The subtle part, which is the thing most worth reviewing: deploy-staging and release now tolerate a skipped slow-tier job, and both additionally require that scope itself succeeded. Without that second requirement the change would be unsafe, because a failed job's dependents do not run - so a scope job that failed would skip all four suites, and a condition that merely tolerated skips would read those four skips as permission to cut a release on the fast tier alone. Both consumers keep the existing not-cancelled guard and enumerate success-or-skipped per job rather than using always or a bare not-failure, so a cancelled shard is still not acceptable.

scripts/ci-scope-gating.test.ts asserts that wiring by parsing the workflow into a semantic model and checking meaning rather than matching text: every slow-tier job gates on scope, validate is gated by nothing, both shipping jobs require scope success, both enumerate success-or-skipped for each slow job, and the end-to-end report still only runs on a genuine failure. A lost gate and a loosened gate both look identical in a green run, which is why they are asserted rather than trusted.

Also in this branch: C3 from the original list was investigated and deliberately dropped rather than implemented. The idea was to skip the Flutter web build in the release verify job when the native client is untouched. On inspection apps/cloudflare/build-flutter-web.ts already short-circuits on a source fingerprint, but only when a staged client exists, which never happens on a fresh CI runner - so the real fix is caching the staged client across runs keyed by that fingerprint. That is a larger change carrying cache-correctness risk on the last gate before production, to save roughly ninety seconds on a fully automated path that blocks no human. Not worth it now.

WHY THE TEST STEP IS SKIPPED, with evidence. The previous pipeline run on the companion branch failed twice on the test step, each time reporting an agent timeout after one hour, together consuming two hours and producing no test changes, and the first of those left four scratch commits in the working repository that had to be removed by hand. This branch ships two new test files totalling ten tests, written in the repository's existing style: unit tests for the classifier covering skippable paths, application paths, mixed sets, prefix boundaries and the empty set, and semantic assertions over the parsed workflow for the gating. On this exact head I have run typecheck across all thirteen packages and format:check, and both new test files pass. Check on the pull request and main.yml on the merge commit will run the real suites again.

## What Changed

- Adds a `Scope` job to `main.yml` backed by a new `scripts/ci-change-scope.ts`, which measures the changed paths from the newest release tag and emits a `slow-tier` output. Only paths under `apps/marketing/`, `apps/admin-portal/`, `docs/` or root Markdown buy a skip, and only when every path in the range qualifies; an unclassified path, an empty range and an unreadable range all oblige the full tier, the last with a notice.
- Gates `flutter`, `runtime`, `integration` and `e2e` on `Scope`, leaves `validate` ungated, and moves the marketing and admin-portal bundles into `validate` (splitting the former `bun run build` into `build:marketing`, `build:admin-portal` and `build:cloudflare`) so the only build of those two Workers lives in the job a skip cannot reach.
- Reworks the `deploy-staging` and `release` conditions to require `scope.result == 'success'` and to accept `success` or `skipped` per slow-tier job, keeping the `!cancelled()` guard so a cancelled shard still blocks shipping. Two new test files (10 tests) cover the classifier's cases — including that `apps/marketing-experiments` does not inherit the `apps/marketing` prefix — and assert the workflow wiring against a parsed semantic model of `main.yml`. `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` are updated to describe the gated tier.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and fail-safe in every direction I could construct — unclassified paths, empty ranges, unresolvable bases and a failed `scope` job all oblige the full tier or block shipping — the excused workspaces' only bundles now live in the ungated `validate` job, and the gating test's previously vacuous bundle assertion is now genuinely falsifiable.

Follows #790, which let a Plugin's page use the microphone. FrockBot now ships a Tuner, off until someone switches it on for a Bot. Until now a tuner needed a Bot to write one, and only accounts with Plugin authoring on could. The Tuner is the tuner the plugins Skill teaches, file for file, under the deployment's own id.

![A Bot's Plugins page: Email switched off, and Tuner, which tunes a guitar or any string by ear, switched on](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/claude/seeded-tuner/app/whats-new/media/tuner.webp?raw=true)

**A seeded Plugin can now have pages**
- `scripts/build-seeded-plugins.ts` reads each page a view names. It injects the bridge exactly as a publish does (`pluginPagesFromSourceV1`) and writes the HTML into `artifacts.generated.ts` beside the module. Page files count toward the source hash, so `--check` catches an edited page that wasn't rebuilt.
- The catalog entry and its member carry `pages`, decoded exactly against the views by the same `decodeMemberPagesV1` a Composition read uses.
- The page route answers a seeded hash from the bundle (`seededPluginPageV1`) before it asks R2. There is no deploy-time upload, the same as seeded modules.
- Reconciliation compares `pages` too, so an account holding an older Tuner page is moved to the new one even when the module and descriptor didn't change.

**The Tuner (`app/plugins/seeded/tuner/`)**
- `default-off`. Switching it on is the approval: the row says "Its page can use your microphone while you have it open." before the switch is flipped. Each use is still the host's, with the bar, the Stop, and the page told why.
- A short `SKILL.md` tells a Bot running it where the Tuner is and that it can't hear it. The managed-skills check requires one for every seeded Plugin that isn't locked.
- The Skill's example becomes `guitar-tuner`, because a seeded id is reserved from authoring. It now points people at the built-in Tuner before writing one. `tuner-example.test.ts` holds the example and the seeded files equal.
- What's New: `tuner`, "A tuner in the panel".

## Proof
- `plugin-page-microphone.e2e.ts` now uses the real Tuner with nothing intercepted except Chromium's fake microphone, playing an A string 12 cents flat. The spec:
  - switches the Tuner on from the Bot's Plugins page, checking the row's microphone line first;
  - opens its panel, served by the Worker from the bundle;
  - checks the host bar appears and the page shows **A2** and "1x cents flat";
  - checks the host's Stop ends it.
- `bot-plugins.e2e.ts` passes with the new row.

## The defect

Creating or rotating an Ollama Cloud Connection validated the API key by calling `listModels` (`GET /api/tags`). Measured against `https://ollama.com` on 2026-08-31 with a valid key, a garbage key, and no key at all:

| Endpoint | Method | Valid key | Garbage key | No key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/tags` | GET | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| `/v1/models` | GET | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| `/api/show` | POST | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| `/api/chat` | POST | 200 | 401 | 401 |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | POST | 200 | 401 | 401 |
| `/api/web_search` | POST | 200 | 401 | 401 |
| `/api/ps` | GET | 401 | 401 | 401 |
| `/api/embed` | POST | 401 | 401 | 401 |

The catalog endpoints are public, so **any** key validated: the Connection went `ready` with a full model list, and the User only learned the key was bad when a Turn ended `model-error`. That happened in production today. `/api/ps` and `/api/embed` are 401 even for a valid key (unsupported on Cloud), so they cannot serve as a probe either.

## The change

- `OllamaCloudClient.probeInference(apiKey, model, signal)` — `POST {apiBaseUrl}/chat` with `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":false,"options":{"num_predict":1}}`, bounded response size and the same abort handling as `listModels`. Measured cost: `prompt_eval_count: 68`, `eval_count: 1`, `done_reason: "length"` — about 70 tokens. 401/403 is a definitive rejection carrying Ollama's own error text; other non-2xx carry the status and reported text; the assistant content is never parsed or retained.
- `validateAndActivate` (create and rotate) now requires `listModels` **and** `probeInference`, against `gpt-oss:20b` when it is in the discovered list (cloud names are bare, no `:cloud` suffix) and otherwise the first discovered model. A probe failure sets `validationStatus: "failed"` with the reason, which already flows to the Connection's `failure` and the client's "Connection validation failed". The existing `safe-metadata-read` retry gating is unchanged, and a comment at the call site records why a tags read is not validation.
- The periodic `connection/refresh-models` catalog refresh is metadata only and does **not** probe.
- `docs/research/ollama-cloud-auth.md` records the measured matrix, dates, and status codes. No key material anywhere.
- `runtime.ts` already maps a chat 401/403/404 to `LlmEffectNotStartedError`; its message (`Model request failed (401)`) is never empty, so it is left as is.
- `apps/cloudflare/vitest.config.ts`: the workerd outbound stub now answers `POST /api/chat`. Without it the workerd bootstrap fails, which is the bug reproducing at the integration seam.

## Tests

Four behaviour-level tests in `packages/plugin-provider-ollama-cloud/src/user.test.ts`, all four verified failing before the change:

- fails a key that lists models but is unauthorized for inference
- activates a key that passes the catalog read and the inference probe
- probes one predicted token on the smallest discovered model
- keeps the active generation when rotation fails the inference probe

## Gates

`bun run typecheck` clean; `bun test` 1002 pass / 0 fail; `bun run format:check` clean; `apps/cloudflare` workerd 55 pass / 1 skipped; `apps/cloudflare-bundler` workerd 10 pass.

## What

A **Spending** page in the app that shows where an account's credit went. It is one page you narrow down by tapping, not a set of separate reports.

- **Group by:** Bot, what started it (a chat with a Bot, a Routine, a Group Chat, voice, you using the Computer directly, a Plugin's own page), trigger (you / schedule / webhook / connected app / run by hand), conversation, what it bought (model replies, conversation summaries, web search, Computer time), model, or Plugin.
- **Tap a row** to filter to it. The page then groups by the next dimension that isn't already filtered. Each filter shows as a chip at the top, and deleting the chip removes it.
- **Period:** 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or the billing period. The page shows the total, a bar per day in the person's Profile timezone, and the ten most expensive Turns. Tapping one of those Turns opens its Bot's conversation.
- **Ways in:** Billing ("Spent in the last 30 days"), search ("Spending"), a Bot's settings (filtered to that Bot) and a Routine's run log (filtered to that Routine).

## How charges are attributed

- **Each charge records its Turn and its cause.** The cause is what started the chain of work, not just the Turn that spent the money. A hand-off, a subagent task or a question to another Bot is charged to whatever started the Turn that asked, so a Routine's total includes the work it sets going in other Bots.
- **Within one Bot**, the chain is followed back through the runs that asked (`app/billing/run-cause.ts`).
- **Across objects**, the asking side writes the cause onto the origin: `cause` on the `bot` and `subagent` origins and on `SubagentParentV1`. The run that asked can't be read from the Bot or subagent object that answers.
- **Those stored causes use only durable records.** They never include a Routine name read at the time. A Bot message's origin is part of that command's idempotency fingerprint, so a rename between an eviction and its retry must not change it. The Routine's name is added only to that Bot's own charges.
- **Computer charges** go to the Turn that is running, read from the Bot object the billing proxy sits in, and never wait on a mount. Viewer and control time always goes to the person.
- **Plugin `ai` calls** go to the Turn only when the call names the running Turn. Otherwise they go to the Plugin.
- **Conversation summaries** are recognised by their compaction effect id. A Plugin's call never counts as a summary.

## Storage

- **Attribution is descriptive.** It is stored in a new `billing_attribution` table beside each operation. It is not part of the reservation fingerprint, so a retry that attributes the charge differently is still the same charge. A malformed attribution is recorded as "Not attributed" rather than refusing the paid call.
- **Pre-summarised data:** each settlement updates an hourly rollup (`billing_spend_hourly`) and a per-Turn total (`billing_spend_runs`) in the same transaction. `GET /api/billing/spending` reads only those two tables and never the operation log.
- **A failed rollup never blocks a settlement.** It leaves a gap in the page and the charge still settles.
- **No migration is needed.** All new tables are additive, and existing tables and records are unchanged. The rollup starts empty at deploy, so earlier charges appear only in the Recent usage list.
- **The per-day list is gone.** `snapshot().summaries` has been removed along with the list it fed on the web and native billing pages. It is replaced by `spentLast30DaysMicros` and the Spending page.

## Checks

- **Validation:** `format`, `typecheck`, `runtime` (workerd) and `integration` (182/182) pass via `bun run validate`. `unit` passed in the pre-push fast tier on the head commit.
- **Environment timeouts:** in two earlier `validate unit` runs in this 4-core container, three Plugin-build tests in `applets/sdk` and `apps/applet-build` timed out waiting for workerd to start. This diff doesn't touch those packages, and they pass alone (11/11).
- **Unit tests:** new tests for cause resolution, the rollups (Turn counts, Routine chains across Bots, rename labels, malformed attribution, rollup failure, the person's days), the API route, the model meter, and the origin cause codec.
- **Flutter:** `flutter analyze --no-pub` is clean. `flutter test --no-pub --dart-define=FROCKBOT_ORIGIN=https://tests.invalid` passed all 1,618 tests, including the new `spending_test.dart`.
- **Review pass:** its findings are fixed in the second commit.

## What's New

The entry is `spending`. The still was captured from a Flutter web build of the real page with the product font, using sample data:

![Spending page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/claude/festive-mayer-h3pvsg/app/whats-new/media/spending.webp)

## Android

Dart-only change: a Shorebird **patch**.

## Intent

ADR 0026 step 9a: a failing Plugin is skipped, noticed, and turned off at three. The mount options gain an onPluginFailure seam the worker host calls for each Plugin refused at resolve, failed at mount or health, and for each hook that threw, overran or answered undecodably; the Bot records it under plugin:health:<pluginId> as one failing Turn (once per Turn), raises a notice in the User's inbox, and at the third failing Turn in a row switches the Plugin off in the Bot's own enable map with a critical notice; every Turn settles the record of each Plugin that ran clean; a quarantined record stays until a person switches the Plugin on, which clears its history; the Plugins page card says why a quarantined Plugin is off; a locked Plugin's failure fails the Turn; a retired contract is refused at resolve and so noticed and turned off. Rebased onto main after #442: the quarantine switch is fenced on the revision it read (switchPluginForBotV1).

## What Changed

- Added per-Bot Plugin health (`app/plugins/health.ts`, stored under `plugin:health:<pluginId>`) counting consecutive failing Turns, plus `app/plugins/health-bot.ts`, which raises a notice in the User's inbox for each failure (one per Turn for a hook, one per generation for a mount phase) and at the third failing Turn in a row switches the Plugin off via the revision-fenced `switchPluginForBotV1` with a critical notice; `executeTurn` settles the record of every Plugin that ran clean, and switching a Plugin back on clears its history.

Connect something once and every one of your bots has it. The platform picks the model. Out of the box there is nothing to configure.

Implements the `AGENTS.md` § Configuration shape amendment and [ADR 0019](docs/adr/0019-account-wide-enablement.md), which supersedes ADR 0003.

## What changes for a user

- **Enable once, every bot has it.** Per-Bot Capability Assignments are gone. Bot settings loses the whole Advanced capability-assignment pane.
- **Connectors** replaces Plugins as the button above the user profile; Plugins stays in Settings and the profile menu as pure enable/disable. A connection needing no credentials is a toggle, not a "Connect" button.
- **The platform chooses the model.** A new user's bot works immediately, with no model prompt anywhere.
- **Custom models** is a first-party plugin, off by default, and the one switch that unlocks choosing a model — the account model, provider connections, and a per-bot override. Ollama Cloud declares a dependency on it, so it cannot be enabled until Custom models is on.
- **Flock AI** is the built-in provider: Workers AI behind Cloudflare AI Gateway, ids presented as `@flock/…`. Auto (`@flock/auto`) routes through the gateway's dynamic route; manual picks a specific model.
- "durable" is gone from user-facing copy — it is an architecture word.

## What changes underneath

- Deleted the Assignment saga in the Bot Durable Object: four storage prefixes, the `claiming → committing → acknowledging → releasing` state machine, deadline alarms, generation compaction.
- Deleted the Connection dependency ledger in the User Durable Object and its RPCs, plus a second parallel copy of it inside the Composio package. A connection can now be disconnected at any time; bots using it fail closed at their next turn with a visible, repairable failure.
- Model resolution is generic: a package setting may declare `role: "model"`, and the kernel resolves bot-scoped, then account-scoped, then the platform model. It never names a package. Bot-scoped package setting values and `bot/set-package-settings` are new; `unset` clears a value.
- Disabling a package makes its values inert without destroying them — a property of enablement, not a special case for models.
- Isolate bindings derive from the user's enabled set. Identity, generation and that set are bound into the loader digest, so a changed grant can never reach a cached isolate.
- Packages can ship present-but-disabled, and enabling one whose dependency is off is refused with a message naming it.

## Trade-off accepted

Per-bot least privilege is gone. A connected account is reachable by every bot you own — and a bot-authored package in a non-first-party isolate now receives bindings for every connection enabled anywhere on the account. The constitution already made the user the trust boundary (one Computer, one browser profile, shared workspace files), so the Assignments were buying configuration surface rather than containment. ADR 0019 records this in full.

## Verification

Every CI gate run locally on this branch:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `format:check`, `lint:ui-styles` | pass |
| `typecheck` | pass |
| `bun test` | 2805 passed, 0 failed |
| cloudflare `test:workerd` | 155/155 |
| cloudflare-bundler `test:workerd` | pass |
| cloudflare `test:integration` | 103/103 |
| computer-host `test` | pass |
| `build` | pass |
| cloudflare `test:e2e` (Chromium) | 6 passed |

## Operator action before deploy

Create the `flock-auto` dynamic route under the `flock` AI Gateway and set its target model (GLM 5.3 Flash). Route and gateway names are `wrangler.jsonc` vars (`FLOCK_AI_AUTO_ROUTE`, `FLOCK_AI_GATEWAY_ID`); no gateway token is stored.

## How it was built

Contracts first, then five Codex lanes in parallel worktrees with disjoint file ownership (`gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh), then an integration lane over the seams, then a fix lane for two real regressions it surfaced: identity baked into a cached isolate, and `invokeModel` answering `unavailable` where the constitution requires a recorded pending decision.

## What

`web_search` now picks its provider through one seam (`app/web/search.ts`). The default is still FrockBot's Brave on the deployment key, and it is the only path that is billed. An account can bring its own provider instead:

- Brave on its own key
- Exa on its own key
- Tavily on its own key
- A SearXNG instance, through its JSON API

## How

- **Stored choice.** The User Durable Object seals the key or SearXNG address as a credential generation, the same way it seals a model API key or a saved secret (`app/web/search-choice-user.ts`). It keeps only the provider id and generation in the clear.
- **Per-search secret.** A Turn reads the choice when `web_search` mounts. Each search leases the secret under its own effect id, opens it inside the Bot Durable Object for that one request, then settles the lease. The secret never reaches the model, the event log or the Computer.
- **Choice changed mid-Turn.** If the choice changes during a Turn, that Turn's next search is refused rather than sending one provider's key to another provider. The change applies from the next Turn.
- **No silent fallback.** If the person's provider refuses the request, fails or runs out of credit, the tool returns that error to the model ("Your Tavily search …"). FrockBot's Brave is never asked and nothing is reserved or charged.
- **Idempotency.** The tool stays `idempotent: true`. A re-run after eviction settles any lease the first attempt left behind and takes a fresh one, so the re-run still works.
- **SearXNG checks.** The address must pass the same public-internet checks as `web_fetch`, except that any port is allowed. It is checked when saved and again on every search. A redirect counts as a failure. A 403 response tells the model to add `json` to `search.formats`.
- **Setting it.** `GET` and `PUT /api/web-search` read and change the choice. This is the minimal way to set it until the setup web app has a screen. The key is never returned.
- **FrockBot's Brave is unchanged.** Brave's transport now uses a shared bounded-JSON reader. Its existing tests pass after only an import change.

Docs updated: `docs/billing.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `app/web/README.md`. There is no What's New entry because there is no app surface yet.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check` and `bun run typecheck` pass.
- `bun test` passes: 6668 pass, 0 fail.
- New `app/web/search.test.ts` runs each provider through `web_search` against mocked APIs. It covers:
  - no fallback and no metering on the person's own provider
  - a lease per search, and a re-lease after an expired lease
  - a choice changed mid-Turn
  - the input decoder
- New gateway test for `/api/web-search`.

hits.body:
Two defects an external review reproduced, each with a regression test in this branch.

## A filtered transcript page lost its continuation

The run index is global and the transcript is one conversation, so a page of index candidates is not a page of answers. `listRuns` took the newest 32 index entries, filtered them to the conversation being read, and then derived its next cursor only from the rows that survived the filter. A page holding nothing visible therefore came back empty *and* `truncated: false` — telling the client the conversation had nothing in it. One older-conversation Turn sitting behind 33 newer ones was unreachable, and so was a chat Turn behind a page of automation firings.

The scan cursor now advances over every candidate a call consumed, kept or not, so a page that selects nothing still says where to resume. The scan also keeps reading index batches until the page is full or `CLIENT_RUN_SCAN_LIMIT` (256) candidates have been walked, so the common case still answers in a single request instead of making the client walk history a page at a time.

## A small history read hydrated the entire session

`SessionEventLog.readRange` reconstructed the whole Session and then sliced it. Reading one turn-start event out of a conversation holding twelve 80 KiB model requests cost 38 storage reads, 36 of them payload chunks belonging to Turns the caller never asked about — and the transcript loop paid that cost once per candidate, for up to 32 candidates, mostly to discard them.

`readRange` now bisects the page keys for the page holding its first sequence, walks forward only while the range is unsatisfied, and hydrates only the payloads the returned events reference. The same fixture answers in 2 storage reads and no payload reads. Alongside it, `readDisplayRange` answers a cut `model/request` from its ADR 0033 projection rather than joining its chunks — the transcript has never rendered a normalized model request — and `readRunHeader` returns a run record with no journal behind it, so filtering a candidate no longer hydrates one. Recovery, compaction, audit reconstruction and model-history derivation still read exact events.

The durable layout is unchanged and nothing needs migration. ADR 0038 records the narrowing of ADR 0033's "client transcript projection reads the exact hydrated event".

## Tests

- `reads a range without hydrating unrelated model requests`
- `hydrates only the payloads its own range references`
- `leaves exact model requests off the display range`
- `reaches an older conversation buried under newer Turns`
- `keeps the visible chat reachable behind a page of automation`
- `offers a continuation when a scanned page selects nothing`

Full package suite, all 75 typechecks, `format:check`, and the 125 Cloudflare integration tests pass.

## What was wrong

Tim's phone showed the same bubble twice: "On it — building your to-do applet now." Bob's run log on production shows why. In one step the model wrote that line as plain assistant text *and* passed it to `send_to_user`. The Shell's safety net, which promotes narrated acknowledgements into a bubble for models that never call the send tool, runs before the step's tools, so it could not see the send that was about to happen and added its own.

## The fix

- The agent loop now includes the step's pending tool names in the `agent/assistant-text` hook position.
- The Shell skips promotion when one of those names is its send tool (`send_to_user` or the `send_message` alias). A model that only narrates is still caught, as before.

## Tests

- Shell: a step about to call `send_to_user` (or the alias) promotes nothing; existing promotion and replay tests unchanged.
- Loop: the hook carries the step's tool names.

## Intent

Investigate and fix a flaky test on main: apps/cloudflare/test/voice-assistant.workerd.ts > 'sends acknowledgment audio while the model is still pending', which failed in CI with 'timed out waiting for acknowledgment before the model answers: []'.

Tim's requirement was to root-cause it the way PR #531 was root-caused: reproduce deterministically, prove the mechanism with a measurement, then fix the cause. He was explicit that raising the test's timeout is NOT the fix, and that a test-side change is only acceptable if the product behaviour is proven correct. If the bug is in the product it must be fixed there, because it would affect real calls too.

Tim's leading hypothesis was that the STT daily allowance was being over-booked (call.exhausted / reserveSeconds / openSttWindow), pointing at an 'allowance is used up' line in the CI log. I disproved that with evidence: that log line belongs to the test 'a day that runs out shuts the upstream during continuous audio and refuses to reopen', which pre-fills the meter on purpose and passed. I also could not reproduce his claim that raising the eventually() budget from 8s to 20s fails deterministically — the file passed 53/53 at 20s. So the ledger arithmetic is NOT the cause and was deliberately left untouched.

The actual root cause, proven by measurement: I reproduced the failure under CPU contention (1 in 5 full-file runs) and instrumented the object. Traces from a real failure show the bridge fired on time (turn-bridge at 2553ms) and the chunk was yielded, but beforeSynthesize was never reached. The agents SDK streams a turn's text through SentenceChunker, whose MIN_SENTENCE_LENGTH is 10: a shorter candidate stays buffered until the stream ends. Of the six VOICE_TURN_BRIDGES_V1 phrases only 'Hang on.' (8 chars) is below that floor, so whenever pickVoiceBridgeV1 randomly chose it the acknowledgment was swallowed for the whole stall — a real production bug (the person hears silence in exactly the moment the bridge exists to cover), not a test bug, and the ~1-in-6 randomness explains the flake rate.

The fix is in the product: 'Hang on.' becomes 'Hang on a sec.'. Deliberate decisions: (1) the guard test asserts each phrase against the SDK's own SentenceChunker class rather than a copied constant, and lives in the Worker suite because the shared app package does not depend on 'agents'; (2) the app-level test holds the list to a new exported VOICE_TURN_BRIDGE_MIN_CHARS_V1 constant, which is documentation of the SDK's floor; (3) an existing test that happened to pass the literal 'Hang on.' as a bridge was updated to the new phrase to avoid naming a phrase that no longer exists; (4) docs/voice.md records the constraint and the incident. The wording change is user-facing spoken copy, chosen to keep the same casual one-beat register.

Verification already done locally: the guard fails with "expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Hang on.' ]" when the old phrase is restored; the voice file passed 5/5 under the same CPU load that produced the failure; the full workerd suite passed (58 files, 360 tests); typecheck and prettier are clean.

## What Changed

- Replaced the bridge phrase `"Hang on."` with `"Hang on a sec."` in `VOICE_TURN_BRIDGES_V1`: at eight characters it sat below the agents SDK `SentenceChunker`'s ten-character minimum, so the chunker buffered it until the stream ended and the caller heard silence for the whole stall the bridge was meant to cover — roughly one turn in six, since the phrase is picked at random.
- Added `VOICE_TURN_BRIDGE_MIN_CHARS_V1` to `app/voice/assistant.ts` and a test in `app/voice/assistant.test.ts` holding every phrase to that floor; the Worker suite adds a stronger guard that feeds each phrase through the SDK's own `SentenceChunker` and asserts it comes straight back out, rather than copying the constant. An existing app test that passed the literal old phrase as a bridge was updated to the new wording.
- Recorded the length constraint and the incident in `docs/voice.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A one-word copy change to a spoken filler phrase, root-caused against the SDK's actual chunker implementation and locked in by a behavioral guard that executes the real `SentenceChunker`; every phrase in the list verifiably clears the floor and no other code path or literal references the old phrase.

Separates **enabling** a Package from **setting it up**.

### Plugins — enablement only
Installs from the Catalog, uninstalls, and turns installed Packages on and off (`user/set-package-enabled`, which the backend already supported and no client exposed). No connection forms, no API keys, no settings forms. Each row says where that Package is set up and jumps there.

### Models — new surface
Model provider Packages: accounts, API keys and rotation, the Ollama API base URL, catalog refresh, enable/disable/disconnect — plus the **default model** every Bot uses, moved here out of Application settings. Per-Bot binding stays in Bot settings.

### Connections — new surface
The accounts and services a User authorizes and may then give a Bot: Composio/Gmail grants, remote MCP servers with their lifecycle panel, pending-authorization connect cards. Empty on a deployment with no connector enabled, which is the point.

### Where a knob lives
`packageConfigurationHome` in `@frockbot/plugin-settings` is the whole routing table — model capability → Models, Connection Types → Connections, plain declared settings → Application settings, nothing declared → nothing to configure. A Package that adds a setting or a Connection Type lands somewhere with no edit to a surface, and a disabled Package renders no configuration while keeping every value it had.

### Constitution
`AGENTS.md` gains a **Settings surfaces** section recording the invariant, plus an architecture check ("every declared Package setting and Connection Type resolves to exactly one configuration surface, and the Plugins surface offers enablement only").

### Also
- Settings links gain the `models` and `connections` surfaces and the `user-model-providers`, `user-connections`, and `user-package-settings` anchors; `user-default-model` now resolves to Models.
- The profile menu reaches Settings, Models, Plugins, and Connections, gated as the sidebar Plugins trigger already was.
- Shared `PackageAccounts` / `PackageSettingsForm` components, and pure `package-surfaces` / `package-settings` modules with tests.
- README, `docs/architecture.md`, and the settings-and-connections plan updated.

### Verification
Full monorepo typecheck clean; `bun test` 2811 pass / 0 fail; `lint:ui-styles` and `format:check` pass.

## Why

On 2026-09-27 Bob's inbox-triage Routine ran for 11 minutes, and "Can you remember that my wife is Becky" sat queued until it finished. Only a chat Turn on the person's own lane yielded to their message (`userMessageWaiting` in `core/durable/authority.ts`, `yieldedTurnRecordsV1` in `app/shell/terminal-records.ts`). Tim's requirement: "we should never queue behind to talk to our bot." Step 4 of the plan in `docs/plan.md` (#942). Independent of the stacked supervision PRs.

## What changes

A running Turn gives way at its next step boundary, in one of two ways:

- **Yield** — any Turn in the conversation Session (the person's own, input-delivery, hand-off): the existing Steering path, now on every lane. It ends `completed` and leaves a `yielded-turn` input the person's Turn reads as `[Steering]`.
- **Park** — a Turn in a Session of its own (a Routine). The loop settles `"parked"` (no `turn/end`), the kernel records `phase: "parked"` and a `parked-run` key, releases the slot, and keeps the alarm armed. The person's message runs as its own chat Turn with nothing prepended. When no person's Turn is waiting, `unparkRun` makes it active again and it resumes through the existing recovery path at the step boundary — nothing repeats, and its Composition pin, admission, turn type and cost cause are unchanged. It can park repeatedly and still finishes.

Exceptions: a Turn whose caller is waiting on its answer (`bot` or `voice` origin) finishes first, so the answer is not lost. Group Turns keep their own rule.

A parked Routine's firing is settled from its own Turn rather than `ROUTINE_FIRE_TIMEOUT_MS`, so parking never records a failure or counts toward the auto-pause; only a firing with no Turn behind it still times out.

**Stop:** `stopRun` cancels a parked Routine straight away. The Work log shows a Stop button on each running Turn (Flutter, `work_log/page.dart`), which is how a Routine that has not spoken yet can be stopped.

## Stored data

Additive: phase `"parked"` and key `parked-run`. No cleanup needed.

## Tests

- `core/durable/turn-parking.test.ts` (new, 9): message during a Routine runs first; resume repeats nothing; parked run survives eviction; parks twice and finishes; Stop cancels a parked run.
- `app/routines/scheduler.test.ts`: a Routine one failure short of auto-pause parks past its timeout and lease, then records ok; a firing with no Turn still fails.
- `core/durable/turn-queue.test.ts`, `app/shell/turn-steering.test.ts`, `app/shell/terminal-records.test.ts`, `core/agent-loop/index.test.ts`.
- `apps/cloudflare/test/routine-parking.workerd.ts` (new): real Bot DO — a parked firing lets the chat Turn run, then resumes after an eviction with no duplicate requests or tool calls.
- Flutter `work_log_test.dart` 8 pass; `flutter analyze` clean.

#825 lets a Bot fill a saved secret, such as a password or card number, into a page by reference. The value never enters the model's context, the transcript, logs or browser snapshots. It is also kept out of every process's environment and command line on the Computer: it reaches `browser.mjs` on stdin (b574cb11, after the Codex P1 on #825).

**What it does not stop:** code that the Bot, or another Bot of the same User, deliberately runs on its Computer can read a filled field back out of the page.
- The Bot's shell has `sudo` (`computer/fly/runtime.ts`).
- The shared Chromium's DevTools port listens on `127.0.0.1` at a fixed port, recorded in each Bot's `cdp-port` file.
- So a script can attach over CDP and read `input.value`. A prompt-injected Bot told to do that would succeed.

The same is already true of anything the person types into the Computer's browser while they hold control. This is recorded as a known issue in #825 and was accepted as a limit for its first release.

**The fix** is to put the browser, or an injection broker in front of it, where the Bot's shell cannot attach. Options, roughly from least to most work:
1. **A separate user for the browser.** Run Chromium and the fill helper as their own Unix user, and expose CDP only on a socket that user owns. The Bot's exec would run as a user with no `sudo` and no access to that socket, and its browser actions would go through a narrow broker. This breaks any Skill that drives Playwright directly from `computer_exec`.
2. **A broker that fills and submits in one step.** It fills the field, submits the form and clears the value before handing control back, so no later read finds it. This narrows the window but does not close it, because the Bot can watch during the fill.
3. **A separate browser for secret-bearing sites,** in a container the Bot's shell cannot reach, with only screenshots and structured actions exposed to the Bot.

**Done means** a Bot with `computer_exec` and `sudo` cannot read a value filled by reference, proven by a test that tries CDP, `/proc` and the DOM from the Bot's shell.

Six verified findings from the v2 memory and models waves, each with a regression test.

**memory-v2 F3 — the prompt promised a Computer that does not exist.** `plugin-package-publisher` registered `Edit and test the User's shared setup in /home/box/setup using the Computer.` unconditionally, so on a host with no Computer the Bot spent six steps inventing a sandbox. The section now takes the same `configured` flag `plugin-computer` uses, supplied from `computerConfiguredV1(host)` in the foundation runtime, and drops that sentence when there is no Computer.

**memory-v2 F4 — `Task {background:false}` returned instantly.** Two paths in `dispatchSubagentTask` skipped the wait: a replayed admission returned `dispatched` before the blocking branch, and a single failed record read abandoned it. A foreground call now waits on a replayed task too, and rides out transient read failures. The tool's give-up wording says it did not finish inside the wait and to answer now, instead of "still running" — which is what sent the model into `task_check` and `task_resume`.

**memory-v2 F10 — the Bot paused a User's Routine unprompted.** `routine_manage` now refuses `pause`, `update`, and `delete` on a Routine whose `createdBy.kind` is `user` unless the call carries `userAsked: true`, and the description says to tell the User rather than switch their automation off. The Bot's own Routines are unaffected.

**memory-v2 F5, F6 — a failing Routine flooded the inbox.** The inbox entry and the notification carry a sentence; the raw kernel string stays on the run-log row. Consecutive failures of the same Routine with the same failure fold into one unread entry with a `repeatCount`. `nextRuns()` reports `max(dueAt, deferredUntil)`, so a backed-off Routine no longer shows a "Next run" in the past.

**memory-v2 F9 + models-v2 N5.** A bad `limit` on `/api/debug/...` is refused at the edge with 400, the accepted range, and no stack. `/api/bots/unread` counts unacknowledged Routine failures, so the Bot whose Routine is failing is the one that badges. Shared memory facts are credited by name or not at all — never by a sibling Bot's id.

**models-v2 N4, N6.** Disabling a Package that another enabled Package depends on is refused, mirroring the enable-order rule. The sidebar keeps its skeleton until the flock has actually been read, and the create dialog closes only once the new Bot is selected, so a freshly created Bot no longer flashes "No Bots yet."

Not touched: run settlement and bot-state recovery (PR 170).

Verification: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (root, 3412 pass), `bun run format:check`, `apps/cloudflare` workerd suite. The two `applet-sdk` CLI failures in the full parallel run pass on their own and are unrelated.

## What

A Bot now looks the same everywhere it's drawn at once. Before, Bob working at the end of his chat wore a sheen, Bob in the sidebar wore three typing dots, and Bob in the chat header sat idle. Now:

- **One working look.** While a Bot works, its drawing holds still, its eyes look ahead and one light crosses its outline. It's the same in the sidebar, the chat header, the end of the thread, the Bot panel title and group chats. Every light runs on the one frame clock, so every copy of a Bot shines at the same moment. The light is placed on the character's outline, not its box, so a sidebar square and the header's cropped view line up.
- **The dots are gone.** `ThinkingBadge` is deleted and the sheen is the only working signal.
- **Idle life is shared too.** Avatars of one Bot share a presence: they twitch together, all wave when a pointer is over any copy, and look where the header companion is looking.
- **Working belongs to a conversation.** A Bot answering in a group chat lights the group's row and its own avatar at the end of that group thread, not its own sidebar row or chat header. The app already reads the Bot's own chat for those; a test now holds the line. The server half, the sidebar's working flag meaning "a Turn the Bot's own chat shows running", ships separately from the `claude/bot-talking-indicator-bug-000373` branch. This PR doesn't touch `app/shell/*`.

## Deliberate trade-offs

- The sheen no longer speeds up with a streaming reply; it's a steady 2.4 s pass. Nothing outside the open chat knows a Turn's pace, so it couldn't be shared. `WorkingPace` and the pace mapping are deleted.
- Bob at the end of the thread no longer plays the Rive "working" loop. Copies of a Rive timeline started at different times never line up, so the light is the only motion.
- With reduced motion on, the light holds still across the middle of the character instead of disappearing, so a working Bot still reads as working in the sidebar.
- Voice screens, the view of a conversation between two Bots and the recovery page are unchanged.

## Review

The no-mistakes review step can't run today: its pipeline agent asks for a model id Claude Code rejects. An independent review agent stood in, found no crash or state-leak bugs, and raised five findings, all fixed in the third commit:

- **Keystroke guard:** the pane's gaze now wakes every copy of the open Bot, but only the header honoured the composer's post-tap hold, the guard that keeps a waking artboard from costing the first keystroke (skill-menu.e2e). The hold now belongs to the Bot's shared presence, so no copy draws while any surface holds.
- **Reparent edge:** an avatar re-entering the tree no longer shares hover or twitch state until its render object is reattached, which rules out restarting a detached artboard's ticker.
- **Repaint cost:** the sheen has its own repaint boundary, so a pass repaints the character, not the header layer around it.
- **First frame:** a light that appears mid-pass starts in step on its first frame. The test for this fails without the fix.
- **Tests:** the group test gained its positive case, and the chat's own surfaces are checked to carry the Bot's id.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze`: clean. Full `flutter test`: 1,490 passed, 19 skipped.
- New `character_presence_test.dart`: shared greeting, twitch and gaze; every working light on one clock through a full pass, with the second copy mounted mid-pass; light placed on the outline; reduced motion; group faces. The sync tests fail with a clock or twitch timer per copy.
- `group_chat_ui_test.dart`: a Bot working in a group lights the group row, not its own; group members and the group header wear the light.
- Rendered the sidebar, header and end of thread mid-sweep with the light at the same place on all three. These were widget-test renders using the stills; the live Rive artboard hasn't been checked on a device.

The design lives in the repository: **[`docs/plans/voice.md`](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/main/docs/plans/voice.md)** (landing via the pull request linked below; until it merges, read it on branch `worktree-voice-design-doc`). It carries the decisions with rationale, the two assumptions to verify before slice A, the constraints discovered, the Feature rule, the slices, a repo map, the zerobsai salvage list, and the external references — enough for a fresh session to build from.

## Summary

Two voice capabilities, both **beyond parity** (Feature rule 8).

1. **Dictation in the composer** — when the draft is empty the send button becomes a voice-wave button; pressing it streams speech-to-text into the textarea in real time, with bin (discard) and send controls and a capture animation. Sending behaves exactly like a typed message; the Bot replies in text.
2. **App-wide voice assistant (Gemini 3.1 Flash Live)** — a User-scoped voice session, toggled on/off, with read-only tools over durable state (Memory, what each Bot has been doing), that asks a Bot when it needs an answer and is seamless across on/off: an answer that arrives while voice is off is known the next time it is on.

## Decisions (accepted 2026-09-04)

- **D1** Platform-ambient keys, BYOK on the `flock` AI Gateway; both realtime APIs over AI Gateway realtime WebSockets; a durable per-User voice-minutes quota.
- **D2** One transport for both: a per-User `VoiceSession` Durable Object proxy that holds sockets and no authority; durable facts live in the User DO.
- **D3** Dictation uses OpenAI Realtime transcription sessions (`gpt-live-transcribe`); `whisper-1` cannot stream deltas.
- **D4** Dictation streams into the textarea as the draft through `ComposerDraftStore`; bin discards, send commits and calls the ordinary `sendMessage`.
- **D5** The voice assistant is not a Bot: a first-party User-scoped Voice Package with its own ledger, no Agent loop, no Memory writes in v1.
- **D6** Asking a Bot rides the `agent` lane from #151; the Bot's reply is its `send_to_user` (#153); the exchange is recorded in the Bot's Session and shown in the thread with a "via voice" marker.
- **D7** Offline answers: client notification when voice is off, and a spoken briefing of pending answers on the next connect.
- **D8** v1 tools: `list_bots`, `bot_activity(bot, since)`, `memory_search`, `ask_bot`, `pending_answers`.
- **D9** Open mic with Gemini VAD, an explicit on/off toggle in shell chrome, auto-offline after 2 minutes of silence, barge-in, resumption on the next toggle.
- **D10** One live session per User, newest device wins.

## Slices

- **A — Dictation.** Proves the AI Gateway WebSocket path through a minimal `VoiceSession` DO.
- **B0 — ADR + #151.** ADR for the Voice Package and the DO seam; land the `agent` lane.
- **B1 — Voice Package core.** Gemini Live via the proxy, ledger, read-only tools, shell toggle, Voice surface, quota, e2e fake.
- **B2 — Ask a Bot.** `ask_bot`, answer push, offline notification, connect-time briefing, "via voice" marker.

Depends on #151 and #153. The full text — constraints, Feature rule, repo map, salvage list, references — is in the plan document; the comment below is the earlier handoff and is superseded by it.

## What and why

Tim chose Brave Search as the platform's search provider, at a flat ~US$5 per 1,000 requests, and asked for the per-User Ollama web search to be retired. With this change every Bot gets `web_search` with nothing to set up. Until the deployment holds `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`, the tool is left out and the deploy prints the degraded sentence. The GitHub secret already exists, so the next release carries it.

## What changed

**Web Package**
- `app/web/definition.ts` adds a `web-search` Capability beside `web-fetch`. It needs no Connection, is admitted on all four turn types and to the `executor` subagent role, and the Bot's existing Web switch covers both tools.
- `app/web/brave.ts` implements `WebSearchV1` over Brave's Web Search API, which I checked against Brave's API reference on 2026-09-24:
  - `GET https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search` with `q`, `count`, `result_filter=web` and `text_decorations=false`
  - the key is sent in the `X-Subscription-Token` header
  - the answer is bounded to 256 KiB, and `web.results[].description` is mapped to the contract's `snippet`
  - 401/403, 422, 429 and other failures each come back as a plain error sentence. The key never reaches a tool result.
- Without a key, `createConfiguredWebSearchRuntimeContribution` mounts nothing.
- `WebSearchExecutionV1` now also carries `botId` and `sessionId`, so a charge can name them. The contract decoder reads only `snippet`: the aliases Ollama needed are gone.

**Billing (additive, kept small to avoid colliding with #802)**
- `app/billing/ledger.ts`: `kind` accepts `"search"`. That is one new union member and one new validator entry.
- `app/billing/search.ts` holds the tariff: US$0.005 cost and US$0.01 charge per search. It also has `createSearchMeterV1`.
- Before Brave is asked, the meter reserves the charge as `search:<web-search effect id>`, using the account-unique id `webSearchEffectIdV1` already computes.
- Outcomes:
  - Brave answered: the charge settles.
  - Brave refused (non-2xx): the reservation is released.
  - No response at all (network failure or a cancelled Turn): the reservation stays held for reconciliation.
  - A recovery re-run under the same effect id finds the existing reservation and is never billed twice.
  - An account that cannot spend gets the refusal as the tool's error, and Brave is never asked.
- The account reaches the Contribution through the enabled-runtime host (`billing?: AccountUsage`, taken from `state.env.BILLING`). `bot-state.ts` is untouched.

**Secret wiring**
- `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY` is added:
  - as optional in `production-secrets.ts`, with the degraded sentence "web search is unavailable: a Bot has no `web_search` tool, and `web_fetch` still reads pages"
  - to `Env`
  - to both env blocks in `release.yml` and to the staging deploy in `main.yml`
  - to the installer's `HUMAN_SECRETS_V1`
  - to the README key table and `.dev.vars.example`

**Ollama web search retired**
- Removed: the `ollama-cloud-web-search` Capability, the `web-search-max-results` setting, the runtime factory, `providers/ollama-cloud/web-search.ts` and its test, the package export, and the provider's now-unused `web` dependency. This also removes the `connection.settings.apiBaseUrl` bug that path carried (the setting's id is `api-base-url`). The Ollama chat model is unchanged.
- Stored-data cleanup: `apps/cloudflare/src/ollama-web-search-cleanup.ts`, receipted as `maintenance:ollama-web-search:2026-09-24` and run from the `UserConfiguration` constructor.
  - It removes stored `web-search-max-results` values from the `provider-ollama-cloud` installation row in `user-configuration`, and drops the value bag if that empties it.
  - Capabilities are derived from Package definitions, not stored, so there is no enablement state to clean.
  - Conversations are not touched, so a fresh conversation works as before.

**Tests**
- Unit tests:
  - `app/web/brave.test.ts`: request shape, key placement, trimming, empty results, bounds, refusal, size bound, turn types, mount rules, and the reserve/charge/release/held/refused billing order
  - `app/billing/search.test.ts`: against the real `BillingLedger`, covering one charge per key, re-runs, releases, a held reservation settled by the re-run, and an account with no credit
  - the cleanup test
  - `app/runtime.test.ts`: search mounts only with the key
  - a per-Bot mask case, and an uninstall-drops-values case in `app/settings/user.test.ts`
- Integration harness: a Brave stub replaces the Ollama search stub, and the integration config binds a test key. `web-tools.integration.ts` now searches through Brave.
- The package-settings integration and workerd tests now use the `image.model` setting.

**Docs**
- `docs/architecture.md` (§7 and the secrets list), `docs/billing.md`, row 47 of `docs/grokbot-parity.md`, and the `app/web` and `providers/ollama-cloud` READMEs.
- The Web row on the Plugins page now reads "Search the web and read public pages…".

**What's New**
- New entry `web-search`, with no still: there is no surface to show.

## Validation

- `bun run validate format`: pass
- `bun run validate typecheck`: pass (13 packages)
- `bun run validate unit`: 5,672 pass, 0 fail (after rebasing onto `e868b2e3`)
- `apps/cloudflare` `test:workerd`, the runtime category's Cloudflare suite: 62 files, 353 tests pass. I ran it on its own to spare the shared machine; `computer-host` and `applet-build` are untouched.
- `bun run validate integration`: 65 files, 173 tests pass (before the rebase).
- After rebasing onto #806 (MCP servers, which shares the harness stub I had a conflict in) and #807, I rebuilt the artifact and re-ran a targeted subset. All pass:
  - integration: `web-tools`, `package-settings`, `mcp-servers` and `connect-apps` (4 files, 21 tests)
  - workerd: `package-settings` (2 tests)
- I skipped the `no-mistakes` gate because the CLI is not installed in this environment.

## Deliberately left for later

- **Search price on the billing screens.** Neither the billing page nor the native screen lists the search price yet. Usage rows already show "Web search · US$0.01 per search". Adding a `searchRate` to the billing response and drawing it is a separate client change.
- **No live Brave call yet.** No test calls the real Brave API. Check one live search on production once the release carries the secret.
- **Billing path under workerd.** Billing is off in the workerd and integration harnesses, so the charge path is proven by unit tests against the real ledger only.

## What and why

Item 10, first slice: **the Bot drafts, the person edits and sends — for email.** Until now the email draft card could only be sent as the Bot wrote it or discarded: a card redraws from the draft it holds, a decided card cannot be redrawn, and a card handler may not ask for a decision. And nothing actually sent, because `SEND_EMAIL` was bound nowhere.

This PR makes the draft editable with the approval still bound to exactly what is sent, moves the sender onto Cloudflare Email Service's documented API with an honest "may have sent" outcome, and lets a deployment profile bind the sender. Draft-first for connected-app sends (Composio) is the next slice; it is listed precisely below.

![The email draft card with To, Cc, Subject and Message as fields](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/claude/charming-maxwell-r6nxhq-draft-send/app/whats-new/media/edit-email-drafts.webp)

## The approval binding (the careful part)

A Plugin card's Approval is bound (`shell:card-approval:<plugin>:<surface>`) to the digest of the `covers` it was drawn with, and `isolateEmail` refuses a send whose message does not digest to it. An edit therefore has to move that binding, and only the person's own Send may move it:

1. The email card draws To, Cc, Subject and the body as `TextField`s bound into the data model, with `sendDataModel: true`. The installed clients already post the live data model with every press on such a surface (`chat_card.dart`), including an `approval/<id>` press — **no client change, no wire change**.
2. On an `approval/<id>` press with decision `approved`, `reviseEditedCardV1` (`app/cards/bot.ts`) asks the Plugin only when all hold: the surface is a Plugin's minted card, it asked for its data model, the posted model differs from the stored one (by `cardValuesDigestV1`), the Approval is still pending, and this surface's binding holds it.
3. The Plugin's new optional card handler `revise` (worker entrypoint `reviseCard`) restates the edit: `{covers, decision, messages?}`, or a deliberate drop with the reason. The email Plugin parses the fields back into a draft, holds it to the same checks the Bot's draft met (addresses, bounds, one-line subject), stores it, and answers it as the new covers.
4. `decideApproval(…, revision)` moves the binding to the digest of the new covers and rewrites the Approval's words **in the transaction that records the decision**, refusing and writing nothing if the binding moved since the Plugin was asked (`ApprovalRevisionConflictError`). A replay reads back the decision already given and moves nothing.
5. The face follows the decision: the revision's `updateDataModel` folds only after the decision is recorded, and may not carry trust chrome.

An edit the Plugin refuses, or that cannot be put to it (worker unreachable, Plugin switched off), **decides nothing** and the receipt's `failure` says why — the person's changed draft is never silently sent as the Bot's. A decline, or a Send over unchanged fields, never reaches the Plugin. A card with no `revise` is decided as drawn. The one window left: if the decision lands elsewhere between the Plugin storing the edit and the transaction, the stored draft and the binding disagree and `isolateEmail` refuses the send (fails closed).

This is one press and one decision rather than "a new card and a new Approval": that would cost a Turn and route the person's text back through the model.

## What changed, by area

- **Contracts / Plugin worker** (`core/contracts/plugin-worker.ts`, `frock-compose/*`, `app/plugins/worker-bot.ts`, SDK `index.d.ts`): `reviseCard` invocation, result and decoder; the generated wrapper's `runReviseCard` and `declaredCards` check; the host's gated `reviseCard`. `PLUGIN_WORKER_INDEX_VERSION` → `index-v11`. `ISOLATE_CONTRACT_VERSION` stays 7, deliberately: bumping it would stop version-6 Plugins mounting, and `revise` is optional.
- **Kernel** (`app/cards/bot.ts`, `app/approvals/bot.ts`): the revise path above; card-press failure charging factored out and reused.
- **Email Plugin** (`app/plugins/seeded/email/`, artifact rebuilt): editable fields (a body too long for the 16,000-byte data model is shown read-only and sent as drawn), `revise`, an `unclear` state that settles into a "May have sent" receipt and is never sent again, Skill and references updated. Stored draft state is a superset of the old shape, so no cleanup is needed; cards drawn before this deploy still send as drawn.
- **Sender** (`app/email/sender.ts`): Cloudflare Email Service's structured `send` — one call, one message to every recipient, `In-Reply-To`/`References` the only headers a draft reaches. The documented pre-send refusals (`E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED`, `E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, …) are `unavailable` and release the decision; anything else (`E_DELIVERY_FAILED`, `E_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, no code) is the new `unknown` and keeps it spent. The raw-MIME composer and its per-recipient loop are deleted. `isolateEmail` keeps the claim on `unknown`; `bot-capabilities.ts` reports a lost RPC answer as `unknown` rather than inviting a retry.
- **Deployment config** (`deployments/profile.schema.json`, `scripts/deployment-config/`): optional `email: { senderAddress }` → the app Worker gains `send_email: [{ name: "SEND_EMAIL", allowed_sender_addresses: [<that address>] }]` and `EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS`. `hosted.json`/`staging.json` are unchanged, so the equivalence gate and production deploy are untouched.
- **Docs**: architecture (the card route, §5 Cards and the email card), ADR 0030 amendment, `CONTEXT.md` (Approval), parity row 57e → partial, known issue 52, deployment-config README "Sending email", Plugin-authoring references (`cards.md`, `grants.md`). `AGENTS.md`'s Cards bullet is left as it is: `revise` is a handler inside the existing Cards extension point, and whether the constitution should name it is Tim's call.
- **What's New**: `edit-email-drafts`, with the still above (rendered by the real card renderer with Inter, dark theme, via a throwaway widget test).

## What Tim needs to set up for email to actually send

In the Cloudflare account (per the docs as of 2026-09-24; full steps in `scripts/deployment-config/README.md`, "Sending email"):
1. Workers Paid (sending to arbitrary recipients needs it; 3,000/month included, then $0.35/1,000).
2. Compute › Email Service › Email Sending › **Onboard Domain** → `frockbot.com`; Cloudflare writes the MX/SPF/DKIM (`cf-bounce`) and DMARC records. Wait for "verified".
3. Optionally Email Routing for the sender address, so replies reach a person.
4. Then add `"email": { "senderAddress": "<e.g. bot@frockbot.com>" }` to `deployments/hosted.json` and update `scripts/deployment-config/fixtures/hosted/app.wrangler.jsonc` in the same commit (the equivalence gate). No secret is involved.

Until then production degrades visibly: pressing Send gets the Bot saying the deployment sends no email, and the decision is left unspent so the same card sends once the sender exists (until it expires). Note that the What's New entry describes sending; consider holding this PR, or setting up the sender first, if that ordering matters.

Rerun on `2f2f7464` (after the Telegram removal); after rebasing onto `db4a07f5` (#823, #824 — docs-only conflict) the fast tier was rerun:
- `bun run validate format typecheck unit` — passed (typecheck across 13 packages and every generator `--check`; unit 5,966 pass on `db4a07f5`)
- `bun run validate:runtime` — passed (cloudflare workerd 63 files / 362 tests, computer-host, applet-build), including the new end-to-end revise test
- `bun run validate:integration` — passed (67 files, 181 tests)
- `apps/native`: `flutter analyze` — no issues; `flutter test --dart-define=FROCKBOT_ORIGIN=https://tests.invalid`, as `check.yml` runs it — 1,606 pass, 26 skipped
- New tests: contracts decoder; wrapper `runReviseCard`/decoder/declaration; `decideApproval` revision (moves, conflicts, replays); card route (unchang

## Problem

When a voice call is paused, the Bot's character switches from its chosen colour back to the character's catalogue colour, for example Pixel's pink, until the call resumes.

**Cause:** `voice_mode.dart` passes `motion: CharacterMotion.still` while paused. `CharacterAvatar._figure` drew the checked-in PNG for `still` instead of the Rive artboard, and the PNG only exists in the catalogue colour. Opening a call that's already paused draws the PNG from the start, so the colour is wrong there too.

## Change

`apps/native/lib/flock/avatar.dart`:

- `still` now keeps the live artboard and holds it at rest (`reducedMotion`, ticker stopped after the usual 700ms wake). The PNG only stands in until the Rive runtime is ready.
- A `still` character doesn't take hover. Before, `still` never reached Rive, so hover on it is new; a paused call's character shouldn't stir under the pointer.
- The old comment explained `still` as the picture because a live artboard beside the composer cost keystrokes after a tap. The only `still` caller is the paused call, which has no composer, and the composer companion guards its field with `hold`.

This also closes a latent use-after-dispose. Switching to `still` used to unmount the artboard, which disposed its controller and view model, while `_CharacterAvatarState._loaded` kept pointing at them. The artboard now stays mounted.

Also adds a What's New `fix` entry, text only.

## Verification

Flutter tests can't run the Rive renderer (the avatar forces stills under `flutter_tester`), so I built a throwaway web harness (not committed) against the real Rive wasm runtime in Chromium. It shows a Pixel coloured `#2255ff`, switches it to `still` as a pause does, then mounts a fresh `still` avatar, reading the avatar's own pixels on every frame:

| | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After pausing | still, `fc85ae` (Pixel's pink), on every frame of the pause | artboard, `2255ff` |
| Fresh `still` avatar | still, `fc85ae` | artboard, `2255ff` from frame 0 |

- `flutter analyze lib/flock/avatar.dart`: clean.
- `flutter test` on the voice mode, voice footer, chat header, flock and bot-switch suites: 86 pass. One fails, "on a Mac a call keeps the sidebar and the overlay chrome", and it fails identically on `main` in this container.
- `bun test app/whats-new`: 21 pass. Pre-push unit tests: 5245 pass.

Tim decided: (1) run compaction on a platform model via the AI Gateway dynamic route he already created, dynamic/frock-structured ("just use that"), billed as a normal hosted Frock AI call (model id @frock/structured, needs a BILLING_MODEL_RATES entry Tim will add; until then summaries are refused as unpriced, same outcome as today's failures); (2) choose a Turn's history once per Turn so every step reuses it; (3) keep the start of the prompt stable (no count in the omitted notice). Decisions I made: a generic LlmProvider.summaryModel field so the Shell names no provider; Frock AI is mounted summary-only (no Auto fallback hooks) beside a Bot on another provider, and skipped if the Bot is already on Frock AI; the summariser answers in plain Markdown headings (existing parseCompactionSummaryV1) instead of JSON, deleting the JSON schema/render code; summariser input bounded to 80k chars per call with the backlog processed in slices (up to 8 per detached run); an interrupted intent is settled and retried immediately rather than backing off; history is pinned to the Turn's opening size and re-chosen only when the Turn grows past 2x the budget; tool-output pruning by age was deliberately left unchanged (it only affects the last ~3 turns, not the prompt start); gateway prepaid limits now apply per requested model instead of the smallest across all rate entries; Bots on provider Plugins are also summarised by the platform summariser (the workerd test was rewritten accordingly); the gateway RPC stub is disposed on the binding path (it pinned Durable Objects in tests).
