Builds §5 of the enthusiast setup plan: the setup chooser on frockbot.com, and the review screen that applies the carried-over choices after sign-up.

## frockbot.com
- **`/setup`**: starting points (Just works, Bring my keys, All mine, Self-hosted) and five questions: where FrockBot runs, the computer, AI per job, web search and connected apps. Each question's two choices are **Ready to wear** (FrockBot's) and **Dress it up** (yours). AI has searchable, grouped provider and model pickers covering every catalog provider. The rules are ported from the Setup Chooser canvas: self-hosting keeps AI on Frock AI; connected apps through FrockBot need BYO, self-hosted too; writing and the other chat jobs follow chat.
- **Result panel**: summary, who-runs-what diagram, suggested plan (Standard US$20 / BYO US$5 / none self-hosted), costs split into *From credit*, *Your accounts* and *Free*, what you gain, and steps. A coming-soon part is never a step: it is listed under **Not ready yet** with what covers it until then. A test walks every single-choice change from every preset to check this.
- **Honest statuses** live in `content/setup-options.json`, audited against main. Available today: frockbot.com, FrockBot's computer, Frock AI, chat on any catalog provider or Ollama Cloud, and FrockBot's search and apps. Everything else is coming soon. Model lists come from `providers/catalog`. `render-setup.ts --check` runs in the build, like capabilities. Later feature PRs flip their option to `available` there.
- **No JavaScript**: the default setup is rendered into the HTML. Runs under the existing CSP (no inline script or style).
- **Homepage**: a teaser section whose three cards open `/setup/#preset=…`. The pricing copy now says credit covers FrockBot's models and computer on Standard and Plus, and top-ups do on BYO.

## Carry-over
- **One shared, versioned format**: `core/setup-choices` (`v: 1`, no imports). The site serves an esbuild copy of it. Unknown or retired values fall back to FrockBot's version of that part, with a note.
- **Saved on the device** under `frockbot-setup-v1`: choices only, storage access guarded. Shows "Welcome back. Saved on this device · Start over".
- **Start with this setup** opens `bot.frockbot.com/setup/apply#setup=<base64url>`. The choices travel in the fragment, never the query string.

## In the app: `/setup/apply`
- The page moves the fragment into this origin's storage **before** any sign-in or checkout redirect, then clears it from the address bar.
- Signed out: Continue with Google, returning to `/setup/apply`.
- Signed in: **"Set up FrockBot the way you chose"** lists each part as Ready, Needs your key (inline field), Needs sign-in, or Coming soon with Frock AI or FrockBot's version for now. The plan row checks out on the suggested plan.
- Billing sends a successful checkout back while a setup is waiting.
- **Apply this setup** or **Start on Frock AI instead**. Nothing is applied silently. Apply uses the same Settings, Connections and Billing commands the app uses.
- Why `/setup/apply` and not `/setup`: the setup web app (`claude/eager-franklin-sy7ssj`, not yet opened as a PR) claims `/setup` and `/setup/{plan,computer,ai,search,apps,accounts}` in the gateway. A second `/setup` handler would be silently shadowed, whichever merged second. That app can adopt this screen by adding an `apply` page and deleting `app/setup/page.ts`.
- **Your Sprites** is named **Your Fly.io account** (id `fly`), because only the host may name Fly's Sprites (`check-computer-host-imports`).
- A What's New entry, `setup-review`, has a still of the review screen.

## Not in this PR
- **frockbot.com/deploy** (timoconnellaus/frockbot#964) should read `frockbot-setup-v1` with `readSavedSetupV1` / `normalizeSetupChoicesV1` from `@frockbot/core/setup-choices` and pass it to the install's first run. That belongs to that PR.

## Hold
Labelled `hold` until timoconnellaus/frockbot#962 (the BYO plan) merges. This PR suggests BYO and starts BYO checkout, and main's Stripe plan list doesn't have it yet. The chooser's price test in `stripe.test.ts` checks every plan the payments Package lists, so it covers BYO once #962 lands.

## Validation
- `bun run format:check`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (6,740 pass, 0 fail).
- `bun run build:marketing` passes. `validate:build` passes, including the white-label fixture and the Worker bundle.
- `validate:runtime`: all suites passed, including the app Worker's workerd suite (408/408). It recorded no success only because a path-only commit landed mid-run.
- Checked in Chromium on the local marketing Worker: desktop and 390px phone, no horizontal scroll, no CSP errors, reload restores the saved setup.
- Checked in Chromium against a mock of the app's APIs, using the real routes: fragment capture → sign-in → connect key → Apply → pending setup cleared.
- The `no-mistakes` CLI isn't installed in this environment, so that gate did not run.

**Draft on purpose: a constitution amendment needs human acceptance, and PRs auto-merge when green.** Mark ready to accept.

Proposes ADR 0021 and the matching AGENTS.md Configuration-shape amendment:

- One Models surface for every User: provider (FrockBot default) → connection (when >1) → model (Auto default). Choosing another provider is the opt-in and installs/enables that provider's Package and dependency closure; connecting happens on the same surface and leaves Connectors. Broken choices fail visibly with a one-click return to FrockBot/Auto; never a silent fallback. Bot override stays a Bot setting defaulting to inherit. Hand-typed models allowed. Subagent models stay separate. Custom models Package retired via migration.
- Platform-owned Packages (application root, no User/Bot control, owner of the ambient model Connection) are installed for everyone, cannot be disabled or uninstalled, are repaired on every read, and are not offered in Plugins — derived from manifest facts, never ids. This names what v0.2.5 (PR #147) already shipped.

Context: the 2026-09-03 'Model unavailable' / 'Custom models won't enable' incident (PRs #143, #147).

## Intent

Simplify provider, Package catalog, and computer identity contracts across the codebase: remove provider-specific connection lifecycle duplication, centralize catalog lookup and policy, preserve existing behavior, and publish a fully validated PR.

## What Changed

- Extracted the Ollama Cloud durable-record connection ceremony into a provider-neutral lifecycle at `providers/model-connections/user.ts`; `providers/ollama-cloud/user.ts` (2604 → 52 lines) and `providers/catalog/user.ts` now just configure it — client, storage prefix/labels, `api-base-url` decoder, probe model, settings validation — so the `OllamaUserBackendHost` / `OllamaCloudUserApplicationHostV1` types become `ModelConnectionUserBackendHostV1` / `ModelConnectionsUserApplicationHostV1` and the `ollamaCloud` host becomes `modelConnections`.
- Added `providers/catalog/registry.ts` as the single policy table for catalog providers (connection settings, runtime adapter, OAuth request auth, model source, settings validation, runtime environment names); `definition.ts`, `models.ts`, `runtime.ts` and the OAuth modules derive from it instead of per-provider `id === …` branches, and `catalogProviderV1` / `validateCatalogSettingsV1` / `catalogRuntimeEnvironmentV1` replace the loose provider-id arguments.
- Added `indexPackageCatalogV1` in `core/contracts` and switched `app/packages.ts` (`FOUNDATION_PACKAGES_V1`/`foundationPackageV1` → `FOUNDATION_PACKAGE_CATALOG_V1`), `core/configuration`, `app/settings/user.ts` and `app/user.ts` onto that one index, dropping the parallel id/version maps and failing fast on duplicate Package ids; `computerBotPathKeyV1` and `computerSpriteNameV1` similarly became the single validated implementations used by `computer/fly` and the Computer host container.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: The refactor is faithful almost everywhere (Ollama strings, durable keys, and catalog resolution semantics are preserved), but it adds an import to the Computer host container whose module is absent from the built image, so the container fails at startup in the deployed artifact while CI stays green.

## Summary

- split browser CI into four balanced core lanes and one isolated publication lane
- skip the Applet build container for the 63 core tests that do not use it
- replace repeated Plugins/Models/create-sheet setup with authenticated product commands, while retaining one full UI journey and checking both paths reach equivalent durable state
- remove CI retries, cap fail-fast behavior at two failures, add a 20-minute Playwright global timeout, and tighten the Marketplace test's failure budget
- harvest fresh per-spec timings and rebalance the core shards from the qualified run

## Why

The latest `main` browser run took more than 21 minutes. Publication journeys were sharing ordinary shards despite being the only tests that need the real build container, repeated UI provisioning dominated many unrelated specs, and deterministic failures could consume a four-minute timeout plus a retry.

Coverage remains intact: 63 core tests plus 2 publication tests, with no overlap. The publication lane still exercises the real build path. First-run and Models UI coverage remains, and `provisioning.e2e.ts` now owns the complete setup journey plus an API/UI equivalence assertion.

## Results

Final qualified run: https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/actions/runs/35429811071

- browser wall time: **8:28**, down from **21+ minutes**
- final core lanes: **8:28 / 8:19 / 8:09 / 8:05**
- core lane spread: **23 seconds**, down from **4:27** before the final rebalance

- all migrated core journeys pass locally, including mobile, unread state, routines, skills, chat continuity, and Applet surfaces

Sets the repo up for one owner of everything after a PR opens. The trigger was an audit of the last 12 days of CI ([FrockBot Delivery Audit](https://claude.ai/artifact/SNVjAx447doy3pE9Pq1AQs), private to Tim):

- `main` was red 29% of the time, and 37% of PRs merged onto a red `main`.
- Since 19 Sep, 3 in 4 red runs were real regressions that `Check` can't see: 13 PRs out of ~170, about 1 in 13. Flakes were 23%.
- Merge → production was 45 min median and 4.2 h at p90. When nothing is red it's ~20 min.

Decisions (Tim, 24 Sep):
- Only the babysitter merges.
- A red `main` stops the line, with a revert if nothing fixes it.
- A `main-health` status enforces this in GitHub.
- Playwright stays at `retries: 0`.
- What's New moves to one file per entry.

## What's in it

- **`scripts/babysit.ts`**: a read-only snapshot of the pipeline:
  - `main`'s health, and when it's red, the failed jobs, when the streak began, and every PR that landed since the last green run, found by walking first parents so both squash and merge commits count
  - the newest release's deploy, via `ci-watch.ts release`
  - a next action for each open PR: `merge`, `fix`, `rebase`, `wait`, `held` or `skip`

  A timed-out run (reported as `cancelled`) and a failed run being rerun both count as red. Fork PRs are skipped for Tim to review.
- **`.claude/skills/babysit/SKILL.md`**: what `/loop /babysit` does on each tick:
  - `main` first: attribute the break, rerun a flake once and file it under `flaky`, then fix, or revert after 30 min with the culprit identified.
  - Production next.
  - Then squash-merge ready PRs, rebase or fix PRs whose author has been idle 30 min, and report.
- **`main-health.yml` + `scripts/main-health.ts`**: a `main-health` commit status on every open PR. It's green while `main` is green, red while it's red, and always green on a `fix-main` PR or a revert from this repo. It uses `pull_request_target` so it can write statuses, and it only ever runs the base branch's script, never PR code. `ci-watch pr` reads a red `main-health` as held, not failed.
- **What's New**: each entry is now `app/whats-new/entries/<id>.ts`, with `added` backfilled from each entry's first commit.
  - `entries.ts` sorts the entries, and a generated index lists them alphabetically, so feature PRs stop colliding in three files.
  - `PREVIEW.md` is deleted; the PR comment already shows the same copy and stills.
  - `published.ts` reads both layouts. Dates came out identical across all 261 tags.
  - The feed wire shape is unchanged. The only order change is two entries that were added in the same commit, which now tie-break by id.
- **Docs**: the AGENTS.md PR, merge and watch bullets are now one rule: hand off at the PR and never merge. README → Releases, the GitHub configuration section, the architecture workflow list and `main.yml`'s header now describe how things actually work.

## Tim: after merging, in this order

1. Wait for the first `Main` run to finish, so `main-health` sets a status on every open PR.
2. Add `main-health` to the `main` ruleset's required status checks. If you add it before the workflow is on `main`, every PR blocks.
3. Start the babysitter in a dedicated desktop session: `/loop /babysit`. It creates the `hold`, `fix-main` and `flaky` labels on first use.
4. Separately: the no-mistakes review agent is still broken (`unrecognized_model "deepseek-flash[1m]"` in the claude-ds config), and has failed every gate run since 23 Sep. Only you can fix it.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run validate format typecheck unit`: 5508 unit tests pass. Run outside the sandbox, which blocks socket binds.
- [x] 81 tests across `babysit`, `main-health`, `ci-watch` and `app/whats-new`, covering the timeout, rerun, fork and revert-title cases. There's a git-backed test for the `--full-tree` fix that fails without it.
- [x] `bun scripts/babysit.ts` checked read-only against live GitHub.
- [x] What's New: `published.ts` output diffed old vs new over the real tags (identical); feed JSON diffed (the same entries); the index bundles for the Worker without `import.meta.url`.
- [x] Independent review in place of the broken gate: 4 blockers and 3 smaller findings, all fixed in the last commit.
- [ ] `main-health.yml` has not run yet. `pull_request_target` workflows only run from `main`, so the first real run is after merge. I didn't run `main-health.ts` by hand, because it writes statuses onto open PRs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes who may merge and adds a `pull_request_target` status workflow that gates all PRs; operational misconfiguration (e.g. requiring `main-health` before the workflow runs) could block merges until fixed.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a **babysitter** as the sole merger after PR checks pass: new `scripts/babysit.ts` snapshots `main`, production, and every open PR (`merge` / `fix` / `rebase` / `wait` / `held` / `skip`), and `.claude/skills/babysit/SKILL.md` documents the `/loop /babysit` tick loop (stop-the-line on red `main`, flake handling, squash merges with `--match-head-commit`).
> 
> **`main-health`** enforces that policy in GitHub: `main-health.yml` plus `scripts/main-health.ts` set a required commit status on PR heads (green when `main` is green; red otherwise except `fix-main` / in-repo reverts). `ci-watch` and docs (`AGENTS.md`, `README`, architecture) now say authors hand off at green PR checks and never merge.
> 
> **What's New** moves from one `entries.ts` list to **one file per entry** (`entries/<id>.ts`) with an `added` timestamp for feed order, an alphabetically generated `entries.generated.ts`, and `published.ts` that reads both old and new tag layouts; `PREVIEW.md` is removed in favor of the existing PR comment preview.

## What and why

A person can now delete their account, or just their Computer, from **You → Delete**. Tim's decision for known issue 27: deletion is immediate once the person confirms by retyping the email they sign in with. There's no grace period. "Delete my Computer" is its own action, and nothing reaps a Computer on a schedule.

![The Delete page: a card to delete the Computer, and a card to delete the account with the sign-in address typed to confirm.](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/claude/charming-maxwell-r6nxhq-account-deletion/app/whats-new/media/delete-account.webp?raw=true)

## Design

**The saga** (`app/account/deletion.ts`, steps in `apps/cloudflare/src/account-deletion.ts`). This is a durable record, `account:deletion:v1`, on the User Durable Object. It names the current step and a cursor, and the User DO's alarm drives it forward. Every step only deletes and can safely run again: when a provider says something is already gone, that counts as deleted. A failure is recorded on the step it happened in and retried with backoff up to 5 minutes, indefinitely. The next alarm is armed before each pass, and passes never overlap. The steps run in this order:

1. **access**: `DeploymentPolicy.closeAccountForDeletion` writes `ended`. This also runs inline before the 202, so the person's other devices are refused on their next request.
2. **voice**: `VoiceAssistant.eraseAccount` closes calls and the model session, then deletes the object's storage and alarm.
3. **groups**: each Group Chat is deleted through its own `group/delete` command. The groups are named in the cursor first, so a group-object destroy that failed is carried again on replay.
4. **bots**: every Bot goes through the existing Bot delete saga, which already purges vectors, R2 roots and the Bot object.
5. **computer**: `ComputerHostV1.teardown`.
6. **connected-apps**: Composio trigger instances, then connected accounts (revoked upstream). These are listed by `user_id` at the provider rather than from our records, so a sign-in that never finished is caught too. One verify pass follows.
7. **payments**: the Stripe customer the ledger recorded, plus any a `frockbot_user_id` metadata search finds, is `DELETE`d. That ends the subscription at once. A recorded customer with Stripe unconfigured is refused and retried, never skipped.
8. **files**: the User's R2 roots (Skills, Memory, Plugin-declared) plus a sweep of this User's Bot roots, one page per pass.
9. **memory-vectors**: User and Group Chat vector ids, from the Memory vector ledger and from pending index intents, are deleted from Vectorize by id, one page per pass.
10. **identity**: a new `AuthPackageV1.deleteStoredIdentity` deletes the D1 `session`, `account` and `user` rows in one batch.
11. **admission**: `DeploymentPolicy.forgetAccount` deletes the access record and any invitation under the address. This runs only after the identity is gone, so no session is left that admission could let back in.
12. **erase**: `deleteAll()`, then the permanent tombstone `account:deleted:v1`.

**The fence.** Once the record exists, the User DO refuses anything that would start new work: `prepareAccount` (so no Turn starts, whether or not billing is on), `reserveUsage`, Bot create/lifecycle, group, Connection and trigger commands, checkout/portal, and push. Every native session reads back as signed out. While a deletion is running, the alarm does nothing else, so no Memory drain upserts a vector behind the purge. After the tombstone, every identity check throws `AccountDeletedError`, which the entry boundary and the Bot list map to 410. The constructor then runs no cleanup, so the object stays as just the tombstone across restarts.

**External effects and idempotency.** None of these steps creates anything, so a retry can only delete again. Stripe takes no idempotency key on `DELETE`, which is idempotent by definition. The one effect that could double-fire is "Delete my Computer" retried after a Bot has already made a fresh Computer. That is receipted per command id (`computer:teardown:<commandId>`). The Stripe webhook now answers `received` for a deleted customer and for an already-deleted account, so Stripe doesn't retry for days.

**Computer teardown.** The host protocol gets a twelfth operation, `teardown` (`/v1/computer/teardown`), carrying only the envelope. The container deletes the Computer by the name it derives from the User, treats 404 as already gone, and drops its cached records. An open still in flight when a teardown lands no longer caches the machine it opened. `FlyHostTransportV1.teardown` and `FlyComputerHostV1.teardown` implement it, and the wire double and the workerd fake do too. The contract suite now runs the idempotent-teardown case against Fly as well as the in-memory host.

**A bug this depended on.** `BotState.executeLifecycle` and `readLifecycle` materialized the Bot before calling Flock, and materializing a tombstoned Bot throws. So a `bot/delete` whose settlement was lost could never learn it had happened, and its saga retried every second forever. Both lifecycle doors now skip materializing, since Flock already checks the tombstone first. There's a workerd test for the replay.

**A deleted Bot stays a tombstone.** When a deleted Bot's object restarted, `BotState`'s constructor ran its receipted cleanups and wrote their `maintenance:*` receipts back next to the tombstone. Main's newer cleanups made this visible after the rebase: 13 receipts on a Bot the account deletion had just removed. A new `isBotTombstoneV1` (`app/flock/bot.ts`) reads the lifecycle record, and `BotState`'s constructor now skips every cleanup for a tombstoned Bot, as the User DO already does after its own tombstone. There's a unit test for the helper, and the workerd suites assert exact keys.

**Client.** `GET/POST /api/account/delete` and `POST /api/computer/delete` are new routes. No existing wire shape changes, so there's no protocol bump and installed apps are unaffected. The Flutter `DeletionPage` has one confirmation dialog for the Computer and a typed-address field for the account, keeps one command id per press across retries, and signs the device out once the deletion is under way. The change is Dart-only, so the Android side can go out as a Shorebird patch. There's also a What's New entry with a 16:9 still.

**Stored shapes.** All additive: `account:deletion:v1`, `account:deleted:v1` and `computer:teardown:<commandId>` on the User DO, plus `updatedBy: "account-deletion"` on an access record, which the existing decoder already accepts. No existing shape changes, so no cleanup is needed, and production Bots are untouched unless their owner deletes their account.

**Docs.** Known issue 27 is resolved, with what's still open. `architecture.md` (User DO, DeploymentPolicy, VoiceAssistant, Computer interface and protocol, Auth, client pages), `beta-access.md`, `billing.md`, the root README and the computer-host README are updated.

## Validation

This branch was rebased onto `main` after #802 (billing rate table), #806 (MCP) and #807 (reply streaming). The `DeploymentPolicy` conflict kept both sides: the rate-table RPCs and storage, and the two deletion RPCs. Account deletion doesn't touch the rate table, since it's deployment-wide. After `bun install`, each category ran one at a time on the pushed head (`6348669e`):

- `bun run validate format`: pass
- `bun run validate typecheck`: all 13 packages pass, plus the import gates, including the Computer vocabulary and auth-package gates
- `bun run validate unit`: 5747 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run validate runtime`: cloudflare workerd 63 files / 361 tests, computer-host 6, applet-build 5, all pass
- `bun run validate integration`: 67 files / 181 tests pass
- `apps/native`, run before the rebases and left to the PR's `Flutter` check since: `flutter analyze` finds no issues. `flutter test --dart-define=FROCKBOT_ORIGIN=https://tests.invalid`: 1542 pass, 24 skipped.
- `no-mistakes` is not i

## What and why

A message can now carry files. The person attaches up to five files of up to 20 MB each: pictures (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, and text, Markdown, JSON or code. Pictures reach a model that can see them. A document reaches the model as its text. Each file stays with the Bot. This is the first slice of parity items 1 and 2 (file upload and image understanding).

![What's New still: a message carrying a chart and a PDF, Fox's reply, and a spreadsheet in the composer tray](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/main/app/whats-new/media/attachments.webp?raw=true)

**How it works.** The app uploads a file as soon as it is attached, before Send. `POST /api/bots/:bot/uploads` admits the file durably: it checks the type from the bytes, extracts a document's text once, counts the file against the account's 5 GB, writes the bytes and the text to R2 under the Bot's own prefix, and records `upload:<sha256>` in the Bot Durable Object. Only then does it answer with the hash. Every step is idempotent by that hash. The Turn command names uploads by hash only, and the Bot resolves each one against its own records before admission. A message can therefore only carry a file its Bot holds. Through the run record, `input/queued`, `user/message`, the working context and the journaled `model/request`, an attachment is a reference with no bytes. `LlmRegistry` fills in the bytes and text after the request is journaled, through a new `ModelAttachmentResolverV1`. A re-dispatch after an eviction reads the same content-addressed objects again, and nothing resolved is ever written to the log.

## What changed

- **Kernel (`core/`)**: `MessageAttachmentV1` and its decoders (`core/contracts/message-attachments.ts`). User `LlmMessage.attachments`. `userMessagePartsV1`, the one way every provider draws a user message. `ModelAttachmentResolverV1` in `LlmRegistry`: a resolver failure is a call that never started. The agent loop takes a files-only message. The run record and admission store attachments. The fingerprint includes the upload ids, and a retry must carry the same ones.
- **App (`app/uploads/`)**: classification, extraction (Workers AI `toMarkdown` with image description off, plus a small Office XML reader for PowerPoint and as Word's fallback), the Bot-side upload records, the account quota ledger, and the per-Turn resolver. The resolver sends the files on the newest 3 attachment-bearing messages: at most 8 pictures of at most 8 MB, and 30,000 characters per document within 90,000 per request. Anything older is named in one line. `generate_image` now returns its picture as a tool attachment, so the Bot sees what it made.
- **Worker (`apps/cloudflare`)**: the upload route (`uploads.ts`) and `GET` for thumbnails (`private, immutable`; a non-image is served as a download under `sandbox`). Turn RPC carries refs only. `UploadNotFoundError` returns a 422. Deleting a Bot deletes its R2 objects and gives its quota back. Deleting the account (#808) deletes every Bot that way, and its file sweep now also covers the whole `uploads/<userId>/` prefix for a Bot lost before its teardown. The User object counts no new upload once deletion begins. Both ids in an upload key are URL-encoded, so one account's prefix never begins another's.
- **Providers**: OpenAI-compatible, Frock AI, the catalog runtime and Bedrock draw image parts or text notes. On the gateway route, Frock AI Auto accepts images (`vision: true`). A schema request, and Auto on the binding path, are told in words that a picture was attached.
- **Billing** (`apps/cloudflare/src/frock-ai.ts`, image rule only): the blanket `image_url` refusal is gone. When checking a request against its model's prepaid bound, each image counts as a fixed 6,000-token allowance in place of its base64. The charge still settles from the usage the model reports. Rebased onto #802: the allowance applies inside the rate table's per-model bounds, and settlement still prices the served model.
- **Protocol**: `UploadRef`, `UploadReceipt` and `Attachment`. A TurnCommand may carry `attachments` with empty `text`. A Run carries `attachments`. `protocolMax` is now 3 and `protocolMin` stays 2, so this is a grace period. The server leaves `attachments` off every Run sent to a protocol 2 client: pages, lookups, Stop receipts and state frames. The state socket sends its protocol as `?protocol=`. Installed 1.4 apps keep decoding every Run exactly. The socket also asks for #807's reply drafts (`drafts=1`); a draft carries no Run, so every socket that asked gets it whatever its protocol, and a reply being written is drawn under a message that carries files.
- **Flutter**: an attach button, drag-and-drop over the chat, ⌘V of copied files or pictures on desktop, and images from an Android keyboard. The tray above the field uploads each file as it is attached and supports retry and remove. Send waits for uploads to finish. Photos are downscaled to a 2,048 px long edge and HEIC is converted on the device. A sent message shows thumbnails and document tiles. New plugins: `file_picker`, `desktop_drop`, `pasteboard`. The macOS app also gets the `user-selected.read-only` entitlement.
- **Compaction is untouched.** Tool payloads are still pruned as before. The summariser reads a message's words, not its files, so a file older than the summary is known only by what the conversation said about it. The newest three messages' files still reach the model verbatim. This is recorded in known issue 49.
- **Stored shapes**: every new field is optional and nothing existing changed shape, so no cleanup is needed. Existing Bots reply as before.
- **Docs**: architecture §4 "Attachments", parity row 57j, known issues 49–50, protocol README. There is also a What's New entry, `attachments`, with the still above.

Rebased onto `main` at #821:

- `bun run validate format`: pass

- `bun run validate unit`: 5890 pass, 0 fail (at #819; the pre-push hook re-ran the fast tier at #821)

- The Computer reaching uploads.

## What and why

A Bot's reply used to appear only after the whole model step had finished and `send_to_user` had run: the visible reply is a tool call, and the OpenAI-compatible adapter dropped the AI SDK's `tool-input-*` parts, so nothing reached the person while the model wrote (known issue 34). This streams the `text` of the `send_to_user` being written to watching clients as a **reply draft**, which the Flutter client draws where the message will land and which the real message then replaces in place.

A draft is a preview and nothing else: nothing new is written to the durable log, nothing is published or replayed, an eviction or a dropped socket just loses it, and the Session still reconstructs every model request exactly.

## What changed

**Normalized stream vocabulary (`core/contracts`)**

- `LlmStreamEvent` gains `{ type: "tool-input-delta", id, name, delta }`: a fragment of a call's JSON arguments while the model writes them. The call still arrives whole as `tool-call`, and that is the only thing the loop acts on. The exact decoder accepts it, so a model-provider Plugin may send it too (bounded like `text-delta`; SDK types and ADR 0032 updated).
- The Plugin `ai` grant's stream is unchanged: the kernel filters `tool-input-delta` out before encoding for the isolate, whose exact decoder would refuse it.

**Providers**

- `providers/openai-compatible` (Frock AI included) yields `tool-input-delta` from the SDK's `tool-input-delta` parts, named with the joined name from the raw chunks. The catalog bridge maps pi-ai `toolcall_delta` the same way.
- Side effect, pinned by a deadline test: argument fragments are now stream events, so a long reply written as tool arguments no longer trips the first-byte or idle deadline.

**Billing (`app/billing/model.ts`)**

- `tool-input-delta` counts as partial data, like text: a provider failure part-way through a tool call keeps its reservation for reconciliation instead of settling at zero. Test added.

**Agent loop (`core/agent-loop`)**

- `AgentOptions.watchToolInput(dispatch)` returns a per-dispatch watcher (`delta`, `end`). `consumeStreamV1` hands it fragments and never journals them. A watcher that throws is ignored and costs the Turn nothing (tested).

**Shell (`app/shell/reply-draft.ts`, `turn.ts`)**

- A partial JSON reader pulls `payload.text` out of each `send_to_user` being written, alone or declared inside a `batch`, in the order the sends will land. A draft is `{runId, ordinal, parts}`: `ordinal` is the run's send count when the dispatch began, so part *i* lands at `ordinal + i`, and an empty part (a card, or text not begun) keeps its place.
- It redraws at most every 100 ms, plus once more when the dispatch ends. The next dispatch clears whatever the last one drew. Only chat and agent Turns in the Bot's own thread draw one; group, automation and subagent Turns do not.
- Past 256 KiB of argument text in one dispatch, the watcher stops reading and the draft stops growing.

**Bot Durable Object and state channel (`apps/cloudflare`)**

- `BotStateChannel.broadcastDraft` sends a `state/draft` frame only to sockets that asked with `drafts=1`. Those sockets carry a second hibernation tag, which survives eviction (workerd test).
- A draft appends nothing and has no cursor. A draft too large for one 64 KiB frame is not sent.

**Wire (`client-wire.schema.json`)**

- `StateFrame` gains `{schemaVersion, type: "state/draft", runId, ordinal, parts}`, with fixtures (valid and invalid) and regenerated TS and Dart. The protocol window stays `[2, 2]`.

**Installed apps (Android via Shorebird, macOS)**

- Their generated `StateFrame` decoder has no `state/draft`, and an unknown frame makes them drop and reopen the socket. So they must never be sent one, and they are not: they never ask with `drafts=1`.
- The opt-in is a query parameter because a browser cannot set `x-frockbot-client` on a WebSocket.
- Compatibility holds in both directions:
  - A new client on an older server: the parameter is ignored and no draft is drawn.
  - An old client on this server: nothing changes.
- There is no stored-shape change, so no cleanup is needed.

**Flutter client**

- The socket asks with `drafts=1`. `state/draft` bypasses the cursor but is queued with committed frames, so it can never be applied after the message that replaces it.
- `ChatController.replyDrafts` is in memory only. It is dropped when:
  - an empty frame arrives,
  - the run settles,
  - a snapshot arrives,
  - the socket drops.
- `projectRuns` draws each non-empty part as the line its message will be, under the same `<runId>:send:<ordinal>` id, so the message fills the same bubble.
- A message that landed mid-Turn is placed above the draft.
- A draft has no message actions and is never reported as read.

**Docs**

- Updated:
  - `architecture.md` (request path, stream consumption, a new "Reply drafts" section, client transport, stream events),
  - known issue 34,
  - `core/protocol-schemas/README.md` (also its stale 4,096-byte frame figure),
  - ADR 0032's event list,
  - the stale `chat.e2e.ts` note.
- `CONTEXT.md` gains **Reply draft**.

**What's New**

- `replies-as-written`: "Replies appear as they are written".
- The still is cut 16:9 from a 4× render of the chat shots harness, which uses the real Inter font. The harness gains a `writing` scene and a `CHAT_SHOTS_SCALE` define.

![A phone chat with Fox: under “Draft the investor update from those notes”, Fox’s reply stops mid-word at “bridge clo”, with Fox working below it.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/claude/charming-maxwell-r6nxhq-streaming/app/whats-new/media/replies-as-written.webp)

## Validation

- `bun run validate format` passed.
- `bun run validate typecheck` passed (all generators fresh, 13 packages).
- `bun run validate unit` passed: 5,607 tests.
- `bun run validate runtime` passed: cloudflare workerd (62 files, 355 tests), computer-host (6 tests) and applet-build (5 tests).
- The runtime run includes two new tests in `bot-state-channel.workerd.ts`.
  - A real Turn through the Bot Durable Object sends a `state/draft` before the message that replaces it.
  - A draft reaches only the tagged socket, and that holds across hibernation.
- `apps/native`: `flutter analyze` found no issues, and `flutter test` passed (1,549 passed, 25 skipped; the skipped ones are the review-still scenes, which run only with `CHAT_SHOTS` set).
- `no-mistakes` is not installed in this environment, so that gate was skipped.
- `bun run validate integration` passed: 65 files, 175 tests.
- The branch was rebased onto main at 0939fa40. The only conflicts were the two generated protocol files, and I regenerated both with `bun run generate:protocol`. After that, `check-client-protocol` passed, the protocol fixture tests passed (TS and Dart), `flutter analyze` and the touched Flutter suites passed, and the pre-push fast tier passed again (format, typecheck, and unit with 5,629 tests).
- Browser specs, run locally after the merge with the container's Chromium (`FROCKBOT_E2E_SUITE=core`): `chat`, `continuous-chat`, `unread-focus`, `mobile` and `errors`.
  - 19 of 20 passed.
  - `chat.e2e.ts` "a conversation opens at its end, and switching back to it does not reload it" failed in all three full-file runs on this code. It passes when run on its own.
  - The same file on the commit before this PR (8eee2960) passed that test in both runs. In the second run a different chat test failed instead, and that failure restarted the page, so this test ran on a fresh account.
  - The failure is in the harness's `expectBotOpen` for a newly created Bot, which could not read the page within 30 s. The machine's load average was about 15 on 4 cores, and the trace shows every page read taking 0.4 to 1.3 s.
  - The same file passed whole on main's CI for the merge commit (core shard 1/4, with this test at 58 s), and all four core browser shards passed there. I read this as load on the shared machine, not a regression.

## Why

The version at the foot of the Profile page didn't match the GitHub releases. The app showed `pubspec.yaml`'s `1.6.0` while the releases are tagged `v0.7.x`, and the signed Mac app showed "Development build" because its release build was given no version at all.

The two numbers had nothing to do with each other. `1.6.0` only ever moved when the deployment had to refuse an older client: it was a compatibility counter, and it duplicated the protocol range the gate already checks. It couldn't be the tag, because a pull request cannot know which tag it will ship as.

## What changes

**The release tag is the app's one version.** It stays on the `0.7.x` line, with no jump to v1.
- `release.yml` sets `FROCKBOT_RELEASE` to the tag it builds for the web client, the Mac app, and the Android release and patch. `scripts/native-metadata.ts` validates it and turns it into the Profile page's version and the native `--build-name`.
- An Android patch carries its own tag and keeps the versionName of the release it patches, so the Profile page names the GitHub release whose code is running.
- Every other build (local, hand-cut, CI staging) is a development build on `pubspec.yaml`'s new `0.0.0` placeholder, and says "Development build".
- The client's hello names the tag, or leaves `nativeVersion` out outside a release. Nothing gates on it.

**The deployment gates on the protocol alone.**
- `minimumNativeVersion` is gone from the schema, the generators and `client-compatibility.ts`. A change an installed client cannot decode raises `protocolMax` (grace period) or `protocolMin` (enforce), in the same pull request.
- `nativeVersion` stays in `ClientHello`, now optional, because installed apps send it and the hello rejects unknown fields.
- Sessions no longer bind `protocolVersion` (`native-auth.ts`). Otherwise raising the protocol would sign everyone out, which the version floor never did. Catalogs stay bound, and every bearer request is still negotiated, so leaving out the header cannot pick a different window. **This is auth code; worth a careful look.**

**Docs:** `apps/native/README.md`, `core/protocol-schemas/README.md`, `docs/app-updates.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/notifications.md` and `AGENTS.md` now describe the tag version and the protocol floor.

**What's New:** a text-only `fix` entry, "Profile names the release". There's no still, because nothing changes on screen except the number.

## Behavior to know about

- **Builds from before 1.6.0 are no longer refused.** They speak protocol 1, the only protocol there is. Raising `protocolMin` is how to shut them out again.
- **Android's versionName goes from `1.6.0` to `0.7.x` at the next full release.** The patch baseline is the newest release by build code, not by name, so it still wins. There's a test for exactly this.
- **The web bundle now changes on every tag**, because the tag is compiled into it, so browsers re-download the client each release.

## Testing

- Unit tier (format, typecheck, 5,247 tests) through the pre-push hook; `bun run typecheck` including every generated-file check.
- Flutter: the full suite with `--dart-define=FROCKBOT_ORIGIN=https://tests.invalid` (1,380 passed, 16 skipped), and `flutter analyze`.
- Python: `native-update`, `native-metadata`, `native-desktop-update` and `native-acceptance` tests.
- A real `flutter build web` through `build-flutter-web.ts`: `FROCKBOT_RELEASE=0.7.999` compiles the label to the literal `"Version 0.7.999"`, and `v0.7.999` stops the build with the validation error.
- Browser suite, run locally (`bun run validate:e2e`): 57 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped.
  - `marketplace-plugins` › "installs a model and leaves a fresh Bot usable" fails on a 404 for `assets/connectors/radius.png`. Plain `main` fails the same spec with the same 404 here, and `main.yml` has been red on `main` since #722 with the same kind of 404 in other specs.
  - `rive-runtime` › "serves Rive's runtime from this origin" passed when rerun on this branch merged with `main`. The runtime loads without blocking the first paint, so the test can check before its response arrives; the bundle carries `/rive/44.0.0/` and the runtime is staged.
- Not run here: the Mac and Android builds, which only a real release run exercises.

One incidental test fix: the provider-setup test "tampered" with a signed URL by swapping its last character for `x`. That character carries base64 padding bits the decoder ignores, and the new hello content happened to end on one, so the "tampered" token still verified. The test now changes a character inside the signature. Nothing can be forged through this (the signature bytes are identical); it's only a second spelling of the same token.

The core stays MIT while FrockBot for Teams is licensed separately. That dual licensing needs the right to relicense contributions, and the time to add a CLA is before outside contributions arrive.

## What changes

- **`CLA.md`**: the individual agreement, v1.0. It is adapted from the Apache ICLA v2.2 and governed by NSW law.
  - Contributors grant Tim a licence they can't revoke, which Tim may pass on under any terms, including closed-source.
  - In return, merged contributions are licensed to everyone under MIT for good (section 3), with a patent licence for those recipients.
  - The agreement covers moral-rights waiver and consent, transfer to a company Tim controls or co-founds or to a buyer, versioning, minors via guardian consent, and AI-assisted contributions.
- **`CCLA.md`**: a corporate agreement for employers or clients who own a contributor's work. People it lists also sign `CLA.md` themselves.
- **`.github/workflows/cla.yml`**: runs `contributor-assistant/github-action` v2.6.1, pinned by SHA. It records signatures in `signatures/cla-v1.0.json` on a `cla-signatures` branch.
  - Exemption is by the account that opened the PR, which GitHub verifies: `timoconnellaus` and `dependabot[bot]`. It never relies on commit author names, which can be forged, and the opener must also have signed.
  - PRs changing fewer than five lines of text, and no binary or generated files, skip the check.
  - The workflow creates the signatures file itself, because the pinned action version doesn't.
  - It never checks out PR code.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** (new) and the README licence section explain the licensing model and how to sign.
- **`scripts/babysit.ts`** and the babysit skill report a failing `CLA` check as skip ("needs Tim"), not fix. Includes a test.

## Review

Three review rounds of five agents each read the drafts. A survey of 19 other projects' CLAs fed in as well, including Harmony, Qt, Grafana, HashiCorp, Infisical, StellarGraph and Cal.com.

## Still open

- **Lawyer's check.** A NSW lawyer has not reviewed the agreements. The open questions:
  - whether a PR-comment signature binds without a deed and meets s 195AWA for moral-rights consent
  - guardian consent under the Minors (Property and Contracts) Act 1970
  - whether the unfair contract terms rules apply
- **End-to-end test.** The check runs from `main`, so it is untested until this merges. To test, open a PR from a second, non-exempt account with at least five changed lines. It should be asked to sign, and should go green after the account comments the signing sentence.
- **Repository settings, for Tim.** Make `CLA` a required check in the `main` ruleset, and protect `cla-signatures` against force-push and deletion.

  - on desktop, cards had a fixed height, so an opened card clipped its key form;
  - OpenRouter, xAI, Copilot, Kimi and Radius each appeared twice.

## What changes

**Settings structure**
- Account features and the account Plugins list are gone, along with their routes (`/api/settings/plugins`, `/api/settings/capabilities`, `/api/settings/marketplace/plugins`) and the `PluginsFrame` protocol type.
- The first-party features and Custom models are now `platformOwned`. The account always holds them, and the Bot's switch is the only one. Every Bot may choose its own model.
- The account read repairs existing accounts to the new state, so no migration is needed.

**A Bot's Plugins page**
- Lists only what that Bot can switch, under **Built in** and **Made by your Bots**.
- Locked card plugins, and plugins that only serve a model, are no longer rows.

**Models**
- Lists only providers that have been added.
- Each provider has one action: "Connect account" until a key is connected, then "Manage provider".
- Frock AI's own models are labelled "built in, no key needed". Frock AI stays the only model provider a new account has; a test now pins that.

**Marketplace**
- "Add" opens the key form. A connected provider's card offers **Choose a model**, which opens Models.
- A removed provider can be added again. Provider rows gain an `installed` flag, since a key left behind no longer counts as added.
- A refused "Add" says why.
- Cards are laid out in rows, so an opened card is never clipped.
- "Add" (`user/choose-model-provider`) now reconciles a provider Plugin into the Composition straight away.
- A deployment without a Worker Loader no longer offers a Plugin-served provider.

**One card per model provider**
- Every row of a model provider carries the provider's name, and the client draws a model Package's rows as one card.
- "Connect" opens that card on **Use an API key** and **Sign in**. Each way sends its own Connection Type's command, as before.
- The Provider accounts page that Models opens uses the same card.
- Connector apps stay one card each.

Docs updated: `CONTEXT.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/profile-settings.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/model-providers.md`, and amendments to ADRs 0026, 0030 and 0032.

Stills captured from the real app:

- `bun run typecheck`: all 13 packages.
- `bun test`: 5,204 pass. This is the pre-push tier, together with format.
- `flutter analyze`: clean. The Flutter suites for connections, plugins, view, settings and first-run pass.
  - 23 other Flutter tests (auth recovery, badge, auth, computer, Mac messages, voice mode) fail in the cloud container, and fail identically on unmodified `main`.
- The workerd tests that changed pass: `plugins-composition`, `provider-plugin`, `provider-plugin-recovery`.
- Browser e2e specs `bot-plugins`, `marketplace-plugins`, `settings-models` and `provisioning` pass locally. They ran with `FROCKBOT_E2E_SUITE=core`, because the applet-builder container can't reach npm through this sandbox's proxy.

## Intent

Follow-up on PR #876 (Plugin jev grant, map item P13, which Tim approved as part of building every Jev use on the map). The generated Plugin worker wrapper text changed in this PR: a ctx.jev member, and the gate's fix giving trigger invocations the registered standalone call identity. PLUGIN_WORKER_INDEX_VERSION says to bump it on any change to the generated text so a changed wrapper is a new worker, so this bumps index-v11 to index-v12.

## What Changed

- Plugins can declare a new `jev` grant, which adds a `ctx.jev.decide({ state, questions })` member. The Bot's `isolateJevDecide` (called through `BotCapabilities.jevDecide`) first checks the request: it must have 1–32 questions of type `choice`, `noul` or `score`, and be no larger than 64 KiB. It also checks that the admitted Plugin declared `jev`. It then calls hosted Jev on the pinned model `jev-1.13.0` and returns the answers without reading them. Each Plugin gets at most 64 calls per run. Contracts, the SDK typings and the plugins skill references describe the grant.
- Usage from these calls is recorded as the Plugin's own. Inside a Turn, a call is added to the Turn log as `package/model-usage` with provider `jev`. A call made outside a Turn is stored on the Bot under `plugins:jev-usage`, which keeps the latest 512. `docs/billing.md` and ADR 0026 describe Plugin Jev calls as product overhead, itemised under the Plugin.
- Trigger invocations now carry the registered standalone call identity (`sessionId`, `runId`, `turnId`, `generationId`) and no longer use a made-up `trigger:<routineId>` identity. Because this and the new `ctx.jev` member change the generated Plugin worker wrapper text, `PLUGIN_WORKER_INDEX_VERSION` goes from `index-v11` to `index-v12`. New tests: a workerd suite in `plugin-jev-grant.workerd.ts`, plus unit tests in the contract, bot, wrapper and host tests.

## Why A Composio Gmail message fetch returns the message's HTML body plus its MIME parts in base64: 70–90 KB, with very few actual words. Connect sent results to the model as raw JSON and refused anything over 128 KB. Four such fetches in Bob's Turn 119 were enough to push the request past Frock AI's prepaid limit. ## What changes `app/connect/result.ts` `connectResultV1` shapes the answer, **for Gmail tools only** (`GMAIL_*`): - A string of 1,000+ characters that begins as HTML is converted with the existing linear-time `htmlToTextV1` (built for untrusted email). The body's `http(s)` links are listed after the text, up to 6,000 characters in total. - A run of 8,000 or more base64 characters is replaced with a line saying encoded data was left out. - A result still over 40,000 characters keeps its first 32k and last 8k characters, with the cut marked. - Every scan is a single pass. No pattern backtracks over the body. Every other app behaves exactly as before: raw JSON, refused past 128 KB. The first version shaped all apps. Review found it could corrupt pages and files a Bot reads and writes back, and could mistake long paging tokens for encoded data, so it is now limited to Gmail. Not included: saving large results to the Workspace with a pointer, which research found is the most common approach elsewhere. Connect tools have no Workspace access today, so that would need `WorkspaceFilesV1` and its durable write-intent protocol wired through the Connect runtime. It's worth a separate change. ## Test plan - [x] A RedBalloon-style HTML email comes through as its text and voucher link, with the style block and base64 parts removed, in under 1 KB. - [x] A small answer is untouched. Text that only mentions `

` and a long paging token are untouched. - [x] A body with 200k spaces is shaped in under a second. The first version's `/[ \t]+\n/g` took about 9 s on 80k. - [x] An over-long Gmail answer keeps its beginning and end and marks the cut. Another app's answer is still refused past 128 KB. - [x] `bun test app/connect/` (97 pass), `validate:typecheck` and `validate:format` pass. - `validate:unit`: everything passes except the sandbox-only `plugin-build.test.ts` Workers start-up timeout, which passes when run alone. Stage 1 of Group Chats, plus the agreed design for the whole feature.

## Steering replaces Supersede

Until now, a message sent while a Bot was working superseded the running Turn: the Turn was interrupted and the Bot started again on the new message. Now the message **steers** the Bot instead.

- **Queue.** A user-lane message sent while a run is active or waiting joins a FIFO queue, `pending-user-run:` with a limit of 32, where the single `pending-run` slot used to be. When the queue is full the send is refused plainly. Background runs still refuse while anything is active or pending.
- **Yield at the step boundary.** `AgentOptions.userMessageWaiting()` is checked in `#stepShouldStop` after every step that would continue, and after every policy hook, so the delivery hook's forced "continue" still gives way. The Turn ends `completed` with everything it did recorded. Nothing in flight is cancelled.
- **Steering note.** When a chat Turn on the user lane ends still owing a reply (`endedOwingReplyV1`), a `yielded-turn` pending input is queued. The next Turn's context then carries a `[Steering]` preamble: read the new message first, then decide whether to carry the earlier work on. Whether it changes course is up to the Bot.
- **Removed:** the `superseded` run status, `supersededAt`/`supersededBy`, `hasModelIntent`, `interruptTurn`, `planSupersede`, the `superseded-turn` input, and the client's Supersede drain UI.
- **Wire.** `RunOutcome` is now `failed | cancelled`, and the superseded Run variant is gone. Installed clients still decode everything the server sends, so no protocol bump is needed. `TurnCommand.supersedes` is still accepted and ignored, because installed apps send it with every message.
- **Stored-state cleanup.** `apps/cloudflare/src/supersede-cleanup.ts` runs once per Bot, guarded by the receipt `maintenance:supersede-removal:2026-09-23`, in the BotState constructor. It:
  - rewrites superseded runs, projected rows and updates as `cancelled`;
  - strips the retired fields;
  - moves the old `pending-run` into the user queue;
  - deletes queued `superseded-turn` inputs and the drain receipts that carry one.
- **Client.** The optimistic greyed queued row stays. A stop request draws only "Stopping…".
- **What's New:** a `steering` entry with a still.

## Group Chat design

`docs/plan.md` gains "Planned: Group Chats replace Projects": the agreed conversation model, how @mentions and the Jev reply judge work, membership, the interface after #721, the architecture (one GroupChat Durable Object per group), and build stages 1–6. Stage 1 is this PR.

## Validation

- Fast tier on the rebased head: format and typecheck pass, and all 5,239 unit tests pass.
- Runtime tier and integration tier: both pass. This includes the new `steering.integration.ts`, which sends a second message mid-Turn and checks it queues, the Turn yields, and the Bot answers.
- Flutter: all 1,371 tests pass.
- Browser: `chat.e2e.ts` "a message sent mid-Turn waits above the working avatar, and is answered" passes. It is no longer `fixme`.
- New unit coverage: `core/durable/turn-queue.test.ts` (FIFO, bound, replay, eviction, Stop), the agent loop's yield tests, the terminal records for yielded Turns, and `supersede-cleanup.test.ts`.

Four client-side fixes from a review of notifications and unread badges. Each one was reproduced first with a widget test that drives the real `AppShell` against a fake server that keeps its own unread record. All changes are in the Flutter client. There are no server or durable-shape changes.

## What changes

**Marking the open Bot unread stuck for only a moment.** Opening a Bot arms a one-time clear of its manual unread mark. The arm was only used up when a read was actually sent, so a Bot opened with nothing unread stayed armed. The next mark the person made (on the open chat, or from another device) was then cleared at once: `[bot/mark-unread, bot/mark-read]`. Now the first read that sees the open Bot uses up the arm either way.

**A reply in the chat being read alerted other devices.** A reply reaches the chat through the state channel a poll before `/api/bots/unread` names it. `_readLatest` compared the two and dropped the presence claim in that gap. Every drain is triggered by a message commit, so the Turn's next `send_to_user` then went out as an alert to every device, including the phone in the reader's hand. The claim now holds while the chat holds the latest message it and the cloud agreed on, or anything newer. The shell also reads unread straight away rather than waiting for its 10s poll, so the receipt follows within one round trip. A cloud that is ahead of the chat, naming a message the chat hasn't drawn, still holds nothing back.

**Scrolled up in the open chat sounded an alert that was then withdrawn.** The badge already treated the open, focused chat as being read wherever it was scrolled. Presence also required the newest message to be on screen. So a reply alerted the phone, and the badge reconcile cancelled the notification a moment later. The transcript now reports its newest message together with whether it is on screen. Presence follows the badge's focus rule. The read receipt still waits for the message to come into view, and leaving without reading releases the alert.

**The Mac dock badge froze while the window was minimised.** `hidden` stopped the unread poll, and a hidden window draws no frames, so the build-time reconcile never ran either. While away, `DockBadgePresenter.needsRefreshWhileAway` keeps a 30s poll going, and the badge is also reconciled straight from the unread listener. Android and web are unchanged.

## Tests

- `apps/native/test/unread_reading_test.dart` (new, 7 tests):
  - Four of them fail without these changes: one for each bug, plus the other-device case.
  - The scrolled-up test fails on the first commit alone.
  - Two tests guard behaviour the fixes must keep: opening a manually unread Bot clears it, and a cloud that is ahead of the chat claims nothing.
- `shell_transcript_test.dart` and `retry_message_test.dart` are updated for the callback's new `(newest, onScreen)` shape. The transcript test also asserts that the newest message is still named after scrolling it out of view.
- Results on the branch rebased onto `fbcd882`:
  - `flutter analyze --no-pub` is clean.
  - `flutter test --no-pub --dart-define=FROCKBOT_ORIGIN=https://tests.invalid`: 1,388 pass, with 19 skipped that were already skipped on `main`.
  - Pre-push fast tier (format, typecheck, unit): 5,247 pass.
- Browser suite, run locally: the `core` corpus passes, 58 of 58, including `unread-focus` and `routine-failure-message`. The `publication` corpus could not start in the session's container, because the Applet build image's `npm ci` can't reach the registry through its TLS proxy. That corpus covers Applet publication, which this change does not touch.

## Docs and What's New

- `docs/notifications.md` describes the presence rule, the one-time manual-unread clear, and the dock while hidden. It also adds a minimised window to the dock release check.
- What's New gets a `fix` entry, `unread-keeps-up`, with no still because no surface changed.

## Worth checking on a real Mac after release

Minimise FrockBot, let a Bot reply, and the Dock badge should update within about 30 seconds.

hits.body:
**Stacked on #946** (review only the last commit). Merge order: #942 → #944 → #945 → #946 → this.

## Why

Steps 9–10 of the plan. A refused call told the model to "ask in conversation", which made consent a text-inference problem — the next Turn's "yes" had to be re-read by Jev with its referent gone. And a Bot could create a Routine, or rewrite or pause the person's, by setting `userAsked: true` itself; the Routine's prompt then authorized its own calls when it fired (audit F2). Plugin tool calls (`package-tool:` ids) skipped supervision entirely, and any unplaceable effect id failed open (F16).

## What changes

**Approval cards for refused outward calls.** When call review refuses a call that reaches outside FrockBot (or lands in a new uncertain band: authorization probability < 0.55 or arguments < 0.5), and nothing tried to steer the reviewer, supervision records the exact tool and canonical arguments and draws a kernel-minted `approval` card. The identical call, made again after approval, runs once without asking Jev; changed arguments need a new card; a decline is final. Reads never get a card.

**Routines don't wait.** In a Routine or hand-off Turn the card goes to the person's conversation and the Routine carries on, saying in its hand-off what is waiting; approving later opens a Turn that makes the call. (This was an open choice; reverse it in `awaitingApprovalResult`, `app/supervision/loop.ts`.)

**Routine changes need the person.** `userAsked` is removed from `routine_manage`. Creating a Routine, changing a prompt, schedule or trigger, and pausing or deleting one the person created all draw a card, and nothing is armed until approved. A firing counts as the person's (`promptBy: "user"`) only if they created the Routine or approved its prompt on a card.

**Plugin calls are supervised.** `package-tool:` calls are placed in their Turn via the `package/tool-call` entry and reviewed; a `mutate` call supervision cannot place is refused.

`core/tools/tools.ts`: every `mutate` call is now ordered, so mutate calls inside a batch run one after another (a refused one may draw a card).

## Behaviour change to know about

A Routine a Bot wrote without the person's approval now fires as the Bot's and asks for nothing. Existing Bot-written Routines (Bob's morning triage is likely one) need one approval: ask the Bot to update it, and approve the card.

## Stored data

Additive only (`askPerson`/`approvalId` on decisions, `promptApprovalId` on Routines, new `supervision:call-approval*` and `routine:intent:*` keys); no cleanup needed.

## Tests and evals

New `app/supervision/{call-review,call-approval}.test.ts`, 8 new `loop.test.ts` cases, rewritten `app/routines/agent.test.ts`, 2 new `app/approvals/bot.test.ts` cases. Call review evals, five repeats: 56/56, no flips; new `askPerson` check 4/4. This branch (the stack top) passes `validate:runtime` and `validate:integration` on current `main`. What's New entry `approval-cards` (no still — none could be captured in this environment).

## Summary

- classify pre-response provider failures as transient, permanent, or unknown with bounded reasons and optional Retry-After
- replace fixed immediate retrying with Turn-deadline-bounded equal-jitter exponential backoff and durable `model/retry` events
- fall back from a permanently rejected manual Frock AI model to Frock AI Auto for the rest of the Turn
- preserve reconciliation semantics after any provider response event and add plain total UI failure copy

## Transport classification

| Transport | Transient | Permanent | Unknown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI-compatible | HTTP 408, 429, 5xx; network/reset/timeout faults; first-byte deadline | HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 413; content/safety policy codes | other statuses or unmatched pre-response faults |
| Ollama Cloud | shared OpenAI-compatible mapping | invalid Connection authority/generation/authorization plus shared permanent HTTP failures | credential lease/open failures and unmatched faults |
| Frock AI Gateway / Workers AI | shared transient statuses and rate/overload/unavailable/timeout/gateway/reset envelopes | shared permanent statuses and invalid/auth/credential/model/content/safety/policy envelopes | unmatched native envelopes |
| Foundation | none declared by its local transport | none declared by its local transport | unexpected pre-response faults |
| Custom Models | delegates to the selected provider transport | delegates to the selected provider transport | delegates to the selected provider transport |

## Backoff

- base: 500 ms
- cap: 8,000 ms
- equal jitter: 50–100% of the exponential ceiling
- Retry-After is a floor and may exceed the cap
- transient failures retry only while the delay fits before the Turn deadline; unknown failures receive one retry; permanent failures do not retry the same model

## Validation

- `bun install --force`
- focused unit suites: 394 tests passed
- Cloudflare integration: 45 files / 119 tests passed
- root `bun run typecheck`: all 73 packages passed, including kernel/computer import checks and generated-artifact freshness
- Prettier check on all touched files

## Intent

Tim asked me to do follow-ups 6 and 10 from my Jev list. (6) The second half of map item P10, the claim check: check a send's factual claims against the pages fetched this Turn. When the Turn's results include web_fetch, web_search or computer_browser, the per-send claim call also asks 'facts' (no_page_facts / supported / unsupported) over the latest 3 pages, each clipped to 4,000 chars. Unsupported at >= 0.7 withholds with a new reason, unsupported_fact: it does not end the Turn, shares the claim check's once-per-Turn limit, and the model is told to say only what the pages say. The loop now names each result by the tool that ran (resolveDynamicToolNameV1), so a web_fetch behind call_dynamic_tool is recognised. (10) The relay case toast-condensed flickered at 0.59 against a 0.6 threshold, because the message described the toast rather than condensing it and the relay choice had no label for that. A 'describes' label now counts as rewriting work the person asked for (0.92 live). eval:response-review is 56/56 live, including 4 new facts cases.

## What Changed

- **Facts check on each send.** When the Turn has successful `web_fetch`, `web_search` or `computer_browser` results, the per-send claim call to Jev also asks a `facts` question (`no_page_facts` / `supported` / `unsupported`). Jev sees the latest 3 pages, each clipped to 4,000 chars, plus flags for clipped pages and a count of earlier pages it is not shown. It is told that anything that could sit in those unseen parts counts as supported. An `unsupported` answer at ≥ 0.7 withholds the send with a new reason code, `unsupported_fact`. The withhold does not end the Turn, it shares the claim check's once-per-Turn limit, and the model is told to say only what the pages say or to say plainly that it could not find it. The Bot audit labels these withholds "said a page said what it did not".
- **Tool names and the relay check.** `priorResults` in `loop.ts` now names each result by the tool that actually ran (`resolveDynamicToolNameV1`), so a `web_fetch` called through `call_dynamic_tool` counts as a page. The relay choice has a new `describes` label, which is treated as rewriting work the person asked for, the same as `condenses`/`rewrites`. The relay check is skipped only when every piece of work it would look at was already sent to the person in full this Turn.
- **Tests, evals and docs.** Added 4 facts cases to the `eval:response-review` fixtures. Added unit, contract and loop tests, plus a new workerd test (`apps/cloudflare/test/claim-facts.workerd.ts`). Raised a load-sensitive `computer/fly` test's timeout to 30s. Updated `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/jev-supervision-plan.md`.

PR 2 of 5 from the Bob Plugin-authoring incident (2026-09-23).

Bob spent five `computer_exec` calls, one of them a 73 s `grep -rl … /`, looking for the Plugin SDK's types. The only SDK on Tim's Computer is the stale `~/.frockbot/applets` copy (0.3.14, no `plugin/` subpath; PR 3 removes it). The real declarations exist only in the applet-build container, and there they typed `theme/assemble`'s `document`, along with most other hook payloads, as `{ [key: string]: unknown }`. A theme document the kernel refused was then dropped with no trace.

## Precise hook types, pinned to the kernel

- Every payload and replacement in `PluginHookPayloads` / `PluginHookReplacements` (`applets/sdk/plugin/index.d.ts`) is now the exact shape the kernel hands the isolate and decodes back:
  - `ThemeDocument`, `BotLook`
  - `PromptAssemblyContext`, `PromptAssembly`
  - `AgentSnapshot`, `StepSnapshot`
  - `ToolSchema` (its index signature is gone; the kernel's exact-key decoder refused extra members anyway)
  - `ToolCall`, `ToolCallContext`, `ToolPreparation`, `ToolCallResult`, `ToolAttachment`
  - `ModelRequest` with its messages, response format and binding
- The file stays self-contained, because the build container copies only `applets/sdk`. New names avoid the SDK's existing `WorkspacePath`, `WorkspaceRoot` and `ToolResult`, which mean other things.
- `app/plugins/sdk-types.test.ts` proves each event's payload identical to `LoopEventPayloadMapV1[event]`, and each replacement identical to `LoopEventReturnMapV1[event]`. It also proves `ThemeDocument` identical to `ThemeDocumentV1`. A mapped check fails if the kernel gains an event.
  - The check is type identity, not mutual assignability. An `any` from a name the `.d.ts` failed to resolve (`skipLibCheck` hides it), a `readonly` difference, or an optional-member difference now fails `tsc -p app`. I mutation-tested both kinds of break.
  - The declarations also compile standalone with `skipLibCheck` off.
- **What stays opaque, and why:** only what the kernel itself leaves opaque.
  - `ToolCall.input` is whatever the model sent.
  - `inputSchema` is a JSON Schema object.
  - `ModelReplayState.content` is provider-owned replay content.
  - `StructuredOutputSchema.enum` is `unknown[]`.
  - `agent/turn-stopping`'s replacement stays `never` where the kernel says `void`, because the kernel refuses any value there. The test pins both halves.
  - `PluginModelRequest`, the model-provider contract rather than a hook payload, is untouched.

## `types.md`, from the file the checker uses

- `scripts/build-applets-assets.ts` now writes `app/plugins/skills/plugins/references/types.md` from `SDK_PLUGIN_TYPES` (`applets/sdk/src/build/paths.ts`), the same path `typeCheckPlugin` maps `@frockbot/applet-sdk/plugin` to.
- It is generated before the Plugins Skill module, which reads it. Its fence is longer than any backtick run inside, so the declarations' own examples cannot close it.
- The existing `--check` in `bun run typecheck` is the freshness guard. A test checks the fenced body is byte-for-byte the declarations and that the shipped reference is what the generator makes.
- SKILL.md, `hooks.md`, `module.md` and `troubleshooting.md` now:
  - point at `types.md`;
  - say the types are not on the Computer and that `plugin_check` resolves them;
  - list the `ThemeDocument` rules exactly as `decodeThemeDocumentV1` applies them:
    - exact members;
    - `approval`/`billing`/`Stop`/`grants` refused anywhere as a key;
    - `#rrggbb` colours;
    - `text` ≥ 4.5:1 against `window` and against `surface`, `muted` ≥ 3:1 against `window`, `onAccent` ≥ 4.5:1 against `accent`;
    - at most 24 phases, each `after` a 24-hour `HH:MM`.
- `hooks.md` also says the kernel checks the chain's final value, and charges a refusal to every Plugin that wraps the event.

## A refused theme is no longer silent

- **How hook failures surface today:** a hook failure in a Turn goes to `package/hook-failed` plus `onPluginFailure` → `notePluginFailureV1`. That gives a notice, a count, and quarantine at three in a row.
- **Why theme was silent:** the theme hook runs in the standalone (no-Turn) mount, whose `recordHookFailure` was a no-op. The kernel's decode failure was dropped there, and `assemble.ts` then fell back to the last document.
- **The change:**
  - The standalone mount takes `hookFailuresAs`, and theme assembly passes `"theme"`. The host's per-Plugin failure record (the throw, the overrun, or the decoder's reason) now reaches the same notice and quarantine a Turn's would.
  - Each assembly is its own run (`theme:<uuid>`, well within the run-id bound), so each refusal counts.
  - A clean assembly settles the count, the way a clean Turn does, so "in a row" stays true. Settling skips a Plugin whose last failure is this same run, so the fallback after a refusal never wipes the refusal.
  - A theme keeps one notice per Plugin per generation, rather than one per hourly assembly.
  - The notice reads "A plugin could not set this Bot's theme: <reason>. Its change to this Bot's theme was not applied."
  - `PluginFailureNoticeV1.card` is renamed `kind` and gains `"theme"`, and `PluginFailureKindV1` gains `"theme"`. Callers updated: `backend-composition.ts`, `cards/bot.ts`, `health-bot.test.ts`. I grepped `origin/main` at 2ad976b4 again before merging and found no other callers. `app/isolates/bot.ts` passes the failure through unchanged.
- **Tests:**
  - A host test: a low-contrast document is recorded against its Plugin.
  - Notice-wording and per-generation tests.
  - A Worker test: a real theme Plugin, the real `assembleTheme` RPC, the notice with its reason, and quarantine after three. It fails with the old no-op recorder.
- What's New gains "A refused plugin theme is reported". It has no still: it is notice copy in an existing surface.

## Validation

- Local, on this head (a127b9a9, which contains `main` at 2ad976b4), run in stages so load doesn't cause timeouts:
  - `bun run validate format typecheck`: pass.
  - `bun run validate unit`: 5226 pass, 0 fail.
  - `bun run validate runtime`: 341 Cloudflare Worker tests in 62 files, Computer host 6, Applet build 5, all pass.
  - `bun run validate integration`: 172 tests in 63 files pass.
- **Browser suite (`bun run test:e2e --forbid-only`):** 58 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed.
  - The failure was `marketplace-plugins.e2e.ts` › "Marketplace installs a model and leaves a fresh Bot usable", a 4-minute timeout waiting for the composer.
  - Rerun alone with `--repeat-each=2`, the file passes 4/4.
  - *Corrected after merge.* I first put this down to `closeOverlay`'s Back presses. The trace from #712's run, where the test failed the same way, shows otherwise. The test clicks Marketplace as soon as the sidebar shows, and under four-worker load that was before `/api/bots/bootstrap` had created the fresh user's General Bot. So no conversation was ever selected. This PR changes none of those requests or the client. Details are in #712.
  - The local e2e run needs this session's proxy CA in the applet-build image. That was a temporary, uncommitted patch, reverted after each run.
- **No-mistakes gate:** this cloud session's permission policy refuses to start the gate's `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` review agent as root. I ran its steps directly: format/typecheck (lint), tests, a docs pass, and an independent code-review pass.
  - The review found nothing breaking CI.
  - Its points are all addressed in this commit: hourly notice repetition, run-id length, and wording when several Plugins wrap the event.
