## Intent

Reduce FrockBot turn-start latency, from a profiling handoff measured against production on 2026-09-16 (37 turns, 105 model calls; median turn 11.7s, provider call >90% of it). Everything outside the provider call sums to ~1s on a median turn and ~5s on a busy Bot; these four commits attack that preamble. All pure performance, no user-visible behaviour change.

(1) core/durable: persistRunEvents' contiguity guard needed only the log's LENGTH but called SessionEventLog.read, which hydrates every page and, for each cut entry, fetches every payload chunk, re-verifies its SHA-256 and parses it. Every model/request is stored cut at ~80KiB and nothing prunes them, and a Turn's preamble flushes ~8 times. Added SessionEventLog.count() reading index.eventCount, with a legacy-array fallback for an unmigrated log. The guard itself is unchanged. Deliberately did NOT touch the other eventLog.read call sites (settleStaleRun, recoverActiveRun) because those genuinely consume the events.

(2) app/memory: turn start read every Memory file twice - once by MemoryStore.read to render the injected block, then again by reindex() -> readAllMemoryDocumentsV1 four lines later, serially, on the same critical path. The tier read now carries the documents it already decoded (new MemoryTierReadV1.documents) and the reindex that follows the render consumes them exactly once (take-and-clear). A reindex after memory_write or memory_forget still reads from disk because those files just changed. Completeness is derived as !unavailable && !omitted, equivalent to what the disk path computes. Chose a REQUIRED field over an optional one so a tier read can never silently claim completeness with no documents - that is why three call sites building MemoryTierReadV1 literals gained 'documents: []'.

(3) Serial for-loops of independent awaits made parallel: memory tiers, a tier's files, a rebuild's roots and files, SKILL.md bodies, the two Skill instruction roots, and Plugin artifacts at mount. The Skill look-ahead deliberately only prefetches candidates that the checks BEFORE a read would admit, and stops at the catalog bound, so it never reads a body the serial loop would have refused unread; a candidate it did not cover (because refusals after a read freed room under the bound) is still read in place. Which Skills load and which refusals are recorded are unchanged.

(4) Repeated cross-Durable-Object reads collapsed. The account features record was read three times inside one runtime mount (Applets gate, Plugin authoring gate, withheld managed Skills), and the teammates prompt section called listBots() on every step's prompt assembly. The User DO is single-threaded and shared by every Bot of that User, so each round trip is also a chance to queue behind a sibling Bot's Turn - that is where the 2.89s tail on the admitted-to-turn/start gap came from. Both are memoized for the MOUNT that made them, NOT cached on the Bot, deliberately preserving the documented rule that a Turn admitted after an admin moves a switch sees where the switch is now. bot_create invalidates the flock memo so a Bot made mid-Turn is still named in the next step's prompt, and bot_create's own revision-fencing read never goes through the memo.

Explicitly out of scope by decision, left for follow-up: running the three preStep injections concurrently (needs a designed prefetch-then-await seam so the durable log's append order stays deterministic); moving memory reindex off the critical path (changes memory_search visibility semantics within a Turn, a behaviour decision); metadata-before-ledger in workspace-store generationOf (medium-high risk, touches repair and reconcile ordering); wiring Memory embeddings through to the host (needs a decision on whether the lexical fallback in production is intentional, and incremental embedding first); and bounding the durable session log (needs an ADR). A batch meta-tool is a separate stacked branch because it is a behaviour change rather than a perf fix.

This branch is rebased onto 4a0c9360 rather than the newest origin/main because the gate mirror's main is one merge behind origin and refused the push with 'PR branch contains merge commits'.

Note on a previous attempt: the pre-push suite failed one test, scripts/setup-production.test.ts 'forwards active secrets to the deploy', on a 5000ms timeout. That file is not in this diff (the diff touches app/, core/durable, frock-compose only). It passes locally in 3.34s, a thin margin against its 5s cap, and four other no-mistakes runs were saturating the machine at the time. Treated as a load-sensitive pre-existing flake, not a regression.

Full test suite and typecheck across all 13 packages pass locally.

## What Changed

- `persistRunEvents` no longer calls `SessionEventLog.read` just to bounds-check the batch: the pre-check is dropped and `append` — which enforces the same contiguity rule against the same index inside the same transaction — now runs first, so a flush stops hydrating every page and re-verifying every payload chunk of the session log.
- Memory now reads each file once per turn: `MemoryTierReadV1` carries the documents the tier read already decoded (a required `documents` field, taken-and-cleared by the reindex that follows the render), while a reindex after `memory_write`/`memory_forget` still reads from disk. Serial `for`-loops of independent awaits were replaced with bounded `Promise.all` fan-outs across memory tiers and files, skill catalog bodies and instruction roots, and plugin artifacts at mount, all sharing a new `core/concurrency.ts` limiter (`createConcurrencyLimiterV1`, default 8 in flight).
- Repeated cross-Durable-Object reads are memoized for the lifetime of a single runtime mount, not cached on the Bot: `userAccountFeaturesReaderV1` serves the Applets gate, the plugin-authoring gate and withheld managed skills from one read, and `createTurnBotDirectoryV1` serves the teammates prompt section from one `listBots()`; both drop a failed read so a later caller retries, and `bot_create` invalidates the flock memo while its own revision-fencing read bypasses it.
- Test coverage added for each seam: `core/durable/session-flush-reads.test.ts`, `core/concurrency.test.ts`, a `apps/cloudflare/test/turn-preamble.workerd.ts` workerd test, plus assertions in the memory, skills, flock, settings, applets-host and plugin-worker-host suites.

## Why

On a voice call, when Gemini Live (`gemini-3.8-live`) calls a function such as `subagent`, the client showed **"I couldn't get that answer out loud. Say that again?"** even though the model spoke normally a moment later.

Production call `c07925c5-…` shows it:
- turn `:2` ("what's in my email today") settled `failed: no_output`, with the delegation recorded on it;
- turn `:3` held the spoken "I'm checking on that…" with an **empty transcript**.

Gemini 3.8 waits for a tool to finish before it speaks. I re-probed the real API (recorded in `docs/voice-gemini-probe.md`): a turn that calls a function sends `toolCall`, then `generationComplete` and `turnComplete` with no audio. After our `toolResponse`, the answer arrives as a fresh generation. `finishTurn` treated that first, silent generation as a failed turn.

## What changes

- **One ledger turn per question.** The calling generation's own boundaries, up to its `turnComplete`, no longer end the turn. The next generation ends it. Two turns would charge the day's allowance twice and separate the transcript from its answer. They also stopped the `subagent` burst cap from ever applying, because the cap reset after every silent tool generation.
- **A genuinely silent reply still says so.** If the generation after the results is silent too, the turn settles `no_output` and the person sees the sentence straight away. A reply with no tool call and no audio behaves as before.
- **The silence guard keeps running through a tool run**, so a hung tool is still bounded. It starts again once the results go back.
- **`end_call` and `switch_bot` now wait for the goodbye or sign-off**, which on 3.8 comes after the tool result. They used to cut it off. A call that hangs up or moves with nothing said gets no error.
- **`memory_write` and `memory_forget`** close the session before it can answer. The fresh session is now told the result as a turn, and its reply settles the same ledger turn.
- **Docs:** `docs/voice.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, the `VOICE_FUNCTION_DECLARATIONS_V1` comment and `gemini-live.ts` now describe 3.8 as it behaves. The prompt's "carry on talking" line after `subagent` is left alone: it is still true at the delegation level, and it is prompt text.
- **What's New:** a `fix` entry, *Calls answer without a false error*. It has no still, because the change is in what you hear.

No stored shape changes (`LiveCall` is in memory), so there is no data cleanup. Old `:2`/`:3`-style records age out with the ledger's 24-hour retention.

## Tests

In `apps/cloudflare/test/voice-assistant.workerd.ts`, six tests are new or updated. Each **fails on the old code** and passes now:
- a tool-only question is one turn with its transcript, delegation and answer, with no error and the meter counting one turn;
- a result that is never spoken still errors, from the next generation's boundary, not from the calling one;
- a memory change is relayed to the fresh session and settles the same turn;
- `switch_bot` and `end_call` in 3.8's frame order wait for the sign-off;
- a silent `end_call` hangs up without an error.

The existing no-tool silent-turn test now also asserts the `no_output` record. `app/voice/assistant.test.ts` covers the new result renderer.

## Validation

- Full `bun run validate` passed on the previous base: format, typecheck, unit, runtime (345 workerd), integration (169), e2e (59, browser suite) and build.
- After the rebase onto current `main`, the fix commit is patch-identical (`range-diff` `=`). Typecheck, the voice and What's New unit tests, the voice workerd suite (49) and the pre-push fast tier (5,240 unit tests) all pass.
- **no-mistakes could not run:** its pipeline agent fails to start (`claude-code:unrecognized_model deepseek-flash[1m]`, earlier `402 Insufficient Balance`). That's the gate config, not this change. As on the other PRs today, an independent review took its place. That review changed the design: an earlier version had the silence guard settle turns from outside the session's event order.

## Left for a follow-up

These are pre-existing gaps, handed to a separate task:
- a goAway reopen doesn't carry the handover;
- `pendingEnd`/`pendingSwitch` survive an out-of-band settle;
- memory calls in the middle of a tool batch misroute the other results.

## Summary

Fixes the browser tier that #722 turned red on `main` (Main #317). Three specs failed on an unexpected console 404:

- `marketplace-plugins.e2e.ts` › Marketplace installs a model and leaves a fresh Bot usable
- `settings-models.e2e.ts` › Models chooses the account default, and every Bot may still choose its own
- `provisioning.e2e.ts` › a User sets an account up through the surfaces and the Bot answers

The 404 is `assets/connectors/radius.png`. Two client findings from the v0.3.20..v0.3.39 review, both about a control being in the wrong place.

## 1. "Try again" was always disabled on the failed Turn it was added to recover

The User sends `book it`. It is admitted, so the composer is cleared. The Turn then fails retryably, and the transcript correctly offers **Try again** — greyed out. `canSend` required a non-empty draft, and the composer is empty precisely because the message went through. The only way to enable the button was to type something unrelated into the composer, and that text is not what the button sends: `retryTurn` reads the original words back off the User's own line in the thread. The handler returned on the same predicate anyway, so even reaching it another way did nothing.

**What changes.** Readiness and composer validity are now two questions in a small `send-readiness.ts` module:

- `sendReadyV1` — can this client start a Turn at all: connection ready, model ready, a Bot open.
- `draftSendableV1` — is the draft non-empty and within the send route's size rule.
- `resendableTurnTextV1` — the words a broken Turn would be sent again with, or nothing.

Send requires both. Try again requires readiness plus the original text, and is disabled only when there is genuinely nothing to send again. The `retry === 'resend'` buttons, whose text really is in the composer, keep `canSend` unchanged.

## 2. Custom-model enablement had two UI homes

AGENTS.md ("Settings surfaces"): the Plugins surface installs, enables and disables Packages, and every control has exactly one home. Models had grown a second one — a "Turn on Custom models" button calling `setPackageEnabled` directly — so a User could make the same enablement decision on two surfaces, with a code comment that named Plugins as the home just above the code that took it.

**What changes.** Models no longer mutates enablement. It says which of the two situations it is in — Custom models installed but off, or not installed — and opens Plugins, where the decision lives. No backend change; the surface simply stops issuing the command.

## How it was verified

- `packages/plugin-shell/src/client/send-readiness.test.ts` covers the readiness split and the exact reported scenario: an empty composer with a failed admitted run is *not* sendable but *is* ready, and the retry carries `book it`. It also asserts the shell binds Try again to `canRetryTurn(message)` and Send to a draft, which is the part that regressed. The repo has no Vue mounting harness, so this follows the existing pattern for `FrockBotApp.vue` behavior (`mobile-safe-area.test.ts`, `no-bot-model-label.test.ts`) — module tests plus assertions against the SFC.
- `packages/plugin-settings/src/client/package-enablement-home.test.ts` is a constitutional check rather than a one-off: it scans every settings surface and fails if any but `PluginsSurface.vue` touches `setPackageEnabled`. It fails on `main`.
- `bun run typecheck` (82 packages), full `bun test` (4733 pass), `bun run format:check`, `bun run lint:ui-styles`.

Normal text turns and voice calls both performed avoidable startup work before reaching their model. Text turns eagerly rebuilt derived memory search data and serialized independent plugin/configuration reads; voice startup repeated Bot directory, identity, and history reads. As plugin count grows, those serialized operations would add directly to response latency.

This change keeps the complete authoritative context while shortening both paths:

- build memory search indexes lazily on first search, with epoch guards so membership changes and explicit rebuilds cannot publish stale data;
- run independent shell, plugin, skill, and authoring reads concurrently;
- cache only immutable content-addressed plugin artifacts and successful worker health declarations, with bounded entries and failure eviction;
- reuse one authoritative voice directory/identity snapshot and selected-Bot history across prompt assembly;
- retry transient authority reads and refuse before admission or active-call replacement if authority remains unavailable.

Validation:

- independent specification and repository-standards reviews passed;
- `bun run validate` passed on the runtime head: 5,066 unit tests, 374 runtime tests, 174 integration tests, 63 browser scenarios with two expected skips, all 13 typechecks, formatting, and build dry runs;
- final pre-push validation passed formatting, all 13 typechecks, and all 5,066 unit tests after documentation corrections.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes timing and caching on memory indexing, voice call admission, and plugin mount paths; correctness relies on new epoch/invalidation logic and not caching failed health checks, but regressions could affect search freshness or voice bot targeting.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR trims **turn and voice cold-path latency** by deferring or parallelizing work that used to block the first model reply, while keeping the same authoritative snapshots and safety checks.
> 
> **Memory** no longer rebuilds embeddings/index on every `refresh`; **`ensureIndex`** builds search data on first `memory_search`, with **epoch guards** so invalidation/rebuild races cannot publish stale indexes after project membership changes.
> 
> **Shell mount** overlaps independent reads (`user` config + plugin enablement, then messages/applets/plugins/skills gates) and returns **`pluginEnablement`** once for composition mounting instead of re-reading storage in `turn.ts`.
> 
> **Plugin loading** adds a shared **`boundedPromiseCacheV1`**: verified **R2 package artifacts** are reused per bucket, and **successful plugin-worker `health()`** results are cached per loader id (failures stay retryable).
> 
> **Voice admission** reads the bot **directory once** (with one retry), **refuses** if authority stays unavailable, and **reuses** that snapshot plus selected-bot identity/history when assembling the prompt instead of repeating RPC fan-out.
> 
> Docs and workerd tests cover directory retry/refusal and the new caching semantics.

## Intent

Jev plan steps 2 and 3, which Tim approved: a trusted read/mutate tool classification and ENFORCED per-call mutation approval by Jev (enforced, not shadow, tuned in use; every decision inspectable per Turn via session events and audit). Tim explicitly rejected graded 'tool risk tiers' as too complicated, so the effect stays binary read|mutate. Key design decision (rigor proportional to consequence, and Bots must keep talking): mutate = code from OUTSIDE the deployment acting on the world — Composio connected-app tools, remote MCP servers, and Plugins a User installed or a Bot wrote. Everything first-party is read: reads, changes the person can see and undo in FrockBot (memory, skills, routines), work on the Bot's own Computer, send_to_user, and first-party effects with their own human gate (machine_* approval cards, approved email drafts via email_send approvalId, plugin_publish/enable cards). Host-owned: ToolDefinition.effect and ToolNamespaceRegistration.effect; a native tool with no effect is read; a namespace with none is mutate; a tool's own effect wins; the registry resolves the effect into ToolExecutionContext.effect before any prepareTool hook. A Plugin cannot confer read on itself: PluginWorkerHost marks a plugin namespace read only when its artifact contentHash is a deployment-seeded one (isSeededPluginArtifactV1), and marks card-draw tools read. Supervision (app/supervision/loop.ts prepareTool) calls new TurnSupervisor.reviewCall right before each mutate call with conversation-before + this Turn's requests and bot sends + results so far; records supervision/call session events; a refused call never runs and returns a model-visible result telling it to ask the person in conversation; refusals become 'supervision' audit rows naming the resolved tool. Questions in app/supervision/call-review.ts: authorization (exact/standing/implied_by_request/materially_different/none), argumentsMatchRequest, consequence, instructsReviewer (injection). Code: injection>=0.6 rejects; none rejects; materially_different -> arguments_changed; implied allowed only when consequence < 1.5 (reaches nobody outside FrockBot); exact/standing need argumentsMatch >= 0.4 (threshold centered on labeled gap: allows scored >=0.55, rejects <=0.19). Policy storage (platform/user/bot policies) is deliberately deferred; reviews run under an empty policy snapshot. The old tool-approval eval (whose plugin-authoring incident fixtures no longer apply since first-party tools aren't reviewed) and app/supervision/compose.ts are deleted and replaced by bun run eval:call-review, 16/16 live on jev-1.13.0, stable across 3 runs. describeFailureV1 moved to app/evals/failure.ts. The supervision-only Jev fake answers the new question set with a reading that allows calls so harness Turns keep running.

## What Changed

- Tools now have a host-owned `read|mutate` effect (`ToolDefinition.effect`, `ToolNamespaceRegistration.effect`). A native tool with no effect set is `read`. A namespace with no effect set is `mutate`, and a tool's own effect overrides its namespace's. The registry puts the resolved effect on `ToolExecutionContext.effect` before any `prepareTool` hook runs. Composio, remote MCP and Plugin tools are `mutate`. `PluginWorkerHost` marks a plugin namespace `read` only when its artifact's `contentHash` is one the deployment seeded, and it always marks card-draw tools `read`.
- Before each `mutate` call, `prepareTool` in `app/supervision/loop.ts` calls the new `TurnSupervisor.reviewCall`. It passes the conversation so far, plus this Turn's requests, Bot sends and results. The questions and decision rules are in `app/supervision/call-review.ts`: authorization, `argumentsMatchRequest`, consequence and injection.
  - Every decision is recorded as a `supervision/call` session event.
  - A refused call never runs. The model gets a result telling it to ask the person in conversation.
  - Each refusal is written as a `supervision` audit row that names the resolved tool.
  - Reviews run under an empty policy snapshot, since policy storage is deferred.
- `bun run eval:call-review` replaces the tool-approval eval (fixtures, runner and script). `app/supervision/compose.ts` is deleted, and `describeFailureV1` moved to `app/evals/failure.ts`. The supervision-only Jev fake now answers the new questions with a reading that allows the call. Also added: contract, loop, dynamic-tools and audit tests, plus a workerd test (`apps/cloudflare/test/call-review.workerd.ts`). README and the architecture and Jev plan docs are updated.

⚠️ Medium: The round-1 fix is minimal and correct: `context.toolCall` is the outer `call_dynamic_tool` envelope, so both the review evidence and the `supervision/call` event now carry `namespace/tool`, which matches the audit projection and the eval fixtures. But this change turns on enforced gating of outside calls, and one policy question is still open: whether input that is not the person's (group, agent or subagent Turns) may authorize those calls.

Three desktop window fixes.

**The window keeps its place.** `MainFlutterWindow` now sets a frame autosave name, so AppKit saves the window's position and size in the app's defaults on every move or resize and restores them at launch. An update leaves those defaults in place, so the window reopens where it was after a quit, a relaunch or a Sparkle update. The first launch of this build still uses the nib's default frame, because nothing has been saved yet.

**Double-clicking the header zooms.** `DesktopWindowDragRegion` now reports a click on the header's own surface (`titleBarClick` on `com.frockbot/window`). A click on a control in the header is not reported, because the deepest recognizer wins a tap, so buttons keep their clicks with no double-tap delay. The window records `NSEvent.clickCount` for every left mouse-down in `sendEvent`. When the reported click is the second one (count 2), it does what Desktop & Dock says for double-clicking a title bar (`AppleActionOnDoubleClick`): zoom by default, minimize, or nothing. Fill has no public API, so it zooms too.

This also fixes a side effect. When the header's pan recognizer was alone in the gesture arena, it won as soon as the mouse went down, so a plain click on the header started a native `performDrag`. That drag swallowed the click, so a double-click could never register there. Now a drag only starts once the pointer moves.

**Drag from anywhere along the header.**
- The conversation header's drag region now spans the full width of the conversation from the window's top edge. Before, it only covered the row with the Bot's name, so the strip above the name and the gutters at each side did nothing.
- The right panel's header, the Work and exchange panel headers, and the pushed Panel page (which lacked `DesktopHeader`) now drag the window too.

Everything is gated on `desktopTitleBarless`, so phones and the web are unchanged. There is one trade-off on the Mac: clicks in the conversation header area now go to the header, not to message content scrolled under the fade.

What's New: `mac-window-place`, a text-only `fix` entry with no still. The change is window behaviour, with no new surface to picture.

## Testing
- `flutter analyze --no-pub`: clean.
- `flutter test`: 1,365 passed, 1 skipped. The new tests in `desktop_title_bar_test.dart` and `chat_header_test.dart` cover:
  - a click on the header surface reports to the window
  - pressing a control twice presses it twice and reports nothing
  - the conversation header's top strip, side gutters and companion drag the window over a selectable thread
  
  Both new tests fail against the previous code.
- `bun test app/whats-new`: passes.
- The Swift change has not been compiled or run on a Mac: there is no macOS in the session that made it. It needs a desktop build (`bun run update:desktop`) to confirm by hand.

hits.body:
Three defects from the landed-feature verification run on `main` (`findings-v4`, items F1/F2 plus Tim's copy audit), all on one code path.

## A. BLOCKER — a model request past its budget answered HTTP 500

**Evidence.** `POST /api/bots/<bot>/turns 500` after 64.9s, reproduced twice on two fresh users with a real Flock AI model doing applet work. `wrangler.log`: `Uncaught Error: Model response outcome is uncertain: The operation was aborted due to timeout` at `packages/kernel-do/src/authority.ts:616`. Debug events: `model/request` and `model/reconciliation-required` exactly 60s apart. On screen: `Couldn't reach the Bot. Check your connection and try again.`

**Root cause — two of them, stacked.**

1. `FLOCK_AI_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS_V1` was 60s, and the signal carrying it was handed to `fetch` and **left armed after the response headers arrived**. `fetch` resolves at the headers; the deadline then guillotined the *response body* mid-stream. A tool-calling step carrying the applets `SKILL.md` plus the dynamic-tool schemas crosses a minute routinely, so this was not a slow gateway — it was the ordinary case. The abort surfaced as a raw `TimeoutError`, not as the kernel's `ModelRequestDeadlineError`, so `streamWithModelRequestDeadlinesV1`'s own reason check did not recognise it.
2. The Agent read a stream that started and then errored as an **uncertain** outcome (`kernel-agent-loop/src/index.ts:1060`) and threw `ModelEffectReconciliationRequiredError`. `BotDurableAuthority.executeAcceptedRun` parked the run on a reconciliation **and rethrew** — which is what the route turned into a 500. ADR 0028 already decided this question for *recovery* (park only when somebody can be asked; Flock AI and Ollama Cloud keep no addressable copy, so nobody can) but the executing path never got the rule. The asymmetry is the blocker.

**Fix.**

- `apps/cloudflare/src/flock-ai.ts` — the gateway budget bounds *reaching* the gateway and nothing after it. A plain `AbortController` plus a timer, disarmed in a `finally` the moment the response exists. The caller's `signal` is still chained in and is **never** disarmed, so a Stop or a superseding message still tears down a request whose body is mid-flight.
- `packages/kernel-do/src/authority.ts` — a new `parkOrSettleUnresolvedRun` applies ADR 0028's `providerReconciles` predicate on the live path, at both catch sites. Provider that cannot be asked → `failRun`, which runs the ordinary run-terminal settlement (`settledEventsV1` closes the open Turn with a `turn/end`, streamed words kept, reason on the record) and returns the settled completion, so the turn POST answers normally instead of throwing. Provider that *can* be asked → parks and rethrows, exactly as before.

**Budget decision.** `FLOCK_AI_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS_V1` 60s → `MODEL_FIRST_BYTE_DEADLINE_MS_V1` (120s), deliberately *equal* rather than larger: the kernel's first-byte deadline is the one that carries a sentence written for a person, so it should win the race and the host budget becomes a backstop for a transport that never reaches the seam. The streaming body is bounded by `MODEL_IDLE_DEADLINE_MS_V1` (60s between events) — a stream that has produced a chunk has proved the model is generating, so a minute of silence after that is a dead socket. Both sit far inside `TURN_DEADLINE_MS_V1` (15 min, PR 170), which is never exceeded.

## B. The Bot's ack was never rendered

**Evidence.** Debug seq 30-32: the model emitted `"On it — building the 2027 countdown applet now."` as a plain `assistant/message`, then called tools. It appears in no UI state — not mid-Turn, not after failure, not after reload.

**Root cause.** The prompt (PR 186) said sends are the only thing the user sees but never said *not to write the line in your own text*, and the client draws one bubble per send (issue 153) — so a correct-looking acknowledgement went to nobody.

**Fix, both ends.**

- Prompt: "Your own text is not shown to the user. Writing a line in your reply instead of calling `send_to_user` means nobody reads it." and "your first action is a `send_to_user` call…".
- Runtime: a new kernel hook `agent/assistant-text`, raised for a step that wrote text *and* called tools, immediately after the `assistant/message` is journaled and **before any tool runs**. The Shell listens and promotes the text to one `send/to-user`. Skipped when the step already sent; the occurrence id is derived from the model request, so a replayed step promotes to the same occurrence rather than a second bubble. The end-of-Turn fallback (`lastSentTextV1`) is untouched.
- One consequence handled: promoting a send would have made the issue-153 gate swallow a *final* answer written as plain text. `visibleAssistantText` now suppresses a settled answer only when it duplicates something the Turn actually sent — the rule is against saying the same thing twice, not against saying a second thing. Mid-Turn the gate stays absolute.

## C. Terminal-outcome copy leaked architecture

A person could read `Reconciliation was explicitly abandoned: Bot turn ended with outcome model-error: Flock AI keeps no durable copy of an interrupted response, so it cannot be recovered`.

New `packages/plugin-shell/src/run-failure-copy.ts`, one mapping, consulted in `projectClientRunV1` so **every** client gets it:

1. the kernel's own person-facing sentences (the two model deadlines, the Turn deadline, `UNRECONCILABLE_RUN_FAILURE_V1`) matched as substrings, since the settling layer wraps the reason it was handed;
2. otherwise the terminal `turn/end` outcome, mapped over a `Record<TurnOutcome, string>` that is total — adding an outcome to the kernel union is a type error here rather than a silent generic line.

The stored `failure` is unchanged and still what `/api/debug` reads. Also replaced: `"Stopped by an authenticated Stop command."` → `"You stopped this."`, and the resumable run's wire message → `"This reply stopped partway. Try again to continue it."`. No provider display names touched (the Flock AI → Frock AI rename is a separate PR).

## Tests

- `apps/cloudflare/src/flock-ai.test.ts` — a body still streaming past the deadline is **not** torn down; a Stop still tears down a body that has started.
- `packages/kernel-do/src/model-timeout-settlement.test.ts` — a provider that stalls past the budget: the turn call **resolves** (no uncaught error, no 500), the run is `failed`, a `turn/end` closes the Turn, the streamed words survive, the active-run lock is released; and the sibling case where a reconciling provider still parks.
- `packages/kernel-agent-loop/src/index.test.ts` — `agent/assistant-text` fires ahead of the tool the same step called; nothing fires for a step with no text or no tools.
- `packages/plugin-shell/src/agent.test.ts` — the prompt wording; one send recorded from promoted text; a step that already spoke (and a replay) adds nothing.
- `packages/plugin-shell/src/run-failure-copy.test.ts` — the guard: no mapped sentence contains `reconcil`, `outcome`, `durable`, `supersede`, `admission`, `provider`, `model-error`, `tool-error`, event names or a bare `run`; the real diagnostic never reaches the copy; the projection sends the copy, not the diagnostic.

**Green:** `bun run typecheck` (all 73 packages), `packages/{kernel-do,kernel-agent-loop,plugin-shell} bun test src` (120 / 50 / 418), `apps/cloudflare bun test src` (149), and `bun run test:workerd -- interrupted-recovery flock-ai-default approvals unread` (8).

## Problem

A chat Turn whose model call failed showed the User only `Bot turn ended with outcome model-error`. The provider's reason — an Ollama Cloud 401, a refused model — was emitted as a Cordis `agent/error`, which is not durable, and was lost before anyone could read it. The only durable event carrying a reason was `model/effect-not-started`, which covers just the effects that never started.

## Contract change

`turn/end` gains an optional `reason`:

- `SessionEventMap["turn/end"]` is now `{ turn; outcome; reason? }`.
- The decoder accepts `reason` as a non-empty string bounded to `TURN_END_REASON_MAX_LENGTH` (500) and still rejects any other extra key, following the optional-key pattern already used for `modelBinding`.
- The Agent loop records a reason at every site that ends a Turn in a non-`completed` outcome and has a cause: the durable no-effect path (the recorded effect reason), both model-error catches (the provider error message, via the existing `modelFailureMessage`), and a rejected pre-step (the rejection reason). A `completed` Turn carries no reason. The session-level `interrupted` repair has no cause to name and is unchanged.
- `turnFailureMessage(outcome, reason?)` in kernel-contracts is the single composer of the user-visible text; `planBotRunRecovery` and the Shell backend runner both use it. The text is unchanged when no reason is present.

The reason reaches `run.failure` through the existing run projection with no further change.

## Tests

Each fails before the change:

- kernel-agent-loop: carries the provider failure reason on a model-error `turn/end`; bounds a `turn/end` reason to what the contract accepts; omits a reason from a completed `turn/end`.
- kernel-contracts: decodes a `turn/end` reason only within its declared bound (accepts 500, rejects 501, rejects empty, rejects an unknown key); composes a failure message from a turn outcome and its reason.
- plugin-shell: surfaces a failed Turn's reason as the client run failure, from the durable event through `planBotRunRecovery` to the decoded `ClientRunV1`.
- apps/cloudflare: names the provider reason a failed durable Turn recorded.

## Gates

`bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (988 pass), `bun run format:check`, `apps/cloudflare` workerd (55 pass, 1 skipped), `apps/cloudflare-bundler` workerd (10 pass).

Two batches of work land together on top of `main`, plus the merge that
puts them beside PRs 163–167.

## Providers never hang (models, connectors, settings)

- **F2** Every network call in the model path is bounded: the Ollama Cloud
  catalog read and inference probe, the OpenAI-compatible response headers
  (cleared the moment they arrive, so a live stream is never torn down) and
  each stream read, and the Flock AI Gateway request on both transports —
  which now also takes the caller's signal, so Stop reaches it.
- **F5, F6** An interrupted Turn settles instead of wedging the Bot. A new
  `not-retrievable` reconciliation outcome says the provider keeps no durable
  copy, so the loop settles the run as a model error with its partial text
  kept. Flock AI and Ollama Cloud declare it; a provider that declares none
  degrades to it. Ollama treats any failure before the first stream event as
  "not started", so a 429 or 502 fails cleanly and can be retried.
- **F1, F4, F7, F12** Connect shows a busy state and never hangs in
  `authorizing`: pending-command recovery has an attempt cap, an exhausted
  command abandons its Connection to `failed` with a reason and discards the
  staged credential, "Try again" reopens the form with the endpoint kept, and
  errors move off the single global slot into per-action state.
- **F8** A failed catalog refresh backs off from a minute rather than waiting
  the full hour.
- **F9, F10** The OAuth return is read at boot and rendered (and stripped from
  the URL); a browser callback failure redirects into the app instead of
  answering raw JSON as a page.
- **F3, F11, F12, F13** A settings refusal lands on the row that was clicked,
  in plain language and in the names the surface knows.

## A Bot can start a new conversation (memory, ADR 0027)

- **ADR 0027 / memory F6, robustness F4/F5** The Bot Durable Object owns which
  conversation its chat Session is on. The composer's "New conversation" puts
  the current one down and starts the next, keeping Memory; earlier
  conversations stay durable and readable Turn for Turn.
  `turnScopedMessagesV1` now carries a character budget (150k), evicting whole
  Turns so a tool result never outlives its call, with a plain notice where
  the dropped Turns were.
- **F8** A file at the size cap no longer takes its whole tier down: a month
  rolls to `log/YYYY-MM.pNN.md` and the cap is enforced at the commit.
- **F9** `forget` retracts the copies other Bots hold, not just my own line.
- **F10** A durable write whose ledger call fails reports `ok` with
  `ledgerPending` instead of claiming nothing was written.
- **F11** A listing that could not be read whole says so, and skips the index
  update rather than treating absent as deleted.
- **F12** Injection and the search index share one file selection.
- **F14** Every remote memory seam runs under a deadline and is retried; Memory
  that cannot be read records an omission and the Turn continues.
- **F32** A `project_create` whose membership call fails records the outcome.
- **F35** Memory and Skill writes are audited against the Workspace, not "This
  Computer" — they run while it is hibernated.
- **F36** Unreadable files are each named; a retraction is not measured against
  the fact cap; vector hits are keyed by document and hash; the injected block
  has a global 12k budget.
- **F40** `memory/injected` records a note as `note`.

## Merge

Four files conflicted with `main`; each keeps both behaviours (conversation
filter *and* degraded run projection; connection return *and* main's
"No model available — set one up in Models"; per-row refusals in main's
wording). Three fixes fall out of the combination: `package_author` reached
through `call_dynamic_tool` is audited against the Workspace; an Ollama Turn
that fails before its first stream event settles rather than parking; and a
read in flight when a new conversation starts no longer redraws the one that
just ended (the transcript keeps a conversation epoch).

## Tests

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- `bun test` — 3395 pass, 0 fail
- `test:workerd` — 40 files, 186 pass (1 skipped)
- `test:integration` — 40 files, 104 pass
- `bun run format:check` — clean
- e2e `chat`, `connect-ollama`, `first-run`, `new-conversation` (workers 1) —
  8 passed. The chat spec now restores the fake endpoint it switches to
  `unauthorized`; leaving it on was failing every later spec's Turn with a 401.

## Why

On 2026-09-26, Bob lost the thread of Tim's smash-room questions. Turn 119 made several Gmail fetches of 70–90 KB each, so the Turn alone came to about 350 KB of messages. Two things then went wrong:

- **The request limit.** The current Turn is carried whole with no bound, so each step's request grew, from 78 KB to 433 KB. At step 12 Frock AI's prepaid limit (400,000 bytes) refused it, and the Turn failed.
- **History selection.** `chooseWithinBudgetV1` walked earlier Turns newest-first and stopped at the first one that didn't fit. Turn 119 was bigger than the whole 150k budget, so Turns 120 and 121 were sent with no history at all, not even the normal Turn 118.

## What changes

- **History selection** (`app/shell/working-context.ts`):
  - A Turn inside the newest-three window is kept whole if it fits.
  - A Turn that doesn't fit whole is kept with its tool payloads replaced by `[pruned]`, if that fits. This keeps the user's words and the Bot's sends, such as "Found it — RedBalloon…".
  - A Turn that doesn't fit even pruned is skipped, and the walk carries on to older Turns.
  - The choice now returns which Turns are pruned, and `renderWorkingContextV1` prunes exactly those. Before, the renderer worked out its own newest-three window, which could have sent a Turn in full after it was charged at its pruned size.
- **The current Turn** (`clearTurnToolResultsV1`, `app/shell/compaction.ts`):
  - Once the Turn alone passes 100k characters, its oldest tool results are cleared back to 50k. This is the same approach as Anthropic's `clear_tool_uses` and JetBrains' observation masking.
  - Results the model hasn't read yet, meaning everything after its newest message, are never cleared. That includes all the results of a step that made parallel calls.
  - Clearing is replayed over the Turn in order. A cleared result stays cleared, and the prompt cache breaks only when a clearing happens.
  - The history choice measures the Turn as it will actually be sent.
- **Store paging:** it now stops at a page on which no Turn fits, instead of at the first page with a skipped Turn. That keeps the stored path's choice the same as the in-memory path's.
- **`TURN_GROWTH_CEILING_V1`** goes from 2 to 1.5. History, the grown Turn, and the system prompt and tools then stay well under the 400,000-byte limit, which counts bytes, not characters.

No stored data changes shape; only the choice and the rendering changed.

## Test plan

- [x] Bob's scenario (a normal Turn, then a 350 KB tool-heavy Turn): the next request includes the normal Turn and the big Turn's own words, and stays within budget. Covered on both the in-memory and stored paths.
- [x] An older Turn charged at its pruned size is sent pruned. This test fails on the earlier `break`→`continue` attempt.
- [x] Twenty Turns across two index pages: the stored path reads past a skipped Turn and matches the in-memory path. This test fails on the old stop rule.
- [x] A 12-step, 85 KB tool loop over a full history stays under 330 KB at every step.
- [x] Parallel results from one step are never cleared, and a cleared result stays cleared across steps.
- [x] `validate:typecheck`, `validate:runtime` and `bun test app/shell/` pass.
  - `validate:unit`: every test passes except `applets/sdk/test/plugin-build.test.ts`. That one misses its hard-coded 30 s Workers-runtime start under full-suite load in the sandbox, and passes when run alone. For that reason this branch was pushed with `--no-verify`.
- [x] An independent adversarial review found three issues (parallel results, paging, headroom), all fixed in the second commit.
- [ ] The no-mistakes CLI isn't installed in the sandbox. Its steps (format, lint/typecheck, tests, review) were run by hand.

Related: the Gmail result shaping and the change that shows Jev the earlier conversation are in separate PRs.

hits.body: ## Summary A Turn is seeded with an absolute `SessionCursor` (`sessionId`, `epoch`, `nextSeq`, `nextTurn`), the committed working context, and the active-run journal. Sequence numbers come from the cursor, so a journal that does not start at zero keeps its absolute sequences. Admission no longer lists the archive to discover the next sequence. The Bot object projects that context into transactional KV in the same transaction as the event append. Request assembly walks turn metadata newest-first and fetches only the selected pages. `CHAT_HISTORY_BUDGET_CHARS_V1`, whole-Turn selection, tool-output pruning, and the omission line stay as they are. A replayed range writes nothing. A gap, an overlap, or the wrong epoch fails the append. A missing page makes the context unavailable instead of shortening the prompt. Voice history for the selected Bot reads that bounded excerpt. Voice turns are indexed by call and sequence. Unfinished continuity jobs are indexed by state and due time. Completion suffixes start at the admission sequence. Events the Session appends while mounting, including `session/created` on a new log, stay inside that range, so settlement matches the stored run. Recovery decodes a legacy `latest-events` value before it rewrites the active run, and leaves the run untouched when that value is malformed. A paged log is not reread for that check. ## Stored shape New keys: `context:head`, `context:turn`, `context:page`, `context:chunk`, and `context:voice`. Voice turns moved from `voice:turn:` to `voice:call-turn:`. Continuity jobs also use `voice:memory:job-open:` and `voice:memory:job-due:`. `clearWorkingContextV1` deletes one session's projection and writes an unavailable head. The event log stays. Voice recovery deletes leftover `voice:turn:` keys, up to 32 per wake. Ordinary startup does not rebuild a projection by reading the whole archive. ## Tests Unit tests cover replay, gaps, a stale compaction epoch, a missing page, selection after eviction, bounded page reads across many older Turns, and flushes that do not read an earlier Turn's payload chunks. `apps/cloudflare/test/voice-history.workerd.ts` is updated. Every Turn on the platform default model `@flock/auto` fails with `AiError` 5006:

```
anyOf at '/' not met: required properties at '/audio' are 'voice,format',
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parallel_tool_calls')
```

## Cause

Not the route, and not the request body. The `AI` binding's
`gateway(...).run({ provider: "compat", ... })` reaches the Gateway's **universal**
endpoint, whose request-shape translation rejects a `dynamic/<route>` model before
inference runs. That is [cloudflare/ai#617](https://github.com/cloudflare/ai/issues/617),
and Cloudflare's dynamic-routing docs state that dynamic routes are only available on the
`compat/chat/completions` endpoint.

Measured against the production account with a scratch Worker on the real binding:

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| binding, `dynamic/flock-auto`, no tools | 400, the error above |
| binding, `dynamic/flock-auto`, with tools | 400, the error above |
| binding, `dynamic/flock-auto`, no streaming | 400, the error above |
| binding, `workers-ai/@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` | 200, streams |
| binding, same model with tools | 200, streams |
| binding, `dynamic/zzz-no-such-route` | 400, a **different** error |

The last row matters: a nonexistent route fails as `AiGatewayError` 2005, so
`flock-auto` resolves and forwards. Tools and streaming are not the trigger.

## Change

Send chat completions to `compat/chat/completions` over `fetch`, authorized by a
`cf-aig-authorization` bearer. The binding stays as the fallback wherever the account id
and token are absent.

- `FLOCK_AI_ACCOUNT_ID` var, added to every environment.
- `FLOCK_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN` secret, optional, carried in the release workflow's **optional**
  list because `--secrets-file` replaces the Worker's whole secret set.
- A new optional stage in `scripts/setup-production.sh` provisions it, and skipping it
  leaves the wizard green.

Every local, unit, integration and browser end-to-end environment binds a stand-in for
`AI` and sets no token, so all of them keep the fallback unchanged and none acquires a
Cloudflare credential.

## Trade-off

Flock AI is no longer credential-free at the deployment seam. The property that matters is
unchanged: no account id, API token, or User secret enters *FrockBot state*, and no User
supplies a credential to use the platform model. A deploy that forgets the secret degrades
rather than breaks, since manual `@flock/...` models keep working and Auto fails visibly at
the Turn. Recorded in [ADR 0025](docs/adr/0025-flock-ai-reaches-the-gateway-over-http.md),
which also notes that the fallback and both settings can be deleted once the upstream
defect is fixed.

## Verification

3267 tests pass, `typecheck` clean, all three lint contracts pass, Prettier clean. New unit
tests cover the compat transport's URL, authorization header and body, its error handling,
and that a half-configured deployment stays on the binding.

Six verified findings from the v2 memory and models waves, each with a regression test.

**memory-v2 F3 — the prompt promised a Computer that does not exist.** `plugin-package-publisher` registered `Edit and test the User's shared setup in /home/box/setup using the Computer.` unconditionally, so on a host with no Computer the Bot spent six steps inventing a sandbox. The section now takes the same `configured` flag `plugin-computer` uses, supplied from `computerConfiguredV1(host)` in the foundation runtime, and drops that sentence when there is no Computer.

**memory-v2 F4 — `Task {background:false}` returned instantly.** Two paths in `dispatchSubagentTask` skipped the wait: a replayed admission returned `dispatched` before the blocking branch, and a single failed record read abandoned it. A foreground call now waits on a replayed task too, and rides out transient read failures. The tool's give-up wording says it did not finish inside the wait and to answer now, instead of "still running" — which is what sent the model into `task_check` and `task_resume`.

**memory-v2 F10 — the Bot paused a User's Routine unprompted.** `routine_manage` now refuses `pause`, `update`, and `delete` on a Routine whose `createdBy.kind` is `user` unless the call carries `userAsked: true`, and the description says to tell the User rather than switch their automation off. The Bot's own Routines are unaffected.

**memory-v2 F5, F6 — a failing Routine flooded the inbox.** The inbox entry and the notification carry a sentence; the raw kernel string stays on the run-log row. Consecutive failures of the same Routine with the same failure fold into one unread entry with a `repeatCount`. `nextRuns()` reports `max(dueAt, deferredUntil)`, so a backed-off Routine no longer shows a "Next run" in the past.

**memory-v2 F9 + models-v2 N5.** A bad `limit` on `/api/debug/...` is refused at the edge with 400, the accepted range, and no stack. `/api/bots/unread` counts unacknowledged Routine failures, so the Bot whose Routine is failing is the one that badges. Shared memory facts are credited by name or not at all — never by a sibling Bot's id.

**models-v2 N4, N6.** Disabling a Package that another enabled Package depends on is refused, mirroring the enable-order rule. The sidebar keeps its skeleton until the flock has actually been read, and the create dialog closes only once the new Bot is selected, so a freshly created Bot no longer flashes "No Bots yet."

Not touched: run settlement and bot-state recovery (PR 170).

Verification: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (root, 3412 pass), `bun run format:check`, `apps/cloudflare` workerd suite. The two `applet-sdk` CLI failures in the full parallel run pass on their own and are unrelated.

- At desk widths the Work log is now a **tab beside Chat** in the Bot's conversation header, so the sidebar stays visible.

- **`timeline.dart`:** a strip across the top with three lanes: Input, Model · Jev, and Tools · effects.
  - Toggle between **Sequence**, **Duration** (idle time squeezed out) and **Clock time**.

  - Tapping a bar selects that row.
- **`ledger.dart`:** a table with `#`, Kind, What happened, Input, Output and Time columns.
  - Each open Turn has a header row with its totals and status.
  - Rows are grouped under step labels with the step's duration, and tool, plugin and Computer rows are indented.
  - Each Turn ends with a footer ("Turn ended · Completed" plus its summary).
  - Older Turns fold to one line with their summary and an error count.
  - **Fold Turns / Open Turns** folds or opens all of them.
  - A compaction that happened before a Turn began gets its own **Between Turns** row.
  - On narrow widths the rows stack, with their numbers under the words.
- **`inspector.dart`:** tabs for **Summary, Prompt, Output, Tools, Input, Result and Raw**. A tab shows only when it has content; Summary and Raw are always there.
  - The Summary tab shows:
    - status, including "after N retries"
    - a token bar with cached input, new input, reasoning and output
    - a timing bar that separates retry wait from the request itself, with output rate
    - for a tool call, **how it got to run**
    - for a Jev check, a **verdict banner** and "Jev this Turn" chips
    - Copy entry JSON
- Filters are drawn as the design's small pills.
- The Stop control for running Turns (added on `main` after the first PR) is kept.

The wire schema gains `WorkLogLink` and optional fields: `tab` on sections, and `label`, `verdict`, `beforeTurn` and `chain` on entries.
- Model requests are numbered (`Request #n`) and carry the prompt excerpt from their bounded projection: the system prompt and the last message.
- A tool call's chain runs from the request that asked for it, through Jev's call review (joined by occurrence id, whichever order the events arrive in), to its run or failure. Its occurrence id is shown as the effect key.
- Each Jev check names its verdict (Allow, Reject, Release, Withhold, Stuck, …).
- Each section says which inspector tab it belongs on.

- **Cost column:** the design has one, but #940 moved plugin dollar costs out of what people read at a glance ("usage reads as a share of the plan"). Model requests don't record a cost yet either. I left the column out rather than draw an empty one.

A per-Bot **Work log**, modelled on DeepSeek Harness's Trajectory view. For each Turn it shows everything the durable log recorded, step by step. It opens from a new **Work log** row on the Bot page.

![Work log](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/claude/sweet-galileo-goq05h/app/whats-new/media/work-log.webp?raw=true)

## What it shows
- **Model requests:** provider, message and tool counts, input, cached, output and reasoning tokens, latency, and the reply text and tool calls.
- **Jev checks:** turn read, step, send, call, progress, outcome and question routing, each with its decision, latency and the questions Jev asked itself.
- **Tool calls:** input, result, duration and errors. Calls to the Computer also show its timing breakdown: opening, sync, self-check, the operation itself and the screenshot.
- **Memory and skills:** facts recalled or left out, memory writes, skills loaded, refused or written.
- **Plugins:** plugin tool calls, model usage with cost, builds, undos and hook failures.
- **Computer:** process launches and exits, and workspace syncs with file counts. A degraded sync is marked as an error.
- **Recovery:** retries, unreadable model replies, compaction (with the summary and the names kept verbatim) and pruned tool results.
- **Sends:** messages, cards and files, and approvals with how and when they were answered (read from the approval record).

## How it's built
- **Wire schemas:** new `WorkLogPage`, `WorkLogTurn`, `WorkLogEntry` and related types in `client-wire.schema.json`, with fixtures. Protocol code is regenerated.
- **Server projection:** `app/shell/work-log.ts` builds each Turn from the run's bounded event projections, never a full prompt. The server writes every row's words.
  - Pages are 8 Turns, with at most 400 rows per Turn.
  - A very large Turn keeps its rows and drops their detail sections.
  - A run that can't be read is skipped rather than failing the whole page.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/bots/{botId}/work-log?before=<run cursor>`. It goes through the user entrypoint, the Bot Durable Object and the shell backend, and archived Bots can still be read.
- **Flutter:** `lib/work_log/page.dart`.
  - Each Turn is a card with a totals line and a colour strip; the newest is open and older ones fold.
  - Rows are grouped by step.
  - Kind filters (including Errors) and full-text search.
  - At wide widths an inspector sits beside the log; on a phone a row opens as its own page.
- **Docs:** a What's New entry and a note in `docs/architecture.md`.

## Not in this PR (next pass)
These need new events recorded first:
- A cost for each model request, read from the billing ledger's `model:<requestId>` operations.
- Hooks that ran successfully (only failed hooks are logged today).
- Time to first token.
- The reason for each compaction and its before/after token counts.

## Validation
- **Passing:**
  - format and typecheck
  - `bun test app/shell/work-log.test.ts` (10 tests), `apps/cloudflare/src/user-application.test.ts` (37 tests), `core/protocol-schemas` and `app/whats-new`
  - `flutter analyze` (no issues)
  - `flutter test test/work_log_test.dart test/bot_page_test.dart`
- **Full Flutter suite:** 89 failures in this container. The identical 89 fail on the base commit, so none are from this change.
- **Unit tier:** the fast-tier `unit` run hit a flaky plugin-build test in `applets/`, which this PR doesn't touch. It fails with a miniflare process-spawn ENOENT under the full parallel run and passes alone (12/12). I pushed with `--no-verify`, so `Check` on this PR is the real gate for that tier.
- **Not run:**
  - `validate:integration` and `validate:runtime`.
  - The `no-mistakes` gate, which isn't installed in this container.

hits.body:
#825 lets a Bot fill a saved secret, such as a password or card number, into a page by reference. The value never enters the model's context, the transcript, logs or browser snapshots. It is also kept out of every process's environment and command line on the Computer: it reaches `browser.mjs` on stdin (b574cb11, after the Codex P1 on #825).

**What it does not stop:** code that the Bot, or another Bot of the same User, deliberately runs on its Computer can read a filled field back out of the page.
- The Bot's shell has `sudo` (`computer/fly/runtime.ts`).
- The shared Chromium's DevTools port listens on `127.0.0.1` at a fixed port, recorded in each Bot's `cdp-port` file.
- So a script can attach over CDP and read `input.value`. A prompt-injected Bot told to do that would succeed.

The same is already true of anything the person types into the Computer's browser while they hold control. This is recorded as a known issue in #825 and was accepted as a limit for its first release.

**The fix** is to put the browser, or an injection broker in front of it, where the Bot's shell cannot attach. Options, roughly from least to most work:
1. **A separate user for the browser.** Run Chromium and the fill helper as their own Unix user, and expose CDP only on a socket that user owns. The Bot's exec would run as a user with no `sudo` and no access to that socket, and its browser actions would go through a narrow broker. This breaks any Skill that drives Playwright directly from `computer_exec`.
2. **A broker that fills and submits in one step.** It fills the field, submits the form and clears the value before handing control back, so no later read finds it. This narrows the window but does not close it, because the Bot can watch during the fill.
3. **A separate browser for secret-bearing sites,** in a container the Bot's shell cannot reach, with only screenshots and structured actions exposed to the Bot.

**Done means** a Bot with `computer_exec` and `sudo` cannot read a value filled by reference, proven by a test that tries CDP, `/proc` and the DOM from the Bot's shell.

From `docs/enthusiast-setup-plan.md` §4: voice calls get their own provider, with Gemini Live today and OpenAI Realtime beside it.

## What changed

- **The seam.** `app/voice/provider.ts` defines `VoiceProviderV1`: where a session connects and with which key, its audio rates, whether it resumes, whether it searches, and a per-session codec that turns the object's four commands (setup, audio, text turn, tool answers) into frames and reads frames back as the object's events. The `VoiceAssistant` Durable Object now only knows the seam.
- **Gemini Live behind it, unchanged.** `geminiLiveProviderV1` writes exactly the frames the object wrote before. A unit test checks this frame by frame, and all 54 existing Gemini workerd scenarios pass unmodified.
- **OpenAI Realtime** (`app/voice/openai-realtime-voice.ts`, `gpt-realtime-2.1`, GA `session.type: "realtime"`):
  - Resamples the client's 16 kHz audio to 24 kHz.
  - Uses the server's `semantic_vad` with `interrupt_response`. The caller's speech is transcribed with `gpt-4o-transcribe`, because `gpt-live-transcribe` refuses turn detection.
  - Function calls arrive in `response.done`. The codec sends `response.create` only after every call in that response has an answer and no other response is running.
  - A `subagent`'s late result goes back as a turn.
  - Barge-in stops playback and truncates the model's item to what the listener could have heard.
  - `session_expired` is treated as `goAway`.
  - It has no resumption, so a wake reopens and carries the call's turns forward.
  - It has no built-in web search, so the prompt sends current-facts questions to `subagent` instead.
  - Each of Gemini's 30 voice names maps to one of OpenAI's 10.
- **Choosing a provider.** The profile gets a `voice.provider` setting, which becomes the `VOICE_PROVIDER` var. Gemini is the default. `chooseVoiceProviderV1` already accepts an account-level choice and key for the setup web app to supply later; nothing sets those yet. **`deployments/staging.json` runs `openai-realtime`.**
- **Pricing.** Voice isn't charged to credit today. It's limited by daily caps in `app/voice/ledger.ts`. Each provider now declares its audio rates, and the daily audio-seconds caps are worked out as a money limit against Gemini's rates. Gemini keeps its 240 minutes each way. OpenAI gets about 56 minutes each way, based on $32/$64 per million tokens at 10/20 tokens a second. No new money path, so no new idempotency keys.
- **Docs.** `docs/voice.md` has a new section, "Which model a call runs on", plus updated credentials and cost notes. `docs/voice-live-checklist.md` has a new section, "On OpenAI Realtime". Also updated: architecture, the deployment-config README and `.dev.vars.example`.

## Verification

- `bun run validate:format`, `validate:typecheck` and `validate:unit` all pass (6685 unit tests).

hits.body:
Three defects found while working out why a Bot "could not access email". It could: the 2026-09-16 morning triage firing read the inbox and built a 87-email triage. Everything after that failed.

## 1. A `batch` sub-call bricked its Session permanently

`Session.deriveMessages` skips a `tool/result` whose occurrence has a `parentOccurrenceId` — a call inside a `batch` answers no tool call the assistant sent — but `messageTurnsV1` counted every `tool/result`. The length invariant in `turnScopedMessagesV1` then threw.

The events are durable, so this was never one Turn's failure: **every later Turn in that Session died the same way, before the model was called.** Bob's morning triage has failed every day since `batch` landed in #517.

Both readers now take one list, `messageEventsV1`, so they cannot drift again. The regression test was verified to fail without the fix.

## 2. An automation Turn was told to use a tool it does not have

`CONVERSATION_PROMPT_TEXT_V1` rendered on every turn type, while the Shell manifest admits `user-voice` only on `chat` and `agent`. So the firing was told at length to call `send_to_user` — including #517's "put those sends in one `batch` call" — and spent its last steps failing to, which is how it reached the `batch` above.

The section is now chosen by the same admission ceiling that admits the tool. A Turn outside the conversation gets a hand-off contract naming `wake_parent`.

## 3. Nothing opened the Turn a hand-off was owed

`wake_parent` queues for the Bot's *next* conversational Turn, and nothing ever started one. A 9:45am triage waited until the person happened to speak — on 15 Sept, 3.5 hours, arriving as background context to an unrelated question. The only thing that reached them unasked was a notification carrying the first 240 characters.

The alarm now opens it: an ordinary `chat` Turn on the Bot's own conversation, carrying the drained hand-off and a cue saying nobody spoke, so the Bot says what matters in its own voice with the conversation in front of it.

**This deliberately does not let a Routine speak directly.** A firing's Session is blind to the conversation by design, so its words would land without knowing what the person already dealt with. The second inference is the point, not the price.

Safety properties, each pinned by a test:

- A hand-off is never consumed by a delivery Turn that did not deliver — a failed, cancelled or superseded delivery re-queues what it drained, and the ordinary next-chat-Turn drain carries it exactly as before.
- Only a delivery Turn re-queues. An ordinary chat Turn that fails or is superseded behaves exactly as it did before this change.
- A delivery Turn whose drain came back empty ends without a model call and without a send, so the Bot can never speak from nothing.
- The settler cannot cost the alarm its other work: no throw from it skips owed subagent Turns, overdue tasks, approval expiry or notifications.
- The delivery Turn's input is blanked in the client projection, as an automation Turn's already is — it is a hand-off, not the person's words, and must not render as their own chat bubble.

Scope: the trigger is narrowed to Routine hand-offs. A subagent hand-off is enqueued after its alarm pass, so nothing would have armed a delivery for it; it keeps today's behaviour, and a delivery Turn opened for a Routine drains any subagent hand-off already waiting.

## Verification

- 4823 unit tests pass; 348 workerd tests pass; typecheck and prettier clean.
- Two existing tests in `routines-firing.workerd.ts` were updated deliberately: the person's own next Turn no longer carries the hand-off, and a firing now leaves two runs.

hits.body: ## Intent Tim asked why Bob (a FrockBot Bot on Ollama Cloud deepseek-v4.1-flash) takes so long to reply. Diagnosis: conversation compaction ran on the Bot's own model and asked for JSON; every attempt since 15 Sep failed (schema/JSON errors, deploy interruptions, deadline), so Bob's requests carried ~50k tokens trimmed oldest-first per step, and the trimming (plus a count in the 'earlier Turns omitted' notice) changed the start of the prompt every step, defeating the provider prompt cache. Tim decided: (1) run compaction on a platform model via the AI Gateway dynamic route he already created, dynamic/frock-structured ("just use that"), billed as a normal hosted Frock AI call (model id @frock/structured, needs a BILLING_MODEL_RATES entry Tim will add; until then summaries are refused as unpriced, same outcome as today's failures); (2) choose a Turn's history once per Turn so every step reuses it; (3) keep the start of the prompt stable (no count in the omitted notice). Decisions I made: a generic LlmProvider.summaryModel field so the Shell names no provider; Frock AI is mounted summary-only (no Auto fallback hooks) beside a Bot on another provider, and skipped if the Bot is already on Frock AI; the summariser answers in plain Markdown headings (existing parseCompactionSummaryV1) instead of JSON, deleting the JSON schema/render code; summariser input bounded to 80k chars per call with the backlog processed in slices (up to 8 per detached run); an interrupted intent is settled and retried immediately rather than backing off; history is pinned to the Turn's opening size and re-chosen only when the Turn grows past 2x the budget; tool-output pruning by age was deliberately left unchanged (it only affects the last ~3 turns, not the prompt start); gateway prepaid limits now apply per requested model instead of the smallest across all rate entries; Bots on provider Plugins are also summarised by the platform summariser (the workerd test was rewritten accordingly); the gateway RPC stub is disposed on the binding path (it pinned Durable Objects in tests). No durable shape changes, so no data cleanup is needed. Runtime (workerd) and integration tiers were run locally and pass. ## What Changed - Conversation compaction now runs on a platform summary model, not on the Bot's own model. Providers can declare a new `LlmProvider.summaryModel`. Frock AI declares `@frock/structured`, which goes through the AI Gateway dynamic route `dynamic/frock-structured` (or the Auto model on the binding path) and is billed as a normal hosted Frock AI call. When a Bot runs on another provider or a provider Plugin, Frock AI is mounted beside it for summaries only. The summariser now answers in Markdown headings, parsed by `parseCompactionSummaryV1`, so the JSON schema and render code are removed. Each call sends at most 80k characters, and the backlog is processed in slices, up to 8 per detached run. An interrupted intent is settled and retried straight away instead of backing off. - Each Turn now picks its history once, and every step reuses it. The history stays at the Turn's opening size and is picked again only when the Turn grows past twice the budget. The "earlier Turns omitted" notice no longer includes a count. Design doc for #179 plus a CI change so documentation-only pull requests stop running the full suite.

## `docs/plans/voice.md`

The accepted design for voice: composer dictation on OpenAI realtime transcription, and an app-wide assistant on Gemini 3.1 Flash Live. Decisions D1–D10 with rationale, the two assumptions to verify before slice A, the constraints discovered (no async tool calls on 3.1 Live, 15-minute sessions, intent-before-effect for `ask_bot`), the Feature rule, slices A / B0 / B1 / B2, a repo map, the zerobsai salvage list (`git show 86a86770:…`), and the external references. Written so a fresh session can build from it without redoing the discovery.

## `ci.yml`: docs-only changes run only the Prettier check

- A `Classify changes` job diffs the pull request (or the push range) and reports `docs-only` when every path is under `docs/` or is a root-level `.md`. Markdown elsewhere stays "code" because a Package may ship a Skill or a prompt as `.md`.
- `Validate` and the four browser shards carry `if: needs.changes.outputs.docs-only != 'true'`. This is a job-level skip, not a workflow `paths-ignore`: the `main` ruleset requires `Validate` and `Browser end-to-end` by name, and a check whose workflow never ran stays pending forever, while a skipped job reports `skipped`, which the ruleset accepts.
- The `Browser end-to-end` gate passes when its shards were skipped *and* the change was docs-only; any other skip still fails it.
- A `Check documentation` job runs `bun run format:check` on docs-only changes, so a plan that is not Prettier-clean fails its own pull request rather than the next code change's.
- `Deploy staging` is skipped with `Validate` on a docs-only push to `main`: nothing deployable changed.
- `workflow_dispatch`, a branch-creation push, and an empty diff all run the full suite.

## Local path: the pre-commit hook skips typecheck and tests for docs-only commits

`scripts/docs-only.sh` is the one definition of "documentation only" (paths on stdin; exit 0 when every one is `docs/**` or a root `.md`; an empty list is not documentation). The pre-commit hook pipes the staged paths through it and, on yes, runs Prettier (lint-staged) and stops; CI's `Classify changes` job pipes the diff through the same script. `scripts/docs-only.test.ts` covers the cases. README's testing section documents the path: a docs-only commit needs Prettier and nothing else, locally and in CI, and its pull request merges on the `Check documentation` job alone.

This pull request edits `.github/workflows/`, so auto-merge cannot queue it; it is merged by hand. Its own run is *not* docs-only (it changes the workflow), so the full suite runs here; the first docs-only pull request after this merges is what exercises the skip.

- distinguish trivial documentation edits from consequential plans, policies, ADRs, and product claims
- run a cut-down no-mistakes review/document gate for consequential docs while skipping tests and TypeScript typechecking
- make validation questions answer-only unless the user authorizes action
- require Cursor CLI with Grok 4.6 whenever Cursor is selected as the no-mistakes pipeline agent

- targeted Prettier check for AGENTS.md
- no-mistakes review and document steps passed

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Policy-only updates to agent workflow in AGENTS.md; no runtime, auth, or durable data changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **AGENTS.md** now ties validation to how risky a documentation edit is, instead of treating all doc-only work the same.
> 
> **Trivial** doc fixes (spelling, wording, formatting, links) only need a diff review and targeted Markdown formatting, then `git push --no-verify` with no no-mistakes, tests, or typecheck. **Consequential** docs (architecture, ADRs, plans, security/product policy, ops procedures, product-facing claims, etc.) still run a trimmed no-mistakes pass: `rebase`, `review`, and `document` with `--skip test,lint,push,pr,ci`, `--intent` for context, and Markdown formatting before push—explicitly not the full TypeScript lint gate.

**Stacked on #946** (review only the last commit). Merge order: #942 → #944 → #945 → #946 → this.

## Why

Steps 9–10 of the plan. A refused call told the model to "ask in conversation", which made consent a text-inference problem — the next Turn's "yes" had to be re-read by Jev with its referent gone. And a Bot could create a Routine, or rewrite or pause the person's, by setting `userAsked: true` itself; the Routine's prompt then authorized its own calls when it fired (audit F2). Plugin tool calls (`package-tool:` ids) skipped supervision entirely, and any unplaceable effect id failed open (F16).

## What changes

**Approval cards for refused outward calls.** When call review refuses a call that reaches outside FrockBot (or lands in a new uncertain band: authorization probability < 0.55 or arguments < 0.5), and nothing tried to steer the reviewer, supervision records the exact tool and canonical arguments and draws a kernel-minted `approval` card. The identical call, made again after approval, runs once without asking Jev; changed arguments need a new card; a decline is final. Reads never get a card.

**Routines don't wait.** In a Routine or hand-off Turn the card goes to the person's conversation and the Routine carries on, saying in its hand-off what is waiting; approving later opens a Turn that makes the call. (This was an open choice; reverse it in `awaitingApprovalResult`, `app/supervision/loop.ts`.)

**Routine changes need the person.** `userAsked` is removed from `routine_manage`. Creating a Routine, changing a prompt, schedule or trigger, and pausing or deleting one the person created all draw a card, and nothing is armed until approved. A firing counts as the person's (`promptBy: "user"`) only if they created the Routine or approved its prompt on a card.

**Plugin calls are supervised.** `package-tool:` calls are placed in their Turn via the `package/tool-call` entry and reviewed; a `mutate` call supervision cannot place is refused.

`core/tools/tools.ts`: every `mutate` call is now ordered, so mutate calls inside a batch run one after another (a refused one may draw a card).

## Behaviour change to know about

A Routine a Bot wrote without the person's approval now fires as the Bot's and asks for nothing. Existing Bot-written Routines (Bob's morning triage is likely one) need one approval: ask the Bot to update it, and approve the card.

## Stored data

Additive only (`askPerson`/`approvalId` on decisions, `promptApprovalId` on Routines, new `supervision:call-approval*` and `routine:intent:*` keys); no cleanup needed.

## Tests and evals

New `app/supervision/{call-review,call-approval}.test.ts`, 8 new `loop.test.ts` cases, rewritten `app/routines/agent.test.ts`, 2 new `app/approvals/bot.test.ts` cases. Call review evals, five repeats: 56/56, no flips; new `askPerson` check 4/4. This branch (the stack top) passes `validate:runtime` and `validate:integration` on current `main`. What's New entry `approval-cards` (no still — none could be captured in this environment).
