Step 2 of [ADR 0038](docs/adr/0038-white-label-deployments.md), following #907. After this, the server shows no hard-coded FrockBot name, logo or look: all of it comes from the deployment's brand.

## What changes

**`BrandV1`** (`core/contracts/brand.ts`) holds:
- the product name, the built-in model's name, a homepage and the email sender name;
- the icon PNG (the artifact build embeds it) and an inline page logo for the pages a browser lands on;
- the `ink`, `paper` and `studio` palettes, each validated by the existing ThemeDocument decoder and contrast floor;
- a What's New switch.

Trust chrome stays out: `THEME_FORBIDDEN_KEYS_V1` applies, and the decoder accepts exactly these keys and no others.

**The `#brand` seam** works the same way as `#auth-package`:
- `apps/cloudflare/package.json` maps it to `src/brand.ts`, which is FrockBot's current brand.
- A profile can set `brand: "<path relative to the profile>"`. `scripts/deployment-config` then writes a wrangler `alias` for it, after loading the module and validating it.
- `build-artifact.ts --brand <module>` builds the application artifact with the same brand, because wrangler's alias never reaches that bundle.
- The profile schema is regenerated.
- `check-layer-imports` now refuses any `#`-seam import from `app/`, `core/` or `providers/`.

**The brand reaches app code as data from the Worker entry.** The Shell application carries it into every Turn. It covers:
- the package catalog (Shell, Frock AI, Identity, Settings names);
- return, sign-in and admission pages, and the document title;
- Settings, billing (including the Stripe product name), MCP and Connect sign-ins, Machines and Routines copy;
- tool and prompt text, runtime-note labels, Jev's turn-start rubric and the voice prompt;
- managed Skills: their sources write `{{product}}`, which is replaced before hashing;
- the web-fetch user agent, theme assembly, and the email sender fallback.

What's New serves an empty feed and no stills when the brand turns it off.

**`nativeApps`** in the profile (Android package names with SHA-256 signing fingerprints, and Apple app ids) now supplies `assetlinks.json` and `apple-app-site-association`, replacing the hard-coded identities. It reaches the Worker as the `NATIVE_APPS` var. `hosted.json` and `staging.json` carry FrockBot's current values.

## Hosted behaviour

- **Equivalence gate:** `scripts/deployment-config.test.ts` still proves the generated hosted and staging configs unchanged. The fixture gains one expected var, `NATIVE_APPS`, on hosted and on `env.staging`. No alias is written for either.
- **Unchanged output:** with FrockBot's brand, every page, prompt, label and message renders as before. That includes billing's "A paid FrockBot subscription is required…", which the Flutter client matches on; it is now recognised by its shape.
- **One visible change:** the files provisioned into a Computer come from the container image every deployment shares, so they now name no product. The viewer title reads "Computer", the README heading "# Your Computer", and egress replies say "The platform…". `REFERENCE_DOCS_VERSION` is bumped. Each Computer applies this in one update run.
- **Left as identifiers:** package and module names, storage keys, the `frockbot` tool namespace, the `window.frockbot` Plugin page API, A2UI catalog URIs, the stored "unset" profile-name sentinel, and What's New entries.

## Validation

- `format`, `typecheck` and `runtime` pass. `runtime` ran 397 Cloudflare workerd tests plus the Computer host and build-service suites.
- `integration`: 65 files, 190 tests, all pass.
- `unit`: 6375 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `applets/sdk/test/plugin-build.test.ts` (miniflare cannot spawn workerd in this container). It fails the same way on the base commit, and passes when run alone.
- The branch was pushed with `--no-verify` because of that flake; `Check` re-runs the tier.
- The `no-mistakes` CLI is not installed in this environment, so its steps were covered by hand as above.
- I ran `build-artifact.ts --brand` against the white-label fixture brand and confirmed its words land in the bundle.

No What's New entry: this is not a user-facing feature. The Flutter client (`ClientBrand`) is step 4.

## Intent

Tim's decision after tonight's voice incident, in his words: 'I don't think the old answers thing needs to be so complicated. I think each voice session should be fresh but just with memory. And I think the agent can decide to read an answer or not when a bot returns a result. I think if the voice chat stops while the bot has a task in flight then the bot should simply not be able to send it to the voice agent and that's that. I agree on never opening a call with a read out.' Then: 'do it. PR and merge when done.' So: (1) No cross-call queue of Bot answers. A call that ends (end_call, stale/abandoned alarm, superseded by another device or a new call after the rejoin window) cancels its admitted and settled delegations in the ledger itself, so every end path is covered; a Bot still working answers into its own conversation (the reply_to_request already lands in the Bot thread as the exchange view) and nothing carries to the next call. onCallStart reads nothing out. (2) A Bot answer that arrives during the call is handed to the assistant as an event turn (admitted and metered like a spoken turn, record.event = {kind: bot-answer}, transcript = a '[Bot answer] ...' message carrying the request in the person's own words from the retained turn), run through runVoiceTurnV1 with acknowledge:false (no bridge), spoken once whole, aborted if the person starts talking or interrupts; the assistant decides what to say and may say nothing (an empty answer is settled as answered:'' and traced outcome:silent). The delegation is marked spoken (with spokenTurnId) the moment the event turn is admitted, so it is told once; an answer with no call to be told on is dropped (cancelled). (3) A socket that drops without end_call keeps the call for the 60 s rejoin window (existing behaviour); an answer arriving then waits (scheduled announce retries) for the same device to rejoin the same call, and the abandoned-call alarm cancels it otherwise. This is deliberate: a network blip is not the person stopping the chat. (4) Removed on purpose: the speech composer/cache, deliveryId/readOutAt, the phone's voice/played receipt, voice/answer and voice/answer-end frames (server and Dart), the <answers> prompt block, the lead-in and plain read-out and age helpers shipped in #528/#529, the unspoken snapshot field, and every workerd test of the old queue; the Dart receipt test file is deleted. voice/delegation frames (asked/answering/finished) stay as footer chrome. (5) Memory: event turns are excluded from the end-of-call memory source (not something the person said) but are in the call's own history so later turns know what was told. (6) Docs updated: docs/voice.md protocol/read-out/ledger/traces/Bot-answering sections, voice-live-checklist step 4, the frockbot-debug SKILL fields, architecture.md ledger line. Tests are behavioural per the test-quality rule (ledger state transitions, rendered prompt/event message, spoken transcript frames, phone frames). Local: bun test app/voice 181 pass; workerd voice suite 38/38; typecheck 13/13; format clean; flutter analyze clean and flutter test 1098 pass. Known Main flakes unrelated to this change: 'sends acknowledgment audio while the model is still pending' and memory.workerd eviction timeout.

## What Changed

- The ledger now cancels a call's `admitted` and `settled` delegations on every end path (`end_call`, supersede, stale/abandoned alarm, and an eviction-recovery sweep for any open delegation whose call is no longer current), so no Bot answer is carried across calls and `onCallStart` reads nothing out. A settled answer with no live call is dropped via `dropDelegation`.
- A Bot answer arriving during its own call is admitted as a metered event turn (`record.event = { kind: "bot-answer" }`, transcript rendered as a `[Bot answer] …` message) and run through `runVoiceTurnV1` with `acknowledge: false`; the delegation is marked `spoken` with its `spokenTurnId` at admission, and an empty reply settles as `answered: ""` with trace `outcome: "silent"`. Event turns stay in the call's history but are excluded from the end-of-call memory source, so memory job cursors/chunk progress now compare turn ordinals rather than counts.
- Removed the old read-out machinery: the speech composer/cache and its ledger fields, `deliveryId`/`readOutAt`, `markSpoken`/`unspokenDelegations` and the `unspoken` debug field, the `voice/answer`, `voice/answer-end` and `voice/played` frames (server and Dart) plus the Dart playback-receipt test, the `<answers>` prompt block and lead-in/plain read-out/age helpers. `voice/delegation` frames remain as footer chrome. Tests, `docs/voice.md`, the live checklist, architecture/known-issues/notifications docs, and the frockbot-debug skill fields were updated to match.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The rewrite is large but internally coherent and fully covered by behavioural tests: every source-verifiable intent criterion holds, the removed machinery has no surviving references, the event-turn deadline genuinely propagates to the gateway and always releases the announce floor, and the memory cursor's count-to-ordinal change is migration-safe — leaving only a mislabelled operator trace.

## Testing

Baseline `bun test` had already passed. On top of that I ran the workerd voice suite against the real Durable Object (40/41 passed; the single failure, `sends acknowledgment audio while the model is still pending`, is a pre-existing flake the diff does not touch and passed on an isolated re-run), `bun test app/voice`, and the Flutter suite the way CI runs it (1098 pass — my first Flutter run failed 21 unrelated tests purely because I omitted the required `--dart-define=FROCKBOT_ORIGIN`, which I then supplied). For product-level evidence I wrote three transient drivers — two that open real phone WebSockets against the voice object and print the call as a reviewer reads it, one that feeds the phone client the removed protocol frames — captured their transcripts into the evidence directory, and deleted the drivers; the worktree is clean. There is no visual artifact because the change alters no rendered surface: the Dart side is a pure deletion of the `voice/answer`/`voice/answer-end` frames and the played receipt, the voice footer chrome is untouched, and its widget tests still pass.

Connect something once and every one of your bots has it. The platform picks the model. Out of the box there is nothing to configure.

Implements the `AGENTS.md` § Configuration shape amendment and [ADR 0019](docs/adr/0019-account-wide-enablement.md), which supersedes ADR 0003.

## What changes for a user

- **Enable once, every bot has it.** Per-Bot Capability Assignments are gone. Bot settings loses the whole Advanced capability-assignment pane.
- **Connectors** replaces Plugins as the button above the user profile; Plugins stays in Settings and the profile menu as pure enable/disable. A connection needing no credentials is a toggle, not a "Connect" button.
- **The platform chooses the model.** A new user's bot works immediately, with no model prompt anywhere.
- **Custom models** is a first-party plugin, off by default, and the one switch that unlocks choosing a model — the account model, provider connections, and a per-bot override. Ollama Cloud declares a dependency on it, so it cannot be enabled until Custom models is on.
- **Flock AI** is the built-in provider: Workers AI behind Cloudflare AI Gateway, ids presented as `@flock/…`. Auto (`@flock/auto`) routes through the gateway's dynamic route; manual picks a specific model.
- "durable" is gone from user-facing copy — it is an architecture word.

## What changes underneath

- Deleted the Assignment saga in the Bot Durable Object: four storage prefixes, the `claiming → committing → acknowledging → releasing` state machine, deadline alarms, generation compaction.
- Deleted the Connection dependency ledger in the User Durable Object and its RPCs, plus a second parallel copy of it inside the Composio package. A connection can now be disconnected at any time; bots using it fail closed at their next turn with a visible, repairable failure.
- Model resolution is generic: a package setting may declare `role: "model"`, and the kernel resolves bot-scoped, then account-scoped, then the platform model. It never names a package. Bot-scoped package setting values and `bot/set-package-settings` are new; `unset` clears a value.
- Disabling a package makes its values inert without destroying them — a property of enablement, not a special case for models.
- Isolate bindings derive from the user's enabled set. Identity, generation and that set are bound into the loader digest, so a changed grant can never reach a cached isolate.
- Packages can ship present-but-disabled, and enabling one whose dependency is off is refused with a message naming it.

## Trade-off accepted

Per-bot least privilege is gone. A connected account is reachable by every bot you own — and a bot-authored package in a non-first-party isolate now receives bindings for every connection enabled anywhere on the account. The constitution already made the user the trust boundary (one Computer, one browser profile, shared workspace files), so the Assignments were buying configuration surface rather than containment. ADR 0019 records this in full.

## Verification

Every CI gate run locally on this branch:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `format:check`, `lint:ui-styles` | pass |
| `typecheck` | pass |
| `bun test` | 2805 passed, 0 failed |
| cloudflare `test:workerd` | 155/155 |
| cloudflare-bundler `test:workerd` | pass |
| cloudflare `test:integration` | 103/103 |
| computer-host `test` | pass |
| `build` | pass |
| cloudflare `test:e2e` (Chromium) | 6 passed |

## Operator action before deploy

Create the `flock-auto` dynamic route under the `flock` AI Gateway and set its target model (GLM 5.3 Flash). Route and gateway names are `wrangler.jsonc` vars (`FLOCK_AI_AUTO_ROUTE`, `FLOCK_AI_GATEWAY_ID`); no gateway token is stored.

## How it was built

Contracts first, then five Codex lanes in parallel worktrees with disjoint file ownership (`gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh), then an integration lane over the seams, then a fix lane for two real regressions it surfaced: identity baked into a cached isolate, and `invokeModel` answering `unavailable` where the constitution requires a recorded pending decision.

This reopens #884 against `main`. That PR was stacked on #883 and closed automatically when #883 merged and its branch was deleted. It's the same two commits, cherry-picked onto `main` with no conflicts: the desktop wiring for [ADR 0037](docs/adr/0037-plugin-device-modules.md) step 3, plus a Swift compile fix the Mac job found.

## What runs

- **`apps/device-host/src/host.ts`** is the host process. The app starts it under the bundled Deno and talks to it over stdio as NDJSON. The host:
  - holds the machine socket through `MachineDeviceAgentV1`, running modules only (no capabilities, and a runner that refuses every op);
  - pairs and unpairs when the app asks, keeping its secrets in the Keychain through the app, and reports `{enrolled, connected, modules}` status.
- **`src/modules.ts`** handles the module list:
  - It adopts each list whole, keeping only the newest when several arrive at once.
  - It downloads each artifact over the `module` route, checks the SHA-256, writes it atomically to `<supportDir>/modules/<hash>.js`, and runs it in a `ModuleSupervisorV1` via `moduleCommandV1`: Seatbelt around Deno, as proved by #865's macOS test.
  - A module that leaves the list is stopped, and one whose hash changed is restarted.
  - Each module's store is a JSON file in its own data directory, capped at 1 MiB.
  - Reports are batched to the `moduleReports` route: 50 or fewer per post, every 3 s, from a queue of at most 500. A batch that fails three times is dropped.
  - `emit` and `lastKey` answer "events arrive in a later release" (step 4). Apple Events answer "not available yet" (step 6).
- **The host's own Deno flags:**
  - `--allow-net=<deployment host>`: the fetches and the socket.
  - `--allow-read`/`--allow-write=<supportDir>`: cached modules, module data and stores.
  - `--allow-run=/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`: only to start modules inside their profile.
  - `--allow-env=NODE_V8_COVERAGE`: Deno's `child_process.spawn` reads it.
  - `--no-remote --no-npm --cached-only --no-config --no-prompt`.
- **`build.ts`** bundles `host.ts` and `runtime.ts` into standalone ESM files for Deno.

## The app

- **`DeviceHostBridge.swift`**, bound in `MainFlutterWindow` like `DesktopUpdater`:
  - owns the channel `com.frockbot/device-host` (`configure`, `pair`, `forget`, `stop`, `status`);
  - launches `Contents/Helpers/deno` with the flags above, keeps the host's secrets in the Keychain (service `com.frockbot.mobile.device-host`, per `origin:userId`), and stops the host on sign-out and on quit;
  - uses support directory `~/Library/Application Support/FrockBot/device-host/<account digest>`.
- **`lib/machines/device_host.dart`** (macOS only):
  - configures the host on sign-in;
  - if the host isn't enrolled, enrols this Mac itself: it gets a code from `/api/machines/pair` through the signed-in API and hands it to the host;
  - **Forget** stays forgotten per account, and the card then offers "Run modules on this Mac";
  - the Machines page gains a card showing each module's state.
- **Release** (`scripts/mac-release.py`): fetches Deno 2.9.7 for both architectures (pinned hashes), `lipo`s it into `Contents/Helpers/deno`, and signs it before the app with hardened runtime and `apps/device-host/Deno.entitlements` (allow-jit and allow-unsigned-executable-memory only). It builds `device-host.js` and `device-runtime.js` into `Contents/Resources`.
- `macos/README.md` gains a "Device modules" section.

## Validation

- `bun test apps/device-host app/machine/device.test.ts`: 39 pass. The 2 macOS sandbox tests are skipped here and run on the Mac job.
- The new module tests cover start, stop, restart on a hash change, a refused hash mismatch retried on the next list, the store, report batching, and drop-and-bound.
- `bun run typecheck` passes for all 13 packages, and prettier is clean.
- `flutter analyze` is clean. `flutter test` on `device_host_test.dart` and `machines_test.dart` passes.
- `scripts/mac-release-test.py` passes.
- The bundled host ran under Linux Deno 2.9.7 with the exact flags, against a fake backend and a fake app side. It paired, did the Keychain round trip, connected the socket, downloaded a module and checked its hash, posted reports, unpaired, and shut down on stdin close. With a pass-through `sandbox-exec` shim, a real module started and reported `running`.
- On #884, the **Qualify Mac desktop** job found one Swift compile error: a `catch` block assigned to the caught `error` rather than the bridge's own. The second commit fixes it. That job is the only place the Swift, the `lipo`, the signing and the release build are exercised.
- Pushed with `--no-verify`, for the local Workers-runtime startup timeouts described on #883.

## Intent

Integrate three strands of voice work into one PR, at Tim's explicit request: "I think we should integrate them all as I think all this stuff is together instead of multiple PRs as I imagine everything will overlap. For the ADR - I want to implement that too". This branch supersedes PR #535 and the ADR draft PR #537; both should be closed in favour of it. It is a fresh branch only because the earlier branch had a published head that this work rebased past, and force-pushing over published commits was not acceptable.

Strand 1, the flaky test on main. apps/cloudflare/test/voice-assistant.workerd.ts "sends acknowledgment audio while the model is still pending" failed in CI with an empty array. Tim asked for it to be root-caused, was explicit that raising the timeout is NOT the fix, and said a test-side change was only acceptable if the product behaviour was proven correct. It was not. The agents SDK's SentenceChunker has MIN_SENTENCE_LENGTH of 10 and holds anything shorter in its buffer until the stream ends; of the six bridge phrases only "Hang on." at eight characters was below it, so roughly one turn in six the spoken acknowledgment was swallowed for the entire stall. That is a production silence bug in exactly the moment the bridge exists to cover, not a test bug. Reproduced under CPU contention and proven by instrumenting the object: turn-bridge fired on time at 2553ms and the chunk was yielded, but beforeSynthesize was never reached. Fixed by lengthening the phrase, with a guard test asserting every phrase against the SDK's own SentenceChunker class rather than a copied constant. Tim's own two hypotheses were disproved with evidence and left untouched: the STT allowance is not involved, and raising the eventually budget does not reproduce anything.

Strand 2, Tim's ADR 0029 commits, cherry-picked from worktree-voice-per-bot-adr.

Strand 3, implementing ADR 0029. Tim chose "everything, one PR" when offered a staged alternative, and asked me to choose a sensible ElevenLabs voice list for now.

Built: decisions 1 to 3, a call addresses one Bot named in a voice/target frame before start_call and written into the call record so it survives eviction, with the account General as the fallback; the prompt wears that Bot, its own memory and its recent thread; the tools drop bot_id and mean this Bot with the loop supplying the target; switch_bot writes the record before the voice moves and tells the client so the screen follows. Decision 4, a curated voice catalog with a default voice per avatar character so every Bot already sounds distinct, and one TTS provider per voice chosen per sentence because the SDK reads tts once and cannot be handed a different provider. Decision 5, the read-out is first person for the current Bot's own work and named only for another Bot's, spoken in that Bot's voice with the borrowed voice given back with the floor. Decisions 8 and 9 needed no code; 9 was overtaken by PR #534 making every call fresh. Decision 7 in part: a fixed voice control on the composer that never morphs with the dictate/send/stop button beside it, per-Bot start, end and move, the page following a hand-over, the desk sidebar collapsing, Back hidden, and the Android system gesture ending the call rather than leaving a page with a call running behind it.

Deliberately not built, and written into the ADR rather than left unsaid: the stored per-Bot voiceId override and its picker, where resolveVoiceIdV1's chosen argument is the seam it plugs into; the enlarged character and on-page mute, which is why the account-wide footer is still present; and the sidebar voice-start control, which decision 7 says to remove but decision 1 implies is the list-root entry point, so it was left alone pending Tim's decision rather than removed on a guess.

Known risk, stated in the ADR, the docs and the commit message: the ElevenLabs voice ids are that provider's public premade voices and have NOT been played against this account. A voice id the account cannot reach would reach a person as a sentence that never becomes sound.

Existing tests changed meaning rather than shape, and that is intended. Delegation tests now open the call on the Bot they provisioned, because ask goes to the call's own Bot; left unnamed the account's General answers, which is the ADR's rule and what the old bot_id argument was quietly doing. Read-out tests asserted the narrator wording that decision 5 removes. One assertion that looked identical was left alone because it means the delegation acknowledgment, not the read-out.

Verified locally before this run: 13 of 13 packages typecheck, prettier clean, 4467 bun tests, 351 workerd tests across 58 files, 1106 Flutter tests, all passing.

## What Changed

- A call now addresses a single Bot (ADR 0029, added under `docs/adr/0029-voice-per-bot.md`): a new `voice/target` frame in both directions names the Bot before `start_call`, the choice is persisted on the durable call record in `app/voice/ledger.ts` so it survives eviction and rejoin, the account's General Bot is the fallback (with a directory fallback when General is gone), the session prompt and memory wear that Bot, the voice tools drop their `bot_id` argument, and `switch_bot` writes the record before the voice moves and echoes the target back so the client screen follows.
- Added a curated ElevenLabs voice catalog (`app/voice/voices.ts`) with a default voice per avatar character and `resolveVoiceIdV1` as the seam for a future per-Bot override; `apps/cloudflare/src/voice-assistant.ts` now picks the TTS provider per sentence, since the SDK reads `tts` once, so a borrowed voice can speak another Bot's work and be handed back. Read-outs are first person for the current Bot's own work and named only for another Bot's.
- The native shell gained a fixed voice control on the Bot composer that never morphs with the dictate/send button, per-Bot start/end/move, page-follow on hand-over, a collapsed desk sidebar and hidden Back during a call, and Android's system back gesture ending the call. Separately, the turn-bridge acknowledgment phrases were lengthened past the SDK `SentenceChunker` minimum — "Hang on." at eight characters was buffered until the stream ended, so roughly one stalled turn in six played silence — with a guard test asserting each phrase against the SDK's own chunker.

> **Known risk:** the ElevenLabs voice ids are that provider's public premade voices and have not been played against this account; an unreachable voice id would reach a person as a sentence that never becomes sound. This is stated in the ADR and `docs/voice.md`.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The branch is large but coherent and well covered by behavioural tests (the bridge fix is pinned against the SDK's own SentenceChunker, and the streaming-TTS regression now has a test that genuinely fails without the fix); the remaining issues are edge paths - a directory read failure that still reports an empty account, and an unvalidated botId reaching durable state - which are worth addressing but do not undermine the main flow.

## Testing

Baseline `bun test` had already passed, so I added only what this diff touches. The voice Durable Object suite ran three times in full plus targeted runs of every new per-Bot test, all driven through real WebSocket sessions against the real VoiceAssistant object in workerd — a call named at a Bot wears that Bot in its prompt and voice, switch_bot moves it durably and pushes a voice/target frame, an answer from a Bot the call left is spoken in that Bot's borrowed voice and the call's own voice returns after, every synthesized sentence went through the streaming branch, and every bridge phrase is emitted whole by the SDK's own SentenceChunker. I wrote and drove two adversarial scenarios the suite did not cover — an account whose every Bot has been deleted, and a client naming a Bot on someone else's account — and both hold: the empty account gets the account-wide prompt with no contradict

First working slice of the terminal-first Computer (`docs/incus-computer-host-plan.md` §10), running on the existing Fly Sprite.

**Jev reviews every command.** `computer_exec` is now a `mutate` call, so every command goes through the existing call review before it runs. That also guards against a prompt-injected `curl` carrying data out.

**Connected accounts from the terminal, with no credential on the Computer.** This slice covers GitHub only.

- When a Turn has a connected account with a route, a foreground `computer_exec` gets a short-lived HMAC-signed token. The token names the Bot object and a nonce, and is signed with `COMPUTER_HOST_TOKEN`.
- The command is prefixed with a prelude that starts a loopback HTTPS proxy on the Sprite (`computer/fly/egress.ts`). The prelude also sets `HTTPS_PROXY`, the CA bundle variables, and a placeholder `GH_TOKEN`.
- The proxy terminates TLS only for routed hosts (`api.github.com`), using a CA it creates with `openssl`. It strips the CLI's `authorization` header and posts each request to `POST /api/computer/egress`. Every other host is a plain tunnel.
- The Worker verifies the token before it addresses any object (`apps/cloudflare/src/computer-egress.ts`). It then calls `answerComputerEgress` on the Bot object, which answers only while that exec call is running.
- Reads are sent as the account through Composio's `tools/execute/proxy` (`app/connect/egress.ts`). Writes (everything except GET, HEAD and GraphQL queries) first go through the Turn's prepare hooks as a `mutate` `credentialed_request` call, so Jev reviews them. A refusal comes back as a 403 whose `message` the CLI prints. A byte-identical write repeated within one command is answered from the first result instead of being sent again.

**Terminal ergonomics**
- New Sprites also install `git`, `gh`, `jq`, `openssl` and Python. Existing Sprites get the proxy files through the normal runtime update, and a Bot installs the CLIs with apt when it needs them.
- The prompt now steers Bots to do work in the terminal: CLIs, plus Python scripts for longer jobs.
- `computer_exec` now says when the host cut output short at 30 KB, and how to read the rest.

**Also in this PR**
- The architecture, Jev plan and Incus plan docs are updated, including known gaps. The main ones: foreground commands only; the token sits in the command's environment; `git` to github.com isn't routed; bodies must be JSON objects.
- `AGENTS.md` notes that Jev's latency and price are negligible.
- A What's New entry, with no still because there is no screen to show.

**Validation**
- `typecheck` and all its gates pass.
- The new unit tests pass. They include an end-to-end run of the real proxy through `curl` against a fake Worker.
- `validate:runtime` passes (397/397 workerd) and `validate:integration` passes (190/190).
- Locally, `applets/sdk` `plugin-build` fails whenever any other test that serves or spawns runs before it in the same process. It fails the same way on a clean `origin/main` in this sandbox, so it isn't this change. `Check` is the judge.

## What and why

A Bot that drives a browser eventually hits a password box or a card form. Until now the only way through was for the person to type it into chat, where it lands in the transcript, the event log and the model's context. This PR is groundwork for item 12: a Bot can **ask for a secret and fill it into a site without the value ever entering its conversation**. It includes no card issuing and no payment provider.

![A Bot asks for a coffee shop password in a card with a masked field, a Save button and the note “Kept out of the chat”.](https://github.com/timoconnellaus/frockbot/blob/claude/charming-maxwell-r6nxhq-secure-fill/app/whats-new/media/secret-fill.webp?raw=true)

**How it works:**

1. **Ask.** The Bot sends a `secret-request` through `send_to_user` with a prompt and a label, plus optional `origin` and `payment`. The `credentials` Plugin draws the card, and the kernel binds the card's one host-drawn `SecretField` to a request it recorded. The kernel refuses a `SecretField` anywhere else: on a Bot-authored card, in another Plugin's draw, or in a handler's answer. Sending the request ends the Turn.
2. **Save.** The person types the value into a masked field. The value goes straight from the client to `POST /api/bots/:bot/secret-requests/:requestId`, never through a card action or the renderer's data model. The Bot Durable Object checks it against the recorded request and hands it to the User Durable Object. The User DO seals it as an account-scoped credential generation under the `secrets` Package. On an input-delivery Turn, the Bot is given only an opaque `secret-…` reference, a name and the terms. A Luhn-valid card number counts as a payment detail whatever the Bot asked for.
3. **Fill.** `computer_browser` `fill` accepts `secret` in place of text. The rules:
   - A non-payment secret fills only on the origin it was saved for.
   - A payment detail needs a fresh Approval of the page origin, the field and the reference. A payment detail is one that was saved as payment, or a fill into a field labelled like "Card number" or "CVC". A fill on any other origin needs the same Approval. The kernel mints it, it can be used once, and it is valid for ten minutes.
   - The value is leased for one action and typed over CDP. On the Computer it reaches `browser.mjs` only as that one process's stdin, and never appears in an environment or a command line.
   - The tool result says only whether the field was filled. Later snapshots leave out marked fields, password fields and `cc-*` fields, and failure text is scrubbed.
4. **Manage.** Settings → Account → Saved secrets lists saved secrets and deletes them.

**What this does not protect against (known issue 51).** A fill by reference keeps the value out of the model's context, the transcript, the event log, audit, logs and snapshots. It does not keep the value from code that the Bot, or another Bot of the same User, deliberately runs on the Computer. The Bot's shell has sudo there, and the one browser all of the User's Bots share answers its debugging port on localhost, so a script can read a filled field back out of the page. The fix is to take the browser out of the Bot's reach: a browser, or an injection broker in front of it, that the Bot's shell cannot attach to. That is a Computer redesign and is left for later.

**Wire compatibility.** The `secret-request` payload on the log keeps its three-field shape (`type`, `prompt`, `secretName`), so the exact-key decoders in installed apps still read it. `origin` and `payment` travel beside it in the tool input (`splitSecretRequestTermsV1`) and are stored on the request the kernel records. An app older than this release draws "This card can't be shown" for the new `SecretField` (known issue 52).

## What changed

- **Contracts:** `core/contracts/send-to-user.ts` reserves `secret-fill-` approval ids to the kernel. `first-party-cards.ts` carries the request terms.
- **App:** new `app/secrets/`, with tests for each file:
  - `shared.ts`: shapes, limits, origin and Luhn checks, value scrubbing.
  - `user.ts`: the vault over the credential store.
  - `bot.ts`: the request store and the save seam.
  - `fill.ts`: the origin and Approval policy, and the one-action lease.
  - `document.ts`: the Settings document.
- **App, shell:**
  - `send_to_user` splits off the terms, refuses a Bot-authored `SecretField`, and ends the Turn on a request.
  - `cards.ts` gains `bindCardSecretFieldsV1`. `backend-composition.ts` calls it to bind the field and record the request.
  - New `secret-saved` pending input and `secret` audit preview.
- **Seeded Plugin:** the `credentials` card now says what the secret is saved as and where it is used, then draws the field and a "Kept out of the chat" note. The artifacts, the Frock catalog JSON and the A2UI Skill references were regenerated with the repo scripts.
- **Cloudflare:**
  - The User DO gains `storeSecret`, `describeSecret`, `leaseSecret`, `settleSecret`, `listSecrets` and `deleteSecret`. It refuses to store or lease while the account is being deleted.
  - The Bot DO gains `submitSecret`.
  - The user application serves the save route.
  - The gateway serves `GET /api/secrets` and `POST /api/secrets/:id/delete`.
- **Computer:**
  - `ComputerBrowserAction` gains `fill-secret`, carrying the origin the page must be on.
  - `ComputerSecretFillSeamV1` asks the Bot's authority before any lease.
  - On Fly, the exec carries the value as extra stdin after the script. The script's prelude reads from `/dev/null`, and its last line `exec`s `browser.mjs`, which reads the rest of stdin. So nothing before the helper can take the value, and bash never reads it as a command.
  - `browser.mjs` checks the origin and fills the field in the page or in a frame. It then masks the field and answers without a snapshot. A refusal uses fixed wording.
  - The fake host carries a one-page browser that follows the same rule, including refusing a fill that arrives without a value on stdin.
  - A new host contract case holds both hosts to "typed only on its origin, never answered back". The vocabulary and import gates pass.
- **Flutter:**
  - A `SecretField` Frock catalog component: masked, with no suggestions or autocorrect. The card keeps the draft in memory only and empties it once saved.
  - `CardSecretsScope`, and `saveSecret` on the card client.
  - `SecretsPage` under Account, with semantics ids.
- **Docs:**
  - `CONTEXT.md`: "Saved secret".
  - Architecture §2, §4, §6 and §10, plus a new Saved secrets section.
  - Parity: 57h is marked groundwork, and a new 57k row is marked partial.
  - Known issues 51–53.
- **What's New:** a `secret-fill` entry, "Saved passwords and cards", with the still above. It was rendered from the real chat pane and card, in Inter on the dark theme, at 1920×1080.

**Proof that the value is recorded nowhere but where it has to go.** The tests check what was actually recorded and delivered, not return values:

- `apps/cloudflare/test/secret-request.workerd.ts` saves a value through the real route, then scans every KV record and every SQL row of both the Bot and the User Durable Objects.
- It then runs a full fill Turn through a fake `COMPUTER_HOST` and scans both objects again.
- The value reaches the host only as the helper's stdin. No exec call carries it in `env`, and it is not in the script.
- It is absent from every durable record: the event log (tool calls, tool results and recorded model requests), the audit rows and the card state. The audit row reads `fill Password secret-…`.
- `computer/fly/computer.test.ts` runs the real generated exec document through real `bash -s` on a streamed stdin. The guard stand-in reads stdin, and the value is valid shell (`… "quoted"; touch pwned` plus a `$(…)` line).
  - The helper receives exactly the value, with nothing in its argv or env.
  - The guard reads nothing, and no command in the value runs.
  - A helper that exits before reading leaves the value unread in the pipe.
  - Removi

## Intent

Tim's voice call with his Bot Bob went haywire and Bob answered a prior question instead of the one asked. Tim asked me to look at the voice conversation and the exchange with Bob, identify what went wrong, fix it, test it and release. Two defects, both fixed here. (1) A question handed to a Bot by the voice session (or by another Bot) runs as an 'agent' Turn, and every work Package's manifest and the restated admission ceilings in tool code admitted only chat, automation and subagent, so Bob on the call was refused his Gmail tools (Connect package) and the Computer tools, and told Tim the app had been disconnected. Fix: add 'agent' to the turnTypes/admissionCeiling of every work tool and model capability (connect, web, image, routines, machine-registry, computer, ollama-cloud web search and models, frock-ai, catalog providers) per parity register row 57 (work tools on every working turn type). machine-control stays chat-only deliberately because it needs an approval card; subagent dispatch stays chat+automation deliberately (depth bound). Regression test: a Gmail tool on an agent Turn executes instead of being denied. (2) A Bot answer that settles on one call and is not heard is read out first on the next call. The read-out sentence is composed once when the answer settles ('a moment ago' framing), cached, and replayed verbatim on the next call an hour later, so it landed as an answer to what Tim had just asked; and the prompt's <answers> block told the assistant to 'mention them first' with no request or age, so the assistant also repeated the old answer as if it answered the new question. Fix: on a call other than the one the question was asked on, a cached sentence is preceded by a plain deterministic lead-in ('Earlier, about an hour ago, you asked Bob about ...'), no extra model call; the <answers> block carries each unheard answer under its request and age and says they are read out separately and are never the answer to what is being asked now. describeVoiceAgeV1 is shared by the lead-in, the composer prompt and the <answers> block. The existing 'ending the call during composition retains the answer for the next call' workerd test now asserts the placed sentence. Tests are kept behavioural (tool execution, rendered prompt, spoken transcript frame) per the test-quality rule. Docs: docs/voice.md updated in both places. Release goes through the ordinary main.yml -> tag -> release.yml path after merge.

## What Changed

- Added `agent` to the `turnTypes`/`admissionCeiling` of every work tool and model capability — Connect, web fetch, image, routines, machine registry, computer/browser control, ollama-cloud web search and models, frock-ai and catalog providers — so a Bot answering over voice or from another Bot is no longer refused its apps and Computer tools. `machine-control` stays chat-only (approval card) and subagent dispatch stays chat+automation (depth bound).
- Reworked unheard delegation read-outs in `app/voice/assistant.ts` and `apps/cloudflare/src/voice-assistant.ts`: the composer no longer states how long ago a request was made and returns nothing on failure (so a plain read-out is never cached), and placement is decided at speak time — by `voiceAgePlacedV1` or by the answer being heard on a different call — prefixing a deterministic lead-in ("Earlier, about an hour ago, you asked Bob about …") with no extra model call. The prompt's `<answers>` block now carries each answer under its request and age via the shared `describeVoiceAgeV1`, and states the answers are read out separately and are never the answer to the current question.
- Extended tests and docs: a Gmail tool executing on an agent Turn, the rendered `<answers>` block and lead-in wording, and the workerd end-of-call retention test now asserting the placed spoken frame; `docs/voice.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/grokbot-parity.md` and the voice live checklist updated to describe agent-turn tool admission and speak-time placement.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Both defects are fixed at the right boundary — placement is decided once at speak time from live age plus call identity and never cached, and the agent turn type was added to exactly the work capabilities the intent names with the four approval-bound ones deliberately left chat-only — and each fix has a behavioural test (tool execution on an agent Turn, rendered prompt, spoken transcript frame) with no reachable wrong-output path found across same-call, cross-call, retry and compose-refused traces.

## Testing

The configured `bun test` baseline had already passed; on top of it I ran the voice session workerd suite (the real Durable Object over real WebSockets) and the targeted unit suites for the admission changes. The six read-out scenarios were driven against the running object rather than read from code, and the evidence is the product's own output: the spoken transcript frames the client receives and the system prompt the object actually emits, both captured live and saved as artifacts, plus a before/after reproduction of the ungrammatical failure sentence. There is no rendered GUI surface in this change — the end-user surface is spoken audio and a model prompt, so the transcripts and the emitted prompt stand in for screenshots. The two tool-admission scenarios were exercised only through package-level test runs against the real Connect package and registry; that is not a live drive of the product, so both are reported untested. The only failure seen was a pre-existing, load-sensitive acknowledgment-audio test unrelated to the diff.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Intent

Part of Tim's Jev plan (context selection, items P2 and P3 on the map he approved). Memory recall rerank: after hybrid recall finds a Turn's automatic recall candidates, the memory host's optional rankRecall asks Jev one Noul per candidate (up to 12) 'does it help the Bot answer or act on the request now'; code drops those below 0.2 and orders the rest by score, candidates past the judged window follow in recall order. Skill nomination: at a Turn's first request, the Skills feature's optional nominate asks Jev one Noul per Skill (only when the catalog has at most 24) and names up to three with noul >= 0.7 in a tail runtime note. Tim's constraints: prompt caching must keep working, so neither touches the system prompt or tool list — recall uses the existing <memory-recall> message, nomination uses a tail runtime note at step 1 only. Both are context quality, not safety (rigor proportional to consequence): Jev failure, timeout (3s) or a non-supervision fake 422 returns undefined/[] and leaves behaviour exactly as before; neither is enforced. Added appendRuntimeNoteV1 in core/contracts so runtime notes from several request hooks (supervision acknowledgement/specialist/question, skills, turn budget) share ONE trailing user message, because some providers refuse two user messages in a row. Labelled eval: bun run eval:context 5/5 live on jev-1.13.0. The hybrid.ts header that said 'No second model reranks' is updated.

## What Changed
- **Memory recall rerank:** the memory host has a new optional `rankRecall`, set up in `app/shell/backend-memory.ts`. After hybrid recall picks a Turn's automatic recall candidates, `app/supervision/memory-recall.ts` asks Jev one Noul per candidate, for up to 12 candidates. Candidates scoring below 0.2 are dropped and the rest are sorted by score. Candidates beyond the 12 that Jev judged keep their recall order after the judged ones. The results still go out through the existing `<memory-recall>` message. The `hybrid.ts` header no longer says "No second model reranks".
- **Skill nomination:** the Skills host has a new optional `nominate`. At a Turn's first request, `app/supervision/skill-nomination.ts` asks Jev one Noul per Skill, but only when the catalog has 24 Skills or fewer. It names up to three Skills scoring 0.7 or higher in a runtime note at the end of the request. Neither feature changes the system prompt or the tool list. If Jev fails, times out (3s) or returns a 422, the feature returns undefined or `[]` and the request goes out as it did before.
- **Shared runtime note:** `appendRuntimeNoteV1` is new in `core/contracts`. The supervision notes, the Skills note and the turn-budget note now go into one trailing user message instead of each adding its own. Unit tests cover the helper, recall reranking and Skill nomination. A labelled eval runs with `bun run eval:context`, and the README and Jev and memory docs describe it.

hits.body:
Three defects from the landed-feature verification run on `main` (`findings-v4`, items F1/F2 plus Tim's copy audit), all on one code path.

## A. BLOCKER — a model request past its budget answered HTTP 500

**Evidence.** `POST /api/bots/<bot>/turns 500` after 64.9s, reproduced twice on two fresh users with a real Flock AI model doing applet work. `wrangler.log`: `Uncaught Error: Model response outcome is uncertain: The operation was aborted due to timeout` at `packages/kernel-do/src/authority.ts:616`. Debug events: `model/request` and `model/reconciliation-required` exactly 60s apart. On screen: `Couldn't reach the Bot. Check your connection and try again.`

**Root cause — two of them, stacked.**

1. `FLOCK_AI_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS_V1` was 60s, and the signal carrying it was handed to `fetch` and **left armed after the response headers arrived**. `fetch` resolves at the headers; the deadline then guillotined the *response body* mid-stream. A tool-calling step carrying the applets `SKILL.md` plus the dynamic-tool schemas crosses a minute routinely, so this was not a slow gateway — it was the ordinary case. The abort surfaced as a raw `TimeoutError`, not as the kernel's `ModelRequestDeadlineError`, so `streamWithModelRequestDeadlinesV1`'s own reason check did not recognise it.
2. The Agent read a stream that started and then errored as an **uncertain** outcome (`kernel-agent-loop/src/index.ts:1060`) and threw `ModelEffectReconciliationRequiredError`. `BotDurableAuthority.executeAcceptedRun` parked the run on a reconciliation **and rethrew** — which is what the route turned into a 500. ADR 0028 already decided this question for *recovery* (park only when somebody can be asked; Flock AI and Ollama Cloud keep no addressable copy, so nobody can) but the executing path never got the rule. The asymmetry is the blocker.

**Fix.**

- `apps/cloudflare/src/flock-ai.ts` — the gateway budget bounds *reaching* the gateway and nothing after it. A plain `AbortController` plus a timer, disarmed in a `finally` the moment the response exists. The caller's `signal` is still chained in and is **never** disarmed, so a Stop or a superseding message still tears down a request whose body is mid-flight.
- `packages/kernel-do/src/authority.ts` — a new `parkOrSettleUnresolvedRun` applies ADR 0028's `providerReconciles` predicate on the live path, at both catch sites. Provider that cannot be asked → `failRun`, which runs the ordinary run-terminal settlement (`settledEventsV1` closes the open Turn with a `turn/end`, streamed words kept, reason on the record) and returns the settled completion, so the turn POST answers normally instead of throwing. Provider that *can* be asked → parks and rethrows, exactly as before.

**Budget decision.** `FLOCK_AI_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS_V1` 60s → `MODEL_FIRST_BYTE_DEADLINE_MS_V1` (120s), deliberately *equal* rather than larger: the kernel's first-byte deadline is the one that carries a sentence written for a person, so it should win the race and the host budget becomes a backstop for a transport that never reaches the seam. The streaming body is bounded by `MODEL_IDLE_DEADLINE_MS_V1` (60s between events) — a stream that has produced a chunk has proved the model is generating, so a minute of silence after that is a dead socket. Both sit far inside `TURN_DEADLINE_MS_V1` (15 min, PR 170), which is never exceeded.

## B. The Bot's ack was never rendered

**Evidence.** Debug seq 30-32: the model emitted `"On it — building the 2027 countdown applet now."` as a plain `assistant/message`, then called tools. It appears in no UI state — not mid-Turn, not after failure, not after reload.

**Root cause.** The prompt (PR 186) said sends are the only thing the user sees but never said *not to write the line in your own text*, and the client draws one bubble per send (issue 153) — so a correct-looking acknowledgement went to nobody.

**Fix, both ends.**

- Prompt: "Your own text is not shown to the user. Writing a line in your reply instead of calling `send_to_user` means nobody reads it." and "your first action is a `send_to_user` call…".
- Runtime: a new kernel hook `agent/assistant-text`, raised for a step that wrote text *and* called tools, immediately after the `assistant/message` is journaled and **before any tool runs**. The Shell listens and promotes the text to one `send/to-user`. Skipped when the step already sent; the occurrence id is derived from the model request, so a replayed step promotes to the same occurrence rather than a second bubble. The end-of-Turn fallback (`lastSentTextV1`) is untouched.
- One consequence handled: promoting a send would have made the issue-153 gate swallow a *final* answer written as plain text. `visibleAssistantText` now suppresses a settled answer only when it duplicates something the Turn actually sent — the rule is against saying the same thing twice, not against saying a second thing. Mid-Turn the gate stays absolute.

## C. Terminal-outcome copy leaked architecture

A person could read `Reconciliation was explicitly abandoned: Bot turn ended with outcome model-error: Flock AI keeps no durable copy of an interrupted response, so it cannot be recovered`.

New `packages/plugin-shell/src/run-failure-copy.ts`, one mapping, consulted in `projectClientRunV1` so **every** client gets it:

1. the kernel's own person-facing sentences (the two model deadlines, the Turn deadline, `UNRECONCILABLE_RUN_FAILURE_V1`) matched as substrings, since the settling layer wraps the reason it was handed;
2. otherwise the terminal `turn/end` outcome, mapped over a `Record<TurnOutcome, string>` that is total — adding an outcome to the kernel union is a type error here rather than a silent generic line.

The stored `failure` is unchanged and still what `/api/debug` reads. Also replaced: `"Stopped by an authenticated Stop command."` → `"You stopped this."`, and the resumable run's wire message → `"This reply stopped partway. Try again to continue it."`. No provider display names touched (the Flock AI → Frock AI rename is a separate PR).

## Tests

- `apps/cloudflare/src/flock-ai.test.ts` — a body still streaming past the deadline is **not** torn down; a Stop still tears down a body that has started.
- `packages/kernel-do/src/model-timeout-settlement.test.ts` — a provider that stalls past the budget: the turn call **resolves** (no uncaught error, no 500), the run is `failed`, a `turn/end` closes the Turn, the streamed words survive, the active-run lock is released; and the sibling case where a reconciling provider still parks.
- `packages/kernel-agent-loop/src/index.test.ts` — `agent/assistant-text` fires ahead of the tool the same step called; nothing fires for a step with no text or no tools.
- `packages/plugin-shell/src/agent.test.ts` — the prompt wording; one send recorded from promoted text; a step that already spoke (and a replay) adds nothing.
- `packages/plugin-shell/src/run-failure-copy.test.ts` — the guard: no mapped sentence contains `reconcil`, `outcome`, `durable`, `supersede`, `admission`, `provider`, `model-error`, `tool-error`, event names or a bare `run`; the real diagnostic never reaches the copy; the projection sends the copy, not the diagnostic.

**Green:** `bun run typecheck` (all 73 packages), `packages/{kernel-do,kernel-agent-loop,plugin-shell} bun test src` (120 / 50 / 418), `apps/cloudflare bun test src` (149), and `bun run test:workerd -- interrupted-recovery flock-ai-default approvals unread` (8).

## Intent

Tim approved a map of Jev uses and asked to build it all, PR by PR. This PR is loop health + the per-send claim check (map items P9/P10). Loop health: from step 5 of a Turn, code detects loop signals (same tool+arguments 3 times, or 3 failed results in a row); Jev is asked a single Noul 'is it moving the work forward' at step 5, then every 4 steps, or every 2 while a signal is present. Stuck = noul <= 0.25, or <= 0.45 with a signal. A stuck Turn gets a tail runtime note (never the system prompt: Tim requires prompt caching to stay intact) telling it to stop repeating, try another approach, hand it to the thinking specialist (the Mentor) when offered, or tell the person what blocks it. Recorded as a supervision/progress session event and reused on resume. Claim check: every text send is also asked (in parallel with the redundancy question, and regardless of its vetoes) whether it says something was done that none of this Turn's calls did; unsupported at >= 0.7 withholds with reason unsupported_claim; it does not end the Turn even as a finish (delivery and stepContinuation both use withheldSendEndsTurnV1), runs at most once per Turn so it cannot loop, and shows in audit as 'claimed undone work'. Supervision is enforced, not shadow; JEV_API_KEY required; a Jev failure retries once then the Turn fails (Tim's decisions). The weighted failure score/decay from the old plan was deliberately not built. Live eval:response-review: claim 10/10, progressing 6/6; one pre-existing relay case (toast-condensed) sits at p 0.59 against a 0.6 threshold and flickers, unrelated to this change.

## What Changed

- **Loop health** (`app/supervision/loop-health.ts`, `loop.ts`, `jev.ts`): from step 5 of a Turn, code watches for loop signals: the same tool with the same arguments 3 times, or 3 failed results in a row. At step 5 Jev is asked one Noul question, "is it moving the work forward?", and asked again every 4 steps after that, or every 2 while a signal is present. A Turn counts as stuck at noul ≤ 0.25, or ≤ 0.45 when a signal is present. A stuck Turn gets a runtime note at the end of the request, never in the system prompt, so prompt caching stays intact. The note tells the model to stop repeating itself, try another approach, hand off to the Mentor when it is offered, or tell the person what is blocking it. Each check is recorded as a new `supervision/progress` session event, and a resumed Turn reuses it.
- **Per-send claim check** (`app/supervision/claim-check.ts`): every text send gets a second question, run in parallel with the redundancy question and whatever that question decides: does the send say something was done that none of this Turn's calls did? At ≥ 0.7 the send is withheld with reason `unsupported_claim`. The check runs at most once per Turn so it cannot loop. A withheld claim never ends the Turn, even on a finish, because `app/shell/delivery.ts` and the step-continuation logic now both use the shared `withheldSendEndsTurnV1`. The Bot audit shows these withholds as "claimed undone work".
- **Contracts, evals, docs, tests**: `core/contracts` gains `ProgressDecisionV1` and its decoder plus the new session event. `eval:response-review` gains claim and progressing fixtures and scoring. The Jev supervision plan and architecture docs now describe this flow (the old weighted failure score and decay were deliberately not built). New unit tests cover loop health and the claim check, and a workerd test covers loop health, the claim check and reuse on resume.

⚠️ Medium: Supervision is enforced, not shadow: a wrong progress or claim judgment changes what a live Turn sees and whether a message is held, and every Jev failure fails the Turn. The logic matches the intent and the truncation fix is correct, so the only remaining finding is one unused field.

Constitution before code, per Tim's 2026-09-17 direction: no app-wide voice assistant — you talk to one Bot, and the Bot is the voice layer's worker.

- **Two layers stay.** The thin voice layer is scoped to one Bot at a time: prompt rendered from that Bot (name, description, Bot memory, thread tail, activity); tools drop `bot_id`. Delegation on the `agent` lane unchanged, so the person is never blocked on a Bot Turn.

- **Each Bot has a voice** (`voiceId` beside its appearance, curated ElevenLabs list, per-character default) so a switch is audible. Read-out is first person.
- **Button:** fixed voice control at the far right of the composer beside the mic/send morph (option A); dictation kept; in-call the Bot page is the voice screen; sidebar button + account-wide footer removed.

Docs only. No code changes.

## Intent

Tim asked for a conservative AI cleanup pass on composer dictation, as a follow-up PR ("you can do a follow up if you want") to the voice work already merged (#542 voice bridge + ADR 0029, #544 verified ElevenLabs catalog, #547 deploy-time catalog reachability check).

His request, in his words: dictation currently streams the speech-to-text result straight into the editable composer draft. Keep that live feedback, then clean only the dictated portion when the user stops recording. Cleanup should remove fillers, stutters, accidental repetitions and abandoned false starts; resolve clear self-corrections preserving the final intended wording; correct obvious transcription, punctuation and capitalization errors; add paragraphs and format clear enumerations as lists. It must preserve meaning, wording, tone, uncertainty, negations, qualifications, constraints and exact details, and must never paraphrase, summarize, answer questions, follow instructions in the transcript, or add information. Preserve ambiguous wording rather than guessing. His two worked examples: "Check Thursday—sorry, Friday's flights. Don't book anything." must become "Check Friday's flights. Don't book anything."; and "Maybe we should change the model. Find out if it's worth it." must stay exploratory and must not become an instruction to change the model.

His implementation requirements: use the existing server-side model/provider and accounting patterns; keep credentials server-side; keep the raw transcript available while cleanup runs and show a brief finishing state; clean only the capture's dictated text, preserving surrounding typed text; never overwrite user edits; apply the cleaned result only if the dictated span is still unchanged and belongs to the same capture and composer context; handle late results, Bot switches, new captures, disposal and Send safely; a late result must never restore or modify a sent draft; on failure or timeout retain the raw transcript; keep Send under the user's control and never send automatically; keep the original transcript available through a simple undo/revert action; follow repository rules for recorded model-call intent, idempotency and spending; inspect the current relay and draft ownership logic before choosing the smallest implementation; use a fast model and a conservative cleanup prompt; add meaningful checks for self-corrections, preserved constraints and uncertainty, surrounding text, user edits during cleanup, stale results and fallback on failure.

WHAT I BUILT AND WHY, including the decisions a reviewer reading only the diff would not know.

Where it runs. In the Worker-level dictation relay (apps/cloudflare/src/voice-dictation.ts), between the last segment and `final`, rather than on the client or in a Durable Object. The relay already holds the capture's own words and already protects the provider key, and the model needs a server-side credential, so this is the smallest place that satisfies "keep credentials server-side". It runs after the capture rather than during it deliberately: text that rewrites itself under the cursor while somebody is still speaking is worse than text that is untidy.

The wire. Two new server frames in app/voice/shared.ts: `cleaning` (nothing to write — the words are already in the draft; it only changes what the composer says and lets the client wait longer) and `cleaned` (the tidied form of the whole capture, at most once, always before `final`). No capture id on the frames: one socket per capture and teardown cancels the inbound subscription, so cross-capture leakage is impossible by construction rather than by checking.

The split that matters. app/voice/dictation-cleanup.ts is pure and holds both the prompt and, more importantly, what we refuse to accept back. The relay owns the policy; the Worker's wiring (voiceDictationCleanup in apps/cloudflare/src/index.ts) has no judgement in it and does exactly two things: book the spend, reach the gateway. That split is the point — the guards are the safety property, and a guard you cannot run without a model is a guard nobody runs. All 23 guard tests run with no model and no network.

The prompt is a request; the guards are the property. A tidied transcript is refused, and the raw text stands, when it is empty, unchanged, meaningfully longer (added information), much shorter (summarised), opens like a model talking to us, had a question that is no longer a question, or dropped every negation or every uncertainty the raw text carried. Tim's two examples are both tests: the Thursday/Friday self-correction is accepted; "Maybe we should change the model" becoming "Change the model" is refused as lost-uncertainty. The "dropped every one" rule rather than "dropped any one" is deliberate: a real self-correction may legitimately drop one "not" while another remains, and refusing that would refuse most real corrections; what this catches is the whole category going missing, which is what an over-eager tidy does. Refusals are named rather than boolean and logged, because "cleanup is off" and "cleanup keeps eating people's negations" look identical without that line.

One hardening beyond the brief. The transcript is fenced between <transcript> markers and declared DATA, because people dictate imperatives constantly. I found that the fence could be closed from inside by a transcript containing the closing marker, so the markers are stripped out of the transcript before it is fenced. Only the prompt is altered; every guard still compares against the untouched transcript, so this can never be the reason text changes in a draft. Nobody dictates "</transcript>" by accident, which is exactly why it is worth removing.

Client safety fell out of existing code rather than being written, which is the main reason the diff is small. apps/native/lib/voice/dictation.dart already had DictationDraftRange, which owns the capture's span, re-anchors on surrounding typing, and fences permanently if the person edits inside the transcript. Applying the cleaned text through that same path gives "apply only if the dictated span is unchanged" and "a late result never modifies a sent draft" for free: an edited span is already fenced and takes nothing more, and a sent draft no longer contains the span at all, so indexOf fails and the range fences. I tested both directly rather than asserting the mechanism, because "it falls out" is a claim that needs evidence.

Revert. DictationController keeps the raw transcript from the moment a tidy-up replaces it and exposes revertCleanup(), which writes back through the same range. The offer is withdrawn once the range is fenced, because from then on the field is partly the person's own edit and swapping it would take the edit with it. The composer shows "Use what I said" — quiet, a TextButton not a filled button, because tidying is done to somebody's words without being asked so the way back must be visible, but it is not an action anybody came here to take.

Spending and idempotency. One model call per capture, booked through the account's own voice object (a new "cleanup" action on the existing dictationLease RPC) before the model is asked, counted in the same daily meter as the dictation seconds that capture spent, 400 per UTC day, never refunded. Never refunded on purpose: an eviction between the booking and the answer should cost the account one call rather than lose the record that a call was made. There is no idempotency key because there is no retry — a tidy-up that fails is not tried again, the raw transcript simply stands. The cleanup cap is deliberately NOT part of VoiceLedgerV1.exceededCap: that one decides whether a voice call may go on, and a day of tidy-ups is no reason to refuse somebody a conversation.

The owner's contract, verbatim: "it should ack straight away, keep the user posted on real beats (result, decision, blocker), it shouldn't do a play-by-play and it shouldn't leave the user hanging on something they're waiting for. And long work gets a short 'on it' or similar then the result when it's ready."

Before this, the only conversational guidance the model got was the `send_to_user` description, which said what the tool does and nothing about when to use it. There is no ADR or research note covering acknowledgement, progress or narration — the docs record only that `SendToUser` is the one voice and that a send is one bubble.

## The prompt section

`plugin-shell` now contributes a `conversation` section (order 1, after identity) beside the tool it governs, so the section and the tool description are written in one module and cannot drift:

```
## Talking to the user

Everything the user sees is a `send_to_user` call; nothing else reaches them.
When a request will take more than a moment, send one short line first — "On it." or "Looking into that." — then go quiet and work.
After that, send only on a real beat: the result, a decision only the user can make, or a blocker you cannot get past.
Never narrate what you are doing, what you are about to do, or which tool you are using.
Never leave a question or a request hanging: before you stop, the user must have the answer, the result, or the reason there isn't one.
When the work is finished, send the result itself, not an account of how you got it.
Keep every message short — a line or two, no preamble and no sign-off.
Don't say the same thing twice.
```

The `send_to_user` description gained the matching "when", ahead of the payload list.

## Mechanics

No runtime change was needed, and the tests now hold the behaviour in place:

- The ack is its own bubble, immediately. `send_to_user` appends `send/to-user` and awaits `session.flush()` inside the tool, so the event is durable and streamed mid-Turn rather than at settle.
- A Turn that ends on prose is not dropped: `executeBotTurn` derives the assistant text and falls back to the last `text` payload, so a final answer reaches the client either way.
- `agent/step-continuation` is the seam where a stronger end-of-turn guard would live; nothing subscribes to it today. Left as is — the prompt carries the rule, and forcing a send from the runtime would be a behaviour change beyond this contract.

## Tests

- `packages/plugin-shell/src/agent.test.ts` mounts `SystemPromptRegistry` and asserts the section is assembled into the prompt, states the acknowledge-then-beats rule, stays under 12 lines, and that the tool description says when to call it.
- `apps/cloudflare/test/integration/turn-admission.integration.ts` scripts the fake provider to send "On it." and then run `computer_exec`, and asserts the `send/to-user` event is recorded before the exec's result.

typecheck, `bun test` for the touched packages, the full integration suite (42 files, 111 tests) and `format:check` all pass.

Stage 5 of "Group Chats replace Projects" (`docs/plan.md`): Bots act on groups.

## What changes

- **Group tools.** In a Bot's own chat and in its Routines (the `groups` package's `group-management` capability, turn types `chat` and `automation`), the Bot gets `group_list`, `group_create`, `group_update` (rename, add or remove members), `group_archive` and `group_post`, plus a `<group_chats>` prompt section that names its groups. `app/groups/agent.ts` holds the tools and `app/shell/backend-groups.ts` the host.
  - Membership commands go to the User object as that Bot, so a Bot can only change groups it belongs to, and delete, restore and arrange stay the User's.
  - Command ids (`gb-…`) and outside-post message ids (`o-…`) are hashed from the User, Bot, run and call. A replay after eviction therefore commits once, and calls from two of the Bot's Sessions can't share a receipt.
- **Posting from outside.** `GroupChat.postFromBot` posts a member's message from its own chat or a Routine, idempotent by message id. It asks members the same way a member's message does: through Jev, or its mentions under the bound.
- **`bot_message` inside a group.** In a group Turn, the new Flock capability `group-bot-messaging` (agent lane) replaces `bot_message`.
  - It refuses a member (members are asked with an @mention in the thread) and folds the run id into its effect id.
  - `<teammates>` in a group lists only the Bots outside it.
  - The group reads each call back with the Turn and writes an Exchange line (`bot-message` event).
- **`@User` pushes.** A member's message that mentions `@User` is marked `mentionsUser`. The group writes `group:push:<seq>` in the post's transaction, and delivery goes through the User object's `deliverGroupPush`.
  - The alarm retries it until it is sent, and it is dropped once the person has read that message.
  - `push.ts` carries `groupId`: presence defers to a device viewing the group, the delivery receipt is keyed by group, and the FCM data includes `groupId`.
  - Routing that tap to the group in the app comes with stage 4.

## Stored state

Only new keys (`group:push:<seq>`, the body's optional `mentionsUser`, the new event type). No existing record changes shape, so no cleanup is needed.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`, and the full `bun test` (5325 pass).
- New unit tests: the tools (`app/groups/agent.test.ts`); the log's push and exchange lines; `mentionsUserV1`; reading a Turn's exchanges back; the group `bot_message` (refuses members, scoped effect id, teammates outside only); group push delivery (deferral, receipt key, FCM `groupId`).
- Integration (`group-chat.integration.ts`): General starts a group with `group_create` from its own chat, finds it with `group_list`, and posts with `group_post`.
- The browser suite is run locally before merge.

## What

Row 47 of the parity register — "Web search, web fetch and image generation as first-class tools" — asks for three tools. This PR lands the third, `generate_image`, as a new `@frockbot/plugin-image`. `web_search` and `web_fetch` landed in #62, which this branch is now rebased onto, so **row 47 moves to `landed`** naming all three Packages. Nothing here depends on `plugin-web`: it is mounted as a Connection-backed assigned Contribution, `plugin-image` as a hosted one, and the two meet only in the register row.

**No schema parity is claimed.** The register records only that GrokBot has a `GenerateImage` tool reached through `CallDynamicTool` and present on every turn type. No measured input schema, bound, or error shape for it exists anywhere in this repo. The contract below is defined from first principles.

## The shape of it

`generate_image` is the first tool whose effect is both **billed and durable**, so it is the pattern later ones copy.

- **Narrow seam.** The Package consumes `ImageModelV1 { run(model, input): Promise<ArrayBuffer> }` and names no Cloudflare type. `packages/plugin-shell/src/backend-image.ts` is the adapter, normalizing the three answers the Workers AI catalog gives — `{ image: "<base64>" }` from the FLUX models, a binary `ReadableStream` from the Stable Diffusion ones, a raw buffer from the binding.
- **Absent binding is a state, not a crash.** `BotStateEnv.AI` becomes optional, the `PACKAGE_BUNDLER` precedent. A host without Workers AI still mounts the Package; the tool refuses visibly on the Turn that calls it.
- **Intent before effect.** `image/generate-intent { effectId, model, promptHash, width, height }` is appended and flushed *before* the model runs; `image/generated` records the generation after the Workspace write settles. The `skill/write-intent` / `skill/written` pattern verbatim. The intent carries a prompt hash, not the prompt: `tool/call` already holds the input.
- **The Workspace is the fence.** Bytes go to a Package-declared durable root, `{kind: "package-declared", userId, packageId: "image", rootId: "generated"}`, at `<botId>/<effectId>.png`, written through the `WorkspaceFilesV1` the Bot Durable Object already builds — R2-backed, generation-recorded, and synced to the Computer as a real file. The object is keyed by the effect, so `reconcile()` reads exactly one path: present means the generation happened and reached storage; absent means it did not. `idempotent: false`, so the registry never retries; **nothing is ever billed twice.**
- **The durable result names the file, never the pixels.** `{path, root, generationId, contentHash, mimeType, width, height}` as stable JSON. `tool/result.content` is replayed into every later model request of the Turn, so base64 there would be re-sent on every step.
- **`width`/`height` describe the file, not the request.** `flux-1-schnell` accepts no size at all, so the tool reads the container header of the bytes it stored. A number in the durable log that no file agrees with is worse than no number. `packages/plugin-image/src/bytes.ts` is a pure PNG/JPEG header reader; bytes it cannot identify are refused rather than written.

Bounds: prompt 1–2 000 printable characters, `width`/`height` ∈ {512, 1024}, `n` = 1, 60 s timeout, a 4 MiB response cap and — the tighter real bound — `WORKSPACE_MAX_FILE_BYTES` (1 MiB), refused with its own reason.

## Model

Default `@cf/black-forest-labs/flux-1-schnell`, verified against Cloudflare's model catalog on 2026-08-31: Cloudflare names it the fastest text-to-image model on Workers AI, its input is `{prompt, seed?, steps?}` and its output is `{ image: "<base64>" }`. Declared as the `image.model` Package setting (manifest v4), with the SDXL and FLUX.2 models in its `enum`.

**One honest gap:** no durable store for Package *setting values* exists in this repo yet — every shipped manifest declares `settings: []` and no runtime reads one. So the setting is declared and the host seam accepts a value; until a store lands it resolves to the default. `resolveImageModelV1` refuses any model outside the declared list rather than passing it to the binding.

## Admission

Manifest v4, Capability `image-generation`, kind `tool`, `connectionTypes: []`, `admission.turnTypes` all four. The `ToolDefinition` declares none (absent = all) and registration passes the ceiling — image generation is a work tool on every turn type, per the register.

## Testing

- **Unit** (27 new): intent-before-effect ordering proven by *where in the log* the model was called; reconcile-after-eviction returns the stored image with `run()` called exactly once; a reconciled replay records `image/generated` once; prompt/size/field validation; absent binding and absent Workspace refusals; unidentifiable bytes never reaching a durable root; oversized image; a model failure carried into durable state; the Workers AI envelope normalizer in all four shapes.
- **Integration** (1 new, `SELF.fetch` through the deployed gateway): `test/workers-ai-fake.ts` binds `AI` to an auxiliary Worker's RPC entrypoint returning a genuine 1×1 PNG and counting its calls, so the production seam `env.AI.run(model, input)` is the one exercised. It asserts the `tool/result` names a Workspace path and carries no bytes, that the object is really in the durable-root store under the key the Workspace layout puts it at, that `image/generate-intent` precedes `image/generated` in the Bot's own log, and that replaying the same command id produces **no second `run()`**.

The `vitest.integration.config.ts` comment about `AI` being deliberately absent is replaced with the reason it is now bound (`MEMORY_INDEX` keeps its half of that note, unchanged and still true).

## Gates

`typecheck`, `format` + `format:check`, `bun test` (1 858 pass), `test:workerd` (88), `test:integration` (68), `lint:kernel-imports`, `build`. Rebased onto `origin/main` at `142188c` (#70).
